Deciphering and tailoring tandem reaction pathway for efficient photoelectrochemical nitrate-to-ammonia conversion at low overpotential
abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) nitrate (NO3-)-to-ammonia (NH3) conversion emerges as a green and efficient approach to recycling the waste nitrogen resources and producing the useful NH3 products at mild conditions. However, due to complex reaction steps, a high reaction overpotential is usually observed in PEC NO3--to-NH3 process, leading to a poor energy efficiency. Herein, we make efforts to decipher a tandem reaction pathway of NO3--nitrite (NO2-)-NH3 for PEC NO3- reduction reaction (NO3RR) at low overpotential and design CuxFey alloys as model cocatalysts to boosting the performance of Si-based photocathode by synergy effect of Cu and Fe active sites. An optimized PEC system with an excellent NH3 yield rate of over 0.4 mg·cm-2·h-1 for NO3- reduction have been successfully achieved at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode under 1-sun illumination. This work offers an insight on the design of robust photocathodes for efficient PEC NO3--to-NH3 conversion.

Overcoming kinetic barriers via continuous absorption-enhanced methanol synthesis in an integrated reactor-absorber process
abstract: Conventional methanol synthesis is constrained by thermodynamic equilibrium, requiring high-pressure synthesis and energy-intensive separations. To overcome these limitations, we demonstrate a sorption-enhanced methanol production synthesis loop using a fixed-bed Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 reactor coupled with an absorber separation column packed with supported MgCl2 (bentonite, silica, or SBA-15). This process circumvents methanol formation equilibration and thus mitigates thermodynamic constraints by effectively lowering the partial pressures of methanol and water via effective removal in the absorber column. This sorption-enabled removal also mitigates catalyst deactivation by H2O, leading to higher methanol formation rates. Under optimized conditions, the reaction-absorption system achieved an average methanol production rate of ~61 mmol gcat-1 h-1, higher than both recycle-only (with inert-sorbent in the loop) (~23.1 mmol gcat-1 h-1) and single-pass (bypassing absorber) (~12.5 mmol gcat-1 h-1) benchmarks. When the absorber column was packed with bentonite-MgCl2, the synthesis loop showed the highest methanol storage capacity (238 mgMeOH/gsorbent at 75 °C) but displayed a poor stability through multiple cycles; silica-MgCl2 offered sharper breakthroughs with a capacity of 223 mgMeOH/gsorbent, improved stability, and the highest product selectivity during staged regeneration; SBA-15-MgCl2 exhibited superior methanol uptake with no apparent degradation over 170 h. ATR-FTIR analysis of the spent sorbents evidenced CH3 and C-O bands, consistent with methoxide formation at MgCl2/MgO domains and confirming a selective solid-gas reaction, alongside physisorption within the porous support. A two-step temperature-programmed regeneration enabled staged product recovery: silica-MgCl2 achieved 91.3% methanol selectivity in the first step and 97.9% water selectivity in the second. Retrofitting conventional process with the absorptive separation suggests a less energy-intensive downstream separation requirement.

Toward carbon-neutral wastewater treatment: Pharmaceutical mineralization via UV/H2O2/persulfate photolysis coupled with CO2 capture using ultrasonically activated olive pomace biochar
abstract: This study presents an integrated strategy toward carbon-neutral wastewater treatment by coupling Advanced Oxidation Processes with in situ CO 2 capture in a closed-loop system using ultrasonically activated olive pomace biochar. The mineralization of a representative pharmaceutical mixture containing amoxicillin, sulfamethoxazole, and nimesulide was carried out using UV-C/H 2 O 2 and UV-C/H 2 O 2 /S 2 O 8 2− processes under mild conditions (natural pH ≈ 9, ambient temperature, low-power UV irradiation). The persulfate-assisted system significantly enhanced mineralization kinetics, achieving complete Total Organic Carbon (TOC) removal within 75 min under optimal conditions ([H 2 O 2 ] o = 375 mg L −1 , [S 2 O 8 2− ] o = 200 mg L −1 ). The CO 2 generated during mineralization was continuously transferred from the aqueous phase to the gas phase and quantified in real time within a closed recirculation loop, enabling direct coupling between oxidation and carbon capture. The produced CO 2 was subsequently captured in a fixed-bed column packed with biochar, demonstrating the feasibility of simultaneous pollutant removal and carbon mitigation. Radical scavenging experiments confirmed that hydroxyl (HO • ) and sulfate (SO 4 •- ) radicals were the predominant reactive species governing degradation. Ultrasonic activation markedly improved the biochar textural properties, increasing the CO 2 adsorption capacity from 17.68 to 168 mg CO 2 g −1 . Regeneration experiments demonstrated high reversibility over five adsorption–desorption cycles. Comprehensive characterization (BET, SEM, Raman, FTIR, and XPS) revealed that ultrasonic cavitation enhances microporosity, removes mineral phases, and promotes surface carbon enrichment. XPS analysis further demonstrated reversible formation of carbonate-type surface species after CO 2 capture and preservation of active sites after repeated cycles. Overall, the proposed system demonstrates that AOP-driven mineralization and CO 2 capture can be effectively integrated within a single platform, providing a novel pathway toward carbon-aware wastewater treatment and circular valorization of agricultural residues.

Coupling upconversion effect with p-n heterojunction on TiAl6V4 to eradicate bacterial biofilms
abstract: Titanium alloys are used as bone implants due to the excellent biocompatibility, high strength and corrosion resistance. To fabricate an antibacterial surface on Ti or alloy implants can be of fundamental research and clinical interest. Here, TC4 alloy (TiAl6V4) was anodized to construct a spaced nanotube arrays (TC4 NT, ~600 nm in length, 110 nm in diameter and 60 nm in spacing). Then, p-type organic semiconductor copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) was electrophoretically deposited on the TC4 NT, followed by hydrothermal deposition of rare-earth NaYF4 upconversion nanoparticles (RE), producing a ternary REx/CuPc/TC4 NT composites, where x denotes RE loading. The optimized RE1/CuPc/TC4 NT exhibited the highest photocurrent density under 980 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation (0.63 μA/cm²). In vitro assays revealed nearly complete inhibition of both planktonic and adherent bacteria, while in vivo antibacterial efficacy reached 97.3% without obvious inflammation in H&E-stained tissues. The antibacterial coating approach can be adopted to 3D-printed TC4 and remained effective under NIR excitation. Mechanistic analyses (Mott–Schottky and EIS) indicated synergistic coupling of the CuPc–TiO₂ p–n junction with RE-mediated upconversion, enabling NIR-to-UV conversion and subsequent disruption of bacterial respiratory processes. In summary, RE1/CuPc/TC4 NT represents a robust NIR-responsive antibacterial coating applicable to both commercial and home-made TC4 implants, offering a promising strategy for infection-resistant biomedical devices.

Zero-dimensional process simulation model of an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer system
abstract: Clean hydrogen is vital for achieving net-zero emissions and reducing carbon output in society. Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis is gaining momentum in the growing electrolyzer market as a means of producing climate-neutral hydrogen when paired with renewable energy sources. Anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers do not rely on precious metals for electrocatalysts and do not require harsh caustic conditions, making them a safe, scalable, efficient, and potentially affordable method for splitting water. This investigation uses a zero-dimensional numerical model to assess the operation of a market-ready anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and its capacity to generate clean hydrogen and recover waste heat. A commercial electrolyzer rack with four nominal 2.4 kW el electrolyzer modules is used to collect experimental data and examine multiple process parameters during dynamic operation from start to steady-state conditions. These include stack temperature, pressure, hydrogen production rate, cell voltage, and current density. The observed average electrolysis efficiencies at the stack and system levels, based on the lower heating value of hydrogen, reach 68.4% and 61.5%, respectively. The recoverability of the generated waste heat at the stack level is approximately 79.4% at 46 °C, providing approximately 340 W th of heating power and about 111 W th of exergy heating rate per module. The developed model accurately reproduces the dynamic behavior of electrolyzers, showing strong correlations with experimental data, achieving R 2 values of 0.95 or higher across various time-dependent process parameters, and providing new insights into process simulation for system integration, design, and scaling. • Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer: Modeling and Process Simulation • Assessment of experimental data of multiple time-dependent process parameters • Evaluation of electrical efficiencies at the system and stack levels • Quantification of recoverable waste heat generation for system integration • Energy balances, energy flow, and exergy rate analysis of usable waste heat

title: Reprogramming macrophages with engineered young mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicle component mitigates osteoarthritis progression
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic inflammatory disorder wherein synovitis and macrophage activation drive disease progression, yet targeted therapies are lacking. Here, we showed that young mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (Y-EVs) and their enriched miR-130b-5p suppressed inflammatory macrophage responses and alleviated OA progression. To enhance its stability and enable OA microenvironment-responsive delivery, miR-130b-5p was encapsulated in a zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) carrier. Further, the ZIF-8@miR-130b-5p complex displayed rapid, acid-triggered release of miR-130b-5p in vitro, validating its pH-sensitive delivery property. In the murine destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM)-surgery induced OA model, intra-articular administration of ZIF-8@miR-130b-5p attenuated synovitis, inhibited inflammatory macrophages, reduced oxidative stress, and preserved cartilage integrity with lowered OARSI scores and enhanced collagen II and aggrecan expression. These therapeutic effects were accompanied by improved subchondral bone architecture and locomotor recovery. Together, our work presents a pH-responsive miRNA delivery platform that disrupts inflammation-driven cartilage catabolism, offering a promising disease-modifying strategy for OA.

Insight into the anti‑sulfur poisoning and NH3-SCR reaction mechanism of CeNbSmTiOx catalyst
abstract: Due to the susceptibility of the active components in CeNbTiOx catalyst to sulfuration, this study innovatively introduces Sm for protection. By adjusting the Sm/Ce ratio, the resistance of CeNbSmTiOx catalyst to H2O and SO2 is enhanced. Comprehensive research results showed that the optimal CeNbSmTiOx-0.3 catalyst exhibits over 90% nitrogen oxide conversion and excellent N2 selectivity in a wide temperature range (200-400 °C). It can maintain 81% activity after 8 hours of SO2 poisoning at 250 °C, and still retain 75% activity after 8 hours of combined H2O and SO2 poisoning. The introduction of Sm species enhances the surface acidity, oxygen storage and release capacity, and NH3 adsorption and activation ability of the catalyst, thereby improving its low-temperature denitrification performance. After SO2 poisoning, Sm doping can moderately enhance NH3 adsorption and activation but does not alter the reaction mechanism of CeNbTiOx catalyst, which still proceeds via the L-H mechanism. In addition, Sm doping forms a Ce4+ + Sm2+ ⇋ Ce3+ + Sm3+ redox cycle, effectively inhibiting the transfer of electrons from adsorbed SO2 to Ce4+, protecting the active components from sulfatation and thus exhibiting excellent SO2 resistance.

title: Morphogeneration: Continuous chaotic flow of flower-shape microstructures
abstract: Radial symmetry is a recurring outcome of morphogenesis in nature, shaping the architecture of flowers, jellyfish, echinoderms, and other organisms where form and function are tightly intertwined. Replicating such complex, symmetric microstructures in engineered materials, however, has remained a persistent challenge. Here we introduce morphogeneration , a fabrication approach that harnesses chaotic fluid dynamics to create finely resolved, radially symmetric architectures with high reproducibility at micro- and nano-level. At the core of this method is a custom-designed static device, the morphogenerator , which transforms fluid motion into controlled, flower-like morphologies by deterministic stretching and folding of interfaces. Through computational fluid dynamics simulations and experiments with sodium alginate hydrogels, we show that microstructural features can be predictably tuned by adjusting device geometry, flow rate, and inlet configuration. Unlike conventional mixers that homogenize fluids, the morphogenerator preserves sharp interfaces while enabling scalable, high-precision patterning across soft matter systems. This strategy provides a versatile platform for translating the generative principles of morphogenesis into engineered contexts, with broad applications in microfluidics, materials engineering, and biomimetic environments. • This paper introduces morphogeneration, a scalable method for producing symmetric, flower-like microstructures. • “The morphogeneration concept, inspired by static mixer architectures, is introduced as a strategy to generate microstructures through engineered fluid stretching.” • “Symmetric radial patterns resembling flower-like morphologies, ranging from two to seven petals, are experimentally demonstrated with feature resolution down to 10 μm using sol–gel systems.” • “The morphogeneration approach generates complex microstructures via flow-driven structuring without extending processing time relative to lower-resolution processes (e.g. 3D printing).” • “Computational fluid dynamics simulations successfully predict the experimentally observed morphologies, providing a reliable tool for structural design.”

Reconstructing oxide layers on photovoltaic waste silicon to enable high initial Coulombic efficiency silicon anodes
abstract: Photovoltaic waste silicon (WSi) has explored as a promising high-capacity anode material for lithium-ion batteries used in energy storage systems. However, its practical application is hindered by significant volume expansion, low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), and the high cost of nano‑silicon sources. In this study, we present an innovative and facile strategy to upcycle the native oxide layer of WSi into high-performance anodes for lithium-ion batteries with excellent initial ICE. The in situ formed LiSiO significantly enhances ionic diffusion kinetics during the initial cycle, while the conformal carbon coating effectively alleviates the volume expansion of the embedded Si. Owing to this synergistic structural design, the WSi/LiSiO@C composite demonstrates outstanding electrochemical performance, achieving a notably high ICE of 90.1% and maintaining excellent cycling stability. Importantly, a full pouch cell fabricated using the WSi/LiSiO@C anode in combination with a commercial NCM811 cathode delivers an energy density of 313.4 Wh kg and retains 81% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1C. This work not only presents a promising approach for the high-value recycling of photovoltaic waste and high-performance anodes but also contributes to the integration of photovoltaic power generation and advanced energy storage technologies.

Effects of droplet length and inner circulation on mass transfer in liquid-liquid slug flow microreactors: experimental study and penetration theory-based modelling
abstract: The mass transfer characteristics and internal circulation patterns during liquid-liquid slug flow through capillary microreactors were investigated experimentally, using both physical and reactive extraction of acetic acid into aqueous phases as a model system. Four inlet mixing junctions of varying sizes were employed to generate droplets of different lengths under the same phasic flow rate and constant aqueous to organic volumetric flow ratio at 1:1. The results of physical extraction show that the overall mass transfer coefficient decreased with increasing the residence time, in qualitative agreement with the penetration theory. Furthermore, the overall mass transfer coefficient increased for shorter droplets or higher mixture velocities at a constant residence time. These observed dependencies can be attributed to two principal factors: (i) different internal circulation patterns being stronger and more uniform in slugs, but weaker and more length-dependent in droplets, as quantitatively characterized through color visualization in reactive extraction experiments; and (ii) more limited mass transfer from the liquid film region for longer droplets, caused by less sufficient supply of solute from the surrounding slugs. Consequently, a mass transfer model based on the penetration theory was proposed to well describe the physical extraction data. In the model, stagnant slugs and droplets that incorporate distinct transfer mechanisms for the droplet cap and film regions are assumed, with the Reynolds number further used to characterize the mass transfer enhancement by internal circulation.

title: Ultrafast sensitive broadband imaging photodetection based on vertically stacked structured GaN/Bi2O2Te/Bi2Te3 p-n heterojunctions
abstract: Bismuth oxychalcogenides (Bi2O2X; X = S, Se, Te) hold promise as novel candidates for room temperature ultrasensitive optoelectronic devices. However, the relaxation of devices caused by the thermoelectric effect severely limits their application in ultrafast photodetectors. In this study, a vertical p-GaN/Bi2O2Te/Bi2Te3 heterojunction is fabricated using a simplified chemical vapor deposition technique, successfully achieving modulation of the response performance of the heterojunction device with the assistance of a weak electric field. The device demonstrates a responsivity of 671.9 mA/W and 9.099 × 1010 Jones detectivity under irradiation at 254 nm with a bias voltage of -0.1 V. Particularly noteworthy is the ultrafast response exhibited by the device in both the UV and NIR bands, with τrise and τdecay of 74.2 μs and 162.0 μs under 405 nm irradiation, and 126 μs and 130 μs under 980 nm irradiation, respectively. Furthermore, the p-GaN/Bi2O2Te/Bi2Te3 device exhibits excellent stability and outstanding imaging capability under broadband irradiation. This significant research lays the groundwork for future applications and the development of novel broadband multifunctional photodetectors.

Stacked quantum dot organic light-emitting diodes in an industrial-grade inkjet printing process
abstract: Quantum dot organic light-emitting diode (QD-OLED) displays offer advantages such as wide color gamut, excellent viewing angles, and high contrast ratios. In addition, QD-OLED technology holds significant potential as a core technology for various next-generation displays, including micro-LEDs, OLED on silicon, and reflective displays. This paper reports the development of a novel stacked QD-OLED panel that outperforms QD-OLED panels currently under development in the display industry. Compared with existing QD-OLED displays, the stacked QD-OLED developed in this study can simplify the panel manufacturing process and reduce manufacturing costs by applying a continuous vertical stacking process on a single substrate. Furthermore, the stacked QD-OLED offers structural advantages at the device and panel levels that can suppress optical interference in high-resolution displays. In particular, the fabrication of QD pixels for the stacked QD-OLED is demonstrated using QD ink, a black pixel-defining layer (PDL) photoresist, and inkjet printing components and equipment suited for industrial-scale display manufacturing. A black PDL material with a high aspect ratio and a process technology that operates below 100 °C, essential for realizing stacked QD-OLED panels, are introduced. Finally, by integrating industrially applicable materials, processes, and equipment technologies, a novel stacked QD-OLED panel with a total of 184,800 subpixels and a resolution of 141 pixels per inch, equivalent to that of a 65-inch 8K television, was successfully demonstrated through a 6-inch large-area manufacturing process.

title: Horizontal dilute-phase pneumatic conveying enhanced by oscillatory wake from a wall-mounted streamlined bluff body
abstract: Achieving stable particle transport at reduced air velocities remains a persistent bottleneck in horizontal dilute-phase pneumatic conveying, primarily because particles tend to settle and accumulate on the pipe floor when the carrier gas velocity is insufficiently high. This work introduces a novel passive flow-control device—a short cylinder featuring an aerodynamically profiled (streamlined) leading edge and a flat rectangular trailing face—mounted on either the floor or the ceiling of the conveying pipe upstream of the solids feed point. The profiled leading edge is tailored to limit the blockage-induced drag penalty, while the blunt trailing face sheds periodic vortices whose strong velocity fluctuations enhance both the lift and the streamwise drag acting on nearby particles. The test facility consists of a horizontal acrylic pipe of 80 mm bore and 5 m length. Spherical polyethylene beads (mean diameter 2.3 mm, bulk density 978 kg/m³) served as the conveyed material. Superficial air velocities spanned 9–16 m/s and the solids mass flow rates were varied between 0.11 and 0.51 kg/s. Relative to the baseline (device-free) operation, the optimally sized and positioned streamlined device delivers concurrent reductions in total pressure drop, critical conveying velocity, minimum-pressure-drop velocity, power consumption, and additional pressure loss. Peak reductions of roughly 6 % in the minimum conveying velocity and 37.5 % in the additional pressure loss were recorded. High-speed particle image velocimetry (PIV) further confirms that the device raises both the mean streamwise particle velocity and the turbulent fluctuation intensity in the acceleration zone, thereby sustaining reliable particle transport at velocities that would otherwise cause deposition.

Quadrupole-regulated morphology evolution by non-fused dimeric acceptors enables efficient ternary organic solar cells
abstract: Rational design of third components in ternary blends remains challenging because their spatial distribution and morphology-regulation roles are often determined empirically. Herein, two zero-dipole non-fused dimeric acceptors, DTV-4F and DTV-4Cl, were designed to investigate how subtle differences in molecular quadrupole moment affect blend evolution and device performance in the D18:L8-BO system. Although the two dimers share nearly identical backbones, DTV-4F exhibits a larger out-of-plane quadrupole moment (Qzz) than DTV-4Cl. When incorporated as a third component, DTV-4F induces more favorable vertical component redistribution, moderates and synchronizes host acceptor crystallization, enhances molecular ordering, and promotes a more continuous charge-transport network. These morphology advantages lead to more balanced carrier mobility, faster charge extraction, and suppressed bimolecular and trap-assisted recombination. As a result, the D18:L8-BO:DTV-4F ternary device delivers a power conversion efficiency of 19.75% with a high fill factor of 82.22%, outperforming both the binary host device and the DTV-4Cl-based ternary counterpart. This work identifies molecular quadrupole moment as an effective descriptor for third-component design and provides a practical strategy for constructing efficient ternary OSCs using structurally simple non-fused dimeric acceptors.

abstract: Abstract Ultrahigh-purity octafluoropropane (C 3 F 8 ) electronic specialty gas is of critical importance for advanced semiconductor and integrated circuit manufacturing. The removal of trace amounts of octafluorocyclobutane ( c -C 4 F 8 ) impurities from C 3 F 8 products remains a challenging endeavor due to their similar physiochemical properties. Herein, an organofluorination engineering strategy is reported to regulate the local microenvironment of zeolite Y for efficient c -C 4 F 8 /C 3 F 8 adsorptive separation. The organofluorinated zeolite Y adsorbents exhibit enhanced c -C 4 F 8 /C 3 F 8 separation efficiency compared to pristine zeolite, with remarkably greater uptakes of c -C 4 F 8 and lower uptakes of C 3 F 8 . Notably, sample ZnY-FU achieves an ultrahigh c -C 4 F 8 /C 3 F 8 selectivity of 1.7´10 10 at 1 bar and 25 °C. Multiple characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the local microenvironment of zeolite Y can be regulated with the fluorinated ligands located at FAU supercages close to the pore entrance. The introduction of fluorinated ligands mainly affects the thermodynamic adsorption behaviors of c -C 4 F 8 and C 3 F 8 on the adsorbents, resulting in highly efficient c -C 4 F 8 /C 3 F 8 separation. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further verify the c -C 4 F 8 /C 3 F 8 separation potentials with ultrahigh-purity C 3 F 8 (99.999%) obtained from c -C 4 F 8 /C 3 F 8 (5: 95, v/v) mixtures.

Low-temperature semi-solid-state H2 battery with high energy density
abstract: Rechargeable hydrogen batteries based on reversible proton-intercalation at the cathode and catalytic H₂ redox reactions at the anode are promising for large-scale energy storage, yet most proton-intercalation cathodes deliver capacities below 60 mAh g-1. Here, we report a semi-solid-state hydrogen gas battery that couples a pre-protonated vanadium hexacyanoferrate cathode with a platinum-based catalytic anode and a bentonite-phosphoric acid solid electrolyte. The cathode achieves a high specific capacity of 132.6 mAh g-1 and excellent rate capability, delivering 73.1 mAh g-1 at 50 A g-1. The full cell attains an energy density of 128.6 Wh kg-1 with 63% capacity retention after 10,000 cycles at 20 A g-1. It also exhibits outstanding low-temperature stability, maintaining 77.4 mAh g-1 and stable cycling at -40 °C, and operates reliably down to -80 °C. The superior performance originates from fast proton transport through a pre-protonation-induced extended hydrogen-bond network and a robust solid electrolyte ensuring interfacial stability.

title: Modulating Pd/C catalysts with nitrogen and silver for formic acid dehydrogenation: Insights from XAS and DFT
abstract: Hydrogen production from formic acid is a promising route for clean energy, but it requires catalysts that are both active, selective, and stable. Here, we explore how nitrogen doping of the carbon support and interaction with silver tune the performance of Pd catalysts. Using XPS and EXAFS, we show that nitrogen groups promote the formation of Pd 2+ species, decrease the Pd coordination number, and stabilize small nanoparticles that remain highly dispersed after reaction. The basic character of the doped carbon support also enhances interactions with key intermediates, contributing to the exceptional stability of these catalysts. In contrast, introducing Ag into Pd nanoparticles changes the electronic environment of Pd, as indicated by charge transfer in XPS and Pd Ag interactions detected by EXAFS, leading to a notable increase in catalytic activity. DFT calculations identify H 2 desorption as the rate-limiting step and reveal that both electron density withdrawn by nitrogen atoms and the electron transfer of Ag ultimately weaken the Pd H bond. Despite their opposite electronic effects, both modifications facilitate H 2 release and boost the overall reaction rate. Taken together, our results show that nitrogen primarily enhances stability, while silver mainly increases activity, and that combining both provides a rational strategy for designing next-generation Pd catalysts for efficient hydrogen generation from formic acid.

Molten GaBi catalyst for low-carbon, cost-effective hydrogen via moderate- temperature methane pyrolysis
abstract: Methane pyrolysis is a promising method for CO 2 -free H 2 production. While conventional solid catalysts suffer from deactivation due to carbon product deposition, molten metal catalysts offer continuous operation for long-term stability by allowing carbon to float on the liquid surface. However, they typically require extreme temperatures above 900 °C to achieve a sufficient H 2 product yield, necessitating the development of catalysts with high activity at lower temperatures. Herein, we present a molten GaBi catalyst that is effective for methane pyrolysis at moderate temperatures of 500–800 °C. The Ga 0.11 Bi 0.89 alloy exhibited the lowest activation energy (67.2 kJ/mol) among reported molten catalysts and maintained stable hydrogen production for 158 h at 800 °C. Ab initio molecular dynamics calculations verified that the exceptional performance originates from the simultaneous suppression of Ga Ga aggregation (coordination number of 0.77) and enhancement of Ga mobility (diffusivity of 0.845 ± 0.012 cm 2 s −1 ). The 552 ton H 2 /day pyrolysis plant with the presented catalyst demonstrated superior economic and environmental feasibility compared to water electrolysis, achieving a net-negative environmental impact, a 80.7% reduction in total installed cost, and an 79.1% decrease in operating cost. The results provide critical insights that advance the design of efficient molten catalysts for methane pyrolysis.

Techno-economic evaluation of molten‑carbonate-mediated ethane ODH as a low-carbon pathway for ethylene production
abstract: Molten-carbonate-mediated oxidative dehydrogenation (MM-ODH) of ethane has recently been proposed as a chemical-looping alternative to steam cracking that integrates ethane conversion, in situ CO 2 capture and conversion, and reverse water–gas shift chemistry within a molten carbonate phase. While prior studies have demonstrated favorable ethylene yields and CO co-production, the system-level energy, emissions, and cost implications of MM-ODH have not been quantified. Here, we present a comprehensive techno-economic and environmental evaluation of MM-ODH using rigorous Aspen Plus® process modeling and NETL QGESS-aligned costing, benchmarked against a modern ethane steam cracking plant equipped with monoethanolamine-based post-combustion CO 2 capture under identical system boundaries. MM-ODH achieves a 34% reduction in net specific energy consumption relative to the reference case by eliminating dilution steam and solvent regeneration while co-producing CO. Although MM-ODH exhibits moderately higher direct electricity-related emissions, displacement credits from CO reduce product-system emission intensities to 0–0.32 t CO 2 -eq/t ethylene. Despite conservative first-of-a-kind contingencies applied to the reactor, MM-ODH delivers levelized ethylene costs competitive with the benchmark, identifying molten-carbonate looping as a viable pathway for low-carbon ethylene production. • MM-ODH couples ethane cracking with in-situ CO 2 capture and CO co-production. • Net energy use is 34% lower than steam cracking with MEA capture. • MM-ODH product-system net emissions fall to 0–0.32 t CO 2 -eq/t ethylene. • Levelized ethylene costs from MM-ODH are competitive despite FOAK contingencies.

A 1D stepped coordination polymer based on Cu4I4 units for X-ray imaging over a broad temperature range
abstract: Organic Cu(I) metal halides have emerged as promising scintillator materials due to their efficient X-ray absorption, tunable radioluminescence properties and excellent low‐temperature solution processability. However, their X‐ray luminescence efficiency is predominantly governed by the competition between the radiative emission from organic ligands and the non‐radiative charge transfer centered on the copper‐halogen units. Here, a one-dimensional stepped coordination polymer scintillator based on Cu4I4 repeating units was successfully synthesized. This material exhibits intense radioluminescence under X‐ray excitation. Photophysical characterization and theoretical calculations confirm that the emission mechanism originates primarily from a copper/iodine‐to‐ligand charge‐transfer process. Notably, this scintillator can automatically switch between TADF and phosphorescence emission modes under X-ray irradiation based on temperature changes, thereby exhibiting highly efficient radioluminescence performance across different temperatures. The minimum detection limits at 298 K and 77 K are 109.99 nGy∙s-1 and 49.30 nGy∙s-1 respectively, and scintillation screens fabricated from such material achieve a spatial resolution of 21.39 lp∙mm-1. This study provides new insights into organic Cu(I) metal halide scintillators that maintain high exciton utilization efficiency and excellent radioluminescence performance over a broad temperature range.

title: Exploring the effect of dissolved oxygen concentration on the heterogeneous oxidation of veratryl alcohol over a Pd/C catalyst
abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis has widespread application in organic synthetic chemistry and the ability to utilise energy gases (O2, H2, CO2) replaces the need for hazardous oxidative/reductive reagents. However, use of such gases in synthesis is mainly limited due to low gas solubility in most commonly used solvents, safety aspects and the requirement of large stoichiometric excesses. Scale-up is also challenging due to complex hydrodynamics and low mass transfer rates, thus enhancing mass transport of the gaseous reagents to the catalytic surface is crucial for reactions to occur. In this work, a dissolved gas technology has been developed, allowing successful separation of the gas to liquid mass transfer step from the liquid to solid reaction steps in multiphase catalytic processes. Implementation of a dissolved gas stream into a heterogeneous packed bed reactor system mimics a typical flow chemistry process and enables controlled O2 concentrations for oxidation of a benzylic alcohol, veratryl alcohol. The concept of this work is to investigate whether predissolution of gas combined with a two-phase heterogeneous packed bed reactor can overcome the typical limitations of three phase gas-liquid-solid reactions. Namely (i) the requirement of a high excess of the gaseous reagent, (ii) lack of gas concentration control and (iii) use of excess catalyst, as this is the main component that provides the mass transfer area. This study has demonstrated successful oxygen dissolution pre-reaction, has explored the oxidation kinetics with respect to O2 concentration, and demonstrated how different dissolved oxygen concentrations affect the selectivity of the oxidation product.

abstract: Silicon (Si) anodes offer a theoretical capacity nearly ten times higher than graphite, yet their practical use in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is impeded by severe volume expansion, particle pulverization, and low conductivity, resulting in rapid capacity decay. Considerable efforts have therefore focused on structural and compositional engineering to mitigate these drawbacks. In particular, alloying with transition metals (e.g., Fe Si systems) has demonstrated notable improvements in buffering volume changes and enhancing electronic conductivity, but the benefits of binary alloys are still limited. Here, we introduce a compositionally complex Si alloy (CCSA) approach to simultaneously achieve high capacity and durability. Medium-entropy CCSAs were synthesized via high-energy ball milling, incorporating multiple elements into Fe Si matrices. Structural analysis revealed lattice distortion and homogeneous elemental distribution, consistent with configurational entropy stabilization. Among them, Mg-containing CCSAs exhibited the best cycling stability and capacity retention. CCSAs are integrated with conductive carbon matrices, including reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs), to enhance conductivity and structural stability. The resulting CCSA anode exhibits stable cycling performance with high reversible capacity. Building upon these results, practical Si/graphite blended composite anodes are fabricated, incorporating up to 30 wt% Si. These composite anodes deliver high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and superior capacity retention, thereby establishing Si-alloy-based materials as a scalable platform for next-generation high-energy-density LIB anodes.

A sequential mucus-penetrating and pH/ROS-responsive organosilica nanoplatform for co-delivery of natural antibiotics to combat drug resistant lung infection
abstract: The treatment of bacterial pneumonia remains severely constrained by the complex pulmonary physiopathological barriers, including the mucus layer and biofilm matrix, which restrict the effective delivery of antibiotics. Moreover, the acidic and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-rich microenvironment at the infection site further impairs the controlled release of therapeutic agents. To overcome this multifaceted challenge, we developed a dual-responsive nanoplatform (PTCSeM) based on diselenide-bridged mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles (SeM) with a design rationale that directly counters each barrier: surface functionalization with chitosan and ROS-labile mPEG-TK enables sequential mucus penetration, pH-responsive drug release, and ROS-accelerated degradation. This nanoplatform co-loaded two natural antibiotics, honokiol (HK) and carvacrol (CAL), enabling targeted drug delivery within the acidic infection site. Notably, ROS-mediated degradation of the nanocarrier facilitated the synergistic integration of antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant effects. In vivo evaluations demonstrated that PTCSeM@HK-CAL markedly reduced bacterial loads in the lungs of animal models infected with multidrug-resistant pathogens. It also exerted robust therapeutic effects by modulating inflammatory cytokine expression and alleviating oxidative stress. Collectively, this dual-stimuli-responsive organosilica-based nanoplatform for the co-delivery of dual antibiotics presents a promising integrated strategy for treating drug-resistant bacterial pneumonia, offering enhanced mucus penetration, stimulus-responsive release, deep biofilm clearance, and potent antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activities.

Unraveling etching mechanism for SiN film in cryogenic hydrogen-fluoride plasmas
abstract: Cryogenic plasma etching is a pivotal technology for next-generation 3D semiconductor devices with high-aspect-ratio and nanoscale features. During reactive ion etching of SiN in hydrogen fluoride (HF)-containing plasmas, an ammonium fluorosilicate (AFS) layer is formed; however, the precise role of the AFS in etching kinetic has remained highly controversial since its discovery in the 1980s. This lack of consensus has left the SiN plasma etching mechanism largely obscure, even within the context of modern cryogenic processes. Here, we elucidated this mechanism using in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry and attenuated-total-reflection FTIR while manipulating substrate temperature (Ts), bias voltage, and HF partial pressure via Ar dilution. We reveal that the etch rate (ER) and the AFS thickness are established through a dynamic balance between HF-induced AFS formation and simultaneous removal by ion bombardment. This interplay results in a characteristic bell-shaped ER dependence on Ts and Ar content. Crucially, whether AFS promotes or retards etching depends on the rate-determining step: in removal-limited regimes, ER is inversely proportional to the AFS thickness, whereas in formation-limited regimes, they are positively correlated. The proposed model suggests that ER at low Ts can be significantly enhanced through high bias voltages or synergistic chemistries that catalyze AFS depletion.

Absorption-based heat storage for electrification of dynamic power-to-chemicals processes
abstract: Heat integration is a well-established approach to increase the energy efficiency in chemical processes. However, conventional steady-state approaches fail in dynamically operated Power-to-chemicals processes where production rate needs to follow the renewable energy generation profiles. Herein, we present a novel strategy to store and release heat by exploiting the high reaction enthalpy of absorption of ammonia (or water) in cheaply available metal halides, where the heat storage temperature can be tuned between 300-500°C. Modelling of the system provides guidance for the tailored design of the heat storage system by balancing heat loses, heat transfer and heat storage rates, with a maximum theoretical efficiency of 81%. In addition, this heat integration strategy can store heat closer to the temperature at which will be subsequently utilized, maximizing the heat quality. The novel heat storage approach is demonstrated for the dynamic operation of a (exothermic) Haber-Bosch reactor for green ammonia synthesis. In comparison to simply storing sensible heat (e.g. ceramic material), the absorption-based heat storage system can store up to 12X more heat and maximizes the quality of the heat by minimizing the temperature swing. Additionally, it keeps the HB reactor hot for up to 10X longer than the reactor alone during idle operation, facilitating the fast re-starts with no energy requirements while increasing the production due to in-situ cooling. The dynamic reactor operation enabled by this new absorption-based heat storage approach highlights the importance of re-designing of Power-to-X processes with novel technologies to enhance their economic feasibility.

abstract: Photo-Fenton process is ruled by complexation of Fe(III); in particular, some inorganic ions inactivate Fe(III) by forming inactive complexes, while some organic ligands, such as catechol (CAT) are able to enhance the performance of the process. The cross effect of both, inorganic anions (F − , Cl − , Br − and BO 3 3− , present in seawater, and PO 4 3− commonly found in agricultural effluents) and CAT has been investigated. For this purpose, a mixture of six pollutants has been used as target. Among anions present in seawater, F − and Br − showed the strongest inhibitory effect at a concentration of 17 mM, which could only be partly removed by the presence of CAT. The nature of the inhibitory effect is different; while F − inactivates Fe(III) by forming complexes that prevent Fe(II) regeneration, Br − acts as scavenger for ·OH. When working at more realistic concentration, inhibition was significantly eliminated, but for Br − , in line with CAT being efficient at avoiding Fe(III) inactivation but not to prevent ·OH scavenging. Experiments with real seawater have demonstrated the efficiency of CAT, despite CAT/Fe ratios above 3 are required. For phosphates, experimental design methodology was used the determine the effect of pH, CAT/Fe and phosphate/Fe. CAT/Fe > 3 where required and the interference was stronger at higher phosphate/Fe ratio. Finally, it has ben shown that efficiency of Fe-CAT system is ruled by the volumetric rate of photon absorption (VRPA) but also by the ability of Fe(CAT) complex, to give an internal electron transfer between CAT and Fe.

A multimodal lateral flow immunoassay driven by a “all-in-one” Au@Pt@ZIF-8 nanocomposite for trace monitoring of 3-phenoxybenzoic acid
abstract: Conventional lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) suffers from limited sensitivity due to single-signal readout, low antibody conjugation efficiency, and steric hindrance associated with bulky conventional antibodies. Here, we develop a multimodal LFIA employing Au@Pt@ZIF-8 (APZ) as a multifunctional nanolabel, prepared by encapsulating peroxidase-like Au@Pt nanoparticles (Au@Pt NPs) within a ZIF-8 framework. The high specific surface area and mesoporous structure of APZ significantly enhance coupling efficiency and probe stability for anti-3-phenoxybenzoic acid nanobodies (3-PBA Nbs), achieving a coupling efficiency as high as 94.75% under identical conditions, compared with 69.61% for Au@Pt NPs. APZ further exhibits a broad absorption spectrum, dual-spectral-overlap fluorescence quenching, and high catalytic activity arising from the intrinsic peroxidase-mimicking activity of Au@Pt, synergistically enhanced by ZIF-8 enrichment/confinement and pH-triggered framework collapse. These properties collectively enable a three orthogonal readout capability on a single test strip, manifested as aggregation-induced coloration, catalysis-induced chromogenesis, and fluorescence quenching. The resulting multimodal APZ-LFIA attains limits of detection (LOD) for 3-PBA of 0.004 ng/mL, 0.001 ng/mL, and 0.0003 ng/mL, respectively. By integrating diverse, complementary, and synergistic signals, this platform not only enhances the flexibility, practicality, and accuracy of trace 3-PBA determination but also demonstrates strong potential for on-site food safety monitoring.

abstract: Ni-rich single-crystal cathodes are regarded as highly promising for the next generation high energy density lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) owing to the grain-boundary-free morphology and high thermal stability. However, they inevitably suffer from surface lattice oxygen release during cycling, which accelerates interfacial reconstruction and severe parasitic reactions, ultimately degrading electrochemical performance. Herein, we propose a surface-gradient Co/B co-doping strategy to enable electronic modulation and interfacial structural regulation in Ni-rich single-crystal cathode. Advanced characterizations combined with first-principles calculations reveal that surface-gradient Co/B co-doping induces interfacial charge redistribution and significantly strengthens local TM–O bonding, thereby effectively suppressing lattice oxygen activation, blocking detrimental phase transitions, and enabling superior electrochemical performance. Benefiting from this interfacial regulation strategy, SNCM-CB delivers a high specific capacity of 158.5 mAh g-1 at 10 C, and retains 80.2% and 93.2% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C at 25 ℃ and -20 ℃, respectively. This work offers a viable pathway toward the development of high energy density, long-life, and safe LIBs.

abstract: Unlike condensation polymers like polyesters and polyurethanes, polyolefins are significantly more challenging to break down to their respective building blocks. Endothermic pyrolysis technology can convert such polyolefins in a complex oil that can be catalytically converted to olefins and aromatics. An alternative to this energy-demanding approach is to use exothermic aerobic oxidation. A challenge here is the required use of solvents such as acetic acid to dissolve the polymer. In that regard it is worthwhile to investigate solvent-free oxyfunctionalization of polyethylene (PE) to alter its surface properties, making it more compatible with polar environments. Direct oxidative PE upgrading is promising, but most reported systems are mass-transfer-limited or rely on thin films to enable backbone oxidation. Here we report on the use of expanded-bed reactor architecture to overcome mass-transfer constraints, enabling up to 20× higher oxyfunctionalization of HDPE, relative to reactive extrusion or conventional batch processing. Comprehensive fractionation and analysis of solids, liquids, and gases (using NMR, GC, GPC) reveals a distribution of oxygenated functionalities (ketones, alcohols, esters, carboxylic acids). The precise reactor operating conditions allow control over both average molecular mass and oxidation extent. Together, these results establish expanded beds as a potentially scalable platform for tunable PE oxyfunctionalization, unlocking a path to partial oxidation as a polymer feedstock conditioning step.

A pathway to high photovoltaic performance in Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells through device configuration and process advancement
abstract: This study systematically provides a comprehensive overview for the configuration of the interface between an absorber and a dry-processed buffer forming a p–n junction in Cu( In , Ga )Se 2 (CIGS) solar cells. Most existing high-efficiency CIGS solar cells employ a CdS buffer layer formed by chemical bath deposition (CBD). However, the deep and continuous diffusion of Cd into the CIGS layer, along with the toxicity of Cd, complicates the control of the diffusion level and may affect long-term device stability. Furthermore, the CBD process poses significant challenges for continuous processing and large-area manufacturing. To address these problems, a Cd-free and nontoxic (Zn,Mg)O (ZMO) buffer layer with improved controllability of the diffusion level was used in this study. ZMO buffer layers were deposited onto RbF-post-deposition-treated CIGS using atomic layer deposition (ALD), a dry process. CIGS solar cells incorporated with ALD-ZMO buffers demonstrated superior performance, exhibiting higher efficiency without fill factor loss compared to conventional CIGS devices using CBD-CdS buffers. Atom probe tomography, supported by density functional theory calculations, confirmed that the diffusion level of the elements within CIGS can be effectively controlled by ALD-ZMO. In addition, the feasibility of using this framework as a bottom cell in tandem solar cell configurations was confirmed.

π-Bridge strategy in conjugated organic polymers activates charge- and energy-involved dual pathways for photocatalytic H₂O₂ production
abstract: Conjugated organic polymers (COPs) are promising organic semiconductors for photocatalysis; however, their performance is typically limited by high exciton binding energy (E b ) and poor charge carrier separation. Herein, we report that the π-bridge in porphyrin-based COPs is an effective strategy to tune the E b , charge separation and surface reactions in photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) production via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR). Initially three COPs with progressively extended π-conjugation were synthesized using distinct linkages between porphyrin units: (i) TBPP-COP featuring an aryl–aryl C(sp 2 )–C(sp 2 ) σ bond, (ii) TEPP-TBPP-COP incorporating an acetylene (–C ≡ C–) bridge, and (iii) TEPP-COP containing a diacetylene (–C ≡ C–C ≡ C–) bridge. Compared with the σ-linked TBPP-COP, the two π-bridged COPs exhibit reduced E b , enhanced charge separation efficiency, and a more negative conduction band position, collectively enabling superior H₂O₂ production. In a visible-light-driven biphasic benzyl alcohol–water system, TEPP-COP achieves an H₂O₂ formation rate of 3845 ± 247 μmol g cat −1 h −1 and an apparent quantum yield of 23.8% at 420 nm, together with good recyclability. Radical-quenching experiments and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, supported by density functional theory calculations, reveal that the enhanced 2e − ORR performance of TEPP-COP originates from a dual-intermediate pathway involving •O₂ − and 1 O₂, and strengthened O₂ adsorption at β-C sites within the diacetylene-linked framework. Overall, this work establishes π-bridge engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing COP-based photocatalysts toward efficient solar-driven H₂O₂ production.

abstract: Polylactic acid (PLA) waste is an increasing environmental challenge that demands valorization routes aligned with circular bioeconomy principles. This study demonstrates an integrated chemical-biological strategy to upcycle PLA into polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) through two pathways: (i) alkaline depolymerization to lactate-rich hydrolysates, acidogenic fermentation to volatile fatty acids (VFAs), and PHA accumulation, and (ii) direct PHA production from lactate-rich chemical hydrolysates. PLA was depolymerized using NaOH pretreatment (0.5–4 M) at 37 and 55 °C, achieving >90% carbon solubilization with kinetics governed by alkali strength and particle size. Mixed-culture fermentation converted lactate mainly into propionate and acetate, with hydrolysates produced at 2 M NaOH giving the highest VFA titers and activity. Cupriavidus necator assays revealed stronger interaction between substrate type and nutrient regime for PHA accumulation. VFA-rich streams under nutrient-sufficient condition supported the highest biomass and PHA production at 2 M, whereas, lactate-rich hydrolysates under nutrient-deficient (nitrogen-limited) condition yielded maximum PHB content of 84.3% ( w /w) at 0.5 M. Comparatively, the direct lactate-based route showed greater practical potential as it enabled higher polymer accumulation while avoiding the intermediate fermentation step required in the VFA-mediated pathway. Overall, the integration of alkaline depolymerization with microbial conversion highlights potential for developing simplified and scalable bioconversion strategies for plastic waste valorization, while supporting sustainable materials recovery within a circular bioeconomy framework.

abstract: The sustainable management of waste activated sludge (WAS) is increasingly urgent due to its vast global generation and associated environmental and health risks. This study proposes an innovative valorisation strategy for protease production by Bacillus licheniformis , using WAS as a renewable substrate. Various pretreatment methods were assessed to enhance WAS solubilisation, with thermal hydrolysis (TH) and wet oxidation (WO) identified as the most effective. Maximum enzyme activities of 654 ± 8 U/mL and 658 ± 10 U/mL were attained from WAS pretreated at 125 °C using TH and WO, respectively. Although higher pretreatment temperatures enhanced biopolymer solubilisation, protease yields increased only moderately (~12% for TH and ~ 6% for WO at 150 °C). Notably, alkaline conditions during hydrothermal pretreatment significantly elevated protease production by 46% (TH) and 49% (WO) relative to unadjusted pH conditions. Bioreactor-scale experiments revealed that agitation and aeration strongly influenced enzyme production, achieving a peak activity of 1220 ± 17 U/mL at optimal conditions (1 L/min aeration combined with 300 rpm agitation). The logistic and modified Gompertz models effectively described this bioprocess, recording a maximum specific growth rate (μ max ) of 0.479 ± 0.008 h −1 and a maximum protease production rate (R p ) of 82.2 ± 1.5 U/mL∙h. Downstream processing via two-step ultrafiltration (100 kDa followed by 3 kDa) enabled effective protease purification and concentration, reaching an enzymatic activity of 8113 ± 88 U/mL (~7-fold increase). The purified proteases were successfully used as detergent bio-additives, achieving substantial blood stain removal compared to commercial detergent alone. This study establishes a promising framework for the sustainable valorisation of WAS and underscores its potential for generating valuable bioproducts within the circular economy.

Silk fibroin lipopeptides: Mechanochemical synthesis and physicochemical characterization
abstract: This work presents a complete approach, from biomass extraction to the production of surfactant molecules using a new methodology, followed by their characterization. Fibroin was isolated from silk cocoons and enzymatically hydrolyzed to generate low-molecular-weight peptides. Then, silk fibroin-derived amphiphilic lipopeptides with variable hydrophobic chain lengths were produced by a novel mechanochemical eco-friendly approach, without the use of chlorinated agents, as an alternative to the conventional Schotten-Baumann reaction. These molecules were investigated in detail for their equilibrium and dynamic adsorption behavior, self-assembling, zeta-potential, emulsifying, foaming and wetting properties, and compared to model synthetic surfactants. The results showed that fibroin lipopeptides can efficiently reduce air/water surface tension and oil/water interfacial tension. The aggregates of lipopeptides were formed from 0.5 to 2 g.L −1 and showed average diameters between 167 and 224 nm depending on the molecule structure. Fibroin peptides demonstrated valuable physicochemical properties comparable to or better than commercial surfactants. They display excellent emulsifying properties, can form a stable and uniform foam, and ensure good wetting performance. These bio-based amphiphilic molecules can be considered as promising potential candidates for replacement of partially or fully petrochemical-derived surfactants in cosmetics, toiletries and pharmaceutical products. • Silk protein is a biopolymer with low carbon footprint and diverse applications. • Silk fibroin lipopeptides are synthesized by new mechanochemical approach. • Fibroin lipopeptides show good surface activity, emulsifying and foaming capacities. • Analysis of functional properties confirms their strong potential for applications.

Assessing PET chemical recycling via neutral hydrolysis: A techno-economic and GHG emissions study
abstract: Chemical recycling of PET waste is a promising approach for the recovery of high-quality monomers that aims at improving the circularity of plastic production. Solvolysis technologies are being developed and include hydrolysis with acid/base catalysts or enzymes to promote depolymerization reactions into PET constituent monomers, terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). However, the use of electricity, steam and organic solvents/chemicals has been identified as main factor affecting the economic and environmental performance of these technologies. This paper studies an alternative neutral hydrothermal process (nHTP), which involves hydrolysis at high temperatures and pressures without the use of catalysts, looking into the impact of water recycling and EG recovery in terms of costs and GHG emissions. The results reveal that recovering EG pays off the higher CAPEX and OPEX and yields a significant reduction in wastewater treatment costs, resulting in a TPA production cost of 1-1.4 EUR/kg and a carbon footprint of 1-1.7 kg CO2e/kg TPA. Although the process demands less electricity and steam compared to other hydrolysis technologies, fuel requirements for high temperature heat might limit its potential in the absence of sustainable heat options. Future studies are recommended to assess the utilization of lower-cost feedstocks (mixed waste and textiles), valorization of the solid by-product, and system integration possibilities to identify synergies between technologies in a broader chemical recycling context.

Impact of brominated flame retardants on the chemical recycling of polystyrene via pyrolysis
abstract: Brominated flame retardants remain a key challenge for the chemical recycling of polystyrene, particularly for expanded polystyrene used in external thermal insulation composite systems. Pyrolysis offers a viable route to recover monomer-rich oils, provided that bromine can be efficiently separated. In this study, the pyrolysis behavior of flame-retarded polystyrene containing hexabromocyclododecane and brominated butadiene-styrene-copolymer is investigated with a focus on bromine release and product composition. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy shows that approximately 90 wt% of bromine is released as hydrogen bromide below 350 °C, largely independent of composition. At elevated flame-retardant contents, stabilization effects emerge at higher temperatures due to interactions between flame-retardant decomposition intermediates and the polystyrene matrix. Pyrolysis-gas chromatography–mass spectrometry indicates that, at application-relevant loadings, the styrene-dominated product distribution remains unchanged. Heating rate variation reveals temporal separation between dehydrobromination and PS depolymerization, with rapid bromine release occurring under conditions relevant to technical pyrolysis. These findings demonstrate that pyrolysis can effectively direct bromine to the gas phase without compromising product quality, providing a basis for temperature-driven process design and advancing circular recycling strategies for flame-retarded polystyrene waste.

abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) suffer from severe Zn anode instability, including dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions, which hinders their practical application. Herein, edible food dyes are, for the first time, introduced as green and low-cost electrolyte additives to stabilize Zn anodes. Three representative dyes-Ponceau 4R Lake (PL), Tartrazine, and Sunset Yellow-are incorporated into a 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte at an ultra-low concentration of 0.3 mM, among which PL exhibits the best overall performance. The PL-modified Zn||Zn symmetric cell achieves an ultralong cycling life of 4500 h at 1 mA cm-2/1 mAh cm-2 and maintains stable operation under high current densities and high areal capacities. Mechanistic studies reveal a synergistic dual-layer interfacial regulation mechanism. Al3+ in PL promotes Zn2+ desolvation and enables in situ formation of a Zn-Al alloyed interfacial layer, while PL anions form an outer organic adsorption layer that guides Zn (002)-preferred deposition and suppresses dendrite growth. This work provides a sustainable dual-layer interfacial strategy for high-performance AZIBs.

Integrated direct air capture–to–ethylene production via CO2 electroreduction: Process modeling and techno-economic analysis
abstract: Ethylene production from atmospheric CO 2 through integrated direct air capture (DAC) and electrochemical CO 2 reduction offers a pathway for atmospheric‑carbon chemicals, but its commercial viability remains uncertain. Previous techno-economic studies have often treated the electrolyzer separately, assumed point-source CO 2 , or considered single-pass conversion as an independent parameter. These approaches overlook a key coupling in alkaline MEA electrolyzers: carbonate crossover through the anion exchange membrane limits single-pass conversion while also increasing the required upstream DAC capacity. The system-level economic impact of this coupling has not yet been quantified in the literature. This work presents a complete process model and techno-economic analysis of an integrated DAC–electrolyzer–separation plant producing 85 kt yr −1 of ethylene from atmospheric CO 2 . A system-level Carbon utilization efficiency, SCUE, is introduced to link electrolyzer performance with DAC capacity. Under base-case conditions, SCUE is only 18.3%, with 64.1% of feed CO 2 lost to crossover, single-pass conversion capped at 22%, and DAC capacity 5.4 times larger than the stoichiometric minimum. The minimum ethylene selling price (MESP) is $8.58/kg, dominated by electricity, which accounts for 56.7% of OPEX, and DAC, which accounts for 81% of equipment cost. Monte Carlo analysis ( N = 10,000) gives a mean MESP of $8.78/kg, with an 80% confidence interval of $7.10–10.55/kg. Electricity price and crossover together explain 71.5% of the variance. Reducing the crossover coefficient from 0.5 to 0.1 decreases MESP by 23%. Independently, near-term material integration through anode CO 2 recovery and O 2 coupling to the DAC calciner lowers the base-case MESP by 26%, from $8.58 to $6.35/kg. Genetic-algorithm optimization over nine electrochemical variables yields a separate 15% reduction, from $8.77 to $7.49 kg −1 . Under GA-optimized operation, fossil parity requires carbon credits of approximately $225–250 tCO 2 −1 for DAC-integrated production, compared with $25–75 tCO 2 −1 for point-source CO 2 . Overall, membrane transport, electricity price, DAC cost, and policy support emerge as the main levers for commercial viability.

abstract: Bio-based silk fibroin (SF) typically exhibits suboptimal piezoelectric performance due to the low proportion of β-sheet crystalline domains and poor interfacial compatibility with inorganic fillers, which limits its application in flexible self-powered sensing. In this study, hydrothermally synthesized MoS₂ nanoflowers were doped into SF, and SF/MoS₂ composite nanofibrous membranes were fabricated via composite electrospinning, with their preparation process and piezoelectric properties systematically investigated. Acting as nucleating agents, MoS₂ nanoflowers significantly promote the formation of β-sheet structures in SF, increasing the content from 40.96% in pristine SF membranes to 47.22%. Synergizing with their intrinsic piezoelectric effect and optimized interfacial stress transfer, the composite membrane achieves an open-circuit voltage of 5.41 V，approximately twice that of pristine SF，and maintains stable output after 3300 cyclic compressions. Assembled into PENG devices, it was applied to human motion monitoring, enabling real-time detection of muscle contraction activities with clear signals, rapid response, and excellent repeatability, thus providing a novel strategy for self-powered sensing and wearable energy harvesting.

Theoretical and kinetic modeling study of hydrazine oxidation
abstract: The present work constitutes the first theoretical and kinetic modeling study of hydrazine oxidation, which may be important for burnout in ammonia-fueled combustion. The kinetics of the oxidation of N 2 H 4 , N 2 H 3 and tHNNH by molecular oxygen were investigated via a quantum chemistry/canonical transition state theory approach. Geometries and anharmonic frequencies were obtained with derived density functional theory, and energies from coupled cluster calculations (CCSD(T)) extrapolated to the infinite basis set limit, with corrections for core-valence electron correlation, scalar relativistic effects, and higher level correlation up to lambda coupled cluster, CCSDT(Q) Λ . The key reactions occurred on the N 2 H 4 O 2 potential energy surface, where the results indicated a fast reaction of N 2 H 3 with HO 2 via singlet adducts to yield tHNNH + H 2 O 2 and HNN(H)O + H 2 O, while reaction on the triplet surface proceeds via a bound complex followed by a tight, submerged barrier to yield N 2 H 4 + O 2 . The results were incorporated in a detailed reaction mechanism, which was used to interpret the shock tube results from Michel and Wagner (1965) on the effect of O 2 on hydrazine conversion at 1100-1400 K. The kinetic model captured qualitatively the observed behavior, but underestimated the reaction rate under oxidizing conditions. The hydrazine pyrolysis chemistry dominated conversion at reducing conditions and/or high temperature. At oxidizing conditions and intermediate temperatures ( ≲ 1400 K), reactions of N 2 -amines with HO 2 and O 2 were important for the oxidation rate. • The present work constitutes the first theoretical and kinetic modeling study of hydrazine oxidation. • The kinetics of the oxidation of N 2 H 4 , N 2 H 3 and tHNNH by O 2 were investigated by ab initio theory. • Reactions on the N 2 H 4 O 2 potential energy surface were particularly important. • The kinetic model captures the effect of O 2 addition on N 2 H 4 , consumption in shock tube. • The hydrazine pyrolysis chemistry dominates at reducing conditions and/or high temperature, while at oxidizing conditions and intermediate temperatures, reactions of N 2 -amines with HO 2 and O 2 were important for the oxidation rate.

Multi-mode and encapsulated droplet-based electricity generator for environmental sensing and cathodic protection
abstract: Droplet-based electricity generators (DEGs) represent one of the most promising energy harvesting devices, capable of effectively converting ambient mechanical energy into electrical power. However, existing DEGs suffer from intrinsic constraints, including limited motion adaptability and mandatory dependence on open-loop configurations, severely limiting their deployment in enclosed or dynamic environments. Here, we propose a novel encapsulated droplet-based electricity generator (ME-DEG) architecture featuring multi-mode responsiveness. Our design employs an encapsulated FEP tube filled with solution to achieve directional charge transfer via gravity-inertial synergized fluid dynamics. Notably, this encapsulated, closed-loop configuration liberates the DEG from open-system constraints, enabling it to respond to multi-mode environmental motions. Fabricated with optimized structural parameters, the ME-DEG achieves a record-high volumetric current density of 318308.64 μA m-3, representing an elevenfold enhancement over conventional droplet energy harvesters. Crucially, the ME-DEG demonstrates dual functionalities. First, it acts as a self-powered sensor: the ME-DEG seamlessly integrates efficient energy harvesting with real-time environmental monitoring, presenting a versatile platform for self-powered systems in dynamic environments. Second, it plays a electrons supplier to 304SS to change it from self-corrosion state (Ecorr~-0.140 (V Vs. SCE)) to cathodic protection state (Ecorr~-0.463 (V Vs. SCE)).

Copper-driven nanoadjuvant reverses immunosuppression in colorectal cancer by orchestrating metabolic dysfunction and innate immune activation
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a formidable therapeutic challenge, particularly in its immunosuppressive “cold tumor” manifestation, which is characterized by impoverished T-cell infiltration and inherent resistance to conventional therapies. Under treatment stress, CRC cells intensify their metabolic adaptability by upregulating glycolysis (the Warburg effect) and macropinocytosis to salvage extracellular nutrients, thereby sustaining bioenergetic and anabolic demands and facilitating therapeutic escape. To counteract these mechanisms, we engineered a multifunctional copper-based coordination nanoadjuvant, designated F/Cu-Ce6@AMI NPs, through the coordinated assembly of chlorin e6 (Ce6), Cu2+ ions, and the macropinocytosis inhibitor amiloride (AMI), with an outer shell of Pluronic F-127 to enhance biocompatibility and tumor accumulation. This system orchestrates a dual metabolic intervention: (i) synergistically inducing mitochondrial dysfunction via Cu2+-evoked cuproptosis and Ce6-mediated photodynamic therapy (PDT), resulting in abrupt ATP loss and profound ROS generation; and (ii) inhibiting macropinocytosis-dependent nutrient scavenging with AMI, leading catastrophic energy failure. The resultant mitochondrial damage promotes mtDNA leakage into the cytosol, activating the cGAS–STING innate immune pathway and subsequently triggering dendritic cell maturation, cytotoxic CD8+T-cell recruitment, and M1 macrophage repolarization, collectively converting the immunosuppressive TME into an immunologically active milieu. Robust antitumor effects and potent immune activation were consistently validated both in vitro and in vivo. Our work unveils a novel metabolic immunotherapy that co-targets tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental metabolic pathways to potentiate antitumor immunity in refractory cold CRC.

Phthalocyanine-based interlayers for reducing ion defects and enhancing stability in perovskite solar cells with an efficiency over 24%
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising option in pursuing sustainable energy solutions owing to their exceptional efficiency and cost-effectiveness. However, persistent challenges such as ion migration, halide vacancy formation, and interfacial instability continue to hinder their commercial viability. In this study, we explore a series of phthalocyanine (Pc)-based molecules coded as EG-2H1 (metal-free), EG-Ni2 (nickel), EG-Cu2 (copper), and EG-Zn2 (zinc), as multifunctional organic semiconductors with Lewis base functionality, aiming to improve both defect passivation and charge transport. Initially evaluated as hole transport materials (HTMs), these Pc derivatives exhibited moderate photovoltaic performance. However, their most promising results were observed when employed as interfacial layers between the perovskite absorber and the HTM. In this configuration, the Pc molecules effectively suppressed interfacial recombination, passivated halide vacancies through their Lewis base functional groups (-Cl end atoms and oxygen-bridge units), and promoted efficient hole extraction due to their inherent p-type character. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations suggest that while all investigated systems contribute to defect passivation on the perovskite surface, the metal-free EG-2H1 exhibits a somewhat enhanced capability, likely due to its comparatively more negative electrostatic potential. The champion cell utilizing EG-2H1 (0.5 mg/mL) as the interfacial layer achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24.3%, with an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.17 V, short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.8 mA/cm2 and a fill factor (FF) of 80.8%. In contrast, the control device without Pc interlayers demonstrated a lower PCE of 22.2% with a remarkable hysteresis. Furthermore, stability tests under continuous illumination revealed that Pc-modified devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 700 h, while the control devices degraded below 70%. These findings highlight the superior role of phthalocyanine derivatives as interfacial layers over their function as standalone HTMs, paving the way for their future commercial realization.

title: A layered approach to secure the safety and therapeutic efficacy of hiPSC-derived functionalized neuronal tissueoid for repair after complete spinal cord lnjury in rats
abstract: The functional integration of donor neurons with host neural pathways is a critical treatment for spinal cord injury (SCl). We constructed human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neuronal tissueoids (Ntoids) transfected with thymidine kinase (TK) to transplant donor neurons into SCl rats. Ntoids were produced after 28-days culture in a 3-dimensional gelatin sponge scaffold and possessed neuronal cells with synaptic transmission and neural network property in vitro. Ganciclovir, a TK substrate, depleted proliferative cells in Ntoids without affecting neuronal tissueoid formation, leaving non-mitotic and functionalized neuronal cells for transplantation. Ntoid-treated SCl rats achieved significantly better functional recovery in paralyzed hindlimbs and improved electrophysiological performance. Eight weeks after transplantation, remarkable surviving of donor cells suffused the entire injury/graft site and did not present discernible long-distance cell migration, leading to intensive innervation of the injury/graft site. Ntoids possessed cholinergic hiPSC-derived neurons that survived at the injury/graft site, successfully integrating with regenerating nerve fibers and neurons via synapse-like contacts. Some donor cells differentiated into astrocytes and formed a chimeric blood/spinal cord barrier with the host's vascular epithelium. Ntoids represent a structural and functional neuronal relay to restore functionality in paralyzed limbs. These findings support the safety and efficacy of the transplantation of mature neuronal tissue with safety-regulatory mechanisms to treat SCI and provide a framework for future clinical application using tissue-engineered Ntoid.

Tailored multifunctional passivation enables efficient and stable flexible perovskite solar cells
abstract: Depositing a passivation layer on perovskite surfaces represents an effective strategy to realize exceptional power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). In this work, 4-Fluoro-Phenethylammonium chloride (4F-PEACl), containing a CH₂-NH₃⁺ moiety, is introduced as a tailored passivation layer. It eliminates deep trap states and reduces non-radiative recombination by occupying formamidinium (FA⁺) vacancies or substituting FA ions at the perovskite surface. Consequently, a significant boost in both the efficiency and stability of the resulting devices is obtained. The optimized rigid p‐i‐n PSCs deliver a champion PCE of 26.57%, while flexible devices achieve a PCE of 25.52%. The unencapsulated devices demonstrate excellent operational stability, retaining 94.6% of initial PCE after 2000 hours under maximum power point tracking and continuous illumination at 65 °C, and 93.5% after 2000 hours of thermal aging at 85 °C. Moreover, the 4F-PEACl-based flexible device preserves 92.7% of its initial PCE following 1000 bending cycles, substantially outperforming the control device (58.6%).

abstract: On-demand wetting transitions enable surfaces with dynamic control over liquid interactions, enabling applications in microfluidics, soft robotics, and self-cleaning technologies. In this work, we developed superomniphobic surfaces with programmable texture by simple, scalable and solvent free CO 2 laser texturing of shape memory polymers to obtain re-entrant texture, followed by surface modification to impart low solid surface energy. Our stimuli responsive superomniphobic surfaces are not only repellent to aqueous and organic liquids, but also display reversible on-demand wetting transitions for multiple cycles on exposure to external stimuli due to rearrangement of molecular chains. We demonstrated the ex situ and in situ on-demand wetting transitions using contact mode (heat) and non-contact mode (NIR laser). We also demonstrated the reversible and erasable liquid patterns on superomniphobic surfaces with programmable wettability. We envision that superomniphobic surfaces with programmable wettability will have wide range of applications including rewritable liquid patterns, liquid droplet manipulations, lab on chip devices and selective chemical reactions.
