Direct 3D printing of molten metal electrodes for perovskite solar cells
abstract: Owing to the solution-processability Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are advancing rapidly in the field of emerging technologies. Layers forming the PSC can be easily printed or coated, the back electrode relies on metals such as gold, silver, aluminum, or copper, deposited via vacuum-based physical deposition, emphasizing the need for printed electrode alternative. This work demonstrates a novel additive manufacturing of printed molten metal electrodes (PME) utilizing StarJet technology. Bulk 57Bi-42Sn-1Ag alloy was printed by jetting directly onto PSC substrates. With this inexpensive and effective electrode material and deposition process, the PSCs achieved power conversion efficiency (PCE) ~11% under STC (1 sun, 1000 W/m 2 AM 1.5). Stability tests revealed a T80 > 1000 h for PME-based cells under ISOS-D shelf life test. While lower in performance, the approach demonstrates strong potential for cost-effective, scalable PSC manufacturing and highlights pathways for further optimization.

title: Tough, swelling-resistant conductive hydrogels for underwater communication
abstract: Conductive hydrogel sensors are extensively employed in fields such as biomedical detection and wearable electronics, owing to their remarkable sensitivity, biocompatibility, and responsiveness to stimuli. However, hydrogels often suffer from swelling in aqueous environments, which undermines their long-term performance stability. Consequently, developing structurally engineered hydrogels that exhibit outstanding anti-swelling properties while maintaining stable conductivity remains a significant challenge. In this work, a robust, swelling-resistant hydrogel was fabricated through hydrophobic interactions and metal-coordination interactions, achieving a swelling rate of only 0.6% over 30 days and enabling stable signal transmission in complex aqueous environments. Furthermore, a highly sensitive honeycomb-structured hydrogel sensor was constructed via reduction photopolymerization-based 3D printing technology. As a proof of concept, this sensor can continuously monitor human motion and reliably transmit emergency signals such as "SOS" in aquatic settings. This study presents an advanced strategy for fabricating conductive hydrogel sensors for underwater applications, demonstrating potential utility in smart wearable sensing devices and marine exploration.

Tin oxide quantum dots/MXenes hybrids: Synthesis methods, properties, and electrochemical energy storage applications
abstract: MXene-based nanocomposites, characterized by high electrical conductivity with layered architecture, coupled with zero-dimensional SnO 2 quantum dots (QDs) with outstanding electronic and electrochemical properties arising from quantum confinement and large surface-to-volume ratios, have attracted significant interest in providing improved energy storage applications. The review examines the latest developments in SnO 2 QDs/MXene nanocomposites, including their synthesis, structural characteristics, and electrochemical performance in supercapacitors and batteries. The combined effect of SnO 2 QDs and MXene improves ionic diffusion, charge storage capacity, cycle stability, and rate performance. The review covers lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), lithium‑sulfur (Li 3 S) batteries, lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) and supercapacitors as well as the case-study to focus on LIBs since they constitute the majority of current SnO 2 QD/MXene systems. In-depth case studies indicate that SnO 2 QD in MXene hybrids suppress two synergistic failure modes of Sn-based electrodes such as pulverization associated with Li-Na + alloying reactions and uncontrolled solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth during the cycling. This dual stabilization contributes to high specific capacitance in supercapacitors and high energy density in batteries. Other synthesis methods and composite architectures are also compared in this review to explain the performance improvements. Although these developments have been made, they have challenges of scalability, long-term electrochemical stability, and cost effective production. Their limitations are critically analyzed and future research directions are outlined to advance laboratory scale innovations in SnO 2 QDs/MXene towards commercially viable energy storage devices.

Construction of bioaffinity antibacterial coatings via piezoelectric effect-enhanced alkaline microenvironment
abstract: The inherent antibacterial properties of titanium and its alloys are limited and cannot meet the antibacterial requirements of clinical implants. Traditional antibacterial methods, such as the release of heavy metal ions and the use of antibiotics, have potential side effects and the risk of inducing bacterial resistance. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop an antibacterial coating for titanium surfaces that also has biocompatibility. In this study, a magnesium oxide composite piezoelectric antibacterial nano-coating was successfully constructed on the surface of titanium based on the essential trace element magnesium for the human body. The regulation of ions by piezoelectric charges enhances the alkaline microenvironment on the coating surface, enabling a synergistic effect of rapid short-term bactericidal activity and sustained long-term antibacterial performance. Additionally, in vitro mineralization and cellular assays demonstrate that ultrasonic stimulation, in conjunction with magnesium ion release, promotes calcium phosphate deposition as well as cell proliferation and differentiation. By leveraging the synergistic bactericidal mechanism of the piezoelectric effect and alkaline microenvironment, this study imparts titanium implants with safe and highly efficient antibacterial properties without relying on drugs or antibiotics, thereby providing a novel strategy for the design of clinical antibacterial coatings.

title: Design of novel multifunctional quaternized algal/PEI hybrid for selective removal of perrhenate and environmental remediation of 99Tc
abstract: The association of alginate (from brown algal biomass) and branched polyethyleneimine (PEI) (through dual crosslinking involving glutaraldehyde with amine groups of PEI, and calcium for ionotropic gelation of the biopolymer) allowed preparing stable support (APEI) that can bind Re(VII) in mild acidic conditions. However, the quaternization of APEI (as Q-APEI, through the grafting of (3-chloro-2-hydroxypropyl)trimethylammonium groups) strongly enhanced perrhenate sorption (from 0.544 to 1.51 mmol Re g−1) at pH 4. The combination of FTIR and XPS spectrometric methods demonstrated that most of the sorption proceeds by ion-exchange/electrostatic attraction of perrhenate anions onto protonated amine groups and quaternary ammonium groups and/or chelation with primary and secondary amine groups (though carboxyl/carbonyl may also contribute to a lesser extent). Equilibrium time was also improved by quaternization: under selected experimental conditions, equilibrium is reduced from 90 to 30 min; the pseudo-first order rate equation fits the kinetics. The Temkin equation simulates sorption isotherms better than the Langmuir equation. The beneficial effect of quaternization was confirmed by the selectivity (and distribution ratio) in equimolar multi-metal solutions and in the presence of increasing amounts of NaCl. Sorbents show remarkable stability in sorption performances for ten successive sorption/desorption cycles; using 0.5 M HNO3 solution as the eluent: the loss in performance did not exceed 5% for Q-APEI at the last cycle (14% for APEI). Perrhenate being a realistic surrogate of pertechnetate, optimized experimental conditions were successfully applied for the removal of 99Tc from a series of synthetic solutions (prepared with variable levels of radioactivity and compositions; increasing the salinity of the solutions). These complementary tests confirm the significant enhancement in sorption performance with quaternized material (in terms of both kinetics and isotherms).

An automated closed-loop fabrication of 3D microscale metal structures via image recognition and voltage feedback in Jet ECD
abstract: To overcome the difficulty of synchronizing the deposition rate with the anode motion trajectory in jet electrochemical deposition (Jet ECD), this study presents an image recognition-assisted electrical signal feedback multi-cycle edge-localization strategy. The method enables fully automated, closed-loop fabrication of 3D microscale copper structures, including unsupported overhang and multi-segment helical columns. During vertical growth, grayscale-based image recognition acts as a displacement trigger for precise positioning. In the overhang stage, voltage feedback dynamically regulates the contact distance between the copper column and the liquid column, enabling real-time synchronization of the deposition rate and motion trajectory. Experimental results demonstrate reliable fabrication of structures with uniform angles and favorable morphology. The standard voltage decreases dynamically with increasing structure height. Significant fluctuations in voltage difference and deposition time per step indicate the nonlinear dependence of the deposition rate on structure height. Linear fitting-based voltage compensation is insufficient to maintain structural stability, underscoring the importance of the multi-cycle edge-localization mechanism. Microstructural characterization reveals a copper purity of 98.5 wt%, with random grain orientation, an average grain size of 0.3 µm, and dense, smooth surface morphology. The proposed strategy offers a robust method for high-precision automated fabrication of complex 3D microscale metallic structures.

Which natural organic matter components limit PFAS removal by activated carbon?
abstract: PFAS are persistent micropollutants subject to strict drinking water regulations. Although granular activated carbon treatment can effectively remove PFAS from water, early breakthrough, especially for short-chain PFAS, requires frequent regeneration and increases treatment costs. While many studies have related the presence of natural organic matter (NOM) to early breakthrough, the mechanisms affecting PFAS adsorption remain unclear. In this study, we used resin and membrane fractionation to isolate distinct NOM fractions based on chemical characteristics and molecular size. Batch isotherm, kinetic, and column experiments showed that the presence of the <3 kDa fraction significantly reduced short-chain PFAS adsorption. As low molecular weight compounds (<3 kDa) are consistently detected in source waters at concentrations comparable to or higher than those included in this study, their removal is crucial to improving short-chain PFAS removal during drinking water treatment. Conversely, long-chain PFAS adsorption was not notably affected by molecular size fractions but was significantly reduced in the presence of the hydrophobic neutral (HON) fraction. The LC-OCD analysis indicated that HON consists of compounds with similar molecular characteristics as long-chain PFAS, suggesting direct competition for adsorption sites between long-chain PFAS and HON. The HON fraction is typically present at lower concentrations compared to other NOM fractions in natural waters. This low concentration of the HON helps explain the delayed breakthrough observed for long-chain PFAS, in contrast to short-chain PFAS, whose breakthrough is rapid due to the high concentration of the <3 kDa fraction. We found that the presence of specific NOM fractions can indicate reduced PFAS removal, suggesting that NOM fractionation techniques could be integrated into monitoring procedures at drinking water facilities, as the presence of specific fractions can indicate reduced PFAS removal.

abstract: In this work, underwater self-healing AMPS hydrogel was prepared by acrylic acid (AA), acrylamide (AAm), 2-phenoxyethanol acrylate (PEA), and [2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl]dimethyl-(3-sulfopropyl)ammonium hydroxide (SBMA). Hydrophobic segments were introduced through hydrophobic groups of PEA. AMPS hydrogel was endowed with excellent anti-swelling performance. The reversible crosslinking points including π-π stacking interactions, electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonds were simultaneously constructed, making the self-healing efficiency of strain and stress reach 98% and 90% after self-healing in underwater environment for 1 h. Furthermore, to cope with the variability of water environment, strain self-healing efficiency after self-healing for 1 h in seawater and corn oil environments could reach over 80%. And the strain self-healing efficiency for 1 h could exceed 80% in high and low-temperature air and water environments. After being soaked in water, seawater and corn oil environments for a month, the strain self-healing efficiency for 1 h still could reach over 80%. Due to introduction of SBMA, AMPS hydrogel possessed favourable electrical conductivity of 0.013 S/m. Thus, AMPS hydrogel-based sensor could detect human movements in air and water environment, indicating AMPS hydrogel possessed promising application prospect in wearable strain sensors field.

Tailoring the electron delocalization in Co3O4 by d-p orbital hybridization to boost the generation of high-valent metal-oxo species for effective degradation of florfenicol via peroxymonosulfate activation
abstract: It is of great significance to develop effective process for advanced degradation of fluorinated antibiotics. Herein, phosphorus-doped Co3O4 (P-Co3O4) as peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activator is synthesized. Introduced phosphorus can react with cobalt site of Co3O4 to trigger the d-p orbital hybridization, thereby promoting the oxygen vacancy formation and regulating the d-band center of Co3O4. Importantly, the existence of oxygen vacancy boosts the binding of Co site with terminal oxygen of PMS, and the d-p orbital hybridization effect enhances the electron delocalization of d-orbital. Thus, PMS adsorbed on P-Co3O4 can be easily activated to generate high-valent metal-oxo species (Co4+=O), which plays an important role in florfenicol degradation. More interestingly, introduced phosphorus can serve as Brønsted base site to capture H+ during the process of PMS, thereby facilitating the formation of active hydrogen that breaks the C-F bond of florfenicol. As a result, the P-Co3O4-mediated PMS system shows satisfactory removal efficiencies of total organic carbon and F ion. Furthermore, florfenicol degradation pathways are investigated, and its by-products are proven to be low toxicity or nontoxic. In short, current work not only elucidates positive role of d-p orbital hybridization, but also provides a promising technique for effective treatment of wastewater containing fluorinated antibiotics.

Voronoi curvature scaffolds rejuvenate senescent stem cells and enhance aged bone regeneration
abstract: Ageing is associated with a progressive decline in stem cell function and regenerative capacity, contributing to impaired bone healing in elderly populations. Cellular senescence and dysregulated mechanotransduction are key factors underlying this age-related deterioration in tissue regeneration. Tissue curvature has recently emerged as an important regulator of cellular behaviour; however, its role in modulating cellular senescence and functional decline remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate how hyperboloidal curvature regulates senescence and osteogenic differentiation in adipose tissue-derived stem cells (ASCs) and its impact on bone regeneration in vivo . Using high-resolution liquid crystal display (LCD) 3D printing, we fabricated biphasic calcium phosphate (BCP) scaffolds with distinct Gaussian curvature profiles, including Cubic, Gyroid, and Voronoi hyperboloidal architectures, and seeded senescent ASCs onto these scaffolds. ASCs cultured on Voronoi-curved scaffolds exhibited the lowest expression of cell cycle repression genes (P16, P21) and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors, together with markedly enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Mechanistically, Voronoi curvature was associated with reduced αVβ3 integrin expression in senescent ASCs and increased nuclear translocation of Yes-associated protein (YAP), suggesting involvement of mechanosensitive signalling pathways. Blocking αVβ3 integrin signalling rejuvenated senescent ASCs and further enhanced their osteogenic differentiation. In an aged rat critical-sized defect model, Voronoi curvature scaffolds significantly improved bone regeneration compared with Cubic and Gyroid scaffolds. Collectively, these findings identify hyperboloidal Voronoi curvature scaffolds as a powerful geometric cue capable of rejuvenating senescent stem cells and enhancing aged bone repair. This work highlights scaffold geometry as a promising strategy for designing anti-senescent biomaterials to address age-related skeletal regeneration.

title: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells-guided mesoporous silica nanoplatform delivering a BET inhibitor exerts anticancer effects by reprogramming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment
abstract: Mivebresib (Miv), a pan-bromodomain and extra-terminal motif (BET) inhibitor currently in clinical trials for several solid tumors, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), primarily exerts its antitumor activity through epigenetic regulation. However, its clinical potential is limited by poor solubility and bioavailability. Moreover, the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a major driver of therapeutic resistance in PDAC. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) represent key therapeutic targets, the predominant immunosuppressive populations within the TME. To address these challenges, Miv was encapsulated into functionalized mesoporous silica nanoparticles (C8-RMSN), yielding Miv@C8-RMSN with uniform morphology, high loading efficiency, and excellent dispersibility. In vitro , this formulation preserved the pharmacological activity of Miv against PDAC cells and TAMs, while promoting M1 macrophage polarization via both tumor–macrophage interaction-dependent and macrophage-intrinsic mechanisms. In vivo , Miv@C8-RMSN demonstrated tumor accumulation, metabolic clearance, and favorable biosafety profiles, while achieving significant antitumor efficacy at an effective dose equivalent to 1/14 of the original dosing regimen (1 mg/kg/day oral Mivebresib administered for 14 consecutive days; total cumulative dose: 14 mg/kg). To further target MDSCs, H6-decorated Miv@C8-RMSN was developed, which enhanced cellular uptake and increased apoptosis-associated cytotoxicity in MDSCs. This system was associated with enhanced antitumor immune activation and induction of immunogenic cell death hallmarks, while achieving comparable therapeutic effects at a further reduced total dose (approximately 0.5 mg/kg Mivebresib), corresponding to an overall 1/28 dose reduction. Collectively, this MSN-based nanoplatform provides a promising immunotherapeutic strategy to potentiate BET inhibitor efficacy in PDAC by remodeling the immunosuppressive TME.

Vacancy-engineered electronic structure enables decoupled polysulfide anchoring and kinetic passivation in lithium-sulfur batteries
abstract: Lithium-sulfur batteries suffer from sluggish liquid-solid sulfur conversion and polysulfide shuttling, issues often exacerbated by interfacial passivation in conventional hosts. Herein, we engineer a sulfur host by incorporating tellurium-vacancy-modulated cobalt telluride (CoTe) into an open, ordered macro-microporous N-doped carbon framework. This hierarchical architecture ensures full exposure of vacancy sites while facilitating rapid mass transport. Synergistically, the porous structure confines polysulfides and enhances ion diffusion, while DFT calculations reveal that tellurium vacancies upshift the Co d-band center by 0.25 eV. This electronic modulation promotes electron transfer and lowers the energy barrier for Li2S2-to-Li2S conversion, effectively overcoming the typical adsorption-activity trade-off. Consequently, the design suppresses interfacial passivation and guides uniform Li2S deposition. Benefiting from this vacancy-enabled regulation of sulfur redox behavior, Li-S batteries employing VCT/S cathodes deliver a high specific capacity of 1391 mAh g-1 at 0.1 C, remarkable rate capability (533.3 mAh g-1 at 5 C), and long-term cycling stability with a low average capacity decay rate of 0.053% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C. Moreover, the cathode maintains superior performance under practical conditions, including high sulfur loading (4.5 mg cm-2) and low electrolyte-to-sulfur (E/S) ratios. This work establishes a generalizable strategy coupling hierarchical pore engineering with vacancy-modulated electronic structure regulation to overcome adsorption-induced passivation in multistep sulfur redox systems.

Unifying CO2 diffusion mechanisms in diamine-functionalized metal–organic frameworks via quantum-accurate machine learning dynamics
abstract: Diamine-functionalized M2(dobpdc) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) (dobpdc4- = 4,4'-dioxidobiphenyl-3,3'-dicarboxylate; M = Mg, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn) exhibit exceptional CO2 capture, yet their CO2 diffusion behavior has remained difficult to rationalize across pore sizes, loadings, and functionalization. Here we resolve this gap by combining diffusion measurements with quantum-accurate machine-learning-potential molecular dynamics (MLP-MD) to establish a unified, loading-dependent mechanism for CO2 transport in Mg2(dobpdc) MOFs. Our MLPs reproduce density functional theory energetics and forces, enabling converged diffusion coefficients and microscopic trajectories. By comparing Mg2(dobdc), Mg2(dobpdc), and Mg2(dotpdc), we show that at low uptake CO2 is transiently trapped near open Mg sites, producing suppressed diffusivity in both MLP-MD simulations and diffusion measurements. With increasing uptake, the progressive saturation of these strong adsorption sites screens their trapping potential, leading to a rise in diffusion coefficients for Mg2(dobpdc) and Mg2(dotpdc), quantitatively consistent with experiments. Diamine functionalization further accelerates CO2 transport by limiting access to open Mg sites and introducing cooperative CO2–diamine interactions. Finally, the same MLPs accurately predict CO2 adsorption isotherms via grand canonical Monte Carlo. Together, the experimentally validated MLP-MD framework reveals how pore size and diamine functionalization synergistically govern CO2 diffusion, providing design rules for high-capacity MOFs with improved mass transport.

Interfacial hydrogen bonding as a key driver for selective phenolic compounds removal via Mg(OH)2-catalyzed peroxymonosulfate activation
abstract: Selective removal of phenolic micropollutants is critical for sustainable water treatment. This study reports a distinct nonradical peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation pathway with unique selectivity for phenolic compounds using Mg(OH)2. Unlike the conventional advanced oxidation processes, the Mg(OH)2/PMS system operates through a hydrogen bond (HB)-mediated mechanism. Mechanistic evidence reveals that basic surface hydroxyl groups on Mg(OH)2 and deprotonated SO52- act as HB acceptors, forming a dynamic complex with phenolic contaminants (hydrogen bond donors) and water molecules. This interfacial HB network facilitates rapid proton transfer which is mediated by the catalyst and water, triggering PMS decomposition and pollutant degradation. Integrating experimental results with theoretical modeling, the degradation rate constant is revealed to be positively correlated with the hydrogen-donating ability of the phenolics which can be indexed by the highest occupied molecular orbitals. While mineralization is limited (~6%), the system proved highly effective for the selective transformation and detoxification of phenolic contaminants in complex matrices. This work elucidates the role of many-body hydrogen bonding in heterogeneous catalysis, offering a promising strategy for the targeted, low-carbon remediation of phenolic-rich wastewater.

Highly performing and stable ordered intermetallic L10-PtCo0.8Ti0.2 alloys for oxygen reduction reaction
abstract: Tertiary platinum-based alloy electrocatalysts on the cathode side of a proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) can help accelerate the sluggish oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), and there is great potential in this area. However, it is still a rather difficult problem to synthesize such a small-sized, structurally ordered ternary alloy catalysts, and no particularly good solution has been found yet. Herein, we report a ternary ordered intermetallic L1 0 -PtCo 0.8 Ti 0.2 nanocatalyst that serves as a highly active and exceptionally stable candidate. During half - cell evaluations, the refined L1 0 -PtCo 0.8 Ti 0.2 catalyst showcases outstanding catalytic capabilities, attaining a half - wave potential (E 1/2 ) of 0.939 V. Significantly, its mass activity (MA) is 9.8 times greater and specific activity (SA) is 7.9 times higher compared to those of the commercially available Pt/C catalyst. Furthermore, in single-cell PEMFC tests, the L1 0 -PtCo 0.8 Ti 0.2 cathode exhibits outstanding ORR performance, delivering an excellent MA of 0.995 A/mg Pt at 0.9 V -iR-free- alongside superior durability. DFT calculations demonstrate that the incorporation of Ti optimizes the balance between intermediate adsorption and desorption by strengthening the interaction with oxygenated intermediates, thereby significantly enhancing the ORR activity. This work provides new information for the rational design of high-performance ORR nanocatalysts.

Multifunctional layer coupling in hybrid carbon nanotube networks enables high-performance catalyst layer in proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: The transition towards low-carbon transport demands a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) with both high efficiency and robust operational stability. Under real operating conditions, the coupling of charge transfer, gas transport, and moisture distribution within fuel cells introduces systemic complexity and poses challenges for catalytic material design. Here, guided by a multifunctional layer coupling strategy, this work achieves multiscale synergistic optimisation from microscopic conductive backbone construction, through mesoscale reaction-interface regulation, to macroscopic integration of membrane-electrode-assembly (MEA) functional layers, by means of controllable surface functionalisation and support hybridisation. Mildly oxidised multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were engineered to establish a conductive core-reactive interface, preserving the graphitic backbone for electron transport whilst introducing an oxygen-containing outer layer for controlled Pt anchoring. When blended with carbon black (CB), the resulting MWCNT-CB hierarchical conductive framework enhances Pt accessibility, reconstructs transport pathways and improves PEMFC performance under operating conditions. In small-scale cells, the optimised Pt/MWCNT-CB 1:1 catalyst delivered a 68% increase in peak power over Pt/CB. Under automotive-relevant conditions, it achieved 1535 mW cm −2 , surpassing the U.S Department of Energy (DOE) targets. Durability testing following DOE protocols confirmed suppressed Pt migration and reduced carbon corrosion. The predicted operational lifetimes of Pt/MWCNT (6 h oxidation) and Pt/MWCNT-CB 1:1 were 16,906 and 14,761 h, respectively, with start-up/shut-down tolerances of 15,110 and 6060 cycles. Both metrics exceed the DOE ultimate durability targets for light-duty fuel cell vehicles (8000 h operation and 5000 start-up/shut-down cycles), highlighting a practical route towards durable, high-performance catalysts for light-duty fuel cell vehicles.

Mixed or functionalized: How sorbent–catalyst architecture limits sorption-enhanced reactors
abstract: Decarbonization requires efficient pathways to convert CO 2 into synthetic fuels. Process efficiency of CO 2 hydrogenation reactions can be enhanced by in-situ removal of (by-)products, which increases conversion. Past research focused on validating the sorption-enhancement effect for the CO 2 methanation reaction, comparing conventional plug flow with sorption-enhanced reactors. However, the influence of the sorbent–catalyst architecture has not been systematically examined. In this work, we compare the two most commonly used architectures: functionalized sorbent pellets and physical mixtures of separate catalyst and sorbent pellets. We evaluate both architectures experimentally over a range of residence times and reactant partial pressures, and we develop mechanistic models to predict water breakthrough time and methane purity. Functionalized sorbent pellets exhibit faster water-transport kinetics and deliver higher methane purity, enabling operation at higher space velocities and lower pressures. The findings indicate that functionalized sorbents are the more efficient materials for sorption-enhanced reactors.

Thermodynamics-electronics synergism in defect passivation enables highly efficient and stable lead-free copper-based halide perovskites
abstract: Defect-induced non-radiative losses currently limit the performance of lead-free Cs3Cu2I5 perovskites. Despite extensive investigations, the identity of the defects responsible for experimentally observed nonradiative recombination remains controversial. Here, combining hybrid-functional first-principles calculations with complementary experiments, we quantitatively identify iodine vacancies (VI) as the dominant nonradiative recombination centers in Cs3Cu2I5. Guided by the elucidated defect-formation mechanism, the introduction of Ga reshapes both the thermodynamic and electronic landscape of Cs3Cu2I5, effectively suppressing the formation of deep-level VI during both nucleation and operation and restoring efficient self-trapped-exciton-mediated radiative recombination. Moreover, the as-formed Ga interstitials chemically diminish metal-halide antibonding coupling and rigidify the Cu-I framework, substantially enhancing resistance to structural decomposition. As a result, Ga-doped Cs3Cu2I5 nanocrystals exhibit significantly enhanced stability and achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield of 95.7%. The resulting deep-blue- and ultraviolet-pumped white light-emitting devices deliver stable emission with a high color rendering index of 95.3 and operational lifetimes exceeding 312 h. Our study unveils the critical but overlooked role of intrinsic electric conductivity characteristics in governing defect formation mechanisms in semiconductors in general. It may also provide a route to enhance the carrier lifetimes and efficiencies of lead-free Cu-based halide perovskites by defect passivation.

title: Scalable room-temperature synthesis of a MOF-based magnetic adsorbent for rapid simultaneous removal of PFAS and micro-nanoplastics
abstract: The growing presence of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and co-pollutants in water poses a major challenge for treatment technologies. MNPs act as vectors that transport PFAS, and metals associated with cancer and systemic health risks, amplifying ecological and human impacts. Most reported sorbents are restricted to micron-scale plastics, rarely achieve submicron capture, and require residence times exceeding 200 minutes, far longer than the 10-60 min windows typical of industrial treatment. Long-chain PFAS remain particularly resistant to capture. We report a magnetically recoverable adsorbent, GDC@FeO@MOF, in which Fe-imidazolate domains are grown directly on carbon-FeO particles at room temperature. This stabilises normally unstable Fe-imidazolates, yielding a nanopillared 2D structure that maximises accessibility and introduces Fe-C/N sites for binding fluorinated surfactants and charged pollutants, while magnetic particles enable rapid recovery. The adsorbent removes >95% of MNPs across 30 nm-8 µm and >85% of PFDA within 60 min. It performs broadly across pollutant classes, with >88% removal of polyester microfibres and dyes from industrial laundry wastewater, which was validated in a 4L prototype using a commercial magnetic separator. Reusability over five cycles and thermal regeneration into a functional magnetic composite confirm durability and circular recovery.

Magnetic droplet carrier robot integrated with AI-fueled on-site detection
abstract: Heavy metal pollution poses urgent threats to environmental and human health, yet existing on-site detection technologies face critical sensitivity limitations and operational constraints in field applications. To overcome these challenges, we pioneer an integrated droplet manipulation-detection system synergising a magnetic droplet carrier robot (MDC-robot) with AI-fueled dynamic analysis. This system establishes an on-site workflow where the MDC-robot leverages a zoned wettability surface and multi-degree-of-freedom magnetic actuation for translation and rotation, enabling lossless 3D droplet manipulation. The Mask RGB-drop (MR) algorithm provides AI-fueled quantification of colorimetric signals during droplet processing. Validated in municipal sludge matrices, the integrated platform achieves a 226% increase in Cu²⁺ detection sensitivity through evaporation-assisted preconcentration, meeting drinking-water quality guidelines. Comparison with standard detection techniques confirms reliability, with recoveries of 96-104% and measurement errors below 7%. The system also delivers significantly improved efficiency, automation, and reduced cost relative to conventional manual detection, which remains the dominant approach in practical environmental diagnostics. It is demonstrated that the AI-fueled, materials-integrated methodology defines a new paradigm for intelligent environmental monitoring.

title: Freeze-drying-free camel-inspired cellulose-based aerogel foam for adaptive building thermal management
Combination of high-throughput droplet radiosynthesizer and design of experiments for efficient radiopharmaceutical optimization
abstract: Radiopharmaceuticals deliver radionuclides to specific biological targets for PET or SPECT imaging or for therapy, enabling rapid and sensitive whole-body assessment or treatment of disease. With the expanding clinical adoption of imaging agents and radiopharmaceutical therapies, there is increasing demand for rapid development of new radiopharmaceuticals targeting emerging biological markers. A major bottleneck in early-stage radiopharmaceutical development is radiosynthesis optimization, which must reliably produce sufficient material for preclinical evaluation and clinical translation. Conventional radiochemistry is labor intensive, limited in throughput, and often requires months of iterative experimentation. Here, we integrate a high-throughput microscale droplet-based radiosynthesis platform with a design of experiments (DoE)–driven closed-loop optimization strategy to accelerate radiochemical development. The platform enables dozens of parallel microscale reactions using 10 μL droplets, while the optimization framework combines D-optimal experimental design with a steepest-ascent method to efficiently explore multidimensional design spaces. Iterative DoE cycles are used to systematically identify optimal reaction conditions with minimal experimental effort. As a proof of concept, we optimized the multi-step synthesis of 3′-deoxy-3′-[ 18 F]fluorothymidine ([ 18 F]FLT), comprehensively investigating seven variables across the fluorination and deprotection steps. Optimal conditions were identified using only two DoE cycles for fluorination and one for deprotection. The optimized microscale synthesis exhibited a final radiochemical yield of 71.2 ± 2.8% ( n = 4) in a synthesis time of 29 min including analytical-scale HPLC purification. This study demonstrates that high-throughput droplet-based synthesis coupled with DoE-guided closed-loop optimization provides an efficient and generalizable strategy for accelerating radiochemistry optimization.

Halite precipitates as porous crystalline networks, not dispersed crystals: Self-enhancing growth mechanisms during CO₂ storage in saline aquifers
abstract: Salt precipitation during CO₂ injection into saline aquifers obstructs flow-controlling pore throats and reduces injectivity, yet reactive transport models assume dispersed, non-porous crystals with negligible fluid flow impact. Here, we demonstrate that halite develops three-dimensional porous networks with 40 ± 15% internal porosity through self-enhancing growth mechanisms. Time-lapse X-ray micro-computed tomography and spectral imaging reveal preferential nucleation at gas-liquid interfaces, where porous hydrophilic aggregates generate capillary suction that draws brine films toward precipitation sites, thereby accelerating growth and expanding the reactive surface area in a positive feedback loop. Spectral tomography identifies two-stage precipitation: dense macrocrystalline cores formed under moderate supersaturation and evaporation, surrounded by microcrystalline overgrowths from rapid late-stage dynamics that produce umbrella-like crusts encapsulating residual brine. This porous architecture explains why modest bulk porosity reduction causes disproportionate permeability decline, as aggregates preferentially obstruct flow percolation pathways rather than uniformly cementing grains or filling pore space. Five interconnected mechanisms drive self-enhancing growth across nano- to centimeter scales: interface nucleation, secondary porous structure formation, steep concentration gradients, hydrophilic substrate film maintenance, and capillary-driven solute delivery. Pore network quantification delivers the first three-dimensional structural characterization of halite growth architecture under GCS-relevant conditions, resolving pore diameter distributions of 20–200 μm, mean coordination numbers of 5, and reactive surface areas averaging 0.04 mm 2 per pore – parameters currently absent from reactive transport models yet essential for predicting injectivity impairment and containment integrity at operational storage scales.

abstract: The design of hierarchical electrode architectures is an effective strategy to improve charge storage kinetics and cycling stability in electrochemical energy storage systems. This work elaborates a hydrothermal synthesis method to develop a nanostructured hybrid electrode with a porous and interconnected morphology, facilitating efficient ion transport and enhanced redox activity. Due to the synergistic combination of fast ion diffusion and abundant electroactive sites, the optimized electrode exhibited a high specific capacitance of 237 F g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 . A symmetric aqueous supercapacitor assembled using the optimized electrode delivers an energy density of 57 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 2000 W kg −1 within a 2 V operating window. In an organic electrolyte system, the device maintains an energy density of 30 Wh kg −1 at an ultrahigh power density of 20,000 W kg −1 , along with excellent long-term stability, retaining 94% of its capacitance even after 100,000 charge-discharge cycles. These findings draw attention to the effectiveness of rationally designed hybrid electrode structures in achieving high energy and power performance, demonstrating their potential for advanced supercapacitor applications.

Fiber-optic SPR sensor based on molecularly imprinted polymers for detection of perfluorooctane sulfonate in water
abstract: Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) is a persistent organic pollutant widely present in aquatic environments, posing a severe risk to human health due to its bioaccumulation and toxicity. To address the urgent need for sensitive on-site detection of PFOS, this study developed a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor based on a multimode-no-core-multimode fiber structure. By immobilizing PFOS- selective molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) onto the gold surface, the sensor achieved good sensitivity and long-term stability. Experimental results show that the proposed sensor has an ultra-low limit of detection (LoD) of 0.84 pg/mL and a wide dynamic linear measurement range from 1 pg/mL to 10 ng/mL (R 2 = 0.9933), outperforming most reported optical/colorimetric PFOS sensors. Furthermore, the sensor exhibited excellent selectivity, satisfactory repeatability (relative standard deviation = 4.63%), and good practical applicability, requiring only simple filtration pretreatment to achieve spiked recovery rates of 79.00%–114.70% in tap and lake water samples. These results highlight the sensor's great potential for on-site PFOS monitoring in complex aquatic environments.

Electronic structure modulation in Co-doped NiFe-LDH for efficient ethylene glycol oxidation in simulated seawater
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste presents a major environmental burden, yet it can serve as a feedstock for value-added chemicals. Here, we report cobalt-doped nickel–iron layered double hydroxides (Co/NiFe-LDH) with tunable Co contents, prepared by a one-step solvothermal route, as efficient electrocatalysts for the ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) in simulated seawater (SW). Among the series, 0.35Co/NiFe-LDH delivers the highest activity, reaching 87.7 mA cm −2 at 1.60 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in simulated SW containing 1 M ethylene glycol (EG), together with a formate faradaic efficiency of 93.8% at 1.60 V. The catalyst also shows strong durability and chloride tolerance, retaining 50.3 mA cm −2 after 6 h of operation and exhibiting robust Cl − resistance. Density functional theory calculations indicate that Co incorporation shifts the d-band center toward the Fermi level, strengthens EG adsorption, and lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining step of the desorption of HCOOH* intermediate, thereby accelerating EGOR kinetics. Notably, the catalyst performs effectively in PET upcycling scenarios by catalyzing EGOR directly in PET hydrolysis products. This work offers a practical strategy to design high-performance, non-precious-metal EGOR catalysts operable in simulated seawater, supporting sustainable plastic waste valorization while reducing freshwater demand.

title: Kinetic investigation of methane pyrolysis over iron-based catalyst in packed bed reactor
abstract: Methane pyrolysis emerges as a promising route to generate high-purity hydrogen and solid carbon without CO 2 emissions. This work investigates the kinetics of methane decomposition over a Fe-Al 2 O 3 catalyst with equimolar Fe/Al ratio, synthesized via fusion-decomposition method and previously identified as the best formulation for activity and carbon accumulation capacity. Experiments were carried out in a packed bed reactor under widely varying operating conditions: temperature (725–800 °C), methane concentration (2.5–95% v /v), gas hourly space velocity (1000–100,000 L(NTP) h −1 kg cat −1 ), and hydrogen co-feeding (0–80% v/v). A one-dimensional dynamic reactor model was applied to develop a predictive kinetic model able to simultaneously describe methane conversion and catalyst deactivation as functions of operating conditions, and local gas-phase and solid phase composition. Specifically, the pyrolysis rate is described with a first-order dependence on methane partial pressure, while catalyst activity is modelled as a declining function of the locally accumulated carbon, a property of the solid that varies spatially and dynamically across the reactor and the time on stream. The model combines formal simplicity with the capability to accurately reproduce methane conversion, hydrogen productivity, and carbon load and distribution under all tested conditions. Surface maps of carbon deposition and catalyst activity across the reactor length could be generated, offering predictive insights valuable for the design of experiments, including strategies for long lasting runs. The results of this study underscore the potential of Fe-based catalysts for CO 2 -free hydrogen production at the industrial scale and provide rate equations validated over an operating field of unprecedented extension, that are expected to enable the scaling up of methane pyrolysis technologies.

Molecular architectures of self-assembling peptides for combating resistant bacteria
abstract: The rapid escalation of antimicrobial resistance has intensified the search for alternative strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. Self-assembling peptides (SAPs) have emerged as a versatile class of antimicrobial materials, capable of forming supramolecular architectures that interact with bacterial membranes, biofilms, and host environments. Rather than acting solely as molecular antimicrobials, SAPs derive their function from architecture-dependent properties, including morphology, charge distribution, and dynamic assembly state. This review critically examines recent advances in SAP design for combating resistant bacteria, with emphasis on the relationship between peptide structure, supramolecular organization, and antibacterial function. We discuss how distinct assemblies modulate membrane disruption, biofilm penetration, intracellular targeting, and antibiotic synergy, while also addressing key translational challenges such as stability, cytotoxicity, and scalability. This review integrates structural principles with biological outcomes to establish a framework in which SAPs are understood as adaptable antimicrobial platforms rather than direct substitutes for traditional antibiotics.

Improving the accuracy of phase distribution measurement with ERT in multiphase flows by correcting fringe-effect artifacts
abstract: 2D Electrical Resistance Tomography (ERT) is widely used for phase distribution measurement in multiphase flows due to its simpler and faster operation compared to 3D ERT. However, 2D ERT suffers from image distortion caused by the fringe effect, in which objects outside the measurement plane are sensed and produce artifacts in reconstructed images. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel boundary measurement correction method that uses only two conventional 2D sensor planes. The core idea is to extract off-plane distribution information from raw measurements based on imaging differences of the same object on two adjacent electrode planes, followed by accurately separating the in-plane measurement components through minimizing differences between dual-plane measurements. By reconstructing images from the corrected measurements, fringe-effect artifacts can be suppressed. Simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of the method. It can suppress fringe artifacts caused by objects of any shape or location outside the measurement plane, achieving significantly better reconstruction quality than 3D tomography with grounded guard electrodes. Experimental results with dynamic objects confirm that the method greatly enhances the fidelity of object contours, counts, and axial distribution, showing promise for reducing systematic errors in phase holdup estimation.

abstract: Herein, we demonstrate that ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) serves as a molecular "expander" to significantly increase the interlayer spacing of organic-modified montmorillonite (OMMT). This structural expansion, driven by the physical binding of vinyl acetate groups within the polymer electrolyte (PE) matrix, bridges isolated conduction channels and reduces crystallinity, thereby facilitating rapid lithium-ion transport as visualized by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The resulting open-framework architecture triggers a three-dimensional nucleation process, promoting the formation of a robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) rich in LiF and Li3N. Consequently, the EVA/LOPPM composite achieves a high tensile strength of 5.56 MPa and a markedly enhanced lithium-ion transference number (tLi+) of 0.72. When paired with LiFePO4 (LFP) cathodes, the solid-state batteries deliver a high discharge capacity of 138 mAh g-1 at 5 C and maintain 106 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles at room temperature, demonstrating superior electrochemical performance and dendrite suppression.

title: Interfacial engineering of upconversion nanoplatforms for optical tracking and overcoming biological barriers in RNAi-based pest resistance management
Tuning CO selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation over CeO2-based high-entropy oxides: Roles of mechanochemical synthesis, entropy-stabilized phases and structural evolution
abstract: High-Entropy Oxides (HEOs) represent a promising class of multifunctional catalysts for direct CO 2 hydrogenation into value-added products. Their capacity to integrate multiple cations into a single lattice, accommodate oxygen vacancies, and stabilize dispersed active sites creates a suitable microenvironment that enhances CO 2 and H 2 reactivity, thereby boosting conversion and selectivity. Herein, a Ce 0.5 (Zn 0.1 Co 0.1 Mg 0.1 Ni 0.1 Cu 0.1 )O x catalyst was successfully synthesized via mechanochemical ball milling. The effects of milling time and calcination temperature (500 and 750 °C) on their structural evolution and catalytic properties were investigated. Physicochemical characterization revealed the formation of a fluorite-type structure with partial incorporation of transition metals into the CeO 2 lattice at 500 °C. Conversely, calcination at 750 °C induced metal exsolution driven by the formation of entropy-stabilized (NiCoCuZnMg)O x domains. These thermally induced structural transformations governed the catalytic performance of both materials. The catalyst calcined at 500 °C (BM-C500) achieved CO 2 conversions of 28–37 % with 75–85 % CO selectivity, whereas the sample calcined at 750 °C (BM-C750) exhibited nearly 100 % CO selectivity across the entire reaction temperature range. Post-reaction characterization revealed the in-situ formation of highly dispersed metallic species (mainly Ni 0 and Cu 0 ) coexisting with a partially preserved oxide matrix, highlighting a key role of dynamic metal–oxide interfacial sites in governing activity and selectivity. Additional experiments using synthesized (NiCoCuZnMg)O x entropy-stabilized oxide (ESO) alone and physically mixed with CeO 2 demonstrated that the catalytic performance cannot be explained by a simple additive effect but seems to arise from the structural integration achieved thanks to the intimated contact allowed by the mechanochemical synthesis of the Ce 0.5 (Zn 0.1 Co 0.1 Mg 0.1 Ni 0.1 Cu 0.1 )O x (BM) catalysts. Long-term stability tests identified one of the samples (BM-4h-C500) as the most robust formulation, sustaining performance with only moderate CO yield attenuation over 100 h on stream. Collectively, the results demonstrate that mechanochemical synthesis is an efficient route for preparing active, highly selective and stable HEOs/CeO 2 catalysts for the reverse Water-Gas Shift (RWGS) reaction.

title: Scalable green-light wavelength-selective organic solar cells for agrivoltaics enabled by a synthetically accessible nonfullerene acceptor
abstract: Ensuring crop productivity while simultaneously generating on-site electricity is a central challenge for sustainable greenhouse operation. Green-light wavelength-selective organic solar cells (GLWS-OSCs) address this need by transmitting blue/red photons for photosynthesis while harvesting green photons for power generation. However, systematic agricultural evaluation has been limited by the difficulty of fabricating large-area GLWS-OSC modules. Here, we report a synthetically accessible non-fullerene acceptor, FNTz-F-CN, enabling scalable production of GLWS-OSC modules. When paired with the donor polymer poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT), cell-sized devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 5.05% while operating selectively in the green spectral region. A comparative scalability analysis shows that the P3HT:FNTz-F-CN system achieves a superior PCE-to-scalability factor metric among representative OSC materials. Optimized ink processing enables roll-to-roll fabrication of meter-scale modules. The P3HT:FNTz-F-CN films exhibit a high green-light wavelength-selective factor of 0.59 and an average visible light transmittance of 51%, supporting photosynthesis as confirmed by strawberry leaf measurements. Importantly, greenhouse crop yield trials conducted under GLWS-OSC modules demonstrate that tomato, sunflower, lisianthus, and spinach yields are comparable to those under control conditions. These findings establish GLWS-OSCs as a scalable and crop-compatible agrivoltaic platform for sustainable greenhouse energy integration.

title: Structural evolution and phase transformation of active sites over Ni-W/Al2O3 catalysts during dry reforming of methane: Tracking W-containing phases and long-term stability in catalytic performance
abstract: In this study, we demonstrated that the structural evolution of tungsten-containing phases during dry reforming of methane (DRM) influenced the catalytic performance and long-term stability of Ni-based catalysts. We investigated the transformation into tungsten carbide (WC) in xWNi@Al catalysts (x = 0, 9, 17, 20, and 31 wt%) to understand how interfacial coupling between Ni and WC, along with the formation of WC defects, contributed to stable catalytic performance. Detailed characterizations revealed that the structural and chemical changes of the active sites were highly dependent on the amount of tungsten loading and the reaction time. The unmodified 0W9Ni@Al catalyst gradually deactivated due to carbon buildup, while the W-modified catalysts exhibited enhanced stability. During the reaction, Ni 17 W 3 phase decomposed into metallic Ni and WC, with neighboring W species also undergoing carburization, leading to the formation of interconnected Ni-WC interfacial domains. WC emerged as the primary active site for CO 2 activation, and the creation of defective WC (WC 1-x ) generated additional oxygen-vacancy sites, thus improving active oxygen production and mobility. This phase transformation in the W-modified catalysts facilitated the continuous reconstruction of new active sites, enhanced CO 2 activation, increased O* generation, and promoted carbon removal, ultimately improving both catalytic performance and catalyst stability.

abstract: Aliphatic alpha, w-dicarboxylic acids (alpha, w-DCAs) are essential monomers for polyesters and polyamides, yet their production remains dominated by energy-intensive and unsustainable chemical routes. This study reports a selfsustained in vitro biotransformation (ivBT) platform that converts renewable fatty acids into alpha, w-DCAs through an enzyme-driven cascade. This system integrates three catalytic modules: an H2O2-dependent cytochrome P450 enzyme MCC for terminal hydroxylation, a bifunctional alcohol dehydrogenase ADH2 for sequential oxidation of alcohol groups to carboxylic acids, and a flavin-bridged catalyst F4 that enables NAD+/NADH cofactor cycling with in situ H2O2 generation. Through enzyme engineering and reaction optimization, 2.06 g/L dodecanedioic acid was produced via a one-pot shake-flask scale reaction, with broad compatibility across even-numbered C8C16 fatty acids. This self-sustained system provides an economically viable route for sustainable alpha, w-DCAs production, establishing a general framework for developing advanced in vitro multi-enzyme catalytic systems.

title: MgO-modified PtSn/Ce-DMSN as an efficient catalyst for oxidative dehydrogenation of propane with carbon dioxide
Polar nanoscale pincers in a robust microporous MOF for selective C2H2 capture from CH4 oxidation mixtures
abstract: Efficient purification of acetylene (C2H2) from methane (CH4) oxidation mixtures is challenging due to the close physicochemical similarity between C2H2 and CO2. Herein, we propose a polar nanoscale pincers strategy to engineer pore microenvironments in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for highly selective C2H2 capture. Guided by this concept, we rationally constructed a microporous MOF, [Zn3(NTA)(μ-OH)(dimatz)2]·2DMF·H2O (NTA-tz-Zn), based on 4,4′,4″-tricarboxytriphenylamine (H3NTA) and 3,5-dimethyl-4H-1,2,4-triazole (dimHatz) ligands. Single-crystal analysis demonstrates that carboxyl groups well positioned within the square channels functionalized as polar nanoscale pincers, enabling interactions with guest gas molecules. Consequently, NTA-tz-Zn exhibits excellent separation performance for C2H2/CO2/CH4 mixtures. The material delivers C2H2 productivities of 23.6 and 20.4 L kg⁻1 (99.5% purity) from binary C2H2/CH4 and C2H2/CO2 mixtures, and one-step recovery of 4.6 L kg⁻1 CH4 as well as simultaneous regeneration of 37.0 L kg⁻1 C2H2 from ternary C2H2/CO2/CH4 mixtures. Notably, the separation performance is well maintained under humid conditions (70% relative humidity), with a stable C2H2 capacity of 11.6 ± 0.1 L kg⁻1 over three cycles. Most notably, the material exhibits exceptional stability and retains its separation performance under humid conditions, thereby strongly highlighting its practical applicability. Molecular simulations confirm that the high density of ordered -COO⁻ moieties from the channels act as polar nanoscale pincers to benefit the efficient separation for C2H2/CO2/CH4 of CH4 oxidation mixtures.

Ba- and Mg-promoted Ni/g-C3N4 for efficient CO2 methanation using in-house data machine learning
abstract: Methanation is one of the solutions for decreasing carbon emissions and synthetic green fuels production, being a potentially large-scale option for CO 2 utilization. However, thermodynamics in conventional reaction conditions limit the CO 2 conversion. In this work, alkaline-earth-metal modified nickel nanoparticles supported on graphitic carbon nitride (g-C 3 N 4 ) were tested in a fixed-bed reactor, being a compelling route for atmospheric CO 2 methanation. The use of g-C 3 N 4 as a support offers a more sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional oxide materials, while maintaining competitive catalytic performance with lower Ni loading and milder activation conditions. The catalysts were synthesized using two synthesis approaches: pre-incorporation and co-impregnation with Ni and Ba or Mg into the g-C₃N₄ lattice. The catalysts were characterised using N 2 physisorption, XRD, H 2 -TPR, CO 2 -TPD, TPR, Raman and XPS. The catalyst, where first incorporating the alkaline-earth metal into the g-C 3 N 4 support (Ni/g-C 3 N 4 -Mg), exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a 17-fold increase in CO 2 conversion (from 3 to 51%) and a substantial enhancement in CH 4 selectivity (from 13 to 94%) compared to the undoped catalyst at 325 °C. The Mg-promoted catalyst has better-dispersed Ni nanoparticles, stronger metal-support interaction, greater proportion of metallic Ni species and more moderate basic sites than Ni/g-C 3 N 4 . Mg incorporation also creates Lewis basic sites and increases overall CO 2 adsorption sites on the eg-C 3 N 4 support. The linked Mg dopant and eg-C 3 N 4 synergy drives high activity and stability for low-temperature CO 2 methanation. The catalyst prepared by pre-incorporating the alkaline-earth Ba into the g-C 3 N 4 (Ni/g-C 3 N 4 -Ba) exhibits degraded textural properties and basicity. The presence of barium promotes the stabilization of ferromagnetic Ni clusters. However, the intense signals from Ni + single sites justify the catalyst's performance. Overall, the increased surface nitrogen concentration and the higher proportion of metallic Ni species are clearly beneficial for CO₂ activation and hydrogenation, underscoring their pivotal role in enhancing catalytic activity. In summary, these results highlight the crucial role of promoter choice in CO₂ hydrogenation catalysts, with Mg or Ba-doped Ni/g-C₃N₄ presenting an effective route for methane synthesis. An in-house dataset (71 CO 2 methanation runs) was used to train a Random Forest model to predict CH 4 yield from six controllable descriptors. The model ranked temperature, metal identity, and support-promoter loading as the main drivers and, through surrogate-based screening, identified an optimum at 350 °C over Ni/g-C 3 N 4 promoted with Mg on the support (CSP = 1.0 mmol) without a metal promoter.

Modular microgel flow reactors for automated glycan synthesis with immobilized enzymes
abstract: Glycans are biomolecules that play roles in numerous biological processes and are becoming increasingly important for applications in biomedicine, nutrition, pharmacy, and research. Their structural diversity makes glycans attractive target molecules, but also poses a challenge in their synthesis. Compared to chemical synthesis, enzymatic glycan synthesis offers various advantages: high regio- and stereoselectivity, the use of mild reaction conditions, and better ecological and economic sustainability. Automated enzymatic glycan synthesis (AEGS) is an essential development step in making defined glycan structures efficiently accessible on a larger scale. Here, we present a modular Mi crogel continuous flow R eactor for A utomated and continuous G lycan synthesis with immobilized E nzymes (MiRAGE). The enzymes are immobilized in microgels, SpyT-agarose particles, or Ni 2+ -IDA beads using different strategies. The immobilized enzymes are integrated into reactor compartments, which are supplied with substrates via a continuous reaction buffer flow. A semipermeable membrane ensures that the enzymes as well as substrates and products are retained in the module, while by-products can be selectively removed via a crossflow stream. The modular design allows several enzymatic reaction steps to be coupled, automating the synthesis of complex glycan structures. To this end, we demonstrate the concept towards the synthesis of the human milk oligosaccharide LNFPIII, Lewis X , blood group-, and Galili epitopes. In addition, we compare the different immobilization techniques and reactor strategies in terms of consistency and yield. MiRAGE represents a robust, scalable, and versatile approach that not only enables the automated synthesis of complex glycans but can also be transferred to other biocatalytic processes. Key points • Immobilization of SpyCatcher-glycosyltransferases on SpyTag agarose and microgels • Embedment of immobilized glycosyltransferases in a continuous flow bioreactor • Enzymatic glycan synthesis with removal of by-products and retention of biocatalysts

Ultra-sensitive self-powered thermogalvanic hydrogel wristband enabled by resistance-gated strategy
abstract: Next-generation human-machine interfaces require energy-sustainable and highly responsive sensing systems. However, most wearable sensors rely on external power supplies and complex signal processing, limiting long-term stability and portability. Here, we propose a self-powered thermogalvanic hydrogel wristband that simultaneously harvests energy from the body-ambient temperature gradient and transduces mechanical deformation into readable electrical signals. The wristband integrates six dual-layer hydrogel patches, each exhibiting high extensibility (534.5%), adaptable modulus (638 kPa), lightweight portability, tunable ionic conductivity, and anti-drying stability for prolonged use. Enhanced sensing is achieved through thermoelectric–mechanical coupling governed by interfacial resistance gating, wherein deformation reduces the resistance barrier and enhances the intrinsic thermoelectric current. This coupling ensures high sensitivity with a response time of merely 40 ms. By integrating deep learning algorithms, the wristband achieves real-time sign language recognition and object authentication with an accuracy exceeding 95%. This work introduces a hybrid strategy for intelligent motion recognition, providing a new insight for sustainable wearable human-machine interaction.

Targeted microbial acclimation and intelligent sensing of diverse livestock wastewater
abstract: Livestock wastewaters impose matrix-specific physicochemical and biological challenges on microbial fuel cell (MFC) biosensors, where uncontrolled microbial variability can affect calibration accuracy and response behavior. Here, we evaluated targeted microbial acclimation as a strategy to shape matrix-dependent anodic biofilm responses. MFC biosensors were systematically acclimated with swine (SW), cattle (CW), and a poultry-manure-derived wastewater matrix (PW) to induce matrix-dependent restructuring of anode biofilms. Following acclimation, for conditioned samples within the tested calibration range, biosensors exhibited strong linear calibration relationships (R2 ≥ 0.97) across 40–280 mg L−1 and improved biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) prediction accuracy, with errors of 6.93% (SW), 11.01% (CW), and 14.49% (PW), which were lower than those obtained before acclimation. Volatile fatty acid (VFA) profiles indicated distinct matrix-dependent response patterns: SW showed more extensive VFA consumption, CW showed propionate and butyrate accumulation consistent with a hydrolysis/fermentation-linked bottleneck, and PW exhibited an acetate-centered response pattern accompanied by reduced voltage at higher loading. Community clustering and network analyses further indicated matrix-associated biofilm restructuring during acclimation. These results indicate that targeted acclimation improved the BOD sensing accuracy of compact MFCs in the tested conditioned livestock-derived matrices, providing a basis for developing matrix-adapted bioelectrochemical sensors for livestock wastewater monitoring.

Effect of mechanical vibration on bubbling and particle migration characteristics in a two-dimensional tapered fluidized bed
abstract: The effects of vertical mechanical vibration on bubbling behavior and particle migration in a tapered fluidized bed were experimentally investigated using a two-dimensional apparatus that enabled direct visualization of bubble motion and particle migration. Glass beads with a mean diameter of 54 μm were used as the fluidizing particles. The vibration frequency was fixed at 40 Hz, and the vibration amplitude was varied to clarify the amplitude-dependent changes in bubbling behavior and particle migration. Non-monotonic trends were observed in the hydrodynamic characteristics of bubbling and particle migration. The minimum fluidization velocity decreased steeply with increasing vibration amplitude up to 0.15 mm and then slightly increased at higher vibration amplitudes. At a given gas velocity, the average bubble diameter in the core region initially decreased with increasing vibration amplitude up to 0.1 mm and subsequently increased with further increases in vibration amplitude. In addition, vibration modified the bubbling behavior by altering the bubble-ascending paths in the core region. The extent of the intrinsic particle-migration region increased with vibration amplitude up to 0.25 mm and then decreased when the vibration amplitude exceeded this value, reflecting changes in the spatial extent of the bubbling region induced by vibration. Both the particle-migration velocity and the particle mass flow rate were strongly influenced by variations in bubble diameter and the intrinsic particle-migration region. Moderate vibration effectively suppressed the formation of stagnant regions near the sidewall, thereby promoting particle migration in the annulus region of the bed, whereas excessively strong vibration induced a secondary particle circulation loop that hindered overall particle circulation. The findings provide practical guidance for selecting optimal combinations of vibration intensity and gas velocity in tapered fluidized beds.

See and destroy bacterial spores: Visual detection and in situ inactivation using a terbium-porphyrin nanoplatform
abstract: Pathogenic bacterial spores present a serious and persistent challenge to public health due to their extreme environmental resilience and potential to cause life‑threatening infections. Current technologies are often limited to either detection or inactivation, creating a critical gap in effective contamination control. To address this, we developed terbium‑tetraphenylporphyrin tetrasulfonic acid nanodiscs (Tb‑TPPS NDs), a multifunctional nanoplatform synthesized via a simple one‑step microwave‑assisted route. By integrating Tb3+ ions and TPPS into a single nanostructure, the platform enables real‑time, dual‑mode (absorbance/fluorescence) visual detection of the spore biomarker dipicolinic acid (DPA) with ultra‑high sensitivity, coupled with efficient photodynamic spore inactivation. The incorporation of Tb3+ enhances intersystem crossing through a heavy‑atom effect and promotes structural rigidification, collectively boosting singlet oxygen generation for effective spore eradication. The system performs reliably in complex media and can be formatted into a portable gel‑based kit, supporting practical on‑site and high‑throughput applications. This “detect‑and‑destroy” approach provides a versatile tool with strong potential in clinical diagnostics, food safety monitoring, and environmental decontamination where rapid, in site response is essential.

title: Engineered norfloxacin-derived carbonized polymer dots for synergistic antibacterial and anti-inflammatory periodontitis therapy
abstract: Oral microecological dysbiosis sustains the chronic inflammation characteristic of periodontitis. Although mechanical debridement with adjunctive antibiotics remains the clinical mainstay, fluoroquinolones often show limited site-specific efficacy because of poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability. Drug-derived carbonized polymer dots (CPDs) have therefore attracted increasing interest for integrating intrinsic pharmacological activity with tunable functional properties. Here, we develop norfloxacin-derived CPDs (NF-CPDs) exhibiting excellent biocompatibility and markedly enhanced antibacterial performance relative to free norfloxacin in planktonic bacterial environments. NF-CPDs preserve the canonical quinolone antibacterial mechanism while establishing a three-dimensional, synergistic inhibition framework spanning metabolism, energy, and bacterial structure. In parallel, NF-CPDs efficiently scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppress pro-inflammatory mediator expression, and attenuate excessive nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling. In vivo, NF-CPDs mitigate alveolar bone resorption and preserve periodontal structural integrity. Collectively, this core–shell NF-CPDs platform enables synergistic antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy, providing a promising strategy for comprehensive periodontitis treatment.

Low-temperature thermochemical energy storage behavior of Zn-doped phosphogypsum-based calcium sulfate dihydrate: Correlating defect evolution with electronic structure
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG), a massive industrial solid waste, consists primarily of calcium sulfate dihydrate (CSD), a promising material for thermochemical energy storage (TCES). However, CSD's high dehydration temperature (~140 °C) limits its compatibility with low-grade industrial waste heat and non-concentrating solar thermal sources. To lower this operating temperature, we introduced Zn²⁺ into a PG-based CSD system using a low water-to-solid ratio, non-equilibrium "dropwise addition–drying" hydration route. Structural and elemental analyses revealed that Zn²⁺ incorporated uniformly without forming independent crystalline phases, inducing an anisotropic unit-cell contraction of ~0.18%.Spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations demonstrated that Zn doping caused broadened coordination environments, nanoscale voids, planar disorder, and rough growth interfaces. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations indicated that Zn–O bonds possess stronger orbital hybridization and higher local stability than Ca–O bonds, acting as the microscopic origin for strain accumulation and defect formation. Consequently, the apparent dehydration peak temperature decreased significantly from 141.5 °C in the undoped control to 73.7–97 °C in the Zn-doped samples. This reduction results from a dual mechanism: altered local bonding destabilizes bulk water molecules, while defect structures enhance water migration kinetics. To ensure cyclic stability and mitigate structural stress, the doped salts were composited with an expanded graphite (EG) matrix. Over 30 ex-situ dehydration–rehydration cycles, the optimal PG-Zn-5.4 composite maintained a dehydration peak of 97.0 °C and a gravimetric energy storage density of 434.1 J g⁻¹. This study highlights transition-metal doping via non-equilibrium crystallization as a robust strategy for tuning low-temperature TCES materials.

Intensifying CO2 desorption in nonaqueous alkanolamines using Fe–N–C heterogeneous catalysts: Kinetics, stability, and mechanistic insights
abstract: High energy consumption during solvent regeneration remains the primary barrier to the widespread deployment of amine-based CO 2 capture. This study presents a synergistic approach by integrating Fe nanoparticles anchored on N-doped carbon spheres (Fe–N–C) with a non-aqueous solvent consisting of 2-(butylamino)ethanol (BAE) and diethylene glycol monomethyl ether (DEGMME). Characterization via XPS and Raman spectroscopy confirmed the presence of active Fe–N x coordination sites and a high density of structural defects (I D /I G = 0.85), which facilitate the catalytic CO 2 desorption. The Fe–N–C catalyst (0.2 wt%) demonstrated profound kinetic enhancement across both aqueous and non-aqueous systems. In aqueous MEA and BAE benchmarks at 90 °C, the catalyst increased CO 2 desorption rates by up to 420%, reducing the relative regeneration heat duty by ~26%. For the BAE/DEGMME nonaqueous system, the catalyst enabled efficient regeneration between 70 and 90 °C, increasing the desorption rate by nearly 380%. Notably, at a reduced temperature of 70 °C, the catalytic nonaqueous system achieved a ~ 73% regeneration efficiency, yielding a ~ 68% reduction in relative heat duty compared to the 30 wt% aqueous MEA benchmark. 13 C NMR and ATR-FTIR speciation analyses confirmed that Fe–N–C facilitates the decomposition of carbamate intermediates, lowering the thermal threshold for CO 2 release. The catalyst exhibited robust structural and functional stability over 20 cycles. This work demonstrates that integrating tailored catalytic surfaces with selected non-aqueous solvents provides a viable pathway for intensifying carbon capture while utilizing low-grade thermal energy.

title: Soft-template synthesis of polypyrrole nanotubes for Ag+ adsorption and subsequent in-situ formation of Ag-AgCl@PPy nanotubes for efficient iodine removal
abstract: The development of multifunctional nanostructured adsorbents is vital for addressing water pollution caused by heavy metals and halogen species. In this work, polypyrrole nanotubes (PPy NTs) were prepared via a soft-template approach using methyl orange as the structure-directing agent and FeCl3 as the oxidant. The resulting PPy NTs exhibited tubular morphology, high surface area, and abundant electron-rich sites, enabling efficient uptake of silver ions (Ag⁺) from aqueous solution. Owing to the intrinsic redox activity and presence of dopant Cl- ions of PPy, the adsorbed Ag⁺ ions were subsequently reduced in-situ to metallic silver and AgCl nanoparticles (Ag-AgCl NPs), yielding well-dispersed Ag-AgCl decorated PPy nanotubes nanocomposite (Ag-AgCl@PPy NTs) without the need for additional reducing or stabilizing agents. The formation of Ag-AgCl@PPy NTs was validated by FTIR, XRD, BET, FE-SEM, HR-TEM-STEM, and XPS, confirming the even distribution of Ag-AgCl NPs across the PPy surface. The hybrid nanocomposites displayed synergistic adsorption that was further exploited for the adsorption of iodine from water. Adsorption experiments in batch mode demonstrated that Ag-AgCl@PPy NTs achieved significantly higher iodine removal efficiency (90.6%) compared to pristine PPy NTs (68.2%), highlighting the role of Ag-AgCl NPs in enhancing halogen sequestration. Maximum adsorption capacity as obtained from Langmuir model was found to be 1481.8 mg/g at 25 °C. Moreover, the nanocomposites exhibited fast removal kinetics and good reusability, underscoring their stability. This dual-functional strategy not only eliminates toxic Ag⁺ ions but also transforms them into value-added hybrid nanomaterials with superior pollutant removal capacity. Overall, Ag-AgCl@PPy NTs emerge as a promising multifunctional adsorbent for sustainable water purification applications.

Asymmetric band engineering for superior multifunctional energy conversion
abstract: Efficient conversion of environmental signals into electrical energy is essential for self-powered devices and sensing technologies. Traditional designs often rely on single-function mechanisms, leading to inefficiencies and scalability issues. In this work, we introduce an asymmetric band engineering strategy that integrates multiple energy conversion pathways within a single composite nanofiber membrane (SCNFM). By exploiting electrode work function differences, the asymmetric energy-level configuration between Al/SCNFM and Cu/SCNFM enhances charge transport and couples thermally induced, humidity-driven, and piezoelectric processes for efficient energy conversion. The SCNFM demonstrates a temperature range of 25–210 °C, humidity detection from 30 to 90% RH, and pressure sensing from 0.5 to 3 N, with stable outputs under varying conditions. Under coupled temperature and humidity stimuli, the device exhibits a 21% voltage enhancement at 70 °C, demonstrating a clear synergistic effect. This design simultaneously converts temperature, humidity, and pressure stimuli into complementary DC and AC signals without external bias, offering a scalable framework for multi-stimulus energy harvesting and self-powered sensing in applications such as flexible electronic skins and wearable health monitors.
