Competitive adsorption–induced non-thermal pseudo-Leidenfrost effect in supercritical CO2 enabling nanoscale dewetting
abstract: During the fabrication of semiconductor chips with micro/nanostructures, wet cleaning processes often lead to water residues trapped within nanostructures, which severely compromise their structural stability. Therefore, a strategy that reduces droplet adhesion without relying on surface structural modification is highly desired. In this work, a novel supercritical CO2-mediated droplet levitation mechanism, termed the pseudo-Leidenfrost effect, is proposed based on the conventional thermally driven Leidenfrost effect. Compared with the thermally driven counterpart, the use of supercritical CO2 significantly reduces energy consumption while forming a denser and more stable vapor cushion. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that this mechanism is dominated by electrostatic interactions between CO2 and H2O, where competitive adsorption of the two species on the surface leads to the formation of a molecular cushion beneath the nanodroplet, thereby enabling droplet levitation. Density functional theory calculations further indicate that the adsorption affinity of CO2 on the surface must be comparable to or greater than that of H2O to ensure the stable emergence of the pseudo-Leidenfrost effect. This work provides a novel low-energy strategy for droplet manipulation, along with atomistic and nanoscale insights into the underlying mechanism.

title: Investigation of high-performance proton exchange membrane fuel cells with integrated bipolar/gas diffusion layer structures: Effects of porosity gradient in tetradecahedral lattice flow field on mass transfer and electrochemical reactions
On-board high purity hydrogen production by ammonia decomposition using a hollow fibre membrane reactor
abstract: Ammonia (NH₃) decomposition is a promising route for on-board hydrogen (H₂) production; however, equilibrium limitations and H₂ inhibition restrict the performance of conventional catalytic packed-bed reactors (PBRs). Here, a catalytic hollow fibre membrane reactor (HFMR) is presented as an effective strategy to overcome these challenges. The reactor consists of a multichannel α-Al₂O₃ hollow fibre support whose outer surface is coated with a defect-free Pd membrane (11–13 μm) via electroless plating, while a Ru/Na–NCX catalyst is packed on the shell side. Electroless plating kinetics showed a linear Pd growth rate of ~3.7 μm·h −1 , and H₂ permeation followed the temperature-dependent solution–diffusion mechanism. The Ru/Na–NCX catalyst contained highly dispersed Ru nanoparticles (~2.5 nm) that remained stable after reaction, while Na promoters stabilised the structure and regulated surface hydrogen coverage. Continuous H₂ removal enhanced NH₃ conversion beyond equilibrium limits within 300–450 °C, achieving 64.5% H₂ recovery at 450 °C. Process analysis for a 100 kW system confirmed feasibility with reduced catalyst demand and no downstream NH₃ purification, highlighting the potential of HFMRs for compact on-board H₂ generation.

A monodisperse model for hetero-aggregate formation in mixing aerosol streams
abstract: A novel population balance equation (PBE) model (hetero-monodisperse) has been developed to describe the growth of hetero-aggregates formed from mixing two or more particle streams. The model extends the monodisperse framework and accounts for various mechanisms critical to hetero-aggregate formation, including binary and unary nucleation, inter- and intra-population coagulation, and condensation, to capture the evolution of hetero-aggregate populations accurately. To assess its accuracy and efficiency, the model is benchmarked against a two-dimensional nodal (sectional) model with the particle volume and composition in a binary hetero-aggregate as primary variables, which was introduced by Shigeta and Watanabe (2010). The results indicate that the new hetero-monodisperse model can predict the dynamics of hetero-aggregation in different material systems with comparable accuracy, while significantly reducing computational complexity: In our benchmark, the computational cost of the hetero-monodisperse model was three to four orders of magnitude lower than for the nodal method (40 bins for particle volume and 57 bins for particle composition). This high efficiency and accuracy make the hetero-monodisperse model a good choice when using CFD to simulate hetero-aggregate dynamics in complex 3D problems.

Dual functional enhancement of H2S gas sensing and fiber dye-sensitized solar cell efficiency using UiO-66 MOFs
abstract: Fiber-based photovoltaic devices are promising power sources for wearable and Internet of Things (IoT) systems. However, improving their efficiency, low-light operability, and multifunctionality remains challenging. To address this issue, this study developed solid-state fiber-shaped dye-sensitized solar cells (SS-FDSSCs) by embedding UiO-66 metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) functionalized with –F and –NH2 groups into a mesoporous TiO2 photoanode via a shrinkage-assisted electric-heating process. The incorporated MOFs enhanced dye loading, accessible surface area, and charge extraction, enabling power conversion efficiencies of 7.16% (UiO-66-F) and 6.63% (UiO-66-NH2), corresponding to 29% and 20% improvements over pristine devices, respectively. Devices modified by UiO-66-F and UiO-66-NH2 exhibited significantly improved low-light performance and effective carrier collection without additional recombination losses. Such devices maintained mechanical robustness, preserving approximately 70% of the initial efficiency even after 1500 bending cycles and > 80% of the initial efficiency after 20 washing cycles. Moreover, the incorporation of UiO-66-F endowed the fiber device with strong H2S gas-sensing capability, which was absent in the pristine TiO2 device. These results show that ligand-functionalized UiO-66 effectively enhances both energy harvesting and gas sensing in fiber devices, advancing their potential for next-generation wearable systems.

Experimental evaluation of 3D printed metal monolithic adsorption bed with fast heat transfer rate for CO2 separation
abstract: Efficient heat removal and low flow resistance are critical for adsorption-based CO 2 separation, because the heat of adsorption increases the adsorbent temperature and thereby lowers the capacity. Although monolithic structures are widely used for their low pressure drop and mechanical robustness, their role as thermally active adsorption beds has remained largely unexplored. Here, a relatively small (50 mm ×10 mm) 3D-printed aluminium alloy (Al-10Si-0.4Mg) monolith was used to construct an adsorption module (Al-MON) coated with HKUST-1 adsorbent and was experimentally investigated and benchmarked against a conventional packed-bed (PB) configuration under identical operating conditions. Temperature measurements during adsorption at different locations demonstrated rapid and spatially more uniform heat dissipation in the metal monolith with minimal temperature gradients within 0.5 °Celsius between the adsorbent and the module’s surface while also showing significantly faster thermal equilibration compared to the packed bed configuration. Breakthrough curves remained sharp across different inlet CO 2 concentrations, 50 % and 100 %, and flow rates, 100 sccm and 200 sccm, indicating effective mass transfer and low axial dispersion through the column despite the presence of straight-channels in the monolithic geometry. In the present experiments, heat removal from the module surface was limited, and the results suggest that faster heat removal may further shorten the adsorption time. A CFD-based analysis confirmed that the presented Al-MON design retains the inherently low pressure drop characteristic of monolithic structures relative to packed beds.

La-promoted Ru/ZrO2 catalysts: Insights about catalytic performance and active site for CO2 methanation
abstract: The establishment of a carbon-neutral society is one of humanity's top priorities. However, the inertness of CO 2 imposes a barrier for its transformation to distinct added-value products at appreciable reaction rates. Therefore, catalysts with improved properties must be developed. Herein, 0.4 wt% Ru catalysts supported on ZrO 2 and La promoted ZrO 2 with different La loadings were prepared by wet impregnation and systematically investigated for CO 2 methanation. Catalytic testing showed that La incorporation enhanced activity, with 0.4Ru/1.5La-ZrO 2 achieving the highest CH 4 formation rate, while maintaining 100% CH 4 selectivity and stable conversion over 72 h. The structural and surface properties of the catalysts were examined by ex-situ techniques (BET, CO 2 -TPD, H 2 -TPR, XPS). Complementary in-situ studies provided mechanistic insights. EPR showed that La stabilized Ru 3+ species that were gradually reduced into active Ru 0 /Ru + clusters during reaction. In-situ DRIFTS analysis revealed adsorbed CO on Ru sites as the main reaction intermediate, with formates and carbonates acted as spectator species, and demonstrated that 1.5 wt% La optimized intermediate coverage, whereas higher La loadings diminished CO adsorption and surface-accessible Ru. The combined ex-situ and in-situ characterization demonstrated that tuning La loading is important to balance basicity and metal-support interactions, offering clear design strategy for efficient and stable Ru-based CO 2 methanation catalysts.

Synergistic regulation of bimetallic d-band centers in NiM-NiMOx (M = Co/Cu) catalysts toward enhancing selective hydrogenation
abstract: To address the long-standing challenge of inadequate synergy between bimetallic d-band center regulation and strong metal-support interaction (SMSI), coupled with weak interfacial integration in conventional alloy-oxide catalysts, this study reports the in situ integrated construction of a NiM-NiMOₓ (M = Co, Cu) bimetallic-oxide catalytic system. Lewis acid sites from metal cations in oxide phases have electron density modulated by SMSI-induced interfacial electron transfer for enhanced reactant anchoring. Under SMSI modulation, the heterointerfaces induce significant charge redistribution, synergistically tailoring the d-band centers of metal active sites to -1.30/-1.34 eV (Ni/Co) for NiCo-NiCoOₓ and -1.23 eV/-1.13 eV (Ni/Cu) for NiCu-NiCuOₓ. For the selective hydrogenation of cinnamaldehyde, NiCo-NiCoOₓ achieves high C=C bond hydrogenation selectivity, while NiCu-NiCuOₓ exhibits superior activity under mild conditions. Kinetic studies show the two catalysts follow first-order kinetics with apparent activation energies of 26.9 kJ·mol⁻¹ and 61.7 kJ·mol⁻¹, respectively. The differences in catalytic performance and reaction kinetics are essentially attributed to the optimized d-band center regulation: the more favorable d-band center in the NiCu-based system promotes H₂ activation and reaction kinetics, while the moderate d-band center in NiCo-NiCoOₓ favors selective C=C bond hydrogenation. The in situ integrated construction of alloy-oxide interfaces provides an effective strategy for synergistically amplifying bimetallic effects and SMSI, with d-band center regulation as the core to overcome the activity-selectivity trade-off in selective hydrogenation reactions.

Covalent Heterointerface engineering: Bridging electronic conductivity and molecular anchoring for robust sodium storage in CuFeS2@CNT anodes
abstract: Conversion-type anode materials for sodium-ion batteries face two major challenges: severe volume expansion and polysulfide shuttling. Conventional physically mixed interfaces cannot maintain structural stability. Here, we propose a covalent heterointerface engineering strategy to in situ construct C-S covalent bonds between carbon nanotubes (CNT) and chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) via a solvothermal method. Spectroscopic characterization and theoretical calculations confirm that these covalent bonds act as strongly coupled ”electronic bridges” to induce a built-in electric field, significantly enhancing charge transfer kinetics. They also serve as efficient ”molecular anchors” that strongly immobilize polysulfides through chemisorption. As a result, the CuFeS2@CNT composite provides mechanical stress buffering at the physical level and suppresses the shuttle effect at the chemical level. The electrode exhibits outstanding sodium storage performance, retaining 94.4% of its initial capacity after 1500 cycles at a high current density of 5 A g-1. This study offers a new paradigm for the rational design of metal sulfide anodes, moving from ”physical confinement” toward ”chemical integration.”

title: Photoactivation engineering enables the dynamic evolution of Cu0-VO associates over Cu-MgO catalysts for efficient photothermal reforming of methanol into hydrogen
Enhanced magneto-mechano-electric conversion with an arc-shaped piezoelectric cantilever for wireless sensor networks
abstract: Magneto-mechano-electric energy harvester (MME-EH) is one of the prospective candidates for powering autonomous Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks by converting ambient magnetic noise into electrical energy. However, conventional flat-shaped MME-EHs face challenges in effectively harvesting energy from the axially symmetric magnetic field surrounding long, straight power cables. In this work, we develop an arc-shaped MME-EH fabricated through monolithic bonding of flexible lead-free piezoelectric polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) polymer onto arc-shaped Ni cantilevers, with NdFeB magnets attached as proof masses. Theoretical analysis, simulation, and experimental results reveal that the arc-shaped MME-EH exhibits a 74% enhancement in output performance compared to its flat-shaped counterpart. Owing to improved strain distribution and elevated electric potential of the arc-shaped PVDF, the optimized device delivers a stable output voltage of 26.2 V, corresponding to a power density of 57 mW m-2 under a 7 Oe alternating magnetic field excitation at the 50 Hz target resonance. Furthermore, a prototype PVDF-based MME-EH is showcased as a persistent power supply for a wireless sensor network, highlighting its potential for large-scale IoT applications.

abstract: The strong ionic nature of Pb2+ enables facile coordination with solvent molecules in solution, which tends to induce the formation of δ-FAPbI3 and vacancy defects. To address this issue, a multifunctional polymer additive, poly(isobutylene-alt-maleic anhydride) (PIMA), was introduced to regulate the crystallization process of FA-based perovskites. Owing to its zigzag molecular structure, PIMA strongly coordinates with PbI2 through a chelation effect, effectively suppressing the formation of the PbI2·solvent complex phase while strengthening the hydrogen-bonding interaction between the solvent and FA+. This modulation promotes a transformation in the formation pathway of FA-based perovskites from PbI2-coordination-dominated synthesis to FAI hydrogen-bond-guided crystallization. The incorporation of PIMA significantly lowers the formation energy of FA perovskites, extending the processing window of the perovskite wet film during blade coating from <1 min to over 10 min. Meanwhile, the spontaneous migration of long-chain PIMA molecules toward interfaces enables effective passivation of surface and interfacial defects in the perovskite film, reducing the trap density (Nt) from 8.68×1015 cm-3 to 3.52×1014 cm-3. As a result, perovskite solar cells fabricated via blade coating achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) exceeding 25% for a 0.09 cm2 device and over 20% for a 7.5 cm2 perovskite mini-module. The small-area devices retain more than 95% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of continuous light soaking.

title: Pyridinic nitrogen enables azo compound with capacity-stability trade-off for high-energy aqueous zinc batteries
abstract: Azo compounds with N=N groups have been employed in rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries owing to high theoretical capacity derived from two‐electron redox reaction. However, their cycling stability remains inadequate due to the high solubility of organic small molecules and discharge products in aqueous electrolytes. Herein, we designed π-conjugated azo small molecule (azobenzene (AZB) and 4,4'-azopyridine (AZPY)) with stable two-electron transfer but slight differences in aromatic moieties as cathode materials for aqueous zinc-organic batteries. Although the electron-rich pyridinic nitrogen atoms render AZPY soluble in water, they readily react with Zn2+ in the electrolyte to form stable metal-organic complexes and act as electronegative acceptors to generate extensive intermolecular hydrogen-bonding networks. The multifunctional roles of pyridinic N endow AZPY with unconventional ”dissolved but more stable” behavior. AZPY hosted in hierarchical porous carbon (HPC) delivers high specific capacity of 382.1 mAh g-1 and stable cycling for 20,000 cycles at high current density. Furthermore, the electron-withdrawing pyridinic N atoms modulate the electron cloud density near the N=N groups and elevate the discharge voltage, enabling Zn||AZPY/HPC cell to achieve high energy density of 349.3 Wh kg-1. The proton-insertion mechanism and dynamic evolution of interfacial structures of azo-based cathodes were verified by density functional theory (DFT) calculations and ex situ characterizations. This work reconciles the capacity-stability trade-off of organic cathodes by modulating the structure-performance relationship, opening new avenue toward high-energy and prolonged-life aqueous organic batteries.

Multiscale solvation-electronic regulation strategy toward stable Zn anode
abstract: The practical advancement of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) is impeded by the intrinsic trade-off between suppressing parasitic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and maintaining fast Zn 2+ kinetics. Herein, we propose a synergistic anion-cation regulation strategy to achieve long-cycling AZIBs using Choline Iodide (ChI) as a bifunctional additive. The atomic-level decoupling mechanism is elucidated by synchrotron radiation X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and density functional theory (DFT). Specifically, ChI acts as an integrated interfacial regulator that facilitates Zn 2+ desolvation, weakens Zn-adsorbate interactions, and promotes the formation of a Zn I inorganic SEI. These coupled effects accelerate Zn plating kinetics while mitigating HER and other parasitic side reactions. Benefiting from this “liquid-solid” dual regulation, the Zn anode exhibits an ultralong lifespan exceeding 11,110 h (>462 days) and over 600 h under 85.47% DOD. Furthermore, full cells coupled with MnO 2 and NH 4 V 4 O 10 cathodes demonstrate outstanding cycling stability, retaining 95.6% (1500 cycles) and 87.5% (1000 cycles) capacity, respectively. Notably, practical pouch cells with a high mass loading of 8.83 mg cm −2 operate stably for over 100 cycles without swelling. This work provides insights into the coupled regulation of interfacial electronic properties and Zn 2+ solvation, offering a feasible strategy for stabilizing AZIBs.

Assessment of bacterial communities and prediction of their metabolic functions in vegetation-activated sludge process treating landfill leachate
abstract: Optimizing the structure and function of microbial communities is crucial in the design and operation of treatment systems, particularly because the species composition of biomass determines the metabolic pathways, which ultimately impacts the treatment quality. As the impact of landfill leachate (LL) on microbial communities in treatment systems remains poorly understood, this study aimed to analyze the composition of bacterial communities and their variability over time in vegetation-activated sludge process (V-ASP) and modified ASP systems. The predicted metabolic functions of microorganisms and their relationship with nitrogen removal from LL were also determined. Treatment efficiency was associated with the composition of microbial communities. The dominant bacterial phyla in all the treatment systems were Pseudomonadota and Bacteroidota. This study confirmed that landfill leachate supports a unique microbiome that is distinct from other microbiomes. The most abundant bacterial phylum in the LL was Patescibacteria, which reached a maximum abundance of over 30%. However, only a small proportion of Firmicutes (from 1.6% to 3.2%) was recorded in the LL. Biofilms on plant roots favored the occurrence of aerobic denitrifying microorganisms, such as Halomonas, which reached an abundance of up to 20% and may be linked to increased nitrogen removal efficiency. Functional prediction based on PICRUSt2 and KEGG indicated that dissimilatory nitrate reduction and denitrification were the dominant predicted nitrogen-related pathways in all treatment variants, with the highest abundance in Phase II. Microbiological characterization provides new information to help understand the role of bacteria involved in LL treatment and is important for its management.

Sustainability assessment of international LOHC-based hydrogen supply chains: integration of social into environmental and techno-economic perspectives
abstract: The emerging global green hydrogen economy may reproduce asymmetric trade patterns, where the Global South acts as a producer while bearing socio-environmental burdens, and the Global North benefits from decarbonization. Current research focuses predominantly on techno-economic and environmental aspects, leaving a gap in the social and integrated sustainability assessment of global hydrogen supply chains. This study addresses this gap through a life cycle sustainability assessment of hydrogen transport using a liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC). A baseline Namibia-Germany scenario is analysed together with six alternative configurations varying production locations and transport routes. The results show that geographical configuration determines sustainability performance, generating trade-offs between environmental, economic, and social dimensions. Production emerges as the dominant hotspot across all pillars. Environmentally, a tension is identified between climate change mitigation and material resource depletion, largely driven by electricity supply, dehydrogenation heat demand, and PGM-catalyst use. Sensitivity analyses using a low-carbon heat and recycled Pt confirms that these trade-offs persist despite reducing dehydrogenation and catalysts-related impacts. Economically, costs vary across regions and are primarily driven by regional energy prices, with limited influence of discount rate variations on cost trends. Socially, the results show strong geographical differences in social risk profiles, with higher values in the Namibian production route than in European configurations. Three strategic pathways emerge: cost-competitive routes with socio-environmental impacts, sustainability-oriented routes with higher costs, and balanced configurations. Overall, the results highlight how the sustainability of LOHC-based hydrogen supply chains depends strongly on geographical configuration and may involve burden-shifting across sustainability dimensions.

abstract: The urgent demand for trace NO2 detection calls for innovative strategies to address the inherent limitations of metal oxide semiconductors (MOS), such as relatively small specific surface area and insufficient active sites. Herein, a structural-size-catalytic (SSC) synergistic effect was established by introducing Ni ions into the In2O3 using a metal-organic framework (MOF) templating method. This strategy intrinsically couples catalytic regulation with electronic structure modulation to optimize charge transport, while maximizing active sites through precise control over nanocrystal size and porosity. The optimized In2O3-6Ni sensor achieves a high response of 158.9 (2.5 ppm) and low limit of detection (LOD) of 25 ppb to NO2 at 50 oC, improved anti-interference capability and moisture resistance. The practical application is further validated by integration into a microcontroller-based NO2 alarm system. Experiments and simulations collectively verify the performance enhancement mechanism and validate the SSC effect as a universal design strategy for high-performance gas-sensing materials.

abstract: Polyurethanes and their derivatives are versatile segmented polymers with tunable chemical structures and mechanical properties for broad applications. However, conventional polyurethanes typically rely on non-renewable segments and exhibit limited damage tolerance and poor degradability. Herein, we constructed a series of mechanically tunable, damage-tolerant, and biodegradable polycaprolactone (PCL)-based poly(urethane-amide)s (PCL-PUA) via polyadditions using PCL diols of varying molecular weights (Mn 530-4000 g/mol) as soft segments, aliphatic and aromatic diamide-diol chain extenders and hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) as hard segments. Both chain extenders were chemically recycled from post-consumer plastics, promoting recycled feedstock utilization. By systematically tuning soft-segment length and hard-segment composition, these PCL-PUA materials displayed regulated microphase separation behavior and distinct microphase-separated morphologies, leading to a transition in mechanical behavior from elastomeric to plastic characteristics. The optimized PCL-PUA achieved a high tensile strength (55.1 ± 1.8 MPa), an exceptional toughness (497.3 ± 13.6 MJ/m3), and outstanding crack tolerance ability for material durability. In addition, the PCL-PUA materials exhibited enzymatic degradability for end-of-life option and great potentials in cushioning layer and adhesive applications. This work provides a framework for the design of tough and sustainable polyurethane-based materials by regulating segmental composition and upcycling post-consumer plastics.

A green aqueous phase impregnation strategy towards hydrophobic materials for efficient oil-water separation
abstract: To overcome the reliance on organic solvents and associated process limitations in conventional hydrophobic functionalization, this study established an aqueous impregnation hydrophobic functionalization strategy for constructing bio-based composites. The synthesized vanillic acid-furfurylamine benzoxazine monomer (VF) is soluble in sodium hydroxide aqueous solution, thereby establishing an aqueous impregnation hydrophobic functionalization system. Employing an aqueous impregnation hydrophobic functionalization strategy, melamine foam (MF) underwent surface hydrophobic modification without the use of organic solvents, yielding the composite material P(VF/MF). The rigid aromatic structure of P(VF) and its phenolic hydroxyl groups form stable intermolecular hydrogen bonds with the amino nitrogen atoms in the MF framework. This enhances the adhesion stability of the modified layer on the substrate surface, thereby improving selectivity and efficiency during oil-water separation. Furthermore, this aqueous impregnation hydrophobic functionalization strategy can be extended to various typical hydrophilic substrates (paper samples, fabric, and poplar), all achieving significant hydrophobicity, verifying the method's universality. The hydrophobic enhancement effect on the porous MF framework was particularly pronounced, demonstrating the strategy's high adaptability to porous materials. Leveraging advantages such as aqueous processing, environmental sustainability, and simplified procedures alongside stable oil-water separation performance, P(VF/MF) demonstrates considerable application potential in scenarios including oily wastewater treatment and emergency oil spill recovery.

Coupling microalgal luxury uptake with hydrothermal carbonization for producing a phosphorus-rich slow-release fertilizer
abstract: Phosphorus (P) is essential for plant metabolism, yet global reserves are declining due to overexploitation of non-renewable rock phosphate, necessitating sustainable recovery strategies. Municipal wastewater, despite its low P levels (5–20 mg/L), offers a viable source for P recycling. Microalgae can sequester P via “luxury uptake”, but this process requires elevated P availability and yields biomass where P is predominantly present in organic and polyphosphate forms, limiting its direct agronomic availability. In this study, luxury P uptake was induced in C. vulgaris through sequential cultivation under P-normal (19.1 mg P/L), P-starvation, and high P-replenishment (48.9 mg P/L) conditions, resulting in a biomass P content of 66.5 ± 3.6 mg P/g, approximately 4-fold higher than under normal conditions. Hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) was subsequently employed to convert organic and polyphosphate P into inorganic and metal-bound P complexes (Ca P and Fe/Al-P). Under optimized HTC conditions (180 °C, 2 h), a hydrochar yield of 56.6 ± 3.1% was obtained with a P content of 103.3 ± 4.8 mg P/g, representing a 1.5-fold enrichment relative to the biomass. When applied as a fertilizer, the P-rich hydrochar exhibited slow-release behaviour, releasing 48.9 ± 3.3% of P over 60 days following the Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetic model, and achieved a P utilization efficiency of 40.7 ± 2.5% in mung bean plants, outperforming chemical fertilizer. This integrated microalgae-HTC approach demonstrates an effective waste-to-resource pathway for producing P-rich algal hydrochar as a slow-release fertilizer, minimizing P losses to groundwater, and enhancing plant uptake efficiency compared to chemical fertilizers.

Multi-site synergistic network-regulated succinonitrile gel polymer electrolyte for lithium metal batteries
abstract: Succinonitrile (SN), a plastic-crystal electrolyte component with favorable ion-transport capability and thermal stability, has attracted increasing interest for safer lithium metal batteries (LMBs). However, side reactions between SN and lithium metal can cause interfacial instability and deteriorated cycling performance. Although anchoring strategies have been used to restrict SN migration, their ability to simultaneously regulate ion transport remains limited. Herein, a multi-site synergistic network-regulated succinonitrile-based gel polymer electrolyte (NR-SNGPE) is developed through in situ crosslinking polymerization of pentaerythritol tetraacrylate and 2-amino-4,4,4-trifluorobutyl acrylate. The resulting polymer network helps regulate SN molecular motion and Li+ transport, thereby reducing SN migration and alleviating interfacial side reactions. Meanwhile, the cooperative coordination between polymer functional sites and nitrile groups contributes to more continuous Li+ transport pathways. As a result, NR-SNGPE delivers an ionic conductivity of 1.50 mS cm-1 and a Li+ transference number of 0.62, along with improved oxidative and thermal stability. Li||Li symmetric cells using NR-SNGPE operate stably for over 1400 h, and Li||NR-SNGPE||NCM811 full cells retain 80.43% of their capacity after 350 cycles at 1 C. This study demonstrates a feasible strategy for coordinating interfacial stabilization and ion transport regulation in semi-solid-state LMBs.

Preparing large number of ultrafine microdroplets using annular ejector
abstract: Ultrafine microdroplets are popular in many liquid-liquid heterogeneous systems. This study systematically examined droplet generation in an annular ejector at low-pressure of 0.05 MPa to address the structural complexity and high energy consumption associated with traditional liquid-liquid dispersion devices. The findings reveal that the Sauter mean diameter (d32) demonstrates a non-monotonic relationship with the continuous phase Reynolds number (Re), while it increases monotonically with the dispersed phase volume ratio (φ). A dynamic equilibrium was attained after a specific circulation period, resulting in a stabilized d32 2.0 μm. The optimal structural parameters were determined as follows: A mixing chamber length (L = 80 mm) and diameter (D = 7.5 mm) yielding a d32 of 2.25 μm, and a diffusion section angle of 30º producing a d32 of 2.4 μm. Therefore, a theoretical foundation for optimizing annular ejectors is provided, offering significant guidance for the dsevelopment of energy-efficient, large-scale microdroplet production.

A mineralizable and electroactive periosteum for promoting infected bone defect repair by remodeling the osteogenic microenvironment
abstract: The clinical management of infectious bone defects a formidable challenge. Existing periosteal substitutes do not actively modulate the dysregulated defective microenvironment or orchestrate a temporally ordered regenerative cascade. Therefore, an electroactive periosteum with an in situ–mineralized architecture, denoted as PCL/ZnO@PDA/HA (PZPH), is developed. This construct comprises a poly(ε-caprolactone) fibrous core incorporating piezoelectric ZnO, while a hydroxyapatite shell is formed on the surface via polydopamine-mediated biomimetic mineralization. The PZPH periosteum exhibits intelligent, stage-dependent regulatory functions during bone repair. In the early anti-infective phase, piezocatalysis generates reactive oxygen species and synergizes with sustained Zn²⁺ release to confer robust antibacterial efficacy. During the subsequent regenerative phase, PZPH promotes M2 polarization in macrophages, enhances tube formation by endothelial cells, and facilitates osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells. In a model of infected bone defect, PZPH-ultrasound stimulation effectively reconstructs a pro-regenerative microenvironment by enhancing angiogenesis and eliciting a regenerative immune response. Mechanistic investigations further reveal that these therapeutic effects are closely associated with Piezo1/Ca²⁺/CaMKII/PI3K–Akt signaling pathway activation. In conclusion, our findings propose a viable integrated therapeutic approach for infectious bone defects, while establishing an experimental basis for designing advanced, wirelessly controlled electroactive implants to support bone regeneration.

Multifunctional drug-loaded cement for microenvironment remodeling to promote osteoporotic bone regeneration in Kümmell's disease
abstract: Kümmell's disease (KD), a severe complication of osteoporotic vertebral fracture, presents significant treatment challenges due to its pathological osteoporotic microenvironment. Here, we developed a multifunctional biomaterial scaffold designed to reverse this hostile milieu. The scaffold, composed of MgO, β-TCP, and CaHPO₄, demonstrated robust biocompatibility and mechanical strength adequate for vertebral support. To augment its bioactivity, we co-loaded oleanolic acid (OA) and chondroitin sulfate A (CSA). Through a combination of omics analysis and molecular docking, we identified that OA exerted its effects by binding to key target proteins. In vitro, the scaffold significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and suppressed osteoclastogenesis by inhibiting RANKL-induced PI3K-AKT and MAPK signaling pathways, thereby rebalancing bone metabolism. Furthermore, it enhanced angiogenesis via promoted endothelial cell migration and lumen formation, and modulated the immune microenvironment by polarizing macrophages and alleviating oxidative stress. In a rat model of KD, implantation of the scaffold resulted in significantly increased vertebral bone density and reconstructed trabecular structures, as confirmed by Micro-CT and histology, demonstrating successful bone repair and microenvironmental reprogramming. This work establishes a promising therapeutic strategy for KD by leveraging a multifunctional scaffold that provides mechanical support while actively reversing the underlying pathological microenvironment.

title: Simultaneous interlayer engineering and interface modulation of MXene via zirconium nanoclusters for enhanced lithium storage
abstract: Layered MXenes have garnered attention as promising anode materials for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) due to their high electrical conductivity, tunable interlayer spacing, and versatile surface functional groups. However, the practical applications are greatly impeded by sluggish ion transport kinetics, primarily resulting from the issue of self-restacking and the presence of strong electronegative surface terminations. Herein, we simultaneously address these challenges by anchoring zirconium atomic clusters (Zr ACs) onto MXene nanosheets via a wet-chemical approach. The optimized material exhibits a high specific capacity of 588.6 mAh g-¹ at 0.1 A g-¹ (over three times than that of pristine MXene) along with outstanding rate capability (191.6 mAh g-¹ at 2 A g-¹) and cycling stability (an average capacity decay of ~0.10% per cycle over 1000 cycles). Notably, it even retains a capacity of 75.4 mAh g-¹ at 0.2 A g-¹ over 100 cycles at −10 °C. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that Zr ACs not only expand the interlayer spacing of MXene nanosheets but also modulate the surface termination chemistry, thereby enhancing reversible Li⁺ adsorption and surface pseudocapacitance. This work underscores a tunable strategy to balance surface chemistry and interlayer structure of MXenes, pushing their applications forward in high-performance energy storage systems.

Study on the upcycling recovery of waste PBAT to PBS via two-step process of electrochemical oxidation and ionic liquid catalysis polymerization
abstract: A widely applied biodegradable plastic, polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT), may even cause severe environmental pollution and resource waste. In this work, a novel Mn3Cr3Mo1 catalyst supported on nickel foam was synthesized via hydrothermal method, which could effectively convert waste PBAT plastic into high-value succinic acid (SA) through electrocatalysis of PBAT hydrolysate-1,4-butanediol (1,4-BDO), and a current density of 200 mA cm-2 at a voltage of 1.53 V (vs. Reversible Hydrogen Electrode (RHE)) with a Faradaic efficiency as high as 98.0% was obtained. Experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed the catalytic active sites and the oxidation reaction mechanism of 1,4-BDO to SA. Furthermore, the higher-valuable poly (butylene succinate) (PBS) plastic was synthesized via thermal polymerization using 1,4-BDO from PBAT hydrolysis and SA from electrocatalysis, with ionic liquids as catalysts. We simultaneously addressed the challenges of PBAT waste disposal and reduction of PBS preparation cost, which breaks through the limitations of traditional degraded utilization of plastic recycling, and achieved the upgraded conversion of pollutants. This work proposes an upcycling strategy for the recycling and utilization of waste plastics through catalytic conversion followed by polymerization regeneration.

title: Ammonia-based direct reduction of iron ores: Modelling and experimental assessment
abstract: The iron and steel industry is a cornerstone of the EU economy, producing materials essential to various industrial sectors but contributing approximately 5% of the EU's total CO 2 emissions. Among the most promising pathways for decarbonising the steel industry is the adoption of Direct Reduced Iron (DRI) technology, particularly hydrogen-based DRI (H 2 -DRI), which has the potential to eliminate CO 2 emissions during the most carbon-intensive stage of steel production by using hydrogen as a reducing agent instead of fossil fuels. However, hydrogen's low volumetric energy density and the complexity of its transport and storage present practical limitations to large-scale deployment. In this context, ammonia emerges as a compelling alternative energy carrier, thanks to its higher volumetric density, established logistics infrastructure, and the ability to decouple hydrogen production from its point of use. This work investigates the feasibility of ammonia-driven DRI (A-DRI) by combining thermodynamic analysis, kinetic modelling, and experimental characterisation of porosity and phase evolution during hydrogen reduction. A reactor-scale model based on the Unreacted Shrinking Core (USC) framework is developed to quantify the coupled effects of temperature, gas composition, and mass-transfer resistances, while ex-situ measurements establish correlations between metallisation, pore structure, and diffusion behaviour. Results show that ammonia can be integrated into a shaft furnace without altering the fundamental reduction pathway: in-furnace cracking on metallic iron efficiently releases hydrogen, whereas ammonia itself does not participate directly in iron-oxide reduction. Although its use increases the thermal load, appropriate gas-recirculation strategies enable operating conditions compatible with existing H 2 -DRI designs. Overall, A-DRI may provide a promising route to low-carbon ironmaking while mitigating the infrastructural barriers associated with large-volume hydrogen supply.

A fountain pen strategy for writing flexible electronics with low-temperature chemical reactive silver ink
abstract: Ink printing has emerged as a cost-effective method for fabricating high-performance flexible temperature sensors in wearable healthcare, electronic skins, disaster prevention, and human-machine interaction applications. However, challenges still remain in conventional ink printing due to the high processing temperature necessary for high conductivity and fine feature resolution, which limit the performance of printed sensors. To address these challenges, we develop a fountain pen direct writing technique that exploits the precision position control of the microcapillary to write high-performance flexible temperature sensors at a low processing temperature as 60 °C. The printed patterns exhibit a high resolution of 1 μm, excellent conductivity of 1.6×107 S m-1, and broad substrate compatibility, enabling personalized customization of flexible electronics. The resulting sensor demonstrates enhanced sensitivity, a rapid response time, and excellent long-term stability, owing to the low-defect silver conductive network and fine feature resolution. Furthermore, the sensor can be employed for monitoring human body temperature and respiration under different physiological conditions, as well as for thermal management in energy storage systems and electronic devices. The proposed technique opens up a general and scalable pathway for developing high-performance flexible electronics.

Kinetic modelling of methane conversion in DBD plasma-catalysis under quasi-isothermal conditions
abstract: Steam methane reforming (SMR) is the primary industrial route for hydrogen production, traditionally driven by thermal catalysis, whereas plasma-catalysis offers an electrified alternative capable of modifying reaction energetics by non-thermal conditions. However, quantitative kinetic analyses under controlled plasma-surface operation remain limited. This work provides the first experimental kinetic study of methane conversion by DBD plasma-catalysis, designed to isolate the plasma contribution from thermal effects. A total of 80 experiments were conducted over a Ni/Al2O3 catalyst under quasi-isothermal and differential conversion conditions (<15%), varying plasma power (20–35 W), CH4/H2O ratio (0.1–10), and incorporating products to the feed (CO, CO2 and H2). The methane consumption rate (rCH4) exhibited an Arrhenius-type dependence with respect to specific energy input, indicating a distinct energetic contribution governed by plasma excitation. rCH4 increased with CH4 partial pressure (PCH4) but decreased with H2O (PH2O), defining an optimal CH4/H2O ratio that reflects a balance between methane activation and competitive surface coverage. Product incorporation revealed moderate effects of CO and CO2, while H2 showed a minor influence in rCH4. An empirical kinetic expression was iteratively derived from experimental data, progressively incorporating adsorption and product terms. The final model reproduced the experimental trends with high precision (R2≈ 0.98, RMSE ≈ 8×10-7) and yielded consistent apparent activation energies (Ea ≈ 306 kJ·mol-1) across tested formulations. Sensitivity and correlation analyses confirmed that plasma energy input and PCH4 dominate the rate response, whereas product terms have a minor contribution within the evaluated range. The resulting rate equation quantitatively describes CH4 activation by plasma-catalysis and provides basis for kinetic interpretation and operating condition assessme

Segregation in circulating turbulent fluidized beds with a broad particle size distribution: A Froude number-based model approach
abstract: Iron production based on direct reduction processes in fluidized beds facilitates the direct processing of iron ore fines, thereby bypassing energy-intensive agglomeration steps. The inherent broad particle size distribution (PSD) of iron ore fines introduces substantial hydrodynamic complexity due to factors such as elutriation. To date, research on particle entrainment has relied predominantly on empirical correlations, leaving a notable void in comprehensive theoretical and dimensionless investigations. This study addresses this critical gap by providing a fundamentally novel modeling approach that specifically incorporates the Froude number to characterize the PSD and entrainment above the bed surface, instead of employing an empirically determined elutriation rate constant. The analysis of the experimental data, recorded with bronze and air, confirms that the Froude number serves as a reliable dimensionless parameter to correlate fluidization velocity with height. On this basis, a Froude number based model is elaborated for the progression of the PSD with height above the dense bed. The model is validated and shows hydrodynamic consistency and good agreement with the two experimentally investigated bed materials (bronze, d50 = 75 µm and d50 = 143 µm). The study further introduces a simple method to estimate the total entrainment flux based on the proposed Froude model. The outcome is successfully compared with experimental data presented in this work.

abstract: Abstract Given the swift advancement of the intelligent era, the development of smart adjustable electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding composites is necessary to tackle the escalating complexity of application scenarios. Herein, a straightforward dip-coating approach was employed to fabricate thermal-adjustable melamine foam (MF)/polydopamine (PDA)/MXene/trans-1,4-polyisprene (TPI) (MPMF/TPI) EMI shielding composite foams, using MF as three-dimensional (3D) skeletons, PDA as bridging agent, MXene as electrically conductive filler, and TPI as shape memory function body. In consequence, MPMF/TPI composite foams exhibit excellent thermal stimulus shape memory function for the adjustment of total EMI shielding effectiveness (SE T ) under self-fixing deformations. Particularly, MPMF/TPI-26.0 foam with 60% compressed strain exhibits the adjustable SE T of 31.4 dB, 36.5 dB, 41.7 dB, and 50.9 dB at the recovery rate of 0%, 33.3%, 66.7%, and 96.6%, respectively, when it is stimulated at 100°C for 0 s, 10 s, 40 s, and 80 s, respectively. Notably, at the recovery rate of 96.6%, the compressed MPMF/TPI-26.0 foam holds excellent 96.0% restoration of EMI SE T on basis of the original MPMF/TPI-26.0 foam (53.0 dB). So as to further enhance the EMI shielding performance, MPMF/TPI/graphite paper (GP) was fabricated by integrating MPMF/TPI foam with GP through a facile all-in-one patch method. Remarkably, MPMF/TPI/GP-5.6 reveals the absolutely green absorption-dominant shielding mechanism with EMI SE T of 74.8 dB and immense A of 0.87. The asymmetrical conductive network construction enables an "absorption-reflection-reabsorption" mechanism, ensuring robust EMI shielding performances and efficient electromagnetic wave absorption. This innovative strategy creates the potential applications of shape memory composites for intelligently adjustable EMI shielding in the areas of advanced electronics and smart devices.

Bioprinting of miRNA-induced spheroids for vascularized, heterocellular bone regeneration
abstract: Successful bone regeneration requires coupled osteogenic and vascular development; however, achieving simultaneous multicellular differentiation within engineered tissues remains challenging. Here, we developed a microRNA (miR)-guided spheroid platform to induce dual osteogenic and endothelial differentiation of human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) for vascularized bone regeneration. hASCs were transfected with miR-148b or miR-210 to promote osteogenic and vascular-associated phenotypes, respectively, and assembled into spheroids that were bioprinted within an nHA-containing GelMA microgel environment using aspiration-assisted bioprinting (AAB). The integrated platform combined miR-guided osteogenic and endothelial differentiation, spatially organized AAB-based spheroid assembly, and an nHA-containing GelMA microgel environment to support vascularized bone tissue regeneration. The engineered constructs maintained high cell viability (> 90%) and supported active cell spreading and migration within the microgel matrix, together with increased osteogenic and endothelial gene expression. To further verify their in vivo regenerative potential, the constructs were implanted into mouse critical-size calvarial defects, where those containing miR-transfected hASCs improved bone regeneration, achieving ~91% of defect closure, and promoted the formation of vessel-like CD31-positive structures compared to controls. Together, these findings demonstrate that combining miR-mediated dual-lineage differentiation with spatially organized spheroid assembly and a supportive microgel environment provides a promising strategy for vascularized bone tissue engineering.

Thermal locking-like behavior in UV-ozone-treated PET exhibiting thermally persistent nanoscale morphology through constrained curvature relaxation
abstract: Surface nanostructures in glassy polymers are intrinsically unstable under thermal conditions due to capillary-driven levelling, which rapidly eliminates curvature above the glass transition temperature. Stabilizing nanoscale surface geometry during thermal processing therefore remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we show that ultraviolet-ozone (UV-ozone) treatment of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) induces laterally uniform nanodomains that exhibit thermally persistent behavior. Microscopy analyses reveal that the characteristic domain size evolves from ∼40–90 nm to ∼80–150 nm with increasing treatment time, while the surface roughness increases significantly ( R z ≈ 11 nm to ≈ 91 nm). Upon thermal annealing at 170 °C for 5–20 min, the roughness rapidly decreases to a finite value (∼20–30 nm) without complete capillary smoothing, and the lateral domain organization remains preserved. This incomplete flattening deviates from classical Mullins-type levelling and indicates the emergence of a constrained curvature regime. Spectroscopic and thermal analyses confirm that the modification is confined to the near-surface region without significant bulk structural change. These results provide direct experimental evidence of a previously unrecognized thermally persistent nanoscale morphology in glassy polymers and support a physically interpretable framework based on constrained curvature relaxation, consistent with thermal locking-like behavior.

A fully adaptive automated system for nanoparticle washing enabled by vision and language AI
abstract: Self-driving laboratories are reshaping materials discovery by combining automated experimentation with AI-driven decision-making. However, the lack of automation in key preprocessing steps such as nanoparticle (NP) washing, remains a major barrier to achieving full experimental autonomy. Effective automation of NP washing requires visual adaptivity to detect subtle changes in the appearance of dispersions or precipitates, and cognitive adaptivity, to handle failure cases like incomplete sedimentation or phase separation. These demands make NP washing uniquely challenging despite its apparent simplicity. We introduce a fully integrated NP washing platform that combines computer vision with a large language model (LLM) to enable intelligent, end-to-end preprocessing in self-driving labs. The system employs YOLACT for real-time robotic manipulation and latent mask R-CNN for uncertainty-aware image segmentation, achieving 100% task success across 60 trials and accurately processing 45 diverse precipitate images. A retrieval-augmented LLM autonomously generates and continuously refines washing protocols based on cognitive feedback from failure detection. The platform was validated on NiFe layered double hydroxides, IrRu nanoparticles, and CdSe/CdS quantum dots. Electrochemical and photoluminescence analyses demonstrated that the automated washing achieves a quality comparable to manual processing. This work represents a critical step toward fully autonomous, closed-loop experimentation by bridging synthesis and characterization through intelligent preprocessing.

title: Interdigitated electric-magnetic gradient MXene-based nanocomposite films for concurrent high-efficiency electromagnetic shielding and sensitive detection
Circumventing the energy gap law via an isomerization-aggregation strategy toward highly efficient solution-processed OLEDs
abstract: Red and near-infrared thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitters hold great promise for advanced optoelectronics, yet their efficiency in solution-processed systems is fundamentally limited by the energy gap law and strong vibrational coupling. Herein, we present a simple and effective isomerization-aggregation strategy to circumvent these limitations. By sterically controlling the displacement of benzene rings at the 9-position of the acceptor unit, we suppress vibrational coupling in red/NIR TADF emitters. This molecular design increases the S₀‐S₁ vibrational quantum numbers, leading to a reduced Franck‐Condon factor and lower non‐radiative decay rates. Both experimental and theoretical analyses confirm that this approach effectively counters the energy gap law. The cis‐isomer (cis‐IQD‐TPA) exhibits aggregation‐induced emission characteristics, enabling solution‐processed doped devices that achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 11.2% at 614 nm with low efficiency roll‐off (7.16% at 1000 cd m⁻²). Furthermore, a non‐doped device based on cis‐IQD‐BPPA attains an EQE of 3.4% at 692 nm. This work establishes a fundamental design principle—isomerization‐aggregation for developing high‐efficiency red/NIR TADF materials and advances the practical application of solution‐processable OLEDs.

Analysis of forced and intrinsic quenching in a plasma reactor for nitrogen fixation by use of three-dimensional simulations and experiments
abstract: Microwave plasma reactors offer a promising route for sustainable nitrogen fixation, yet the efficiency of NO x production is often limited by fast backward reactions at elevated temperatures. This study employs three-dimensional CFD simulations, validated against experimental measurements, to investigate the impact of forced jet quenching on the thermo-fluid-chemical dynamics of NO x formation. A split-feed configuration (10 SLM tangential plasma feed plus 10 SLM impinging quench jets) is compared with a conventional single-feed system relying solely on intrinsic quenching. The quench jets reorganize the flow, intensify local turbulence, and impose sharp thermal gradients that rapidly cool the plasma tail region where gas temperature falls from ∼3500 K to below 800 K upon injection, suppressing NO x destruction and stabilizing reaction products. Net reaction rates indicate that forced jet-quenching suppresses NO x destruction and sustains higher yield across 400–800 W microwave power. These gains are achieved without an energy-efficiency trade-off, as evidenced by lower specific energy costs. Parametric analysis identifies the influence of jet location: positioning jets too near the plasma core leads to incomplete stabilization, while farther downstream offers negligible gains. Overall, forced jet quenching emerges as a robust, controllable complement that augments the reactor's intrinsic quenching to boost yield and energy efficiency. The validated modeling framework provides mechanistic insight and shows how to identify the configuration-specific upper bound in performance for a given reactor design.

Mussel-inspired multifunctional supramolecular hydrogel sensor enabled by machine learning for Morse code information communication
abstract: Multifunctional hydrogel sensors have garnered significant interest for their potential in emerging applications such as health monitoring, wearable electronics and human-machine interfaces. However, practical deployment remains challenging due to the difficulty in integrating key functionalities including mechanical robustness, self-healing, environmental stability, strong adhesion, and high conductivity within a single material system. Herein, we present a mussel-inspired polyvinyl alcohol/sodium alginate/polydopamine/borax (PSPB) hydrogel fabricated via a straightforward one-pot method, based on a supramolecular coupling effect of ionic coordination, reversible borate ester bonds, and hydrogen bonding. Benefiting from these intermolecular interactions, PSPB hydrogel demonstrates high fracture strength, excellent elongation, good conductivity, universal adhesion, rapid self-repairing capability with high efficiency, and frost resistance. Owing to its strong skin adhesion and low interfacial impedance, PSPB hydrogel-based strain sensor enables real-time motion recognition and high-quality recording of electrophysiological signals even under demanding conditions. Remarkably, integrated with machine learning-assisted signal processing, the PSPB hydrogel sensor shows great potential for Morse code communication, remote medical monitoring and real-time transmission of emergency information. This work highlights its promise for intelligent healthcare and assistive communication systems by enabling advanced human-machine interaction, voice activity detection, and proactive health management

Scalable Lagrangian network modelling of trickle-bed reactors with coupled hydrodynamics and reaction performance
abstract: Trickle bed reactors (TBRs) are central to modern reaction engineering for producing high-value chemicals and fuels, yet computational limitations have historically constrained industrial-scale simulations. Most state-of-the-art methods neglect local multiphase interactions and phase distribution, while also being computationally prohibitive when scaled to large size systems. To overcome these challenges, this work introduces a novel modular simulation framework based on a Lagrangian approach that captures both local and global multiscale phenomena within TBRs. The novelty of the framework lies in its ability to couple particle-scale bed morphology, local liquid distribution, catalyst wetting, and reactor-scale reaction performance within a scalable Lagrangian network formulation. The framework integrates three interconnected modules: packing generation, hydrodynamics, and reaction system modelling, through a Lagrangian rivulet-tracking approach that explicitly resolves contact point topology and local wetting. Validation against purpose-built experimental setup demonstrates excellent agreement, with deviations of less than 1.5% in static holdup and approximately 4% in dynamic holdup for 4 mm particles (15% for 6 mm particles) while remaining consistent with literature data. The method achieves simulation times of 10-25 min for systems with up to 88,090 particles on desktop hardware, demonstrating a substantial computational advantage compared to particle-resolved CFD studies, which typically require high mesh resolution and substantially larger computational resources for smaller resolved domains. The framework successfully captures channelling, maldistribution, and wetting heterogeneity (4.8-19.5% wetted particle fractions) beyond conventional pseudohomogeneous models, and demonstrates the influence of partial wetting on reaction performance. The reaction module was validated against AMS hydrogenation experiments, with a mean conversion deviation of less than 1%. These results show that the proposed framework not only bridges critical gaps in multiphase reactor modelling, but also provides a scalable and versatile tool for advanced TBR design and optimisation.

Thioctic acid–functionalized silica for selective palladium adsorption from chloride–based solutions
abstract: Selective recovery of Pd from chloride-rich hydrometallurgical leachates, such as those derived from automotive catalytic converters, remains challenging due to the chemical similarity of PGMs and the stability of their chloro-complexes. Here, we report a green, selective sorbent (TA@Si) prepared by covalently grafting the naturally occurring disulfide ligand, thioctic acid, onto mesoporous silica via silane chemistry. In multi-metal batch experiments, TA@Si exhibited excellent selectivity for Pd over Pt, Rh, and base metals (Fe, Zn, Ce) across a wide acidity range (0.05–10 M HCl). The process was endothermic and entropy-driven, remaining thermodynamically favorable under strongly acidic conditions, and adsorption followed pseudo-second-order kinetics, best described by Sips and Temkin isotherm models, reaching a maximum capacity of (49.5 ± 12.4) mg·g −1 at 0.2 M HCl. XPS, Raman spectroscopy and SEM-EDS analyses indicate that Pd(II) coordinates to disulfide-derived sulfur sites of TA, forming stable surface-anchored Pd-S/Cl complexes. Adsorbed Pd (along with minor Pt) was quantitatively recovered using thiourea in dilute HCl, and the sorbent maintained performance over at least five adsorption-desorption cycles. Fixed-bed column studies demonstrated that this selectivity translates to continuous operation, with delayed Pd breakthrough, minimal co-adsorption of competing metals, and efficient Pd recovery through continuous thiourea-assisted desorption. This work introduces an acid-stable thioctic-acid-functionalized silica adsorbent for selective Pd recovery from chloride-rich PGM leachate simulants, demonstrating the combined advantages of TA-disulfide coordination chemistry, broad HCl tolerance, multi-metal Pd selectivity, regenerability, and fixed-bed compatibility.

Single-precursor-enabled surface/near-surface engineering for stabilizing oxygen redox in high-voltage Li-rich layered cathodes
abstract: Li-rich layered oxide cathodes offer high energy density but suffer from severe oxygen-related structural degradation and interfacial instability under high-voltage cycling. Herein, ammonium tetrathiomolybdate ((NH 4 ) 2 MoS 4 ) is employed as a multifunctional precursor to regulate the surface and near-surface chemistry of Li-rich cathodes through facile thermal treatment. The resulting S-LRO cathode features a MoS x -derived interphase coupled with a reconstructed subsurface region, where spinel-like domains, modulated oxygen-defect environments, and Mo O interactions are simultaneously generated. This integrated architecture stabilizes lattice oxygen activity, suppresses transition-metal migration, mitigates anisotropic lattice strain, and restrains the continuous growth of cathode-electrolyte interphase during prolonged cycling. Consequently, S-LRO delivers enhanced rate capability and durable cycling performance, maintaining 81.8% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1C and 79.4% after 200 cycles at 45 °C. Furthermore, the fully delithiated S-LRO electrode exhibits significantly improved thermal stability, with the exothermic onset temperature increased by 69.5 °C compared with the pristine counterpart. This work demonstrates an effective surface/near-surface regulation strategy for mitigating oxygen-related degradation and interfacial failure in high-energy Li-rich layered cathodes.

Dual-enhancement strategy for high-performance multimodal hydrogel sensors in deep learning-assisted speech recognition systems
abstract: Conductive hydrogels under large deformation often suffer from stress concentration and pronounced hysteresis, compromising their mechanical integrity and sensing reliability. Here, we propose a dual-reinforcement strategy to develop a multimodal hydrogel sensor based on amphiphilic polymer chains and MXene nanosheets. The reinforced hydrophobic micelles integrate hydrophobic association, triple hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to mitigate stress concentration and hysteresis, while MXene introduces nanoscale confinement and strong interfacial interactions, enhancing elastic recovery and reducing energy dissipation. The resulting hydrogel exhibits excellent stretchability (>1000% elongation), high toughness (2.75 MJ m-3), low hysteresis (4.1% at 400% strain), an ultralow detection limit (0.1%), and stable sensitivity (GF = 1.16) over a wide strain range (0.1-500%) with outstanding fatigue resistance (10,000 cycles). It also enables multimodal sensing of deformation and temperature (TCR=-2.13%°C-1), and can monitor environmental perturbations such as wind and hail impact. Combined with a deep learning framework, the sensor achieves 97% recognition accuracy for language-related inputs. Moreover, its intrinsic biodegradability reduces environmental impact. These features highlight its promise for healthcare monitoring, AI interfaces, and electronic skin systems.

abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation technology for saline water desalination, with advantages such as environmental friendliness and low cost, is of great significance for alleviating global water scarcity. However, salt scaling on the evaporator surface can reduce the evaporation rate and seriously threaten the system stability. Here, a sustainable inverted cone-shaped solar evaporator was fabricated using Ulva prolifera and sodium alginate as raw materials, achieving the synergy of efficient freshwater production and salt recovery. Under 1 sun irradiation, the fully marine biomass-based evaporator exhibited evaporation rates of 3.37 kg·m-2·h-1 and 3.02 kg·m-2·h-1 for 3.5 wt% and 10 wt% NaCl solutions, respectively, with no significant decay after 5 cycles. The unique 3D inverted-cone structure combined with the concentration gradient-induced Marangoni convection (verified by COMSOL simulation) promoted the saline radial transport and directional crystallization, enabling a salt collection rate of 3.13 kg·m-2·day-1 in 10 wt% NaCl. Furthermore, laboratory and outdoor performance tests using simulated seawater and real seawater demonstrated its application potential. This study provides a novel strategy for efficient seawater desalination and resource utilization.

Spatially synergistic sulfur reduction catalysis enabled by spinel-modified Janus bilayer carbon nanofibers
abstract: The practical deployment of lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) is fundamentally limited by uncontrolled lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttling and sluggish multistep sulfur reduction kinetics. Conventional electrocatalysts, typically confined to a single functional domain, fail to concurrently optimize polysulfide anchoring and conversion and often suffer from progressive interfacial passivation during cycling. Herein, we propose a spatially regulated catalytic strategy based on a Janus bilayer carbon nanofiber (CNF) interlayer to enable continuous and synergistic sulfur reduction reaction (SRR) kinetics. By asymmetrically integrating geometrically complementary Co–Mn spinel phases, the Janus architecture spatially decouples and sequences elementary SRR steps. The sulfur-facing Co1.2Mn1.8O4/CNF layer provides moderate adsorption toward long-chain LiPSs via tetrahedral Co3+ and octahedral Mn3+ sites, promoting efficient liquid–solid conversion while suppressing polysulfide diffusion. In contrast, the separator-facing Co1.2Mn1.8O4/CNF@Fe0.6 layer reconFig.s local electronic states through enhanced Co–O–Fe d–p orbital coupling, thereby accelerating solid–solid conversion and facilitating charge transport. Experimental and theoretical analyses demonstrate that this spatial orchestration establishes an ordered and uninterrupted SRR pathway, effectively mitigating interfacial passivation. Consequently, LSBs equipped with the Janus interlayer deliver an ultralow capacity decay of 0.044% per cycle over 500 cycles at 1C with excellent rate performance, highlighting the effectiveness of spatial architectural regulation for multistep electrochemical reactions.

title: Reconfigurable bio-inspired honeycomb metamaterials enabled by 4D printed shape memory composites with tunable microwave absorption
Microwave-assisted rapid synthesis of CAU23 and MIL53 MOFs from an unusual aluminum source and their application in CO2 capture
abstract: This study presents the synthesis of CAU23 and MIL53 MOFs using saline slags as an aluminum source and evaluates the effect of microwave treatment on the preparation process. The saline slags underwent chemical treatment with HCl or NaOH to produce Al 3+ or AlO 2 − solutions, which were used for MOF synthesis while simultaneously reducing the hazardous nature of the waste. The MOF were characterized using several techniques as powder X–ray diffraction, FT–infrared spectroscopy, thermal analysis, N 2 adsorption–desorption isotherms at −196 °C, laser diffraction, and electron microscopy. The results demonstrate that these MOF types can be successfully synthesized from saline slags and that microwave treatment significantly reduces synthesis times; specifically, CAU23 was obtained after 90 min of microwave treatment (compared to 3 or 6 h under reflux), while MIL53 required only 5 min. Finally, the CO 2 adsorption capacity was evaluated at several temperatures from 50 to 200 °C and up to 80 kPa, with the CAU23 series showing the highest results, ranging from 0.80 to 1.08 mmol CO2 /g.

Dry reforming of methane on supported nickel catalysts: Recent advances on process modelling, carbon pathways and life cycle assessment
abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) is a process that converts CH 4 and CO 2 into synthesis gas (H 2 /CO), offering a dual environmental benefit by utilizing two major greenhouse gases toward the production of valuable chemicals. However, the widespread and sustainable application of DRM over supported Ni catalysts is limited by catalyst deactivation, primarily caused by carbon deposition originating from methane cracking and the reverse Boudouard reaction. A comprehensive examination of carbon formation and removal steps during DRM is presented. The influence of Ni metal particle size and morphology, the support and promoter chemical composition, and the metal-support interactions in governing resistance to carbon accumulation are discussed. Carbon mitigation pathways, and the use of basic and reducible metal oxide supports of nickel are analyzed in depth. Recent advances in operando characterization techniques, isotopic labelling, and DFT calculations have provided insights into the mechanism and dynamics of carbon formation and gasification, as well as the dynamic restructuring of active sites under DRM reaction conditions. In addition, kinetic modelling and microkinetic simulations, and reactor-level numerical analysis have emerged as powerful tools to predict carbon formation trends, evaluate deactivation behavior, and optimize catalyst performance. Furthermore, the industrial applications of DRM and the role of modelling and numerical analysis in scaling up this process are discussed. The principal challenges and prospective avenues in catalytic DRM, particularly regarding modelling and numerical analysis, are delineated, thereby facilitating future research in this area. Finally, this review integrates the framework of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) within the DRM context, emphasizing the environmental and resource-efficiency implications of process design, catalyst selection, and system boundaries.

title: Spirofluorene-grafted triazine branched poly(aryl piperidinium) anion exchange membranes for high performance water electrolysis and flow batteries
Unravelling support-dependent photoelectrocatalytic activity of high-valence Ir single atoms on TiO2 nanofilms
abstract: Single-atom catalysts based on iridium have attracted significant attention for water splitting. However, the role of Ir oxidation states and their dependence on the electronic structure of the support material are not well understood. Here, we investigate the catalytic behavior of single-atom Ir anchored on anatase TiO2 nanofilms, using this platform system to study the valence-dependent activity toward hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER). High-valence Ir6+ single atoms exhibit excellent HER activity and outstanding operational stability under alkaline conditions, including at elevated electrolyte temperatures at 80 °C, but show negligible OER activity on TiO2 nanofilms. Through controlled electrochemical cyclic voltammetry and secondary annealing, Ir6+ species are partially converted into Ir4+ along with a concurrent reduction in deep-trapped oxygen vacancies and reconstruction of the local electronic environment of the host TiO2. This valence modulation leads to a pronounced enhancement in OER performance, with Ir4+ species dominated single-atom sites delivering lower overpotentials with –0.42 ± 0.04 V vs RHE at 10 mA cm⁻2. Density functional theory calculations reveal more favorable adsorption energetics for OER intermediates on Ir4+ compared to Ir6+ sites, which is in agreement with our experimental observations.

abstract: Additive manufacturing enables the realization of diverse and complex reactor channel geometries, substantially increasing the number of feasible design variants. While this design freedom offers opportunities for improved performance, it also complicates the systematic selection of geometries suitable for a given application. This paper presents a data-driven framework to support this selection process in the early reactor concept design phase. The framework employs surrogate models to predict key physical characteristics such as heat transfer, radial temperature difference, pressure drop, and flow profile, and integrates these into a multi-criteria decision making method to guide process engineers in selecting appropriate channel geometries. By focusing on fundamental physical characteristics rather than reaction-specific results, the framework ensures that the surrogate models remain transferable across different reaction systems. Incorporating probabilistic dimensioning further narrows the solution space and reduces the need for iterative experimental campaigns or computationally demanding simulations in reactor design. The applicability of the proposed framework is demonstrated through two case studies in methanol synthesis, highlighting its potential to streamline early-stage reactor development.

Gas separation in industrial bulk chemistry and relevance for transitioning to industrial plasma chemistry
abstract: Products of the chemical industry shape our daily lives and are in a transition towards increasing use of renewable resources and energy. Bulk chemistry is governed by the development and adoption of advanced gas separation technologies, as the corresponding reactions are not highly selective and require extensive work-up. Bulk-chemical separation is the key to optimise reaction efficiency, ensure product purity, and enhance economic and environmental sustainability. This review critically evaluates established bulk-chemical separation methods such as (cryogenic) distillation, membrane separations, pressure swing adsorption (PSA), and chemical looping, and evaluate their application in industrial settings. Each technology is analysed in terms of operating principles, industrial maturity, energy demand, scalability, and compatibility with plasma-specific characteristics such as low conversion, high energy consumption, moderate operating temperature and pressure windows, fluctuating operation, and decentralised production. These separation technologies are a key enabler for the introduction of new, emerging reaction technologies, such as plasma-assisted chemical processes. Plasma processes are recognised for their potential to enable cleaner, more efficient chemical production, and, therefore, have potential to reshape bulk-chemical industry. Despite extensive investigations on plasma reactions in the past two decades, the enabling potential of separation for plasma processes has hardly been tackled. Therefore, this review aims to fill that gap and substantiates the potential of separation by one plasma process study at bulk-scale. Apart from providing perspective (forecast), concrete quantified evidence is given by a case study on plasma-assisted bi-reforming of methane (BRM) for high-purity syngas production is presented, integrating a revisited SMR-DMR benchmark with an original bulk-scale process model, to investigate the capacity of further scale-up towards bulk-chemical separation. Overall, this review demonstrates that separation technology must not be treated as a downstream add-on, but rather as a core design driver that fundamentally shapes the feasibility, efficiency, and scalability of industrial plasma chemistry.

title: Water-regulated generation of reactive bromine species for selective electrochemical synthesis in an aqueous electrolyte
abstract: Electrochemical synthesis of halohydrins and vicinal dihaloalkanes via halogenation of olefins presents a sustainable alternative solution to conventional methods, yet precise control over selectivity remains a fundamental challenge that requires designed catalyst and additives to manipulate the generation of various reactive species. Here, we report water-regulated electrochemical generation of reactive bromine species in an aqueous electrolyte, thus achieving selective synthesis of bromohydrin and vicinal dibromide in an undivided cell at low cell voltage with Faradic efficiency exceeding 90%. Hypobromous acid (HBrO) is the predominant reactive species generated from the oxidation of bromine anions, which directly reacts with alkenes to create bromohydrins in water-rich electrolyte. A reduced concentration of water in electrolyte facilitates the conversion of generated HBrO to elemental bromine (Br2), thus promoting the formation of vicinal dibromoalkanes. The water-regulated electrochemical bromination is also valid at higher concentrations of reactants with a broad substrate scope, enabling the use of a solar-powered flow system for scaling up. The minimum effort for purification and separation endorse the upgrade of electrochemically synthesized bromohydrins to value-added cyclic carbonates via esterification using CO2, showing potential for applications.
