Evaluating the influence of air sparging technique on PFAS desorption and mobilization in soil using short-term column experiments
abstract: Air sparging is a promising in situ technique for mobilizing per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) via air–water interfacial processes and advective mixing. The short-term effects of air sparging on PFAS desorption were investigated using field-contaminated soil collected from the Sundsvall Timrå Airport site (Sweden). Experiments were conducted under a fixed influent flow of 50 mL/min. Trial 1 employed a single soil column operated sequentially under water-only conditions, followed by air sparging. Trial 2 used two parallel columns: one operated under water-only flow, and the other under combined water flow and air sparging. In Trial 1, sparging increased aqueous perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) concentrations by ~30-fold, while 6:2 fluorotelomer betaine (6:2 FTAB) and 6:2 fluorotelomer sulfonate (6:2 FTSA) increased ~8-fold and ~ 1.5-fold, respectively. In Trial 2, the water-only column resulted in declining aqueous PFAS masses (0.01–0.30-fold of initial values), indicating redistribution without effective mobilization. In contrast, the water-air column exhibited substantial increases in aqueous-phase mass, indicating enhanced soil-to-water mass transfer. Long-chain sulfonates such as perfluoroheptane sulfonate (PFHpS), perfluorohexane sulfonate (PFHxS), and PFOS showed pronounced mobilization and foam enrichment under sparging conditions. Foam generated during sparging acted as an additional removal pathway, capturing up to 38% of perfluorooctanoate (PFOA), 21% of PFHpS, and 16% of 6:2 FTAB. Most PFAS decreased in the soil phase under sparging, with evidence of compound-specific redistribution (e.g., PFHxS). Overall, air sparging enhanced PFAS transfer from soil to mobile phases and promoted interfacial enrichment, supporting its application for targeted in situ management of saturated PFAS source zones.

Lithium-doped calcium silicate scaffolds induce miR-130a-rich M2 macrophage EV-accelerating diabetic bone healing through angiogenesis–osteogenic coupling and mitochondrial repair
abstract: Diabetic bone regeneration remains a formidable clinical challenge owing to persistent chronic inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and severe cellular mitochondrial dysfunction within the hyperglycemic defect microenvironment. Although cell-free therapies using extracellular vesicles (EV) are promising for regeneration, their therapeutic efficacy is compromised by harsh physiological conditions. To overcome these multidimensional barriers, we engineered a bio-instructive lithium-doped calcium silicate (LiCS) scaffold system. This ion-releasing platform was specifically designed to reprogram the local immune responses by stimulating M2 macrophages to secrete functionally enriched EV (LiCSM2EV). In vitro investigations demonstrated that LiCSM2EV successfully dictate a prohealing immunomodulatory shift. Furthermore, under high glucose stress, these engineered EV effectively alleviated oxidative damage and restored mitochondrial bioenergetics, including ATP production and membrane potential stability, in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) and Wharton's jelly mesenchymal stem cells (WJMSC). Transcriptomic profiling via next-generation sequencing identified exosomal miR-130a as a pivotal therapeutic target. Mechanistically, miR-130a orchestrates robust angiogenesis–osteogenesis coupling by dually targeting distinct pathways. It promotes robust endothelial tube formation in HUVEC by suppressing GAX to activate the AKT/HIF-1α/VEGF signaling axis, while simultaneously accelerating osteogenic differentiation in WJMSC by inhibiting HDAC4 to significantly upregulate RUNX2 and its downstream extracellular matrix proteins. In vivo evaluations using a diabetic rabbit bone defect model confirmed that the synergistic LiCSM2EV system significantly promoted anti-inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, rapid neovascularization, and mature bone tissue formation. This study highlights a scaffold-based EV-mediated therapeutic paradigm that integrates ion-doped biomaterials with targeted exosomal microRNA delivery to successfully restore mitochondrial function and accelerate diabetic bone healing.

Mechanistic insights into E. coli inactivation by MnOx-anode electrochlorination: coupled Fenton-like, active-chlorine and 1O2-pathways
abstract: Our study explored E. coli inactivation by electrochemical chlorination using MnO x anodes, and the results support a multi-oxidant mechanism involving active chlorine species (ACS), cathodically generated H 2 O 2 , downstream 1 O 2 formation, and Fenton-like oxidative stress. E. coli inactivation was elucidated using assays with scavengers (catalase, tBuOH, bicarbonate), kinetic isotope experiments, and gene knockout mutants (catalase, superoxide dismutase, Mn 2+ transport, and DNA repair). The experiments were conducted at a current density of 11.67 mA/cm 2 and an electrolyte concentration of 0.05 mol/L NaCl, measuring complete inactivation of 10 8 CFU/mL within 90 min using a MnO anode (MnO x -A). The delay period prior to cell death was consistent with the intracellular generation of •OH and Cl• through Fenton-like reactions with electrochemically produced HOCl/OCl − and H 2 O 2 , supporting 1 O 2 generation and O 2 •− participation in the disinfection process. Subsequently, cell death was triggered by combined intra- and extracellular oxidation, comprising damage to the cell membrane, cytoplasmic components, and DNA. Interestingly, as validated by XPS, when preparing the MnO 2 anode (MnO x -B), the inactivation time decreased to 20 min, attributed to the further 1.69-to-1.81-fold increase in ACS generation (Current efficiency = 21.4%). Discerning the differences between MnO x anodes impulses innovation in electrochemical disinfection technologies, creating opportunities for metal-oxide-facilitated bacterial control.

abstract: The zero-gap CO 2 electrolyser with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) is a promising candidate, owing to its alkaline condition, which suppresses hydrogen evolution reaction and stabilises the catalyst. Nevertheless, crystallisation of salt and flooding in the gas diffusion electrodes (GDE) are still issues for long term operation. While prior studies have examined water permeation and cation crossover individually, their combined impact on Faradaic efficiency and carbon utilisation remains poorly understood. In this study, systematic experiments were conducted in a zero-gap electrolyser with cathode water injection to evaluate the potassium crossover, the water balance, and the carbon utilisation of the membrane electrode assembly (MEA). The, results showed that 45% of the ionic current through the membrane derives from potassium ion crossover in case of Fumasep® AEM at 200 mA/cm 2 , which is nearly twice that of PiperION Ⓡ AEM which showed only 27% ionic current crossover. Furthermore, this cation movement was found to drive water transport across the membrane through electromigration rather than diffusion, linking to GDE flooding and salt crystallisation. Finally, a positive correlation was established between potassium crossover, water permeation and the observed cell potential underscoring their coupled impact on performance. This investigation highlights that precise control of cation crossover and water balance is critical for enhancing the durability of AEM CO₂ electrolysis systems. Prioritizing the development of AEMs specialised to minimize cation crossover is a key step towards feasible scaling up of AEM-based CO 2 electrolysis.

abstract: Lithium–sulfur (Li-S) batteries represent a promising candidate for next-generation energy storage systems; however, their practical deployment is impeded by polysulfide shuttle effect and the strong temperature dependence of redox kinetics. Here we develop a wide-temperature Li–S cell enabled by a Ni@JZ-VO2//PP modified separator. The functional interfacial layer consists of a Ni/VO2 heterojunction is uniformly anchored on nitrogen-doped porous carbon derived from distiller’s grains. This architecture effectively regulates polysulfide chemistry from -20 to 60 ℃. The cell delivers 891 mAh g-1 at 4C (50 ℃) and maintains 72.7% capacity after 200 cycles at -20 ℃. At ambient temperature (25 ℃), it provides 766 mAh g-1 at 4C and retains 505 mAh g-1 after 1000 cycles at 1C, corresponding to an exceptionally low average capacity fade rate of 0.054% per cycle. Mechanistically, in-situ XRD and DFT calculations disclose a dual-site catalytic relay: Ni converts in-situ to active NiS2 coupled with Li2S deposition/dissolution, while the NiS2–VO2 interface strengthens Li2S4 binding and alleviates Li2S2 trapping, accelerating polysulfide conversion and suppressing shuttle. This sustainable heterojunction strategy provides a scalable pathway toward high-performance, wide-temperature Li–S batteries.

Boron-doped sludge biochar to efficiently activate ferrate (VI) for sulfonamides removal with a wider pH range in waters: Transforming and evolving pathways of reactive species
abstract: Ferrate (VI) (Fe (VI))-based oxidation system possessed multiple functions for water treatment, however, a stable pH environment was essential for ensuring the efficiency. This study used facile pyrolysis to synthesize boron-doped sludge-derived biochar (BSBC), which effectively activated Fe (VI) and mitigated the pH dependence of the reaction system. The Fe (VI)/BSBC system (0.40 g/L of BSBC and 100 μM of Fe (VI)) achieved 96.54% removal rate of sulfamethoxazole (SMX) with overcoming the pH dependency of Fe (VI) in the reaction. The mechanism analysis indicated that BSBC shifted Fe (VI) activation pathway from electron transfer toward reactive oxygen species (ROS) production with Fe (IV/V) formed in different reaction solutions. Deeper mineralization was facilitated in water by a more diverse oxidizing species. The non-radical removal pathways conferred stronger anti-interference ability and broader pH range to the Fe (VI)/BSBC system. The Fe (VI)/BSBC system demonstrated its practical viability by sustaining stable catalytic activity over multiple cycles, achieving high removal rates in different real waters, and operating robustly in a continuous-flow setup. Combined characterization and theoretical calculations confirmed that O-B-O configurations reconfigured the electronic structure by generating electron-rich regions and reduced the bandgap, thereby enhancing electron transfer and Fe (VI) activation. Three major degradation pathways of SMX were proposed, and it was confirmed that the products exhibited reduced ecological toxicity. This study elucidated a novel mechanism for Fe (VI) activation by BSBC in water and established a fundamental theoretical framework to guide the practical application of Fe (VI)-based removal technologies.

abstract: The prolonged use of plastic mulch films and chemical herbicides has led to persistent soil contamination and rising ecological risks. Meanwhile, existing biodegradable mulch films often suffer from incomplete degradation and potential microplastic formation, limiting their practical sustainability. In this study, a multifunctional biodegradable chitosan/silk fibroin (SF) composite film (CS) was developed by incorporating SF fiber powder derived from waste Antheraea pernyi cocoons generated from large-scale natural enemy mass production into a chitosan matrix. Structural characterization indicated that SF fibers were uniformly dispersed within the matrix, forming a reinforced network that significantly enhanced mechanical strength and light-shielding properties. This compact structure enabled a high loading capacity for pendimethalin (PL) (90.70%) and a controlled release behavior, only 63.26% of PL was released within 26 h, which was 34.52% lower than that of the PL-loaded chitosan film. In addition, leaching studies demonstrated that CS effectively retained PL, thereby reducing its migration and accumulation in soil while prolonging herbicidal activity. Pot experiments revealed that CS achieved 92.59% weed suppression, approaching complete weed control, using only one-quarter of the recommended commercial herbicide dosage, while simultaneously promoting crop growth. Ecotoxicological and biodegradation evaluations further confirmed that CS was readily biodegradable and exhibited no adverse effects on earthworms or Chlorella vulgaris , while potentially supporting soil ecological functions through enhanced earthworm growth. This study provides a sustainable valorization strategy for waste silkworm cocoons and offers a multifunctional biodegradable mulch film for efficient weed control with reduced herbicide input and improved environmental safety.

title: Hyperoside-based self-assembled hydrogel for modulating osteoimmune microenvironment to combat bacterial infections and facilitate bone repair
abstract: Infected bone defects (IBDs), primarily caused by Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), remain a major clinical challenge due to persistent bacterial colonization, dysregulated immune responses, and disruption of the osteogenic microenvironment. Here, a multifunctional hydrogel system composed of Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) and hyperoside (Hyp), Zn 2+ , Indocyanine green (ICG) self-assembled nanoparticles was developed to achieve a synergistic “antibacterial-immunomodulatory-osteogenic” therapeutic cascade. Upon near-infrared (NIR)-triggered photothermal therapy (PTT), the Hyp/Zn/ICG nanoparticles exhibited potent antibacterial activity against MRSA. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that PTT treatment disrupted bacterial ribosome assembly and protein synthesis pathways, leading to downregulation of MRSA resistance genes. Simultaneously, PTT-assisted therapy promoted macrophage M2 polarization and suppressed M1 polarization, thereby remodeling the osteoimmune microenvironment. Furthermore, the system enhanced osteogenic differentiation by upregulating RUNX2, COL1A1, and OPN, increasing alkaline phosphatase activity, and promoting matrix mineralization through the BMP signaling. In vivo , PTT-assisted treatment effectively eradicated MRSA, induced M2 polarization, and accelerated bone regeneration in infected bone defects. Collectively, this work introduces a safe, antibiotic-free therapeutic strategy for IBDs, leveraging a coordinated antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic mechanism for efficient infection control and bone tissue repair.

Conceptual design and experimental validation of a novel pilot-scale crystallizer for Mg(OH)2 recovery from concentrated saline solutions
abstract: Reactive crystallization of magnesium hydroxide from concentrated saline solutions represents an effective route for magnesium recovery yet being challenging due to the complexity in controlling crystallization phenomena. This study presents the numerical model–guided design and experimental validation of an innovative pilot-scale crystallizer, the Multiple Feed Plug Flow Reactor (MFPFR). The reactor configuration was optimized through CFD simulations with local supersaturation analysis, identifying the hydrodynamic conditions that minimize local supersaturation peaks, thereby slowing nucleation processes and promoting crystal growth. The prototype was then constructed and tested using concentrated bitterns ([Mg 2+ ] ≈ 2 M) and 0.5 M NaOH solution as alkaline reagent. The produced Mg(OH)₂ suspensions exhibited excellent solid–liquid separation performance, with initial settling velocities up to 440 mm/h and filtration rates above 80 kg/(m 2 ·h), outperforming literature data. The obtained solids showed a high degree of crystallinity, while the overall process achieved magnesium recoveries exceeding 99%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the integrated modeling–experimental approach and confirm the potential of the novel MFPFR for high-quality Mg(OH)₂ production from concentrated saline streams.

Flow and heat transfer in fixed beds of spherical catalyst supports with internal voids
abstract: For hydrogen generation by steam methane reforming spherical catalyst particles with holes have been proposed. Advantages may be lower pressure drop, higher surface area and easier packing compared to cylinders. Evaluation of the newer supports in reactor models is difficult as the standard correlations for pressure drop, heat transfer, etc. may not apply. This work reports particle-resolved computational fluid dynamics (PRCFD) simulations on identical beds of spheres with and without holes, to evaluate the standard correlations for pressure drop and particle-fluid heat transfer in the perforated spheres. These were investigated for 4-hole spheres with tube-to-particle diameter ratios N of 3, 5 and 7 and for three diameters of the holes for N = 5 . In fixed beds with perforated spheres, the preferred orientation is with the holes perpendicular to the axial flow direction. Pressure drop was decreased due to the increase in void fraction for spheres with holes. The choice of reference length and whether to neglect internal particle void space for friction factor correlations depends on the size of the holes relative to the sphere diameter, as it controls the access of the fluid to the internal particle volume. Heat transfer from particles to fluid increased for the 4-hole spheres, but not as much as anticipated from the increase in particle surface area. The fluid inside the particle holes can equilibrate with the particle surface, so that some surface area is ineffective. This depends on flow rate, particle size and hole diameter and orientation of the holes to flow direction.

Engineering ionic percolation in high-loading ASSB cathodes through solid electrolyte coating on CAM via resonant acoustic mixing
abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) require composite cathodes that combine intimate active material–electrolyte contact with continuous ionic pathways, particularly at high cathode loadings. However, existing dry and wet coating methods often rely on strong mechanical forces, solvents, or complex processing, limiting scalability and risking particle damage or inhomogeneity. Here, resonant acoustic mixing (RAM) is introduced as a media-free, mechanically gentle, and scalable route for fabricating solid electrolyte (SE)–cathode active material (CAM) composites. Using LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 and Li 6 PS 5 Cl as a model system, RAM produces homogeneous mixtures with boundary-associated and surface-adherent SE distributions around the CAM particles together with minimal agglomeration. The resulting electrodes exhibit enhanced densification, an 83% increase in effective ionic conductivity, and improved rate capability and cycling stability compared to ball milling. These improvements arise from a continuous ionic percolation network and well-integrated CAM–SE interfaces. RAM thus provides a tunable and industrially relevant strategy for designing high-performance composite cathodes for next-generation ASSBs.

title: Bioinspired anisotropic architectures in AgNWs/MFC/SA/PDMS composite aerogels for enhanced wearable piezoresistive sensors
abstract: Wearable piezoresistive sensor devices show good potential for analyzing motion, monitoring health, and in human-computer interactions. However, traditional sensing materials have defects such as low sensitivity, insufficient flexibility and poor environmental adaptability. To solve these problems, a novel honeycomb composite aerogel (AMS-3055) was prepared by freeze-drying using silver nanowires (AgNWs) as the conductive network, calcium chloride as the crosslinking agent (CaCl₂), microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) and sodium alginate (SA) as the polymer skeleton, inspired by the material transport channel structure inside Taro macrophylla. Here, vacuum-assisted impregnation was utilized for the introduction of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) to acquire an AMS-3055/PDMS composite aerogel elastomer. Encapsulation of PDMS on the aerogel’s surface enhanced its mechanical stability and environmental resistance, and more importantly, the elastomer exhibited an antibacterial rate of up to 95%. Moreover, experiments demonstrated that the wearable piezoresistive sensor assembled using AMS-3055/PDMS composite aerogel elastomer exhibited high measurement factor (GF = -20.792 @ 0-2%), rapid response time (response/recovery time of 65/40 ms) and superb cycle stability (1000 cycles). Moreover, real-time finger, neck, elbow, wrist, and knee joint motions were monitored. This work offers a compelling approach for developing flexible electronic devices with broad potential applications in the fields of health monitoring, motion analysis, and human-computer interaction.

title: Self-powered flexible tactile sensors based on galvanic battery for smart sports and human-machine interaction
abstract: Flexible tactile sensors with high sensitivity and self-powered capabilities are highly desirable for the development of wearable health monitoring electronics, intelligent robots, and human-machine interaction systems. However, self-powered static tactile sensing are still challenging despite the achievement in dynamic tactile sensing. With the help of redox-induced electricity, a bio-inspired graphite/polydimethylsiloxane piezoresistive composite film acting both as the cathode and pressure sensing layer, a novel tactile sensor is presented here to detect not only the dynamic but also the static pressures without an external power supply. Uniquely, a sweat-activated galvanic mechanism is introduced by employing a copper anode and graphite/polydimethylsiloxane cathode, where the sweat acts as a natural electrolyte of the galvanic battery. Additionally, the tactile sensors are successfully demonstrated their applications in human-robot interaction, real-time human motion monitoring and action recognition. This new strategy could pave a pathway for the development of low-power human-machine interaction systems and smart wearable devices.

Solid base catalysts for pentaerythritol synthesis: Activity, stability, and recyclability of catalysts based on alkali and alkaline earth metals
abstract: The substitution of homogeneous bases with solid basic catalysts is highly desirable for the synthesis of pentaerythritol (penta), as liquid alkalis generate waste, accelerate reactor corrosion, and require extensive separation steps to isolate pure penta. This study investigates the catalytic activity of alkali and alkaline earth metals Ca, Na, and Mg supported on SnO 2 , TiO 2 , and γ-Al 2 O 3 for the conversion of formaldehyde and acetaldehyde to penta. Reaction parameters including temperature, feed ratios, reaction time, and catalyst loading were examined to find optimized conditions to maximize penta selectivity. Among the tested systems, 22% Mg/γ-Al 2 O 3 catalyst demonstrated the best performance, achieving 76% penta selectivity at 49% formaldehyde conversion under the following conditions: 90 °C, a 5:1 M ratio of formaldehyde to acetaldehyde, 0.2 g catalyst and 15 min reaction time. However, the leaching of Mg was siginficant. Mg on γ-Al 2 O 3 with different Mg loadings were evaluated, showing that 9 wt% Mg/γ-Al 2 O 3 catalyst exhibited the least amount of leaching, from 9 for fresh catalyst to 7.5 wt% Mg for spent catalyst (after reaction at 70 °C) and a penta selectivity of 61%, albeit at a slightly lower formaldehyde conversion of 41%. However, the accumulation of formate species on catalyst surface was observed with DRIFT spectroscopy, which resulted in deactivation of the catalyst. The catalyst partially regained the activity when recycled in multiple cycles after regeneration of spent catalyst. These findings highlight the potential of Mg-based solid catalysts for pentaerythritol synthesis, while also underscoring the need for further research to enhance catalyst stability and recyclability for industrial applications.

title: Hierarchically engineered MXene/metal−organic framework-derived Fe2O3 heterointerfaces for high-performance flexible asymmetric supercapacitors with enhanced redox kinetics and electronic structure modulation
abstract: MXene/MOF heterostructures have emerged as promising candidates for advanced energy storage systems due to their high electrical conductivity, abundant redox-active sites, and well-defined porous architecture. Leveraging these advantages, this study reports the fabrication of the MXene/MOF-derived Fe 2 O 3 negative electrode via a roll-coating method. In parallel, MOF-derived MnCo 2 O 4 was synthesized and directly grown on carbon cloth to serve as a positive electrode, providing enhanced mechanical stability and flexibility suitable for wearable energy storage devices. The MXene/MOF-derived Fe 2 O 3 exhibited a high specific capacitance of 421 F g −1 at a current density of 1 A g −1 , which is further supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Furthermore, the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor (MXene/Fe 2 O 3 //MnCo 2 O 4 ) delivered a specific capacitance of 84.4 F g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , along with an energy density of 30 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 400 W kg −1 . Notably, the device retained 92.2% of its initial capacitance after 10,000 charge−discharge cycles, demonstrating the durability and high electrochemical performance of the developed electrode materials.

Water-induced CO2 roll-up and regeneration complexity in zeolite 13× during humid direct air capture: Breakthrough, ex situ FTIR, and reduced-order modeling
abstract: Commercial zeolite 13× is a benchmark hydrophilic FAU adsorbent with high dry-CO 2 capacity, but its application in humid direct air capture (DAC) is strongly limited by water competition. Here, 13× is used not as a new sorbent candidate, but as a model material to link bed-scale breakthrough, ex situ FTIR signatures, regeneration behavior, and reduced-order modeling during humid-air exposure. N 2 physisorption, mercury porosimetry, XRD, and FTIR confirmed a predominantly microporous FAU-type zeolite with a BET surface area of 710.1 m 2 ·g −1 and a micropore volume of 0.253 cm 3 ·g −1 . Under humid DAC conditions, the bed initially retained CO 2 , but the CO 2 breakthrough curve subsequently exhibited roll-up above unity, evidencing displacement of previously adsorbed CO₂ by the advancing water front. The maximum transient CO 2 uptake was only 0.0909 mmol·g −1 , whereas the final H₂O loading reached 13.38 mmol·g −1 and accounted for 96.4% of the measured bed mass increase. Staged ex situ FTIR supported this interpretation by showing early growth and later collapse of the molecular CO 2 band, together with progressive strengthening of H 2 O and carbonate−/bicarbonate-like regions. Dry pure- CO 2 adsorption was used as an upper-bound reference for intrinsic CO 2 affinity. Under this dry condition, the retained CO 2 loading reached 3.19 mmol·g −1 and breakthrough was monotonic, confirming that poor humid-DAC performance arises from competitive water adsorption. Thermal regeneration and reduced-order modeling further supported a water-driven CO 2 displacement mechanism, highlighting the need for humidity management, regeneration control, or sorbent modification in practical DAC processes.

Swift heavy-ion induced defects and strain evolution in GaN epitaxial heterostructures
abstract: Radiation hardness is a critical requirement for Gallium Nitride (GaN)-based devices operating in space and radiation-intensive environments. This work investigates irradiation-induced microstructure evolution and strain development in multilayer GaN heterostructures irradiated with 950 MeV 197Au swift heavy ion (SHI) at fluences 1×1012, and 8×1012 ions cm-2. Structural modifications were characterized using high-resolution X-ray diffraction (HRXRD), and cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and the results were compared with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. HRXRD analysis reveals an anisotropic lattice distortion with increasing ion fluence, characterized by tensile strain along the c-axis (~1.25%) and compressive strain along the a-axis (~−1.55%). Diffraction peak broadening and diffuse scattering indicate a significant reduction in crystalline coherence length accompanied by increased mosaicity. TEM analysis directly confirms that irradiated GaN layer contains nanoscale cavities which follow the path along the ion-trajectories throughout the entire layer. The average cavity diameter increases from around 1.6 to 2.1 nm as fluence levels become higher. The corresponding cavity swelling increases from ~0.23-0.33% at the highest fluence. MD simulations reproduce the experimental trends which show a positive strain along the c-axis and negative strain along the a-axis and suggest enhanced cavity growth because of the overlapping ion tracks at higher fluence. The results provide a correlated experimental–computational picture of how SHI-irradiation modifies the lattice response and defect landscape in epitaxial GaN, offering mechanistic insight relevant to the radiation tolerance of GaN-based device structures.

AuxCuy alloying induced lattice distortion and phase engineering driven efficient plasmonic effect for photoelectrocatalytic water splitting
abstract: Utilizing the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effect of metals provides an effective approach to addressing key issues in photoelectrocatalysis. Among SPR effect metals, Au possesses the optimal chemical stability yet suffers from high cost and easy agglomeration, while Cu is prone to oxidation and exhibits poor stability. Accordingly, this study fabricates AuxCuy alloy and optimizes the SPR effect as well as interfacial charge transfer by regulating the Au/Cu atomic ratio to induce lattice distortion and phase engineering. Experimental results demonstrate that the photocurrent density of ZnFe2O4/Au1Cu1 reaches 4.70 mA·cm-2, which is 2.01 times that of ZnFe2O4/Au. The enhanced performance is attributed to the regulation of the d-band center via lattice distortion and crystal reconstruction of the Au1Cu1 alloy, as well as the optimization of interfacial energy band matching and built-in electric field, which facilitate carrier separation and transport. Furthermore, we reveal for the first time that the alloy transforms into a face-centered tetragonal phase at an Au/Cu atomic ratio of 1:1, constructing rapid charge transport channels and enhancing interfacial charge transfer induced by orbital overlap, thereby effectively suppressing carrier recombination after SPR excitation. This work offers a novel insight for efficient photoelectrocatalytic water splitting through the synergistic modulation of lattice distortion and phase engineering via an alloying strategy.

A narrow-bandgap organic photothermal material enabling efficient solar driven sustainable electricity-water cogeneration
abstract: Solar-driven power-water cogeneration is a promising solution to global energy and freshwater shortages, but organic small molecule photothermal materials suffer from narrow solar absorption and low photothermal conversion efficiency—rooted in inadequate regulation of molecular electronic structures and non-radiative relaxation pathways. Herein, a planar rigid conjugated molecule (TDT) derived from tetraamino-p-benzoquinone (TABQ) was rationally designed to optimize photothermal mechanisms. Its expanded π-conjugated system, tailored donor-acceptor-donor-acceptor (D-A-D-A) intramolecular motif, and reinforced electron delocalization collectively narrow the bandgap to 0.77 eV, enabling broad-spectrum absorption (250-1840 nm) for solar energy harvesting. Moreover, stable cationic radicals and intermolecular π-π stacking/hydrogen-bonding networks promote non-radiative relaxation and enhance photostability by suppressing radiative recombination and molecular degradation. Integrating TDT with thermoelectric generators achieved efficient photo-thermal-electric conversion, delivering a maximum power output of 0.79 W m-2 under 1-sun illumination. Meanwhile, A TDT-loaded hydrophilic fabric evaporator exhibited a high evaporation rate of 1.54 kg m-2 h-1 and 89% solar-to-vapor efficiency. Further integration into a cogeneration system realized simultaneous steam and power production. This work pioneers TDT’s application in solar-driven cogeneration, reveals the structure-mechanism-performance relationship for organic photothermal molecules, and provides a rational design paradigm for high-efficiency clean energy conversion materials.

title: Vacancy-modulated cationic potential with dual functions of activating anionic redox and integrating biphasic configuration for wide-temperature sodium storage
abstract: The energy density of layered oxides in sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) is restricted by the finite electron supply of conventional transition metal (TM) redox chemistry. Activating oxygen redox is a crucial strategy for surpassing the inherent limitation of energy density. In this work, we regulate the ionic potential via introducing cationic vacancies at TM sites to improve the oxygen redox activity in Na0.76Ni0.33Mn0.34Ti0.33O2. Cationic vacancies decrease the TM-O covalency by lowering the cationic potential, which encourages electrons to accumulate around oxygen atoms and facilitates O-O dimerization. Furthermore, the low cationic potential promotes the formation of P2/O3 biphasic configuration, which mitigates the structural degradation induced by oxygen redox, as evidenced by low volume variations of 1.12% for P2 and 0.95% for O3. Consequently, the optimized cathode Na0.76Ni0.33Mn0.34Ti0.28£0.05O2 achieves a remarkable capacity of 150.1 mAh g-1 and maintains a capacity retention of 92.1% over 350 cycles at 5 C. Benefiting from the improved charge transfer kinetics and reduced apparent activation energy, the material also shows superior electrochemical performance across a wide temperature range (107.2 mAh g-1 at -20 ℃; 153.4 mAh g-1 at 50 ℃). This work offers a novel insight for achieving reversible oxygen redox and offers a feasible approach for high-energy SIBs.

title: Hydrothermal extraction of phytic acid from wheat bran: experimental, thermodynamic, and kinetic evaluation
abstract: Phytic acid (IP 6 ) is a dominant organic phosphorus species that represents both a valuable bio-based chemical and a key contributor to phosphorus mobility during biomass processing. In this study, pressurized water extraction or hydrothermal extraction in a sealed vessel was investigated as a solvent-minimized approach for recovering phytic acid from wheat bran. The experiments were conducted using 0.1 g of wheat bran in 5 mL water at 75–150 °C for 1–48 h, and phosphorous behavior was quantified using complementary elemental (ICP-OES) and molecular-specific (LC-MS) techniques. Total dissolved P measured by ICP-OES increased strongly with temperature and time, highlighting the limitations of bulk elemental analysis in complex biomass systems. In contrast, LC-MS revealed a non-monotonic dependence on extraction severity, with IP6 yield increasing with temperature from 75 to 125 °C and with time up to 6 h, reaching a maximum of approximately 9.7 g . kg −1 wheat bran, but declining at 150 °C and extended residence times, despite continued increases in total dissolved phosphorus. This divergence indicates a transition from extraction-dominated behavior to transformation-dominated regimes, in which intact IP6 undergoes loss and redistribution into non-IP6 phosphorus-containing species. Moreover, thermodynamic analysis showed that IP6 recovery is endothermic ( ∆ H = 31.81 kJ/mol) and entropy-driven ( ∆ S = 81.94 J/mol.K), with ∆ G becoming increasingly favorable as temperature increases. Kinetic modelling favored Peleg and two-site models, consistent with a biphasic extraction and transformation behavior. Finally, solid residues were shown to retain wheat-bran-like composition and functionality (CHNS/TGA/FTIR), indicating limited undesirable matrix alteration under the studied conditions.

title: Decoding molecular fingerprints of halogenated organic compounds generated from the photodegradation of microplastics in sunlit seawater
abstract: Halogenated organic compounds (HOCs) are ubiquitous in marine environments, while photochemical halogenation of autochthonous dissolved organic matter (DOM) is considered the principal source of natural HOCs in surface seawater. Microplastics (MPs), as carbon-rich polymers, can release abundant DOM that may serve as exogenous precursors for photohalogenation, yet the formation mechanisms, molecular traits, and implications of MP derived-HOCs (MP-HOCs) in marine systems remain unclear. Herein, we conducted 180-day artificial weathering experiments in sunlit seawater using polyethylene, polypropylene, and polystyrene as models, investigating the molecular signatures of MP-HOCs. Ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrum yielded a total of 2768 unique HOC formulas across various MP leachates. Electron paramagnetic resonance and molecular network analyses indicated recombination with carbon-centered radicals (e.g., •CH 3 ) induced by halogen radicals (e.g., •X) as the potential mechanism for MP-HOC formation. Comparison between MP-HOCs and naturally occurring aquatic HOCs in the Yangtze River Estuary (YRE-HOCs) revealed an overlap of 296 formulas, accounting for 59% of YRE-HOCs. Notably, there was still ~90% of HOC formulas that were unique to MP leachates, showing higher aliphatic/proteins-like composition (40% vs. 15%) but lower oxygen-to‑carbon ratio (0.38 vs. 0.42) and molecular weight (399 vs. 462 Da) than YRE-HOCs. Furthermore, MP-HOCs exhibited longer potential biochemical transformation times and greater hydrophobicity and biotoxicity compared with non-HOCs based on the molecular-predicted results, which might affect marine ecosystem functions. This work provides the first systematic molecular fingerprints of MP-HOCs in sunlit seawater, demonstrates their significant contribution to the oceanic HOC pool, and offers a new perspective on the marine ecological effects of global plastic pollution.

Rational design of core functionalized N-alkylated corroles for controlled film gas sensing and methanol detection
abstract: Porphyrinoid macrocycles have long been employed as active materials in chemical sensing, relying on molecular engineering of peripheral functionalization to direct the formation of ordered, supramolecular architectures. In contrast, modifications at the macrocyclic core have predominantly involved metal insertion into the inner cavity, whereas the introduction of organic functional groups directly at the core has been comparatively less explored. In contrast, this study investigates an alternative N-alkylation strategy to modulate molecular organization and fine-tune sensitivity and selectivity in gas-sensing devices. Transferring the alkyl chains from the periphery to the corrole core inverts the conventional design paradigm for porphyrinoid-based sensing materials, enabling a more direct control over molecular packing and analyte diffusion. We synthesized 11 compounds, differing in alkyl chain length, branching, and substitution pattern, and integrated them into quartz microbalance (QMB) transducers to construct an innovative corrole-based electronic nose. Systematic exposure to Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) revealed that N-alkylation effectively tunes the sensitivity and selectivity profiles according to the alkylated groups, their position, and, ultimately, the molecule charge. Unlike classical approaches, correlation analyses and multivariate data treatment confirmed that alkylation preserves selective interactions while reducing the contribution of non-specific dispersion forces. As a proof-of-concept, the optimized sensor array successfully discriminated methanol adulteration in both real and synthetic wine samples, achieving a near-perfect classification with low estimation error for methanol concentration. This approach establishes N-alkylation as a promising alternative to metallation for the rational design of porphyrinoid-based e-noses, offering a versatile and scalable strategy for detecting methanol and other contaminants in complex matrices.

Design and fabrication of structured adsorbents with enhanced mass transfer for direct air CO2 capture
abstract: Structuring powdered adsorbents is essential for the scalable deployment of direct air capture (DAC), but conventional shaping often sacrifices low-concentration CO2 capture due to increased mass-transfer resistance. Here, charged zeolite-templated carbon (ZTC-K+) powder is engineered into transport-optimized monolithic configurations to improve mass transfer and increase the effective diffusion coefficient. Conventional densification compromises DAC performance by imposing mass-transfer limitations, whereas a nickel-foam-supported thin-sheet architecture preserves the intrinsic adsorption capacity of ZTC-K+ by enhancing interfacial accessibility and shortening diffusion pathways. The nickel foam scaffold also imparts mechanical robustness and structural integrity, enabling the adsorbent to retain its macroscopic shape and 82.8% of its initial CO2 capacity after 20 adsorption-desorption cycles. When further assembled into ordered honeycomb and tile architectures and evaluated in a fixed-bed reactor, the structured adsorbents exhibit high selectivity for CO2/N2 and CO2/H2O of 1525.0 and 2.1, respectively. Density functional theory calculations reveal that CO2 adsorption on ZTC-K+ is dominated by electrostatic interactions, with dispersion forces providing a secondary contribution, thereby accounting for its high CO2 selectivity. Fluent simulation at 7 m/s showed that the tile-shaped ZTC-K+ delivered the most uniform flow field and the lowest pressure drop, indicating its superior potential for practical CO2 capture. Together, these results show that transport-oriented structural design can bridge the gap between high-performance powdered sorbents and application-ready DAC adsorbents.

Divergent lithium polysulfide-ion association pathways in lithium-sulfur batteries: Implications for sulfur reduction kinetics and anode stability
abstract: Lithium‑sulfur (Li S) batteries are limited by sluggish sulfur reduction reaction (SRR), lithium polysulfide (LPS) shuttling, and Li-metal instability, all governed by Li + coordination. Yet solvation tuning alone cannot predict sulfur redox once LPS are involved. Here, by employing two structurally analogous sulfonate additives, methanesulfonate (MS) and trifluoromethanesulfonate (TFMS), paired with a weakly coordinating counter-cation, we decouple solvation effects from LPS-mediated Li + association. Molecular dynamics simulations, density functional theory, and 7 Li nuclear magnetic resonance confirm nearly identical perturbations to the Li + solvation sheath in LPS-free electrolytes. Upon LPS formation, however, MS strengthens Li + -LPS association, restricting Li + transport and moderating the liquid-to-solid sulfur conversion, whereas TFMS weakens Li + -LPS interactions, preserves Li + mobility, and promotes more favorable sulfur-conversion behavior with reduced polarization and activation energy. Importantly, the electrochemical consequences of these divergent SRR pathways depend strongly on electrolyte availability. Under practical low electrolyte-to‑sulfur (E/S) conditions, the favorable sulfur-conversion behavior in TFMS enables superior sulfur utilization and stable cycling beyond 300 cycles at 87% capacity retention (695 mAh g −1 ). In contrast, flooded electrolyte conditions largely mask electrolyte-dependent differences, highlighting the dynamic coupling between sulfur-conversion behavior and electrolyte availability. Despite their opposite effects on SRR behavior, both additives enhance durability through distinct mechanisms: MS limits parasitic degradation by moderating SRR behavior, whereas TFMS uniquely induces polymerization of 1,3-dioxolane, forming a TFMS-associated polymer-rich interphase on Li metal. These findings identify LPS-mediated Li + association as an important factor linking SRR behavior, electrolyte management, and interfacial stability, providing mechanistic guidance for additive design in practical Li S batteries.

title: Metal-free carbocatalytic treatment of analgesics - an atypical non-radical pathway and degradation enhancement by ultrasound
abstract: Metal-free carbonaceous materials from rice husk were obtained via a single-step pyrolysis at temperatures of 250, 500, and 800 °C, then their carbocatalytic abilities to deal with acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diclofenac in water were explored. The material prepared at 800 °C (BRH-800) efficiently activated peroxymonosulfate-PMS. The three target analgesics showed different degradation efficiencies, denoting a dependence on their chemical structure, with the acetaminophen elimination being more favorable. Through diverse analytical/instrumental and theoretical/computational tools, the predominance of a non-radical pathway in the carbocatalytic process was evidenced. It was proposed that the defects close to Si-containing functional groups of the material lead to the formation of an initial complex (named PMS-BRH-800*), which withdraws electrons from the pharmaceuticals, thus leading to the oxidation process. In the case of acetaminophen, a primary by-product was identified, which, according to the ECOSAR analysis and phytotoxicity assays, had a lower toxicity for living organisms. Additionally, the BRH-800/PMS system was stable to pH changes, with the carbonaceous material exhibiting good performance even after the third reuse cycle. The combination of carbocatalysis with ultrasound (BRH-800/PMS/US) improved the degradation of ACE and IBU via mechanical effects (carbonaceous particles disaggregation) mainly. Finally, the sonocarbocatalytic treatment of the analgesics in the spiked hospital wastewater and tap water showed that, despite the interfering effects of the matrix components, a partial degradation of pollutants was found. Hence, this work showed that carbocatalysis and sonocarbocatalysis with metal-free materials are promising treatments for degrading some specific analgesics in aqueous samples.

Defect-anchored Ru clusters enable accelerated water dissociation for diversified carbon-source reforming
abstract: Efficient water activation remains a pivotal challenge in the steam reforming of diverse carbon sources. This study addresses the limitation by anchoring Ru clusters on N-terminated defects of hexagonal boron nitride nanosheets (h-BNNS), leveraging electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) to stabilize highly dispersed, electron-deficient Ru sites. The resulting Ru/h-BNNS catalyst achieved up to 100% conversion of C1 feeds (CO, CH3OH) at 250–300 °C and complete conversion of C2+ feeds (ethanol, isododecane) at 550–600 °C, delivering high H2 yield and long-term stability that are highly competitive with representative noble-metal catalysts. In-situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that defect-induced electronic modulation accelerated H2O dissociation and strengthened RuO binding, thereby lowering water activation barriers and suppressing metal sintering. These attributes establish a “Diversified Carbon-Source Steam Reforming to Hydrogen” strategy (CxTH, x refers to CO, methanol, ethanol, and hydrocarbons), which aligns with the Green Carbon Science framework by enabling efficient H2 production with high catalytic activity and enhanced Ru atom utilization.

High-permeability nanophotosensitizer eliminates biofilm-associated infection through concurrent lipid peroxidation and extracellular DNA degradation
abstract: Biofilms are the root of persistent infections, while photodynamic therapy (PDT) shows promise in biofilm eradication. However, extracellular polymeric substance matrix, together with hypoxic and acidic environments, hinder the penetration and bacterial elimination of photosensitizers. To address these challenges, this study reports a nano-photosensitizer (Ag-Ru NP) that self-assembled via ruthenium-silver conjugates to strengthen PDT-mediated biofilm clearance. The hydrophobic donor-π-acceptor architecture of nanophotosensitizer not only endows the strong affinity toward bacterial membranes and extracellular DNA (eDNA) for deep intra-biofilm penetration, but also enables the light-responsive release of antimicrobial Ag+ into the biofilm interior, together amplifying PDT efficacy. Meanwhile, such a Type I photosensitizer enables robust generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), including O2- and ·OH, especially under hypoxic and acidic biofilm microenvironments. The overproduced ROS trigger lipid peroxidation and eDNA degradation concurrently in bacterial membranes, further destabilizing the biofilm matrix and promoting bacterial killing. Taken advantages of combined photodynamic biofilm disruption with targeted intra-biofilm antimicrobial delivery, Ag-Ru NPs markedly accelerate the healing of P. aeruginosa-infected wounds and alleviate bacterial keratitis in two murine models. Overall, this work establishes a synergistic strategy that couples lipid peroxidation and eDNA degradation, highlighting the potential of sophisticated nanophotosensitizer for the management of biofilm-associated infections.

Assessment of Clostridium kluyveri fermentation in batch and continuous bioreactor and development of a kinetic model
abstract: Medium-chain fatty acids (MCFAs) are high-value compounds with applications in the biofuel, bioplastic, and chemical industries. Chain elongation via reverse β-oxidation by Clostridium kluyveri is a promising route for converting low-value carbon streams into MCFAs under anaerobic conditions. This study presents an integrated experimental and modelling framework for describing MCFA production in both batch and continuous reactors. A dynamic kinetic model was developed, explicitly accounting for the two-step elongation pathway: (i) ethanol and acetic acid conversion to butyric acid and biomass, and (ii) ethanol and butyric acid conversion to hexanoic acid and biomass. Model parameters/yields were estimated through regression of experimental data collected under a wide range of operating conditions. The model reproduced the main experimental trends, with an average R 2 of 0.89 and an average NRMSE range of 9.60% across the calibration and validation datasets and captured the effect of operating conditions on system performance. Continuous experiments revealed an optimal dilution rate window (0.04–0.083 h −1 ), maximizing hexanoic acid production while maintaining stable biomass concentrations. Batch experiments showed that butyrate enhanced chain elongation efficiency, resulting in higher hexanoic acid production (up to 17.5 g/L). The model supported a process-level interpretation of the two elongation steps, indicating that biomass growth was mainly associated with the acetate-to-butyrate step, whereas hexanoate formation was mainly linked to the butyrate-to-hexanoate step. Sensitivity analysis, complemented by bounded Morris screening, showed that model behaviour was controlled by both kinetic parameters and apparent yield coefficients. Ethanol allocation and apparent hexanoate yield were the main drivers of hexanoic acid prediction, while kinetic parameters associated with the second elongation step remained influential under specific conditions, confirming the importance of butyrate-to-hexanoate conversion for hexanoate formation. Overall, the proposed model provides a calibrated dynamic framework for interpreting batch and continuous C. kluyveri fermentation within the investigated operating window and for supporting process-oriented analysis of medium-chain fatty acid production from ethanol- and short-chain-carboxylate-containing substrates.

DL-driven dual-modal proprioceptive-exteroceptive fusion for multi-joint soft grippers
abstract: Dexterous multi-joint pneumatic soft grippers are indispensable for daily object manipulation due to their inherent compliance. However, existing research suffers from a critical trade-off: multi-joint soft grippers only enable single-modal sensing, while dual-modal perception is limited to single-joint structures, which impedes precise control in complex scenarios. To address this issue, we propose the DM-BioGrip—a bio-inspired, deep learning (DL)-driven dual-modal proprioceptive-exteroceptive fusion system for multi-joint soft grippers, based on an optimized 6 wt% carbon black/silicone composite. This composite exhibit super stretchability (>300% strain) and reliable sensitivity with a gauge factor of 5.9 ± 0.37 (mean ± standard deviation, n = 5) at 200% strain, and the distributed sensing array of DM-BioGrip (6 proprioceptive sensors and 28 exteroceptive sensors) enables synchronous and high-precision capture of multi-joint bending states and contact interaction features. Experimental results from 10-fold cross-validation on 7 categories of spherical objects (900 grasping trials per object) show that the DL fusion strategy of DM-BioGrip achieves a 99.7% object recognition accuracy, outperforming the exteroceptive-only (99.0%) and proprioceptive-only (96.6%) single-modal strategies by resolving feature overlaps in single-modal perception. This work pioneers an integrated dual-modal perception strategy for multi-joint soft grippers, offering a practical and reliable solution for intelligent daily object manipulation and the engineering deployment of such devices.

Highly selective electrochemical urea synthesis via CN coupling from CO₂ and nitrate reduction on Cu2S/CuS catalyst
abstract: Electrochemical urea synthesis through CO₂ and nitrate reduction reaction is a promising sustainable alternative but is limited by inefficient C-N coupling and competing hydrogen evolution. Here, we report a sulfur-modulated Cu₂S/CuS electrocatalyst that promotes selective urea formation by tuning the adsorption of key intermediates. The catalyst achieves a urea yield of 260.8 ± 10.2 μg h⁻¹ cm⁻² with the highest remarkable faradaic efficiency of 80.0 ± 2.8% at -0.4 V versus RHE for a Cu-S based catalyst. In situ FTIR spectroscopy identifies *CO and *NO intermediates along with a C-N stretching signal, while isotopic HRMS confirms nitrate-derived nitrogen in the product. These results support a mechanism in which sulfur-modulated Cu^(δ+) -S sites enhance *CO-*NO coupling while suppressing hydrogen evolution (HER). This work highlights sulfur incorporation as an effective strategy to regulate intermediate adsorption and enable selective C-N coupling for urea electrosynthesis.

Experimental study and numerical simulation on a multi-stage counter-current continuous fluidized bed reactor for activating iron-based Fischer-Tropsch synthesis catalyst
abstract: Rapid and robust activation of iron-based catalysts is critical for industrial Fischer-Tropsch synthesis. This work introduces a multi-stage, counter-current continuous fluidized-bed system that enables uninterrupted catalyst activation, addressing key limitations of conventional batch fluidized beds. Compared with previous studies that mainly addressed batch activation or conventional fluidized-bed activation, the novelty of this work lies in the combined cold-flow, CFD, and hot-flow validation of a multi-stage counter-current continuous fluidized-bed reactor for iron-based catalyst activation. Cold-flow tracer-based RTD experiments were conducted in a transparent acrylic reactor, and hot-flow activation tests were performed in a stainless-steel reactor under syngas at 265 °C and 0.2 MPa. Cold-flow experiments show that the inter-stage overflow design ensures unidirectional particle transfer, markedly suppresses back-mixing, and improves plug-flow behavior. The dimensionless variance of the residence time distribution decreases from 1.0 to 0.475, while the fitted tanks-in-series number increases from 1.0 to 2.34. CFD simulations accurately reproduce the observed hydrodynamics and extend the analysis to operating limits, predicting an upper gas-velocity threshold of 0.29 m/s under cold-flow conditions. Hot-flow simulations based on the validated model identify a slightly lower limit of 0.27 m/s, which provides practical guidance for reactor design and scale-up. Hot-flow experiments confirm stable fluidization at 265 °C and 0.2 MPa with continuous catalyst feeding and withdrawal. The catalysts activated in the multi-stage continuous system exhibit CO conversions of 51 to 53% and CH 4 selectivities of approximately 1% in a stirred-tank evaluation reactor, achieving performance comparable to that obtained with our batch fluidized bed activation method.

Humidity-sensing and light-controlled steering azobenzene liquid crystal elastomer actuators
abstract: A main-chain liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) with amino-azobenzene mesogens was synthesized via thiol-acrylate Michael addition reaction and used to make rod actuators with aligned mesogens. The use of amino-azobenzene mesogens endows the LCE actuator with dual capabilities of colorimetric humidity sensing and light-controlled rolling motion on a hot substrate surface. On the one hand, a simple acid treatment results in protonation of surface amino-azobenzene moieties, enabling the LCE to change color reversibly depending on the relative humidity of its environment, with high humidity leading to deprotonation and low humidity prone for protonation. On the other hand, for LCE rod actuator rolling on a hot surface, localized light irradiation perturbs this self-sustained motion through photoisomerization and photothermal effects, achieving light-controlled braking, reversal, and steering. The irradiation intensity and position precisely modulate the parking time (duration of still state) and the curvature change, allowing navigable and obstacle-avoiding locomotion. This study demonstrates an integrated strategy to couple thermal and optical stimuli within a fully azobenzene-based LCE system, opening new opportunities for adaptive soft actuators and robots.

Stable single-membrane pH-decoupling aqueous all-organic flow batteries
abstract: The advancement of pH-decoupling aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) would enable high cell voltage and circumvent challenges in molecular engineering. However, traditional pH-decoupling AOFBs need the complicated three-chamber, two-membrane configuration and suffer from severe crossover issue. In the present work, stable pH-decoupling aqueous all-organic flow batteries (AAOFBs), separated with a single ion-exchange membrane, were first constructed by using the crossover-free NH2/NH3+ grafted bipyridinium and N-heterocycle-linked TEMPO (TMP-TEMPO) redox pair. The bipyridiniums with NH2/NH3+ terminals require minimal preparation steps and do not need an additional silica gel column. Notably, the NH2 and NH3+ groups, being strong hydrogen bond acceptor and donor respectively, restrict free diffusion of proton and hydroxide ions through the low-cost anion-exchange membrane and avoid their crossover contamination. As a consequence, stable single-membrane pH-decoupling AAOFBs at low concentration are demonstrated with an extremely low capacity fade rate of 0.22% per day over 638 cycles (~7 days), a high energy efficiency of ~88% and Coulombic efficiency of ~100%. The high-concentration pH-decoupling AAOFBs exhibited stable cycling performance even in a high O2 content environment (100 ppm) with a practical capacity of 10.7 Ah L-1, a capacity fade rate of 1.30% per day for 500 cycles, a Coulombic efficiency of ~99.8%, and an energy efficiency of 87%.

Antibacterial liquid tympanic membrane bandage for perforation repair and instant hearing restoration
abstract: Tympanic membrane (TM) perforation is a common otologic problem that can lead to conductive hearing loss and increase the risk of middle ear infection. However, current clinical repair techniques rely on complex procedures and autologous graft harvesting, which cause extra tissue injury and make rapid intervention difficult. Herein, we presented a convenient liquid-based TM repair strategy in which a “liquid TM bandage” can be dropwise applied onto the perforation and transformed to a thin and adherent membrane within 30 s at room temperature. This liquid-to-film transition enabled rapid functional restoration, improving auditory thresholds by approximately 20–30 dB sound pressure level (dB SPL) across multiple frequency bands and approaching normal hearing levels. Meanwhile, the liquid TM bandage possessed broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, reducing in vivo bacterial load by approximately 88% and thereby minimizing infection risk following perforation. Long-term evaluation demonstrated that liquid TM bandage induced no excessive inflammation or abnormal tissue reactions. This rapid, minimally invasive, and infection-resistant strategy represents a promising approach for TM repair and warrants further investigation toward future clinical translation.

A universal kinetic modeling framework based on SMILES-matrix mapping for emerging energy conversion processes
abstract: Modern petrochemical processes require precise kinetic descriptions of complex hydrocarbon conversion processes. Traditional modeling methods, which rely on predefined structural units, face challenges in exploring unknown chemical spaces introduced by new technologies such as external field intensification during the low-carbon transition of petrochemicals. To address this, this study proposes a SMILES-based Matrix Reaction Modeling (SMRM) framework. It uses SMILES as a universal molecular description foundation. By establishing a bidirectional mapping between SMILES and a multi-layer feature matrix, it formalizes chemical reaction rules into matrix-based operations, thereby eliminating dependence on predefined structures. The feature matrix is designed based on atomic connectivity and bond type principles, possessing independent global properties. Cases on catalytic pyrolysis and catalytic reforming demonstrate that this framework can generate complex networks containing hundreds of reactions based on SMILES and reaction rules. The absolute error in predicting all product yields from the model does not exceed 2.55 wt.%, showing good prediction accuracy and universality. This study provides a universal modeling approach for simulating complex reaction processes and exploring unknown chemical spaces.

title: Fe3O4@Fe SAN for peroxymonosulfate-assisted catalytic inactivation of Microcystis aeruginosa and degradation of microcystin-LR: Efficiency, mechanism and toxicity assessment
Continuous microfluidic assembly of core-shell DNTF composite microspheres via in situ photocuring for enhanced thermal stability and mechanical safety
abstract: The high mechanical sensitivity of 3,4-bis(3-nitrofurazan-4-yl)furoxan (DNTF) severely limits its safe processing and practical applications. Here, we developed a continuous microfluidic assembly strategy combined with in situ ultraviolet (UV) photocuring to produce DNTF/fluororubber (F2604)/hexafluorobutyl acrylate (HFBA) composite microspheres with a core–shell structure and high sphericity. By precisely matching multiphase fluid dynamics to photocrosslinking kinetics, a dense three-dimensional F/HFBA network was rapidly formed on the droplet surface, which resisted crystallization-induced stress and stabilized the interface. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations revealed enhanced interfacial interactions, in which HFBA, acting as a crosslinking monomer, increased the binding strength between DNTF and the polymer matrix. Differential scanning calorimetry showed that the dense shell layer shifted the thermal decomposition peak to 293–294 °C. Meanwhile, the viscoelastic dissipation of the crosslinked network significantly improved mechanical safety, reducing impact sensitivity from 100% to 44% and increasing friction sensitivity from 112 N to 360 N. This work provides an effective chemical engineering approach for stabilizing high-sensitivity energetic crystals and achieving safer high-energy composite systems.

title: Structurally disordered PdNi bimetallenes for coupled hydrogen production and PET upcycling at industrial-level current densities
abstract: The sustainable electrochemical upcycling of plastic waste into value-added chemicals while co-generating clean hydrogen offers a compelling strategy toward circular energy and materials systems. Herein, we report the synthesis of ultrathin, structurally disordered palladium–nickel bimetallenes (PdNi-bm) via a one-step solvothermal method. The incorporation of Ni into the Pd lattice induces charge redistribution and form heterogeneous Pd–Ni interfaces that enhance electron transfer and modulate the d-band structure. As a result, PdNi-bm exhibits exceptional bifunctional electrocatalytic activity for both the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) in alkaline media. The optimized PdNi-bm delivers a low overpotential of 86 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² for HER outperforming monometallic Pd metallenes. For EGOR, PdNi-bm achieves a significantly reduced overpotential (1.38 V vs. RHE) at 10 mA cm⁻² and high Faradaic efficiency (> 87%) for formate production. When applied to real PET hydrolysate, PdNi-bm enables efficient electro-upcycling at substantially anodic potentials, simultaneously generating hydrogen and valuable oxidation products (mainly formate). Integrated into a zero-gap membrane-electrode assembly, the PdNi-bm-based system achieves industrially relevant current densities of 0.6 A cm⁻² at only 1.82 V and maintains excellent operational stability over 100 h. This work highlights structurally disordered PdNi-bm as a robust and scalable bifunctional catalysts for simultaneous hydrogen production and PET waste valorisation.

title: Twisted biphenyl-mediated chain-packing regulation enables polybenzimidazole-based amphoteric membranes to decouple ionic conductivity from vanadium crossover for vanadium redox flow batteries
Supramolecular peptide coacervates for dual-hormone glycemic control via opposing glucose recognition mechanisms
abstract: Regulation of blood glucose requires coordinated, glucose-dependent secretion of insulin and glucagon, a balance lost in diabetes. While substantial effort has focused on engineering glucose-responsive insulin, strategies that integrate counter-regulatory glucagon delivery remain limited. Here, a fully synthetic, dual-hormone delivery system is reported that mimics key features of pancreatic function through inverse glucose-dependent release of insulin and glucagon. The system comprises a core-shell architecture in which a glucose-stabilized liquid–liquid phase separated core sequesters glucagon, while a glucose-responsive polymer shell presents insulin through competitive glucose binding. The core forms via supramolecular phase separation of a phenylboronic acid-modified peptide amphiphile and a glucagon analogue in the presence of glucose, releasing the glucagon under hypoglycemia. In parallel, insulin modified with a diboronate glucose-binding motif is retained in the shell via dynamic-covalent interactions and released preferentially at elevated glucose concentrations. This architecture yields reciprocal hormone release profiles across physiological glucose levels. In diabetic mice, the dual-hormone system corrects hyperglycemia while reducing the incidence and severity of hypoglycemia compared to insulin-only controls, including with repeated glucose challenges. These findings demonstrate a materials-based strategy for coupling glucose-responsive insulin delivery with intrinsic hypoglycemia protection, advancing the development of bioinspired, autonomous systems for diabetes management.

title: Tailoring a functional micro-environment via Pt single atoms on Ni4Mo to suppress OH poisoning for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Cost-effective transition-metal catalysts are attractive for industrial alkaline water electrolysis, yet their oxophilicity often causes overly strong OH* adsorption that blocks active sites and suppresses continuous H2O activation and H* turnover. Here, we construct a Pt-centered functional microenvironment by anchoring platinum single atoms on nickel-molybdenum (PtSA/Ni4Mo) via a two-step electrodeposition process, which regulates OH* at the interface. Pt single-atom modification substantially enhances Ni4Mo, decreasing η10 to 19 mV and η500 to 137 mV (Ni4Mo: 51 and 268 mV), while maintaining an advantage over Pt/C at high current and delivering kinetics (28.9 mV dec-1). Furthermore, the catalyst enables an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) to reach 1 A cm-2 at 1.97 V with stable operation beyond 200 h. Integrated SCN- poisoning, in situ Raman, CV, and EIS analyses collectively identify that Pt single atoms accelerate OH clearance on the OH-affinitive Ni₄Mo surface, thereby restores interfacial sites for water activation and shifts the kinetics toward a Heyrovsky-limited pathway. Density functional theory (DFT) further confirms weakened OH adsorption near Pt and a dramatically reduced OH desorption barrier, rationalizing the accelerated alkaline HER kinetics. This work highlights single-atom micro-environment engineering as an effective route to suppress OH poisoning for industrially relevant alkaline HER.

Molecular mechanisms of thermochemically-promoted precursor transformation to indole-3-acetic acid from sewage sludge via hydrothermal treatment: Comparative roles of H+/OH−
On environmental science computational labs
abstract: Environmental decisions increasingly require integration and quantification of numerous processes in models that connect molecular chemistry to landscape scales. Along with constraining data, such models can be used to discern the processes of greatest importance, to evaluate management options and to predict future trends. We elaborate on the concept of environmental science computational labs (ESCLs), namely coordinated virtual infrastructures and capabilities linking multiscale models, data systems and validation standards. We illustrate the relevance of this concept through elaborating on three physically different, but naturally interconnected environmental challenges related to perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). These include PFAS effects on natural source zone depletion (NSZD) of petroleum hydrocarbons, in-situ sensing in soil and groundwater and thermal destruction in incinerators.

Morphology and mechanism of highly SO2-resistant Pt/TiO2 catalyst for CO oxidation
Multiscale fluid transport in low-temperature electrolyzers and fuel cells: Linking transport phenomena with analytical technologies towards improved performance
abstract: Fluid transport in low-temperature water electrolyzers (LTWEs) and low-temperature fuel cells (LTFCs), spanning multiscale heterogeneous structures, significantly influences the production rate and energy conversion efficiency of green hydrogen energy. However, the contributions of underlying transport processes to the practical performance remain difficult to interpret, leading to a largely black-box understanding of transport-performance relations. This challenge is fundamentally constrained by the capabilities of available analytical techniques, particularly under realistic operating conditions. To address this gap, this review establishes a measurement-centred framework that links fluid transport phenomena with their intrinsic observability, thereby defining the current limits of performance interpretation. We first derive the key requirements of analytical techniques from fluid transport-induced performance limitations. Based on these requirements, we critically assess the capabilities and limitations of established optical, X-ray, and neutron based analytical methods. Particular emphasis is placed on emerging strategies, including embedded miniaturized sensors and ultrasonic techniques, which enable the transition from lab-scale observations towards operando diagnostics at device and system levels. Rather than treating these analytical techniques in isolation, this review highlights their complementary roles, defining the current observable space of fluid transport across scales. Recognizing the remaining gaps, it suggests that synergetic combinations of complementary analytical techniques may improve the effective interpretation of transport-performance relations across scales.

abstract: Recovering platinum efficiently and selectively from spent automotive catalysts has significant importance in easing the scarcity of platinum resources. In this work, a covalent organic framework connected by imine linkages, denoted as BTC-BN-COF, was rationally designed and synthesized via a one-step Schiff base reaction of 1,3,5-benzenetricarbaldehyde (BTC) and 4,4’-bianiline (BN). This research systematically explored critical factors such as pH value, contact time, initial Pt(Ⅳ) content, and interfering ions-influence the adsorption of Pt(Ⅳ) onto the BTC-BN-COF material. The adsorption results demonstrate that BTC-BN-COF exhibits a high Pt(Ⅳ) uptake capacity reaching 460.83 mg·g-1, and the adsorption behavior follows a typical monolayer chemisorption mechanism. Notably, BTC-BN-COF exhibits exceptional selectivity toward Pt(Ⅳ), with an adsorption efficiency exceeding 90% in a complex solution system. XPS and SEM analyses reveal that Pt(Ⅳ) adsorption is driven by electrostatic interactions between protonated imine nitrogen atoms and Pt(Ⅳ) chloro-complex anions. This study not only develops a stable and high-performance adsorbent but also provides a promising strategy for the efficient and selective recovery of platinum from spent automotive catalysts.
