Turning harm into benefit: Harnessing intratumoral bacteria as immunopotentiators for cascade-enhanced therapy of bacteria-associated colorectal cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy has shown promise in colorectal cancer, yet many patients fail to achieve satisfactory responses due to the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment promoted by intratumoral Fusobacterium nucleatum ( Fn ) colonization. Additionally, tumor hypoxia favors anaerobic bacterial growth while compromising oxygen-dependent therapies. Herein, a “turning harm into benefit” cascade strategy is developed to transform intratumoral bacteria from harmful factors into immunopotentiators through the ultrafacile intratumoral injection of potassium permanganate (KMnO₄). This KMnO₄-based cascade strategy not only utilizes its strong oxidative properties to achieve bactericidal and tumoricidal effects but also alleviates tumor hypoxia through in situ MnO₂ generation. Furthermore, it substantially enhances the subsequent cascade of Ce6-mediated sonodynamic therapy and anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (αPD-L1)-mediated immunotherapy for bacteria-associated colorectal cancer through multistep, orderly amplification effects. Besides, this in situ generation strategy achieves high raw material utilization and enables specific responsiveness to the tumor microenvironment. Compared to conventional nanomaterials, it also eliminates the need for complex external preparation and purification processes and overcomes the limitation of low tumor accumulation efficiency. Overall, the KMnO₄-based cascade strategy enabled by minimalist in situ injection provides a novel and practical approach for the treatment of bacteria-associated tumors.

title: Magnetically anchored nZVI on aldehyde-regulated Fe3O4 phenolic resin composites for efficient Fenton-like degradation of organic dyes: Performance, mechanism, and life cycle assessment
Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6-δ double perovskite for chemical-looping hydrogen production from water splitting
abstract: Chemical-looping water splitting represents a promising route for efficient and sustainable hydrogen production. In this work, H 2 generation was enhanced by engineering the B-site of SrFeO 3 -based perovskites (SFO) through Mo substitution (SFMO), yielding structurally stable oxides with improved redox properties. These materials were evaluated in CO-assisted chemical-looping water-splitting cycles inspired by the water-gas shift process. The Mo-doped double perovskites exhibited superior redox performance, absence of crystallographic transitions, resistance to morphological degradation, and stable operation over at least 24 consecutive cycles. A comprehensive parametric study was conducted—exploring reaction temperature, gas flow rates, and mass loading—to identify suitable operating conditions and extract data for kinetic modeling. To gain mechanistic insight into the water-splitting step, controlled H 2 -assisted reduction experiments were performed for transient kinetic analysis. The transient redox kinetic model developed revealed that, in materials with high oxygen diffusion rates, water splitting is governed by thermodynamics (i.e., equilibrium-limited) rather than reaction kinetics. Regarding the water splitting capacity, SFMO exhibited a H 2 production of ∼14 mL/g for 24 cycles, whereas it was 4.3 mL/g for SFO. This is a 3-fold increase in the H 2 yield, indicative of the benefits of Mo-incorporation on the water splitting reaction. These findings provide valuable insights into the development of robust oxygen carriers for scalable hydrogen production in chemical-looping systems.

title: One-step fabrication of bioinspired dual-domain hierarchical wrinkled superhydrophobic strain sensors for intelligent perception
abstract: Flexible strain sensors face a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and sensing range. Furthermore, the interfacial modulus mismatch induced by traditional multi-step fabrication often leads to delamination under complex operating conditions. Inspired by the hierarchical skin morphology of crocodile flanks, we report a one-step regional spraying method to fabricate a superhydrophobic sensor. Driven by a strain-stiffness mismatch, this sensor features a dual-domain hierarchical parallel wrinkled structure, consisting of a polydimethylsiloxane/carbon nanotubes (PDMS/CNTs) composite integrated onto a flexible latex substrate. By differentially modulating the microscopic conductive spacing, this structure achieves an exceptional hierarchical electromechanical response. Specifically, the dense wrinkles in the thin regions act as "strain amplifiers," inducing the rupture of percolation pathways under minute deformations. Conversely, the broad and sparse wrinkles in the thick regions function as "geometric strain buffers," maintaining the connectivity of the conductive network under large strains through geometric unfolding. Moreover, the in-situ induced wrinkles construct a stable Cassie-Baxter superhydrophobic barrier. This integrated "structure-interface-function" design effectively resolves the sensitivity-sensing range trade-off, delivering a high gauge factor (GF) of 7825.3 alongside a broad sensing range of 212%. The sensor additionally exhibits a low detection limit (0.5%), low hysteresis (4.82% at an extreme strain of 200%), and a rapid response time (180 ms). Crucially, the sensor maintains stable electrical and interfacial performance even after 20,000 s of dynamic fatigue testing, immersion in highly corrosive environments, and continuous fluid scouring. Integrated with machine learning clustering algorithms, the proposed sensor exhibits promising potential for intelligent interaction and advanced engineering applications across complex scenarios, including multidimensional physiological monitoring, underwater robotic perception, and tactile object recognition for smart grippers.

title: Highly efficient perovskite-based electrocatalyst with in-situ nanoparticle exsolution and oxygen-vacancy enhancement for solid oxide cells

abstract: Carbon materials containing dispersed nickel single atoms have shown excellent activity as electrocatalysts in different areas. This study reports the first application of a catalyst with Ni–N–C moieties to cathodic persulfate (PS) activation, an innovative route that triggers the in-situ production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). The presence of NiN 4 sites was unveiled via HAADF–STEM and synchrotron analysis. Ni–SAC was employed in persulfate reduction reaction (PSRR) to electrogenerate SO 4 •– radical in oxygenated medium. A remarkable decoupling of PSRR from undesired oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) was achieved, as evidenced by the much higher onset potential of the former (i.e., ∼1.16 V|RHE vs ∼0.45 V|RHE). Great selectivity was determined for PSRR (1e − route, yielding SO 4 •– ) and ORR (4e − route, yielding H 2 O). Degradation tests showed the ability of Ni–SAC to attain the complete elimination of the antibiotic piperacillin at 20 mA cm −2 , in both model and actual water matrices. Electron paramagnetic resonance revealed that SO 4 •– rather serves as precursor of other ROS like • H, • OH and H 2 O •+ . Of note, water radical cations are detected for the first time in PS-based advanced water treatment. Overall, our observations bring about new possibilities for more efficient wastewater treatment.

Sponge iron enables decoupled iron-driven autotrophic nitrate and ammonium removal from secondary effluent
abstract: Iron-driven autotrophic nitrogen removal offers a promising route for treating carbon-limited secondary effluent. Existing nitrate-dependent ferrous oxidation (NDFO) and ferric iron-mediated anaerobic ammonium oxidation (Feammox) systems, though effective, require strict stoichiometric coupling between nitrate and ammonium that is rarely satisfied in real wastewater. Results showed sponge iron functions as a solid-phase iron buffer, decoupling NDFO and Feammox. An anammox-inoculated up-flow anaerobic reactor treating simulated secondary effluent (10 mg N/L NO– 3 and 5 mg N/L NH+ 4) achieved stable effluent total nitrogen below 6.5 mg N/L, with nitrate and ammonium removal efficiencies of 56% and 52%, respectively. Batch experiments confirmed that nitrate was removed via Fe(II)-dependent NDFO without ammonium accumulation, while ammonium was oxidized via Fe(III)-mediated Feammox even in the absence of nitrate. Together, these results demonstrate the functional independence of the two nitrogen conversion pathways. Iron speciation and mineralogical analyses showed that sponge iron continuously supplied Fe(II) and Fe(III) mineral accumulated after long-term operation. Although mineral crystallization caused performance deterioration, acid regeneration of sponge iron restored the Fe(II)-releasing capability of sponge iron, thereby recovering its nitrate and ammonium removal performance. These results establish sponge iron-driven decoupled iron redox cycling as a robust platform for advanced autotrophic nitrogen removal from secondary effluent.

Sustainable production of WTR-derived adsorbents: Integrating life cycle assessment, hotspot analysis, and process optimization
abstract: Municipal drinking water treatment residuals are commonly landfilled despite containing aluminosilicate and metal hydroxide phases that can be converted into functional adsorbents. However, waste-derived materials are not inherently environmentally beneficial, particularly when chemical activation and thermal processing are required. This study developed ZnCl₂-activated adsorbents from water treatment residuals (WTR) and integrated material characterization, cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment, and machine-learning-based multi-objective optimization to identify synthesis conditions that balance adsorbent characteristics with environmental burden. Five synthesis scenarios were evaluated by varying pyrolysis temperature and ZnCl₂/WTR ratio. The optimal condition, 500 °C and ZnCl₂/WTR = 1.5, increased BET surface area from 107.97 to 271.38 m 2 g −1 and produced a micro-mesoporous structure while retaining surface hydroxyl functionality. ReCiPe 2016 midpoint and endpoint results showed that adsorbent production imposed higher impacts than direct landfilling per kilogram of WTR managed, mainly due to ZnCl₂ production, thermal energy demand, and drying operations. However, when expressed per kilogram of adsorbent, the optimized material showed a global warming potential of 5.35 kg CO₂ eq kg −1 , below reported coal-derived activated carbon benchmarks. Gaussian Process Regression coupled with Differential Evolution identified the 500 °C, 1.5 ratio condition as the sole Pareto rank-1 solution within the investigated design space. This study highlights that waste valorization is not inherently sustainable and becomes environmentally defensible only when process design is constrained by life cycle performance rather than driven solely by material optimization.

Intensification of chemical looping CO2 splitting process by reusing the CH4-rich tail gas stream from Fischer-Tropsch synthesis
abstract: The integration of Chemical Looping CO 2 Splitting (CLCO2SPLIT) technology with Fischer–Tropsch (F-T) synthesis offers a promising pathway to produce carbon-neutral, sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs). However, the effective utilization of F-T tail gas, particularly its methane fraction, is not yet fully understood. This study systematically evaluates the impact of CH 4 on the CLCO2SPLIT process using a highly reactive Fe-based oxygen carrier (ZrMg/Fe), combining mechanistic studies in a batch fluidized-bed reactor with performance tests in a 1 kW th continuous prototype. Continuous tests reveal CH 4 conversion rates of 70–75%, CO yields closely matching the predicted value based on thermodynamic equilibrium for the ZrMg/Fe material composition, and H 2 /CO ratios above the optimal range for F-T synthesis, regardless of the CH 4 injection point. The latter finding suggests that introducing CH 4 into the splitting reactor is more advantageous, as it enables hydrogen recirculation strategies in the fuel reactor to meet the composition and H 2 /CO ratio requirements at the F-T unit inlet. Supplementing the ZrMg/Fe material with a small amount (3 wt% of the mixture) of a Ni-based oxygen carrier, named as Ni18-αAl:HI, significantly reduces the concentration of unreacted CH 4 in the splitting stage, bringing it well below the maximum tolerable concentration in an F-T reactor. Overall, the results indicate that applying CLCO2SPLIT technology, combining the ZrMg/Fe oxygen carrier with small amounts of Ni-based materials, is an effective strategy to optimize the utilization of carbon introduced into an F-T unit for SAF production.

title: Enhanced activation of peracetic acid by Cu2O under sunlight through coordination environment regulation: Improved charge separation and peracetic acid adsorption/complexation via uncoordinated Cu atoms
Exhaust gas aftertreatment of dimethyl ether as a challenge for the carbon-neutral fuel in internal combustion engines
abstract: This study investigates the extent to which existing series exhaust aftertreatment catalysts, such as diesel oxidation catalysts (DOC) and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) catalysts, can be used to reduce emissions of unburned HC slip in the exhaust gas from the use of CO 2 -neutral dimethyl ether (DME) in internal combustion engines. It is shown that not all DOCs were able to completely prevent DME slip under the selected, close to realistic conditions such as gaseous hourly space velocity and temperature range. Also, the formation of toxic secondary emissions can be measured, during the light-off experiments. Furthermore, it is shown that depending on the SCR catalyst, the presence of DME at temperatures above T > 300 °C can lead to the release of significant amounts of toxic products such as HCN, CH 2 O, CH 2 O 2 and CO. These could furthermore deactivate the NH 3 -SCR catalyst. In addition, the DeNO x -performance is inhibited for the temperature range above T > 350 °C, when DME is converted during the SCR. Another novel finding is that the presence of formic acid may lead to a shift in the NO/NO 2 equilibrium and production of NO 2 in the corresponding temperature range.

Lignin supported bio-based multifunctional cellulose nanocrystal photonic films for sensing applications
abstract: Cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) derived photonic materials hold transformative potential for sustainable photonics, particularly in applications such as multifunctional sensors, intelligent detection, and information storage devices. However, their practical implementation is limited by mechanical fragility, strong dependence on substrate background for color visibility, and compromise between mechanical and optical properties associated with conventional plasticizers. Herein, a fully bio-based lignin-CNC-glycerol bilayer architecture is developed, where a CNC photonic layer is assembled on glycerol-doped lignin substrates to enhance flexibility, hygroscopicity, adhesion, and tune optical properties. Lignin provides intrinsic light-absorbing properties, serving as a built-in dark background for background-independent structural coloration. The resulting bilayer films exhibit pronounced angle-dependent structural color and markedly improved thermal stability, with maximum decomposition temperatures delayed to 390–393 °C due to the high thermal resistance of lignin and strong CNC-lignin interfacial interactions. Nanoindentation analysis reveals glycerol-induced surface softening of the photonic layer, which regulates swelling behavior and enables reversible optical responses under humidity and solvent stimuli. Furthermore humidity-driven bending arises from swelling-induced strain mismatch between layers, producing reversible actuation across 64–94% relative humidity. Overall, this work offers a multifunctional, sustainable platform for responsive photonic materials, providing a versatile approach for environmentally friendly sensors, smart coatings, and information storage systems.

title: Condensate-boosted SOD/CAT-mimetic nanozyme reactivity for antioxidant therapy of wear particle-induced periprosthetic osteolysis
Reversed adsorption of C2H6 over C2H4 in amino-functionalized MOFs for one-step ethylene purification
abstract: In the current chemical industry, the one-step efficient separation of ethylene from acetylene/ethane/ethylene ternary mixtures remains a technical challenge. This study proposed a Lewis basic functionalization strategy by introducing amino functional groups into JLU-Liu37, successfully constructing two functionalized materials, JLU-Liu37-NH2 and JLU-Liu37-(NH2)2. Experimental results demonstrated that the incorporation of amino groups significantly enhanced the binding affinity for acetylene, increasing the C2H2 adsorption capacity from 4.16 to 5.16 mmol·g-1 (JLU-Liu37-NH2) and 5.05 mmol·g-1 (JLU-Liu37-(NH2)2), respectively. Concurrently, IAST selectivity calculations revealed that the C2H2/C2H4 (50/50) selectivity increased from 1.2 to 1.36 and 1.45. Furthermore, calculations based on the Qst confirmed that JLU-Liu37-(NH2)2 exhibited the most pronounced variation in the Qst between C2H2 and C2H4. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further validated the strong performance of JLU-Liu37-(NH2)2 in C2H6/C2H4 separation. GCMC calculations indicated that JLU‐Liu37‐(NH2)2 functionalized with nitrogen sites interacted more favorably with acetylene and ethane in comparison to ethylene. Therefore, JLU-Liu37-(NH2)2 demonstrated practical potential for one-step ethylene separation.

Dynamic non-covalent synergistic zwitterionic hydrogel for wearable strain sensing and human-machine interaction
abstract: Inspired by the synergistic coupling of multiple weak interactions in natural extracellular matrices, here a triple-synergistic biomimetic double-network ionic conductive hydrogel (Zn-ICH) strategy is proposed to achieve high-performance flexible strain sensors with balanced comprehensive properties. Specifically, the rigid polyacrylamide/sulfobetaine methacrylate (PAM/SBMA) covalent network provides structural stability under large deformations, while the reversible Zn²⁺-sodium alginate (Zn²⁺-SA) dynamic coordination network enables efficient energy dissipation, and the zwitterionic glycerol hydration microenvironment ensures continuous ion transport, robust interfacial adhesion and wide-temperature tolerance, breaking the inherent performance trade-offs of conventional conductive hydrogels. The Zn-ICH-based strain sensor exhibits a gauge factor of 0.93-1.29 over 0-500% strain, enabling reliable detection of human motions and physiological signals. Furthermore, the constructed wearable human-machine interaction system enables stable and near-real-time robotic arm actuation with a motion synchronization accuracy of 99%. Additionally, when used as a zinc-ion capacitor electrolyte, the Zn-ICH hydrogel enables the flexible device to deliver a specific capacity of 150 mAh·g-1 at 0.3 A·g-1 and maintain 95% capacity retention after 5000 cycles. This work establishes a universal design principle for multifunctional conductive hydrogels, offering broad application prospects in wearable electronics and flexible energy storage.

Machine learning-optimized coarse-grained simulations reveal multicomponent solvent-regulated phase separation for precise control of porous polymers
abstract: Precise control of pore structures in porous polymers is critical for optimizing their functional performance. Although third solvent-assisted phase separation has been experimentally demonstrated to promote pore interconnectivity and structural tunability, the molecular mechanisms governing this process remain largely unresolved. Here, we develop a machine learning-assisted dissipative particle dynamics (DPD) force fields that bridges all-atom-level accuracy and coarse-grained efficiency through data-driven force field generation. By training on structural descriptors derived from all-atom simulations, the optimized DPD force fields reliably reproduce intermolecular interactions in multicomponent solvent systems. Applying this optimized force field to polylactic acid ternary solvent systems, we reveal how the third solvent modulates phase separation behavior and propose a quantitative solvent-selection principle based on polarity and interaction energy. Experimental validation confirms the predictive capability of the model in guiding pore morphology control. Together, these results provide molecular-level insights and a practical framework for multicomponent solvent engineering, offering a pathway toward the rational fabrication advanced porous polymer materials with precisely controllable structures.

abstract: Nanoplastics are widely recognized as persistent environmental pollutants that require removal from aquatic systems. Here, we propose an alternative strategy based on the functional valorization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) nanoplastics through their integration into magnetic hybrid materials. Mesocrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers (NF) were synthesized via a rapid microwave-assisted polyol route, producing multicore magnetic architectures capable of efficiently capturing dispersed PET nanoplastics. The NFs exhibit a capture capacity of up to 10,000 mg of NanoPET per gram of magnetic collector, enabling rapid magnetic harvesting of nanoplastics from aqueous media. Instead of treating the collected plastic as waste, the captured NanoPET is incorporated into PET/NF hybrid materials, where the nanoplastics become a structural and functional component of the system. FTIR analysis reveals the interfacial interactions responsible for NanoPET/NF formation, confirming the adhesion of the nanoflowers to the PET surface. The resulting NanoPET/NF combine magnetic recoverability (v s= 1.35 × 10 −4 m/s with ∇H = 24 T/m) with adsorption and catalytic functionalities, exhibiting adsorption capacities of 25 mg/g for methylene blue and achieving a 11% higher degradation than at 25 °C under alternating magnetic field activation (200 kHz, 24 kA/m), through localized magnetic heating without bulk heating of the medium. The sample retained both their magnetic recoverability and catalytic activity over multiple reuse cycles. This work provides a pathway to valorize plastic nanowaste into recoverable systems for magnetically-assisted advanced water treatment.

Transparent and thermally super-insulating κ-carrageenan aerogels
abstract: This study presents a facile strategy for fabricating transparent κ-carrageenan aerogels via multivalent metal-ion crosslinking, polarity-gradient solvent exchange, and supercritical carbon dioxide drying. The structural evolution of the κ-carrageenan gel network toward a nanofibrous architecture was further elucidated by SAXS. The resulting aerogels exhibited a unique combination of high optical transparency (up to 79.39%), high specific surface area (442.9-504.9 m2 g-1), ultralow thermal conductivity (14.84-17.22 mW m-1 K-1), and low bulk density (54.42-77.33 mg cm-3). In addition, the crosslinking-induced structural and chemical changes in κ-carrageenan were systematically investigated by FT-IR, XRD, and XPS, while the thermal stability and compressive mechanical performance of the aerogels were also comprehensively evaluated. Owing to their highly transparent nanostructure and excellent thermal insulation capability, the κ-carrageenan aerogels developed in this work demonstrate a highly competitive property profile among polysaccharide-based aerogels reported to date and hold considerable promise for transparent thermal insulation applications.

title: Interrogating vascular determinants of repair: Biofabricated constructs for precision intervention in peripheral neuropathies
abstract: Peripheral neuropathies (PN) exact a devastating global toll, manifest across traumatic and non-traumatic spectra and culminating in intractable pain, sensorimotor impairment, and chronic disablement. Converging upon a shared pathological crux, these conditions implicate destabilization of the neurovascular niche, a derangement that impairs perfusion, metabolic supply, and axonal pathfinding signals. Vascular dysfunction thus constitutes a unifying therapeutic lever. Synthesizing clinical, bibliometric, and single-cell transcriptomic evidence, this review delineates neurovascular crosstalk as instrumental to both disease progression and regenerative capacity. Advanced biomaterial-enabled, vascular-guided engineering platforms, refined through contemporary fabrication technologies, present incisive interventions to surmount this barrier. Therapeutic strategies are demarcated by PN subtype, while modifications aimed at promoting concurrent angiogenesis and neural repair receive exhaustive exposition. Prevailing evidence consolidates in advocacy of a vasculocentric framework. Translational impediments and emergent prospects are surveyed to accelerate clinical fruition.

abstract: Two-dimensional conductive metal-organic frameworks (2D c-MOFs) have shown great potential as advanced functional materials, among which Ni3(HITP)2, a newly developed 2D c-MOF material, has attracted extensive research interest due to its unique structural and electronic properties. However, the effective regulation of the gas-sensing performance of Ni3(HITP)2 remains a critical challenge in the field of 2D c-MOFs. To address this challenge, we propose a rational dual-functionalization regulation strategy by combining metal oxide quantum dots and noble metal nanoparticles, aiming to provide new insights for the performance regulation of 2D c-MOFs. Specifically, 2D Ni3(HITP)2 nanosheets were first synthesized through a solvothermal method, then functionalized with SnO2 quantum dots (QDs) to construct stable heterostructures, followed by the incorporation of Au nanoparticles for further modification. This dual-functionalization strategy effectively regulated and significantly enhanced the NO2-sensing properties of Ni3(HITP)2, with key performance parameters: an enhanced response (30.49% at 100 ppm), rapid response/recovery speeds (24/55 s), a low detection limit (90 ppb), as well as excellent repeatability, long-term stability, and good humidity resistance. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations from the first-principles perspective were employed to clarify the underlying regulation mechanism, confirming the crucial roles of Au nanoparticles and SnO2 QDs. This work successfully achieves effective regulation of Ni3(HITP)2 and offers a feasible strategy for the performance regulation of 2D c-MOF materials.

Dual-level electron storage in cyano-modified carbon nitride/MoO3(WO3) heterojunctions for round-the-clock photocatalysis
abstract: Conventional photocatalytic systems typically suffer from a rapid decline in catalytic activity once light irradiation ceases, rendering them poorly suited to the practical demand for continuous purification under natural day-night cycling conditions. In this work, a ”dual-level electron storage” strategy is proposed to construct all-weather photocatalysts based on heterojunctions composed of molten-salt-assisted synthesized cyano-modified carbon nitride (CCN) coupled with MoO3 or WO3 (denoted as CCN-M and CCN-W). In this architecture, CCN functions as a shallow-level electron reservoir, while MoO3/WO3 serves as a deep-level, high-capacity electron storage medium via reversible valence-state transitions and oxygen-vacancy-mediated trapping, thereby achieving a synergistic integration of high photocatalytic activity and large-capacity energy storage. Performance evaluations demonstrate that under visible-light irradiation, the system enables rapid and efficient inactivation of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, while retaining pronounced antibacterial efficacy in the dark after photocharging. Moreover, CCN-M3 and CCN-W3 exhibit considerable degradation potential toward polystyrene (PS) microplastic model pollutants under xenon lamp illumination, LED illumination, and simulated daily light–dark cycling conditions. Comprehensive characterization further confirms the sustained generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) during both illuminated and non-illuminated stages. The electron storage capacities of CCN-M3 and CCN-W3 reach 1.209 and 1.006 mmol·g-1, respectively, with stable energy retention exceeding 40 days under inert atmospheres. This study offers a novel design paradigm for the development of efficient, robust, and continuously operable photocatalytic materials capable of round-the-clock environmental remediation.

abstract: With the rapid expansion of electronic technologies, electromagnetic (EM) pollution has become a major concern, threatening device performance and human health. In this study, thin and flexible PVDF-based nanocomposite films containing 5 wt% graphene oxide (GO) and 5 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT) showed high electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness (EMI SE) and absorption for EMI protection. The films were fabricated via solution casting using an acetone/dimethylformamide (DMF) mixed solvent system. The solvent ratio strongly influenced crystallinity, dispersion, and electrical conductivity, thereby affecting EMI SE. At 70 vol% acetone, the PVDF/CNT/GO film achieved an average EMI SE of 20.9 dB and a normalized EMI SE (SE/t) of 131.1 dB/mm, with a reflectance coefficient of 0.85 and conductivity of 1.5 S/m. Building on these results, multilayer structures were designed to reduce reflectance and enhance EMI SE, mitigating secondary EMI pollution. A four-layer structure composed of PVDF/CNT/GO and PVDF/GO conductive layers separated by PVDF spacers showed superior performance. The multilayer structure was fabricated by a simple stacking method using PVDF solution as binder at room temperature, eliminating hot-press or compression molding, reducing energy consumption, and preserving filler distribution. The resulting structure achieved an SE/t of 40.8 dB/mm at a thickness of 0.6 mm and a reduced reflectance ratio of 0.55. The multilayer films exhibited ductile mechanical behavior with a yield strength of 10 MPa and strain at break of 80%. Furthermore, their strain-sensing capability with a gauge factor of 143.5 suggests potential use for flexible and sensitive film applications. Overall, this study presents a lightweight, flexible, and robust EMI shielding films for advanced electromagnetic protection applications.

Interfacial proton shuttling driven by tertiary amine enrichment enables low-energy CO2 desorption for biphasic ionic liquid systems
abstract: Industrial phase-change CO2 absorbents remain constrained by high regeneration energy and sluggish kinetics. Here, seven representative tertiary amines were systematically screened, identifying N, N-dimethylethanolamine (DMEA) as an optimal regulator. A multicomponent phase-change solvent was thus constructed using water, ethylene glycol butyl ether (EGBE), a functionalized ionic liquid ([DETA+MTZ−]), and DMEA (2:5:2.5:0.5, denoted as 2H5E2.5D0.5A). The incorporation of DMEA couples interfacial activity with proton transfer, simultaneously accelerating phase separation and enhancing mass transfer. As a result, the system exhibits markedly enhanced desorption performance, achieving high regeneration efficiency (81.57% at 373.15 K) over 55 cycles with less than 18% overall performance decay (including CO2 absorption capacity and desorption efficiency), together with a low regeneration energy consumption of 1.77 GJ·t−1 CO2. Mechanistic analyses combining NMR and theoretical calculations reveal that protonated DMEA dynamically reconstructs the hydrogen-bond network and destabilizes carbamate species. Assisted by water-mediated proton shuttling, the reaction pathway shifts toward a bicarbonate/carbonate-dominated route, thereby promoting CO2 release. In addition, interfacial enrichment of DMEA reduces interfacial tension and suppresses droplet coarsening, further intensifying interfacial mass transfer. Overall, this work establishes a synergistic mechanism of interfacial proton shuttling and phase-transition regulation, offering a viable pathway toward low-energy and rapid CO2 capture.

title: Cascaded catalytic amplification by a phenylboronate ester-based double-network hydrogel for synergistic eradication of multidrug-resistant bacteria and diabetic wound healing
abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are plagued by hyperglycemic microenvironments, multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial colonization and biofilm formation. In this study, glucose oxidase (GOx)/ 60 nm CuS nanoparticles were incorporated into an adhesive phenylboronic acid-modified, hyaluronic acid/quaternized chitosan (HA-PBA/QCS) dynamic boronate hydrogel (GS 128 @HPQ). GOx catalyzes glucose to generate H 2 O 2 , and CuS, under 808 nm near-infrared irradiation, acts as a Fenton-like catalyst to generate ·OH and also displays photothermal activity that elevates local temperatures to 45–65 °C in vitro, resulting in a synergistic antibacterial effect. The hydrogel has a porous structure with a pore size of approximately 50 μm, exhibits reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive drug release, possesses excellent mechanical properties including favorable rheological behavior, a tensile strength of 140 kPa, and self-healing capacity, and demonstrates adhesion properties ideal for wound dressing applications. In vitro, HA-PBA/QCS showed >98% MDR bacterial and more than 85% biofilm clearance. In diabetic mouse infected wound models, the wound area was <5% on Day21, with a > 70% downregulation of inflammation biomarkers IL-6/TNF-α and upregulation of VEGF/CD31, enables rapid re-epithelialization and collagen maturation, while the hydrogel has a hemolysis rate of less than 5%. This hydrogel provides a safe, efficient, and multifunctional platform for treating chronically infected diabetic wounds.

Can semiconductor photocatalysis be driven by bio-based irradiation? Quantitative analysis of photon flux thresholds and physical limits
abstract: In this work, we present the first quantitative evaluation of biological light sources, including fluorescence from UV-excitable Green Fluorescent Protein (GFPuv), the luciferin-luciferase system, and bioluminescent Vibrio harveyi , as irradiation sources for ZnIn 2 S 4 (ZIS)-based photocatalysts for hydrogen generation. Dedicated photoreactor prototypes were developed to improve photon transfer and light coupling between biological emitters and photocatalytic systems, enabling quantitative assessment of the engineering feasibility of biologically driven photocatalysis. A highly active visible-light photocatalyst (7.5% Cu-doped ZnIn 2 S 4 modified with 0.5% Pt nanoparticles) achieved a hydrogen evolution rate of 25.8 mmol g −1 h −1 under visible-light irradiation (λ > 420 nm), while the apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) reached 2.7% at 320 nm and 2.6% at 400 nm. The cultivation conditions of GFP-tagged Vibrio harveyi were optimized, resulting in a maximum bioluminescence emission power of 0.45 μW. Furthermore, the minimum light intensity required to initiate photocatalytic hydrogen evolution was experimentally determined to be approximately 20 μW, revealing a significant photon flux gap between biological emission and photocatalyst activation requirements. This work establishes, for the first time, quantitative engineering criteria for biologically driven photocatalytic systems, including spectral matching between emission and photocatalyst absorption, minimum excitation thresholds, emission stability, and efficient photoreactor design for effective photon utilization.

abstract: As a pivotal functional motifs in advanced dyes, pharmaceuticals, and optical storage systems, azobenzene compounds demand sustainable synthetic routes; yet, achieving exceptional selectivity in the aerobic oxidation of anilines without harsh reagents continues to be a formidable challenge. Plasmonic photocatalysis offers a sustainable pathway, but integrating multiple functional components to simultaneously coordinate light harvesting, charge separation, and reactant activation remains a major limitation. Herein, we propose a closo-[B12H12]2--mediated in situ construction strategy to successfully fabricate a ternary Ag/FeB/BCN plasmonic photocatalyst for the visible-light-driven, high-efficiency aerobic oxidation of aniline to azobenzene. By exploiting the dual role of the boron cluster as both a dopant and reducing agent, we enable the nucleation of Fenton-like FeB nanoparticles within a two-dimensional boron carbon nitride (BCN)matrix. Subsequently, silver (Ag) nanoparticles (average diameter 4.15 nm) are photodeposited to broaden light absorption and facilitate hot-electron injection via the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect, injecting hot electrons while the FeB sites continuously activate molecular oxygen. Under 450 nm blue-light irradiation at room temperature, the optimal 6% Ag/FeB/BCN catalyst achieves a 70.1% azobenzene yield with >99% selectivity, a turnover number (TON) of 12.6, and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 1.58 h-1. Radical trapping experiments reveal that four reactive species-·O2-, h+, e-, and ·OH-cooperatively participate in a cascade reaction. The catalyst displays broad substrate scope for 11 aromatic amines, affording yields of 59%-82%. The developed boron cluster-mediated in situ construction strategy provides a highly programmable platform for designing complex plasma structures and advances the green synthesis of azobenzene compounds.

Assembloid-like odontogenic-angiogenic microspheroids promote dental-pulp regeneration via CX26-CFOS signaling
abstract: Conventional two-dimensional (2D) dental pulp culture models are limited by their inability to recapitulate native tissue complexity and their frequent dependence on exogenous scaffolds. Here, we engineer scaffold-free, assembloid-like microspheroids that integrate stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHED) with human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) to model physiological odontogenic-angiogenic coupling. Three-dimensional (3D) SHED micro-spheroids significantly upregulate key odontogenic markers (DMP1, DSPP) and the angiogenic factor VEGFA compared to 2D cultures. When co-assembled with HUVECs, the resulting microspheroids further amplify the expression of angiogenic markers (CD31, EMCN) and the osteo/odontogenic transcription factor RUNX2. Subcutaneous transplantation in nude mice reveals that these SHED–HUVEC microspheroids generate robust type H vascular networks and extensive mineralized dentin-like structures, outperforming SHED-only constructs. Mechanistically, 3D self-assembly activates the gap junction protein connexin 26 (CX26) and the immediate-early transcription factor CFOS in SHED. CX26/CFOS signaling collectively promote the upregulation of VEGFA, DMP1, and DSPP, a regulatory axis validated through loss-of-function studies. Our findings establish a potent, scaffold-free micro-spheroid platform for functional dental pulp regeneration and uncover the CX26/CFOS pathway as a master regulator of vascularized dental tissue formation, offering a translatable strategy for clinical pulp engineering.

A safety-driven approach for the scale-up of membrane production processes
abstract: The development and scale-up of innovative chemical processes require the simultaneous optimisation of performance, sustainability, and safety. However, safety is often marginally considered in early-stage design, leading to suboptimal scale-up. In this work, a phenomenology-driven methodology is proposed for inherent safety assessment by integrating mechanistic interaction mapping with targeted experimental validation. The approach combines identification of key monitoring and influencing parameters with production of interaction matrices and controlled thermal-stress data to detect critical process–material interactions at low technology readiness levels. The methodology was applied to novolac-based carbon membranes, focusing on replacing N -methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) with γ-valerolactone (GVL). Cone calorimeter tests (7–50 kW/m 2 ) were conducted to assess ignitability, flame behaviour, and exhaust emissions. The novolac/NMP system showed rapid ignition and sustained combustion, with peak heat release rates above 1000 kW/m 2 . In contrast, novolac/GVL exhibited reduced ignition propensity (∼10–15%) and lower smoke and CO emissions (up to ~30%), as quantified through normalised safety-ranking indicators derived from cone calorimeter measurements (based on time-to-ignition, heat release rate, mass loss rate, and gas emission metrics), while maintaining similar thermal activation of the polymer. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables comparison of alternative formulations by jointly addressing performance and safety under thermal stress, supporting safer and more sustainable early-stage process design.

title: Liquid metals as active triboelectric media: Dynamic soft-matter architectures for adaptive energy harvesting and soft intelligent systems
Green and blue methanol: Biomass or DAC carbon combined with SMR and Allam–Fetvedt cycle
abstract: Low-carbon methanol production faces a trade-off between cost and depth of decarbonization. This study compares four small modular reactor (SMR)-assisted methanol pathways at 100 kt MeOH/yr: biomass with the Allam–Fetvedt cycle (Case 1), biomass only (Case 2), direct air capture (DAC) with the Allam–Fetvedt cycle (Case 3), and DAC only (Case 4). Solid oxide electrolysis produces syngas or hydrogen and oxygen; in Allam–Fetvedt-integrated cases, oxygen is used for oxy-fuel combustion with geological CO 2 sequestration. The levelized cost of methanol (LCOM) is $802, $762, $1167, and $1,068/ton for Cases 1–4, respectively. The gross carbon footprint is reduced by 83.5%, 93.5%, 64.8%, and 96.2%, relative to the fossil baseline of 0.630 tCO 2 /tMeOH. Under chemical use, Cases 1, 3, and 4 are carbon-negative, with Case 3 reaching − 2.429 tCO 2 /tMeOH. Under fuel use, reemission of DAC-derived CO 2 shifts Cases 3 and 4 to − 0.913 and 0.024 tCO 2 /tMeOH. The required carbon price, C P ∗ , quantifies this trade-off: despite the highest LCOM, Case 3 has the lowest C P ∗ at $251/tCO 2 (chemical use) due to high mitigation depth. Under fuel use, C P ∗ for Cases 3 and 4 rises to $497 and $1,102/tCO 2 . With 45Q tax credits (chemical use), these decrease to $155 and $222/tCO 2 , both below the IEA NZE 2050 benchmark ($250/tCO 2 ); under fuel use, no pathway meets this threshold. Nuclear lifecycle water contributes 51%–69% of the water footprint, constraining deployment beyond carbon pricing. Capture-based incentives partly close the fossil-methanol cost gap.

abstract: Focused microwave (MW) heating of Ni/SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 catalysts achieved “ultra-fast” catalytic pyrolysis of lignocellulose. The MW frequency and the cavity resonator's quality factor effectively accelerated the pyrolysis of bamboo to produce hydrogen more rapidly than conventional heating. In situ XAFS and in situ XRD provided experimental evidence for the formation of locally heated regions on Ni nanoparticles under MW irradiation. In particular, MW irradiation induced rapid Ni nanoparticle sintering at apparent bulk temperatures of 350–400 °C, whereas comparable sintering was not observed under conventional heating even at 1000 °C. These results support the presence of local high-temperature regions on Ni nanoparticles, although the exact local temperature under reaction conditions remains difficult to quantify. We conclude that MW irradiation accelerates the catalytic reforming of biomass by directly coupling MW energy to Ni nanoparticles and generating local hot spots.

Engineering electrode-scale conductive interfaces for durable micron-sized silicon anodes
abstract: Micro-sized silicon particle (SiMP) anodes offer high practical energy density and good manufacturing compatibility for lithium-ion batteries but suffer from severe volume expansion and interfacial instability during cycling. Herein, we report a simple and scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize SiMP anodes by post-coating pre-fabricated electrodes with a water-processable poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) and poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) mixture as a functional overlayer. The conformal PEDOT:PSS/PAA (P:PP) layer simultaneously provides mechanical buffering and electronic conduction, enabling homogeneous current distribution and regulated interfacial reactions. As a result, the P:PP-coated anode exhibits markedly improved cycling stability and rate capability, along with reduced interfacial resistance compared to the bare Si anode. Morphological analyses reveal that deformation and electrode thickening are effectively constrained beneath the P:PP layer, preserving macroscopic surface planarity and mitigating the electrical isolation of fractured Si fragments. Furthermore, post-mortem analyses indicate that the P:PP overlayer promotes the formation of a LiF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with reduced accumulation of fluorophosphate species, suggesting more effective interfacial passivation. Notably, the P:PP-coated SiMP anode retains ~80% of its capacity (~2,160 mAh g-1) after 150 cycles at 0.5C (2.1 A g-1), highlighting the effectiveness of this scalable aqueous post-coating strategy for durable, high-capacity Si anodes under practical conditions.

Stress-homogenized and solvation-regulated biomass hydrogel inducing Zn (101) epitaxial growth for ultra-stable anodes
abstract: Crystallographic orientation and interfacial integrity dictate the reversibility of aqueous zinc-ion batteries at high current densities. To mitigate unstable growth, weak interactions, and uneven stress on the (002) and (100) planes, mechanically confining deposition to the robust (101) facet is vital, as its strong adsorption and rapid charge transfer prevent dendrite-induced failure at high cumulative capacity. Herein, we designed a degradable, mechanically tough, and carboxyl-rich biomass hydrogel to induce sustained Zn (101) epitaxial growth. It is shown that abundant carboxyl groups reconstruct the Zn2+ solvation sheath, suppressing free water activity and selectively shielding reactive (002) and (100) facets via competitive occupation, thereby thermodynamically directing (101) nucleation. Simultaneously, the cross-linked cellulose network delivers high toughness and a high elastic modulus, dissipating interfacial stress to preserve structural integrity against volume fluctuations. This dual regulation lowers the desolvation barrier, homogenizes ion flux, and physically suppresses dendrites, enabling dense (101)-textured deposition. Consequently, symmetric cells achieve an exceptional cumulative capacity of 6000 mAh cm-2 at 5 mA cm-2/5 mAh cm-2, while Zn//Cu cells maintain 99.31% coulombic efficiency over 2000 cycles. This work establishes a precise mechano-chemical strategy for crystallographic regulation toward ultra-stable zinc anodes.

Polyphenol-assisted photocatalytic antibacterial efficacy enhancement of graphitic carbon nitride
abstract: Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is capable of efficiently absorbing electromagnetic waves in the visible light range, thereby generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) with excellent antibacterial activity. However, the ROS produced by photocatalysis exhibit non-selectivity toward bacterial cells, which may lead to oxidative damage to surrounding tissues during the sterilization process. This inherent limitation has hindered the practical application of g-C3N4 in the biomedical field. In this work, surface modification of g-C3N4 nanomaterials was carried out using polyphenols. The modified g-C3N4 nanomaterials not only displayed a significantly enhanced photocatalytic antibacterial effect but also avoided oxidative damage to normal cells and tissues induced by excessive ROS. Furthermore, the polyphenol layer anchored on the surface of the nanomaterials facilitated the loading and targeted delivery of drugs, enabling a dual antibacterial effect through the synergy of photocatalysis and drug therapy. This synergetic effect further improved the overall antibacterial efficacy and expanded the potential application scope of g-C3N4. Additionally, combining modified g-C3N4 with hydrogels yielded composite hydrogels, which exhibited excellent antibacterial and wound-healing-promoting effects in infected wound repair. This study provides a referenceable strategy for photocatalytic materials in biomedicine.

abstract: Integrated CO₂ capture and methanation (ICCM) provides a direct route for converting captured CO₂ into synthetic methane, but its large-scale implementation is limited by material stability and sustainability. Here, we report NiCeO₂/ionic clay hybrid materials, where the ionic clay is a Mg–Al carbonate layered double hydroxide (LDH) acting as an adsorbent matrix for NiCeO₂ catalytic nanoparticles. The hybrids exhibit enhanced CO₂ uptake, efficient low-temperature operation (300 °C) with 100% CH₄ selectivity, and excellent cyclic stability under ICCM conditions. Although the NiCeO₂/LDH hybrids show lower methane productivity per unit mass of total material than NiCeO₂ alone, they significantly improve catalyst utilization, producing up to four times more CH₄ per unit mass of NiCeO₂. Operando XANES reveals a reversible Ni⁰/Ni²⁺ redox transition under alternating CO₂/H₂ atmospheres, demonstrating that the active Ni phase dynamically adjusts its oxidation state during CO₂ adsorption–hydrogenation cycles. Life cycle assessment demonstrates a markedly reduced environmental footprint for the hybrid materials compared with NiCeO₂ for the same methane output, highlighting NiCeO₂/LDH hybrids as sustainable and scalable platforms for integrated CO₂ capture and conversion.

Core–shell hard carbon with enriched closed pores and controlled defects for enhanced sodium-ion battery performance
abstract: The synergistic regulation of pore structure and defects is essential for optimizing the sodium storage performance of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Herein, we combine pre-oxidation with N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide (MBA) crosslinking for precise structural modulation of starch at the molecular level, enabling the formation of a thermally stable three-dimensional network. During pyrolysis, the starch-derived network inhibits carbon skeleton collapse and disordered graphitic rearrangement while inducing controlled bending of carbon layers to generate abundant closed pores. Concurrently, nitrogen heteroatoms are covalently incorporated into the carbon lattice, generating extrinsic defects that modulate the electronic structure and enhance sodium-ion transport kinetics. Subsequently, a uniform, ultrathin, and conformal carbon shell is deposited onto the hard carbon via chemical vapor deposition (CVD). This shell effectively seals open pores, promotes stable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation, and mitigates interfacial side reactions and irreversible Na loss. The resulting core–shell hard carbon anode delivers a high reversible capacity of 372 mAh g⁻¹ at 30 mA g⁻¹, an impressive initial Coulombic efficiency of 88.2%, along with superior rate capability and cycling stability. In situ X-ray diffraction and electrochemical analyses reveal that this precisely tailored microarchitecture enables a sequential sodium storage mechanism of ”adsorption–intercalation–pore filling.” This study establishes a scalable and commercially viable strategy for converting renewable starch into high-performance hard carbon anodes for next-generation SIBs.

Microporous photocrosslinked silk-tropoelastin hydrogels for tissue engineering applications
abstract: Hydrogels are widely used in tissue engineering, but conventional nanoporous hydrogel structure can restrict nutrient diffusion and hinder cell infiltration and migration. Silk fibroin (referred to as ‘silk’) hydrogels crosslinked through di-tyrosine bonds are elastomeric and compatible with modern light-based fabrication approaches, but their nanoporosity and time-dependent mechanical stiffening constrain their performance in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine applications. Here, we present a facile strategy to simultaneously enhance porosity and stabilize the mechanical properties of silk hydrogels by incorporating tropoelastin and photocrosslinking native tyrosine residues in both proteins without chemical modification. The addition of tropoelastin induced the formation of tunable nano- to microscale particles through hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions, modulating globule coalescence and enabling controlled porous network formation. Hybrid hydrogels prepared by combining silk and tropoelastin at equal weight concentrations exhibited markedly reduced mechanical stiffening and enhanced cellular infiltration and migration in vitro and in vivo relative to silk-only hydrogels, attributable to their unique microporous structure. Following subcutaneous implantation in mice, hybrid hydrogels showed reduced fibrous encapsulation compared to silk-only formulations, while avoiding the rapid degradation observed in tropoelastin-only systems. In addition, the photocrosslinked hybrids effectively sealed ex vivo wound models and supported high-fidelity patterning for advanced light-based biofabrication. This work demonstrates how leveraging intermolecular protein interactions provides a versatile materials-engineering platform for tailoring hydrogel structure and mechanical stability.

title: Low-cost pillar-ligand engineering toward ultramicroporous MOFs for efficient SF6/N2 separation
abstract: Efficient capture of SF6 from dilute SF6/N2 mixtures remains challenging because high uptake, high selectivity, and low production cost are rarely achieved simultaneously. Here, two pillar-layered Ni-based coordination networks, Ni(BTC)(DABCO) and Ni(BTC)(PYZ), were constructed from inexpensive building blocks to evaluate pillar-ligand engineering as a cost-effective strategy for SF6/N2 separation. Replacing DABCO with pyrazine ligand contracts the pore aperture from 5.73 to 5.45 Å while maintaining comparable surface area and pore volume. As a result, Ni(BTC)(PYZ) exhibits a markedly enhanced SF6 uptake of 2.69 mmol g−1 at 0.1 bar and an IAST-predicted SF6/N2 selectivity of 170.9 at 298 K, both significantly higher than those of Ni(BTC)(DABCO). The estimated production cost of Ni(BTC)(PYZ) is only 201.69 $ kg−1, highlighting its strong cost competitiveness among SF6 adsorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments further confirm the improved separation performance and cycling stability of Ni(BTC)(PYZ). GCMC and DFT calculations reveal that the superior performance originates from pore-size matching and confinement-enhanced host–guest interactions. This work demonstrates that low-cost pillar-ligand engineering is an effective route to ultramicroporous MOFs for efficient SF6/N2 separation.

Graphene oxide–driven in situ bismuth reduction enables highly efficient electroreduction of CO2 to formic acid
abstract: To enable large scale efficient electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) to formic acid (HCOOH), it is important to develop catalysts that can be operated in a wide potential window with good stability. Herein, we successfully synthesized Bi 2 O 3 catalyst supported on graphene oxide (GO) and graphene (G) and found that Bi 2 O 3 /GO catalyst had a better overall performance than Bi 2 O 3 /G. The Bi 2 O 3 /GO catalyst demonstrated an outstanding CO2RR performance with a greater than 90% faradaic efficiency (FE) across a wide applied potential window from −0.9 to −1.7 V vs. RHE, a HCOOK production rate of 1700 μmol h −1 cm −2 at −1.7 V vs. RHE, and excellent long-term operational stability maintaining >90% FE over 84 h in a conventional H-type cell. Comprehensive characterization revealed that metallic Bi dominated the reaction performance rather than initial electron transfer rate over the Bi 2 O 3 /GO catalyst. Carboxyl functional groups (-COOH) on GO promoted the in situ reduction of Bi 2 O 3 and Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 to metallic Bi. Although metallic Bi exhibited a relatively weak affinity for CO 2 and the *OCHO intermediate compared to Bi 2 O 2 CO 3 , the conversion of CO2RR to HCOOH over metallic Bi proceeds with a more favorable (downhill) energy profile, thereby, resulting in enhanced CO2RR performance.

BMIM-SCN-mediated bulk-interface co-tuning of composite electrolytes enables dendrite-free solid-state LiS batteries
abstract: The global transition to sustainable energy demands energy storage systems balancing ultrahigh energy density, intrinsic safety, and long cycle life. Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, with a theoretical energy density of 2600 Wh kg-1, represent a transformative alternative to lithium-ion batteries, yet their commercialization is constrained by polysulfide shuttling, poor solid-solid interfacial compatibility, and lithium dendrite growth. Herein, we report a 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium thiocyanate (BMIM-SCN)-mediated bulk-interface co-tuning strategy for poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP)/F127-based composite solid-state electrolytes (CSEs), addressing these challenges via a four-fold synergistic effect. This tuning modulates polymer crystallinity, promotes lithium salt dissociation, optimizes interfacial wettability, and induces a stable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The resultant CSE-BS exhibits a room-temperature ionic conductivity of 1.20 × 10-3 S cm-1, Li+ transference number of 0.70, tensile strength of 33.4 MPa, and electrochemical stability window >4.78 V. Integrated into all-solid-state Li-S batteries, CSE-BS delivers an initial discharge capacity of 1499 mAh g-1 at 0.1C, retains average capacity 840 mAh g-1 after 200 cycles at 0.2C (0.13% per-cycle decay), and maintains average capacity 667 mAh g-1 after 200 cycles at 1C. Mechanistic studies confirm BMIM-SCN induces a low-crystallinity (8.9%) polymer bulk and a LiF-rich SEI, collectively suppressing dendrite growth and stabilizing the electrode-electrolyte interface. This work establishes a scalable bulk-interface co-optimization strategy for CSEs, advancing practical high-energy solid-state Li-S batteries and empowering next-generation energy storage technologies.

Advanced oxidation processes for PFAS destruction: From interfacial degradation mechanisms to field-scale treatment
abstract: Per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are among the most persistent contaminants in aquatic environments because of their high mobility, chemical stability and strong C F bonds. Conventional separation technologies, including adsorption, nanofiltration and reverse osmosis, can remove PFAS from water but do not destroy them, instead generating PFAS-rich waste streams that require further treatment. This limitation has spurred the development of destructive advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), including electrochemical oxidation, electrical discharge plasma, photocatalysis and photoelectrocatalysis. This review examines recent progress in AOP-based PFAS destruction, with emphasis on the interfacial mechanisms governing PFAS activation, chain shortening and defluorination. Direct charge transfer, radical-mediated oxidation and reductive pathways are discussed in relation to PFAS structure, surface adsorption and reactive species generation. We evaluate materials design strategies, including anode and cathode engineering, heterojunction construction, doping, defect engineering and surface modification, that enhance charge separation, PFAS adsorption and subsequent C F bond activation. Finally, we assess pilot-scale and field-relevant treatment trains that couple PFAS preconcentration with downstream destruction, highlighting their energy requirements, matrix effects and scalability. By linking degradation mechanisms with materials and reactor design, this review identifies key opportunities and remaining challenges for developing efficient, durable and verifiable PFAS destruction technologies.

abstract: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) is widely recognized as one of the most promising conductive polymers for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) owing to its excellent optical transparency and solution-processability. However, the hygroscopic and heterogeneous nature of PEDOT:PSS induces substantial defect formation at the buried perovskite interface and accelerates interfacial degradation, thereby severely limiting device efficiency and operational stability. Here, we report an integrated doping-passivation strategy based on sodium thiosulfate (Na2S2O3) to simultaneously tailor the physicochemical properties of PEDOT:PSS and optimize the buried perovskite interface. The incorporation of Na2S2O3 significantly enhances the conductivity of the PEDOT:PSS film through ion-exchange interactions while preserving its high optical transparency. More importantly, the modified PEDOT:PSS layer effectively regulates perovskite crystallization, leading to enlarged crystal grains and substantially reduced interfacial defect densities, thereby markedly suppressing non-radiative carrier recombination. As a result, the optimized PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.03% with a high open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.046 V, representing one of the highest values reported for PEDOT:PSS-based inverted PSCs. In addition, unencapsulated devices retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 3000 h of storage, while maintaining more than 90% of the initial efficiency after 1200 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under illumination. This work provides an effective interfacial engineering strategy for realizing highly efficient and operationally stable inverted PSCs based on PEDOT:PSS.

Stratified regulation strategy of oxygen vacancies for high-efficiency printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells
abstract: The characteristics of the buried interface are key factors determining the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (p-MPSCs). Herein, a stratified regulation strategy of oxygen vacancies (OVs) based on interface engineering is developed to achieve the modulation of buried interfacial defects at the microscale. Firstly, treating the mp-TiO2 film with high-concentration hydrochloric acid (HCl) increases the surface and bulk phase OVs. Subsequent treatment of the mp-TiO2 film with low-concentration hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) selectively removes the surface OVs while retaining the bulk phase OVs, thereby achieving the goal of stratified regulation. This two-step synergistic process in the OVs stratified regulation strategy not only yields an mp-TiO2 ETL with low surface defect density, high conductivity and high carrier mobility, but also contributes to slowing down the perovskite crystallization synergistically, releasing residual stress in the perovskite film, and optimizing energy level alignment. The resulting p-MPSCs achieve an impressive PCE of 20.85%, and still maintain approaching 90% of their initial PCE after 3300 hours of storage under unencapsulated, dark conditions at 40 ± 5% relative humidity and 30 ± 5 oC. Our work provides a new reference for enhancing the efficiency and facilitating the industrial application of p-MPSCs.

Thermal plasma treatment of simulated medical waste using CO2 as a gasification agent for carbon utilization at pilot scale
abstract: Treatment of hazardous medical waste streams represents a significant environmental challenge, commonly associated with greenhouse gas emissions and limited energy recovery. This study experimentally and theoretically investigates the valorization of simulated medical waste (SMW) via a thermochemical upcycling approach, employing a pilot-scale (up to 160 kW) high-enthalpy (>100 MJ kg −1 ) direct-current (DC) discharge thermal plasma reactor processing 6.2–9.0 kg h −1 of feedstock with CO 2 injection rates of 0–164 slm as a reactive gasifying agent, corresponding to an input CO 2 -to-SMW mass-flow ratio of 0.0–2.1. The unique reactor environment, characterized by temperatures of 1250–1450 °C is favorable for the decomposition of potentially hazardous compounds while enabling Carbon capture and utilization (CCU). The results demonstrate that externally supplied CO 2 actively participates in high-temperature gasification, promoting carbon monoxide formation through dry reforming and Boudouard reactions. The produced syngas was rich in CO and H 2 , with lower heating values (LHV) ranging from 13.9 to 18.8 MJ kg −1 . A key finding was the successful upgrading of low-grade waste into a valuable fuel usable for downstream applications, evidenced by a chemical energy ratio of the output syngas to the input waste fuel reaching up to 1.9. The cold gas efficiency experimentally reached nearly 56%, while equilibrium-based analysis indicates a theoretical upper limit exceeding 62% under optimized power matching. Overall, this study shows that CO 2 -assisted thermal plasma gasification of simulated medical waste has strong application potential for the treatment of real hazardous medical wastes, enabling efficient syngas production while utilizing CO 2 as a reactive gasification agent.

Recovery of rare earth metals from NdFeB magnets using antisolvent crystallization: scale up and life cycle assessment
abstract: Recycling of rare earth elements (REEs) has become of paramount importance for permanent magnets used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and motors. There is an imbalance in supply and demand of this commodity and the REE has been identified as critical raw materials by the European Union. This study focuses on the recovery of REEs (La, Pr, Nd, Dy, Y) from sulfuric acid leach solutions using antisolvent crystallization, scaling up the process by hybrid process modelling, and performing environmental impact assessment. Ethanol is used as an antisolvent to crystallize REE2(SO4)3∙8H2O. The impact of inorganic impurities including Cu(II), Co(II), Al(III), B(III), Fe(II) and Fe(III) on the quality of the crystal product, in terms of purity and morphology, has been investigated. Higher purity (above 99%) is obtained for seeded experiments, and the purity is higher for higher seed loading and lower antisolvent dosing rate. Furthermore, the REEs have a tendency to be precipitate as a mixed phase, i.e. REE2(SO4)3∙8H2O. By balancing the addition of antisolvent and seed loading the optimum conditions in terms of high purity and productivity can be found. Scale-up of the process to 100 kg/batch, with solvent recovery of ethanol and H2SO4 (aq.), waste heat reutilization and trade-off analysis, potentially reduces the global warming potential from 40 kg CO2 eq to 0.96 kg CO2 eq /kg REE2(SO4)3∙8H2O. The results can provide valuable insights to understand and optimize the recovery of REEs from sulfate media as a pure concentrate from impure leach liquors. The potential for scaling up the process is also demonstrated resulting in relatively low impacts on global warming.

Sunlight driven generation of superhydrophobic photocatalysts via self-diffusion of free oligomers in cross-linked polydimethylsiloxane
abstract: The integration of superhydrophobicity with photocatalytic functionality offers a powerful pathway toward surfaces capable of autonomous self-cleaning through both passive liquid repellency and active pollutant degradation. However, achieving this combination remains fundamentally challenging, as low-surface-energy modifiers often suppress photocatalytic activity or undergo photo-induced degradation. Here, we present a sunlight-driven strategy for generating superhydrophobic photocatalyst surfaces by leveraging the self-diffusion of free oligomers in cross-linked PDMS (CL-PDMS) films. By depositing hydrophilic photocatalyst nanoparticles onto CL-PDMS surfaces and exposing the system to sunlight, PDMS oligomers are selectively grafted onto the photocatalyst surface, creating a concentration gradient that directs the spontaneous diffusion of PDMS free oligomers toward the air interface. This self-diffusion process transforms hydrophilic photocatalysts with a contact angle of ~6° into superhydrophobic, photocatalytically active entities exhibiting contact angles of up to 172° and sliding angles as low as 2°, without compromising their catalytic performance. Our findings reveal that oligomer diffusion in CL-PDMS, traditionally regarded as an undesirable phenomenon, can instead be harnessed as a functional mechanism for precise control over surface properties. This work establishes a new materials paradigm where sunlight-induced polymer diffusion enables scalable fabrication of bifunctional superhydrophobic–photocatalytic coatings for self-cleaning, antibacterial, and environmental remediation applications.

title: Multifunctional thermally regulated aerogels for efficient solar-driven evaporation and thermoelectric power generation
abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation is a promising approach for freshwater production; however, its practical application is limited by intermittent solar irradiation and interfacial salt crystallization, which lead to reduced evaporation rates during continuous operation. Herein, a composite aerogel evaporator is constructed by integrating graphene oxide (GO) and phase-change material-loaded dendritic mesoporous silica nanoparticles (PCMs/DMSNs) within a chitosan framework, followed by a polypyrrole (PPy) photothermal coating. The confined PCMs store and release heat, helping to sustain a stable evaporation process, while GO promotes water transport and salt dissolution, stabilizing the evaporation process. Under 1.0 sun irradiation, the GPCA1.0@PPy evaporator achieves an evaporation rate of 2.03 kg m-2 h-1 and maintains 0.98 kg m-2 h-1 under light-off conditions. Stable evaporation (~1.8 kg m-2 h-1) is sustained in 20 wt% NaCl solution for 6 h without observable salt accumulation. The system also enables effective removal of organic dyes and heavy metal ions. When coupled with a thermoelectric module, a power density of 0.3-0.8 W m-2 is achieved. This work provides a strategy for coupling thermal regulation with water transport, enabling stable solar evaporation under practical conditions.

abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to formate is often limited by the inefficient regulation of key *OCHO intermediates and sluggish HCOOH desorption. Herein, a Ce-induced defect-rich Bi2O2CO3 nanosheet catalyst was constructed via ion-exchange reconstruction from a Ce-BiOCl precursor. The process preserves the two-dimensional morphology and generates abundant nanodefects and undercoordinated active sites, driven by the migration of CeOx species. Meanwhile, the remaining dispersed Ce species modulate the local electronic environment. In an H-type cell, the catalyst achieved a high formate Faradaic efficiency of 96.2% at -1.1 V (vs. RHE) with a current density of 31.8 mA cm-2 and exhibited excellent stability over 30 h. In a flow cell, a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 96.8% was obtained at -1.0 V (vs. RHE), corresponding to a formate partial current density of 394.1 mA cm-2, which further increases to a total current density of 466.2 mA cm-2 at -1.2 V. In situ FTIR and DFT results revealed that nanodefects and Ce modulation synergistically optimize *OCHO adsorption, facilitate HCOOH desorption, and suppress HER, thereby enhancing CO2RR kinetics and formate selectivity. This work highlights an effective strategy for regulating reaction intermediates via defect engineering.

title: Machine learning-assisted modeling of tandem catalytic polymerization for tailoring comb-branched polyolefin elastomers
Acid-catalyzed ethanol pretreatment of sugarcane bagasse enables electrochemically improved hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Feedstock properties play a significant role in preparing high-performance hard carbon (HC) anode materials for advancing sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) as a viable alternative energy storage solution. In this study, an acid-catalyzed ethanol pretreatment approach was used as an effective technology platform to fractionate sugarcane bagasse into cellulose-rich pulp (EC) and high-purity lignin (EL) for subsequent synthesis of HC. Comprehensive electrochemical analyses reveal that acid-catalyzed ethanol pretreatment enables improved performance in both lignin- and cellulose pulp-based HC compared to HC anodes derived from whole sugarcane bagasse, dilute acid pretreated pulp as well as cellulose pulp and lignin fractions from alkaline pretreatment. EC-HC demonstrates a reversible capacity of 297.7 mAh g −1 with an initial coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 69.6%, which is greater than other cellulose-pulp-based HC. This improvement is mainly attributed to the higher C C content, fewer surface structural defects, reduced open porosity and higher crystallinity resulting from the increased cellulose content. Simultaneously, EL-HC exhibits superior electrochemical performance, achieving the highest reversible capacity of 316.3 mAh g −1 and an enhanced ICE of 78.0%. Moreover, EL-HC maintains exceptional long-term stability, retaining 88.1% of its initial capacity even after 250 cycles. This superior performance of EL-HC primarily originates from their reduced oxygen functional group, lower defects and minimized open porosity, which stem from the improved structural homogeneity of lignin. These results demonstrate that acid-catalyzed ethanol pretreatment provides a highly efficient platform for converting agricultural biomass into HC anode materials with enhanced performance for next-generation SIBs.

A nitrogen-rich pyridine–melamine porous network for integrated CO₂ capture and hexavalent chromium remediation
abstract: Multifunctional adsorbents that integrate greenhouse gas capture with hazardous metal remediation are rare because simultaneously optimizing pore architecture and reactive adsorption sites remains challenging. Herein, a nitrogen-rich pyridine-based poly-melamine porous network (Py-PMAN) was synthesized via Schiff base polycondensation for integrated CO 2 capture and Cr 6+ remediation. The as-prepared polymer combines accessible porosity (S BET of 511.76 m 2 /g) with reactive amino–pyridine sites that additionally enable oxyanion sequestration. Benefiting from its nitrogen-rich porous structure and abundant amino functionalities, Py-PMAN showed a high CO 2 uptake capacity of 153.03 mg/g at 273 K and 1 bar. Distinct from conventional high-capacity Cr 6+ adsorbents that rely predominantly on electrostatic uptake, Py-PMAN couples adsorption with reduction- immobilization within a porous polymer network. Optimum conditions for Cr 6+ uptake were determined to be pH 3 and a dosage of 0.11 g/L using response surface methodology. Adsorption equilibrium and kinetics were well fitted by the Langmuir isotherm and the pseudo-second-order models, respectively, suggesting monolayer chemisorption and a high Cr 6+ adsorption capacity of 188.68 mg/g. Thermodynamic studies revealed a spontaneous adsorption process. Py-PMAN maintained high Cr 6+ removal efficiency across five adsorption–desorption cycles, indicating excellent reusability and structural stability, while competitive ion experiments confirmed strong selectivity for Cr 6+ . FT-IR and XPS analyses revealed that Cr 6+ removal proceeds through synergistic proton-assisted electrostatic binding, reduction-coupled immobilization, and coordination to amino-rich sites, with adsorption governed by these mechanisms. This work presents a robust, multifunctional porous organic network for integrated carbon capture and hazardous-metal remediation, offering a promising strategy for coupled gas purification and wastewater treatment.

title: A dual-functional smart sensor integrating 3D-printed technology and thermoresponsive hydrogel for mechanical sensing and adaptive thermal management
Microalgal membrane photobioreactors coupled with chemically enhanced primary treatment for resource recovery and low-carbon water resource recovery facilities
abstract: This study evaluated the integration of CEPT and a MPBR for organic matter recovery, nutrient removal and energy–environmental performance. CEPT provided efficient clarification and recovered 61% of total COD. This effluent was treated in a MPBR operated under different hydraulic (HRT: 62, 44, and 39 h) and solids (SRT: 10 and 22 d) retention times. Biomass productivity increased with decreasing HRT, reaching 184 mg TSS L −1 d −1 at 39 h. Molecular analyses revealed a stable microalgal community dominated by green algae, primarily Scenedesmus sp., coexisting with heterotrophic bacterial populations. The most stable performance was achieved at HRTs of 44–62 h combined with an SRT of 10 d, under which the MPBR consistently attained 94% and 96% removal of total nitrogen and phosphorus, respectively, producing permeates with concentrations below 2 mg N L −1 and 1 mg P L −1 . The nitrogen balance indicated that biomass assimilation accounted for 60%, 48%, and 47% in Phases I–III, respectively , and only 15% in Phase IV. Furthermore, extending the SRT to 22 d reduced biomass productivity (55 mg TSS L −1 d −1 ) and promoted nutrient accumulation. The energy assessment indicated a net electricity surplus of 0.044 kWh m −3 after biogas valorization via CHP, mainly driven by low membrane aeration energy demand. The GHG and carbon balances resulted in emissions of 0.043 kg CO 2 e m −3 , lower than values typically reported for conventional MBR systems, and showed complete carbon-balance closure at 0.260 kg C m −3 , with MPBR biomass carbon originating from atmospheric CO 2 fixation (0.061 kg C m −3 ) and heterotrophic incorporation of dissolved organic carbon (0.031 kg C m −3 ). Overall, CEPT–MPBR represents a promising low-carbon strategy for wastewater treatment and water reuse.

Self-powered tribophotonic devices for nonlinear electro-optic modulation
abstract: Electro-optical modulators (EOMs), operating via linear and non-linear electro-optical effects, are well-established components in optical communication systems, laser modulation, and photonic integrated circuits (PIC). However, conventional bulk crystal EOMs require high bias voltages, typically supplied by the power grid or large-capacity battery systems, thereby constraining their portability and overall sustainability. In this research, a green, environmentally friendly alternative is investigated that combines triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) with photonics to produce a self-powered tribophotonic device capable of stimulating EOMs in a lower frequency range. For this purpose, we achieved precise control of TENG output characteristics by engineering triboelectric nanomaterials synthesized through oblique-angle deposition. Different TENG operating conditions demonstrated a successful non-linear response in a Fabry-Perot transmission-based EOM. Our study demonstrates that TENG-generated bias fields, with voltage densities ranging from 4.25 ∙ 10 5 V/m 2 to 8.95 ∙ 10 5 V/m 2 , enabled continuous tuning of the EOM transmission at 993 nm, achieving modulation depths between 17.5% and 64.7%. This result indicates the potential of TENG-driven EOMs for photonic applications, including optical communication systems, where modulation of near-infrared region wavelengths can be exploited for data transmission and signal processing.
