Tussah silk-inspired bionic fiber integrating ultrasensitive sensing and active biological protection
abstract: Achieving the synergistic integration of high-performance strain sensing and active biological protection within a single fiber remains a formidable challenge for advanced wearable textiles. Herein, inspired by the hierarchical architecture of tussah silk, we propose a bionic fiber integrating sensing and biological protection via wet-spinning and interfacial self-assembly. Specifically, a thermoplastic polyurethane/ Ti3C2Tx MXene conductive core was employed to mimic the mechanical skeleton. Subsequently, interfacial self-assembly of polydopamine/Ti3C2Tx MXene was conducted on the fiber surface to form a robust ”second conductive network”. This interfacial synergy dramatically boosts the gauge factor from 8360 to 83810 and broadens the working strain range to 114%. Finally, a water-based polyurethane/ZIF-8/Fluralaner bionic shell was designed to replicate the biological defense of the outer cocoon. The resulting fiber exhibits excellent biocompatibility (93.17% cell viability), high-efficiency broad-spectrum antibacterial activity (>99% against Staphylococcus aureus and >98% against Escherichia coli), and a notable mosquito repellency rate of 60.14%. This work provides a scalable strategy for constructing intelligent fibers that integrate sensing and biological protection, showing great potential for wearable electronics and smart protective textiles.

Interlayer engineering with imidazolium cations: A design strategy for high-performance aqueous zinc-ion batteries
abstract: Aqueous zinc (Zn)-ion batteries (AZIBs) are a promising candidate for large-scale energy storage owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and high theoretical capacity of Zn metal. However, the development of cathode materials is hindered by sluggish Zn 2+ diffusion, limited conductivity, and structural instability upon cycling. Herein, we report the intercalation of imidazolium-based cations, 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium (BMIM + ) and 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium (EMIM + ), into layered vanadium oxide hydrates (VOHs) through a facile hydrothermal approach. Structural characterization confirms that organic cation intercalation significantly expands the interlayer spacing, with BMIM + providing the greatest lattice expansion due to its longer alkyl chain, which thereby stabilizes the layered framework. Electrochemical tests demonstrate that BMIM–VOH delivers a high reversible capacity of 458 mAh/g at 300 mA/g, superior rate capability with nearly 100% recovery when returned to 200 mA/g, and remarkable cycling stability with 94% retention after long-term cycling at 5000 mA/g, outperforming both VOH and EMIM–VOH. Furthermore, various ex-situ analyses reveal reversible interlayer breathing, multivalent redox transitions, transient Zn-containing phase formation, and preserved nanosheet morphology during cycling. Density functional theory calculations further corroborate these results, showing interlayer expansion to 8.34 Å, narrowed band gaps (∼0.76 eV), strong Zn-O bonding, and reduced Zn 2+ migration barriers compared to the VOH. This work establishes imidazolium cation intercalation as an effective strategy to engineer interlayer environments and electronic structures in layered VOH, offering a pathway toward high-capacity durable cathode materials for next-generation AZIBs.

Engineering coordinated molecular junctions in MOFs for photo-responsive dual-phase hydrogels toward accelerated infected wound healing
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) hold great potential as antibacterial wound dressings, yet their efficacy is often limited by inadequate reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and poor integration into functional matrices. Herein, by precisely regulating the coordinated molecular junctions within MOFs, we have synthesized a series of MOFs, and subsequently employing it as functional component to develop an MOF-based ”fiber film‐hydrogel” dual-phase wound dressing. Among them, Ce‐PCN‐224, constructed from redox‐active Ce nodes and photosensitive porphyrin ligands, demonstrates the optimal performance. The strong electronic coupling between the Ce³⁺/Ce⁴⁺ redox pair and the extended π‐conjugated porphyrin system enhances the separation and migration of photogenerated charge carriers, enabling efficient photo-responsive ROS generation and antibacterial activity. After the film material is prepared via electrospinning and coated with hydrogel, the resulting Ce‐PCN‐224/gel film can effectively kill S. aureus (99.9999%) and MRSA (99.99%). In the mouse wound infection model, the dressing demonstrates outstanding anti-infection and tissue‐repair capacity, accelerating wound healing by approximately 35% and demonstrating excellent biocompatibility. This study presents an innovative strategy to design MOF photocatalysts through electronic structure regulation, and demonstrates their effective application in infected wound via a dual-phase dressing design, thereby paving new avenues for MOF-based materials in chronic wound care.

abstract: Bioresorbable thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs) based on poly(gly co lide- co -ε-caprolactone) (PGC) diols were synthesized through bulk polymerization and processed into 3D-printed scaffolds. Three TPUs derived from poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) diol and PGC macrodiols with 10 (10PGC) and 30 (30PGC) mol-% glycolide were prepared and characterized. Increasing glycolide content reduced thermal stability and significantly accelerated hydrolytic degradation in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), with mass losses of 3.6% for PCL and 12.5% for 10PGC-based TPUs after 92 days, and 42.3% after 50 days for 30PGC-based TPUs. Mechanical tests showed that the PCL-based TPU had superior tensile strength and elongation at break, while the addition of PGC increased stiffness. Melt extrusion 3D printing of PCL-based TPU and 10PGC-based TPU produced scaffolds with highly consistent architectures. Cytocompatibility tests using human neonatal dermal fibroblasts showed no cytotoxicity, and direct contact experiments revealed a time-dependent increase in metabolic activity over 7 days, with significantly higher activity on 10PGC-based TPU scaffolds as well as well-spread, elongated cell morphologies on both materials. Overall, the solvent-free PGC-based TPU offered excellent 3D printability, cytocompatibility, and tunable degradation controlled by glycolide content, providing a versatile and customizable structure that could be explored as a candidate scaffold for soft tissue engineering applications.

Carbon fabrics for electrified direct air capture: From substrate morphology to module-scale operating trade-offs
abstract: Polyethyleneimine (PEI)-impregnated carbon fabrics are structured direct air capture (DAC) sorbents whose electrical conductivity enables resistive temperature swing regeneration. However, how substrate morphology translates intrinsic sorbent properties into module-scale DAC performance under continuous flow remains poorly understood. We investigate this using a resistively heated spiral wound module (SWM). Two carbon fabrics, a macroporous non-woven (E20) and a microporous activated carbon cloth (FM10), were characterized. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed a trade-off between CO 2 capacity and kinetics: higher PEI loading enhanced capacity but slowed sorption and desorption. FM10 showed faster kinetics than E20, yet its higher surface area did not increase CO 2 uptake, indicating that accessibility rather than amine content governed the usable capacity. The kinetically favorable FM10 was deployed in the SWM under DAC-relevant conditions (400 ppm CO 2 ). Comparison of intrinsic and dynamic performance revealed that only 15-30 % of the intrinsic capacity was utilized under continuous-flow operation, demonstrating that DAC performance is governed by transport limitations rather than equilibrium sorbent properties alone. Reducing gas flow rate improved dynamic yield at the expense of productivity. Humid operation enhanced yield through water-induced PEI swelling while reducing the specific regeneration energy. This energy was dominated by parasitic heat loss rather than by the sorbent, identifying module heat management, alongside dynamic utilization, as a design-limited lever. These results show that the dominant challenge in electrified DAC is not maximizing intrinsic sorbent capacity, but maximizing its dynamic utilization through the coupled design of substrate morphology, PEI distribution, module architecture, and operating strategy.

title: Atomic-scale matrix partitioning of polar and antipolar motifs for high-density energy storage capacitors
abstract: The optimization of dielectric capacitors is fundamentally constrained by the structural coupling between macroscopic polarization and electrical breakdown in single-phase systems. Decoupling this trade-off requires shifting from conventional bulk-phase engineering to mesoscale structural heterogeneity. Here, a strong-relaxor/weak-antiferroelectric cooperative architecture is constructed in PbZrO3-based solid solutions. Atomic-scale polarization vector mapping directly visualizes a spatially partitioned configuration, wherein a dynamically reversible paraelectric-rich matrix physically isolates embedded ferroelectric-like nanoregions and dispersed antiferroelectric motifs. This matrix partitioning interrupts long-range polar and antipolar connectivity, thereby suppressing macroscopic hysteresis and restricting breakdown pathways, while the localized active regions maintain high polarizability. Governed by this mesoscale decoupling mechanism, the optimized ceramic delivers a recoverable energy density of 13.16 J cm-3 with 90.4% efficiency. Furthermore, it exhibits an ultrafast discharge time (104 ns) and a peak power density of 348.15 MW cm-2, alongside robust electromechanical reliability. This atomic-scale spatial partitioning mechanism provides a fundamental mesoscale structural design strategy for ultrahigh-power dielectric capacitors.

title: Thermally programmable mesoporous silica nanoreactor integrating metal adsorption, stabilization, and confined phase transformation
abstract: A thermally programmable mesoporous silica nanoreactor was developed that integrates copper adsorption, stabilization, and confinement-driven phase transformation within a single ordered host. It is based on SBA-15 mesoporous silica functionalized with propyl-phosphonate groups, which act as immobile high-affinity coordination sites for Cu 2+ during aqueous adsorption. In parallel, mobile Cu(acac) 2 complexes diffuse through the hydrophobic mesopore channels and serve as uniformly distributed molecular copper precursors. This dual-functional architecture combines strong interfacial binding with preserved molecular mobility, enabling efficient copper capture while allowing copper species to reorganize and react within the confined pore environment. Structural analyses demonstrate that copper incorporation and thermal treatment induce controlled mesoscopic reorganization without disrupting the long-range hexagonal order of SBA-15. Small-angle diffraction reveals a moderate shift of the (100) reflection consistent with lattice contraction caused by pore filling and framework densification. At the same time, transmission electron microscopy confirms preservation of the ordered cylindrical mesopore structure. Wide-angle diffraction and Raman spectroscopy exclude the presence of bulk crystalline Cu(acac) 2 , confirming high dispersion and confinement of copper species within the pores. Upon thermal activation, confined copper precursors decompose and undergo diffusion-driven restructuring, forming spatially confined copper phosphate and copper hydrophosphate nanophases. Statement of environmental implications From the perspective of environmental protection and resource efficiency, the proposed SBA-15-based system can operate in two complementary modes: in the first, a reusable-adsorbent scenario, Cu 2+ ions can be removed by controlled acid washing prior to thermal treatment, consistent with regeneration strategies for Cu-loaded functionalized SBA-15 materials; in the second, the spent material can be subjected to calcination as a post-use valorization step transforming immobilized copper into confined copper phosphate or hydrophosphate-type nanophases within the mesoporous matrix. Hence, thermal treatment should be considered a waste-to-material conversion pathway rather than a true adsorbent regeneration process. As a result, the system enables effective immobilization of Cu 2+ ions, thereby reducing their mobility and environmental risk while simultaneously providing a route for stabilization and potential recovery of captured metal species, in line with circular economy principles that integrate water remediation with resource valorization and reduced dependence on primary copper extraction. Practical implementation, however, will require further validation, including adsorption–desorption cycling, performance in multi-ion and real wastewater systems, leaching stability studies, and techno-economic and scalability assessments.

Markov chain Monte Carlo-assisted kinetic modeling of CO2 methanation over Ru/YSZ catalyst
abstract: The efficient conversion of CO 2 into renewable CH 4 continues to motivate the development of advanced methanation catalysts. In this work, CO 2 hydrogenation was investigated over a ruthenium-based catalyst supported on yttria-doped ZrO 2 (Ru/YSZ), reduced at 150, 250, and 500 °C. IR-CO spectroscopy and XPS analyses demonstrate that reduction temperature governs the local Ru environment, with interfacial and partially oxidized Ru δ+ species predominating at low reduction temperatures, resulting in enhanced catalytic performance. To overcome the common limitations of conventional kinetic analysis, an advanced data-reconciliation methodology using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations was implemented. The combination of spectroscopic studies and multiple reparameterizations with MCMC simulations identified direct CO 2 dissociation as the preferred kinetic pathway, rather than the H-assisted formate mechanism on the 250 °C reduced Ru/YSZ sample, with apparent activation energies predicted to be 0.94 eV and 2.58 eV, respectively. Posterior parameter correlations further reveal a strong coupling between CO 2 activation and active-site regeneration mediated by terminal water.

title: Bioinspired self-healing polyurethane/epoxy interpenetrating network toughened by dopamine-functionalized MXene for corrosion protection
Solar photo-thermocatalytic valorization of biomass waste to biofuel precursors using inexpensive Ni–P/graphite catalysts
abstract: Developing efficient, low-cost catalytic routes for biomass upgrading for sustainable fuel and chemical production is a crucial step toward a greener society and circular economy. Ni–P/graphite catalysts prepared by electroless deposition on graphite microflakes were used for photo-thermocatalytic transfer hydrogenation of levulinic acid (LA) to γ-valerolactone (GVL) in isopropanol, without external H 2 or noble metals. Graphite provides broadband optical absorption and localized heat generation; the Ni P coating supplies the active hydrogen-transfer sites, with isopropanol serving as hydrogen donor. Under near-infrared laser irradiation at 105 °C, complete LA conversion was achieved in 120 min, 2.5-fold faster than the solvothermal process at the same temperature. Solar-driven tests using a parabolic concentrator (105 °C, 2.5 mg mL −1 , 100 mL scale) yielded 99.1% GVL after 80 min; over-reduction to valeric acid became significant only at 120 min. The catalyst retained near-quantitative activity over five consecutive cycles with negligible cumulative Ni and P leaching. Tests with a synthetic biomass hydrolysate approximating wheat-derived acid hydrolysate composition (LA/furfural/formic acid, 104:1:36 M ratio) showed LA conversion exceeding 99.9% at 40 min and complete furfural conversion by 80 min. The furfural hydrogenation network yielded furfuryl alcohol, 2-methylfuran, tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol, and 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (23.2% at 120 min). Formic acid decomposition supplemented isopropanol as hydrogen donor under mixed-feed conditions. The optimal catalyst loading of 2.5 mg mL −1 was 36-fold lower than the Raney Ni dose required for comparable photo-thermocatalytic LA conversion, which additionally demanded a reaction temperature of ca. 130 °C.

title: Dual-induced Ni/CoOOH generation on lignin-derived carbon decorating MoNi3-Co3Mo heterostructure for enhanced urea electro-oxidation
abstract: Despite the promise of nickel/cobalt-based catalysts for the urea electro-oxidation reaction (UOR) to replace the oxygen evolution reaction of water electrolysis at the anode for energy-saving hydrogen production, their activity and stability in alkaline electrolytes remain challenging. Here, a lignin-derived carbon (LC) decorating MoNi3-Co3Mo heterostructure (MoNi3-Co3Mo@LC) catalyst with a self-supported architecture is designed to achieve s stable and efficient catalysis. In 1.0 M KOH with 0.5 M urea, MoNi3-Co3Mo@LC drives current densities of 10 and 1000 mA cm-2 at lower potentials of 1.26 and 1.37 V, respectively. Besides, operando electrochemical impedance and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that the UOR on MoNi3-Co3Mo@LC proceeds via an indirect oxidation pathway, with Dual synergy of lignin-derived carbon and the heterostructure (among MoNi3, Co3Mo, and LC) facilitating rapid the formation of Ni/CoOOH active species. Furthermore, MoNi3-Co3Mo@LC can achieve 120 h stability at 1000 mA cm-2, with a minimal potential decay of only 0.46 mV h-1 and well-preserved morphology, owing to its self-supported structure ensuring rapid gas-liquid transfer and the lignin-derived carbon enhancing corrosion resistance, thereby improving its UOR durability. This work reports not only a high-performance UOR catalyst but also provides a novel strategy for engineering lignin-derived carbon materials to meet industrial operational demands.

title: Spatial regulation of Pt sites enables balanced hydrogen generation and electrochemical CO2 reduction with the assistance of hydrogen spillover
abstract: The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to formate is emerging as a promising approach for industrial-scale CO2 upgrading. In-based materials have been recognized as promising catalysts for this reaction because of their low toxicity and excellent selectivity; however, their low reactivity hinders their practical application. Beyond the conventional proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway, an alternative H*-mediated route has recently been proposed; however, its efficiency on In-based catalysts is hindered by sluggish H2O dissociation and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we demonstrate that the spatial modulation of Pt in In-based catalysts provides an effective strategy to precisely control H* generation and utilization, thereby enhancing CO2-to-formate efficiency. Although surface-deposited Pt substantially facilitates H2O dissociation, excessive H* accumulation leads to the undesired HER and lowers formate selectivity. By contrast, incorporated Pt strengthens CO2 adsorption, enables balanced H* generation, and reduces energy cost for H* migration. As a result, Pt@In achieves a high formate Faradaic efficiency of 90% at -1.1 V, outperforming pure In (69%) and Pt/In (43%) under the same conditions. This work highlights the importance of spatially regulating hydrogen generation and transfer for designing highly selective CO2 reduction electrocatalysts.

Synergistic bulk–interfacial regulation for wide-temperature aqueous zinc batteries
abstract: Aqueous Zn batteries operating across wide temperature ranges are limited by the coupled instability of bulk ion transport and interfacial Zn deposition under thermal extremes. At low temperatures, strengthened hydrogen-bond networks and rigidified solvation structures hinder ion migration and interfacial charge transfer, whereas at elevated temperatures, accelerated parasitic reactions and unstable Zn growth undermine reversibility. Here, we report a synergistic bulk–interfacial regulation strategy by integrating a deep eutectic electrolyte with an in-situ Sn interphase. The deep eutectic electrolyte reconstructs the hydrogen-bond network and modulates the Zn²⁺ solvation environment, thereby suppressing water crystallization, lowering water activity, and preserving ion transport under subzero conditions. Meanwhile, SnCl₄ undergoes spontaneous galvanic displacement on Zn to form a zincophilic Sn-rich interphase, which suppresses hydrogen evolution, lowers the kinetic barriers for Zn deposition, and promotes uniform Zn growth. Through this cooperative regulation of bulk liquid-state stability and interfacial deposition kinetics, Zn||Zn cells achieve stable cycling for over 2500 h at -40 °C and maintain durable operation up to 70 °C. Zn||PANI full cells sustain over 3000 cycles at 70 °C and operate reversibly across a broad temperature window. This work establishes a bulk–interfacial design framework for wide-temperature aqueous Zn batteries.

Dispersible graphene/FeNi-N-C heterojunctions with dipole polarization for electromagnetic absorption and heat dissipation from vapor-induced graphite exfoliation
abstract: The growing integration and power density of electronics require materials that combine efficient electromagnetic wave absorption with thermal management. However, synthesizing lightweight, processable 2D materials that exhibit strong electromagnetic attenuation alongside high thermal conductivity yet electrical insulation remains a challenge. Here, we present a vapour intercalation-deposition approach of merging graphite exfoliation and metal-nitrogen-carbon atomic-layer growth to synthesize a graphene bonded dual-atom FeNi-N-C heterojunction. The solution-processable heterojunction exhibits outstanding electromagnetic attenuation of a low reflection loss of -75.3 dB, a broad absorption bandwidth of 6.08 GHz at 1.75 mm, a radar cross-section reduction of 51.4 dB·m2. It also shows low electrical and high thermal conductivities (10.6 W·m-1·K-1 in-plane, 4.0 W·m-1·K-1 out-plane). Mechanistic studies reveal that interfacial coupling between graphene and Fe(Ni)-N4-C atomic layers synergistically enhances dipole polarization and dielectric loss, thereby boosting electromagnetic attenuation, while also optimizing the balance between electrical insulation and thermal transport. This work offers a low-cost, scalable route to adaptable two-dimensional heterojunctions for integrated electromagnetic wave absorption and heat dissipation in next-generation electronics.

Cascade delivery and synergistic ferroptosis-apoptosis induction via hybrid-membrane-coated MOF nanoparticles for glioblastoma therapy
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most lethal brain tumors due to its highly invasive nature, frequent recurrence, and the formidable blood-brain barrier (BBB) that restricts therapeutic delivery. Here, we report a multifunctional nanoplatform based on a zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8, MOF), in which ursolic acid (UA) was loaded into the porous ZIF-8 framework and Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles were integrated into the ZIF-8-based composite, followed by cloaking with a neutrophil-glioma hybrid membrane (UFZ-HM). UFZ-HM was prepared through sequential UA loading, Fe₃O₄ integration, and hybrid membrane coating, followed by systematic physicochemical characterization and in vitro / in vivo evaluation. UFZ-HM exhibited a uniform nanoscale morphology with an average size of approximately 200 nm. This rational design enables cascade delivery across the BBB, inflammation-mediated tumor microenvironment targeting, and homotypic uptake by glioma cells, thereby achieving spatially programmed drug delivery. Upon exposure to the acidic tumor microenvironment (TME), the pH-responsive MOF core gradually disassembles, releasing the cargo to simultaneously induce ferroptosis via Fe-mediated Fenton catalysis and apoptosis via UA activation. The novelty of this design lies in the integration of dual-cargo MOF-based ferroptosis/apoptosis therapy with hybrid membrane-mediated cascade targeting in a single biomimetic nanoplatform. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate efficient BBB penetration, selective glioma accumulation, robust tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and favorable biosafety. In healthy BALB/c nude mice receiving UFZ-HM at 10 mg/kg for five consecutive days, no significant changes were observed in body weight, hematological parameters, liver function-related biochemical markers, or major-organ histology. This work presents a promising strategy for glioma therapy by integrating intelligent delivery with synergistic cell-death induction in a single biomimetic nanoplatform.

title: 15.5-fold boost in photosynthetic photon conversion efficiency at high irradiance in Spirulina platensis via pulsed red light
Engineered TGF-β-enriched exosomes delivered by dissolving microneedles for androgenetic alopecia therapy
abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is a common type of hair loss, primarily caused by the miniaturization of hair follicles induced by dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Current therapies are limited by systemic side effects and poor patient compliance. In this study, we engineered TGF-β-enriched exosomes (MSCT-Exos) through lentiviral transduction of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and delivered them via dissolving hyaluronate microneedles (MNs) for sustained transdermal release. In vitro characterization confirmed that MSCT-Exos retained typical exosomal properties, while MNs exhibited robust mechanical strength and rapid dissolution. In vivo studies using a DHT-induced AGA mouse model demonstrated that MN-mediated delivery of MSCT-Exos significantly increased the proportion of anagen hair follicles. Immunohistochemistry revealed upregulation of hair follicle stem cell marker CD34 and proliferation biomarker Ki67. The transcriptomic analysis indicates that the therapeutic effect is achieved through the Notch pathway. This minimally invasive strategy provides a targeted, compliant approach to AGA treatment with translational potential for tissue regeneration.

title: Supercritical water gasification of polyolefins and polystyrene-based polymers
abstract: The efficient valorization of plastics is one of the key challenges for contributing to the pollution mitigation and promoting the circular economy of resources. This work focuses on the supercritical water gasification (SCWG) of polyolefins (polyethylene, polypropylene) and polystyrene-based polymers at two different temperatures (450 °C and 600 °C). The impact of polymer type and temperature on product formation was investigated. Polystyrene exhibited poorer gasification compared to polyolefins, with a gas yield of 5.2 mol/kg at 600 °C, whereas polyolefins achieved a gas yield of around 20 mol/kg at the same temperature. A few similar patterns of behavior were nevertheless observed across all polymers: raising the temperature from 450 °C to 600 °C resulted in improved gasification and a preferential conversion to methane (>70 mol%). In each case, the proportion of carbon recovered in the aqueous phase was very low, less than 1% of the carbon initially introduced into the process. Furthermore, for each polymer, an oily organic phase was recovered at 450 °C while a char residue was recovered at 600 °C. All the chars exhibited similar carbon content and amorphous structure. In contrast, the organic phases recovered at 450 °C were very different depending on the polymer introduced. Polyethylene oil was rich in olefins and paraffins, polypropylene oil contained saturated aliphatic, unsaturated aliphatic but also cyclic and aromatic compounds and PS oil was mainly composed of benzene and naphthalene derivatives. Thus, SCWG of plastics at 450 °C seems more promising than at 600 °C for the production of plastic monomers and intermediates for the chemical industry.

A fluidized bed moisture-based direct air capture system for carbon capture and utilization applications
abstract: Direct air capture offers a decentralized pathway for supplying CO₂ to low-concentration utilization applications, including controlled environment agriculture, microalgae cultivation, biocatalytic conversion, and enhanced weathering. Solid sorption is favored for these applications, yet existing technologies require complex and expensive equipment to manage heat for desorption. Here we present a fluidized bed direct air capture system that uses controlled liquid water spray to drive moisture-swing desorption from a commercial ion exchange resin, eliminating the need for external high-grade heat. Breakthrough experiments revealed moisture-activated CO₂ uptake, with optimal performance at 20–40% relative humidity and capacity reaching 3 mmol g⁻¹ at 35 °C. A prototype operating cyclically on 2.8 kg of sorbent achieved productivity of 8.7 gCO₂ kgsorbent⁻¹ h⁻¹ and specific energy consumption of 2.5 kWh kgCO₂⁻¹. We demonstrate performance is strongly governed by regeneration conditions, water injection volume and inlet air conditions, with warm, dry conditions yielding the best performance.

Continuous struvite production from liquid sidestream digestate using a planar oscillatory flow crystallizer: Kinetic analysis and process assessment
abstract: The recovery of phosphorus and nitrogen from municipal wastewater is receiving growing attention across Europe as a strategy to reduce dependence on conventional fertilizers and advance circular nutrient management. In this context, several full-scale systems have been implemented at wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) to recover nutrients from liquid sidestream digestate (SD), a by-product of anaerobic digestion. In this study, a planar Oscillatory Flow Crystallizer (planar-OFC) was evaluated as an alternative approach for the continuous recovery of nutrients as struvite, a slow-release fertilizer, from SD. The influence of key operational parameters, including hydraulic retention time, reagent dosage, temperature, and pH, was systematically assessed under both batch and continuous modes. In parallel, thermodynamic analyses were conducted to better understand struvite solubility and ionic equilibria in SD matrices. Under the best conditions identified in this study, phosphorus recovery exceeded 80%, with a maximum struvite production of 1.1 kg/m 3 . The kinetics of phosphate recovery were well described by a pseudo-first-order model within the investigated operating conditions, with rate constants above 14 h −1 . Thermodynamic results further identified a favorable temperature range for struvite crystallization. The recovered solids were confirmed to consist predominantly of struvite as the main crystalline phase, with overall chemical purities of at least 92%. Overall, the results demonstrate that the planar-OFC is an effective and compact technology for nutrient recovery, capable of producing high-quality struvite despite the complex composition of SD streams. The findings also validate the proposed kinetic model and highlight the robustness of the reactor design for practical applications.

A biomimetic biofilm-inspired hydrogel for enhanced ultraviolet- shielding and anti-scouring ability of microbial pesticides
abstract: Bacillus thuringiensis is a widely used microbial pesticide but suffers from rapid degradation under ultraviolet radiation and wash-off due to rainwater, limiting its field persistence. Bacterial biofilms are formed by communities that are embedded in a self-produced matrix exhibit a set of “emergent properties” such as ultraviolet- resistance and viscosity. While conventional hydrogels primarily function as passive carriers, this study develops a novel supramolecular hydrogel formulation combining B. thuringiensis spores and crystals simulating a biofilm to enhance environmental resilience. The B. thuringiensis hydrogel exhibits a three-dimensional porous network structure, significant shear-thinning behavior, and rapid self-healing properties, facilitating spray application and adhesion. Compared to conventional B. thuringiensis wettable powder, the hydrogel demonstrates superior anti-scouring ability, increasing 47%–55% insecticidal protein deposition on the surface due to inhibited droplet bouncing and increase in adhesion force by about 85% to tomato leaves. It also enhances ultraviolet resistance, retaining 64–73% more insecticidal proteins after ultraviolet exposure indoors and outdoors, thus, inducing more damage on the gut of target insect larvae. Consequently, the field control efficiency of the hydrogel reached 73% against tomato leafminer after 14 days, 27% higher than the wettable powder. This hydrogel offers a promising approach to prolong microbial pesticide persistence in sustainable agriculture.

Fiber-saturation-point-guided microfibrillation of hemp hurd enabling concurrent performance enhancement of thermoplastic starch/polybutylene adipate terephthalate
abstract: Microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) derived from lignocellulosic agricultural residues holds considerable promise for reinforcing biodegradable thermoplastic starch/polybutylene adipate terephthalate (TPS/PBAT) composite films. However, hornification during drying irreversibly collapses the microporous fibrillar network, severely diminishing its reinforcement efficiency. Herein, a physicochemical dual-control strategy combining fiber saturation point (FSP)-guided moisture conditioning with alkyl ketene dimer (AKD) surface modification was proposed to suppress hornification in microfibrillated hemp hurd (MFH) biofillers. Differential scanning calorimetry established the FSP at approximately 30% moisture content, and a pre-milling moisture content of 37% was identified as the critical optimum for balancing milling brittleness with residual free water retention. AKD modification further sterically inhibited interfibrillar hydrogen bonding via esterification, yielding an AKD-treated MFH, AMFH_37, with a significantly reduced particle size, enhanced specific surface area, and well-preserved porous fibrillar architecture compared to its unmodified counterpart. When incorporated into TPS/PBAT films at 10 wt% loading, AMFH_37 achieved a 26.2% improvement in tensile strength, reduced water vapor and oxygen permeability, a water contact angle of 101.4°, and a relative biodegradability of 99.4% at 45 days. This study demonstrates that simple oven drying combined with optimized moisture pre-conditioning is sufficient to produce hornification-resistant MFC biofillers with outstanding reinforcing efficiency and compostability, establishing a practical and scalable alternative to energy-intensive drying techniques for high-performance biodegradable packaging applications.

title: Integration of microbial hydrolysis by the hyper-thermophilic cellulose- degrading Caldicellulosiruptor bescii with anaerobic digestion
abstract: Integration of 15-d HRT mesophilic primary sludge (PS) digesters with hyperthermophilic hydrolysis (HTH) was evaluated in continuously stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) operated with and without enrichment of Caldicellulosiruptor bescii (CBC). Two CSTRs (R1control and R2 CBC) were operated over four phases, including periods without HTH, HTH operation at a 2-day hydraulic retention time (HRT), CBC inoculation, and reinoculation with an increased HRT of 4 days, with the HTH effluent recirculated to the mesophilic digesters. Across all phases, PS biodegradation efficiency in the R1 control was not different from the R2 CBC i.e. the recirculation of the HTH with and without CBC did not improve the methane yield, with average values ranging from 53%–64%. Offline testing of the control and test HTH reactors 2, and 14 days after CBC inoculation with cellobiose and cellulose confirmed that the CBC did not offer any improvement in the acidification rates. To further assess CBC viability and competitive dynamics, confirmatory offline batch tests conducted using PS slurry and dried PS with HTH inoculum, in the presence and absence of CBC demonstrated that CBC fermentation occurred with a more pronounced effect observed for dried PS where competition from native fermenters was reduced. A modified ADM1-based kinetic model calibrated for cellulose removal showed that under the applied operating conditions (HTH HRT 2–4 days; mesophilic HRT 15 days), more than 80% of the CBC inoculum was washed out 7 days after inoculation. Microbial analysis showed that the inoculated species (CBC) failed to achieve long-term dominance. Instead, reactor performance was dictated by native communities selected by the temperature and the substrate used

title: Synergistic Ag single atoms and nanoclusters on defect-engineered In2S3 for enhanced H2O2 production and in-situ pollutant oxidation
abstract: To address the rapid recombination of photogenerated charge carriers in indium sulfide (In2S3) and meet the growing demand for efficient photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production systems, this study proposes a rational design. Leveraging active nitrogen species generated from urea decomposition during hydrothermal treatment, we successfully doped the In2S3 lattice to construct a nitrogen-modified indium sulfide (N-In2S3) substrate, and subsequently co-anchored silver single atoms and clusters (AgSA+C/N-In2S3) onto it for efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production and pollutant degradation. Nitrogen (N) doping induced sulfur vacancies and lattice distortion, enhancing charge separation and surface reactivity. Ag species were atomically dispersed and firmly anchored onto the N-In2S3 support, serving as efficient electron sinks and active sites. The optimized AgSA+C/N-In2S3 achieved a remarkable H2O2 production rate of 965 μmol g-1 h-1 in pure water via a predominant two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e⁻ ORR) pathway, significantly outperforming pristine In2S3 and N-In2S3. Combined with experimental characterization and DFT calculations revealed that Ag single atoms optimized the adsorption of the *OOH intermediate and reduced the reaction free energy barrier, while Ag clusters facilitated electron redistribution and enhanced oxygen activation. It also demonstrated superior photocatalytic degradation efficiency for organic pollutant like perphenazine (95% removal in 30 min). This study highlights the synergistic effect of bulk doping and surface atomic-level engineering in developing high-performance photocatalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis and environmental remediation.

Constructing a “switch” for photo-thermal catalytic pathway: Directional regulation of NO reduction product distribution by the coordination mode at the La site over Pd–La/CeO2
abstract: The photo-thermal catalysis of NO, CO and H2O to synthesize NH3 has become an effective alternative to the traditional Haber-Bosch process. However, the insufficient understanding of the mechanism of reaction selectivity changes results in the NH3 synthesis of unsatisfactory efficiency. In this study, it’s demonstrated that the coordination environment of La sites acts as an atomic-level “switch” to precisely control the pathway selectivity in the NO-CO-H2O photo-thermal catalytic reaction over Pd–La/CeO2. By synthetically constructing La in a high-coordination doped state versus a low-coordination La2O3 interfacial phase, the dominant product can be programmatically switched between NH3 and N2. Combined in-situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal the underlying mechanism: high-coordination La doping creates sites that efficiently dissociate H2O, providing continuous active H* to drive NO hydrogenation to NH3. In contrast, the low-coordination interface induces specific oxygen vacancies (La–Ov–Ce) that strongly adsorb and activate NO, promoting its direct coupling to N2 in a hydrogen-lean environment. This work establishes “coordination environment engineering” as a general strategy for designing catalysts with programmable selectivity for complex reactions. And this provides a reliable reference for improving the electronic structure of the catalyst to achieve efficient NH3 synthesis.

Synergistic system of bipyridine derivatives and ionic liquid for highly selective lithium ion extraction from complex salt lake brine
abstract: Efficient Li+ extraction from brine rich in Na+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ is crucial for meeting the ever-growing demand for Li. This paper proposes a novel Li+ extraction system based on the N-heterocyclic chelating ligand 6,6'-dimethyl-2,2'-bipyridine (6-Bipi) and the ionic liquid bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([NTf2]-), enabling highly selective Li+ extraction from complex brine. A systematic investigation of how methyl substitution positions on the bipyridine rings regulate on the extraction performance revealed that the precise steric hindrance introduced by ortho-methyl substitution substantially enhances the separation of Li+ from Mg2+, Na+, and Ca2+. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirmed the formation of a four-coordinate distorted tetrahedral complex, [Li(6-Bipi)2][NTf2], which serves as the extractant. Density functional theory calculations helped elucidate the microscopic mechanism underlying the extraction selectivity through thermodynamics, electronic structure, and energy analyses, confirming that the steric hindrance of the ortho-methyl group is the primary driver of the high selectivity. Under optimal conditions, the single-stage Li+ extraction efficiency of this system exceeded 90%, while the extraction efficiencies of Na+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ remained below 5%. Even in brine with Li+ concentrations as low as 0.02 mol/L, the system maintained excellent Li+ extraction performance (73%). This study presents a novel Li+ extraction system characterized by high selectivity and strong adaptability to complex brine and provides valuable theoretical basis and experimental support for the molecular design of N-heterocyclic Li extractants.

abstract: Although Ni-based catalysts hold promise for replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in water electrolysis to energy-saving hydrogen production, their activity and long-term stability require further improvement. Herein, we developed a self-supported catalyst composed of lignin-derived carbon (LC) encapsulating a FeNi3/Ni2V2O7 heterojunction (LC@FeNi3/Ni2V2O7) to tackle these challenges. LC@FeNi3/Ni2V2O7 requires low potentials of 1.22 V and 1.39 V at 10 and 1000 mA cm2. According to operando analysis, the UOR follows an indirect mechanism on the LC@FeNi3/Ni2V2O7 surface. This reaction pathway is facilitated by the synergy between the lignin-derived carbon and the heterointerfaces, which promotes the generation of active NiOOH species and enables a lower potential than catalysts without these components. In addition, the self-supporting structure ensures efficient gas-liquid release, while the carbon layer enhances corrosion resistance, allowing it to achieve a current density of 1.5 A cm2 at only 1.84 V under non- membrane electrode assembly conditions, with a potential decay of only 100 mV over 1100 hours, demonstrating its potential for commercial applications. This work presents not only an efficient UOR catalyst but also a novel strategy for engineering lignin-derived carbon materials to achieve industrial-scale urea-assisted water electrolysi

Synergistic poly(imidobiphenyl-spirofluorene) framework in amino-polybenzimidazole for high-temperature proton exchange membranes with enhanced conductivity and acid retention
abstract: In this study, a poly(imidobiphenyl-spirofluorene) (SBF) framework was incorporated into the molecular chains of amino-functionalized polybenzimidazole (AmPBI) through rational molecular structure design, resulting in the successful preparation of a series of novel high-temperature proton exchange membranes. The imidazole functional group forms strong hydrogen bonds with phosphoric acid (PA), while the microporous framework constructed by spirofluorene units creates continuous additional proton transport pathways. The synergistic effect of these dual advantages significantly enhances PA uptake capacity and high-temperature proton conduction efficiency of the resulting membranes. In addition, the unique pore structure of the phthalimide units effectively traps free PA molecules within the membrane matrix, thereby inhibiting PA leaching and markedly improving PA retention capability. Electrochemical test results show that the AmPBI-SBF-40 membrane exhibits a proton conductivity as high as 203.3 mS cm-1 at 180 ℃. Under the same temperature conditions, its single-cell peak power density reaches 1018.6 mW cm-2. After undergoing a 240-hour long-term acid leaching test under extreme high-temperature conditions of 160 ℃/0% RH, the PA retention rate of the AmPBI-SBF-20 membrane remained at 84%. These results confirm that this series of modified composite membranes exhibits excellent high-temperature proton conductivity, single-cell output performance, and long-term chemical stability.

Fe and oxygen-vacancy engineering unlock coupled AEM-LOM pathways for active and durable alkaline OER
abstract: Developing oxygen evolution electrocatalysts that combine high activity, long-term durability, and low cost remains a central challenge because these properties are often constrained by competing reaction pathways. The adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) is limited by linear scaling relationships, whereas the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) offers higher activity but typically suffers from structural degradation due to lattice oxygen loss. Here, we demonstrate that Fe doping in NiCo 2 O 4 creates a synergistic interplay between Fe active sites and oxygen vacancies, enabling both enhanced activity and durability. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal a dual-mechanism pathway: oxygen vacancies facilitate OH − adsorption to accelerate the AEM, while Fe species regulate O covalency to activate the LOM. Consequently, the optimized NiCo 1.4 Fe 0.6 O 4-y catalyst achieves an ultralow overpotential of 196 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, oxygen vacancies are proposed to facilitate lattice‑oxygen replenishment during LOM operation, thereby helping to mitigate structural degradation. This dynamic regeneration mechanism underpins the excellent long-term stability of more than 290 h. Overall, this work offers a practical strategy to break the activity–stability trade-off in oxygen evolution catalysis through oxygen-vacancy engineering of dual-mechanism pathways.

CRISPR-programmable nanoparticle transport in salt-gated porous media for visual DNA detection
abstract: Paper-based diagnostics typically treat porous cellulose as a passive capillary medium, with nanoparticle transport governed by channel geometry and capture chemistry. Here we show that CRISPR-programmable nanoparticle surface chemistry can actively regulate transport in paper through a salt-activated adhesion mechanism. Gold nanoparticles functionalized with hydrophobic Cy5-labeled DNA exhibit strong adhesion to cellulose fibers at elevated ionic strength (~1.5 M local NaCl generated upon rehydration of preloaded salt), whereas particles lacking hydrophobic domains migrate freely. This phenomenon enables a distance-based visual readout, in which the length of the colored nanoparticle front provides a semi-quantitative measure of DNA target concentration. Optical and electron microscopy reveal that nanoparticle immobilization arises from extensive fiber adhesion rather than pore occlusion or particle aggregation. As a proof of concept, coupling Cas12a-mediated cleavage of Cy5-labeled DNA probes to this salt-gated transport system enabled naked-eye, distance-based detection of Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) DNA with a limit of detection of 100 aM in ~45-60 min. Evaluation of 40 clinical samples showed excellent agreement with qPCR, achieving 96.2% sensitivity and 100% specificity. More broadly, this work establishes a general strategy for programming nanoparticle transport in porous media by encoding functionality directly into nanoparticle surface chemistry.

A pseudo-bilayer organic photoanode for solar water oxidation
abstract: Organic photoelectrochemical (PEC) cells for solar water splitting typically utilize bulk heterojunction (BHJ) structures to circumvent the intrinsically short exciton diffusion lengths of organic semiconductors. However, stochastic donor/acceptor networks in BHJs often result in disordered interfacial contacts, leading to severe charge recombination. Herein, we report a pseudo-bilayer (PS-Bi) organic photoanode featuring a vertically ordered donor–acceptor configuration established via sequential deposition. Our systematic investigation reveals that this PS-Bi structure promotes selective charge transport and suppresses recombination due to its high domain purity, thereby facilitating efficient charge transfer at the interface. Consequently, the optimized PS-Bi photoanodes deliver an enhanced average photocurrent density (Jph) of 1.75 ± 0.03 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode for solar water oxidation, while simultaneously exhibiting a significant cathodic onset shift and extended operational stability compared to the BHJ counterpart (Jph = 1.44 ± 0.07 mA cm−2). This study demonstrates that employing the PS-Bi structure is a promising strategy for achieving high-performance and stable organic PEC systems for sustainable solar fuel production.

Ultrastable γ-Al2O3 catalyst co-doped with zinc and phosphate for stable CF4 hydrolysis over 3700 h
abstract: Tetrafluoromethane (CF 4 ) is among the most persistent greenhouse gases, with a global warming potential of 6500 and an atmospheric lifetime that exceeds 50,000 years, making its abatement a critical environmental challenge. Among the various abatement strategies, catalytic hydrolysis over alumina-based materials has received significant attention. However, γ-Al 2 O 3 catalyst readily transforms into catalytically inert α-Al 2 O 3 upon exposure to hydrofluoric acid (HF), resulting in poor long-term stability and making its practical application highly challenging. In this study, ZnAlPO 4 catalyst is prepared by simultaneously incorporating phosphate (P) and zinc (Zn) into a γ-Al 2 O 3 framework. Phosphate addition provides thermodynamically stable phosphate-alumina interaction that suppress HF-induced phase transitions, thereby improving durability. Meanwhile, zinc incorporation modifies the electronic structure of alumina, generating strong Lewis acidic environments and promoting charge-transfer interaction with CF 4 , thereby facilitating activation. The optimized Zn(20)AlPO 4 catalyst, containing 20 wt% Zn, achieves complete CF 4 conversion at 700 °C and maintains 100% activity for over 3700 h under 5000 ppm CF 4 . These findings demonstrate that Zn(20)AlPO 4 is a stable and economically viable candidate for long-term CF 4 hydrolysis.

Robust NiO-based catalysts with lattice-surface La/Si synergy for efficient and poison-resistant methane combustion
abstract: In this work, highly active and durable NiO-based catalysts featuring La-Si-NiO triple interactions were prepared via controlled precipitation for methane combustion. In the optimally co-doped catalyst, both Si and La were incorporated into the NiO lattice to inhibit crystallite growth, while simultaneously forming surface Si-O-La species and dispersed small La2O2CO3 crystallites. This unique structure enriched active Ni2+ species and surface acid-base sites for methane adsorption and activation, while also improving the reducibility of Ni species and increasing surface oxygen species to accelerate methane dissociation and deep oxidation, ultimately delivering excellent catalytic activity with a T90 of 380 °C. Moreover, dispersed La2O2CO3 crystallites preferentially reacted with SO2 and shielded Ni2+ active sites from sulfation. Hydrophobic Si-O species and Brønsted acid sites improved water tolerance, while reactive oxygen species promoted sulfite formation and inhibited H2O adsorption. These effects synergistically endowed the catalyst with remarkable sulfur and water tolerance, enabling efficient methane conversion under harsh SO2/H2O coexisting conditions and underscoring its practical potential.

Oscillatory motion of trickle-bed reactor can break up liquid channeling and thus increase reaction efficiency
abstract: We report that applying an oscillatory pitching motion can substantially increase the reaction efficiency in trickle-bed reactors used for the hydrogenation of liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHC). In the present experiments, steady-state reaction was reached 14 times faster and with approx. 25% larger mean efficiency for the pitching reactor compared to the conventional non-moving reactor. Increasing the pitching amplitude from 1° to 4° accelerated the reaction by about 45%. Strong memory effects were observed, with increased reaction efficiency being maintained for 2 h in a non-moving reactor, if the reactor had been operated under oscillatory pitching motion beforehand. Therefore, the present results indicate that substantial efficiency increases do not require continuous oscillations, instead already occasional reactor motions may suffice. We hypothesize that the increase in efficiency is due to breaking-up of liquid channels. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations and cold-flow experiments are reported that strongly support this theory. It is anticipated that the present findings will be applicable to many other types of trickle-bed reactors as well.

Comparative evaluation of ceramic pellet architectures for Rh-based catalysts in on-board hydrogen production via ammonia decomposition
abstract: On-board hydrogen production via ammonia decomposition requires catalytic reactor designs that balance high activity with space and weight constraints. This study presents a systematic comparative evaluation of six ceramic pellet architectures as supports for rhodium (Rh)-based catalysts, including commercial γ-alumina spheres, microchannel-structured smart pellets, three types of ceramic proppants (referred to as ISP (Intermediate Strength Proppant), LWP (Lightweight Proppant), HSP (High Strength Proppant)), and SiO 2 . A scalable resorcinol–formaldehyde sol–gel method (0.5 kg batches) was used to deposit carbon xerogel (CX) coatings on the pellets, followed by impregnation with 2 wt% Rh. Catalytic performance was assessed in terms of ammonia conversion, turnover frequency (TOF), and thermal stability. Among the supports tested, commercial γ-alumina spheres exhibited the highest activity, achieving a TOF total = 79 mol NH3 ·mol Rh −1 ·h −1 , TOF surface = 308 mol NH3 ·mol Rh −1 ·h −1 , and H₂ space-time yield = 1013 (mol H2 ·m −3 ·h −1 ) at 450 °C (second light-off experiment), attributed to their high surface area and enhanced wettability, which promoted uniform Rh nanoparticle dispersion. Other architectures showed lower activities (with second light-off experiment TOF surface between 10 and 131 molNH 3 ·mol Rh −1 ·h −1 at 450 °C, following the order: Rh/CX smart > Rh/CX ISP = Rh/CX HSP > Rh/CX SiO 2 > Rh/CX LWP). Significant activity increases were observed upon a second light-off cycle for all the catalysts, indicating surface reconstruction effects. Long-term stability tests, including 10 thermal shocks and 100 h of continuous operation, confirmed the robustness of the commercial γ-alumina spheres. These findings highlight the critical role of pellet architecture in the design of efficient catalytic reactors for on-board hydrogen production via ammonia decomposition.

title: Near-wall bubble dynamics in water electrolysis on vertical dual microelectrodes
abstract: Bubble coverage during hydrogen evolution in water electrolysis reduces the effective reaction area and increases interfacial resistance. Promoting early bubble detachment through coalescence is therefore an important strategy for enhancing electrolysis performance. In this work, a microscale vertical dual platinum-wire microelectrode system capable of stable and independently controlled bubble generation was established to investigate the near-wall dynamics of coalesced bubbles under different overall voltages and inter-electrode voltage difference. Three typical post-coalescence modes were identified, namely direct-detachment bubble (DDB), detachment-return bubble (DRB), and non-detachment bubble (NDB). The dominant mode was found to change sequentially from DDB to DRB and finally to NDB as the overall applied voltage increased or the inter-electrode voltage asymmetry became stronger. In the DDB regime, the maximum wall-normal jumping distance followed a 3/2 power-law scaling with the departure radius. Based on the geometric relation between the post-coalescence bubble and newly generated bubbles in the near-wall region, together with the competition of characteristic time scales, a critical current model was established for the DDB/DRB transition. An energy-based criterion incorporating Marangoni effects was further proposed for the DRB/NDB transition. Compared with horizontal dual-electrode and single-electrode systems, the vertical dual-electrode configuration more effectively promoted coalescence-induced detachment and suppressed repeated near-wall interactions, thereby yielding a higher average current and a shorter detachment period. This work provides new physical insight into bubble regulation at gas-evolving electrochemical interfaces and provides guidance for optimizing electrode configurations.

title: Local lattice strain in layered double hydroxides enhances flexoelectric effect for hydraulically driven water disinfection
abstract: Hydraulically driven flexocatalysis offers a sustainable water disinfection strategy that requires no chemical disinfectants or energy-intensive inputs. However, its efficiency is limited by insufficient strain gradients and weak flexoelectric polarization. Herein, we employ a local strain modulation strategy by incorporating Te atoms into NiMn layered double hydroxides (Te-NiMn LDH) to achieve hydraulically driven flexocatalytic disinfection. Te sites serve as local strain centers that amplify strain gradients under mechanical stress to enhance flexoelectric polarization. The asymmetric Ni–O–Te coordination promotes dipole polarization, enhances Ni–O covalency, and accelerates electron localization at electron-rich Te sites, boosting O2 adsorption-activation for increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) under mechanical stress. Moreover, the strong interaction between Te-NiMn LDH and cell membranes enables in situ ROS attack to disrupt bacterial protective barriers, followed by rapid impairment of metabolic and self-defense systems, thereby enhancing reaction selectivity. Therefore, Te-NiMn LDH inactivates 99.74% of Escherichia coli under 60 min of stirring in a batch reactor. Notably, the fabricated continuous flow-through reactor based on the loaded Te-NiMn LDH achieves over 91% removal of Escherichia coli in real secondary effluent and over 95% in surface water matrix under high-speed stirring. By enhancing the flexoelectric effect through local strain engineering, this work advances a low-carbon and high-performance hydraulically driven catalytic approach for water disinfection.

Nitrogen fixation using a pin-to-pin arc plasma: Effects of operating parameters on NOx formation characteristics and arc stability
abstract: Atmospheric-pressure plasma-based nitrogen fixation has attracted significant attention as a promising alternative to the conventional Haber–Bosch process due to its potential for decentralized operation and compatibility with renewable energy sources. In this study, nitrogen oxidation in a pin-to-pin arc plasma reactor was systematically investigated to evaluate the effects of key operating parameters on NOx formation, NO selectivity, energy cost, and arc stability. The parameters examined included pin-to-pin gap distance, swirl intensity, gas flow rate, oxygen concentration, and delivered power. Arc dynamics and plasma characteristics were analyzed using high-speed imaging combined with spectral proper orthogonal decomposition (SPOD), while optical emission spectroscopy (OES) was employed to characterize the thermal state of the plasma and the formation of reactive species. The results showed that increasing the gas flow rate and the pin-to-pin gap enhanced NOx production and reduced the energy cost. The minimum energy cost achieved in this study was approximately 2.5 MJ/mol, indicating the potential of pin-to-pin arc plasma technology as an energy-efficient and scalable nitrogen fixation process. Oxygen concentration was also identified as a critical parameter influencing both nitrogen oxidation efficiency and discharge stability. The highest NO production was observed at an intermediate oxygen concentration of approximately 30%, while the maximum total NOx production and the lowest energy cost were obtained at an oxygen concentration of 40%. In terms of delivered power, lower power conditions resulted in higher energy cost and reduced arc stability, indicating the existence of an optimal operating window. Therefore, further reductions in energy consumption are expected to be achievable through optimization of operating parameters, including delivered power, oxygen concentration, and swirl intensity.

Multi-scale error-triggered latent assimilation for reduced-order digital twins of gas–solid flow reactors
abstract: Gas-solid flow reactors are complex dynamical systems in chemical engineering, characterised by highly coupled, multi-scale physical fields that evolve over space and time. Accurate and efficient prediction of these reactors is essential for monitoring and optimisation, yet remains challenging due to limited and noisy measurements for validation, as well as the prohibitive cost of large-scale high-fidelity simulations. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a correction-enhanced reduced-order modelling (ROM) approach with multi-scale latent assimilation for gas-solid flow reactors. The method conditionally corrects the prior predictions obtained from a data-driven ROM by assimilating observations in a low-dimensional latent space. In the offline stage, multi-scale Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and β -Variational Autoencoder (mPOD– β -VAE)compress the system into multi-scale latent spaces, significantly reducing both dimensionality and computational cost. During the online stage, forecast errors between the encoded observations and the ROM prediction are checked. When this error exceeds a dynamically determined threshold value, latent assimilation is triggered to update the prior latent state using an ensemble Kalman filter. The corrected latent state is subsequently decoded and reconstructed to obtain a more accurate state estimate. This methodology is demonstrated using a lab-scale fluidised bed reactor. The results show that the proposed framework achieves superior reconstruction of both observable and unobservable variables, reduces latent-state prediction errors through stable and well-conditioned assimilation updates, and delivers a substantial reduction of computational load. This approach reduces the computational complexity by 99.8% compared to conventional CFD-DEM and improves predictive accuracy by 44.4% over a standalone ROM, while maintaining a computational cost comparable to the standalone ROM. Overall, the proposed approach offers a promising tool for real-time prediction and monitoring in chemical engineering applications, paving the way towards a next-generation digital twin for gas-solid flow reactors.

Hybrid cryogels of cellulose nanofibers and phase-change capsules for smart dual-function thermoactive packaging
abstract: Herein, sustainable dual-function thermoactive cold-chain packaging architectures were fabricated by integrating ionically crosslinked calcium alginate–coated biogenic phase-change material (PCM) capsules into a super-insulating cellulose nanofiber (CNF) cryogel scaffold with ultrahigh porosity (>99%). This hybrid structure combines the exceptionally low thermal conductivity of the nanofibrous cryogel matrix (0.022 ± 0.001 W·m −1 ·K −1 , even below that of air) with the high latent-heat storage capacity of the encapsulated PCM (91.19 J·g −1 ), enabling simultaneous passive insulation and active thermal regulation. The PCM capsules exhibited a phase-change temperature of 6.5 °C and retained structural integrity and thermal functionality over 250 melting–freezing cycles. Thus, they effectively suppressed leakage and interfacial degradation within the CNF network. An optimized formulation with a CNF-to-PCM mass ratio of 1:1.5 (CNF PCMC 1.5 ) integrated mechanical robustness and thermal buffering performance, maintaining cushioning stability under ambient and cold storage conditions. It also delayed the surface temperature rise by up to 7 °C compared with the pristine CNF cryogel (CNF PCMC 0 ). Soil burial tests demonstrated the degradable nature of the prepared hybrid cryogels. A packaging prototype designed using CNF PCMC 1.5 demonstrated superior thermal buffering capability compared with that designed using CNF PCMC 0 , underscoring its suitability for temperature-sensitive smart packaging.

Decoupled sulfur redox pathways governed by initial chemical states in all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries
abstract: All-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems owing to their high energy density and enhanced safety. However, their practical implementation is hindered by the limited understanding of sulfur redox reactions in solid-state environments, which are often assumed to follow the conventional S8–Li2S conversion mechanism established in liquid electrolytes. Here, we demonstrate that the redox pathways of sulfur in ASSLSBs are fundamentally governed by the initial chemical state of sulfur, leading to distinct and non-equivalent reaction mechanisms for S8 and Li2S cathodes under unpressurized conditions at room temperature. Comprehensive X-ray-based analyses combined with electrochemical characterization reveal that the S8-based ASSLSB delivers a high discharge capacity of ~1400 mAh g−1 but undergoes irreversible conversion without regenerating S8, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and rapid capacity fading. In contrast, the Li2S-based ASSLSB exhibits reversible redox behavior through short-chain sulfur species (S2–4), enabling stable cycling with a capacity of ~1200 mAh g−1 and near-unity Coulombic efficiency. These findings establish that, contrary to the conventional conversion paradigm, the initial sulfur speciation determines the redox pathway in solid-state systems. Therefore, controlling sulfur speciation offers a new design strategy for achieving stable ASSLSBs under practical operating conditions.

abstract: The rise of drug-resistant bacterial infections poses a critical threat to global health, underscoring an urgent need for effective antibiotic-free therapeutic strategies. Here, we present hierarchical flower-like PtCuTe nanozymes, which synthesized via a straightforward solvothermal method, that integrate photothermal therapy (PTT) with chemodynamic therapy (CDT) to achieve synergistic antibacterial effects. PtCuTe nanozymes possess exceptional photothermal performance, elevating the dispersion temperature to 85.2 °C upon 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, coupled with robust Fenton-like catalytic activity that efficiently converts H2O2 into highly toxic ·OH. This dual functionality yields a pronounced synergistic effect, achieving high bactericidal rates of 93.45% against S. aureus and 99.45% against E. coli in vitro. Notably, it also demonstrated remarkable efficacy against clinically relevant drug-resistant strains, with bactericidal rates of 95.31% against methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and 98.43% against multidrug-resistant E. coli (MDR E. coli). Transcriptomic analysis unveils a distinctive “stress-exhaustion” antibacterial mechanism. Furthermore, PtCuTe nanoflowers show excellent antimicrobial property, notably accelerating wound healing and excellent biocompatibility for further Wound healing application. The PtCuTe nanoflowers emerge as a safe and highly promising antibiotic-free nanoplatform. This work establishes a “stress-exhaustion” therapeutic paradigm, providing a promising antibiotic-free strategy for combating drug-resistant bacterial infections.

Operating parameters and sorbent properties affecting Ca(OH)2 carbonation for direct air Capture (DAC) applications
abstract: Direct Air Capture (DAC) based on Ca(OH) 2 carbonation has emerged as a promising route for atmospheric CO 2 removal. However, the maximum attainable carbonation conversion (X Max ), a key parameter governing sorbent utilization and process performance, is strongly influenced by operating conditions and sorbent properties. In this work, X Max was investigated over a wide range of CO 2 concentrations (500–120,000 ppm), relative humidity (10–95%), and temperatures (30–80 °C), using both commercial standard and high-surface-area Ca(OH) 2 materials. The results show that X Max exhibits a sigmoidal dependence on relative humidity and is strongly affected by sorbent surface area. Higher CO 2 concentrations increase initial carbonation rates but may reduce the maximum attainable conversion, while temperature has a comparatively smaller influence on X Max within the investigated range. Based on the experimental dataset, an empirical correlation was developed to calculate X Max as a function of CO 2 concentration, relative humidity, temperature, and sorbent specific surface area. The proposed correlation provides a simple tool for estimating X Max within the range of conditions investigated and may facilitate material screening, operating-condition assessment, and preliminary evaluation of Ca(OH) 2 -based DAC systems.

abstract: Selective electrodialysis (SED) is a promising technique for Li + separation; however, its application in Li-ion batteries (LIBs) recycling requires further studies to assess its feasibility under long-term operation and to develop maintenance protocols that enable continuous operation as a step toward scaling up the process. This work proposed a long-term SED process comprising three sequential stages for Li + separation from LiFePO 4 (LFP) battery leachate. First, the effect of pH (1.0–2.4), Li + concentration (3.2–6 g/L) and coexisting ions (Fe 2+ and Al 3+ ) were evaluated to elucidate system behavior and to define operating conditions for long-term experiment. Li + separation was performed in the first two stages using fresh LFP leached solution, followed by a final purification stage. System limitations were observed (e.g., ion leakage, membrane scaling, maintenance operation and recovery-purity trade-off). Final solution in the process contains 3 g/L Li + (7.8 × 10 −5 to 8.6 × 10 −5 mol/(cm 2 ·h) and 91% purity) with residual 0.3 g/L Fe 2+ and 0.003 g/L Al 3+ reaching Li + separation over 74%, with selectivity values of 5.3–18.8 (Li + /Fe 2+ ) and 18.3–279.9 (Li + /Al 3+ ). Ion-exchange membranes changes were further evaluated revealing degradation of both cationic and anionic membranes, while the monovalent ion-exchange membrane structure and morphology remained unchanged demonstrating its chemical stability after 160 h of operation. Overall, this work advances the understanding of SED for LIB recycling and provides insights for process optimization prior to scaling up.

Ultrasound-assisted physical cleaning for rapid restoration of surface nanofiltration membrane permeability in direct surface water treatment
abstract: Submerged nanofiltration (SNF) is an emerging approach for the direct treatment of surface water. Controlling membrane fouling during SNF is key to establishing a chemical-free system. This study evaluated intermittent ultrasonic (US) cleaning for controlling membrane fouling during SNF treatment using a polyamide nanofiltration (NF) membrane. Unlike previous studies that focused mainly on flux recovery, this study assessed US cleaning based on membrane integrity, effects of repeated SNF operations, and permeate stability. US exposure was applied at 26 kHz, 50 W, and a power density of 32.4 W/cm2. In the 2 cm probe-to-membrane distance configuration, MgSO4 rejection decreased slightly from 90% to 86% after 540 min of cumulative exposure. In contrast, US exposure at a 4 cm distance across another membrane did not affect MgSO4 rejection, suggesting a lower risk of membrane deterioration. Over 6 days of SNF treatment of dam water, the permeance of the NF membranes decreased by 24% due to membrane fouling. Cleaning with US for 5 min at a 4 cm probe-membrane distance fully restored membrane permeance. The effectiveness of US cleaning was further demonstrated over five SNF cycles for 30 days with a 5 min US cleaning duration, resulting in stable rejection of turbidity (93–97%) and organic matter, evaluated by DOC (77–88%) and UV254 (81–90%). Membrane characterization revealed that US cleaning removed major foulants, including proteinaceous organic matter and inorganic substances. These results suggest that periodic US cleaning is a promising strategy for stable operation without frequent chemical cleaning. Chemical Engineering Journal, 545, art. no. 179650; 2026

Feed-gas-modulated reactive nitrogen selectivity in plasma-activated water using microbubble-enhanced corona processing
abstract: Cold plasma activation generates nitrogen-enriched plasma-activated water (PAW), but control over nitrite–nitrate selectivity remains to be established for target applications from nitrogen fixation. Here we demonstrate how to control aqueous speciation by modulating feed gas (nitrogen and air mixture) composition and its flow dynamics in a microbubble-enhanced cold plasma activation (MB-CPA) platform. By utilizing a gastight module integrated with a needle–corona plasma generator, reactive species delivery via microbubbles can be tuned by varying the N 2 volume fraction ( X N 2 = 78 –100 vol%) and the gas-flow regime (represented by Reynolds number, R e g =101–404). N 2 -rich operation yields nitrite-dominant PAW with low nitrate selectivity ( ) ∼ 0.1 , whereas air feeds accelerate nitrite-to-nitrate conversion, driving near-exclusive nitrate production ( ). Furthermore, intensifying the gas flow regime allows for the continuous tuning of selectivity from 0.11 to 0.79 while achieving a yield of 2818.7 μ m ol- /kWh within 1-min treatment. Notably, doubling the plasma discharge scale preserves the selectivity while enhancing the formation rate by 2.8-fold in pure nitrogen. We further demonstrate that increasing the alkalinity of the treated water shifts the oxidation–accumulation balance, allowing nitrite to persist ( > 60 μ M) even as nitrate increases to ∼ 200 μ M. Finally, N 2 -activated PAW outperforms air-activated alternatives, significantly enhancing the proliferation and biomass yields of the model microalgae, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii , due to its optimized nitrogen speciation. These results provide effective approaches for selective, energy-efficient PAW production in MB-CPA systems and support scalable, application-specific tuning between oxidative treatment and nitrogen-enriched cultivation media.

title: Constructing single-atom Fe sites in NH2-UiO-66 for efficient and sacrificial-agent-free photocatalytic uranium extraction
Cold atmospheric plasma triggers Bacillus subtilis membrane vesicles secretion through SOS-endolysin pathway and iron homeostasis modulation with antipathogen efficacy
abstract: Gram-positive bacterial membrane vesicles (MVs) are natural biomaterials with great potential in intercellular communication and antipathogen defense, while the thick cell wall leads to extremely low natural yields, severely limiting their large-scale production and practical application. Herein, we developed a green and efficient physical strategy using cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) to induce high-yield MVs from Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis), a widely used probiotic and biocontrol agent. CAP treatment condition was identified, achieving a 10.19-fold increase in MVs particle yield compared with the untreated control, with superior production efficiency to traditional ultrasonic disruption. Mechanistically, the synergistic action of CAP-generated acidic stress, reactive oxygen/nitrogen species (RONS), and physical discharge caused cell wall/membrane damage and intracellular oxidative stress, which further activated the SOS response, endolysin pathway, and iron metabolism regulation. Material characterization confirmed that CAP-induced MVs (CAP MVs) retained a conserved spherical nanostructure with uniform size distribution, and shared 96.2% protein components with control MVs, ensuring biosafety. Meanwhile, CAP MVs were enriched with functional proteins related to oxidative stress response and cell wall degradation. Moreover, both control and CAP MVs exhibited antipathogen activity against Gram-positive/negative bacteria and fungi, with CAP MVs showing enhanced efficacy due to altered protein composition. Notably, the B. subtilis MVs was first identified as a key inducer in antipathogen activity. This study provided a green strategy for high-yield MVs production and uncovered a novel application for B. subtilis MVs, advancing the biogenesis of extracellular vesicles in prokaryotes.

title: A detailed kinetic study of selective electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia
abstract: The electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (eNO 3 RR) offers a dual benefit of converting nitrate pollutants into valuable ammonia while circumventing the limitations of the nitrogen reduction reaction. However, this complex multi-step proton-electron transfer process with stable intermediates necessitates highly active and selective catalysts. Despite extensive progress in catalyst development, a fundamental understanding of eNO 3 RR kinetics remains limited. Herein, we present a detailed kinetic evaluation of the individual eNO 3 RR steps using accessible electrochemical approaches, including impedance analysis, diffusion coefficient calculations, and multistep Bulter Volmer kinetic analysis. Spinel NiCo 2 S 4 nanoparticles were employed as the model catalyst, showing an ammonia yield rate of 3223.9 ± 168.3 μg h −1 cm −2 at −0.30 V RHE with a Faradaic efficiency of 64.0% in 0.1 M KOH containing 0.5 M KNO 3 electrolyte. The kinetic dependence on NOx reactants and electrolyte concentration was further analyzed to evaluate the contribution of individual reaction steps. Combined with in situ spectroscopic identification of surface intermediates, the kinetic analysis enabled identification of the rate-determining step in eNO 3 RR. This study provides mechanistic and kinetic insights into eNO 3 RR and proposes a practical working model that can be extended to other eNO 3 RR catalysts.
