Closed-loop recyclable and ultra-low temperature resistant underwater adhesive
abstract: Ultra-low temperature resistant underwater adhesives are crucial for marine engineering and flexible electronics, yet integrating low-temperature tolerance, underwater adhesion, and closed-loop recyclability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we design a crown ether-tackified poly(thioctic acid) adhesive, where dibenzo-18-crown-6 ether regulates the water state by converting free water into bound water via hydrogen bonding, preserving interfacial integrity and preventing embrittlement at ultra-low temperatures. The adhesive exhibits excellent underwater adhesion on various substrates and maintains a wide tolerable temperature range from -196 °C to 110 °C. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations further confirm the key role of crown ethers in enhancing both adhesive strength and low-temperature resistance. Notably, the adhesive achieves closed-loop recycling of crown ether and thioctic acid, with recovery rates exceeding 90%. Importantly, the crown ether-tackified strategy provides a universal approach for designing cryogenically tolerant and recyclable underwater adhesives. Collectively, this work offers new insights for advancing sustainable adhesive materials for extreme cryogenic environments.

title: Engineering a covalent S-scheme heterojunction in TpBpy/MIL-68(In) to boost interfacial charge transfer for efficient solar-to-hydrogen conversion
abstract: Engineering high-efficiency S-scheme heterojunctions with robust interfacial charge transfer channels is critical for simultaneously achieving spatial charge separation and preserving the strong redox potential of photogenerated carriers. Herein, we report the first construction of a novel covalently integrated TpBpy/MIL-68(In) S-scheme heterostructure via an in situ solvothermal strategy. Uniquely, MIL-68(In) nanorods function as dynamic quasi-templates, in which partial structural dissolution orchestrates an in situ self-etching process to guide the epitaxial growth of TpBpy via Schiff-base condensation. This dynamic evolution transforms simple two-dimensional physical contact into a three-dimensionally interlocked covalent interface, thereby maximizing the effective contact area. The optimized covalently integrated heterostructure exhibits an outstanding photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 13.7 mmol·g-1·h-1 under simulated sunlight, representing a remarkable enhancement of 68.5-fold and 1.9-fold compared to pristine MIL-68(In) and TpBpy, respectively. Furthermore, combined in situ irradiated XPS and DFT calculations provide direct evidence for the interfacial electron cloud redistribution induced by chemical bonds. These robust covalent bridges establish a strong built-in electric field (IEF) and continuous low-impedance channels, effectively circumventing the high contact resistance and severe charge recombination typical of physically mixed systems. This work provides a meaningful paradigm for the interfacial engineering of MOF/COF-based covalent heterojunctions to achieve advanced solar-to-hydrogen conversion.

Understanding the deactivation mechanisms of ethanol conversion over Cu-Y/Beta catalyst
abstract: Direct conversion of bioethanol to C₃⁺ olefins is a promising pathway for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production, but catalyst deactivation limits long-term operation. The stability and deactivation mechanisms of multifunctional Cu–Y/Beta zeolite catalysts were investigated for ethanol-to-olefins conversion over 300 h time-on-stream in the presence of H2. Catalytic testing reveals progressive losses in ethanol conversion and C₃⁺ olefin selectivity accompanied by increased acetaldehyde formation. The catalyst testing studies correlate with a suite of characterizations of fresh, spent, and regenerated catalysts to identify the deactivation factors. The loss of Y Lewis acid sites is the primary deactivation element. Reversible acid site deactivation is caused by coke deposition, which blocks Y-derived Lewis acid sites responsible for aldol condensation, MPV reduction, and alcohol dehydration. Minor irreversible deactivation is observed and possibly results from hydrothermal dehydroxylation of Y–silanol interactions. This causes permanent loss of Lewis acidity without zeolite framework degradation or Y aggregation. Cu sites undergo limited agglomeration into small nanoparticles but contribute insignificantly to catalyst deactivation under the investigated time frame. Oxidative regeneration removes coke and redistributes Cu sites, leading to full recovery of the initial catalytic performance though the Y Lewis acid sites are unable to fully recover. These findings establish Lewis acid site degradation as the primary deactivation mechanism impacting long-term catalyst stability.

Anode-free solid-state batteries: Interfacial engineering across solid electrolyte classes toward practical implementation
abstract: Anode-free batteries markedly improve cell-level energy density by eliminating a pre-loaded anode. In this configuration, lithium ions extracted from the cathode are electrochemically deposited onto the current collector during charging, thereby minimizing the need for excess lithium. Moreover, the anode-free concept can simplify manufacturing by avoiding the handling and lamination of reactive Li metal. Most early progress in anode-free batteries has been made in liquid electrolytes, where continuous exposure of freshly deposited Li to the electrolyte drives persistent electrolyte consumption and interphase growth, accelerating cell failure. In recent years, attention has shifted toward anode-free solid-state batteries, where the dominant challenges differ from those in liquid cells. In solid-state systems, contact loss, void growth, and chemo-mechanical instability at buried solid–solid interfaces become the major failure modes. The severity of these issues depends strongly on the solid electrolyte class and the interfacial chemistry and mechanical integrity of anode-free electrodes. Here, we summarize the characteristics of oxide, sulfide, halide, and polymer-based solid electrolytes and highlight state-of-the-art anode-free electrode strategies, including carbon interlayers that mediate Li transport and deposition, reaction-driven metal or compound approaches that regulate nucleation via reversible chemistry, and electrolyte-side engineering that generates lithiophilic nucleation sites in situ. Finally, we outline advanced operando/in situ and ex situ characterization methods that enable mechanistic interpretation of buried interfacial processes and provide an outlook on integrated materials and engineering directions toward practical anode-free solid-state batteries.

title: A bone-homing DNA tetrahedral framework nucleic acids nanodevice orchestrates osteogenic regeneration to rescue postmenopausal osteoporosis
abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) represents a pervasive metabolic crisis driven by a dysregulated bone microenvironment, where the chronic inflammation leads to rapid deterioration of bone microstructure. However, the clinical management of PMOP remains fundamentally limited by a “delivery dilemma”: conventional osteogenic agents suffer from abysmal bioavailability, rapid systemic clearance, and indiscriminate biodistribution, often necessitating high doses that induce severe extraskeletal toxicity. To overcome these physiological barriers, a programmable, bone-homing nanotherapeutic strategy needs to be engineered. First, tFNA is conjugated with the osteogenic targeting peptide (SDSSD) to confer bone-homing capability. Genistein (Gen) is then encapsulated within the rigid DNA nanocage of tFNA-SDSSD, forming a multifunctional nanodevice (tFNA-SDSSD/Gen) with high cellular uptake efficiency and efficient bone-homing. Mechanistic studies reveal that tFNA-SDSSD/Gen acts as a "molecular switch" to reverse inflammation-induced osteogenic arrest of osteoblasts within the PMOP microenvironment by synergistically activating the PI3K/AKT and MAPK signaling cascades. Systemic administration in ovariectomized mice significantly mitigates trabecular bone loss and restores bone microarchitecture quality with negligible off-target toxicity. These findings demonstrate the great potential of tFNA-SDSSD/Gen in the treatment of osteoporosis, thus providing a robust strategy for targeted therapy of metabolic bone diseases.

Deciphering sulfidation chemistry of nanoscale zerovalent iron for enhanced reductive defluorination of trace PFOA: Precursor-driven core-shell engineering and electron transfer
abstract: The high stability of C-F bond makes PFAS reductive destruction a significant challenge. Here we show that sulfidation can dramatically enhance nanoscale zerovalent iron (NZVI) reactivity when sulfur precursor and synthesis procedure are rationally paired. A library of sulfidated NZVI (SNZVI) was synthesized using three precursors (Na₂S₂O₄, Na₂S₂O₃, Na₂S) and two procedures. The Na₂S₂O₄-mediated two-step sulfidation (SNZVI-2/Na₂S₂O₄) achieved a 9.08-fold increase in observed rate constant (kobs=0.0047 min⁻¹) and approximately 15% defluorination of trace PFOA (50 μg/L) within 60 min under ambient conditions—a performance not previously reported at such low concentration without external energy input. Surface area-normalized rate constants confirmed enhanced intrinsic reactivity. Mechanistic analysis demonstrated that this superiority stems from a well-defined core-shell heterostructure. The two-step procedure preserves a structurally intact Fe⁰ core by preventing competitive nucleation, while Na₂S₂O₄ strips native oxides to form a thin, conductive FeS shell. Partial least squares (PLS) modeling identified five co-varying descriptors that collectively represent core-shell integrity as a single latent variable. The optimized material demonstrated progressive detoxification, robust performance in real water matrices, and partial regenerability. This work deciphers the sulfidation chemistry governing PFAS defluorination, providing a mechanistic framework for designing high-performance reductive nanomaterials.

Carbon-support-dependent interfacial environments governing electrode activity and degradation in PEMFCs: Insights from distribution of relaxation time analysis
abstract: Carbon supports play a critical role in determining the performance and durability of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells. However, the fundamental principles by which carbon supports govern electrode activity and degradation remain poorly understood, owing to their unclear role in defining electrochemical environments. Herein, we uncover the crucial role of carbon supports by tracing the evolution of electrochemical characteristics of electrified interfaces within porous electrodes. Through operando capacitance estimation via distribution of relaxation time analysis and carbon-corrosion-induced accelerated stress test using carbon supports with varying intrinsic properties, we show that electrode activity is strongly correlated with accessible electrochemical interfaces within porous electrodes, whose dynamic evolution during operation and reconstruction upon carbon oxidation-induced degradation are governed by the intrinsic carbon natures. This work establishes a cornerstone for bridging the long-standing gap between material characteristics of carbon supports and electrochemical properties of porous electrodes, providing a rational understanding of how carbon support govern electrode functionality and degradation.

title: Biomimetic hierarchical scaffold with Zn2+/Mg2+ dual-ion synergistic release for sequential immunomodulation to enhance bone regeneration
Beyond adsorption: Metal species and interfacial perturbation govern urease inhibition by engineered nanoparticles
abstract: Engineered nanoparticles (ENPs) can alter soil enzyme activity, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying ENP-mediated enzyme inhibition remain insufficiently understood. Here, we combined biochemical, interfacial, structural, radical, and peptide-level analyses to elucidate urease inhibition by representative ENPs. Moving beyond adsorption-based interpretations of ENP-induced enzyme inhibition, we show that urease inhibition cannot be predicted solely by adsorption capacity and instead involves material-dependent interfacial interactions and dissolved metal species. nCuO and nZnO caused pronounced inhibition, with dissolved Cu/Zn species contributing to activity loss, while particle-associated interfacial interactions remained essential. nFe 3 O 4 produced moderate inhibition mainly through surface-mediated interactions and oligomeric perturbation, with limited contribution from dissolved Fe species. In contrast, nSiO 2 strongly adsorbed urease but caused negligible activity loss because it induced only minor secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structural perturbations, revealing clear adsorption–inhibition decoupling. EPR, probe-based assays, scavenger controls, and aerobic/anaerobic experiments indicated that bulk hydroxyl-radical- and superoxide-related processes were unlikely to be major contributors. Notably, peptide-level LC–MS/MS revealed material-dependent oxidative modifications of urease-derived peptides, with nCuO exhibiting the highest peptide oxidation level. These modifications were more likely associated with localized Cu-mediated interfacial oxidation and/or conformational exposure of oxidation-sensitive residues rather than freely diffusible solution-phase radicals. Overall, ENP-induced urease inhibition arises from dissolved metal species, interfacial perturbation, multilevel structural reorganization, and localized peptide-level oxidative modifications. These findings provide a refined framework for evaluating nanoparticle–enzyme interactions in soil environments.

Betaine-based natural deep eutectic solvents for biogas upgrading: Thermodynamic and molecular insights
abstract: Achieving efficient removal of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from biogas is crucial for energy utilization and environmental protection, yet developing absorbents that are highly efficient and eco-friendly remains challenging. Herein, several natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) were prepared by combining betaine with different hydrogen bond donors for the VOCs removal from biogas. The effects of absorption temperature, VOC feed amount, and absorbent composition on VOC capture were investigated. Betaine:levulinic acid at a 1:3 M ratio (Bet3lev) exhibited good absorption performance for VOCs in terms of partition coefficients, with 9.17-, 1.28-, and 82.35-fold enhancements compared to water for dichloromethane, methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), and toluene, respectively, and a dynamic absorption capacity of 0.77 mg/g using DCM as the model VOC. Moreover, Bet3lev demonstrated excellent thermal stability, maintaining an absorption ratio above 95.5% across five absorption-desorption cycles. Energy decomposition analysis revealed that, while electrostatic interactions were dominant in the NADES-based absorption of dichloromethane and MEK, both electrostatic and dispersion interactions were dominant driving forces for the absorption of toluene. Overall, NADES based on betaine and levulinic acid is outstanding as an absorbent for eliminating VOCs from biogas, providing a remarkable combination of high absorption capacity, good recyclability, and inherent sustainability.

A genetically engineered biomimetic nanomedicine with radio-taxis and CD47 blockade for precision tumor radio-immunotherapy
abstract: The combination of radiotherapy (RT) and immunotherapy holds great promise yet remains suboptimal in clinic due to inefficient drug accumulation and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. To address this, we developed a genetically engineered biomimetic nanomedicine (diABZI@PLGA@SIRPα-M1M) by coating STING agonist-loaded nanoparticles with membranes derived from M1 macrophages and engineered to overexpress SIRPα, the main receptor for CD47. This design leverages the inflammatory taxis of M1 macrophages, which allows the nanoparticles to be actively recruited to the RT site and achieve enhanced tumor-specific accumulation. Furthermore, the surface SIRPα protein efficiently blocks the CD47 “don't eat me” signal, potentiating phagocytosis and antigen presentation by macrophages. Utilizing the immunostimulatory effects of the released STING agonist, this nanoplatform robustly reprograms the immunosuppressive microenvironment and synergizes with radiotherapy to trigger potent systemic antitumor immunity, significantly inhibiting local and distant tumor growth in murine models. This work presents a novel radio-tactic nanomedicine that precisely target RT site and deliver immunomodulators for effective combinational tumor therapy.

Optimizing demonstration-scale electrochemical CO2 capture: Single versus dual cell systems
abstract: Electrochemical carbon capture is a potentially energy-efficient alternative to conventional solvent-based processes. However, it requires careful innovation and adjustments of operating conditions to achieve the required energy efficiency and stability. The absorber recirculation flow is a key variable and was found to be a critical lever for system performance. In this study, a demonstration-scale electrochemical capture unit was tested on industrial flue gas at a magnesia production site in Greece. Single-stack and dual-stack cell configurations were compared in terms of overall CO 2 desorption and electrochemical performance metrics. The single-stack mode initially outperformed the dual-stack setup. This was caused by insufficient absorber recirculation, which limited CO 2 loading and resulted in higher energy consumption. When the absorber recycle flow was adjusted to better match the available regeneration capacity, the dual-stack performance improved and became comparable to single-stack operation. The simple change was unexpected but can be explained by the increased rich loading which enhanced the performance of the electrochemical solvent regeneration. Overall, while the energy consumption of the process remains high, the findings highlight the absorber recirculation flow as a decisive parameter for future development of scalable electrochemical CO 2 capture. Future development may enable operation that combines high throughput with efficient and selective ion transport for low energy consumption CO 2 capture.

CNT-wired large-area porous LiMn2O4 nanoweb for ultrafast lithium extraction from real brines
abstract: Selective lithium extraction from brines using LiMn2O4 (LMO) electrodes is often constrained by sluggish Li+ diffusion, poor electronic conductivity and structural instability during cycling. Here, we report a large-area porous LMO nanoweb electrically wired with carbon nanotubes (CNT/LMO-NW) as a high-rate cathode for hybrid capacitive deionization. Constructed through aramid-nanofiber-templated crystallization and subsequent CNT assembly, the electrode forms a laterally extended porous two-dimensional nanoweb with continuously integrated LMO nanocrystallites. This architecture provides abundant ion-accessible pathways and ultrashort diffusion distances, while CNT wiring enables efficient long-range electron transport. Consequently, CNT/LMO-NW achieves a Li+ diffusion coefficient of 7.19×10-9 cm2 s-1, ~13 times that of bulk LMO. In hybrid capacitive deionization, the optimized electrode delivers a Li+ adsorption rate of 0.36 mmol g-1 min-1 and a capacity of 5.43 mmol g-1 (10 mmol L-1, 25 mA g-1), with 91.48% capacity retention over 200 cycles. The electrode maintains high Li+ selectivity in real brines, yielding a Li-enriched recovery stream with ~81% Li+ purity. Calculations further reveal that the porous CNT-wired framework accelerates ion transport and improves electronic conduction. This work establishes a framework-level ion/electron pathway engineering strategy for fast, selective, and durable lithium recovery from complex brines.

Bioinspired hierarchically structured liquid metal-composited eutectogel for energy conversion and intelligent perception
abstract: Inspired by the hierarchical structure of brain’s blood vessels and neural networks, which enables synergistic trade-offs among multiple properties, we developed a structural biomimetic strategy to create liquid metal (LM)-initiated polymerizable deep eutectic solvents (PDES) eutectogels. In this design, the polymerizable hydrogen bond donor forms polymer chains that mimic vascular walls and provide mechanical support, while the hydrogen bond acceptor enables ion transport for signal transmission, analogous to neurotransmitter-mediated communication. LM acts as a ”growth factor” to induce the formation of a biomimetic hierarchical network in PDES-based eutectogels. Specifically, LM introduces ionic coordination bonds to construct a hierarchical supramolecular network, while simultaneously serving as a conductive filler to establish an ion-electron conductive network, with interfacial modification promoting the dissociation of hydrogen bond acceptors. Consequently, the resulting eutectogels achieve a balanced combination of mechanical strength, ultrastretchability ((451.8 kPa, 1106%) ~substantially outperforming LM-free PDES eutectogels), high elasticity (energy dissipation rate <15% within 500% strain), and excellent ionic conductivity (~31.19 mS cm-1). This strategy effectively overcomes the practical application limitations of PDES eutectogels arising from their insufficient mechanical performance and low ionic conductivity. Furthermore, based on this platform, a ”dynamic-static” self-powered system enables low-grade heat and mechanical energy conversion into electricity while serving as a supercapacitor (SC) electrolyte for energy storage. Integrated with a convolutional neural network (CNN), the PDES-LM20 eutectogel enabled multi-channel gesture recognition with 99.5% accuracy for ten gestures. This work bridges structural biomimicry and functional synergy, advancing integrated gel platforms for energy conversion, storage, and intelligent perception.

Enzymatic reaction kinetics within Pickering emulsions through progress-curve analysis
abstract: Pickering emulsions are attracting increasing attention in biphasic biocatalysis because their particle-stabilized interfaces provide a large contact area between enzymes in the aqueous phase and water-insoluble substrates. Despite growing interest, a comprehensive kinetic framework for enzymatic reactions in Pickering emulsions remains lacking. Here, a progress-curve-based kinetic description of a hydrolysis reaction is presented for the first time and compared with both a single-phase system and a particle-free biphasic system. Transitioning from an aqueous single-phase system to a biphasic system the maximum reaction velocity v m a x increased threefold, while the apparent Michaelis–Menten constant increased by four orders of magnitude, indicating significant interfacial mass-transfer contributions. Notably, Michaelis–Menten kinetics derived from initial rates failed to predict product formation at elevated concentrations due to product inhibition. Direct fitting of integrated rate equations to full progress curves enabled efficient parameter estimation and captured product inhibition while substantially reducing experimental effort compared to conventional initial-rate analysis. Both competitive and non-competitive inhibition models adequately described the data. Comparison with a particle-free biphasic system revealed similar kinetics at high stirring rates; however, under reduced energy input, the Pickering emulsion retained its kinetic parameters and activity, whereas the biphasic system became mass-transfer limited. Overall, this study establishes macrokinetic parameters for Pickering emulsions using progress-curve analysis and demonstrates their advantages under low-stirring conditions, providing a basis for process development.

abstract: Photocatalytic technology paves a highly promising way for the sustainable production of H2O2. However, photocatalytic efficiency has long been constrained by the core bottlenecks of high carrier recombination rates and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. In this work, biomass-derived BC@M@ZIS (BC: biomass carbon; M: Ni, Fe, Co; ZIS: ZnIn2S4) was precisely designed and constructed via the combination of solvothermal and carbothermal reduction methods. By employing a dual strategy of band structure optimization and targeted regulation of active sites, the synergistic enhancement of directional transfer for photogenerated charges and surface reaction kinetics is achieved. The energy level difference between ZIS and BC@Ni establishes an efficient directional carrier transport pathway, which significantly promotes the separation of photogenerated charge. Meanwhile, the precise regulation of active sites enables the targeted capture of photogenerated charges and rapid catalytic conversion of reactants. In addition, the hydrophobic properties and nanoporous structure of BC@Ni substantially enhance the mass transfer of O2 during the reaction process. Ultimately, after optimization, BC@Ni@ZIS exhibits a remarkable photocatalytic H2O2 production performance of 1101 μmol g-1 h-1 under visible light irradiation, which is 3.15 times that of the monomer ZIS. The strategy proposed in this work, which synergistically enhances carrier separation efficiency and surface reaction kinetics, offers a novel insight in designing high-performance photocatalysts for H2O2 production.

abstract: The persistent degradation of Magnéli phase electrodes critically limits the electrochemical destruction of per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances. This work systematically elucidates the activity and ultimate failure mechanisms of the mixed-phase TiO x nanotube array electrodes (TiO x NTAs) for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) oxidation. Optimized TiO x NTAs achieve 99.9% PFOA degradation and 91.0 ± 1.4% defluorination under mild conditions (5.0 mA/cm 2 , 5 h). The markedly faster PFOA degradation in NaClO 4 than in Na 2 SO 4 highlights the regulation of TiO x /electrolyte interfacial chemistry by supporting electrolyte anions as a key determinant of PFOA degradation kinetics. Crucially, systematic interrogation of failure mechanisms leads to the conclusion that the ultimate operational lifespan is governed by irreversible fluoride-induced structural corrosion rather than surface fouling. Fluoride ions (F − ) liberated during PFOA mineralization aggressively etch the TiO x NTAs framework that was originally created through F − -assisted anodization, causing catastrophic structural collapse and non-recoverable activity loss after only four cycles. This work clearly defines a key design target for next-generation PFOA destruction electrodes: i.e., maintaining direct electron transfer-active sites while robustly protecting the conductive oxide matrix against F − attack.

“Tensile strain + X” multimodal sensors: Decoupling, anti-interference, and applications
abstract: Conventional flexible strain sensors can only detect mechanical deformation, which limits their ability to perceive multiple physical stimuli in complex scenarios such as health monitoring and human–robot interaction. To overcome this limitation, ”tensile strain + X” multimodal sensors that integrate strain sensing with other modalities (e.g., pressure, temperature, humidity, magnetic field, and bioelectricity) have emerged as a promising solution. This review provides a systematic overview of recent progress in these sensors, with an emphasis on decoupling strategies and anti‐interference methodologies. According to the output signal type and decoupling principle, existing devices are classified into four categories: single‐output, multi‐output, structurally/spatially separated, and algorithm‐assisted decoupling. Single‐output sensors exploit polarity, temporal, or amplitude differences for signal separation under constrained conditions. Multi‐output sensors achieve inherent crosstalk freedom via heterogeneous signals (e.g., electro‐optical, resistance‐voltage). Structural/spatial separation physically isolates sensing units through modulus modulation or modular design. Algorithm‐assisted decoupling employs frequency‐domain filtering, matrix algebra, and data‐driven models (e.g., LSTM, CNN) to reconstruct individual physical quantities from mixed signals. Key anti‐interference strategies, including intrinsically insensitive materials, encapsulation layers, and temporal/scenario separation, are also discussed. The applications of these sensors have expanded from limb motion monitoring to sports rehabilitation, simultaneous respiration‐behavior tracking, human‐machine interaction, and structural health monitoring. Finally, future directions are outlined, focusing on intrinsically decoupling materials, edge intelligence, and multimodal fusion for robotics and embodied intelligence. This review offers a comprehensive framework that guides the design of next‐generation intelligent multimodal sensors.

Biomimetic organo-specific scaffolds reveal lineage-specific adaptations of breast cancer cells in bone metastasis
abstract: Bone metastasis is a major clinical complication of breast cancer, regulated by dynamic interactions between disseminated tumor cells and the bone extracellular matrix (ECM). Experimental models that accurately replicate the biochemical, structural, and mechanical features of the bone niche remain limited. Here, we engineered three-dimensional organo-specific ECM scaffolds to investigate how bone-mimetic matrices regulate breast cancer cell behavior, phenotypic plasticity, and therapeutic response. Collagen-based scaffolds mimicking primary breast tumor ECM and collagen–hydroxyapatite (coll-HA) scaffolds reproducing bone ECM were developed. Physicochemical characterization confirmed that coll-HA scaffolds showed effective hydroxyapatite integration, trabecular-like organization, physiological porosity, and elastic properties consistent with the bone metastatic niche. Upon cellularization with breast cancer cells, the scaffolds reproduced key histological features and tumor cell morphologies observed in human bone metastasis. Using four breast cancer cell lines representative of distinct molecular subtypes and degree of bone tropism, we demonstrated that organ-specific ECMs profoundly influence cell growth dynamics and phenotypic plasticity. In the bone-mimetic niche, tumor cells exhibited reduced proliferation and adopted subtype-specific epithelial–mesenchymal states. Transcriptomic profiling revealed lineage-dependent metabolic reprogramming and modulation of bone metastasis-associated signaling. The bone-mimetic ECM also enhanced tumor cell sensitivity to bone-targeted therapies and osteoclastogenic ability, highlighting the role of tumor–ECM interactions in shaping the osteolytic microenvironment. Collectively, organo-specific ECM scaffolds provide a physiologically relevant platform to study breast cancer adaptation to the bone microenvironment, offering mechanistic insights into microenvironment-driven plasticity, metabolism and therapeutic vulnerabilities, with implications for improving treatments for bone metastatic disease.

title: Performance of micro-nanobubbles for synergistic control of ultrafiltration membrane fouling and emerging contaminants during nutrient recovery from biogas slurry
abstract: The safe and efficient concentration of biogas slurry via ultrafiltration (UF) is constrained by severe membrane fouling and the potential enrichment of emerging contaminants (ECs). This study proposes an integrated strategy incorporating micro-nanobubble (MNB) pretreatment to simultaneously mitigate fouling and enhance contaminant control. Over five consecutive fouling-cleaning cycles, MNB pretreatment increased cumulative overall water recovery from 40 to 64% while maintaining a flux recovery rate above 80%. Mechanistic analysis revealed that MNB significantly altered foulant layer composition, suppressing the deposition of inorganic salts (particularly K and Ca) despite an increased organic foulant load. The resulting more homogeneous fouling layer improved cleaning efficiency and reduced long-term refouling. In parallel, MNB slightly enhanced the removal of antibiotics from 68 to 77% and key antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), especially those ARGs for tetracyclines and lincomycin, by approximately 10%. Notably, MNB concentrate met the standard requirements of Biogas Slurry for Agricultural Use (GB/T 40750-2021), with humic acid (10.3 g/L), total nutrient content (9.1 g/L), faecal coliforms (1 × 10 3 MPN/100 mL), and heavy metals all within permissible limits, yielding a nutrient-rich liquid fertilizer with low cost and a high germination index (>70%). Overall, this work demonstrates a promising approach to improve the performance, sustainability, and utilisation potential of membrane-based nutrient recovery from biogas slurry.

Experimental validation of a dynamic 2D model for catalytic methanol steam reforming in a fixed bed reactor
abstract: The growing adoption of renewable power in the chemical processing industry shifts many processes into the dynamic operating regime. The common 1D reactor models used for process design are no longer necessarily adequate for representing transient operation. In this study, a 2D pseudo-homogeneous dynamic model of a fixed bed reactor is developed and validated using methanol steam reforming as focused case. The model is experimentally validated with combined measurements of reactor bed temperature and outlet carbon monoxide concentration in time. The study found that the 2D model matches well in values and trends with experimental data despite numerous parameter uncertainties and use of standard expressions from the literature. The largest influence on model prediction was found in external practical heating non-uniformities, such as heat losses and added heat capacity of the reactor support structure. The non-uniformities can cause up to 20% change in CO concentration at the outlet, and double the transient time in certain cases. The model is shown to capture well the reactor transient characteristics, and is regarded fit for design of reactors in the unsteady operating regime. The applicability of the model can be broadened by incorporating alternative reaction kinetics, providing a foundation for the unsteady-state design of other conversion processes.

Pharmaceutical degradation by ozone nanobubbles: degradation kinetics and matrix-dependent effects
abstract: This study investigated the degradation performance of ozone nanobubbles against five representative pharmaceuticals: ibuprofen (IBU), metronidazole (MTZ), sulfamethoxazole (SMX), naproxen (NPX), and carbamazepine (CBZ) under various operational and water matrix conditions. Results show that molecular structure governed their degradation by ozonation. SMX, NPX, CBZ, and MTZ were completely degraded at a low ozone dose (1.5 mg/L). By contrast, IBU showed greater resistance, requiring 5.5 mg/L, and was therefore selected for further investigation. Evaluation of operational and water-matrix conditions showed that increasing ozone concentration from 1.5 to 5.5 mg/L improved degradation but reduced ozone utilisation efficiency, while IBU degradation was enhanced at neutral pH within the investigated range of pH 3 to 7. Background organic matter from humic acid promoted IBU degradation at low DOC (0.5–1.5 mg/L) but inhibited the degradation at higher DOC (3.5–6 mg/L). In comparison with conventional bubbles, ozone nanobubbles exhibited a 2.8-fold higher ozone mass transfer coefficient (0.17 vs 0.06 min −1 ), maintained a higher attainable saturation concentration of dissolved ozone, and achieved a 1.4-fold greater IBU degradation rate constant at the same dissolved ozone concentration. Under a more complex matrix simulated by humic acid at 3.5 mg/L DOC, ozone nanobubbles maintained the superior IBU and colour degradation compared with conventional bubbles. Findings from this study highlight the benefits of ozone nanobubbles over traditional ozone bubbles and their prospective use in advanced water and wastewater treatment for pharmaceutical abatement.

A compressor-free dry-cathode PEM electrolyzer for efficient on-site hydrogen peroxide production from air
abstract: This study reports a self-engineered dry-cathode proton exchange membrane electrolyzer (DC-PEM-H₂O₂) for sustainable hydrogen peroxide production using a waste biomass-derived carbon catalyst. The device features an initially dry, air-exposed cathode in a membrane-based configuration. Using carbon cloth with 10% wet proofing as cathode support, 100% faradaic efficiency was achieved at 50 mA·cm −2 with an electrochemical specific energy consumption (ESEC) of 4.2 kWh·kg −1 H₂O₂, producing droplets exceeding 6 wt% H₂O₂ (>60,000 mg·L −1 ). Increasing hydrophobicity to 60% wet proofing enabled operation at 100 mA·cm −2 , reaching 45 mg·cm −2 ·h −1 with ~70% faradaic efficiency and ~8.4 kWh·kg −1 H₂O₂. This simultaneous achievement of high concentration, competitive production rate and moderate energy demand positions the reactor among the most balanced electrochemical configurations reported to date. Long-term tests demonstrated stable operation for >100 h without catalyst degradation; performance losses at high current density were reversible and associated with temporary cathode wetting. A system-level energy assessment was introduced by separating electrochemical (ESEC) and non-electrochemical (NESEC) contributions to determine total specific energy consumption (TSEC). Remarkably, ESEC accounted for only 5–14% of total energy demand, whereas auxiliary devices dominated overall consumption. These results demonstrate that reporting electrochemical energy alone substantially underestimates real process requirements and highlight the importance of holistic energy evaluation for reactor design and scale-up of electrochemical H₂O₂ production.

abstract: Controlling Cu-metal oxide interfacial sites is key to efficient methanol steam reforming (MSR). Here, we employ a continuous sequential precipitation strategy in a tubular reactor to control the addition order of Cu, Zn, and Ce precursors, thereby tuning the catalyst nanostructure and interfacial architecture. In binary Cu/ZnO catalysts, precipitating Cu first produces smaller Cu nanoparticles and more Cu-ZnOx interfacial species. Building on this Cu-first precipitation strategy, ternary Cu/ZnO/CeO2 catalysts were further constructed. Among them, the catalyst prepared with the Cu-Zn-Ce addition order exhibits the smallest Cu nanoparticles (6.6 nm), the highest H2 production rate of 102.3 mmol H2 g-1 h-1, and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 53.6 h-1 at 200 °C. In situ CO-DRIFTS and quasi in situ XPS reveal that TOF scales linearly with the fraction of Cu-ZnOx interfacial sites, establishing Cu-ZnOx as the primary active site for MSR. CeO2 acts predominantly as a structural promoter that helps maintain smaller, better-dispersed Cu nanoparticles, thereby increasing the population of accessible Cu-ZnOx interfacial sites. These findings offer a practical synthesis strategy for constructing tunable Cu-ZnOx interfacial architectures and maximizing the density of active interfacial sites in Cu-based MSR catalysts.

Self-assembling peptide hydrogels mitigate hypothermic injury during short-term storage of anchorage-dependent cell therapies
abstract: To improve the clinical translation of cell-based therapies there is a growing need for biomaterials that serve dual functions: preserving cell viability during storage and enabling direct delivery without additional processing at the point of care. Unlike cryopreservation, which requires cytotoxic cryoprotectants and complex thawing steps, hypothermic storage (1–35 °C) offers a simple and cost-effective cell preservation alternative. However, hypothermic cell injury remains a major barrier to the prolonged storage of cell therapies, limiting their clinical utility. Here, we present injectable, bioactive self-assembling peptide (Fmoc-SAP) hydrogels as a dual-function platform for hypothermic preservation and localized delivery of retinal pigment epithelial (ARPE-19) cells. Encapsulation within Fmoc-SAP hydrogels that mimic the extracellular matrix (ECM) sustained high cell viability and minimized intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) after 3-day storage at 15 °C, outperforming non-bioactive controls. Despite reduced ROS, mitochondrial membrane potential declined significantly, identifying mitochondrial dysfunction as a key driver of hypothermic injury. Importantly, the shear-thinning behavior of Fmoc-SAP hydrogels enabled minimally invasive injection and precise cell localization in in vitro delivery models. These findings establish bioactive peptide hydrogels as a promising strategy for cold-chain storage and targeted administration of anchorage-dependent cell therapies, addressing critical challenges in clinical translation.

abstract: Amine-supported materials have been extensively studied as economically viable adsorbents for CO 2 capture. Nevertheless, their water tolerance and the costs associated with support materials remain challenging. This study aims at developing water-stable amine-based CO 2 adsorbents through epoxy-crosslinking of PEI with or without incorporation of G10 silica. It was demonstrated that CO 2 adsorption capacity, water stability, and amine efficiency of crosslinked PEI can be improved by incorporating silica particles. Addition of 10 wt% G10 silica with respect to PEI during the crosslinking process at a 2.5% epoxide-to-amine molar ratio (100–G10@CPEI–2.5) led to a material with a CO 2 uptake of 3.01 mmol/g in the presence of 15% CO 2 /N 2 at 75 °C, representing a 33% increase compared to its G10-free counterpart (CPEI–2.5). Moreover, a CO 2 uptake of 4.18 mmol/g was obtained for 100–G10@CPEI–2.5 at 75 °C with 50% relative humidity. Notably, incorporation of G10 in CPEI–2.5 not only enhanced the PEI efficiency (mmol CO 2 /g PEI) but also improved its stability upon prolonged exposure to liquid water (up to 10 days), maintaining 87.5% of its initial CO 2 adsorption performance. Furthermore, cyclic CO 2 adsorption–desorption of 100–G10@CPEI–2.5 demonstrated excellent stability, retaining 96.1% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles under dry conditions, while its H 2 O/CO 2 co-adsorption capacity remained stable throughout all cycles in the presence of 15% CO 2 /N 2 with 50% RH.

Synergistic effects of temperature and geometry on hydroxyl radical production in micro- and macroscale hydrodynamic cavitation reactors
abstract: Hydrodynamic cavitation (HC) has been increasingly investigated as a process-intensification platform for advanced oxidation processes, where localized collapse events, pressure fluctuations, rapid mixing, and interfacial renewal can enhance oxidative pathways. However, the coupled effects of reactor geometry, nominal micro−/macroscale configuration, and bulk liquid temperature on the cavitation-induced oxidative activity require further clarification, particularly when true microfluidic HC reactors and macroscale benchmark reactors are compared under controlled operating conditions. This study addresses this gap by systematically evaluating the triiodide ( I 3 − ) formation in three silicon-glass microscale HC reactors and two macroscale HC reactors using the potassium iodide (KI) dosimetry. Experiments were conducted at upstream pressures of 0.69–3.10 MPa and bulk liquid temperatures of 25 °C and 45 °C. I 3 − formation was quantified via UV–Vis spectrophotometry and linked to cavitation dynamics through high-speed imaging and void fraction analysis. Among all configurations, the micro-venturi reactor had the best performance, achieving the highest derived I 3 − concentrations (peaking at 6.3 × 10 −4 g L −1 ) and cavitation yields. Raising the liquid temperature to 45 °C consistently intensified the performance across all micro-reactors, indicating that the beneficial effects of reduced viscosity and surface tension outweighed thermodynamic suppression. By contrast, the best performing macroscale design, the multi-orifice reactor, still produced around 80%, 56.5% and 8% lower derived I 3 − concentrations than the micro-venturi, micro-step and long micro-diaphragm reactors, respectively, despite operating at higher specific energy inputs. Economic analysis further confirms the superior efficiency of the micro-venturi, which has up to ~70% lower specific energy costs than the macro-reactors at the same upstream pressure. These findings provide valuable guidelines for designing temperature-optimized and geometrically refined HC reactors for enhanced oxidative environments in intensified advanced oxidation processes.

Programmable hydrogen release via cocktail assembly of magnesium hydride modules engineered by RAFT polymerization for reinfection-resistant antibacterial therapy
abstract: Hydrogen (H 2 ) antibacterial therapy has lately garnered burgeoning interest due to its unique characteristics as a non-antibiotic strategy for infection control. However, its bioefficacy remains controversial across infectious disease settings and its broad application is considerably constrained by the absence of delivery systems that enable localized and controlled H 2 release. Here, we report a programmable H 2 delivery platform by employing the modular assembly of block copolymer-grafted magnesium hydride (MgH 2 ) microparticles. Modules with distinct H 2 release kinetics were prepared by surface-initiated reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization, which enabled robust polymer grafting and precise control over copolymer composition. Strategic cocktail assembly of modules with varying release profiles generated customizable H 2 release programs tailored to specific therapeutic requirements. In acute infection and reinfection models, fast-, medium-, and slow-release assemblies showed distinct antibacterial activities. The fast-release formulation achieved the highest initial bacterial eradication rate of 99.9%, whereas the slow-release formulation effectively suppressed bacterial regrowth after reinfection. In an in vivo wound reinfection model, the slow-release formulation produced more than 90% antibacterial efficacy and significantly accelerated wound healing with a single administration, while the fast-release formulation showed limited therapeutic benefit.

abstract: The lack of amyloid (Aβ)-targetability and poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetrability of existing contrast agents cannot enable magnetic resonance (MR) imaging to visualize Aβ plaques for diagnosis and prognosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). We present herein an advanced multimodal theranostic nanoprobe that can bind Aβ aggregates, conduct NIR fluorescence imaging, perform dual-mode T 1 - and T 2 -weighted MR imaging as well as inhibit Aβ self-aggregation and exhibit neuroprotection against Aβ-induced toxicity for in vivo real-time detection and visualization of Aβ plaques for precise diagnosis of AD. The nanoprobe was designed and developed from silica-enclosed superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles that were surface-functionalized with cyanine fluorophore conjugated gadolinium(III) complex molecular dyads. This versatile nanoprobe showing excellent Aβ selectivity and targetability as well as BBB permeability, was highly effective for in vivo and ex vivo NIR fluorescence imaging of Aβ aggregates in various age groups of AD mouse model, Furthermore, the greatly enhanced longitudinal relaxivity ( r 1 = 43.68 mM −1 s −1 ) and large transverse relaxivity ( r 2 = 110.89 mM −1 s −1 ) enabled the nanoprobe for highly sensitive real time in vivo and ex vivo dual-mode T 1 - and T 2 -weighted MR imaging of Aβ aggregates in various age groups of AD mice enabling the differentiation from the normal counterparts.

Molecularly imprinted Fe-MOF with confined pores for synergistic selective enrichment and electrocatalytic degradation of estriol
abstract: Estriol (E3), a typical natural estrogen, is hardly removable by conventional treatment technologies and poses serious threats to ecosystems and human health. Herein, a molecularly imprinted iron-based metal-organic framework (Imp-Fe-MOF) with confined pore channels was successfully fabricated via an in-situ self-assembly strategy, featuring specific 3D imprinted cavities similar to E3 and integrated with native MOF channels for enhanced recognition efficiency. The Imp-Fe-MOF possesses a regular octahedral morphology, high specific surface area (216.7 m2 g-1), large pore volume (0.323 cm3 g-1), excellent E3 selectivity, and a high adsorption capacity of 68.8 mg g-1. When electropolymerization on nickel foam (Imp-Fe-MOF@NF), the electrode achieves over 95% electrocatalytic degradation of E3 within 120 min, with the Fe2+/Fe3+ redox cycle driving the generation of •OH and SO4•- radicals to realize deep mineralization of E3 into CO2 and H2O. Notably, the degradation products exhibit significantly reduced bioaccumulation and ecological risks, and the electrode maintains 81% degradation efficiency after four cycles in real wastewater. XAFS characterization demonstrated the modulation of the electronic structure and coordination environment of Fe species in the molecularly imprinted Fe-MOF, significantly enhancing its adsorption capacity and electrocatalytic degradation efficiency for estriol. This work proposes a synergistic ”selective enrichment-confined catalysis” strategy for efficient removal of endocrine-disrupting chemicals, which promotes the environmental application of MOF materials in sustainable water remediation.

Differential pressure bypass-driven triboelectric-piezoelectric hybrid gas sensor: Mechanism of steady-transient signal extraction for high-precision flow monitoring
abstract: High-precision monitoring of dynamic gas flows remains challenging for active sensors due to electromagnetic interference and flow disruption. The recent advancement of triboelectric nanogenerators offers a promising strategy to resolve the bottleneck in achieving compatible measurements of both steady-state and transient conditions in passive sensors. Herein, we propose a differential pressure bypass-driven triboelectric-piezoelectric hybrid gas sensor (TPHG) for non-invasive, self-powered gas flow sensing. An orifice plate in the main pipeline generates a stable static pressure difference, which is transferred via a bypass to a lateral chamber housing a PVDF/BN/PTFE composite membrane. This architecture effectively eliminates direct flow impingement on the sensing elements. Mechanistically, the piezoelectric nanogenerator (PENG) layer responds instantaneously to dynamic compressive strains induced by high-frequency vortex shedding (transient capture). Simultaneously, the triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) layer exhibits a threshold-triggered output governed by the average physical gap, which is modulated by the steady-state differential pressure. The BN interlayer prevents internal short-circuiting, enabling crosstalk-free signal extraction. Fluid-solid-electric simulations confirm that unsteady vortex structures act as high-frequency excitations superimposed on the steady-state pressure boundary. Experiments demonstrate that the PENG module linearly tracks transient gas flow fluctuations (10-100 L·min⁻¹, R² = 0.9671), whereas the TENG module nonlinearly encodes the steady-state operating point (50-100 L·min⁻¹). The TPHG achieves cross-modal, real-time detection of both average flow and dynamic disturbances, offering a new paradigm for EMI-free, high-precision gas flow sensing.

title: Polymer flocculation for tailings dewatering: From empirical screening to endpoint-specific design
abstract: The efficient dewatering of tailings—the largest waste stream generated by the mining industry—is crucial for water recovery, solids handling, and environmentally responsible mineral processing. Although polymer flocculants are widely used for this purpose, their performance depends on particle mineralogy and size distribution, slurry chemistry, and process hydrodynamics. This review examines how polymer structure and interfacial phenomena govern aggregation, settling, clarification, and dewatering. Emphasis is placed on the coupling between polymer molecular design and process conditions, including adsorption, bridging, patch attraction, and coagulation–flocculation interactions. Conventional polyacrylamide-based flocculants are discussed alongside recent advances in synthetic polymers and bio-based alternatives. A consistent picture emerges across these systems: no single flocculant optimizes all process objectives simultaneously. Rapid settling, low turbidity, high underflow solids, and improved filtration or consolidation often requires different—and sometimes competing—molecular features and operating conditions. Future progress will depend on moving beyond empirical screening toward endpoint-specific flocculant design, validated under realistic tailings compositions, recycled-water chemistries, and process conditions.

A predictive framework for the reproducible seed-mediated synthesis and functionalization of gold nanorods
abstract: Gold nanorods (AuNRs) are versatile plasmonic nanostructures due to their tunable geometry and optical properties. The localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) can be adjusted across visible and near-infrared spectral domains through controlled growth. Despite their broad utilization, reproducible and predictive synthesis of AuNRs via seed-mediated growth remains challenging, as minor variations in seed solution often led to large discrepancies in final nanorod physicochemical properties. In this work, we present a comprehensive experimental and predictive framework that links the actual concentration of gold nanoseeds (AuNSs) to AuNR properties and systematically dissects and quantifies critical seed synthesis parameters. By investigating the influence of NaBH 4 concentration, aging time, alkaline treatment, and precursor variability, we demonstrate that the seed optical response at 478 nm provides a robust empirical marker of active seed concentration. Across five distinct protocols, a reproducible linear relationship is observed between the longitudinal plasmon resonance (LPR) and the inverse absorbance within a well-defined growth regimen. Geometrical modeling is combined with experimentally determined nucleation and gold deposition yields, enabling kinetic insight and establishing predictive relationships among nanorod length, width, volume, and concentration in the growth solution. Analysis of the volume intercept reveals that AuNR formation proceeds through cooperative growth involving multiple nanoseeds, rather than a one-seed-one-rod mechanism. The 3D (length, width, concentration) theoretical model predicts nanorod dimensions and plasmonic response in excellent agreement with experimental data. The integration of absorbance-based kinetic descriptors and a validated 3D growth model marks a shift from empirical optimization to rational synthesis. Moreover, we demonstrate effective post-synthetic functionalization through entire ligand exchange of cytotoxic cetyltrimethylammonium bromide with a multidentate thiol-based polymer, yielding colloidally stable and biocompatible AuNRs without altering their plasmonic properties.

Sprayable androgen receptor PROTAC degrader for immunomodulation and accelerated skin regeneration
abstract: Despite extensive pharmacological efforts to apply targeted protein degradation (TPD) across diverse disease contexts, strategies enabling its convenient and practical use remain limited. To expand the therapeutic landscape of TPD, we herein design a proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) degrader with excellent compatibility in aqueous hydrogels, thereby establishing a sprayable system for dermatological conditions. This sprayable hydrogel allows user-friendly topical application and ensures prolonged skin retention of the PROTAC through robust tissue adhesion. Targeted proteolysis of the androgen receptor (AR) generates a pro-regenerative microenvironment by inducing a macrophage phenotypic shift from the proinflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 state. Consequently, topical spraying of the PROTAC-loaded hydrogel accelerates skin regeneration, highlighting its potential as a versatile therapeutic platform for both wound repair and psoriasis management. Extending beyond conventional PROTAC research, which has primarily focused on target identification and chemical optimization, this study introduces a practical design strategy for translating TPD into regenerative medicine.

Closo-type complex hydride-derived interphase for stable aqueous zinc metal batteries
abstract: Aqueous Zn metal batteries hold great promise for large–scale energy storage systems due to their inherent safety and high energy density. However, parasitic side reactions at the Zn metal anode interface, including undesirable electrolyte decomposition and the formation of byproducts, induce unstable Zn deposition, thereby accelerating performance degradation. In this study, we propose a closo –type complex hydride as an electrolyte additive that stabilizes the Zn metal anode by regulating the interfacial reactions. The closo –type complex hydride, Zn(B 12 H 12 ), dissociates into Zn 2+ and [B 12 H 12 ] 2− , and the resulting [B 12 H 12 ] 2− complex hydride anions interact only weakly with surrounding species without significantly altering the bulk electrolyte structure. Such weak coordination behavior allows [B 12 H 12 ] 2− to remain available for interfacial reactions at the Zn metal surface, contributing to the formation of a hydride−rich interphase containing reducing B H bondings. This interphase suppresses ZnO formation and parasitic reactions while promoting uniform Zn nucleation and compact Zn growth at the electrode surface, thereby enabling homogeneous Zn deposition during repeated cycling. Consequently, Zn||V 2 O 5 batteries maintain superior cycling stability over 5000 cycles at a high rate of 10 A g −1 . This study highlights the potential of complex hydrides as electrolyte additives and their broader applicability in regulating metal−electrolyte interfacial reactions for stable aqueous metal batteries.

Starvation-protected dual-nanoplatform with antibacterial and angiogenesis properties for diabetic wound remodeling
abstract: Hyperglycemic wounds face the huge challenge of overall niche disintegration and severe healing difficulties due to blocked angiogenesis and persistent biofilm infection. Although the current reactive oxygen species (ROS) technology offers an alternative to antibiotics for diabetic wound infections, it fails to provide satisfactory long-term wound healing due to non-selective attack on normal tissues and neglect of improving blood supply. In this study, a dual-nanoplatform consisting of MoS2@GOx nanoparticles (MG NPs) and Zn single-atom nanozyme@mSiO2@GOx nanoparticles (ZSG NPs) was developed to achieve the remodeling of the diabetic wound microenvironment through the simultaneous intervention of efficient antibacterial and microvascular regeneration. Under the starvation-effect protection provided by GOx, MG NPs and ZSG NPs remained friendly to normal tissues but selectively attacked pathogenic bacteria. The MG NPs with peroxidase (POD) activity and photothermal property could generate highly toxic hydroxyl radicals (·OH) in the presence of H2O2 supplied by GOx, combining the efficient chemodynamic therapy of ZSG NPs to finally achieve the cascade amplification of ·OH production and eventual disintegration of pathogenic bacteria. The low pH provided by glucose acid induced the release of Zn2+ from ZSG NPs, directly promoting angiogenesis by upregulating the HIF-1α/VEGF signaling pathway. Moreover, this dual-nanoplatform promoted the polarization of M1 macrophages into M2 macrophages. In conclusion, the MoS2/Zn-SAN dual-nanoplatform offers a promising clinical treatment paradigm for diabetic wound healing through a multi-dimensional therapeutic strategy combining pathogen clearance, promotion of angiogenesis, and immune regulation.

Engineering Schizochytrium sp. within an RVE mode for circular and cost-effective production of DHA-enriched raw milk
abstract: Synthetic biology offers new opportunities for advancing the circular economy by enhancing substrate utilization and improving target product yields. Schizochytrium sp., a major industrial microorganism for docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) production, is widely used for DHA oil and DHA-enriched raw milk production. However, in DHA-enriched raw milk production, Schizochytrium sp. powder and milk wastewater reduce overall economic performance. Here, we propose a novel production mode termed the RVE (Reusability, Value, Economy). Reusability was validated by evaluating the effectiveness of Schizochytrium sp. HX-308 as a dietary supplement for DHA-enriched raw milk production and its capacity to utilize milk wastewater. Dual-copy overexpression of endogenous β-galactosidase significantly improved lactose hydrolysis, enhancing wastewater reutilization. To improve Value, the complementary expression of Δ6 desaturase and overexpression of Δ19 desaturase enabled strain S06 to produce an additional 4.35% of the functional fatty acid C18:3 under 4% milk wastewater conditions. This reduced the ω6 DPA ratio by 16.19% and increased DHA content by 7.93%. To enhance Economy, overexpression of WRINKLED1 (WRI1) enabled strain S10 to achieve a lipid titer of 67.07 g/L under 4% milk wastewater conditions, representing a 9.71% increase relative to S06. Techno-economic analysis (TEA) revealed that the RVE mode reduced the unit production cost of DHA-enriched raw milk by 7.94% compared with the conventional mode, demonstrating its potential for circular economy.

title: High-salinity coupled bioanode-biocathode systems: Lessons from 290 days of waste-to-carboxylates operation
abstract: Coupling bioanodes and biocathodes in three-compartment bioelectrochemical systems (BES) enables waste-to-chemicals conversion with simultaneous carboxylate production and extraction, yet long-term performance under high-salinity conditions remains unexplored. Here, 290 days of continuous operation are reported for triplicate high-salinity (HS, 626 mM NaCl) and low-salinity (LS, 26.7 mM NaCl) BES fed with food waste hydrolysate at the bioanode and CO 2 at the biocathode. Microbial electrocatalysis under both conditions reached comparable performance levels, with similar anodic current densities (8.8 vs. 8.1 A·m −2 ) and maximal cathodic carboxylate productivities (1.1 vs. 1.7 g·m −2 ·d −1 ). Critically, salinity did not compromise microbial electrocatalytic activity but acted as an ecological filter, selecting distinct communities: Geoalkalibacter vs. Geobacter anodireducens at anodes, and Alkalibaculum bacchi vs. Acetobacterium at cathodes. HS conditions markedly suppressed methanogenic competition while yielding diversified products (formate + acetate), whereas LS cathodes produced predominantly acetate with up to 94.9% electron recovery. Despite an initial eight-fold lower internal resistance in HS systems (20.9 vs. 158.3 Ω), ion accumulation driven by anodic pH control progressively eroded the initial resistance advantage and limited carboxylate extraction by electromigration. Notably, these operational constraints emerged under both salinity conditions, revealing that ionic loads resulting from anodic pH management constitute a critical long-term challenge for compartmentalized BES coupling bioanodes to biocathodes, irrespective of initial electrolyte salinity.

Establish prediction rules for microcrystalline structure regulating fast slope-region sodium storage of hard carbon anodes
abstract: Regulating slope-region sodium storage is essential for high-performance hard carbon anodes, yet its microcrystalline structural origin remains unclear. Herein, a structural factor (SF) is established for pitch-based hard carbon by integrating interlayer spacing, lateral crystallite size, and carbon-layer non-planarity. Increasing SF, characterized by enlarged d₀₀₂, reduced Lₐ, and enhanced AD₂/AG, shows a strong positive correlation with slope-region capacity, increasing the 1.0–0.1 V capacity from 132 to 235 mAh g⁻¹. The optimized high-SF hard carbon features expanded interlayer spacing, short curved carbon layers, abundant defect/edge sites, and interconnected microcrystalline pathways, enabling accelerated Na⁺ adsorption, intercalation, and transport. GITT and impedance analyses reveal an approximately two-order-of-magnitude enhancement in Na⁺ diffusivity, while in situ Raman and ex situ XPS identify an adsorption-induced concentration-gradient effect that drives Na⁺ migration from defective carbon layers into interlayer domains and closed ultramicropores. Consequently, the optimized hard carbon delivers 420 mAh g⁻¹ at 30 mA g⁻¹ and 290.6 mAh g⁻¹ at 1 A g⁻¹. This work provides a physically interpretable structural descriptor for designing fast sodium-storage hard carbon anodes.

Exploiting highly humidity-resistant flexible NH3 gas sensors based on hot-stirred PEDOT: PSS coupled with dual-phase VOx nanofibers
abstract: We exploit the hybrid organic/inorganic PEDOT:PSS/VOₓ as the promising strategic design for the realization of applicable paper-based NH3-gas sensors in outdoor applications. The organic PEDOT:PSS matrix treated via the hot-stirring procedures promoted the benzoid to quinoid conformation transition of PEDOT chains and removal of excess PSS molecules, served as robust and interconnected networks with outstanding flexibility. On the other hand, dual-phase VOx nanofibers as the fillers of hybrid gas sensors facilitated to alleviate the surface-state induced capacitance interference and maintained the dynamic response stability. We visualized the organic/inorganic heterojunctions via both electrochemical and spectroscopic analyses, illustrating the essence of created PEDOT:PSS/VOx interfaces that alleviated the significant modulations of environmental humidity to the sensing stability. Moreover, the theoretical calculation further revealed the significant electron transfer (0.11e) and adsorption energy (-1.19 eV) occurred at heterointerfaces that underscored the sensing characteristics. The outperforming room-temperature detection responses were displayed, including Limit of Detection reaching 30 ppb, wide detectable range up to 50 ppm, affirmed interference selectivity against five different gases, long-term stability with trivial 1.6% degradation over 63 days and remarkable humidity resistance with the deviations < 4.1% over 13.2±2.2% to 86.2±3.7%. We further visualized the real-time monitoring of NH3 targets in outdoor application, where the multifaceted outputs including the classification of danger levels and dynamic monitoring of NH3 concentration with high statistical accuracy were exploited.

title: Synthesis of lithium titanium oxide-PAN/PVP granules with finger-like porous morphology and high stability for lithium recovery from aqueous sources
abstract: Lithium titanium oxide, LTO (Li 2 TiO 3 ), is a promising material for the fabrication of ion-exchange composite adsorbents for lithium recovery from aqueous brines. In this study, composite lithium ion sieve (LIS) granules were developed by binding LTO with polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and incorporating polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a pore-forming agent. The use of PAN as the primary binder and PVP as the pore-forming agent combines the hydrophilic characteristics of PAN and its strong interactions with LTO with the high solubility of PVP, leading to a uniform pore-size distribution and significantly improved lithium adsorption performance. The optimal pore-forming agent ratio (PVP:PAN = 0.4:0.8 g/g) facilitates the controlled diffusion of the coagulation medium into the composite slurry, thereby regulating the rates of PVP extraction and PAN gelation. This engineered composition promotes the formation of well-connected, finger-like pores that are uniformly distributed throughout the LIS granules, as confirmed by SEM and BET analyses, thereby contributing to enhanced adsorption performance. The LIS granules exhibit a porosity of 76% and an adsorption capacity of 66.92 mg/g in brine containing 1000 mg/L lithium at 60 °C. Overall, the incorporation of PVP increased the adsorption capacity by 63.3–82.9% over a range of lithium concentrations (1000–100 mg/L). The LIS granules also exhibited good adsorption selectivity toward lithium over competing ions, following the order Li + > Mg 2+ > Na + > Ca 2+ > K + . Furthermore, the LIS granules demonstrate a good reusability, maintaining their structure and adsorption performance with an average Ti loss of less than 0.2% after 30 adsorption-desorption cycles, thereby confirming their mechanical and chemical stability.

title: Experimental and model-based analysis of H2/CO2 mixotrophic lactate metabolism reveals thermodynamic constraints on carbon efficiency in Clostridium luticellarii
abstract: The sustainable bioproduction of chemicals and fuels in microbial fermentations requires strategies that improve carbon efficiency to compete with petrochemically derived chemicals. Lactate-based chain elongation has emerged as a promising platform for waste valorization; however, its conversion is often constrained by redox limitations and the requirement of acetate supplementation. Mixotrophic co-feeding of H 2 /CO 2 offers a potential strategy to overcome the limitations of lactate metabolism by providing additional reducing power for carbon fixation and energy conservation. The acetogenic bacterium C. luticellarii can grow on lactate as well as H 2 /CO 2 . However, the role of H 2 /CO 2 co-feeding in lactate metabolism in this organism remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effect of H 2 /CO 2 supplementation on lactate metabolism using a combined experimental and genome scale modeling approach. Our results show that increasing H 2 partial pressure from 80 kPa to 160 kPa enhanced growth (~0.040 to ~0.044 h −1 ) and lactate utilization rates (~4.93 to ~6.71 mmol gDW −1 h −1 ) while simultaneously reducing net CO 2 production. Moreover, H 2 /CO 2 co-feeding restored the growth under conditions without externally added acetate, although residual acetate from inoculum carryover remained present. Constraint-based modeling further indicated that Wood-Ljungdahl pathway flux is required to satisfy the observed redox and product-formation constraints under H 2 /CO 2 -fed conditions, consistent with model-predicted internal acetate requirement of ~81.7 mM comparable to the 100 mM exogenously supplied. Our work highlights the potential for H 2 /CO 2 mixotrophic coupling with lactate fermentation to simultaneously enable waste valorization and improve carbon efficiency while improving the process efficiency in acetogens.

title: Electric field-enhanced removal of Mn2+ from electrolytic manganese residue leachate by Mg/Fe layered double hydroxide
Weibull kinetics-driven gelation for enhanced gel-impregnated membranes in semi-solid-state batteries
abstract: The development of semi-solid-state batteries (SSSBs) requires gel electrolytes that simultaneously exhibit high ionic conductivity and excellent mechanical properties. We refined the gel-impregnated membrane (GIM) fabrication process by modeling gel crosslinking kinetics, enabling reproducible and scalable production of high-performance GIMs. We demonstrated that optimized crosslinking density is critical for achieving both high ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness. By correlating rheological properties, spectroscopic characteristics, conversion, and resistance of ionic conduction with gel crosslinking, we found that these properties collectively follow the Weibull kinetic model, providing a quantitative framework for predicting gel crosslinking density. This breakthrough enables systematic fabrication of gel electrolytes with controlled crosslinking. Through percolation analysis, we identified a critical monomer concentration of 4 wt% for gelation and confirmed that 5 wt% monomer content ensures Weibull kinetic behavior, leading to complete gelation in trimethylpropane ethoxylate triacrylate (ETPTA) system. The resulting GIM demonstrated no leakage, superior mechanical strength, and ionic conductivity exceeding 1 mS cm −1 , enabling stable SSSB operation. This study establishes a quantitative model for gel crosslinking, advancing the development of high-performance GIMs for next-generation solid-state batteries.

Nutrient-activated silica nanocomposites for enhancing biodegradation of polyester blends
abstract: Polyesters like polylactide (PLLA), poly(butyleneadipate- co -terephthalate) (PBAT), and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are widely adopted as biodegradable alternatives to commodity plastics, but their varied biodegradation kinetics can lead to environmental concerns: PLLA is notoriously slow, while faster-degrading polymers like PBAT and PHAs are blended with PLLA to tune properties for applications like 3D printing. These blends often remain limited by the slow degradation of the PLLA-phase under realistic end-of-life conditions. Here, we present a nanocomposite approach accelerating the biodegradation of these polymers and their blends by nutrient-loaded (YMG: yeast extract, malt extract, and glucose) silica nanoparticles (YMG–SiNPs). The YMG–SiNPs are synthesized in inverse microemulsion and encapsulate YMG during their preparation. During composting (ISO 14855-1:2012), mineralisation quantified by CO₂ evolution confirms enhanced biodegradation for neat polymers and blends including YMG. In wastewater and soil, incorporating YMG–SiNPs increased the degradation rates of all polyesters. The approach is compatible with fused deposition modeling 3D-printing. Filaments based on blends containing YMG–SiNPs can be successfully printed and faster biodegradation: printed objects of PHB-PLLA retaining only 16% of their mass after 14 days of composting, compared with 63% for the neat blend. Overall, this work demonstrates that nutrient-loaded silica nanoparticles can accelerate the end-of-life degradation of biodegradable polyester blends while remaining compatible with melt processing and fused deposition modeling (FDM) fabrication.

Fe-doping enhanced Pt-rich heterojunction nanorods for efficient direct formic acid electrooxidation catalysis
abstract: Developing platinum-based catalysts with simultaneously enhanced activity, stability, and CO tolerance for the formic acid oxidation reaction remains a significant challenge. Owing to synergistic electronic interactions between the heterojunction and dopant atoms, the PtTe 2 Fe@Pt 3 Fe HNs/C catalyst achieves exceptional mass and area activities of 8.2 A mg Pt −1 and 15.9 mA cm −2 , respectively, surpassing most current Pt- and Pd-based benchmarks and highlighting its strong competitiveness. Meanwhile, PtTe 2 Fe@Pt 3 Fe HNs/C exhibited excellent stability in chronoamperometry tests. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, in-situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy demonstrate that Fe-doping not only increases active site density and modulates the heterostructure's electronic properties but also promotes the dehydrogenation pathway while effectively suppressing CO generation and adsorption. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the dehydrogenation pathway is more favorable on its surface. The high energy barrier for CO production and the relatively weak binding of CO jointly contribute to its superior CO tolerance. Furthermore, PtTe 2 Fe@Pt 3 Fe HNs/C, serving as an anode catalyst for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, achieves a current density of 1 A cm −2 at 1.25 V and maintains stable operation for over 100 h under highly corrosive conditions. This work advances the synthesis of 1D doped Pt-based heterojunction nanomaterials, providing an important reference for the structural design and construction of high-performance noble metal nanomaterials in other electrocatalytic systems.

Impact of flue-gas impurities and pelletization in TAMOF-1
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are attractive adsorbents for post-combustion CO 2 capture from complex multicomponent streams. The practical implementation of MOF-based carbon capture devices requires understanding how flue-gas impurities and pellet shaping influence adsorption behavior. Molecular and numerical simulations are powerful tools for predicting and rationalizing adsorption and separation performance for a wide range of adsorbates. Recently, we demonstrated that TAMOF-1, a readily synthesized and water-stable MOF, delivers 1.3 mmol g −1 CO 2 at 298 K and 1 bar with a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 120 from a mixture containing 10% of CO 2 . In this work, we combine multiscale simulations and experiments to assess how flue-gas impurities and the pelletization of TAMOF-1 affect its adsorption and separation performance. Using classical and quantum calculations, we elucidate the adsorption mechanisms and kinetic behavior of several impurity species, including NO, NO 2 , O 2 , and trace SO 2 . We further examine the influence of pelletization on adsorption properties by integrating experimental measurements with numerical modeling. These insights are then used to predict breakthrough behavior and selectivities in the presence of low concentrations of NO x impurities in a pelletized bed. Finally, we validate the simulation-based predictions through fixed-bed breakthrough experiments, which confirm that pellets retain 75% of the powder capacity, enable efficient CO 2 separation, and recover > 94% of the working capacity after ten vacuum cycles.

Zinc-iodine batteries with high polyiodide adsorption and utilisation in low-cost electrochemical iron platform alleviating polyiodide shuttling
abstract: Aqueous zinc‑iodine (Zn I 2 ) batteries herald huge potential for energy storage devices because of the constitutional safety of the zinc anode and attractive energy density. However, cathode hosts with low iodide utilisation and adsorption, sluggish redox kinetics, lengthy and costly fabrication process impede their scalability and electrochemical performance. Herein, we propose a low-cost electrochemical iron-based cathode to expand the Zn I 2 battery's electrochemical performance by harnessing iron earth richness, high conductivity and redox versatility. A straightforward and scalable electrodeposition approach is demonstrated at room temperature to fabricate AC-FeOOH cathode iodine host. The assembled Zn I 2 cell for AC-FeOOH | | Zn device displayed an excellent capacity of 0.56 mAh cm −2 at 2 mA cm −2 . The outstanding performance of the AC-FeOOH based device corresponds to the integration of FeOOH on the matrix of AC, which enhances the iodide adsorption and utilisation, alleviating the polyiodide shutting effect and Zn anode corrosion. The present technique provides a cost-effective route to employ iron for Zn I 2 battery systems, making the process more economical for grid-scale energy storage applications, delivering a sustainable route for alleviating the shortcomings of Zn I 2 battery system, and paving way for their implementation in wider areas in the electrochemical energy storage devices.
