A review on lignocellulosic fillers for sustainable thermoplastics
abstract: The transition toward renewable, low-carbon footprint materials has intensified interest in lignocellulosic fillers as sustainable reinforcements for thermoplastic composites. These bio-derived fillers mainly include wood flour, agricultural residues, micro- and nanocellulose, and lignin-based particulates. They are especially appealing due to their low density, functional surface chemistry, mechanical reinforcement ability, potential biodegradability, and low environmental footprint. Their practical implementation requires an understanding of the complex interplay among filler morphology, surface chemistry, and polymer–filler interactions. Here, we critically review recent advances in the structure-property-performance relationships in thermoplastic composites reinforced with lignocellulosic fillers. Key considerations include microstructural characteristics, dispersion mechanisms, crystallization behavior, mechanical reinforcement efficiency, viscoelastic/rheological properties, and thermal stability. Special emphasis is placed on compatibilization strategies, interfacial engineering approaches, and derivatives obtained upon carbonization, such as biochar. These carbonaceous fillers improve adhesion, enhance nucleation activity, and provide superior thermo-mechanical robustness. Beyond performance, the review is enriched by updated environmental impact metrics of lignocellulosic fillers and their composite materials, highlighting their potential to advance circular and sustainable bio-based material systems. By considering multiple scales, this work outlines design principles and identifies persistent challenges that must be addressed to enable the use of lignocellulosic fillers in next-generation sustainable thermoplastic composites.

Non-equilibrium hydrate kinetics induced by swelling-deswelling dynamics in clay matrices
abstract: Natural gas hydrates (NGHs), predominantly composed of methane, represent a vast carbon reservoir and a potential energy resource, particularly in clay-rich marine sediments. However, their destabilization poses serious environmental risks, including methane release, seabed subsidence, and ecosystem disruption. While previous studies have primarily focused on NGHs in sandy sediments, the role of clays remains poorly understood. Smectite clays exhibit complex swelling behavior, including osmotic swelling that allows substantial interlayer expansion and may fundamentally alter hydrate formation pathways. Recent field observations of anomalously low large-to-small cage occupancy ratio (θ LC /θ SC ) in smectite-rich sediments further suggest a potential influence of clay mineralogy on NGHs. In this study, we investigated methane hydrate growth in clay matrices using a combination of neutron diffraction and Raman spectroscopy. We provide direct experimental evidence of hydrate formation within swelling clays, demonstrating that cyclic interlayer swelling and deswelling induce localized mass transfer limitations, which fundamentally alter hydrate growth kinetics and cage occupancy. These results reveal a distinct, non-equilibrium hydrate formation regime in swelling clays, highlighting the need for accurate prediction of CH 4 recovery yields and geological CO 2 storage capacities that account for mineral-specific transport constraints, rather than relying on idealized models.

abstract: The linear nitrogen economy, characterized by energy-intensive fertilizer production and resource-destructive wastewater treatment, has intensified the demand for sustainable ammonium management. Here, we develop a nitro-functionalized π-delocalized organic electrode, NTPZ, for highly efficient and selective NH4+ capture in a hybrid capacitive deionization system. Benefiting from its electron-deficient conjugated framework and abundant nitrogen active sites, the NTPZ electrode delivers a high NH4+ desalination capacity of 307.79 mg g–1 at 1.2 V, together with a rapid average adsorption rate of 34.21 mg g–1 min–1 and a low energy consumption of only 0.50 Wh g–1. The device retains 93% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles and, upon scale-up, rapidly reduces the NH4+ concentration in real municipal wastewater to below the stringent EU discharge limit within 10 min, while maintaining a purified water yield of 96.5–97.7%. More importantly, the captured ammonium can be directly recovered as a concentrated nutrient solution for agricultural reutilization. Life-cycle assessment further reveals a low carbon footprint of only 0.323 t CO2 eq per ton of NH4Cl treated. This work provides a practical electrochemical route for simultaneous wastewater purification and nitrogen resource recovery toward a circular nitrogen economy.

Slurry hydroprocessing of solid technical lignins and lignin-derived bio-oils with transition metal sulfide catalysts: From batch to continuous processing
abstract: The current study demonstrates an efficient strategy for slurry hydroprocessing of solid technical lignins and lignin-derived bio-oils. Semibatch hydroprocessing experiments were performed in a lab-scale 1 L reactor using three technical lignins, and bio-oils (Lignol®)derived by derivatisation from two of these lignins. Four different supported molybdenum or tungsten catalysts, as well as an unsupported molybdenum-based catalyst formed in-situ from a lipophilic molybdenum salt, were tested for the hydroprocessing of lignin bio-oils. All tested supported catalysts exhibited good hydrotreating activity with an overall deoxygenation degree over 80%. The molybdenum-based catalysts yielded fractions with slightly lower oxygen content but higher acidity and a broader boiling-point distribution than the tungsten-based alternatives. The unsupported catalyst showed superior activity with a hydrodeoxygenation degree of 90%. Conversion into bio-oils significantly increased lignin reactivity. Potential chemical differences due to lignin origin appeared secondary to factors, such as sugars or ash content. The process was scaled up to a continuous slurry hydroprocessing process with two different molybdenum-based catalysts, and over 20 kg of lignin-containing feedstock (30 wt% lignin) was processed successfully with each catalyst, achieving up to 87% oxygen removal. Characterisation of the fresh and spent catalyst revealed no indications of significant deactivation when lignin-derived bio-oils were used.

Spatially distinct biomineralization patterns across granules and biofilms enhance phosphorus recovery in hybrid anammox reactor with simultaneous nitrogen removal
abstract: Calcium (Ca)-induced biomineralization enables simultaneous nitrogen removal and phosphorus (P) recovery in anammox systems, yet P recovery remains limited at low influent P concentrations. This study investigated a hybrid anammox reactor integrating granular sludge with biofilm carriers to enhance P recovery, and revealed spatially distinct biomineralization patterns across granules and biofilms together with microbial and metabolic responses. P recovery was markedly enhanced, with 60.1% of P retained in granules and an additional 22.3% accumulated on biofilms. Micro-computed tomography visualized three-dimensional mineral distributions, showing internal mineral formation in granules and surface encrustation on biofilms. Minerals in granules were identified as hydroxyapatite (HAP) with a crystallinity of 42.7%, whereas those on biofilms were mainly carbonate-substituted HAP with a crystallinity of 10.6%. These contrasting patterns were potentially associated with nonclassical and classical nucleation pathways in granules and biofilms, respectively, and biofilms exhibited a specific P removal rate 2.1-fold higher than that of granules. Internal biomineralization in granules preserved anammox function, with specific anammox activity (SAA) increasing by 13% and metagenomic profiles indicating stable nitrogen and carbon metabolism. In contrast, surface biomineralization in biofilms was associated with a 68% decline in SAA, reduced Candidatus Kuenenia abundance and coordinated suppression of nitrogen and carbon metabolism. Overall, enhanced P recovery was underpinned by the functional complementarity of granules and biofilms, with granules maintaining metabolic stability and biofilms expanding HAP formation capacity. These findings provide guidance for designing hybrid anammox systems for efficient P recovery and nitrogen removal.

Green synthesis of defect-engineered BiOBr via Urtica dioica extract for enhanced mineralisation of mixed pharmaceutical contaminants under simulated solar irradiation
abstract: The increasing presence of pharmaceutical contaminants in aquatic environments necessitates the development of efficient and sustainable photocatalysts capable of operating under realistic multicomponent conditions. In this work, BiOBr photocatalysts were synthesised via a green hydrothermal route using Urtica dioica leaf extract as a natural structure-directing agent. Response surface methodology was employed to optimise the synthesis parameters and establish structure-property-activity relationships. Comprehensive characterisation demonstrated that the plant extract regulates crystal growth, promotes preferential exposure of {110} facets, facilitates the formation of hierarchical rose-like microspheres with enhanced mesoporosity and surface area, and induces surface oxygen vacancies that improve charge separation. Consequently, the extract-assisted BiOBr exhibited superior photocatalytic activity, achieving complete degradation of acetaminophen together with enhanced mineralisation efficiency (46%) compared with pristine BiOBr (16%). The photocatalyst also showed excellent activity toward a ternary pharmaceutical mixture containing acetaminophen, carbamazepine, and ibuprofen under simulated solar irradiation. Reactive species trapping and adsorption studies revealed contaminant-dependent degradation pathways governed by competitive adsorption and distinct contributions of photogenerated holes, electrons, superoxide radicals, and hydroxyl radicals. LC-QTOF-MS analysis enabled the tentative identification of the principal transformation products, while ecotoxicity predictions indicated that transient intermediates were further degraded toward less hazardous species. In addition, excellent recyclability, negligible bismuth leaching, and preserved structural integrity confirmed the durability of the photocatalyst. These findings demonstrate that Urtica dioica -assisted synthesis provides an effective and sustainable strategy for engineering highly active BiOBr photocatalysts for advanced water treatment.

Polymerized chlorquinaldol-integrated fibrous membrane as a dual-functional barrier for anti-adhesion therapy
abstract: Posttraumatic peritendinous adhesion, a frequent complication following tendon repair, often leads to poor functional outcomes. Current therapeutic strategies employing either physical barriers or pharmacotherapies alone are often insufficient. Here, we present a dual-functional barrier membrane that integrates a polymerized form of the drug chlorquinaldol (Poly-CQD) within an electrospun fibrous scaffold for enhanced anti-adhesion therapy. The Poly-CQD was synthesized and blended with poly(L-lactic acid) to create enzyme-responsive nanofibrous membranes. These membranes exhibited stable, lipase-sensitive drug release, enabling sustained local delivery. In vitro, the released chlorquinaldol potently suppressed fibroblast proliferation, adhesion, and spreading. In vivo evaluation in a rat Achilles tendon model demonstrated that Poly-CQD membranes significantly reduced peritendinous adhesion formation and fibrotic collagen deposition without compromising the biomechanical strength of the healed tendon. Mechanistically, transcriptomic and western blot analyses revealed that chlorquinaldol exerts its anti-fibrotic effects by inhibiting the AKT/mTOR/c-MYC signaling axis. By combining a physical barrier with localized, enzyme-triggered drug delivery, this Poly-CQD-integrated membrane offers a promising and effective multifunctional strategy for preventing posttraumatic peritendinous adhesions.

title: A simple, reproducible, and rapid droplet culture method for the formation and characterization of microbial biofilms
abstract: Biofilms pose a growing global challenge across diverse fields, particularly in healthcare. However, the development and translation of effective anti-biofilm strategies are hindered by limitations in current in vitro evaluation methods, including suboptimal reproducibility, insufficient biofilm biomass, limited compatibility with most analytical techniques, and reliance on substrates lacking relevance to applications. Here, we present the droplet culture method, a simple and versatile approach for rapid, high-throughput assessment of anti-biofilm efficacy across diverse pathogenic biofilms grown on clinically relevant materials. In our method, biofilms are cultivated within a small inoculum droplet on a defined planar surface, facilitating oxygen diffusion and biomass production while improving reproducibility compared to conventional microtiter plate methods. The planar substrate geometry enables direct analyses with various surface characterization techniques, including confocal laser scanning microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Using this method, we demonstrate a tenfold increase in tobramycin tolerance of P. aeruginosa biofilms and strong antibiofilm activity of two novel antimicrobial nanocoatings based on antimicrobial peptides and silver oxides. This platform offers a valuable tool for biofilm preparation and analysis, supporting the development and translation of next-generation anti-biofilm solutions.

Nano-plasmonic sensing for investigating and predicting fouling during seawater RO desalination
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) desalination is critically impaired by membrane fouling caused by the accumulation of organic matter, inorganic scales, and other contaminants; however, existing fouling indices often provide limited insight into interfacial fouling processes and their relation to membrane performance. Here, we explore localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) sensing as an approach for probing fouling processes during seawater RO desalination. LSPR sensors were engineered to mimic the surface chemistry of commercial polyamide RO membranes through an aromatic oligoamide coating and applied to model and real seawater systems. Fouling by organic compounds, silica-associated scaling, dissolved crude oil fractions, and real seawater before and after pretreatment was monitored in real time through shifts in the plasmonic extinction peak. LSPR detected early foulant accumulation (~5–200 ng cm −2 ) within ~20 min of exposure and exhibited strong correlations with RO fouling behavior (R Pearson up to 0.891, p < 0.001). Beyond fouling prediction, LSPR provided insight into distinct interfacial fouling processes including protein aggregation, silica-associated fouling under undersaturated conditions, organic-assisted silica deposition, and hydrocarbon adsorption. Notably, organic matter enhanced silica-associated fouling even under mildly undersaturated conditions, indicating the importance of organic–inorganic coupling during fouling initiation. Experiments with real seawater further showed that pretreatment markedly reduced interfacial foulant accumulation despite comparable bulk total organic carbon (TOC) concentrations. Altogether, these findings demonstrate the potential of nano-plasmonic sensing as a diagnostic platform for investigating interfacial fouling processes and improving fouling assessment in seawater desalination systems.

title: Microwave-mediated pore engineering of curcumin-based bio-MOF for Candida rugosa lipase immobilization: Mechanistic insights into efficient enzymatic synthesis of biodiesel
Incineration of the ultrashort-chain PFAS trifluoroacetic acid: Reactor surface impacts on the evolution of transient decomposition and recombination intermediates
abstract: While thermal destruction remains one of the most effective treatments for ultrashort-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) such as trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) at the full scale, their evolution during incineration processes remains poorly understood, particularly those promoted by material surfaces in contact with the PFAS stream. Here we resolve the intrinsic and surface-mediated mechanisms of the pyrolysis of TFA and its non-PFAS analogue difluoroacetic acid (DFA) using synchrotron vacuum-ultraviolet photoionization mass spectrometry. Both compounds decompose primarily via HF elimination followed by decarboxylation or decarbonylation. Surprisingly, alumina surfaces facilitate the elimination of HF from TFA, but promote the formation of tetrafluoroethylene and perfluorocyclopropane as products of incomplete destruction (PIDs) from a bottom-up growth of CF 2 . These findings suggest that perfluorocyclopropane may serve as a promising indicator of surface-catalyzed recombination reactions during full-scale incineration. In contrast, DFA generates hydrogen-containing intermediates that undergo rapid secondary reactions, suppressing the formation of PIDs and enhancing overall incinerability. Our findings provide benchmark mechanistic insight into ultrashort-chain PFAS decomposition and call for systematic evaluation of surface effects that promote PID formation.

Famine-end settling enables granulation without loss of PHA enrichment in integrated nutrient-decoupled PHA production
abstract: Producing Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) from organic waste using mixed microbial cultures is increasingly attractive. While the conventional three step process of acidogenic fermentation, enrichment, and accumulation is well established, integrating enrichment and accumulation in a single reactor remains insufficiently examined, particularly when sludge settleability is poor. This study evaluated settling strategies in sequencing batch reactors (SBRs) operated with nutrient decoupling and integrated enrichment and accumulation in a single process. To isolate the effect of settling-phase placement, the feast-to-famine ratio was fixed at 0.20 in all reactors. Three configurations were tested, including settling applied at the end of the feast phase, at the end of the famine phase, and at the end of both phases. All strategies induced sludge granulation and improved settleability, achieving SVI30 values of approximately 50 mL/g compared with 806 mL/g in the flocculent control. However, only settling at the end of the famine phase (R2) maintained high PHA accumulation in granular sludge, reaching 46.7 wt%, comparable to the control reactor. Lower PHA accumulation under settling at the end of the feast phase (R3) or at the end of both phases (R4) coincided with increased extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), indicating diversion of assimilated carbon from intracellular storage to matrix synthesis. Microbial community shifts were consistent with these process-level differences, with famine-end settling enriching storage-associated denitrifying genera, whereas feast-end settling promoted taxa linked to EPS production. Overall, settling at the end of the famine phase enabled granulation and improved sludge and water separation without compromising PHA accumulation.

Humic acid-enhanced electron transfer facilitates anammox nitrogen removal: coupling extracellular electron interactions, electroactive microenvironments and intracellular metabolism
abstract: Humic acids (HA) participate in electron shuttling within the anammox process as multilevel redox mediators, yet the underlying extracellular and intracellular regulatory mechanisms remain largely unresolved. In this study, anammox sequencing batch reactors were operated under HA gradients of 100, 200, and 500 mg/L. It showed that 200 mg/L HA significantly enhanced nitrogen removal performance. The nitrogen metabolism synergy between anammox bacteria and electroactive DNRA-associated bacteria was promoted through the HA-enhanced extracellular interspecies electron transfer. At the pericellular level, HA-associated functional groups modified the EPS layer to form a redox-active interface, thereby increasing the electron availability for active electron exchange between extracellular and intracellular compartments. Consequently, intracellular electroactivity was enhanced, as indicated by increased abundance of hdh and ccsA genes. TEM observations suggested accelerated glycogen consumption, potentially supplying reducing equivalents for intensified nitrogen conversion. The HA-induced multilevel electron transfer contributed to proton motive force generation for improved nitrogen conversion efficiency. These findings provide mechanistic insights and potential strategies to enhance anammox system stability and performance in wastewater where HA is commonly present.

Beneficiation-free direct lithium recovery from graphite/LFP-dominant industrial lithium-ion battery waste containing NCM and Cu/Al foils
abstract: Conventional selective lithium recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) generally relies on beneficiation or physical separation processes to obtain relatively purified black mass or cathode materials prior to leaching. In this study, a beneficiation-free and acid-emission-free strategy was developed for direct selective lithium extraction from industrial mixed LIB waste containing lithium iron phosphate (LFP), graphite, copper/aluminum foil, and minor cross-contaminated lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide (NCM) components. Unlike conventional processes requiring extensive physical separation, the proposed HCOOH–H 2 O 2 system enables selective lithium leaching while effectively suppressing impurity metal dissolution in a highly heterogeneous industrial waste matrix. To systematically optimize the leaching process, orthogonal experiment design, response surface methodology, and regression modeling were integrated to investigate the coupled effects of HCOOH concentration, H 2 O 2 concentration, and liquid-to-solid ratio (L/S) on lithium recovery and leaching selectivity. Under the optimized conditions, the lithium leaching efficiency reached 99.39 ± 0.58%, while the leaching efficiencies of Fe, Al, Co, Cu, Mn, and Ni were controlled at 0.09 ± 0.02%, 0.14 ± 0.07%, 0.50 ± 0.16%, 0.14 ± 0.03%, 0.91 ± 0.06%, and 0.74 ± 0.08%, respectively. The post-leaching solution remained near-neutral, thereby preventing the formation of acidic wastewater. In addition, the developed modeling strategy enabled the identification of a balanced operational window between high lithium recovery and impurity suppression, which would be difficult to accurately determine using conventional one-factor-at-a-time experimental optimization approach. This study demonstrates the feasibility of direct selective lithium recovery from realistic industrial mixed LIB waste without beneficiation and provides new insights into simplified and more sustainable recycling strategies for complex spent LIBs. By eliminating conventional beneficiation and physical separation operations, the proposed strategy has the potential to reduce process complexity, energy consumption, equipment requirements, and associated environmental burdens during industrial LIB recycling.

Biomimetic multistage drug delivery system for reversing chemoresistance in osteosarcoma
abstract: Abstract Osteosarcoma (OS) remains the most prevalent primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents, with chemotherapy resistance significantly limiting the efficacy of current treatments. To address the challenges of chemoresistance driven by DNA repair mechanisms and drug efflux, we developed a biomimetic cascade-targeting drug delivery system, TAT-mPDO@cRGD-M. This system combines a polydopamine (mPDA) core with strong photothermal and drug-loading capacities, enabling the co-delivery of cisplatin (CDDP) and olaparib (OLA). Surface functionalization with the nuclear localization peptide TAT and cloaking with osteosarcoma cell membranes modified with cRGD peptides allows for selective tumor recognition, nuclear targeting, and stimuli-responsive drug release. Upon near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, the platform enhances DNA damage, suppresses the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, and promotes apoptosis while inhibiting epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that TAT-mPDO@cRGD-M exhibits potent antitumor activity against cisplatin-resistant osteosarcoma, maintaining strong therapeutic efficacy under low-power NIR irradiation without causing significant damage to normal tissues. This study highlights a highly specific and biocompatible therapeutic approach that offers promising potential for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in osteosarcoma and advancing clinical treatment strategies.

title: Molten-salt-etched Mo2VC2Tz MXene for zinc-ion supercapacitors
A biomimetic integrated photothermal–photoelectrocatalytic all-weather interfacial evaporator for the stable production of safe drinking water and VOCs removal
abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation holds promise for energy-efficient and sustainable freshwater production, yet its application is hindered by volatile organic compounds (VOCs) co-evaporation and solar intermittency. Inspired by plant transpiration, a photothermal-photovoltaic synergistically driven interfacial evaporation system was proposed for all-weather freshwater production in complex water quality by integrating TiO2-x-modified carbon felt (TiO2-x/CF) photothermal-photovoltaic catalytic materials with adaptive voltage regulation. The system achieved a stabilized freshwater output of 2.25 L/(person·d) across the full range of solar irradiance (0–1 kW/m2) through dynamic voltage regulation (0–0.93 V for 6 h over a 1 m2 evaporation area). This stable water yield is driven by the excellent photothermal and electrothermal efficiencies of TiO2-x/CF. Its superior catalytic activity further arises from an extensive surface area and defect-engineered Ti3+ and oxygen vacancies, effectively narrowing its band gap from 3.2 eV to 2.8 eV. Consequently, for source water contaminated with 5 or 100 μg/L phenol, biases of 0–0.4 V and 0–4.5 V were applied, respectively, to ensure that the resulting condensate water met the volatile phenol standard (< 2 μg/L). Furthermore, outdoor testing using Baiyangdian Lake water (0.71 kW/m2 for sunlight evaporation) demonstrated a 35.5% enhancement in cumulative water production (6.2 vs. 4.02 kg/m2 (sunlight)) under a 5 V bias over 7 h. Notably, TDS was reduced by orders of magnitude, and TOC decreased to 1.95 and 1.68 mg/L, comfortably satisfying US EPA drinking water standard. Ultimately, this study provides a robust paradigm for all-weather interfacial evaporation, facilitating the large-scale deployment of solar-driven purification technologies.

title: Ultraconductive carbon film/fiberboard heterostructure integrating superior EMI shielding and efficient joule heating
Rational design of noble-metal-free dual-metal catalysts for selective electrocatalytic oxidation of alcohols
Photocatalytic impacts of BaTiO3 on Mn redox cycling in complex aquatic environments
abstract: Barium Titanate, BaTiO 3 (BTO), is increasingly explored as a polarization-assisted photocatalyst for water treatment due to its reactive oxygen species (ROS)-generation capacity. Because these ROS interact strongly with redox-active metals, it is important to evaluate the influence of BTO on the cycling of redox-active elements, such as manganese (Mn), in aqueous environments. Many engineered and natural waters where BTO may be applied contain high salinity and elevated sulfate concentrations. This study investigated how high-salinity and sulfate-rich water chemistries alter BTO's interfacial properties and, in turn, Mn redox chemistry. Under simulated sunlight irradiation (1.78 ± 0.71 kW/m 2 ) in 0.5 M NaCl at pH 8.5, BTO produced superoxide and hydroxyl radicals that promote substantial MnO 2 formation. Interestingly, 28 mM sulfate increased Mn oxidation by 1.4-fold (65.7 ± 4.0 μM MnO 2 -equivalent with 4 g/L BTO at 6 h). Sulfate-driven BaSO 4 formation and oxygen-defect-associated Ti 3+ generation restructured the BTO surface, potentially facilitating charge separation and enhancing ROS-mediated Mn oxidation. This sulfate-induced restructuring was associated with increased dielectric response and enhanced photocatalytic dye degradation, effects not reproduced by MnO 2 deposition alone. These findings show that naturally abundant sulfate can actively restructure BTO surfaces, altering defect-associated redox reactivity and Mn cycling in saline waters, while highlighting the importance of long-term material stability and performance for practical applications in sulfate-rich wastewater or natural aquatic systems.

Monoamine structure and its effect on fully reacted substructures to synergistically toughen epoxy amine networks via topological control
abstract: A systematic investigation of oligomeric epoxy monoamine substructures as reactive tougheners of epoxy amine networks highlighting the control of topology and dangling chains is presented here. Fully reacted substructures (mFRS) are synthesised from off-stoichiometric molar ratios of a flexible trifunctional epoxy precursor and alkyl monoamines of varying chain lengths and aniline. Detailed characterisation of the mFRS structure using near infra-red spectroscopy (NIR), size exclusion chromatography (SEC), rheology and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) is also presented. Their incorporation into bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (DGEBA) and epoxy diethyl toluene diamine (DETDA) networks produce simultaneous improvement in fracture toughness, strain to failure, strength and to some degree modulus, despite a reduction in glass transition temperature (T g). The octylamine (OCT) mFRS is the most effective modifier among the series of monoamines while aniline (An) also displays excellent topological toughening. These results highlight the role of topological control as an additional route to toughening epoxy networks where the focus is upon controlling the polymer network structure rather than the microstructure.

title: Tunable polyphosphonate–acrylate networks for reprocessable flame-retardant thermosets via dynamic PC bond exchange
abstract: Thermosetting polymers are widely used in high-performance applications but suffer from inherent limitations in fire safety and recyclability due to their permanently crosslinked structures. Herein, we report a tunable polyphosphonate–acrylate network platform that integrates intrinsic flame retardancy with reprocessability enabled by dynamic P C bond exchange. The networks are formed via base-catalyzed phospha– Michael addition between multifunctional acrylates and polyphosphonates, yielding crosslinked structures with controllable phosphorus content and architecture. Spectroscopic analysis and model compound studies reveal that the resulting P C linkages, traditionally considered inert, undergo thermally activated dissociative exchange via a retro-phospha– Michael mechanism, operating in conjunction with associative transesterification. This dual dynamic behavior enables efficient stress relaxation and network rearrangement under moderate conditions without compromising thermal stability. The materials exhibit high thermal resistance (T 5% > 320 °C in air) and significantly reduced heat release, with peak heat release rates decreasing by more than 50% at elevated phosphorus loadings. The dynamic nature of the network allows for multiple reprocessing cycles and facilitates solvent-assisted recovery of carbon fibers from composite laminates. Furthermore, leachate analysis indicates composition-dependent toxicity, highlighting the role of network design in mitigating environmental impact. This work establishes dynamic P C covalent exchange as a versatile tool for designing recyclable, flame-retardant thermosets and composites with tunable performance.

Multi-functional porous nanochitin films for PFAS removal and supercapacitor applications
abstract: Chitin nanocrystals (ChNCs), and their deacetylated form, chitosan nanocrystals (ChsNCs), have shown promise in both water remediation and energy storage applications. Owing to their positive surface charge, chitin and chitosan aerogels and cryogels are effective adsorbent materials for per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). However, disposal or destruction of PFAS-impregnated adsorbent materials is a persistent concern in the field. As a result, in this article a hybrid strategy is employed to allow for upcycling of PFAS-impregnated ChNC-based adsorbent materials, converting them to activated carbon for use as supercapacitor electrodes. Porous ChNC films are fabricated using a sequential film casting-swelling-supercritical drying process to preserve the chiral nematic organization of ChNCs. Adsorptive performance is optimized first using perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) at higher concentrations. Then, competitive adsorption of PFOA, perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS), hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), and perfluorobutane sulfonic acid (PFBS) at lower concentrations is explored through liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Finally, the subsequent activation of PFAS-impregnated films is shown, and their performance as symmetric supercapacitor electrodes is demonstrated. This study describes a possible route to improved circularity of PFAS adsorbent materials through upcycling for energy storage applications.

A bimodal stem cell therapy for diabetic wound healing via sensory neuropeptide-mediated neuro-immune reactivation and CXCL12/CXCR4-dependent stem cell recruitment
abstract: Diabetic wounds present a significant clinical challenge due to neuropathy, persistent inflammation, and impaired angiogenesis. The loss of sensory neuropeptide substance P disrupts the neuro-immune regenerative axis, contributing to impaired wound healing. Here we report a bimodal stem cell therapy that synergistically integrates exogenous and endogenous stem cells by reactivating substance P-mediated neuro-immune signaling. An injectable hydrogel is co-loaded with iPSC-derived endothelial cells (iPSC-ECs) and stem cell membrane-coated substance P. The stem cell membrane coating functions as a biomimetic depot, enabling the sustained release of substance P to closely emulate its physiological signaling dynamics. The released substance P acts as a key pleiotropic signal, exerting dual functions: it initiates early M2 macrophage polarization via neuro-immune activation, while simultaneously upregulating the CXCL12/CXCR4 axis to recruit host mesenchymal stem cells. In turn, the recruited stem cells bolster immunomodulation and establish a pro-angiogenic niche that enhances both the survival and angiogenic activity of the transplanted iPSC-ECs. Meanwhile, the hydrogel scaffold protects both cell populations from the high-glucose, oxidative microenvironment. Consequently, by reactivating the substance P-driven neuro-immune axis, this bimodal strategy synergistically coordinates exogenous and endogenous stem cell functions, offering a potent and translatable approach for diabetic wound healing.

Scalable printed Janus textiles for sustained wearable hygroelectric energy harvesting driven by human-environment vapor exchange
abstract: Harvesting energy from ubiquitous ambient moisture offers a sustainable pathway for autonomous wearable electronics. However, conventional moisture-enabled electric generators (MEGs) suffer from rapid gradient decay due to liquid saturation and exhibit poor geometric adaptability to the natural skin-environment humidity gradient. Here, we report a cactus-inspired, textile-based MEG (TMEG) featuring a scalable screen-printed Janus architecture. This bioinspired design spatially decouples moisture absorption and evaporation, entirely preventing liquid saturation and establishing a persistent trans-tissue thermodynamic non-equilibrium state. Fundamentally, we elucidate that this macroscopic gradient is synergistically amplified by a microscopic competitive ion-occupation mechanism, wherein Li+ dynamically releases mobile protons from immobilized sulfonate sites. Coupled with interfacial electrochemical driving forces from an asymmetric Cu-Al electrode configuration, a single TMEG unit delivers an exceptional open-circuit voltage of 0.87 V, a short-circuit current of 160 μA, and a peak areal power density of 15.6 μW cm⁻2, alongside remarkable 15-day operational stability. Furthermore, the automated printing protocol enables industrial-scale integration in series and parallel arrays. Operating exclusively on natural human transepidermal water loss, these flexible fabrics seamlessly power commercial wearable electronics, establishing a robust, biomimetic paradigm for scalable hydrovoltaic systems.

Targeting extracellular DNA for broad-spectrum biofilm eradication and efficient microbiologically influenced corrosion mitigation
abstract: Biofilm formation and microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) are persistent challenges in water-related and industrial system, leading to equipment degradation and increased operational costs. Herein, we scanned a series of plant-derived polyphenols and identified tea polyphenol-copper complexes (TP-Cu2+) as an effective system for targeting extracellular DNA (eDNA) within biofilms. The TP-Cu2+ system induces eDNA degradation, thereby inhibiting biofilm formation and eradicating pre-established mature biofilms formed by Gram-negative Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus mutans. Electrochemical analyses further revealed that TP-Cu2+ effectively mitigates the MIC of 304L stainless steel caused by these bacterial strains. Building on these findings, the strategy was further extended to Cu-bearing 304 stainless steel (304Cu SS), where in situ-released Cu2+ cooperates with TP to form TP-Cu2+ complexes directly at the metal interface, enabling sustained antibiofilm activity against S. aureus. This self-sustaining interfacial mechanism highlights the potential of Cu-bearing alloys, when combined with TP, for long-term biofilm control and MIC mitigation. Overall, this work offers an economical, broad-spectrum, and environmentally benign strategy for integrated biofilm and corrosion control by targeting biofilm eDNA, offering a durable solution for the protection of metallic materials in water treatment, industrial, and biomedical applications.

Toward environmentally stable magnesium metal anodes via Bi interphase engineering for rechargeable magnesium batteries
abstract: A core challenge for the practical application of Mg anodes is their extreme environmental sensitivity. This sensitivity leads to the spontaneous formation of a passivation layer, which in turn causes rapid cycling failure. In this work, an artificial interface was fabricated to combine enhanced resistance to water/oxygen environment durability for regulating Mg2+ interfacial kinetics. The obtained functional metallic bismuth (Bi) interface on Mg (Bi@Mg) anode suppresses passivation via intrinsic stability, while its strong magnesium affinity with cycling-generated intermediate Mg3Bi2 phases enhances Mg2+ transport, synergistically enabling uniform Mg deposition. The designed Bi@Mg anode maintains stable cycling for 1000 h with a low overpotential at 1 mA cm-2 and 1 mAh cm-2, even after 12 h of water immersion or air exposure. The full cell paired with an Mo6S8 cathode demonstrates a high-capacity retention of 76.8 % after 3000 cycles at a 5 C. The application of a Bi metal interfacial layer with synergistic stability and magnesophilicity provides a feasible strategy for developing highly environment-stable anodes.

title: Biochar alters the active sulfamethoxazole degraders and degradation pathways in paddy soils as revealed by stable-isotope-probing and Raman-activated-cell-sorting
abstract: Sulfamethoxazole (SMX) is an emerging contaminant and its degradation mechanisms in paddy soils are important for risk control. This study combined DNA stable-isotope-probing (DNA-SIP) and Raman-Activated Cell Sorting (RACS) to explore the active SMX degraders and degradation pathways in paddy soils driven by seawater rice straw biochar amendment. Biochar significantly accelerated SMX degradation rate with the highest degradation efficiency of 96.38% achieved in the presence of 2% biochar. Both DNA-SIP and RACS consistently identified the active SMX degraders (e.g., Pseudonocardiaceae, Geodermatophilaceae, Mycobacteriaceae, Micromonosporaceae, Myxococcaceae, Anaeromyxobacteraceae, Oxalobacteraceae, and Thermomonosporaceae), while the degradation pathway was reconstructed based on DNA-SIP-derived metagenomic data and metabolites. Biochar changed the composition of the active SMX degraders by enriching Burkholderiaceae, Caulobacteraceae, Geodermatophilaceae, Mycobacteriaceae, Nocardiaceae, Oxalobacteraceae, Longimicrobiaceae, Planococcaceae, as well as some key degradation genes (sadA, sadC, chqB, E1.3.1.32, pcaJ, pcaI, pcaF and fadA), shifting the pathway from ”benzene hydroxylation → sulfonamide cleavage” to ”direct sulfonamide cleavage → desulfonation → ring opening and mineralization”. RACS captured a broader diversity and higher abundance of active microorganisms at the single-cell level, whereas DNA-SIP preferentially enriched core functional degraders harboring degradation genes, highlighting their complementary roles in resolving microbial identity–function relationships. Overall, this study reveals that biochar enhances SMX biodegradation by shaping microbial communities, functional genes, and metabolic pathways, providing molecular mechanisms of biochar-mediated remediation in paddy soils.

Vanadium passivated TiO₂ nanoplate for selective molybdenum recovery from spent HDS catalysts
abstract: Selective recovery of molybdenum (Mo) from spent hydrodesulfurization (HDS) catalysts is hindered by chemically similar vanadium (V) oxoanions in strongly acidic leachates. We report an adsorption strategy that couples crystallographic facet engineering with dynamic surface passivation to achieve high Mo selectivity under harsh conditions. Acid-stable TiO₂ was employed as a suitable platform, and its adsorption energetics were enhanced by increasing the exposure of high-energy {001} facets, enhancing Mo adsorption independent of surface area. However, intrinsic Mo/V selectivity remained limited due to similar adsorption behavior. To overcome this, vanadium was introduced as a surface modifier, forming anchored VOₓ species that block V-reactive sites while preserving reversible Mo adsorption. Repeated adsorption–desorption cycles induced progressive surface reconstruction and self-limiting passivation, suppressing V uptake while maintaining Mo capacity. Consequently, Mo/V selectivity increased from approximately 2–4 to >160 after second cycle. The system showed rapid kinetics, stability in 1.0 M H₂SO₄, and efficient regeneration, enabling >95% Mo recovery with 99.6% purity. Moreover, validation with industrial spent HDS catalysts confirmed its practical applicability. This work demonstrates a separation principle that repurposes an interfering species as a functional modifier, dynamically amplifying selectivity beyond electrostatic limits for scalable metal recovery from acidic streams.

title: Molten salt-derived Co-intercalated TiS2/MXene heterostructure for boosting alkaline overall water splitting
abstract: Two-dimensional MXenes have emerged as versatile platforms for electrocatalysis due to their tunable surface chemistry and layered structures. However, the intrinsic activity of MXenes is limited by their vulnerability in oxidizing and alkaline environments. Herein, we report a one-step molten-salt topochemical transformation that simultaneously tailors MXene surface terminations and constructs an in situ Co-TiS 2 /MXene heterointerface. This method effectively disperses hexagonal Co-TiS 2 nanoparticles, increases the exposure of active sites, and prevents the oxidation and aggregation of Ti 3 C 2 T x , significantly enhancing the overall water splitting performance. The incorporation of S promotes the transformation of the Ti 3 C 2 T x to the Co-TiS 2 derivative, modulates the electronic structure, and is predicted by DFT calculation to provide more favorable adsorption energies of reaction intermediates. Combined experimental characterization, including X-ray absorption spectroscopy, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, and in situ synchrotron-based Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, reveals that the MXene-derived Co-TiS 2 stabilizes the Co atoms, facilitating both hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions. Consequently, the Co-TiS 2 /Ti 3 C 2 T x (T x = S, Cl, O) catalyst exhibits enhanced bifunctional activity in 1 M KOH, with lower overpotentials and excellent stability than pristine Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene. This study highlights the potential of surface-engineered MXenes and their derivatives for the rational design of highly efficient electrocatalysts and provides insight into the role of surface terminations in tuning structure and catalytic performance.

Citrate-mediated structure and enthalpy-entropy trade-off in Ni-CeO2 catalysts for low-temperature CO2 methanation
abstract: Catalytic activity in heterogeneous reactions is often interpreted in terms of activation enthalpy, although reaction rates are governed by the activation free energy, which includes both enthalpic (Δ H ‡ ) and entropic (Δ S ‡ ) contributions. This simplification is particularly limiting in CO 2 methanation under non-stoichiometric conditions, where performance is highly sensitive to hydrogen availability. Here, we investigate how the Δ H ‡ -Δ S ‡ balance determines the apparent activation free energy governing catalytic performance in Ni-CeO 2 catalysts. A series of catalysts was synthesized by varying the citrate-to-metal ratio as a single preparation parameter, enabling modification of metal-support interactions, defect density, and interfacial structure. Kinetic analysis based on transition state theory reveals a trade-off between the apparent activation enthalpy and entropy across the catalyst series. The most active catalyst (NiCeO 2 –1.37Cit) exhibits the highest activation enthalpy (100 kJ·mol −1 ) but a more favorable activation entropy, resulting in a lower apparent activation free energy and enhanced activity at low-temperature. This behavior is maintained under varying H 2 /CO 2 feed ratios. Under lean conditions (H 2 /CO 2 = 1:1) and 275 °C, NiCeO 2 –1.37Cit achieves 95% CH 4 selectivity, corresponding to a methane yield of 7.5%, compared to 3.5 and 4.3% for the compared catalysts under identical conditions. Structural characterization correlates this performance with increased Ce 3+ concentration, enhanced reducibility, lattice distortion, and a more developed Ni-CeO 2 interface, consistent with a catalytic surface associated with a more favorable entropic contribution to activation. The enthalpy-entropy balance provides a framework to rationalize the relationship between catalyst structure, kinetic response, and catalytic performance, offering insight into catalyst design through control of the enthalpy-entropy balance.

Synergistic alkaline etching and nitrogen lattice occupation strategy enables gradient defluorinated cathode for high-performance Li/CFx batteries
abstract: A higher F/C ratio leads to poor conductivity of the fluorinated carbon (CFx) material, resulting in slow kinetics of the lithium-fluorine reaction and thus hindering its application in special fields such as high-power energy storage. By designing and constructing a new type of CFx structure, it is of great significance for improving the rate performance of Li/CFx batteries. Herein, a synergistic strategy of alkaline etching and nitrogen lattice occupation is proposed to construct a CFx material (F‐RG‐US/M) with a gentle gradient defluorination. NaOH achieves gradient defluorination, forming a gentle step-like gradient structure in the material. This structure provides abundant Li+ diffusion pathways while maintaining a reasonable F/C ratio to ensure specific capacity. Urea alters the distribution of electron clouds through nitrogen doping, enhances conductivity, and reduces the C-F bond energy. MWCNTs form an elastic conductive network, which further accelerates the transmission of electrons and ions. Consequently, F‐RG‐US/M exhibits outstanding electrochemical performance, delivering a specific capacity of 765 mA h g-1 with 87.8% capacity retention at a high rate of 20 C. This work not only enables a green, closed‐loop recycling route for spent graphite but also provides a viable pathway for the industrial deployment of high‐power CFx cathodes.

title: Kinetic modeling of sorption-enhanced methane steam reforming in a PdAg membrane reactor for sustainable H2 production
Study of a silicon carbide catalytic heat-exchanger reactor for titanium-catalyzed epoxidation of alkenes: Experimental and modeling insights
abstract: This work investigates a milli-structured silicon carbide heat-exchanger (HEX) reactor for the epoxidation of cyclohexene over heterogeneous titanium-based catalysts. The channels in this reactor allow for the arrangement of catalyst particles as milli-fixed bed reactors in series. Experimental investigations were combined with residence time distribution analysis, kinetic modeling, and multiphysics simulations to evaluate the performance of the continuous-flow system for two different catalyst supports: silica and silicon carbide extrudates. Batch-derived kinetic data for the Ti-SiO 2 catalyst were successfully transposed to the continuous system by equating the catalyst-liquid contact times. The milli-fixed bed HEX reactor was then used to evaluate the reaction kinetics of the Ti-SiC catalyst. For both catalysts, epoxidation proceeded according to the Eley-Rideal mechanism with inhibition, but with different activation energies due to internal diffusion limitations. The thermal effects inside the reactor were further analyzed using pseudo-homogeneous 1D and 2D axisymmetric models, and an original 1D-3D hybrid approach including temperature gradients within the solid structure of the reactor. Simulations showed how the SiC structure efficiently removed heat from the system. Moreover, the use of SiC as catalyst carrier not only reduced internal diffusion limitations, but also helped maintain near-isothermal conditions inside the milli-fixed bed for severe conditions, including solvent-free operation. The results highlight how combining milli-structuration with a high thermal conductivity material, such as SiC for both reactor construction and catalyst support, enables safe and efficient operation, even for highly exothermic catalytic reactions.

title: A methyl-β-D-galactopyranoside breath probe for early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma
NIR-II photoacoustic/Raman multimodal imaging for early detection of arteriovenous fistula fibrosis
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis. However, excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition leading to progressive fibrosis causes AVF dysfunction. Effective methods for accurate visualization and semi-quantitation evaluation of fibrosis progression, particularly at early stages, are still lacking. Herein, we developed a CREKA (Cys-Arg-Glu-Lys-Ala) peptide-functionalized near-infrared-II (NIR-II) photoacoustic (PA)/Raman multimodal probe, PBBT@CREKA nanoparticles (NPs), targeting fibrin–fibronectin complexes overexpressed in the AVF fibrotic microenvironment. By integrating the deep tissue penetration and minimal imaging artifacts of NIR-II PA imaging with the high spatial resolution and strong background resistance of Raman imaging, this platform enables complementary and precise assessment of AVF fibrosis. In the Sprague-Dawley rat AVF models, PBBT@CREKA NPs achieved non-invasive NIR-II PA imaging detection of early fibrosis at depths of 4–10 mm. Simultaneously, Raman imaging provided high-resolution delineation of fibrotic boundaries and detection of microfibrotic foci as small as 0.38 mm × 0.6 mm). Notably, PA/Raman multimodal imaging identified fibrotic lesions prior to morphological changes detected by conventional ultrasound and further revealed that chronic kidney disease aggravates AVF-associated vascular fibrosis, enabling dynamic monitoring of early disease progression. Therefore, this multimodal imaging strategy offers a potential approach for early diagnosis and progression evaluation of fibrosis-driven AVF dysfunction.

Photothermal-promoted formic acid dehydrogenation over PdCu nanoalloys enabled by alloy-induced electronic modulation
abstract: In this study, PdCu alloy nanoparticles supported on CeO2 nanofibers were synthesized and applied to visible-light-enhanced formic acid dehydrogenation via photothermal promotion. The PdCu/CeO2 catalyst exhibits a high turnover frequency of 3909 h⁻¹. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal pronounced Pd→Cu electron transfer and strengthened metal–support interactions, demonstrating alloy-induced electronic modulation in PdCu/CeO2. Mechanistic investigations indicate that visible-light irradiation enhances the reaction primarily through photothermal promotion, in which light absorption by the PdCu alloy generates localized heating that accelerates the thermally activated dehydrogenation process. Meanwhile, alloy-induced electronic modulation optimizes the electronic structure of active sites and regulates H* adsorption and recombination. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining alloy engineering and photothermal promotion for efficient hydrogen production from formic acid.

title: Magnetically recoverable Prussian blue−Fe3O4−resorcinol-formaldehyde spheres for cesium ion adsorption from aqueous solution: in situ synthesis and enhanced uptake performance
abstract: Efficient removal of radioactive cesium from wastewater, generated during the remediation of contaminated soils, requires adsorbents that exhibit high uptake capacity, fast uptake rate and efficient post-treatment recovery. Prussian blue (PB) is one of the most effective sorbents for Cs + , but its practical utilization is limited by the difficulty in the recovery of fine PB particles from the aqueous phase after adsorption has been completed. In this paper, we report a magnetically recoverable adsorbent, with PB and Fe 3 O 4 dispersed within resorcinol–formaldehyde (RF) matrix. Physicochemical characterization confirmed the mechanical and structural integrity of this novel adsorbent, and most importantly it exhibits high Cs + adsorption capacity and high uptake rate. When the adsorptive capacity is scaled against the PB content, it was one order of magnitude higher than that of PB powder. This enhancement is attributed to the highly dispersed PB nanoparticles within the confined nanopores of the RF matrix. Furthermore, the adsorbents are readily retrieved by a magnetic field, thereby overcoming the limitations of recovery encountered with PB powders. These findings demonstrate that PB–Fe 3 O 4 –RF is a practical, high-performance adsorbent for the treatment of Cs-contaminated wastewater and provide a rational design strategy for magnetically separable radionuclide sorbents.

title: Sericin-regulated biomimetic spinning and assembly of regenerated silk fibers for ionic sensing and programmable optical information encryption
abstract: In native silkworm silk glands, sericin actively regulates the assembly and solidification of silk proteins during fiber formation. However, conventional regenerated silk fibroin (RSF) fibers are typically produced after complete degumming, which disrupts the intrinsic multicomponent regulation mechanism of natural silk spinning. Here, we systematically investigate the effect of different degumming rate (0%, 10.7%, 20.7%, and 30%) on the structure and properties of regenerated silk fibers. Sericin-regulated spinning dopes suppress the formation of dense fibroin skin layers during dry spinning, forming instead a loose sericin-rich shell that accelerates solvent diffusion and reduces solidification time from ~50 min to ~4 min. Meanwhile, sericin decreases the effective solvent concentration acting on fibroin domains, facilitating β-sheet formation during spinning. The resulting fibers exhibit enhanced mechanical properties, high ionic conductivity, and stable strain-sensing capability. Notably, sericin-regulated regenerated silk fibers (SRSFs)-0% achieve an ionic conductivity of 3.9 ± 0.9 S m⁻¹ while maintaining excellent elastic recovery and cyclic stability. After high-humidity stretching, the fibers display strong birefringence and anisotropic optical properties. Based on the Maltese-cross extinction phenomenon, programmable binary optical encryption and grayscale-readable information storage are further demonstrated. This work provides a biomimetic strategy for multifunctional regenerated silk fibers and offers a promising strategy for multifunctional information-security textiles.

Temperature-conditioned molecular representation for organic solubility prediction
abstract: Solubility prediction across temperature is crucial for solvent selection and process design, yet remains challenging for data-driven models because temperature is typically treated as a simple scalar input. Such treatment limits the ability of data-driven methods to represent temperature-dependent solute–solvent interactions within their latent feature spaces. Here, we introduce a temperature-conditioned (T-conditioned) molecular representation that embeds temperature directly into learned features through feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) after dimension expansion. We evaluate this approach using two representative solubility prediction architectures: Chemprop, based on learned graph-based representations, and Fastprop, based on fixed descriptors. Trained on BigSolDB and assessed under both interpolation and extrapolation to unseen solutes using the Leeds and SolProp datasets, Tconditioning consistently reduces prediction error by up to 38% for Chemprop, with particularly strong improvements at elevated temperatures (up to 51% RMSE reduction above 330 K), while gains for Fastprop remain modest. Analysis of the T-conditioning parameters reveals that temperature-dependent modulation increases with temperature, indicating that the T-conditioning layer captures temperature-sensitive latent features relevant to solubility. An application study on pyrazinamide solubility prediction further demonstrates improved agreement with experimental trends and highlights the utility of representation-level conditioning when mechanistic models are constrained by parameters. These results demonstrate that T-conditioning enables accurate and physically meaningful prediction of temperature-dependent properties by embedding temperature directly into molecular representations.

title: Water-mediated stabilization of oxyl radicals as a driving force for the oxygen evolution reaction
Multiply modulations of double-sided comb-like Ni@NiWO4@WO3@C composites enabling exceptional electromagnetic protective and thermal management properties
abstract: The booming evolution of advanced electronic systems urgently requires multifunctional materials integrating superior electromagnetic protection and heat regulation functions, yet the inherent functional incompatibility severely hinders their synergistic optimization and scalable practical application. Herein, a distinctive comb-like Ni@NiWO4@WO3@C composite is rationally synthesized by multiple synergistic modulation of composition, defects, and heterointerfaces, which can effectively break the above performance trade-off. Owing to complementary magnetic-dielectric dual-loss mechanism, multiple heterointerfaces and well-designed hierarchical configuration, the optimized composites attain excellent EMW absorption performance with a large effective absorption-band/thickness ratio (3.90 GHz/mm), strong absorption (-47.92 dB), remarkable radar cross section (RCS) reduction (32.61 dB). Moreover, its thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) film exhibits a large thermal conductivity (3.73 W/(m·K)), which is 32.7% higher than that of pure WO3 counterpart. Such enhancement stems from well-matched phonon transport, minimized lattice defects and electron-phonon co-transfer. Besides, the as-prepared TPU composite film also possesses superior waterproof and mechanical properties, including large water contact angle (104.249°), excellent flexibility (elastic deformation = 643.52%) and high tensile strength (17.85 MPa). This work proposes a feasible multi-synergistic modulation strategy for constructing advanced multifunctional composites targeting next-generation heat regulation and electronic packaging systems.

Unravelling the kinetics of NH3 decomposition over highly active Ru/CeO2 catalysts: Effect of the support on H-poisoning and rate determining steps
abstract: Ru/CeO 2 catalysts have recently gained attention for low temperature NH 3 decomposition: the combination of a highly active metal as Ru with a support as CeO 2 , known to enhance several catalytic processes thanks to the ability to create oxygen vacancies, makes this formulation highly promising. In this study, the performances and kinetics of NH 3 decomposition over Ru/CeO 2 were investigated and compared with those of a reference Ru/Al 2 O 3 catalyst by applying multiple techniques. Steady-state activity tests under diluted and concentrated conditions were performed to study the main kinetic dependences, develop rate laws and identify the nature of the rate determining steps. Dynamic experiments of adsorption/desorption and DRIFT experiments under flow conditions and with H 2 /D 2 switch were conducted to identify and quantify the adsorbed species as well as the storage capacity and mobility of H-species, thus providing a support to the kinetic interpretation. The remarkable intrinsic activity exhibited by Ru/CeO 2 catalyst can be associated to the important mitigation of the H-poisoning effect that, instead, limits NH 3 decomposition over Ru/Al 2 O 3 . On Ru/CeO 2 , intermediate H* species would easily migrate from the Ru-sites to the support, thereby hindering the formation of Ru-hydrides, which instead were visible on Ru/Al 2 O 3 . The higher catalytic activity of Ru/CeO 2 allowed a wider operating temperature range, which revealed that with decreasing temperature below 300 °C the rate-determining step of the reaction shifts from ammonia activation to N* associative desorption.

Tribo-thermoelectric energy harvesting in Ag2Se-modified rayon fabric triboelectric nanogenerators
abstract: Incorporating inorganic semiconductors into fabric triboelectric nanogenerators (F-TENG) offers a pathway to mitigate charge-density saturation effects and enhance charge generation. By explicitly exploiting friction-induced temperature gradients within the fabric, this study introduces a tribo-thermoelectric textile concept that goes beyond purely triboelectric F-TENG architectures. In this work, n-type silver selenide (Ag 2 Se) is integrated into a rayon fabric matrix to harvest mechanical energy while simultaneously recovering frictional waste heat. Structural characterization confirms the uniform dispersion of single-phase Ag 2 Se across the textile matrix. Thermal imaging reveals significant friction-induced heating during F-TENG operation, which is utilized by the Ag 2 Se component to contribute an additional thermoelectric voltage. At optimum conditions, the rayon/Ag 2 Se composite exhibits a thermoelectric power factor of 7.94 nW·m − 1 ·K −2 and produces a thermoelectric voltage ( V T ) of ~98 mV at a temperature gradient (ΔT) of ~40 K; at higher ΔT, slight deviations from linear V T–ΔT behavior are observed. The combined action of triboelectric and thermoelectric effects is consistent with promoted carrier excitation and transport in Ag 2 Se, leading to enhanced electrical output. The device achieves a peak open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) of ~64.4 V, a short-circuit current ( I SC ) of ~168.8 μA, and a maximum power density of ~83.8 μW·cm −2 . This performance enhancement is likely influenced by the coupling of triboelectrification with a proposed thermoelectric-driven carrier injection mechanism, which may facilitate charge transport and help reduce charge recombination within the F-TENG system. This work demonstrates a scalable strategy for developing self-sustaining electronic textiles that more fully utilize both mechanical and thermal components of frictional energy, advancing clean energy harvesting and enabling innovative wearable technologies that align with the Sustainable Development Goals.

Carbon nanotube–interfaced lab-on-a-chip sensor coupled with a quantum dot sandwich assay for rapid and selective detection of airborne Aspergillus fumigatus spores
abstract: Rapid and selective detection of airborne fungal pathogens is critical for environmental monitoring and public health surveillance. Herein, we report a carbon nanotube (CNT)–interfaced lab-on-a-chip electrochemical biosensor coupled with a quantum dot (QD)–based sandwich assay for sensitive detection of airborne Aspergillus fumigatus spores. The sensor chip comprises 24 interdigitated microelectrodes (1 mm × 2 mm active area; ~70 μm electrode width), functionalized with carboxylated CNTs to enhance surface area and electron transfer kinetics. Anti-Asp f1 antibodies were covalently immobilized via EDC/NHS chemistry for selective spore capture, followed by signal amplification using QD–receptor conjugates in a sandwich configuration. The CNT–QD hybrid architecture shifts the sensing mechanism from steric blocking to electrochemical signal amplification, resulting in a linear amperometric response over 10²–10⁶ spores/mL with a detection limit of 100 spores/mL. Selectivity studies confirmed negligible response toward non-target fungal species. A custom aerosol collection unit enabled controlled nebulization and condensation of airborne spores directly onto the sensor surface, validating performance under real-world aerosol conditions. The platform demonstrated reproducible responses, stable operation over extended storage, and preserved functionality during aerosol deposition. The synergistic integration of conductive CNT networks and electroactive QDs provides enhanced sensitivity, specificity, and rapid response, highlighting the potential of this miniaturized lab-on-a-chip biosensor for real-time airborne pathogen monitoring.

Quantum size-dependent modulation and interfacial interactions of CuInS2 QDs confined within covalent triazine frameworks for efficient photocatalytic H2 generation
abstract: Nanoscale engineering and a fundamental understanding of heterojunction interfacial interactions are essential for developing highly efficient photocatalysts. In this study, advanced hybrid materials based on a covalent triazine framework (CTF), serving as a host matrix, and size-controlled CuInS 2 quantum dots (QDs) were designed and prepared for photocatalytic hydrogen generation. Post-synthetic encapsulation enabled the uniform dispersion and spatial confinement of the QDs within the CTF pores, promoting efficient charge separation and enhanced light-harvesting. Precise tuning of CuInS 2 QD diameters enabled control over electronic band alignment and charge transfer, revealing a well-defined size-dependent photoactivity in QDs/COF systems. The optimally designed composite (2.5 nm CuInS 2 , 0.75 wt% loading) demonstrated remarkable photocatalytic efficiency for H 2 production (5367 μmol·g −1 after 4 h). In addition, a multiscale GFN1-xTB/DFT computational strategy was developed to realistically model large (~1600 atoms) QDs/CTF interfaces. This enables explicit, facet-dependent adsorption and pore confinement analysis, providing predictive insight into the structure–property relationships governing photocatalytic performance. The most energetically favorable configuration identified was CuInS 2 quantum dots with the Cu/S/In-terminated facet positioned at the hollow site of the mesoporous CTF. This study establishes a new design paradigm by integrating atomic-scale structural insights, quantum confinement effects, and interfacial engineering to guide the development of high-performance materials for sustainable hydrogen production.

Controllable and fast carbon nanostructure growth in molten-salt CO₂ electrolysis enabled by a high-entropy perovskite anode
abstract: Production of high-value carbon materials from CO₂ using molten salt capture and electrolysis appears promising toward carbon neutrality. Nonetheless, additional advancement of this electrolysis is limited by the structural integrity, interface compatibility, and reaction controllability of inert anode materials in high-temperature molten salt environments. This research utilizes a LaTMO₃-type high-entropy perovskite anode (TM: transition metals), synthesized by sol-gel, for fast growth of carbon materials via CO₂ electrolysis in Li₂CO₃–K₂CO₃–CaCl₂–Na₂B₄O₇ molten salt. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicates significant alterations in valence states and reconfiguration of the oxygen environment on the perovskite surface are responsible for fast carbon growth. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations show that surface reconstruction and improved interfacial activity are driven by hybridization between transition metal 3d and O 2p orbitals and M–O-terminated surfaces' low work function. It is found that sintering temperature impacts structural characteristics and crystallinity, electron transport and electrochemical performance, high-temperature wetting behavior, and surface reconstruction. In particular, samples sintered at 900–1000 °C demonstrate reduced interfacial transfer impedance, enhanced anodic reaction kinetics, and superior wettability at elevated temperatures. Moreover, carbon products’ morphology is controllable by manipulating the sintering temperature, evolving from particles/sheets to helical nanowires to fibrous/tubular carbon nanostructures by increasing the temperature. This study not only introduces high-entropy perovskites as new anodes for CO₂ electrolysis but also clarifies how the initial structure, surface reconstruction, and interfacial behavior regulate the synthesis of carbon nanostructures during molten salt electrolysis of CO₂.

ELEVATE-LNP: Empty lipid nanoparticle enabled validation and AI-guided therapeutic evaluation for efficient formulation optimization for mRNA delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as a leading platform for mRNA delivery, particularly following the success of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines. However, identifying effective LNP formulations remains time-consuming because of the large and complex multicomponent formulation space. Here, we present ELEVATE-LNP an Empty-LNP-Enabled Validation and AI-Guided Therapeutic Evaluation platform by integrating a high-throughput parallelized microfluidic preparation with physicochemical characterization and machine learning for mid-stream and downstream LNP formulation optimization when ionizable lipids are shortlisted. A broad formulation space comprising four ionizable lipids, different helper lipids, lipid ratios, and process conditions was first screened using empty LNPs to identify formulations with desirable particle size and polydispersity index (PDI). Machine-learning analysis was then used to determine the formulation and process parameters associated with empty-LNP properties. Selected candidates were subsequently evaluated following mRNA encapsulation by assessing particle size, PDI, encapsulation efficiency, cell viability, and transfection performance. The results revealed lipid-dependent relationships between formulation parameters and the physicochemical properties of empty LNPs. Six features were strongly associated with particle size, while eleven features contributed to variations in PDI. GFP expression in CFBE cells demonstrated that SM-102-based LNPs achieved higher transfection efficiency than CKK-E12-based formulations. In a separate CFTR mRNA evaluation, DOPC-containing LNPs produced higher CFTR protein expression than their DSPC-containing counterparts. By integrating empty-LNP prescreening with subsequent payload-based validation, the ELEVATE-LNP workflow reduces the number of candidates and the amount of nucleic acid required for functional testing. The platform therefore provides a practical approach for narrowing lipid-ratio and formulation-condition spaces within preselected ionizable lipid systems.

Oxygen-vacancy-mediated BrO3− electroreduction: Positively charged microenvironment enables directional diffusion and spontaneous adsorption
abstract: Abstract Ozonation can disinfect the drinking water without producing chlorinated byproducts, but bromate (BrO3−) emerges as a carcinogenic by-product. Although the electroreduction could theoretically convert BrO3− into non-toxic bromide (Br−), the detoxification process was hindered by the electrostatic repulsion of BrO3− from the negatively charged cathode. In this work, a commercial Fe foam was employed for electrochemically reducing 1.0 mg/L BrO3− via direct electron transfer mechanism (k1, 0.7796 min− 1), during which microcrystalline magnetite (Fe3O4) was in-situ generated with abundant oxygen vacancies (Ovs). The Ovs could shape neighboring Fe2+ atoms into positively charged microenvironment for accelerating the directional diffusion of BrO3− toward themselves. Compared to negatively charged surface, the positive microenvironment could enhance the BrO3− diffusion with coefficient change from 0.0059 m2/s to 0.0387 m2/s. Furthermore, Ovs activated the neighboring Fe2+ atom into a highly active site for BrO3− adsorption with an adsorption energy (Eads) of 4.21 eV, in comparison to the energy-demanding adsorption on intact Fe3O4 lattice (Eads, -2.17 eV). Afterwards, BrO3− underwent complete detoxification through sequential deoxygenation, with Ovs assisting throughout the whole process from BrO3− to Br−. By the in-situ defect engineering, the research pointed out a high-efficient approach to create positively charged microenvironment for enhancing oxyanion electroreduction.

abstract: Durable, low-loading platinum-group metal (PGM) catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are critical for advancing proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). Here, we report a continuous-flow synthesis of ultrasmall (1.5 ± 0.5 nm) PtNiRu medium-entropy alloy nanoparticles on defect-rich few-layer graphene (FLG) to form (Pt 5 Ni 3 Ru 2 @G). This approach overcomes the asynchronous reduction kinetics of conventional batch methods, yielding a homogeneous single-phase solid solution with surface Ni O species, a pre-catalyst architecture revealed by synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy. During acidic HER, electrochemical surface activation of the pre-catalyst progressively lowers the overpotential from 123 to 70 mV at 0.1 A cm −2 , while the Tafel slope decreases from 60.36 to 35.74 mV dec −1 . Post- operando characterizations show surface Ni O species are reduced under cathodic polarization, while Pt and Ru electronic structures remain unchanged. Translation to a single-cell PEMWE device confirms the activation mechanism and the Pt 5 Ni 3 Ru 2 @G-based cell delivers 1.0 A cm −2 at 1.6 V, while exhibiting operational stability for over 300 h at 0.5 A cm −2 . Notably, such remarkable durability is achieved with 20.5% PGM-loading, potentially reducing PEMWE cost. The findings establish continuous-flow synthesis as a versatile protocol for producing entropy-stabilized alloy catalysts with dynamically restructuring surfaces for durable, PGM-reduced water electrolysis.

abstract: A multistage resonant gradient-impedance metastructure was fabricated by integrating PACF absorbing units, low-loss N-PA spacer layers, and a laser-induced LI-PACF lossy reflective base through fused deposition modeling, while its optimal geometric parameters were determined by machine-learning-assisted surrogate prediction and multi-objective screening. PACF provided conductive loss, dipolar polarization, and interfacial relaxation, while the N-PA layers regulated impedance transition and interlayer coupling. Meanwhile, the LI-PACF substrate, featuring enhanced surface conductivity and strengthened interfacial polarization, acted as a lossy reflective boundary for secondary attenuation. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of gradient impedance evolution and staged resonant complementarity, the optimized metastructure achieved a simulated effective absorption bandwidth of 33.8 GHz for RL < -10 dB and 24.83 GHz for RL < -20 dB at normal incidence, with a minimum reflection loss of -43.56 dB at a thickness of 14.7 mm; experimental arch-method measurements confirmed EAB proportions of 88.94% (RL < -10 dB) and 65.47% (RL < -20 dB) under TE polarization. Remarkably, under 60° TE incidence, it still retained effective absorption bandwidths of 33.01 and 17.12 GHz for RL < -10 and -20 dB, respectively. Additionally, it exhibited an average radar cross-section reduction of 23 dBsm over 2–40 GHz, together with a compressive modulus of ≈1.8 GPa, a first peak compressive strength of 129.5 MPa, and rapid deicing within 60 s at 25 V.

Enhanced hydrogen storage in acid-treated and palladium loaded natural zeolites at high pressure and near ambient temperature
abstract: Natural clinoptilolite is an abundant, low-cost candidate for solid-state H2 storage, but its near-ambient capacity is limited by low surface area and cation-blocked channels. In this study, we systematically evaluated acid activation (0.5–8M HCl) and Pd functionalization for H2 adsorption at near ambient conditions (298 K and up to 53 bar) using a patented gravimetric adsorption apparatus with significantly larger sample-mass capacity (6.7-7.8g). Comprehensive structural and physicochemical characterization identified 2M HCl as the optimal activation agent, balancing decationization and dealumination while preserving framework integrity. Under this treatment, surface area increased from 47.45 to 134.57 m² g⁻¹ and micropore volume from 0.0055 to 0.0422 cm3 g⁻¹, enhancing H2 uptake at 50 bar from 0.405 wt.% (raw) to 0.500 wt.%. More severe treatment (4–8 M) caused framework degradation and lower usable pore connectivity, reducing performance despite further dealumination. Homogeneous deposition-precipitation of Pd onto the 2M-modified sample generated highly dispersed Pd species (0.013 wt.%) without detectable bulk PdO and produced the highest H2 uptake, reaching 0.525 wt.% at 50 bar. This performance is superior to those of the vast majority of the MOF- and carbon-based adsorbents included in the present comparison under similar conditions, indicating that efficient Pd dispersion can enhance hydrogen storage even at very low metal loading. The materials showed rapid, reversible desorption (~4 s) and good cycling reproducibility. Freundlich fits (R² > 0.999) captured the near-linear isotherms, with adsorption capacity constant KF increasing by 57% from raw to optimally treated samples.
