abstract: Deep removal of trace Ne from He feedstocks at liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K) is an important and challenging problem due to their similar molecular dimensions and weak polarizability difference. Herein, the Ne/He separation performance in fluorinated ultramicroporous metal-organic framework, KAUST‐7, was systematically investigated at 77 K. KAUST‐7 features narrow 3.5 Å channels lined with highly electronegative fluorine atoms, generating a localized negative electrostatic field in the confined pores. Static adsorption measurements revealed a Ne uptake of 2.95 mmol·g-1 at 77 K versus only 0.0227 mmol·g-1 for He in KAUST‐7. IAST calculations predicted an exceptional Ne/He selectivity of 3.6 × 103 for a 0.1/99.9 feed, remaining 262 at 87 K. Kinetic tests demonstrated rapid Ne capture in KAUST‐7, which can reach 67% of equilibrium uptake within 10 s at an initial rate of 0.198 mmol·g-1·s-1, with a kinetic selectivity of 216.05. DFT calculations yielded Ne and He binding energies in KAUST‐7 was -9.92 and -0.22 kJ·mol-1, respectively, confirming fluorine‐induced polarization as the origin of selective Ne capture. Breakthrough experiments tests confirmed excellent dynamic separation performance at 77 K. This work highlights the synergistic effect of ultramicroporous confinement and fluorine‐functionalized pore chemistry for ultrahigh‐selectivity Ne/He separation.

title: Enriching triboelectric signal characteristic toward vibration waveform recognition by electron-beam irradiation
Physicochemical characterisation and pyrolysis evaluation of simulated, pre-sorted heterogeneous laboratory plastic mixtures for chemicals and energy recovery
abstract: Laboratory plastic wastes comprise diverse polymers, copolymers, and both organic and inorganic additives, resulting in substantial compositional heterogeneity. Despite this variability, these materials remain energy-dense feedstocks suitable for thermochemical conversion by pyrolysis. This study evaluates ten simulated heterogeneous laboratory plastic streams (P1-P10) prepared using site-specific procurement data, homogenised by cryogenic milling and characterised to enable comparison between measured feedstock compositional characteristics and pyrolysis behaviour. Batch pyrolysis was conducted under uniform conditions (450 °C, 60 min, 20 g), and product yields, compositions, and physicochemical properties were quantified to assess energy distribution and utilisation potential. All feedstocks generated high liquid yields (73.2–95.3 wt%), accompanied by gases (1.9–14.0 wt%) and solid residues (0.4–17.6 wt%). The resulting oils exhibited high heating values (34.4–42.9 MJ kg −1 ) and low viscosities (0.71–3.01 cP at 25 °C), supporting potential use in fuel blending and chemical recovery. GC–MS analysis revealed compositional diversity, with oils dominated by single-ring aromatics, aliphatic, cycloaliphatic, or long-chain hydrocarbons, reflecting feedstock differences. Gas heating values ranged from 14.0 to 31.2 MJ kg −1 . Solid residues contained high fixed carbon but variable ash contents, indicating differing additive loadings. Ash contents were determined using ICP-OES and SEM-EDS, to identify major inorganic constituents, while additional tests examined whether plastic derived ash influenced pyrolysis of virgin HDPE, but showed negligible changes in product distributions and oil compositions. Multivariate analyses (including one-way ANOVA, principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA)) demonstrated that feedstock heterogeneity strongly governed product quality and energy partitioning. However, the batch pyrolysis conditions used in this work and feedstock diversity may constrain broader applicability, indicating future work must incorporate more real-world variability and diverse additive chemistries around processing of laboratory plastic waste streams.

Carbon quantum dots-mediated interface engineering of dual S-scheme heterojunctions for efficient charge separation and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
abstract: Broad light harvesting and precisely regulated interfacial charge transfer are critical for efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. To achieve this goal, an interfacial engineering strategy mediated by biomass-derived carbon quantum dots (CQDs) is developed for the in situ construction of a ternary dual S-scheme heterojunction via a one-step hydrothermal method. Comprehensive structural characterizations (e.g., Kelvin probe force microscopy and in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy) and density functional theory calculations reveal that the CQDs reconstruct the interfacial electronic structure between CdS and ZnIn2S4 (ZIS) in the ternary heterojunction, intensifying the built-in electric field and optimizing interfacial contact. Moreover, the CQDs function as charge-transfer bridges, establishing bidirectional carrier-migration pathways across the CdS/CQD and CQD/ZIS interfaces. Consequently, the constructed ternary heterojunction optimizes the H* adsorption free energy, lowering the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of CQDs-mediated interface engineering and directed charge transfer, the optimized CQDs/CdS/ZIS-5 photocatalyst achieves an apparent quantum efficiency of 15.8% at 365 nm and an outstanding hydrogen evolution rate of 6728.41 μmol·h-1·g-1, representing 9.53-, 8.50-, and 3.20-fold increases relative to pristine ZIS, CdS, and the CdS/ZIS binary heterojunction, respectively. This study offers a feasible strategy for constructing high-efficiency dual S-scheme photocatalytic systems through CQDs-mediated interfacial electronic regulation.

Multilayered self-protection mechanisms sustain the stability and resilience of acidic activated sludge for mainstream wastewater treatment
abstract: Acid-tolerant ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB)-driven processes are emerging as a promising strategy for sustainable wastewater treatment, yet their reliability has been questioned because they typically operate under extreme in situ free nitrous acid (FNA, > 1 mg N/L) accumulation. Here, we systematically evaluated the stability and resilience of acidic activated sludge (AAS) by operating three parallel reactors for over 300 days under short-term anoxic and aerobic starvation stress and long-term neutral pH perturbations. Contrary to long-standing concerns, AAS demonstrated remarkable stability and resilience. Typical 24-h anoxic and aerobic starvation stresses caused only transient disruptions, with nitrogen and organic matter removal recovering to >80% within three days. Even under prolonged neutral pH stress, acidic AOB activity persisted for 15 days and nitrite accumulation for 60 days, while organic matter removal consistently exceeded 80%. Comprehensive analysis revealed multilayered self-protection mechanisms. Under short-term stress, AAS intensified EPS production to maintain floc integrity and alleviate the biocidal impact of FNA through rapid alkalinity regeneration, thereby preventing sharp activity losses. These effects, together with the kinetic buffering capacity of the acid-tolerant AOB ( Candidatus Nitrosoglobus), sustained system pH in the acidic range. During long-term neutral pH stress, exclusive enrichment of Candidatus Nitrosoglobus delayed the rise of canonical nitrifiers ( Nitrosomonas , Nitrobacter , Nitrospira ), prolonging acidic nitritation before its eventual collapse. In parallel, abundant heterotrophic populations and functional redundancy ensured stable organic matter removal despite drastic community succession. Overall, this study demonstrates that AAS is not a fragile niche process but a self-protecting system, highlighting its potential for mainstream sustainable wastewater treatment.

title: Rigid-flexible dynamic covalent network from aldehyde-functionalized lignin-containing cellulose nanofibrils and aminated polyvinyl alcohol for high-performance wood bonding
Effects of cell design and operating parameters on oscillatory instability in an anion-exchange membrane CO2 electrolyzer
abstract: Periodic oscillations in cell voltage and CO2 reduction product selectivity are commonly observed in laboratory studies using membrane electrode assembly (MEA) CO2 electrolyzers with anion-exchange membranes (AEM). These oscillations hinder mechanistic studies and progress toward industrial deployment of CO2 electrolyzers. To understand how to mitigate these oscillations in laboratory experiments, we investigated the effects of three electrolyzer design parameters on system stability: (i) membrane type and thickness, (ii) gas diffusion layer (GDL) properties, and (iii) cell compression, characterized as a normalized thickness difference (NTD) between the GDL and gasket and assembly torque. In our system, we found pairing a higher ionic conductivity AEM with a GDL with a cracked microporous layer (MPL) at a medium cell compression (NTD: 40%, torque: 2 Nm), led to the most stable CO2 to CO electrolysis with pseudo-steady-state CO Faradaic efficiency of around 85% achieved at 100 mA cm–2 for over 50 h. In contrast, lower conductivity AEMs showed earlier and more frequent oscillations related to water flooding, enhanced K+ crossover, and eventual short-circuiting. A lower compression assembly (NTD: 0%, torque: 2 Nm) exhibited a higher initial CO selectivity (>95% for 50 h) but developed more frequent oscillations associated with salt accumulation in the cathode flow channel. Our hypotheses are further supported by tests of an ”over-compressed” cell (NTD: 40%, torque: 4 Nm), which exhibited poor water drainage, rapid salt accumulation in the cathode gas channel, and an increased risk of electrode short-circuiting. These observations lead to practical AEM electrolyzer design rules: pairing high-conductive AEMs with crack-rich MPLs and optimizing cell compression to balance membrane-electrode interfacial contact and water drainage to maintain selective and stable CO2 electrolysis.

title: Exsolution of active and thermally stable Ru nanoparticles on CeO2 via one-pot infiltration for enhanced direct-ammonia solid oxide fuel cells (DA-SOFCs)
abstract: Direct-ammonia solid oxide fuel cells (DA-SOFCs) offer a promising energy conversion approach by eliminating the need for external ammonia decomposition to produce H 2 fuel. We report a facile and scalable one-pot infiltration method to synthesize highly active, thermally stable Ru nanoparticles exsolved on CeO 2 (Ru/CeO 2 ) supports. Structural analyses reveal uniform ~2 nm Ru nanoparticles that remain firmly anchored and highly dispersed after prolonged high-temperature operation with strong metal-support interaction. Incorporating exsolved Ru/CeO 2 catalysts into commercial SOFC anodes via one-pot infiltration substantially improves ammonia decomposition, achieving >91% conversion at 650 °C and enhancing DA-SOFC performance by 23% over unmodified cells. The role of Ru/CeO 2 catalysts extends to H 2 -fueled operation, demonstrating dual functionality in both ammonia decomposition and hydrogen oxidation. The method was scaled to a large-area commercial cell (12 × 12 cm 2 ), demonstrating performance under industry-relevant operating conditions with stable operation over 150 h.

abstract: The global challenge of declining raw water availability for potable and irrigation uses, especially in semi-arid areas, calls for alternative raw water sources such as urban stormwater. However, stormwater contains potentially harmful chemicals, such as tire rubber additives, that can threaten human and ecosystem health. This study investigated the use of a visible light-activated photocatalyst to degrade diphenylguanidine (DPG), a synthetic rubber additive commonly found in stormwater. The photocatalyst was a composite of nitrogen- and zinc-doped TiO 2 on phosphorus-treated canola straw biochar. This composite exhibited better photocatalytic activity than pristine TiO 2 , with enhanced visible-light absorption. The biochar provided a high surface area and adsorption capacity, preventing semiconductor agglomeration and reducing electron-hole recombination, thereby enhancing degradation efficiency. Adding 2 wt% nitrogen and zinc, respectively, and 10 wt% biochar increased the surface area to 213.2 m 2 /g (up from 144.6 m 2 /g for TiO 2 ). This increase led to inhibited TiO 2 crystal growth, improved photon absorption, and a reduction in the band-gap energy from 3.19 eV to 2.68 eV. Complete DPG degradation was achieved under visible light at pH 7, with an initial concentration of 250 μg/L, in 80 min. The findings confirm the synergistic effect of the catalyst and visible light. This composite material has strong potential for treating stormwater in real-world applications. This study highlights the value of innovative materials derived from renewable resources and powered by visible light to combat environmental pollution.

abstract: Bioinspired approaches based on soft biological tissues have driven major advances in artificial materials for applications. Many natural tissues, particularly muscles, exhibit anisotropic mechanical behavior and efficient energy dissipation. Here, we present a new strategy that transforms conventional composites into microscale artificial musculoskeletal systems. This is achieved by redefining inorganic nanosheets (PCNC-M) from passive reinforcing components to active structural frameworks, and by elevating the organic polymer from a simple matrix to a multifunctional, dynamic adhesive, and responsive medium. Through synergistic, physically guided co-assembly, pre-stretching drives the ordered alignment of PCNC-M nanosheets, while, poly (propylene carbonate) (PPC) acts as a dynamic adhesive, energy dissipating matrix, and multifunctional thermal and electrical regulator. The resulting multilayer composites exhibit a high tensile strength of 35.7 MPa, an in-plane thermal conductivity of 7.2 W/mK, and exceptional electrical insulation of 2.5 × 10¹⁵ Ω·cm. When applied to high-power LED modules, smartphone CPUs, and control transformers, the material achieves temperature reductions of 19.1,12.4, and 16.0°C, respectively. It also displays pronounced shape-memory behavior, with shape fixity (Rf) and shape recovery (Rr) ratios of 90.3% and 92.4%, respectively. Notably, after 120 days of soil burial, the composite achieves a degradation rate of 43.7%. This strategy transcends the conventional passive filler-matrix paradigm, enabling a dynamic artificial musculoskeletal system for next-generation thermal management in flexible and high-power devices.

Overcoming major challenges in lignocellulose catalytic pyrolysis by combination of low-temperature thermal decomposition and co-processing with vegetable oils over ZSM-5 zeolite: boosted production of aromatic hydrocarbons and prolonged catalyst lifetime
abstract: The current study addresses the major challenges of lignocellulose catalytic pyrolysis over zeolites: the low hydrocarbon yields and the fast catalyst deactivation. The results here reported demonstrate how these hindrances can be sharply improved by the combination of low-temperature lignocellulose pyrolysis and catalytic co-processing with vegetable oils. This strategy has been successfully applied here to different combinations of lignocellulose (oak woodchips and acid-washed wheat straw) and vegetable oils (camelina and jatropha). The experiments were carried out in an ex-situ fixed-bed reactor with continuous feeding systems for both substrates, enabling the evaluation of the catalyst performance over time on stream. A nanocrystalline ZSM-5 zeolite was used as a catalyst. In comparison with conventional catalytic pyrolysis, the combination of low-temperature pyrolysis (350 °C) followed by catalytic co-processing resulted in a sharp enhancement of both the production of aromatic hydrocarbons (AR) and catalyst lifetime. Thus, the AR yield was boosted in the co-processing tests, reaching values of c.a. 22 wt% (≈40% carbon yield) at the beginning of the reaction (1 h of time on stream). Simultaneously, the deactivation kinetic constant (first order model) was reduced by a factor of about eight by combining low-temperature lignocellulose pyrolysis and vegetable oil co-processing, substantially improving catalyst stability. A preliminary comparative economic analysis was carried out to determine the product revenues that could be obtained, whereas an assessment of the CO 2 carbon sequestration potential was also performed. In both analyses, the proposed low-temperature lignocellulose pyrolysis and vegetable oil co-processing approach outperformed clearly the other considered cases.

abstract: Calcium oxalate crystal-induced kidney injury (COC-KI) is characterized by excessive oxidative stress and inflammation. Nanozymes can partially mitigate COC-KI through superoxide dismutase (SOD)- and catalase (CAT)-like activities, but their therapeutic efficacy is often compromised by the coexisting peroxidase (POD)- and oxidase (OXD)-like activities, which may paradoxically generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). Additionally, the lack of targeted delivery remains another challenge. To overcome these limitations together, metal-organic framework (MOF)-based nanozyme PCN222-Mn (PM), which exhibits prominent SOD- and CAT-like activities with negligible POD/OXD-like activities, was chosen for the treatment of COC-KI. To achieve precise renal targeting, we functionalized PM with hyaluronic acid (HA), yielding PCN222-Mn@HA (PMH). Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that PMH effectively accumulated in injured renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) and provided superior protection against COC-KI. Mechanistic investigation via RNA sequencing revealed that PMH exerted its renoprotective effects primarily by suppressing NF-κB signaling, which in turn downregulated the expression of NLRP3 and MCP-1, thereby inhibiting inflammasome activation and macrophage recruitment. Collectively, this work proposes a novel and effective targeted nanozyme strategy for the treatment of COC-KI.

abstract: During charge and discharge, enhancing the Li+ transport capability of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) while simultaneously blocking electronic conduction is an effective strategy for suppressing lithium dendrite growth and mitigating volume expansion at the Li-metal anode interface. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations of Gibbs free energies were used to identify 2-fluoro-3-nitropyridine (FNP) as a dual-source oxidant providing both fluorine and oxygen. Upon reacting with metallic lithium, FNP facilitates the formation of an SEI layer composed of interlaced LiF crystallites, which provide high ionic conductivity, and Li2O crystallites, which offer superior electronic insulation. This architecture enables the fabrication of a highly stable Li-metal anode, denoted as LiF/Li2O-Li. The formation mechanism was verified via in situ Raman spectroscopy, while in situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed significantly suppressed volume expansion. After 500 cycles, the LiF/Li2O-Li anode thickness increased from 55 μm to 105 μm (an expansion factor of 1.9), whereas the pristine Li anode expanded from 89 μm to 198 μm (a factor of 2.2). Symmetric Li||Li cells utilizing this anode exhibited stable cycling for 600 h at a current density of 1 mA cm-2 and areal capacity of 1 mA h cm-2 respectively. Furthermore, lithium-sulfur cells employing the LiF/Li2O-Li anode demonstrated excellent stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.201% per cycle over 120 cycles at 0.2 C, maintaining superior performance even under high sulfur loading and lean electrolyte conditions.

abstract: Photocatalytic urea synthesis is a sustainable and cost-effective route for green chemical production, but remains challenging owing to the intrinsically low reactivity of the reactants, the difficulty of C-N coupling, and the sluggish dissociation of H2O for proton (H⁺) supply. Overcoming these limitations requires the synergistic action of multiple active sites. Herein, a photo-induced strategy is reported to construct a ZnS-Pt-x catalyst integrating three cooperative active sites (Pt1, Ptx, Sv) for N2, H2O, and CO2 activation. The optimized ZnS-Pt-0.5 achieves a urea yield of 13.0 μmol g-1 h-1, which is 4.6 times that of pure ZnS, while exhibiting excellent cycling stability. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Pt1 sites effectively activate N2, Sv sites activate CO2 to generate *CO intermediates, and Ptx sites dissociate H2O to provide H⁺. This tripartite synergy promotes the formation of the key *NCON intermediate and subsequent hydrogenation reactions. This finding provides new insights into the rational design of multi-active-site synergistic catalysts and lays a theoretical and experimental foundation for solar-driven green urea synthesis.

abstract: Sodium metal batteries (SMBs) are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage. However, uncontrollable dendrite growth and unstable solid-electrolyte interphases (SEI) hinder their practical application. In this study, we present a scalable and cost-effective approach for fabricating stable three-dimensional (3D) carbon hosts for SMBs using recycled carbon fiber papers (CFPs). A facile carbonization process combined with a subsequent washing treatment generates oxygen-functionalized amorphous carbon layers on the surface of the carbonized CFPs (wcCFP). These surface layers lower the Na nucleation overpotential to approximately 5 mV and facilitate the formation of a mechanically robust, NaF-rich SEI, thereby effectively suppressing dendrite propagation. Consequently, Na@wcCFP symmetric cells exhibit ultrastable cycling performance for over 2000 h. Furthermore, full cells coupled with this anode demonstrate a remarkable capacity retention of 90.0% after 1000 cycles at a high rate of 5C while maintaining a Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%. Notably, the electrochemical performance of wcCFP is highly competitive with previously reported carbon-based Na hosts despite being fabricated through a simple metal additive-free process without elaborate surface engineering. These findings demonstrate that oxygen-functionalized carbon layers on 3D carbon hosts provide a scalable, sustainable, and cost-effective route for stabilizing Na metal anodes. Beyond improving Na metal stability, this work highlights the potential of recycled carbon materials for sustainable next-generation energy storage technologies.

Balancing interfacial hydrophilicity and effective reaction space accessibility in mesoporous TiO2/SBA-15 photocatalysts: Insights from NMR
abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) supported on ordered mesoporous SBA-15 is a promising photocatalytic system because the mesoporous framework regulates the dispersion of TiO 2 , interfacial properties, and molecular transport. However, the relationship among TiO 2 loading, interfacial hydrophilicity, transport behavior, and photocatalytic performance remains unclear. In this work, a series of TiO 2 /SBA-15 composites with TiO 2 loadings ranging from 20 to 80 wt% were synthesized to systematically investigate the coupling between pore structure, interfacial properties, and photocatalytic activity. Structural characterization confirms that the ordered SBA-15 framework is preserved, while TiO 2 gradually evolves from highly dispersed intrapore species to partial pore filling and external surface deposition with increasing loading. The catalyst containing 40 wt% TiO 2 /SBA-15 exhibited the highest photocatalytic activity among the investigated compositions, achieving approximately 56% Congo red degradation within 90 min. To elucidate the origin of this optimum, low-field NMR relaxation and diffusion measurements were employed to probe water–surface interactions and molecular transport within the mesoporous channels. Increasing TiO 2 loading enhances interfacial hydrophilicity but simultaneously reduces the effective molecular diffusion coefficient, leading to increased apparent pore tortuosity. Damköhler number analysis suggests that classical intraparticle diffusion is unlikely to be the dominant limitation under the stated model assumptions. The deterioration in photocatalytic performance at high TiO 2 loadings is therefore more consistent with reduced effective reaction-space accessibility caused by progressive pore obstruction and restricted active-site accessibility; changes in the internal optical environment may also contribute. The superior performance at intermediate TiO 2 loading therefore results from a favorable balance between enhanced interfacial interactions and the preservation of accessible reactive space. This work highlights the importance of simultaneously considering interfacial chemistry and reaction-space accessibility for the rational design of mesoporous photocatalysts.

Bowl-shaped conductive filler enabled low-modulus conductive ionic elastomer for conformal and efficient near-field electromagnetic shielding
abstract: Lightweight and conformable electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are highly desirable for wearable communication and embodied artificial intelligence. However, simultaneously achieving extremely high electrical conductivity and low modulus in conductive elastomers remains a significant challenge. Herein, a novel bowl-shaped silver-coated expanded polymer beads (Ag@EBs) incorporated polyvinyl alcohol/phytic acid (PVA/PhA) conductive ionic elastomer with silver/ion dual conductive network structure is fabricated for conformal and highly efficient near-field (NF) EMI shielding. The bowl-shaped Ag@EBs, featuring an open-ended architecture, enable dense in-plane stacking to form the primary conductive network and can readily deform with the soft PVA/PhA ionic elastomer matrix. Meanwhile, H⁺ ions released from the PhA moieties serve as a synergistic ionic conductive pathway, reducing the contact resistance between adjacent Ag@EBs and thereby stabilizing the conductive network. As a result, the prepared composite film exhibited a rather low modulus of only 299 kPa and an exceptional EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of 92.6 dB at the thickness of only ~200 μm. Notably, the dual-conductive network also ensured the stable conductivity of the elastomer even under large deformation, with only a negligible decrease at a tensile strain of ~200%. Owing to its soft and robustly conductive characteristics, the film exhibits excellent conformability to complex surfaces and achieves a remarkable near-field EMI shielding effectiveness (NF-SE) of -53.28 dB, comparable to that of copper foil shields. Our work provides a new strategy for designing conformable EMI shielding materials which are highly promising for conferring reliable NF shielding to stretchable and wearable electronics

abstract: Wearable smart sweat sensors hold promise for non-invasive health monitoring, but existing devices often face issues with user discomfort and inefficient sweat collection. Herein, we present a novel sandwich-structured bionic skin with dual-layer nanofibers integrating multifunctional detection of glucose, lactate, uric acid, Na + , K + , NH₄ + , skin impedance, and temperature. Fabricated via thermal transfer printing and zone-specific localized compression, the device reduces production time and cost. The inner polyacrylonitrile (PAN/F127) layer enhances sweat absorption, achieving over 8× faster absorption than microchannels, while the outer polydimethylsiloxane (PVB/PDMS) layer provides waterproofing, radiative cooling, and antifouling, ensuring comfort and enzymatic stability. The sensor exhibits high sensitivity, selectivity, and retains over 84% performance after nine days. Integration with a redesigned Deep Learning Continuous Analyte Monitoring with Real-time Engagement (D-CARE) system, featuring two flexible circuits and a deep learning attenuation correction algorithm, enables precise real-time monitoring and health anomaly alerting. In situ exercise tests confirm continuous, accurate physiological monitoring, advancing personalized healthcare with a reliable, user-friendly wearable platform.

abstract: High-performance cellulose-based materials are promising sustainable alternatives to petrochemical plastics. However, their scalable fabrication remains challenging due to the densely packed microfibrillar structure and the limited processability of cellulose. Herein, we report a swelling-assisted dissolution strategy based on a zinc chloride/lactic acid (ZnCl2/LA) deep eutectic solvent (DES) combined with ZnCl2·3H2O for rapid room-temperature dissolution of cellulose. In this system, ZnCl2/LA DES first induces effective swelling and structural loosening of cellulose, thereby increasing interfibrillar spacing and improving solvent accessibility. This pretreatment facilitates the rapid penetration of ZnCl2·3H2O into the cellulose microstructure, enabling complete dissolution within 5 min after swelling pretreatment. SAXS, NMR, and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the synergistic interactions among Zn2+, Cl-, LA, and H2O promote the dispersion of cellulose chains and stabilize dissolved cellulose chains through coordination and hydrogen-bond interactions. The solvent system exhibits broad applicability toward cellulose feedstocks with different degrees of polymerization and lignin contents (≤27%). The dissolved cellulose can be regenerated into transparent and mechanically robust materials with a tensile strength of 144 MPa and a toughness of 118 MJ·m-3 after crosslinking. This work provides a mild and efficient strategy for cellulose dissolution and offers insights into the role of swelling-assisted solvent diffusion in cellulose processing and biomass valorization.

Competitive hydrated eutectic electrolyte for 9650 h long-lived aqueous Zn-ion batteries with wide-temperature operability
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising candidates for low-cost energy storage in harsh or remote environments. However, their practical deployment is impeded by Zinc dendritic growth and water-driven parasitic reactions at the Zn anode, which jointly deteriorate reversibility and cycling life, particularly under subzero conditions. Herein, a eutectic electrolyte system designed by introducing dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and ethylene glycol (EG) as co-solvent in ZnSO4 aqueous electrolyte. This innovative strategy generates a significant synergistic effect and induces competitive reconstruction of the solvation structure and interfaces. It assigns distinct roles to DMSO and EG in regulating Zn2+ solvation structure, hydrogen-bond networks, and the zinc anode interface, enabling DMSO to participate more extensively in hydrogen-bond networks and interfacial modulation of the zinc anode. Consequently, it triggers outstanding low-temperature and interfacial operational performance. The designed electrolyte not only enables the Zn||Zn symmetric cell to operate for over 9600 hours at room temperature, but also allows the cell to stably work at -40 ℃. The fabricated Zn||I2@AC and Zn||NVO batteries shows high specific capacity, excellent cycling stability, and low-temperature operation capability. This study underscores a competitive co-solvent strategy that couples solvation-structure engineering with interfacial stabilization for long-life AZIBs with good environmental adaptability.

abstract: Hydrocarbon (HC)-based electrolytes have emerged as promising alternatives to perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) materials for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) owing to their low gas permeability, structural tunability, and reduced fluorine content. However, the development of high-performance and durable all-HC-based membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) remains challenging because of the limited durability of HC membranes and the difficulty of achieving optimized catalyst layer structures using HC ionomers. In this study, a high-performance all-HC-based PEMWE MEA is developed using the SP50 HC electrolyte and a spray-coated electrode architecture. Systematic optimization identifies 3 and 20 wt% as the optimal ionomer contents for the anode and cathode catalyst layers, respectively. The optimized all-HC-based MEA delivers a current density of 5.94 A cm −2 at 1.9 V and 80 °C, outperforming a PFSA-based reference MEA (5.20 A cm −2 ) under identical conditions. Durability analysis reveals that membrane degradation is the dominant performance-limiting factor, resulting in a degradation rate of 410 μV h −1 and 38% reduction in membrane molecular weight after 100 h of operation at 2 A cm −2 . To mitigate membrane degradation, a CeO 2 radical scavenger is incorporated into the SP50 membrane, reducing the degradation rate to 320 μV h −1 and suppressing molecular-weight loss to 25%. These results confirm that membrane stabilization is critical for improving the durability of all-HC-based PEMWE systems. Overall, the combination of catalyst layer optimization and radical-scavenger-assisted membrane stabilization provides an effective strategy for realizing high-performance and durable fluorine-free PEMWE systems.

Towards a robust and scalable perfusion process to produce bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells for allogeneic cell therapy
abstract: Cell therapies hold the promise to fundamentally change healthcare by curing previously untreatable diseases. Both autologous and allogeneic cell therapies rely on donor cells for expansion. The variety of diseases, cell types, and inherent growth kinetic variabilities puts a high demand on the manufacturing process. The production process must be robust, comply with cGMP guidelines, and be scalable in order to make the treatments available for patients and reduce costs for society. To this end, we developed a perfusion process for the expansion of allogeneic human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (hMSCs) on microcarriers in a 100 mL working volume ( V ) bioreactor. This process achieved an expansion factor of 14 within 8 days of culture. A further optimized process was applied to the cells of three donors, where an expansion factor of 12 or higher (20 highest) was achieved for all donors. The process was then scaled 20-fold to 2 L V . An expansion factor of 18 was achieved, demonstrating good comparability to the down-scale model of 100 mL V . The 2 L process was further scaled to the pilot-scale of 15 L V , again showing comparability to the smaller scales. The cells produced in the different scale's bioreactors were tested in an extended functional quality panel, including cell viability, hMSC phenotype profiling, differentiation and immunomodulatory licensing molecules, as well as T-cell suppression capacity assessed by mixed lymphocyte reactions. These analyses demonstrated comparability to the 2D-expanded cells at earlier passages. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that a perfusion process has been applied for the expansion of hMSC at pilot-scale, and represents an important step towards large-scale, GMP-compliant manufacturing of hMSCs.

title: DGFE-SELEX-based de novo design of an aptamer–ASO delivery system with dual knockdown function for enhancing tumor immunotherapy
Multivariate quantification of methotrexate in the presence of mercaptopurine on lab-on-disc: double filtration assay
abstract: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) is crucial for ensuring patient safety and treatment efficacy, particularly for medications with a narrow therapeutic window. Current gold standard techniques, such as HPLC, are highly accurate but limited by high costs, long processing times, and reliance on centralized laboratories and trained personnel for operation. Multiplexing in TDM, lacking in most of the currently used techniques, offers an opportunity to enhance analytical throughput and reduce sample volumes, thereby improving patient comfort and ultimately could also reduce the cost of analysis. Therefore, we are introducing a Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS)-based centrifugal microfluidic platform enabling simultaneous detection of two drugs from less than 20 μL of patient sample. A key feature of the system is on-disc integration of precipitation and filtration, using regenerated cellulose membrane. This serves as an effective sample pretreatment strategy that enhances reproducibility and spectral quality by reducing biological interference. A second filtration step directly on the SERS substrate embedded in the disc, driven by centrifugal forces, proved to enhance further quantification of drugs from blood samples. The developed platform demonstrated reliable analytical performance for two target analytes, methotrexate (MTX) and mercaptopurine (6-MP), where MTX was successfully validated with patient samples, confirming clinical relevance. An average relative recovery (RR%) of 93% confirmed the clinical feasibility of this approach and its applicability to real-world scenarios. These results highlight that a SERS-based platform with integrated sample cleaning has strong potential for point-of-care TDM.

Mechanisms of syngas production in deep inclined coal seams enabled by in situ thermochemical conversion technology
abstract: In situ thermochemical conversion technology (ITCC) provides a promising approach for the efficient in situ utilization of deep coal resources and has the potential to support low-carbon utilization when integrated with carbon capture, utilization, and storage. However, under realistic geological conditions, the coupled mechanisms governing syngas generation and cavity expansion remain insufficiently understood. In this study, field-scale data from the deepest ITCC pilot in China were integrated with a three-dimensional thermal-hydrological-mechanical-chemical coupled numerical model to investigate syngas production and cavity expansion in a deep inclined coal seam. The model reproduced the stage-dependent production behaviour of major gas components and captured the spatiotemporal development of the cavity. The simulated cavity volume of approximately 4000 m 3 agrees well with the water-injection inversion result, and the predicted expansion pattern is consistent with electromagnetic inversion. The results show that thermally driven gas redistribution, sustained high-temperature reactions, and permeability enhancement induced by coal degradation jointly control syngas generation and cavity expansion. This study not only supports the development of a potential low-carbon utilization pathway for deep coal resources, but also proposes an integrated industrial chain encompassing ITCC, surface processing, downstream utilization, and CCUS, including CO 2 -enhanced oil recovery, thereby providing a scientific basis for the development of low-carbon energy systems.

Degradation of organic micropollutants in urban tertiary treated wastewater by dielectric barrier discharge plasma: chemical removal and cyanobacteria toxicity reduction
abstract: Discharge of organic micropollutants (OMPs) from urban wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) poses a growing environmental concern, as effluents contain complex mixtures of pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). This study evaluated nonthermal dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma as a reagent-free advanced oxidation process (AOP) for OMP removal and ecotoxicity reduction in unspiked tertiary treated wastewater. Of 343 targeted compounds, 67 were detected; 15 of 28 quantified compounds exceeded the limit of quantification prior to treatment. At 16 kV, 30 min of plasma treatment achieved >90% removal of most quantified OMPs, including clarithromycin, carbamazepine, diclofenac, and venlafaxine, with a median electrical energy per order (EEO) of 4.8 kWh m −3 order −1 . Extending treatment to 90 min yielded no proportional improvement in removal efficiency. PFAS, particularly perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), were recalcitrant to DBD treatment under the conditions tested. The untreated effluent had an EC10 of 6.9 ± 1.1 relative enrichment factor (REF), whereas the EC10 exceeded 100 REF after treatment, corresponding to >93% reduction in cyanobacterial growth inhibition. Four antibiotics and herbicides explained 63.8% of the observed toxicity, with clarithromycin contributing 52.6%. All four compounds fell below detection or quantification limits after treatment. By integrating native OMP mixtures, energy demand, and biological effects, a more environmentally relevant picture of DBD plasma performance is provided than by chemical removal data alone. Broader validation across trophic levels and endpoints is necessary before conclusions on ecological safety or full-scale readiness can be drawn.

Regulating interfacial electronic structure in Fe2O3/g-C3N4 heterogeneous Fenton catalyst for efficient low-temperature flue gas denitrification
abstract: To overcome the challenges associated with low-temperature industrial flue gas denitrification, this study presents a highly efficient Fe2O3/g-C3N4 heterogeneous Fenton catalyst synthesized via a facile impregnation approach. This composite effectively activates H2O2 for deep NOx elimination. Under optimal alkaline conditions, the Fe2O3/g-C3N4 system achieved a remarkable maximum NOx removal efficiency of 93.2%, while demonstrating exceptional durability by retaining over 80% efficiency across five consecutive reaction cycles. Comprehensive experimental characterizations coupled with density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidated that g-C3N4 serves as an electron-rich reservoir. This framework systematically accelerates the rate-limiting Fe2+/Fe3+ redox cycling on the Fe2O3 surface through enhanced interfacial charge transfer. Crucially, the alkaline environment uniquely steered the reactive oxygen species (ROS) evolution pathway toward the highly selective generation of superoxide radicals (O2•-). These predominant O2•- species rapidly oxidized NO to form peroxynitrite intermediates, driving its deep conversion into valuable nitrate and nitrite resources. This work not only provides a robust and scalable strategy for low-temperature NOx purification, but also offers fundamental mechanistic insights into modulating radical selectivity through precise microenvironmental control.

title: Na-rich Na3.2V1.9Fe0.1O2(PO4)2F cathode unlocks high energy density and wide-temperature operation in sodium-ion batteries
Real-time quantification of sorption-enhanced CO2 hydrogenation to methanol over zeolite 4A
abstract: Sorption enhanced reaction processes (SERP) were successfully evaluated in the CO2 hydrogenation reaction, by leveraging the sorption benefits to enhance the formation of methanol. In this work, a dedicated experimental protocol and an analytical setup were developed to quantitatively investigate the coupling between reaction and sorption during the transient regime. This system enables the direct quantification of all molecules at the reactor outlet, including methanol and water, thus allowing an accurate real-time mass balance analysis and improved understanding of the phenomena occurring during sorption-enhanced operation. Experiments performed at 230°C and 30 bar using a Cu / ZnO / Al2O3 commercial catalyst combined with LTA zeolite (4A) demonstrated that sorption significantly enhances methanol production beyond the thermodynamic equilibrium predicted for a conventional reactor, while the impact on CO production remains limited. Substantial adsorption of both water and methanol within the zeolite framework was assessed. Indeed, the LTA sorbent exhibited a methanol sorption selectivity of 31%, which significantly enhanced the total methanol production during the sorption-enhanced effect. Indeed, 56% of the total methanol formed was temporarily retained within the zeolite, highlighting the key role of the methanol sorption in promoting CO2 hydrogenation with respect to the reverse water-gas shift reaction (RWGS), while water removal influences both reactions. As a result of this sorption-enhanced effect, the quantities of methanol and CO produced increased by 168% and 55%, respectively, compared with the reference experiment for a 60 min period. Structural characterization (XRD and 27Al MAS NMR) confirmed that the LTA zeolite framework remained stable after the experiment despite the harsh conditions of high pressure and temperature in the presence of steam.

Microstructure engineering of bimetal-doped carbon nanospheres for accelerated electrochemical nitrobenzene reduction
abstract: Transition metal-doped carbon nanospheres featuring well-defined nanoporous structures are promising electrocatalysts, however, integrating abundant metal active sites while maintaining structural integrity has remained a significant challenge for optimizing metal loading and catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report a template-free strategy to construct Co/Fe-bimetal-co-doped carbon nanospheres (xCoyFe@C) by carbonizing metal-incorporated resorcinol-formaldehyde resins (xCoyFe@RF) with various Fe/Co molar ratio, enabling precise microstructure engineering. Systematic investigations reveal that the iron precursor serves as a morphology-directing agent and, in concert with metal salt identity, dosage, precursor addition sequence, and reaction time, governs the polycondensation kinetics and structural evolution. A progressive transformation from solid to yolk-shell architectures is observed with increasing Fe/Co molar ratio, elucidating the pivotal role of bimetallic interactions in tailoring nanostructures. When evaluated for electrocatalytic nitrobenzene reduction, all bimetal-doped carbon materials exhibit enhanced activity relative to single-metal and metal-free counterparts. Notably, the yolk-shell 1Co1Fe@C achieves a superior conversion of 92.6% and 85.3% selectivity toward azoxybenzene. The improved performance is attributed to the synergistic effects between cobalt and iron species coupled with optimized porous architecture, which facilitates mass transport and active site accessibility. This work provides a versatile platform for designing cost-effective bimetal-doped carbon nanostructures and offers insights into structure-performance relationships for selective nitrobenzene hydrogenation.

title: Unraveling the stabilization mechanisms of CO₂-in-water fracturing foams under thermo-chemical variations: Experimental and molecular dynamics insights
abstract: CO₂-in-water (C/W) foam fracturing technology is widely used to enhance coalbed methane (CBM) recovery; however, elevated reservoir temperatures adversely affect foam stability, thereby diminishing recovery rates. This study examines how varying sodium dodecylbenzene sulfonate (SDBS) concentration can mitigate this temperature-induced decline in foam stability. The interfacial rheological properties and aging behavior of the foam were analyzed using an interfacial rheometer and a foam scanner, while molecular dynamics simulations were employed to investigate molecular interactions at the gas-liquid interface. Additionally, foam and solution conductivity measurements were conducted to monitor changes in surfactant concentration. The findings demonstrated that increasing the SDBS concentration mitigated the loss of foam stability caused by elevated temperatures, with the critical concentration exhibiting a positive correlation with temperature (e.g., 0.2 wt% at 65°C). At the molecular scale, elevated temperatures led to enhanced water diffusion, thereby decreasing the hydration and relative concentration of water molecules around the SDBS molecules and consequently altering the interaction energy. On a macroscopic level, elevated temperatures reduced surface tension, viscoelasticity, and foam stability, resulting in smaller foams, thinner liquid films, and lower conductivity. However, increasing the SDBS concentration effectively counteracted these detrimental effects on C/W foam stability. This research provides crucial theoretical insights for optimizing C/W foam fracturing fluids, thereby enhancing both CBM recovery efficiency and economic performance.

Manipulating the sizing behavior of polyamide-imide on carbon fibers by electrostatic interactions and enhancing the interfacial adhesion and mechanical properties of CFs/poly ether ether ketone composite laminates
abstract: Despite the widespread use of heat-resistant sizing agents in carbon fiber (CF)/polyether ether ketone (PEEK) composites, issues such as filament sticking, non-uniform infiltration, and incomplete impregnation persist, hindering continuous compounding of large-tow CFs with high-viscosity melt. Herein, by incorporating various potential regulators during polyamide-imide (PAI) sizing, the uptake and spatial distribution of PAI are effectively tailored via modulating electrostatic interactions among CFs, PAI, and PRs. Specifically, electrostatic attraction between cationic cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and anionic PAI reduces the PAI adsorption rate onto the positively charged CF, enabling smooth adsorption kinetics that yields a thin, uniform coating with optimal uptake, suppressing aggregation and sticking. Consequently, the CTAB-regulated CF/PEEK composite exhibits an interfacial shear strength of 89.4 MPa (132% increase), with tensile and flexural strengths of 1005.4 MPa and 1425.3 MPa, respectively. In contrast, the co-adsorption of anionic sodium dodecyl sulfate and PAI onto CF surface triggers intense adsorption kinetics, destabilizing the PAI sizing. This led to excessive local enrichment, uneven coating, and filament sticking, which hindered impregnation of the CFs by the PEEK melt and ultimately compromised interfacial and mechanical properties of the composite. And the nonionic octoxinol exertes a physical barrier effect that moderately limited PAI adsorption, thereby facilitating a more controlled sizing process and promoting effective impregnation as well as interfacial adhesion during the formation of composite. This work offers a new perspective for achieving complete impregnation and uniform coating of heat-resistant sizing agents on CFs without compromising fiber spreadability, paving the way toward high-performance and scalable CF/PEEK composites.

title: Plastic waste to sustainable aviation fuel: Enabling circular economy through integrated techno-economic, environmental, and waste management assessment
abstract: Aviation decarbonization requires scalable low-carbon fuel pathways, yet sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production remains constrained by feedstock availability. Converting plastic waste to SAF addresses both challenges. This study presents integrated techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) of plastic waste-to-SAF (PW-SAF) processes across five plastic types (LDPE, HDPE, PP, PS, and PET). Polyolefin-derived SAF demonstrates unit production costs (UPC) ranging from 1.04 to 1.21 $/kg, competitive with established SAF pathways, and net CO2 emission (NCE) intensities ranging from 13.7 to 19.1 gCO2eq/MJ, representing 42 to 58% reductions relative to the EU RED II threshold of 32.9 gCO2eq/MJ. SAF derived from aromatic plastics shows higher UPC (1.51 to 1.96 $/kg) and NCE (18.8 to 26.2 gCO2eq/MJ), yet remains viable while complying with regulatory requirements. Waste management emission (WME) ranging from 0.65 to 0.79 kgCO2eq/kg represents approximately 70% reductions compared to incineration (1.9 to 2.6 kgCO2eq/kg). These findings demonstrate that PW-SAF transforms plastic waste from a disposal liability into a decarbonization asset for aviation, establishing a new SAF pathway while delivering substantial environmental gains. Polyolefin-derived SAF achieves the highest integrated performance across economic, energy, and environmental metrics with an overall score of 4.45.

Low-temperature roll-coatable particle-free Cu–urushiol metallo-polymer coatings for breathable antibacterial and antiviral mask-derived nonwovens
abstract: Breathable nonwoven textiles for protective and hygiene applications require antimicrobial coatings that combine rapid pathogen inactivation with low-temperature processability, strong adhesion, thermal robustness, preserved porosity, and acceptable biological safety. Herein, we report a roll-coatable, particle-free, bio-derived Cu–urushiol metallo-polymer coating enabled by copper 2-ethylhexanoate, which transforms urushiol into a robust crosslinked coordination network through accelerated thermal curing at ≤100 °C. In this system, copper is retained within the cured matrix as highly dispersed mixed-valence Cu+/ Cu2+—O coordination sites rather than as free metal or metal-oxide particles, thereby creating a contact-active antimicrobial and antiviral interface. Spectroscopic analyses reveal that in situ Cu–catechol complexation drives a coordination-assisted redox pathway that promotes oxidative polymerization while stabilizing copper within the hybrid network. Direct roll coating further demonstrates that this formulation produces a strongly adhered, particle-shedding-resistant, and thermally robust coating on porous, heat-sensitive nonwoven fabrics without blocking the fibrous microstructure. The optimized coatings achieve ≥99.9% reduction of Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Bacillus cereus within 2 h and exhibit strong antiviral activity, including 99.773% reduction of influenza A (H1N1). Whereas raw urushiol lacquer shows severe cytotoxicity with cell viability below 30%, Cu–urushiol coatings display significantly improved cytocompatibility, with most formulations maintaining >80% viability. These results establish a scalable low-temperature coating strategy for durable, breathable, and contact-active antimicrobial textiles.

Dextranase-loaded pH and near-infrared dual-responsive Cu2O-embedded mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles for biofilm disruption and microecology-friendly caries prevention
abstract: Dental caries remains a significant public health challenge due to the persistent presence of cariogenic biofilms. Cuprous oxide nanoparticles (Cu₂O NPs) show promise in inhibiting biofilm formation; however, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) form a robust barrier that limits nanoparticle penetration and diminishes their anti-caries effectiveness. To address this, we loaded dextranase (DEX) onto Cu₂O-embedded periodic mesoporous organosilica (PMO) nanoparticles (Cu₂O-PMO@DEX/PEG NPs), which integrate enzymatic EPS hydrolysis, pH-triggered release of copper ions, and near-infrared (NIR) photothermal therapy, providing a multifaceted approach to overcome biofilm barriers. Cu₂O-PMO@DEX/PEG NPs exhibited potent activity against S. mutans , achieving a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) value of 78.125 μg/mL, corresponding to an effective Cu₂O dose of ~5.4 μg/mL. In a rat caries model, Cu₂O-PMO@DEX/PEG NPs achieved caries-preventive efficacy comparable to chlorhexidine (CHX). The 16S rRNA sequencing showed that the system suppressed pathogenic taxa, preserved commensal flora, without the enrichment of antimicrobial-resistance-associated taxa observed in the CHX group, demonstrating superior microecological compatibility compared with CHX-induced dysbiosis. Biosafety of this system was confirmed by cytotoxicity testing and in vivo histopathological evaluation. This work establishes a strategy to combat cariogenic biofilm barriers and provides a microecology-friendly design foundation for next-generation caries prevention materials.

Mild pyrolysis-derived asymmetrically coordinated cobalt single-atom catalyst for ampere-level H2O2 electrosynthesis
abstract: High-temperature pyrolysis (>700 ℃) is generally applied for synthesis of carbon-supported single-atom catalysts, thus suffering from the aggregation/agglomeration of single metal atoms and limited coordination engineering because only very few hetero-atomic species could survive the harsh treatment. Herein we report a mild pyrolysis strategy to synthesize single-atom catalyst by applying a mild annealing temperature of 400 ℃ to metal-impregnated hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) precursor, delivering a highly efficient single-atom catalyst (CoN3O1-Nax/C) for electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). The mild pyrolysis produces rich N/O-containing species to form asymmetrically coordinated Co single-atom moieties with planar hetero-coordination (N3O1) and axial N-ligation. The electronic structure of Co atoms was synergistically regulated in such asymmetrically coordination, leading to optimal *OOH binding strength situating near the activity volcano apex. CoN3O1-Nax/C achieves 81.6% Faradaic efficiency (FE) for H2O2 electrosynthesis at industrial-level current of 830 mA cm-2 in gas diffusion electrode (GDE), and maintains >90% FE over 32 h at 200 mA cm-2. This work paves a mild route to synthesis of single-atom catalysts while offering great possibility of coordination engineering for advanced electrocatalysis.

abstract: Glycerol is an underutilized waste product that is abundantly available from the biodiesel industry. Electrocatalytic oxidation of glycerol (GOR) to formate offers an environmentally friendly and cost-effective approach to valorizing glycerol. In this study, we have developed new types of metal-doped cobalt metal-organic frameworks, which are grown directly on a carbon matrix via a one-pot synthesis as electrocatalyst precursors. In-depth structural analysis has revealed that, in the Ni-doped cobalt MOF, Ni substitutes a fraction of Co sites isomorphically, forming isolated Ni(II) centers, while Cu is present as a mixture of Cu(II) and metallic Cu, with the majority in the oxidized form as highly dispersed species and a small fraction forming nanoparticles. These materials were then subjected to a controlled potential-induced surface reconstruction to produce mixed-metal oxide/oxyhydroxide-like environments interconnected through M-O-M motifs, the extent of the reconstruction depending strongly on the dopant metal. The metal-doped derivatives were tested as electrocatalysts for the alkaline electrooxidation of glycerol using in-house designed electrochemical reactors with different cell configurations and operating modes. We demonstrated that metal-doped derivative phases exhibit improved electrocatalytic activity for GOR compared to the monometallic counterpart. These catalysts yield significant glycerol conversion rates under single-pass operation, with improved Faradaic efficiencies towards formate (up to 70%) and low energy consumption (< 320 kWh kmol −1 ), while suppressing the complete oxidation of glycerol to carbonate or CO 2 . This work provides new insight into the rational design of metal-doped MOF derivatives as highly active and selective electrocatalysts for the practical glycerol valorization.

abstract: In this study, a casein (CAS)-based dual-mode smart film was developed by incorporating pyridine-modified black soybean seed coat anthocyanins (mBSSC) and ZIF-67 for real-time freshness monitoring and preservation of chilled mutton. The mBSSC/ZIF-67 hybrid was uniformly dispersed within the CAS matrix, producing a compact structure with good integrity and satisfactory mechanical performance. Among the formulations, CAS/mBSSC/Z2 provided the best balance between functional performance and material economy. Compared with neat CAS, mBSSC/ZIF-67 reduced water vapor permeability from 12.4 × 10 −11 to 6.2 × 10 −11 (g·m −1 s −1 m 2 ·Pa −1 ) while improving water resistance, antioxidant capacity, and antibacterial activity. During refrigerated storage, the optimized film enabled dual-mode monitoring through visible color evolution under ambient light and fluorescence activation under 365 nm ultraviolet (UV) irradiation, with fluorescence “turn-on” occurring at approximately Day 6. The colorimetric mode enables convenient routine observation, whereas the high-contrast fluorescence mode facilitates detection in low-light or dark environments and can provide rapid confirmatory screening using a portable UV source. CAS/mBSSC/Z2 also retarded mutton spoilage, delaying time required for total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) to reach 15 mg/100 g until approximately Day 10 and limiting the final microbial load to 8.8 log CFU/g, compared with 12.6 log CFU/g in the Z1 group. Furthermore, the films showed substantial disintegration and mass loss under the tested soil-burial and seawater conditions. These findings identify the film as a multifunctional platform integrating barrier enhancement, preservation, and complementary colorimetric-fluorescence sensing.

title: Unlocking dual-site regulation in perovskite-modified separators for efficient polysulfide conversion in lithium-sulfur batteries
Topological planarization toward dielectric loss regulation
abstract: Dielectric polymers with low dissipation factor (Df) have significant application value in high-frequency communication technology. Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) has the lowest Df among dielectric polymers and plays an irreplaceable role in high-frequency communication materials. However, existing methods for Df regulation cannot further reduce its Df to meet the development needs of high-frequency communication technology. Herein, through theoretical calculations, it is firstly confirmed that the rotational polarization of fluorinated groups induced by the conformation change results in the Df formation of PTFE. Subsequently, on the basis of the topological planarization concept, a two-dimensional PTFE named highly oriented fluorinated graphene (HOFG) has been proposed to regulate fluorinated groups’ conformation, which is fabricated by atomic fluorination. It is demonstrated that HOFG contains highly oriented and symmetrically distributed C-F bonds and a fixed conformation, leading to restrained rotational polarization of fluorinated groups. Furthermore, the conformation regulation ability of HOFG could spill over to the interface region in HOFG/PTFE composites, forming a planarized area of PTFE molecules with a thickness of 3–20 Å and inhibiting the rotational polarization of PTFE chains around HOFG sheets. Thus, HOFG and HOFG/PTFE composites achieve record-low Df values of 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ and 1.2 × 10⁻⁴, respectively. These findings provide new insights into Df regulation.

abstract: Pore-defined metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and MOF-enabled materials have emerged as versatile electrocatalytic platforms because multiscale porosity can be integrated with chemically programmable active sites. This review establishes a two-dimensional framework that distinguishes the material state — intact or reconstructed MOFs, MOF-based composites, and MOF-derived materials — from the dominant active-site motif, including nanoparticles, nanoclusters, single atoms, and heterointerface-coupled hybrid sites. We first differentiate the functions of micropores, mesopores, and macropores in molecular enrichment, solvated-species transport, active-site accessibility, and gas management, and explain why hierarchical porosity is advantageous only when pore connectivity, tortuosity, and interfacial chemistry are jointly optimized. Representative systems for the hydrogen evolution reaction, oxygen evolution reaction, oxygen reduction reaction, nitrate reduction reaction, and carbon dioxide reduction reaction are then critically assessed. Particular attention is given to separating transport and confinement effects from changes in composition, defects, coordination environments, conductivity, and operando reconstruction. Selected reported performance metrics and test conditions are summarized. Finally, key challenges in controllable synthesis, structural stability, quantitative structure-activity relationships, standardized reporting, scale-up, and the integration of operando characterization, theoretical simulation, and data-driven discovery are discussed.

abstract: Lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxide (LRMO) cathodes face significant challenges to their commercial viability, including structural degradation, progressive capacity fade, slow kinetics, and severe irreversible oxygen evolution. While individual strategies, such as transition metal doping and surface modification, have been shown to mitigate certain issues, they often lead to a compromise in material capacity. In this study, we propose a novel surface reconstruction strategy, wherein a lithium sulfate (Li2SO4) layer is applied to the cathode surface. This layer effectively suppresses side reactions between the electrode and electrolyte while enabling the sulfate ions (SO42-/SO32-) to participate in redox reactions, thereby enhancing the overall capacity. Moreover, this method induces oxygen vacancies, reduces particle size, and facilitates the incorporation of S2- anions into the bulk structure. The generated oxygen vacancies improve conductivity, ion mobility, and carrier concentration, while reducing the oxidation state of nickel and cobalt. This contraction of the lattice, resulting from weaker electrostatic repulsion, alleviates mechanical stress during cycling. During the calcination process, the Li2SO4 coating prevents the agglomeration of primary particles, thus reducing average particle size, shortening the Li⁺ diffusion path, and enhancing electrochemical performance. After 400 cycles at 1 C, the modified cathode exhibits a remarkable capacity retention rate of 95.79%, with an initial reversible capacity of 282.44 mAh g-1 at 0.1 C. These findings provide a strategic framework for enhancing the performance of next-generation high-performance cathode materials.

A multiscale self-assembling electrolyte system for stable zinc-ion batteries: Hydrogen-bond network reconfiguration and dynamic interface engineering
abstract: The practical application of aqueous zinc-ion batteries is hindered by interfacial instability at the Zn anode and degradation at the cathode. Herein, the bio-derived naringin is introduced as a multifunctional electrolyte architect, which spontaneously constructs a hierarchical electrolyte system in ZnSO4 solution through dynamic and multiscale self-assembly. This unique system comprises soluble molecules, nano-colloids, and micro/macro-scale supramolecular complexes in equilibrium, enabling spatiotemporally decoupled yet synergistic regulation. Naringin-derived species reconfigure the bulk hydrogen-bond network and weaken Zn2+-H2O interaction, suppressing water activity. On the Zn anode, they pre-deposit to guide uniform nucleation and form a robust hybrid solid electrolyte interphase for dendrite-free plating. On the MnO2 cathode, they induce the formation of a cathode electrolyte interphase. This multiscale system maintains lower and more stable pH, mitigates Mn dissolution, suppresses byproducts, and inhibits Jahn-Teller active Mn3+ formation. Consequently, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell achieves stability exceeding 4800 h at 1 mA cm-2, while the Zn||MnO2 full cell delivers 84.2% capacity retention after 4000 cycles at 0.8 A g-1. This work establishes multiscale self-assembling electrolyte engineering as a powerful strategy for stabilizing both electrodes in aqueous batteries.

abstract: The development of deep-blue organic emitters that simultaneously satisfy the stringent BT.2020 color gamut standard (0.131, 0.046) and achieve high electroluminescence efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we demonstrate that regioisomerism engineering of intramolecular weak interactions provides a powerful strategy to address this issue. By altering the pyridine N‐atom position, the resulting emitter oPTPH uniquely establishes synergistic through‐space n–π interactions and C–H···N hydrogen bonding, forming a dual non‐covalent conformational lock that rigidifies the molecular scaffold, suppresses vibrational relaxation, and promotes hybridized local and charge‐transfer excited state. Theoretical analyses provide direct evidence for these synergistic interactions. A doped device based on oPTPH achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency of 6.58% with CIE coordinates of (0.158, 0.038), closely approaching the BT.2020 deep‐blue standard. The near‐degenerate S1–T4/T5 energy gaps revealed by theoretical calculations, together with the nanosecond decay and linear current density–luminance relationship, support the operation of hot‐exciton reverse intersystem crossing mechanism. This work establishes regioisomerism engineering of weak interactions as viable conformational design tool for achieving BT.2020‐compliant deep‐blue OLEDs with high efficiency and excellent color purity.

abstract: Metallic monolithic substrates are emerging as a next-generation platform for structured catalysts due to their high thermal conductivity, mechanical robustness, and excellent mass-transfer characteristics. Here, metal honeycomb monoliths based on 17–4PH, 316 L, and Inconel 718 alloys were fabricated by fused deposition modeling (FDM)-based metal additive manufacturing (AM) and employed as support for NiO-CeO 2 nanoparticulate catalysts in CO 2 methanation reaction. Particular emphasis was placed on correlating the microstructural, mechanical, thermal, and corrosion properties of the printed alloys with their suitability as catalytic supports. Although all monoliths exhibited thermal expansion coefficients close to those of fully dense alloys, markedly lower flexural Young's modulus and hardness (HRB) values were obtained because of the residual porosity and microstructural heterogeneity inherent to the FDM printing and sintering route. These results underline the high sensitivity of the mechanical properties to incomplete densification in additively manufactured metals, while still providing sufficient mechanical integrity for catalyst handling, coating and stable operation under the CO 2 methanation reaction conditions investigated in this work. H 2 -TPR, TEM, and XPS analyses confirmed that catalytic behavior was governed by the NiO-CeO 2 active phase and remained essentially independent of the metallic substrate, resulting in comparable catalytic activity and methane selectivity among the three alloys. In contrast, accelerated corrosion tests revealed pronounced alloy-dependent durability, with 316 L providing the most favorable balance between oxidation resistance, mechanical stability, and material cost. These results demonstrate the potential of metal additive manufacturing to produce robust and application-oriented catalytic monoliths for CO 2 conversion under harsh industrial conditions.

abstract: This study focuses on the design and assessment of a photocatalytic solar-based flat reactor for water purification. It consists of a stainless-steel multi-step cascade solar reactor (MSCR) of 5 L coupled with two independent and removable sets of stairs coated with TiO2-P25 suspensions at 100 and 200 g/L. The performance was assessed by simultaneously monitoring the inactivation of E. coli (106 CFU/mL initial concentration) and the removal of three organic microcontaminants (OMCs) (imidacloprid, sulfamethoxazole, and trimethoprim at 100 µg/L each) in isotonic water. Boundary processes (including dark and solar-only radiation) and the influence of different water flow rates (140 and 340 L/min) were also investigated. Results demonstrated no significant differences between both catalysts and different flow rates, with removal of >5 Log of E. coli and >80% of ∑OMCs with solar UV-doses of 191 and 235 kJ/m² (90 and 105 min treatment time). A disinfection kinetic rate enhancement compared to solar-only treatment of 2.5 and 2.0 times was achieved with each set of stairs. The stability of the immobilized TiO2 layer was also assessed, and a slight decrement in roughness and thickness was observed; however, any TiO2 release was detected after 52 and 76 hours of operation; as well as treated water showed no toxicological effects against Aliivibrio fischeri.

Oxygen etching-modulated defect-dependent pore structure of hard carbon for enhanced sodium-ion storage performance
abstract: Hard carbon (HC), a highly promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries, faces critical bottlenecks in improving sodium storage performance, primarily due to challenges in the precise construction of closed pore structures and the targeted regulation of carbon defects. To address this issue, a defect-oriented mild oxygen etching (DMOE) strategy is proposed to achieve synergistic optimization of the microstructure and sodium storage performance of hard carbon. Based on the resin intermediates generated by medium-temperature carbonization, combined with the DMOE strategy, the carbon-oxygen radicals are effectively localized around defect sites, enabling directional regulation of sub-nanometer pores and microstructures. The optimized hard carbon material achieves a reversible specific capacity of 405.2 mAh g-1, with a platform capacity of 303.1 mAh g-1 and an initial coulombic efficiency of 90.4%. Long-term cycling stability is demonstrated by a retained capacity of 226.1 mAh g-1after 800 cycles at a current density of 1 A g-1. This study elucidates the defect-mediated closed pore formation mechanism and the structure-property relationship of hard carbon for sodium storage, providing a feasible design strategy for the controllable preparation of high-performance hard carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries.

title: Energy-efficient reverse water gas shift reaction in a gliding arc plasmatron
abstract: The reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a key process for CO₂ valorization, enabling the production of CO-rich syngas for downstream synthesis. We investigated a gliding arc plasmatron (GAP) reactor for efficient, catalyst-free RWGS conversion, with emphasis on thermodynamic understanding and process optimization. We systematically varied the H₂:CO₂ ratio (0.25–4), discharge power (600–1200 W), and total flow rate (7–20 SLPM), corresponding to a specific energy input (SEI) range of 2.3–6.4 kJ·L⁻¹. Our results demonstrate outstanding performance, achieving a maximum CO₂ conversion of 93% under H₂-rich conditions (H₂:CO₂ = 4) with 100% CO selectivity across all operating conditions. At stoichiometric conditions (1:1), the conversion saturates at ~68%, which closely matches the thermodynamic equilibrium limit of the RWGS reaction at ~2000 K and atmospheric pressure, indicating that the process is not kinetically but only thermodynamically limited. The lowest energy cost of 264 kJ·mol-CO⁻¹ is obtained at an SEI of 3 kJ·L⁻¹. Benchmarking against other plasma technologies shows that the GAP reactor greatly outperforms dielectric barrier discharge systems and demonstrates superior or comparable performance to other warm plasma reactors. These findings establish GAP reactors as a promising platform for energy-efficient RWGS and highlight the importance of thermodynamic constraints in GAP reactor design, providing suggestions for further process optimization.

Gradient-magnetized conductive nerve conduits enable enhanced wireless electrical stimulation for peripheral nerve regeneration
abstract: Enhancing peripheral nerve regeneration without implanted power sources remains a major clinical challenge due to the difficulty of delivering sustained, localized bioelectrical stimulation in a minimally invasive manner. Herein, we report a gradient-magnetized conductive nerve conduit (G-MNC) with layered polycaprolactone (PCL) architecture and Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles concentrated at both ends. Under an alternating magnetic field from a Helmholtz coil, the gradient magnetic configuration enhances electromagnetic induction and establishes a homogeneous stimulation environment. Compared with a uniformly magnetized conduit (U-MNC), the G-MNC generates 22.5% higher induced current and a stable endogenous electric field gradient along the conduit axis. In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, the G-MNC significantly accelerated peripheral nerve regeneration. At 12 weeks post-implantation, it exhibited a 15.3% increase in myelinated axon area fraction (70.72 ± 3.20%) and an 11.1% increase in muscle fiber diameter (72.36 μm) versus U-MNC group. Mechanistically, the gradient electromagnetic microenvironment promotes directional Schwann cell migration and axonal maturation, with 13.2% upregulation of β-tubulin expression, leading to enhanced muscle reinnervation and improved functional recovery. Overall, gradient magnetization coupled with electromagnetic superposition enables spatiotemporally homogeneous neuromodulation, offering a promising strategy for wireless bioelectronic peripheral nerve repair and the clinical translation of remotely activated regenerative therapies.

abstract: The pollution of water systems by emerging contaminants (ECs) has caused severe environmental and human health impacts, necessitating the development of advanced nanomaterials to remove them from water efficiently. This study fabricated 3D hollow carbon nanospheres (HCNSs) utilising a water-in-oil (W/O) microemulsion method. In a novel approach, the adsorptive performance of HCNSs was compared with that of their corresponding resorcinol-formaldehyde hollow nanospheres (RF-HNSs) to assess the effect of carbonisation on adsorption behaviour. The hollow spherical nanostructure and textural properties were determined by electron microscopy and N 2 /CO 2 adsorption-desorption experiments, respectively. The HCNS-800 (carbonised at 800 °C) had an outer diameter of 52 ± 7 nm and a shell thickness of 6 ± 1 nm and exhibited a surface area of 1225 m 2 g −1 , significantly higher than those of HCNS-600 (600 m 2 g −1 ) and RF-HNSs (1.8 m 2 g −1 ). The adsorptive performance of the materials was evaluated against acetaminophen (ACT), atenolol (ATE), carbamazepine (CBZ), and lamivudine (LMD) using batch adsorption experiments. HCNS-800 demonstrated superior adsorption performance toward the target pharmaceuticals due to its larger accessible adsorption surface. The material exhibited high maximum adsorption capacities ranging from 60.3 mg g −1 to 155.9 mg g −1 , and adsorption equilibrium was rapidly reached within 6–15 min. The estimated costs for removing 1.0 g of ACT, ATE, CBZ, and LMD from water were USD 64.29, USD 35.10, USD 45.41, and USD 90.74, respectively, with the five-cycle reusability factored in. These findings demonstrate that HCNSs are promising, sustainable, and cost-effective adsorbents for removing pharmaceutical contaminants from water.
