A ternary logic inverter based on tribotronic transistor and its application in digital combination lock
abstract: Multi-valued logic (MVL) circuits hold great promise for applications in memory and cryptosystems due to their high information density and reduced system complexity. However, traditional transistor-based MVL circuits require external gate voltage supply, which complicates their design and increases their physical footprint. In this study, we present a ternary logic inverter based on tribotronic transistor and demonstrate its application for mechanical displacement activated high-storage-density digital combination lock, which is capable of storing 3 n passwords through direct key-pressing without applying gate voltage. The basic ternary logic unit is constructed by connecting a WSe₂ transistor in series with a WSe₂/MoS₂ heterojunction transistor, which demonstrates negative differential transconductance, exhibits an impressive retention time of up to 10,000 s, and maintains stable rewrite capabilities for over 100 cycles. When integrated with a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) to construct a tribotronic device, the ternary logic unit can be triggered directly by mechanical displacement. Moreover, a 3 × 3 array of ternary logic units can store 19,683 unique passwords by varying the TENG displacement. Our findings provide a straightforward strategy for developing high-storage-density digital combination lock activated by mechanical displacement, improving information assurance, and reducing the footprint.

title: Wave-adaptive floating platform for hybrid triboelectric-electromagnetic energy harvesting toward marine IoT systems
abstract: Ocean wave energy harvesting based on triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) holds great promise, yet the industrial application necessitates advancements in manufacturing and environmental adaptability. Here, a triboelectric-electromagnetic hybrid generator designed for an energy-harvesting floating bridge (EB-TEMG) is proposed. The TENG component is fabricated using fully encapsulated 3D printing, while the integrated electromagnetic generator (EMG) component efficiently harvests mechanical energy during device operation. Furthermore, a tuned float whose length is matched to the dominant wavelength maximizes pitch motion for efficient wave energy capture. Multiple EB-TEMG units can be interconnected via hinges to form an energy-harvesting floating bridge, offering a scalable alternative to meter-scale device designs while seamlessly integrating infrastructure with clean energy harvesting. The device exhibits excellent output performance across a broad frequency range (0.5–2 Hz), with peak powers of 10.91 mW (TENG component) and 51.32 mW (1 coil in EMG component). Additionally, the device shows only a 6% decay in the output of the TENG component after 324,000 cycles in a linear motor. The EB-TEMG can not only power small electronics but also enable continuous real-time wireless transmission of marine data, thereby contributing to the further development of Marine Internet of Things (IoT) systems.

Rapid biphasic synthesis of phosphatidylglycerol by phospholipase D in an oscillatory baffled reactor
abstract: Phospholipase D (PLD)-catalyzed transphosphatidylation offers a mild route to functional phospholipids, but implementation is limited by poor substrate accessibility, long batch times and poorly controlled liquid–liquid interfaces. Here, we established a formulation-controlled biphasic platform for converting phosphatidylcholine (PC) to phosphatidylglycerol (PG) in a 250 mL oscillatory baffled reactor (OBR). The study integrates formulation screening, operational kinetics, reactor benchmarking and multiscale characterization. A toluene-rich mixed organic solvent enabled high PC loading, while an organic-to-water ratio of 1:3 and a PLD loading of 0.1 wt% performed best among the tested conditions. In operational benchmarking, the OBR achieved the highest PG formation within 120 min and the most uniform dispersion, while its estimated nominal power density was of the same order of magnitude as that of the Applikon reactor. Its resolved-droplet apparent interfacial area density was approximately 11-fold and threefold higher than those of the beaker and Applikon systems, respectively. Under the selected OBR conditions, PG accounted for 96.14% and 99.26% of the quantified PC–PG pool after 60 and 120 min, respectively, while apparent PA formation was 0.34% after 120 min. Microscopy, ATR-FTIR and SAXS/WAXS further revealed phase-ratio-dependent differences in microscale aggregation, local phospholipid environments and lamellar organization. These results demonstrate how organic-phase design and reactor-generated dispersion can be jointly engineered to intensify high-loading biphasic lipid biocatalysis.

A one-stone-three-birds strategy: Manipulating sodiation depth of SnTe anode enabling fast ion conduction, shuttle avoidance, and sodium replenishment for durable sodium-ion batteries
abstract: SnTe is a promising anode material for sodium-ion batteries, yet its practical application is severely hindered by polytelluride shuttling and substantial volume expansion. Herein, the reaction mechanism and capacity fading mechanism of bulk SnTe in an ether-based electrolyte are first systematically elucidated, revealing that the desodiation of Na2Te to form soluble polytellurides occurs at a considerably higher potential than that of NaxSn desodiation. Based on this key insight, a strategy is proposed to precisely control the desodiation depth by adjusting the charging cutoff potential, thereby avoiding the further oxidation of Na2Te into soluble polytellurides while preserving it in situ as a functional additive that simultaneously enables three beneficial functions. The in-situ-formed Na2Te serves as a fast-ion-conducting skeleton that facilitates Na+ transport and buffers volume expansion, whereas the suppression of polytelluride generation largely mitigates the shuttle effect. Moreover, in full-cell configurations, Na2Te acts as a sodium reservoir to replenish the cathode when active sodium is consumed by side reactions. Consequently, the SnTe anode maintains a stable capacity of 299.6 mAh g-1 after 1000 cycles, corresponding to a high retention of 97.3%, while the full cell delivers 77.2 mAh g-1 after 2000 cycles at 2 A g-1 with an impressive retention of 88.2%. This work establishes a new strategy of in-situ conversion for multifunctional stabilization for conversion-type anode materials.

From mixed battery waste to next-generation cathode: A green co-precipitation route for LMFP from spent LMO/NCA and LFP streams
abstract: Spent lithium-ion battery cathodes are an increasingly important waste stream as regulations such as the EU Battery and Waste Batteries Regulation drive recycled content in new cells. However, mixed waste cathodes have received little attention for direct upcycling into next-generation materials. Here we demonstrate a co-precipitation synthesis of olivine-type LiMn₀.₅Fe₀.₅PO₄ (LMFP) produced from waste leachates of a blended LiMn 2 O 4 /LiNi 0.8 Co 0.15 Al 0.05 O 2 (LMO/NCA) cathode and a spent LFP cell. Using a scalable and simple ambient co-precipitation route where high-pressure reactors and toxic reducing agents are avoided. Mn 2+ is selectively recovered from the LMO/NCA cathode using ascorbic acid (1.25 M, 70 °C), while Fe 2+ and (PO₄) 3− are co-leached from spent LFP using dilute H₂SO₄ (0.5 M). Neutralisation of the combined leachates at ambient pressure (65 °C, pH 5) produces a hydrated Mn Fe phosphate precursor identified as a metaswitzerite-type phase ((Mn₀.₅Fe₀.₅)₃(PO₄)₂·4H₂O), which has been characterised by PXRD, TGA–DTA, and FTIR. Solid-state firing of this precursor with Li₃PO₄ and sucrose at 700 °C under Ar yields phase-pure LMFP (97.7 wt%), with a uniform carbon coating (2–4 nm) confirmed by TEM. Li half-cell electrochemical testing demonstrated clear Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ and Mn 2+ /Mn 3+ redox couples at 3.51/3.46 V and 4.09/3.99 V, respectively, a specific lithiation capacity of 97.4 mAh g −1 , and 97% capacity retention over 100 cycles. This proof-of-concept study establishes a simple, reagent-lean, ambient-pressure upcycling route applicable to the mixed cathode waste streams generated by first-generation EV fleets. Furthermore, the step-by-step characterisation of the Mn Fe precursor provides a mechanistic foundation for process optimisation to meet legislated recycled-content targets in next-generation battery manufacture. Synopsis This work advances the principle of “Wastes as Resources” by demonstrating that blended, mixed-chemistry EV battery waste streams, which are poorly served by conventional recycling routes, can be converted directly into a next-generation cathode material via a reagent-lean, ambient-pressure co-precipitation process. By combining Mn-rich leachate from spent LMO/NCA cells with iron- and phosphate-rich leachate from spent LFP cells, both waste streams are valorised simultaneously, supporting circular-economy targets and the recycled-content mandates of the EU Battery and Waste Battery Regulation.

abstract: Gas-fed electrochemical CO 2 reduction (CO 2 R) to multicarbon products is fundamentally constrained by mass-transport limitations that suppress selectivity and stability at industrially relevant current densities. Here, we demonstrate that these bottlenecks can be overcome by engineering a porous aerophilic polymer microenvironment around a simple Cu x O electrocatalyst without altering the intrinsic catalyst. By systematically replacing conventional PFSA ionomers with mixed aerophilic binders and applying a mild thermal treatment, we construct mechanically stabilized, gas-accessible overlayers that regulate the local gas-liquid microenvironment balance at the three-phase boundary (TPB). This approach drives a dramatic enhancement in ethylene production, increasing the partial current density from 135 mA cm −2 at 27 ± 5% Faradaic efficiency for Cu x O with PFSA ionomer to over 650 mA cm −2 at 65 ± 4% Faradaic efficiency upon incorporation of a porous and aerophilic FEP/PTFE overlayer. Comprehensive microscopy and spectroscopy reveal intimate polymer-catalyst integration and overlayer consolidation, while COMSOL multiphysics modeling links enhanced CO 2 availability to mitigated flooding rather than intrinsic kinetic acceleration. These results establish transport engineering as a powerful, catalyst-agnostic lever for advancing gas-phase electrosynthesis under high-rate operating conditions.

Decelerating in-situ polymerization kinetics for integrated quasi-solid-state lithium metal batteries
abstract: Here, we identify a critical, yet previously overlooked, detrimental effect arising from the excessively rapid kinetics of in-situ polymerized quasi-solid-state electrolytes (ISPEs). This phenomenon manifests through three primary limitations that hinder the practical realization of quasi-solid-state batteries: i) inhomogeneous Li-ion flux, ii) incomplete cathode–electrolyte interfacial contact, and iii) the formation of an undesirable, solvent-dominant native solid-electrolyte interphase (n-SEI) on the lithium metal anode. To address these fundamental constraints, we introduce the concept of a “polymerization decelerator”, which enables precise kinetic regulation of the in-situ polymerization process. Using a 1,3-dioxolane (DOL)-based ISPEs system as a model, density functional theory (DFT) calculations and time-resolved nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy elucidate the mechanistic origins of this kinetic retardation. Guided by these insights, we demonstrate that the decelerated polymerization simultaneously reinforces all three critical domains -bulk electrolyte transport and both the cathodic and anodic interfaces - ultimately leading to superior electrochemical performance. The versatility of this strategy is validated in Li||Li and Li||Cu cells, as well as Li||LiFePO4 full cells with stable operation demonstrated across coin, pouch, and cylindrical cell formats. This study establishes in-situ polymerization kinetics as a decisive, previously unrecognized design parameter for the realization of practical, high-performance quasi-solid-state lithium metal batteries.

Lymph node-targeted H2S-self-releasing multifunctional prodrug for the dual remodeling of immunological and redox homeostasis in autoimmune uveitis
abstract: Autoimmune uveitis is a vision-threatening disease where lymph nodes (LNs) are recognized as a key location of pathological imbalance. The dysfunction of the LNs aggravates immune imbalance, redox disturbance, and inflammation. Therefore, precise targeted therapy for restoring homeostasis of LNs may offer a new strategy for autoimmune uveitis. Herein, a multifunctional prodrug (Dex-BDATC-Dex) was fabricated by conjugating dexamethasone (Dex) with a trithiocarbonate-based linker, which self-assembles into 20 nm nanoparticles (named LNTMP) with a size that facilitates accumulation in LNs. This LNTMP is capable of redox-responsive release of Dex and in situ generation of hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S), triggered by redox microenvironment. It can effectively redirects macrophage polarization from the M1 to the M2 phenotype both in vitro and in vivo . In experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU) mice, LNTMP preferentially accumulates in LNs for at least 120 h and reverses the Th1/Th17/Treg imbalance. Futher studies confirm that LNTMP exhibits immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities, which effectively preserve retinal barrier integrity and alleviate EAU. Mechanistically, LNTMP acts by downregulating the ZBP1/RIPK3/NF-κB pathway. Collectivelly, this study presents a novel LN-targeting nanoplatform for the co-delivery of a corticosteroid and a gasotransmitter, thus offering a novel synergistic therapeutic strategy for autoimmune uveitis.

title: Effect of elemental electronegativity on the cyclic stability of V-based hydrogen storage alloys
abstract: Vanadium-based alloys possess high hydrogen storage capacities but suffer from severe cyclic decay. Herein, we demonstrate that the electronegativity difference between V and alloying elements (ΔχV-M) fundamentally governs local hydrogen distribution, thereby dictating phase evolution and cyclic stability. Specifically, alloying with Fe (ΔχV-M = −0.20) intrinsically weakens local H–metal interactions, giving rise to H-depleted regions. The resulting heterogeneous hydrogen distribution suppresses irreversible interstitial H trapping and spatially confines the phase transformation. Consequently, localized atomic rearrangement is effectively restricted, mitigating lattice mismatch and significantly reducing continuous capacity degradation. In contrast, alloying with Zr (ΔχV-M = +0.30), strengthens H–metal interactions, promotes local hydrogen enrichment, expands the phase transformation region, and accelerates cycling degradation. These findings reveal the pivotal role of electronegativity in regulating degradation behavior from an electronic-structure perspective and establish ΔχV-M as a practical design descriptor for developing highly cycle-stable hydrogen storage alloys.

Flexible and biodegradable pH fiber sensors for continuous monitoring of intestinal microenvironment in ulcerative colitis
abstract: Ulcerative colitis is characterized by chronic mucosal inflammation accompanied by dynamic alterations of the intestinal microenvironment. However, current clinical monitoring relies on intermittent and invasive examinations, limiting dynamic assessment of disease activity and therapeutic responses. Here, a biodegradable pH fiber sensor (BPFS) is developed for continuous in situ monitoring of intestinal luminal pH. The BPFS integrates a proton-responsive polyaniline sensing layer with a transient polymer fiber substrate, providing a sensitivity of 57 mV pH −1 , mechanical stability under repeated deformation, and an effective sensing lifetime of approximately two weeks. In vivo studies demonstrate accurate and stable pH sensing with excellent biocompatibility. Continuous monitoring reveals that luminal pH dynamics after 5-aminosalicylic acid treatment correlate with therapeutic outcomes, mucosal injury, epithelial barrier integrity, and inflammatory responses in DSS-induced colitis. These results establish BPFS as a platform for evaluating intestinal microenvironmental changes and therapeutic responses in ulcerative colitis.

abstract: Increasing industrial and agricultural activity has led to the widespread release of persistent pesticides like imidacloprid (IMD) and atrazine (ATZ), posing critical risks to human health and the environment. This study investigated the application of the Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) MIL-53(Fe) activated by UV-C radiation and persulfate (S 2 O 8 2− ) for the photocatalytic degradation of IMD and ATZ. The S 2 O 8 2− acted as a photo activator and precursor for different radical species, which possess high oxidizing potential. The MIL-53(Fe)/S 2 O 8 2− /UV-C system comprehensively characterized by XRD, FTIR, Raman Spectroscopy, FEG-SEM, TEM, XRF, DRS and electrochemical techniques. Under optimized conditions the proposed catalyst promoted 91% IMD and 75% ATZ degradation efficiencies in 60 min only. The catalyst also demonstrated robustness when applied in real water matrices, achieving about 80% and 60% removal in well and river water, respectively. A thorough analysis of the inorganic ions and scavengers showed that they mainly affected the formation of O 2 •- species. The MIL-53(Fe) exhibited excellent stability and reusability, maintaining a satisfactory performance over ten consecutive degradation cycles with negligible iron leaching, as confirmed by the post-reaction structural analysis, evidenced by the FTIR and XRD data. Furthermore, phytotoxicity assays conducted using Eruca sativa seeds and HPLC analyses confirmed a significant reduction of toxicity in the treated effluents. LC-MS/MS analysis identified various pesticide degradation products, showing strong agreement with theoretical Fukui indices calculated from Density Functional Theory. These results show that the MIL-53(Fe)/S 2 O 8 2− /UV-C system is a highly efficient and sustainable alternative technique for IMD and ATZ removal from contaminated water.

abstract: By using one-dimensional silk nanofibers (SNFs) as reinforcing agent and boron ions as a dynamic cross-linker, a multiscale interfacial engineering strategy was developed to prepare Ti3C2Tx/SNFs/boron (TSB-3) fiber electrode with excellent electrochemical performance and good flexibility. The introduction of SNFs with high-aspect-ratio suppressed the reassemble of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets, induced their ordered alignment, and reinforced the structure, while O-B-O covalent bond formation between boron ions in the coagulation bath and surface hydroxyl groups on Ti3C2Tx NSs constructed a conductive network and strengthened the interfacial interaction. Owing to the three-dimensional interconnected framework and well-organized structure, the as-prepared TSB-3 fiber electrode delivered a specific capacitance of 1610 F cm-3, retained 84% of its capacitance at 10 A cm-3, and exhibited an electrical conductivity of 3842 S cm-1. In addition, it showed a tensile strength of 241 MPa. The assembled all-solid-state TSB-3//PANI/rGO-7 asymmetrical fiber supercapacitor achieved a volume-specific capacitance of 529 F cm-3, with 86% capacitance retention after 10000 cycles, a voltage window of 1.2 V, and a volumetric energy density of 105.8 mWh cm-3 at a power density of 299.9 mW cm-3, while maintaining good flexibility. These results provide a useful strategy for balancing capacitance and flexibility in Ti3C2Tx-based fiber electrode materials.

Generative AI-guided conductive carbon-network regulation in heterogeneous carbon–ceramic composites for transient energy dissipation
abstract: Advanced pulsed-energy systems require dielectric materials that can dissipate transient electrical energy rapidly while resisting localized failure. Carbon–ceramic composites represent a typical heterogeneous ceramic dielectric in which conductive carbon networks, insulating ceramic skeletons and pores coexist across different length scales and jointly govern energy-dissipation behavior. However, carbon aggregation and nonuniform conductive-network distributions readily form locally percolated low-resistance pathways, causing current crowding, localized Joule heating and premature thermomechanical degradation. Such multiscale heterogeneity makes conventional trial-and-error optimization inefficient and also challenges generic data-driven models, which often fail to preserve phase occupancy, conductive connectivity and physical-response consistency under limited characterization data. Here, we propose a generative AI-guided framework for conductive carbon-network regulation in heterogeneous carbon–ceramic composites. A multiphase pseudo-RGB tensor encoding strategy is first developed to represent the carbon phase, ceramic skeleton and pore phase within a unified physically interpretable feature space. A WGAN-GP model constrained by physical-statistical descriptors is then used to expand the microstructure design space while preserving carbon fraction, spatial uniformity and agglomeration characteristics. A phase-field-informed optimization model further redistributes highly agglomerated carbon regions toward more uniform and multibranched conductive networks under mass-conservation, interfacial-regularization and spatial-smoothness constraints. Electrothermal–mechanical simulations and pulse-impact experiments demonstrate that the regulated carbon network suppresses current crowding and localized thermal accumulation, increasing the maximum permissible single-pulse absorbed energy density by approximately 78%. This work establishes a generative-AI route that links image-based microstructure characterization with conductive-network regulation for improved transient energy dissipation in heterogeneous ceramic composites.

abstract: Plasma-assisted deposition of thin dynamic covalent plasma polymer (DCPP) coatings based on benzoxazine chemistry is reported using a low-viscosity dual-polymerizable formulation. A multifunctional benzoxazine monomer containing ester, hydroxyl, and methacrylate groups was combined with 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) to enable sequential UV and thermal polymerization. A two-step curing strategy involving initial UV-induced free radical copolymerization was first studied using bulk model systems to predict the behavior of plasma-deposited coatings. The formulation was then processed by liquid-assisted atmospheric plasma polymerization (LA-APP), producing uniform coatings with thicknesses around 15 μm. Spectroscopic analyses showed that the plasma process preserved the essential structural features of the precursor, including benzoxazine rings and dynamic ester bonds. Consequently, the deposited films retained the ability to undergo further thermal polymerization, improving thermomechanical performance. The dynamic ester bonds also imparted self-healing, reversible adhesion, and controlled degradation properties. These findings demonstrate that plasma-induced polymerization can successfully translate vitrimer chemistry into functional thin coatings while maintaining dynamic covalent functionality, opening new opportunities for adaptive, repairable, and sustainable surface engineering applications.

Moderate reduction–induced spontaneous CoO anchoring on NiMo oxide electrodes for synergistic water dissociation and efficient bubble detachment in alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Hydrogen production via alkaline water electrolysis has been studied intensively but remains constrained by the additional water-dissociation step in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and by bubble accumulation that aggravates ohmic losses. We designed heterointerface catalysts, Ni-NiO-CoO on MoO3-x, and synthesized the materials via a spontaneous segregation driven by the varying decomposition kinetics of mixed molybdate precursors. This architecture results in hydrophilic cobalt oxide species, which promote bubble detachment and optimize OH and H2O binding energies. In half-cell HER tests (1 M KOH), the electrode results in overpotentials of 8 mV at 10 mA/cm2 and 57 mV at 100 mA/cm2 with a Tafel slope of 29 mV/dec. Notably, when integrated as the cathode in an anion-exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the electrode with an optimized loading of 3 mg/cm2 exhibits the current of 6.07 A/cm2 at 2.0 V and 80 oC, comparable to Pt/C benchmarks. In situ Raman spectroscopy visualizes that cobalt-induced hydrophilicity reduces adsorbed OH coverage and promotes water dissociation. In addition, in situ attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy analysis reveals suppressed bubble interference and increased free water at the Ni-NiO-CoO interface, confirming that these conditions facilitate water dissociation during alkaline HER. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggests that CoO promotes water activation, whereas the Ni-containing heterointerface tunes hydrogen binding strength toward thermoneutral values, consist with the experimentally obserbed enhancement in HER activity. These findings establish a practical, cost-effective pathway to accelerate alkaline HER via rational heterointerface design.

title: Effective pore-window engineering and packing densification of biomass-derived carbon cathodes for zinc-ion hybrid capacitors under high mass loading
Experimental study of microalgae chemical looping gasification with ilmenite, LD slag and iron sand in a 1.5 kWth unit
abstract: Chemical looping gasification (CLG) enables production of nitrogen-free syngas without need of air separation, thus offering a promising route for efficient biomass conversion. Microalgae, as a third-generation biofuel feedstock, present advantages in sustainability but pose challenges due to their high ash content. In this study, ilmenite, LD slag (a steelmaking byproduct from the Linz-Donawitz process), and iron sand were evaluated as oxygen carriers for microalgae CLG in a 1.5 kW th unit. The experiments were performed in various operating conditions and lasted 20–25 h with each oxygen carrier. Effects of key operational parameters including oxygen-to-biomass ratio (λ, 0.13–0.51), fuel reactor (FR) temperature (860–920 °C), and gasifying agent composition (H 2 O/CO 2 ratio, 100/0, 50/50 and 0/100) were investigated. The CLG performance was assessed with product gas composition, biomass conversion, carbon emitted from AR, syngas yield, cold gas efficiency, and tar formation that are essential for gasification processes. Oxygen carrier samples before and after the experimental campaigns were characterized with ICP-AES, XRD and SEM-EDX techniques to study changes in the physicochemical properties of the materials and their interactions with ash components of the microalgae. A TGA analysis was done to study the reactivity change of the materials during the campaign. Among the three materials, the LD slag exhibited the most promising overall performance. With this oxygen carrier, the syngas reached 1.5 Nm 3 /kg microalgae and the tar yield was suppressed to 0.5 g/kg. The outstanding performance with LD slag is deemed as a result of rich Ca content in the material, as calcium is a classical catalyst promoting gasification.

Interfacial assembly of bilayer plasmonic films with dynamic hotspot regulation for ultrasensitive surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy detection
abstract: Interfacial assembly of plasmonic nanostructures provides a versatile strategy for engineering Surface-enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) substrates, yet the fundamental mechanism governing multilayer SERS enhancement remains poorly understood. Here, we report interfacially assembled bilayer plasmonic films with precisely controlled Au nanoparticle layer numbers and uncover a previously unrecognized nonmonotonic enhancement behavior, in which the bilayer configuration unexpectedly outperforms both monolayer and multilayer counterparts through a dynamic hotspot regulation mechanism. The bilayer architecture exhibits optimal SERS performance, achieving ultralow limits of detection of 1.05 × 10 −14 M for crystal violet (CV) and 1.0 × 10 −11 M for paclitaxel (PTX) with excellent reproducibility (RSD < 5%). Time-resolved SERS measurements and Raman mapping reveal that solvent-driven analyte enrichment and interlayer nanogap evolution generate temporally stabilized plasmonic hotspots, producing a robust signal plateau window and establishing a direct structure–dynamics–performance relationship fundamentally distinct from conventional static hotspot amplification models. Benefiting from this mechanism, the bilayer films enable quantitative PTX detection in human serum with a limit of detection of 6.9 × 10 −10 M and show strong agreement with LC–MS analysis in 50 clinical samples (R 2 = 98.78%). Furthermore, in an orthotopic breast cancer mouse model, SERS-guided dose adjustment maintains antitumor efficacy while reducing systemic toxicity. This work not only provides insights into a previously unexplored mechanism of hotspot regulation in multilayer plasmonic assemblies but also provides a mechanistically guided interfacial engineering strategy for designing robust SERS substrates for ultrasensitive quantitative detection in complex biological environments.

Miniaturized yet scalable: A novel 3D-printed corrugated-sheet packing for laboratory distillation
abstract: Miniaturized laboratory distillation columns are highly attractive for process development and scale-up because they reduce energy demand, chemical consumption, holdup, and safety-related effort. However, further reducing the column diameter below the commonly recommended range of 40 mm to 50 mm worsens wall effects and aggravates the geometric and installation-related inhomogeneities of conventional corrugated-sheet packings. In this work, these drawbacks are analyzed and a novel additively manufactured corrugated-sheet packing for a DN20 laboratory column is presented. The new structure, termed the Corrugated Alternating Zigzag packing (CAZ-Pak), was developed by combining established corrugated-sheet packing principles with geometric design features enabled by additive manufacturing. These include homogeneous sheet termination, exact and repeatable inter-elemental mating, elimination of wall wipers, and orientation rings for precise and controlled stacking. The packings were manufactured from polyamide 12 by selective laser sintering and experimentally characterized under total reflux using the cyclohexane/n-heptane mixture at 900 mbar. Separation efficiency was evaluated in terms of HETP and NTSM . In DN20, the CAZ-Pak showed the highest average NTSM of the investigated additively manufactured packings together with a horizontal efficiency trend over the investigated vapor load range. In DN30, it exhibited a 27.5% higher average NTSM than Sulzer's DXM laboratory metal-sheet packing despite the moderately higher pressure drop. Moreover, the CAZ-Pak retained comparable performance in DN50, DN30, and DN20 columns, indicating favorable scalability characteristics for laboratory process development and scale-up.

abstract: Elucidating the impact of shaft configuration and wastewater flow velocity on the release of hazardous gases—specifically hydrogen sulfide (H2S)—during sewage transport is essential for mitigating environmental impacts and enhancing the safety of wastewater conveyance and treatment operations. This study employs a combined approach of ANSYS numerical simulations and laboratory-scale experiments to evaluate the performance of drop manholes configured with vertical pipe structures, siphon structures, and structureless (conventional) configurations. Experimental results demonstrate that under relatively unfavorable conditions, the mass transfer coefficients for H2S were 4.22×10-7m/s for the siphon structure, 8.00×10-7m/s for the vertical pipe structure, and 2.34×10-6m/s for the structureless shaft. Comparatively, the siphon structure exhibited the lowest H2S release rate, achieving a reduction of 16.29% relative to the standard curve. Our findings provide a scientific basis for the future design and optimization of drop manhole structures.

Geometry-driven near-zero foreshortening foldable 3D-printed PLA stent for paediatric coarctation of the aorta
abstract: Stent implantation is a widely accepted treatment for coarctation of the aorta (CoA); however, conventional metallic stents are non-degradable and lack design flexibility, limiting their application in paediatric patients. In this study, a foldable polylactide (PLA) stent fabricated via fused deposition modelling (FDM) is proposed, featuring a geometry-driven design that enables near-zero foreshortening during expansion. The stent architecture is based on a rotation-dominated deformation mechanism, in which the inclined strut elements undergo geometric reconfiguration, resulting in near-zero Poisson's ratio behaviour that is primarily governed by structural parameters rather than material properties. The effects of structural thickness and joint configuration on expansion stability and mechanical performance were systematically investigated. Experimental results show that the optimised thickness of 0.4 mm effectively suppresses structural distortion during balloon expansion. The stent expands from an initial diameter of 4.5 mm to 12 mm with negligible axial shortening and exhibits controlled recoil to 8.7–8.9 mm. Planar compression tests indicate a radial support strength of approximately 0.05 N/mm, which is comparable to other 3D-printed polymer stents and sufficient for temporary vascular support. Preliminary in vitro studies indicate short-term endothelial cytocompatibility, while accelerated degradation tests reveal controlled hydrolytic behaviour with approximately 90% mass retention after 4 weeks. Overall, the proposed design demonstrates a geometry-dominated deformation strategy that enables large expansion with minimal axial deformation, providing a promising framework for the development of deployable biodegradable stents for paediatric applications.

Oriented β-phase and porous architecture synergistically boost piezoelectricity of poly(vinylidene fluoride) films for wearable electronics
abstract: Oriented β-phase crystallites and well-defined porous structures are two well-established routes to boost PVDF piezoelectricity, yet integrating both in a single material remains an unsolved challenge. Here, we report a film processing strategy by combining ZnO incorporation, irradiation crosslinking, melt stretching, and acid etching to address this issue. ZnO nanoparticles play a dual role, serving as both a promoter to enhance flow-induced β-phase formation and a sacrificial template for pore generation. The synergistic effects of high ZnO loading (60 wt%), slight chain crosslinking, and strong melt stretching (20×) yield highly oriented β-phase with a fraction as high as 81.7%. Meanwhile, flow-induced redispersion of ZnO aggregates forms an interconnected nanofiller network, enabling complete ZnO removal upon acid etching to generate anisotropic pores. The resulting porous architecture, together with the oriented β-phase, enhances piezoelectric performance through three synergistic mechanisms: the intrinsic piezoelectricity of the β-phase, reduced dielectric permittivity, and the piezoelectret effect of the pores. The optimized film achieves a high piezoelectric coefficient (d33) of 69.6 pC/N and a figure of merit of 4.6 × 10-11 m2/N, with robust mechanical properties. The corresponding piezoelectric device exhibits a broad force-response range, high sensitivity to weak stimuli, and excellent cyclic stability. Flexible sensors based on these films can monitor human motion and physiological signals, and integration with a two‐dimensional convolutional neural network enables Morse-code-based transmission with 98.4% accuracy. This work offers a scalable melt-processing route for high-performance porous PVDF piezoelectric films toward flexible wearable electronics and self-powered sensing systems.

Integrating machine learning and CFD-derived hydrodynamics for predictive scale-up of combined cooling and antisolvent crystallization
abstract: Scale-up of crystallization processes remains a major challenge due to the complex interplay between operating conditions, hydrodynamics, and particle-level phenomena. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting product particle size distributions (PSD) in a combined cooling and antisolvent crystallization process across laboratory and pilot scales. Partial least squares (PLS) regression models with bootstrapping-based uncertainty quantification were constructed using three categories of input variables: (i) operating conditions alone, (ii) operating conditions with empirical hydrodynamic descriptors, and (iii) operating conditions with both empirical and CFD-derived hydrodynamic descriptors. At small scales (400 mL, 500 mL, and 3 L), both (ii) and (iii) improved predictive accuracy relative to (i), with consistent performance across train–test splits. For extrapolation to mid-scale (5 L) and large-scale (100 L) crystallizers, only models including CFD-derived hydrodynamic features provided accurate predictions, demonstrating their critical role in scale-up. The variable importance scores of the PLS models revealed the key operational and hydrodynamic factors that influence PSD predictions across scales. The proposed framework offers a generalizable digital design tool aiding scale-up of crystallization processes, integrating mechanistic hydrodynamic insights with machine learning to enable predictive, data-efficient, and interpretable scale-up.

Kinetics of steam methane reforming over Ni/Mo2C/Al2O3 catalyst in a direct Joule-heated fluidized bed
abstract: Electrification of steam methane reforming (SMR) via direct Joule heating (DJH) in fluidized bed reactors can enable decarbonized hydrogen production. However, a reliable DJH reactor design at scale requires comprehensive kinetic models that account for volumetric heating resulting from the DJH, where the solid catalyst temperature T_p exceeds the measured bulk-bed temperature T_bulk. The kinetic model should also capture special reactive characteristics of the electrically conductive nickel/molybdenum-carbide/alumina (Ni/Mo2C/Al2O3) catalyst employed in our system. With this catalyst, increasing steam-to-carbon ratio (S/C) decreased methane conversion contrary to thermodynamic expectations, while X-ray diffraction confirmed progressive oxidation of Mo2C to molybdenum oxides. This indicates that steam alters catalyst state in addition to gas-phase driving force for the reaction. To capture this behavior, we developed a dual-site redox-responsive kinetic framework that couples a reversible Ni-centered SMR rate modulated by a bounded Mo2C-phase fraction θ_C, and a water-gas shift reaction rate whose effective site availability increases as the Mo phase becomes more oxygenated. We fitted the model to 50 steady-state experiments (T_bulk = 600–800°C, S/C = 1–3, and two gas hourly space velocities) and validated it against 10 independent interpolation and extrapolation experiments. The model reproduced methane conversion and carbon monoxide selectivity with training and test R^2 of 0.95/0.93 and 0.90/0.89, respectively, and the predicted θ_C showed semi-quantitative agreement with XRD-derived Mo2C fractions of spent catalysts at 700°C. Recasting the fitted T_bulk-referenced parameterization onto an estimated T_p-basis showed that DJH decreases apparent Arrhenius barriers by approximately 26% relative to intrinsic counterparts. This gap is a thermal artifact of the solid-bulk temperature difference created by selective solid-phase heating under DJH, clarifying how volumetric heating modifies kinetic interpretation in electrified reformers.

Multimodal E-textiles based on industrial textile technologies for next generation human machine interfaces
abstract: Although wearable electronics have demonstrated significant potential in fields such as motion management, biomedicine, and virtual reality, the low-cost and scalable fabrication of flexible devices that combine multimodal sensing with excellent wearability remains a critical bottleneck for practical deployment. To address these challenges, this paper reports a multimodal electronic textile (e-textile) based on mature industrial textile technologies. In this work, the sensing yarns were developed using a wrapping technique, where silver-coated nylon and nylon yarns were helically wrapped around a highly elastic spandex core. Following the preparation of a custom-knitted pointelle substrate, the capacitive sensor was realized by integrating two sensing yarns via an embroidery process. The e-textile exhibits responsive performance to mechanical stimuli, including stretching, compression, and directional bending, while also providing robust sensing for non-contact proximity, demonstrating high sensitivity, a wide sensing range, and stability. Based on this, a smart wearable glove system was developed, encompassing specifically developed circuitry and visualization software. Combined with a deep learning model, the system achieved a gesture recognition accuracy of 99.8%, enabling the precise control of a robotic arm. This work not only offers a feasible approach for the development of multimodal flexible e-textiles but also facilitates the integration of wearable devices into next generation human-machine interfaces.

title: A-site ionic size modulates bulk exchange interaction and surface reconstruction for enhanced oxygen evolution
abstract: Regulating catalytic activity through non-active lattice sites represents a compelling yet underexplored strategy in transition metal oxides. In ABO 3 perovskites, this opportunity has been largely overlooked because conventional approaches predominantly focus on directly tuning the catalytically active B-site cations, whereas the role of A-site ions in governing bulk electronic interactions and surface reconstruction remains poorly understood. Here, by systematically tuning the A-site cation from larger to smaller ions (A = La, Sr, Ca, Sm), we demonstrate that the A-site ionic size in ACoO 3 perovskites serves as a key tuning parameter to remotely modulate catalytic behavior across multiple length scales. As the A-site ionic radius decreases, lattice distortion progressively intensifies, leading to lattice contraction and increased Co oxidation state. This structural evolution modifies bulk electronic interactions, including charge transport and exchange coupling, which in turn regulate surface reconstruction behavior under OER conditions. Notably, although all samples undergo reconstruction toward Co-based oxyhydroxide species, the reconstructed surface retains key electronic characteristics of the parent bulk, revealing strong bulk–surface coupling. Consequently, (Sm,Ca)CoO 3 , with the smallest A-site ionic radius, exhibits the highest OER activity owing to the combined effects of enhanced Co O hybridization, increased electronic delocalization, and favorable surface reaction kinetics. In contrast, (La,Sr)CoO 3 , with the largest A-site ionic radius, displays relatively fast kinetics due to more efficient bulk charge transport, whereas its overall activity is limited by less favorable surface reaction energetics. Our work demonstrates a non-active-site engineering strategy that bridges bulk spin polarization, surface reconstruction, and catalytic activity, offering new insights into the rational design of high-performance electrocatalysts.

title: Molecularly engineered hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent–holey graphene interfaces for matrix-resilient PFOA removal from complex waters
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent and hazardous water contaminant, yet practical adsorptive treatment remains constrained by the lack of materials that combine rapid uptake, high capacity, neutral-pH performance, and stability in complex water matrices. Here, we systematically engineered a hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent (HDES)-modified holey graphene nanosheet (HGN) adsorbent, introducing HDES incorporation onto defect-rich HGN for aqueous PFOA capture. An experimentally validated COSMO-RS workflow covering 30 DES constituents across six chemical families and ten HGN-DES adsorbents identified TBAC:DecA (1:2) as the highest-performing tested formulation, achieving about 1.9-fold higher PFOA removal than pristine HGN. Characterization confirmed HDES modification and formation of an HDES-enriched, electrokinetically modified lamellar graphene interface. HGN-HDES reached about 75% of its final capacity within 15 min, compared with about 30% for pristine HGN, and increased maximum adsorption capacity from 563.8 to 834.2 mg g −1 . Statistical-physics modeling identified a double-layer adsorption mechanism involving multi-site surface association, limited second-layer buildup, and thermally promoted site occupation. HGN-HDES retained 65.3% of its initial capacity after five adsorption–desorption cycles. At 0.5 mg L −1 PFOA and pH 7, HGN-HDES removed 92.4% from ultrapure water, 89.5% from municipal wastewater, and 91.4% from seawater, despite organic matter or high ionic strength. An ensemble artificial neural network (ANN) implemented in an interactive GUI further translated the 13-point experimental dataset into an exploratory in-domain process map restricted to the investigated ranges of C₀, t, and T. This DES-enabled graphene strategy offers a modular route to matrix-resilient PFAS adsorbents under environmentally relevant conditions.

Soluble-electron mediator assisted bioelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonium for nitrogen recovery
abstract: Bioelectrochemical reduction of dilute nitrate (NO 3 − ; sub-mM) to ammonium (NH 4 + ) is a promising route toward circular nitrogen management from nitrate-contaminated groundwater and surface waters. However, conventional bioelectrochemical systems (BES) rely on extracellular electron transfer through electrode-attached biofilms, restricting catalysis to a few electroactive bacteria in direct contact with the electrode. Here, we developed a soluble-mediator-assisted BES in which a diffusible mediator shuttles electrons to suspended cells throughout the catholyte, enabling weakly electroactive bacteria to serve as nitrate-reduction catalysts. Three biocatalysts ( Escherichia coli , Shewanella oneidensis , and Candidatus Brocadia sinica), nine soluble mediators spanning viologens, quinones, and phenazines, cathodic potentials from −0.3 to −0.9 V, and pH 6.5 to 8.5 were screened, and NO 3 − reduction to NH 4 + was confirmed using a 15 NO 3 − tracer. With E. coli cells and methyl viologen, NO 3 − was reduced to NH 4 + at a maximum volumetric rate of 10.9 mmol-N L −1 day −1 and a low NO 3 − -affinity constant ( K s = 0.19 mM). This rate was 8-fold higher than previously reported biofilm-based systems, and NO 3 − reduction was repeated over three successive NO 3 − additions during 48 h of operation. Furthermore, the soluble-mediator-assisted BES showed high performance even in natural groundwater and surface water, with a Faradaic efficiency of 50–59% and an electricity consumption of 188–192 kWh kg-NO 3 − -N −1 , substantially lower than metal-catalyst systems at comparable NO 3 − concentration. These findings demonstrate that soluble-mediator-assisted BESs provide an energy-efficient platform for converting NO 3 − in natural water into a recoverable NH 4 + form, with full nitrogen recovery additionally requiring downstream NH 4 + concentration or separation.

Reactor stability for the hydrogenation of liquid organic hydrogen carriers
abstract: Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers (LOHCs) are promising alternatives for the safe storage and transportation of hydrogen. Among the available LOHCs, the toluene/methylcyclohexane pair has attracted significant attention owing to its favourable hydrogen-storage capacity, chemical stability, and compatibility with existing fuel infrastructures. However, the development of efficient catalytic systems and the understanding of reactor-scale operability remain critical challenges for their industrial deployment. In this work, an integrated experimental and numerical framework is proposed for the assessment of toluene hydrogenation processes. A Ru/CNF catalyst was synthesized and deeply characterized. The catalyst was subsequently tested in a laboratory-scale trickle-bed reactor under different operating conditions of temperature and hydrogen pressure. A Langmuir–Hinshelwood–Hougen–Watson (LHHW) kinetic model accounting for competitive adsorption phenomena and gas-liquid mass transfer effects was developed and calibrated using the experimental data. Kinetic parameters were estimated through a robust multi-start optimization strategy based on weighted residuals and a Soft-L1 objective function. The validated kinetic model was subsequently integrated into a dynamic reactor framework representative of an industrial-scale hydrogenation unit. Dynamic simulations, eigenvalue analysis, Strozzi–Zaldívar divergence assessment, and pseudo-arc-length continuation studies were performed to evaluate reactor operability and safety. The results demonstrated stable reactor operation throughout the investigated conditions, with no evidence of multiplicity, hysteresis phenomena, or thermal runaway behaviour. Furthermore, a batch-to-continuous start-up strategy was shown to significantly reduce the time required to reach the desired operating regime compared with conventional continuous start-up procedures.

title: Confinement-driven mitigation of alkali migration in iron-zeolite tandem catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation
abstract: Tandem alkali-promoted iron-zeolite catalysts enable one-step conversion of CO₂ into value-added hydrocarbons. However, close integration of the two components frequently triggers alkali migration from the iron phase to the zeolite, thereby impairing catalytic performance and necessitating larger intercomponent separations that undermine synergistic effects. In this work, Na-promoted Fe catalysts supported on carbon nanotubes (FeNa/CNT) with varied iron confinement within CNT channels (20–93%) were engineered and coupled with H-ZSM-5 at distinct intercomponent distances to elucidate the role of iron confinement during CO₂ hydrogenation. Catalysts exposing a substantial fraction of iron nanoparticles outside CNT pores exhibited progressive declines in CO₂ conversion and increased CO and CH 4 selectivity over time, accompanied by reduced aromatization activity, hallmarks of alkali migration. In contrast, catalysts with highly confined iron nanoparticles maintained stable performance even at minimal iron-zeolite separation. Quasi-in situ XPS analysis provided spectroscopic evidence consistent with a pronounced Na migration during reaction only in poorly confined systems. These findings demonstrate that confining iron nanoparticles within CNT pores effectively mitigates alkali migration, providing a robust strategy for designing stable, single-bed iron-zeolite tandem catalysts operating in close-contact configurations.

title: Thermally responsive MXene hydrogel for reversibly tunable broadband electromagnetic shielding and temperature sensing
Gel-confined conductive fiber composites with synchronous strain sensing and EMI shielding for wearable applications
Rapidly assembled anti-freezing hydrogel for multimodal sensing and intelligent seatbelt monitoring
abstract: Hydrogel-based flexible sensors are attractive for wearable electronics and compliant human-machine interfaces, but freezing-induced stiffening and conductivity loss restrict operation in cold environments. Here, an anti-freezing conductive hydrogel was prepared from poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), glycerol, boric acid (BA), and Ti3C2Tx MXene. After the stock components were prepared, final mixing yielded a self-standing hydrogel within 5-10 s. Glycerol regulated the water-rich phase and preserved low-temperature compliance, while MXene established deformation-sensitive conductive pathways. The optimized hydrogel sustained macroscopic elongation beyond 1500%, rapidly re-established electrical continuity after recontacting cut surfaces, conformed to diverse substrates, and maintained conductivities of approximately 1.0 S m-1 at 20 °C and 0.17 S m-1 at -20 °C. As a resistive sensor, it captured joint motion, throat vibration, radial pulse, sliding, handwriting, droplet loading, and airflow. At -20 °C, joint-motion and sliding signals remained distinguishable, with response/recovery times of 337/242 ms, compared with 213/148 ms at 20 °C. After 300 repeated 180° bending-release cycles, peak-response retention reached 96.9% at 20 °C and 92.6% at -20 °C. The combination of rapid final gelation, retained subzero conductivity, and deformation-dependent resistance enabled direct construction of a tube-confined seatbelt sensor. The device generated distinct resistance waveforms during braking and right-turning events under winter conditions, indicating its potential for low-temperature vehicle-interface monitoring.

abstract: A sidestream ozone (O₃) injection (SSO3I) system incorporating a pressurized micro/meso-structured NETmix static mixer (NETmix SSO3I) was developed for the pre-oxidation of freshwater intended for human consumption. The NETmix reactor features a unique geometry that increases the intensity of gas-liquid mass transfer, offering intrinsic advantages for O3 dissolution in sidestream configurations. Installed in a water treatment plant (WTP) in northern Portugal, the NETmix SSO3I was benchmarked against a full-scale Venturi-based sidestream injection system (Venturi SSO3I). Comparative analyses focused on disinfection efficacy, removal of contaminants of emerging concern (CECs), and enhancement of downstream coagulation/flotation process. The NETmix SSO3I demonstrated effective inactivation of pathogenic bacteria (including coliform bacteria, escherichia coli, and enterococci) with log reductions exceeding 1.5-2 units at low O3 doses (0.8 gO3/m3) and short hydraulic residence time (0.15 min). For CECs removal, NETmix SSO3I achieved >80% abatement of 12 target micropollutants, including pharmaceuticals and pesticides, at normalized doses ≥0.2 gO3/gDOC, attaining equivalent performance to Venturi SSO3I, but at 20% shorter contact time and lower operating pressure. Additionally, NETmix SSO3I enhanced turbidity and specific ultraviolet absorbance (SUVA) removal during coagulation/flotation, despite the predominance of hydrophilic natural organic matter in the raw water. The results highlighted the NETmix superior O3 mass transfer efficiency and its potential for scalable integration into conventional WTPs.

Plasma processing as green alternative for advanced treatment of zirconium minerals: environmental and economic impact assessment
abstract: Amidst the rising demand for nuclear energy and the urgent need to decarbonize critical metal supply chains, conventional zirconium production remains energy-intensive and waste-heavy. This review critically evaluates plasma-based pathways, including thermal-arc, inductively coupled, and hybrid systems, using a comparative framework of process intensification metrics and sustainability indicators. We present a techno-economic assessment and life-cycle assessment on a cradle-to-gate basis (1 kg ZrO₂). Results show that plasma processing achieves extreme intensification, with volumetric productivities (~15,000 kg·h −1 ·m −3 ) and residence times (10–100 ms) outperforming conventional alkali fusion by 3–4 orders of magnitude. Environmentally, plasma processing reduces greenhouse-gas emissions by up to 80% (1.9 vs 8.4 kg CO₂-eq kg −1 ) when integrated with low-carbon electricity. Economically, it reaches cost parity with commercial benchmarks at industrial scales (>100 t/day), with a projected break-even price of 5.27 USD/kg. However, competitiveness remains sensitive to electricity pricing, reactor durability, and the utilization of silicon-bearing coproducts (e.g., SiCl 4 , SiC, SiO 2 ), which significantly influence the net process economics. This study provides a strategic roadmap for researchers and industry, identifying electrode erosion and SiO₂ removal as the primary engineering bottlenecks. By bridging the gap between laboratory metrics and industrial requirements, it provides a decision-making framework for prioritizing research and investment toward the electrified future of zirconium metallurgy.

Electron beam and protease–induced modifications of ECM protein hydrogels: Collagen- and elastin-specific structural insights via fast green staining and fluorescence lifetime CLSM
abstract: Collagen–elastin hydrogels have gained increasing attention as versatile extracellular matrix-based biomaterials for tissue engineering, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine. Their tunable mechanical properties, inherent biocompatibility, and responsiveness to external cues make them ideal yet complex systems for biomedical applications. Recent studies have demonstrated that high-energy electron beam irradiation offers a reagent-free approach for crosslinking collagen-elastin hydrogels, enabling precise modulation of network density, mechanical behavior, and thermo-responsiveness under sterilizing conditions. To better understand and visualize the effects of electron beam treatment and enzymatic degradation on the microarchitecture of these hybrid materials we employed fluorescence lifetime-based confocal laser scanning microscopy combined with Fast Green staining. This technique enabled the simultaneous differentiation of collagen and elastin subnetworks at the fibrillar level and facilitated the investigation of the behavior of individual protein components during radiation-chemical processing, enzymatic degradation, and combinations thereof. Electron beam treated and untreated gels were exposed to selective enzymatic degradation using trypsin and elastase, providing insights into the proteolytic stability of the individual matrix components. Lifetime based imaging revealed significant differences in collagen and elastin susceptibility to enzymatic cleavage following electron beam treatment. To support the analysis, machine learning-based segmentation was applied, with a primary focus on voxel-wise classification using the 3D pixel classifier in AIVIA, allowing for a volumetric and spatially resolved characterization of the datasets. The findings highlight the potential of fluorescence lifetime-based confocal laser scanning microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis for characterization of extracellular matrix-mimetic biomaterials and their dynamic remodeling behavior, with implications for optimizing scaffold design in bioengineering applications.

Dry reforming of methane via plasma-catalysis: Interplay between plasma, active metal, support, and reactor configuration
abstract: The dry reforming of methane (DRM) is evaluated in a dielectric barrier discharge reactor over a range of commercial catalysts (Pt/α-Al 2 O 3 , Ru/α-Al 2 O 3 , Pd/γ-Al 2 O 3 , Rh/γ-Al 2 O 3 , and Ni/SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 ), with performance analysed on the basis of activity metrics, time-on-stream stability, characterisation, electrical diagnostics and BOLSIG+ simulations. The synergistic combination of metal, support and plasma is the key to determining performance, with the combination of Rh and Pd with γ-Al 2 O 3 performing the best. CH 4 and CO 2 conversion over these samples exceeded 30% and 50%, respectively, a substantial increase from 10% and 5% observed in the absence of catalyst at equivalent conditions. All catalysts deactivated over time to a variable degree, with Rh/γ-Al 2 O 3 displaying the highest stability. The impact of pellet size, electrode length, and power on the discharge were further evaluated over Rh/γ-Al 2 O 3 , revealing a multitude of conflicting positive and negative macroscopic effects that impact the performance of even high activity catalysts. The catalyst screening and parametric study results demonstrate that high DRM activity requires a balance of plasma power density and catalyst amount. The former ensures the effective methane and CO 2 activation and vibrational excitation in the plasma, while the latter facilitates the dehydrogenation of methane on the metal and its oxidation through active O species provided through metal-support interfacial sites.

Tailoring highly efficient and air-stable n-type carbon nanotube webs via synergistic low-energy Ar+ irradiation and tetrabutylammonium fluoride doping for flexible thermoelectric generator
abstract: Achieving efficient and air-stable n -type carbon nanotube (CNT) thermoelectric (TE) materials remains challenging because electron-withdrawing oxygen species on CNT surfaces promote the spontaneous recovery of p -type transport and hinder efficient n -type doping. In this study, a synergistic surface deoxygenation and interfacial charge-transfer engineering strategy is proposed using low-energy Ar + irradiation and tetrabutylammonium fluoride (TBAF) doping. Mild Ar + irradiation selectively removes weakly adsorbed oxygen species while preserving the intrinsic sp 2 -conjugated CNT framework, thereby suppressing competing p -type doping effects and enhancing the interfacial affinity toward TBAF-derived ionic species. Consequently, Ar + irradiated CNT webs exhibit substantially enhanced n -type doping efficiency, enabling complete p -to- n conversion at a 20-fold lower TBAF concentration (10 mM) than that required for pristine CNT webs (200 mM). The optimized n-type CNT webs achieve a high power factor of 284.9 μW m −1 K −2 and maintain stable n -type TE performance with less than 20% variation in the Seebeck coefficient over 30 days under ambient conditions without encapsulation. A flexible TE generator comprising 10 complementary p–n pairs delivers a maximum output power of 1.21 μW at a temperature gradient of 20 K and demonstrates stable body-heat harvesting under ambient conditions. These results reveal the critical role of surface oxygen chemistry in governing n -type doping behavior of CNTs and provide an effective strategy for developing high-performance, air stable, and flexible TE materials for wearable energy-harvesting applications.

abstract: Persistent luminescent nanoparticles (PLNPs), particularly chromium-doped zinc gallate (ZnGa2O4:Cr3+) (ZGO NPs), provide a radically innovative strategy to push the detection limits of ELISA-based antigen detection into ultralow concentration regimes previously inaccessible. In contrast to our previous work, this study introduces a simpler process for obtaining and using ZGO NPs, by avoiding previous need for grinding and fractionation steps, thereby achieving 100% yield while preserving exceptional optical properties. This approach drastically reduces both preparation time, experimental complexity and equipment. This is particularly useful for a future application of this type of material (particularly for a commercial use), and represents a paradigm shift in the use of persistent luminescence (PersL) materials for biodetection. The newly prepared ZGO were employed in a non-functionalized form, as well as functionalized with detection antibodies (ZGO-AbD) or via an avidin–biotin system, offering unparalleled flexibility for diverse analytical needs. Signal amplification using hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), either generated in situ or added exogenously, produced an enhancement of persistent luminescence, allowing improving assay sensitivity. Integration into both sandwich and direct ELISA formats enables ultrasensitive detection of antigens, such as rabbit immunoglobulin G (IgG) and prostate-specific antigen (PSA), achieving detection limits of 2.85 pg. mL-1 and 3.14 pg. mL-1 respectively, which represent values far below those obtained using commercial kits. Moreover, the coefficient of variation was consistently found to be inferior to 15%, confirming the robustness and reproducibility of the assay. Importantly, these systems exhibited remarkable robustness in complex biological media, including undiluted human serum. This work establishes a new fast-prepared nanomaterial for ultrasensitive, versatile, and clinically applicable antigen detection in vitro.

abstract: Methyl ketones have recently been identified as a promising candidate for biofuels among other uses. They can be produced via biomass fermentation using Pseudomonas taiwanensis VLB120 Δ 6 pProd. However, the literature does not contain a complete early stage design proposal including upstream bioreactor design and downstream product purification at industrial scale. We present a model-based design approach for methyl ketone production based on renewable resources, including fermentation and product purification. We apply OptKnock to propose beneficial gene knockouts in the strain and adapt our SimulKnockReactor methodology to optimize the bioreactor for the production of methyl ketones. We then apply an enhanced version of our COSMO-CAMPED framework for the downstream purification of the fermentation broth. Extraction-based separations offer substantial potential for efficient purification of chemical products, particularly from the dilute aqueous streams of biotechnological fermentations. Finding a solvent with the required thermodynamic properties, bio-compatibility, and benign environmental properties is vital for the overall process performance. We propose three gene deletions to P. taiwanensis VLB120 Δ 6 pProd, namely, inorganic diphosphatase, polyphosphate kinase, and inorganic diphosphatase. We identify isopentyl-isopropyl-ether as most suitable extraction solvent among several others that outperform our literature benchmark of Di-n-butylether. We present an optimized layout for the combined upstream and downstream process that produces methyl ketones at a bulk production capacity of 1 × 10 7 kg a −1 for a total cost of 4.2 U S D kg −1 .

Reverse hydrogen spillover enhances selective hydrogenolysis of CO bonds
abstract: The selective activation and cleavage of C-O bonds through directional hydrogenation play a critical role in numerous industrial catalytic applications. Traditional noble metal catalysts often face challenges due to their strong propensity for active H₂ dissociation, leading to active site occupation by hydrogen atoms and subsequently hindering the efficiency of selective C-O bond cleavage. Furthermore, achieving selective cleavage of high-bond-energy C-O bonds while preserving lower-energy ones remains a significant challenge requiring further exploration. Herein, we present the design of a Rh single-atom catalyst anchored on Co for the selective cleavage of the high-bond-energy C2-O bond in furfural, serving as a model reaction. Through combined experimental investigations and density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Rh1Co single-atom alloys effectively lower the activation barrier for furfural hydrogenation, converting the C-O bond cleavage process from an endothermic reaction to an exothermic one. This catalytic behavior is notably absent in conventional Rh catalysts. The strong interactions within the Rh1Co alloy enhance the surface basicity and oxygen vacancies concentration, significantly promoting the hydrogenolysis of the C2-O bond and achieving a 1,5-pentanediol yield of 60.3%, surpassing most previously reported catalysts. Most importantly, Co sites facilitate H2 activation, while isolated Rh sites serve as the centers for C-O bond cleavage, introducing a reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism distinct from traditional hydrogenation processes. This reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism addresses the issue of hydrogen-induced deactivation of precious metal active sites, offering a promising pathway for broader application across diverse catalytic hydrogenation systems.

Self-adhering conductive hydrogel–wood scaffold for multidirectional wearable sensors
abstract: Conductive hydrogels are promising for wearable sensors, but the accurate resolution of human motions is limited by their isotropic network structures, while an intrinsic trade-off also exists between interfacial adhesion and mechanical robustness. Here, a wood-guided asymmetric bilayer conductive hydrogel is developed to integrate anisotropic sensing, mechanical support, and intrinsic skin adhesion within a single material system. The asymmetric architecture integrates a wood-reinforced polyvinyl alcohol/phytic acid (PVA/PA) top layer for anisotropic mechanical support with a PA-enriched bottom layer that enables compliant and robust skin adhesion, achieved through freeze-thaw-induced interfacial crystallite entanglement. The aligned cellulose microchannels within the wood scaffold impart directional mechanical reinforcement and guide ion transport, resulting in distinct electromechanical anisotropy with gauge factors of 3.3 and 1.98 along orthogonal directions. The integrated adhesive interface ensures conformal, residue-free skin contact without external fixation, minimizing motion artifacts. The sensor further exhibits a rapid response time of 0.36 s and good cyclic durability over 500 cycles. In addition, the system exhibits antibacterial activity and soil degradability. This work provides a scalable paradigm for harnessing the intrinsic anisotropy of natural biomass to develop eco-friendly wearable sensors that integrate directional sensing capability with stable skin contact.

All-active insulin-mimetic metal-phenolic networks for integrated diabetes-driven tumor therapy and post-surgical wound healing
abstract: Hyperglycemia in diabetes mellitus promotes tumor progression and severely compromises therapeutic efficacy. Although insulin effectively manages glycemic levels, it may inadvertently stimulate tumor proliferation via growth factor cross-activation, presenting a major clinical dilemma. To address this challenge, we rationally developed insulin-free, all-active V-TA-MET metal-phenolic networks (MPNs) through coordination-driven self-assembly of vanadium ions, tannic acid, and metformin. By exploiting synergistic interplay among all three components, these MPNs restore systemic glucose homeostasis, alleviate oxidative stress, and effectively suppress tumor growth. Leveraging intrinsic photothermal properties, they couple localized photothermal ablation with systemic metabolic regulation, realizing integrated photothermal-metabolic synergy. Beyond tumor control, the MPNs promote diabetic wound repair through metabolic-driven dual-phase regulation. In a postoperative diabetic mouse model, they eliminated residual tumor cells and accelerated functional wound healing by restoring microenvironmental homeostasis. This integrated therapeutic strategy offers comprehensive clinical management of both diabetes-driven tumor complications and postsurgical wound healing.

Morphology-engineered edge-enriched two-dimensional bismuth oxysulfide for high performance NO2 sensing
abstract: Two-dimensional materials (2DMs) have attracted great attention on gas sensing due to their high surface-to-volume ratio. However, conventional studies are largely limited to basal-plane-dominated adsorption. In contrast, edge sites exhibit higher catalytic activity and stronger gas-molecule interactions, yet controllable strategies to engineer edge-rich 2DMs remain underexplored. Here, we report a morphology-engineered synthesis of edge-enriched two-dimensional bismuth oxysulfide via in situ selective etching and sulfurization of Bi x Ga 1-x oxyhydroxide derived from phase-separated Bi Ga alloys. The intrinsic phase separation enables spatial segregation of Bi and Ga oxyhydroxides, allowing morphology evolution into nanobutterfly, nanoflower, and nanoworm structures after selective removal of gallium oxyhydroxide. Among them, the nanoflower morphology, featuring the longest edge length, delivers the highest NO 2 sensing response. A clear positive correlation between gas response and edge length is established, independent of surface area, highlighting the dominant role of edge-active sites. The optimized sensor achieves a high response of 433.3% towards 10 ppb NO 2 at room temperature under visible-light activation, surpassing most reported NO 2 sensors. This work provides a scalable pathway for engineering edge-active sites in 2DMs and establishes morphology-driven design principles for high-sensitivity gas sensing.

Specific, label-free and real-time sensing of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) in 0.5 μL drop of whole blood with a field-effect biosensor
abstract: Accurate and timely diagnosis of brain disorders is a major unmet clinical need. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) is a promising biomarker for detecting brain pathology. The study demonstrates specific and label-free detection of GFAP in 0.5 μL drops of whole blood with the Meta-Nano-Channel (MNC) field-effect (FET) biosensor. Importantly, the detection is performed directly in unprocessed as-is whole blood and no pre-measurement washing steps are performed. The suggested method may therefore be suitable for point-of-care, bedside or homecare settings. The MNC biosensor is specifically designed to address the challenge of solution potential in FET-based biosensors, and the challenge of localized gating induced by molecular interactions. The surface bound recognition layer is composed of anti-GFAP antibodies. The study reports limit-of-detection of 10 fg/mL, a dynamic range of 11 orders of magnitude, and with excellent linearity and sensitivity. The MNC biosensor is fabricated using a standard complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process, leveraging the inherent semiconductor-grade stability, robustness, and established infrastructure required for scalable, low-cost mass production. Furthermore, CMOS-driven miniaturization enables unparalleled multiplexing capabilities within ultra-small sample volumes, seamlessly integrated with on-chip circuitry for enhanced signal processing. The study is supported by three-dimensional numerical device calculations, surface characterization of biofunctionalizations, and control measurements to validate specificity and to quantify the extent of non-specific signals.

title: Multidimensional host-guest coupling in a fluorinated covalent organic framework for selective separation of o-xylene from xylenes
Synergistic dynamic doping and band sharpening via Cu/Sn co-doping for enhanced thermoelectric performance in n-type PbTe
abstract: Thermoelectric (TE) materials simultaneously require a high average zT avg and a high average power factor PF avg , as these parameters respectively determine the energy conversion efficiency and output power density of practical TE devices. Achieving concurrent optimization of zT avg and PF avg , however, remains challenging due to the intrinsic coupling between charge and phonon transport. Here, we report a synergistic strategy that integrates dynamic carrier doping with conduction-band sharpening to decouple electrical and thermal transport in n-type PbTe. Interstitial Cu doping enables regulation of carrier concentration over a broad temperature range, while Sn alloying effectively sharpens the conduction band, leading to a pronounced enhancement in carrier mobility. Furthermore, the unique defect structures introduced by Cu/Sn co-doping, including point defects, strain-field fluctuations, and localized nanoscale amorphous regions, establish efficient multiscale phonon-scattering pathways, thereby substantially suppressing the lattice thermal conductivity. Consequently, the optimized Cu 0.002 Pb 0.97 Sn 0.03 Te composition delivers a peak zT of ~1.6 at 723 K, accompanied by a high PF avg of 31 μW cm −1 K −2 and a high zT avg of ~1.1 over the temperature range of 300–773 K. A TE device comprising seven p-n leg pairs based on this material achieves a conversion efficiency of ~9.3% under a temperature difference of 470 K. These results demonstrate an effective design paradigm for simultaneously enhancing zT avg and PF avg , providing a promising route toward high-performance n-type PbTe-based thermoelectric devices.
