Predicting and improving lignin depolymerization processes with coupled graph modeling and kinetic Monte Carlo simulation
abstract: Lignin depolymerization offers a promising route to renewable aromatics, but our understanding of this process is limited by the large mismatch between model compound kinetics and the behavior of the real polymer. Here, we use computationally generated lignin populations and a kinetic Monte Carlo framework to capture the hydrogenolysis of real lignin using model compound kinetic parameters. Our simulations show that model compounds can reflect real lignin behavior, but only when the stochastic nature of lignin is accurately captured. We confirm the importance of free phenolic structures, which largely control depolymerization rates and favour an unzipping mechanism. Specific interunit C C linkages, although not cleaved, appeared to significantly accelerate depolymerization because of their free phenolic nature, as confirmed with an Arabidopsis thaliana mutant enriched in C–C-associated free phenolic linkages that depolymerized faster than the wildtype. This approach offers a foundation for better controlled lignin depolymerization and rational lignin design.

title: Molecular-structure-dependent dual-interphase regulation of sulfur-containing additives for high-stability NFM||HC sodium-ion pouch cells
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage, yet their practical application is still limited by unstable electrode/electrolyte interphases in full cells. This issue is particularly critical for NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM)||hard carbon (HC) pouch cells, where oxidative electrolyte decomposition on the high-voltage cathode and reductive side reactions on the low-potential anode occur simultaneously. Herein, two sulfur-containing cyclic additives, 1,3,2-dioxathiane 2,2-dioxide (PCS) and 1,3,2-dioxathiolane-2,2-dioxide (DTD), are comparatively investigated to clarify how molecular structure governs dual-interphase regulation in carbonate-based sodium-ion electrolytes. Density functional theory calculations and linear sweep voltammetry reveal that DTD exhibits a lower LUMO energy, stronger PF6⁻ association, and lower oxidation potential of the DTD-PF6⁻ complex, enabling earlier reductive and oxidative activation than PCS. NMR, Raman spectroscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, and electric-double-layer analysis show that DTD does not substantially reconstruct the bulk Na⁺ solvation sheath, but more effectively strengthens local additive-anion association and enriches DTD/PF6⁻-associated species near the reactive interfacial region. Post-cycling characterizations further demonstrate that DTD redirects interfacial reactions from uncontrolled carbonate/salt decomposition toward regulated additive/anion-derived passivation, forming thinner and more uniform CEI/SEI layers enriched with NaF-rich inorganic species and sulfur-containing passivation components. Consequently, the DTD-containing pouch cells deliver an initial Coulombic efficiency of 79.04%, an initial discharge capacity of 936 mAh, 87.40% capacity retention after 300 cycles, and 759 mAh at 2.0 C. This work identifies molecular-structure-dependent dual-interphase-forming capability as a key descriptor for designing advanced sodium-ion electrolyte additives.

abstract: The conventional DMSO/DMF system for vacuum‑flash perovskite fabrication requires ultrahigh vacuum (<10 Pa) to forcibly remove solvents, but often causes excessive desorption, intermediate‑phase disruption, and bottom‑interface voids, resulting in an extremely narrow processing window (<20 s). We address this by introducing an NMP/DMF solvent system, which exploits the large volatility difference between NMP and DMF. Under a moderate vacuum of 50–100 Pa, DMF is selectively and rapidly removed, while NMP is kinetically retained owing to its low volatility and strong coordination, yielding a stable, dense intermediate film. This extends the processing window to several minutes and markedly improves reproducibility. The optimized devices achieve 26.75% efficiency (Jsc = 26.51 mA cm⁻², Voc = 1.171 V, FF = 0.862) with negligible hysteresis, and mini‑modules (15 cm²) deliver 23.92% with a T90 lifetime >700 h under continuous illumination at 45 °C. This work provides a mild, scalable solvent‑engineering approach for fabricating high‑quality perovskite films with wide process tolerance.

abstract: Oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) is a promising route for methane valorization, yet achieving high activity, selectivity, and stability through rational engineering of active-species distribution remains a major challenge. Herein, a selective chemical vapor deposition (CVD) strategy was developed to enable site-selective deposition of tungsten (W) atomic species on manganese (Mn) surfaces, creating a distribution of active species that is inaccessible through conventional impregnation methods. Structural characterization revealed that W species were selectively anchored as isolated atoms or sub-nanometric clusters on Mn surfaces, forming a highly dispersed core (Mn)-shell (W atomic species) configuration. The CVD-prepared W-Na-Mn/SiO2 catalyst exhibited 4.65 times higher mass activity (based on CH4 conversion), 1.60 times higher turnover frequency (TOF), and 6.50 times higher mass activity (based on C2 yield) than its impregnated counterpart after 30 hours of reaction. The optimized architecture enabled efficient utilization of W species while maintaining high C2 selectivity and stability after 180 hours of operation. This study demonstrates that selective CVD-driven deposition governs the spatial distribution of active species and thereby catalytic functionality. The findings establish a catalyst manufacturing strategy based on site-selective atomic deposition, providing a transformative paradigm for highly active, stable, and selective OCM catalysts.

abstract: Pure-bromide quasi-2D perovskite promises efficient blue perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs), while is challenged by the carrier trapping at lattice edges due to the lattice vibration. Herein, present work demonstrates molecular-gear based lattice edge toughening strategy that substantially suppresses lattice vibration by immobilizing edge Pb ions at their central position. The adopted molecule of triptycene (TPC), characterized by rigid Y-shape-molecular-gear structure that anchors with Pb ions through bidentate coordination, which reshuffles the crystallization of quasi-2D perovskite, and spatially confines Pb ions thus damps the lattice vibration. Moreover, the molecular-gear meshing of π-π stacked TPC improves the edge electrical contact of inter-lattices, further promotes carrier transport for boosting efficiency of quasi-2D blue PeLEDs. Such lattice toughened quasi-2D perovskite exhibits homogenous energy landscape across a 2.5 cm × 2.5 cm substrate, and results in blue PeLEDs with a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 14.60% (emitting-area of 0.04 cm2) and 10.60% (1.0 cm2 emitting-area), which represent the top-ranking performances for large-area pure-bromine blue PeLEDs.

Syngas conditioning via Molten Carbonate Electrolysis Cell: an experimental study on waste gasification
abstract: Syngas conditioning is a crucial step in waste gasification-based processes to produce renewable fuels and chemicals, as syngas composition often does not meet the requirements of downstream synthesis units. In this work, the capability of a Molten Carbonate Electrolysis Cell (MCEC) to perform integrated syngas conditioning is experimentally investigated using synthetic gas mixtures representative of air- and oxygen-blown gasification. Experiments were carried out on a laboratory-scale single cell at 650 °C under galvanostatic operation. The electrochemical behavior of the cell and the evolution of syngas composition were analysed as a function of applied current and inlet gas composition. The results show that the MCEC enables simultaneous hydrogen enrichment, H 2 /CO ratio modulation, and carbon dioxide removal. Depending on the inlet syngas composition and electrical load, hydrogen concentrations above 90 vol%, H 2 /CO ratios from 1.8 up to 14, and CO 2 removal efficiencies approaching 99% were achieved. Oxygen-blown syngas exhibited the strongest conditioning performance, reaching near-complete CO 2 removal and hydrogen-rich outlet compositions at high current densities. The ability to electrically control syngas composition highlights the potential of MCEC technology as a compact and flexible alternative to conventional syngas conditioning schemes, with promising implications for process intensification and integration with renewable electricity sources in low-carbon fuel and chemical production pathways.

abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), particularly those featuring donor-acceptor (D-A) architectures, hold immense potential in photocatalytic applications. However, their performance is frequently hampered by insufficient charge separation efficiency. To address this challenge, we implemented a acceptor1-donor-acceptor2 (A-D-A) structural strategy. Herein, we report an efficient A-D-A COF photocatalyst (TP-BTD-COF), constructed with triazine and benzothiadiazole as dual acceptor motifs. In the presence of a photosensitizer and sacrificial agent under visible light irradiation, TP-BTD-COF achieved a superior CO2 photoreduction performance of 1936.39 µmol g-1 h-1 with 92.2% selectivity, representing an 18.99-fold enhancement over its parent catalyst, PB-DT-COF (101.95 µmol g-1 h-1). Systematic characterizations reveal that the A-D-A configuration significantly promotes charge transfer efficiency and lowers the activation energy barrier for *COOH intermediate formation (1.27 eV vs. 1.00 eV). HOMO-LUMO analysis further confirms a higher degree of charge delocalization in TP-BTD-COF, facilitating carrier migration. Furthermore, the Lewis basic sites derived from triazine and benzothiadiazole facilitate CO2 activation, while photoluminescence and Hall effect measurements verify the superior charge separation capability of TP-BTD-COF. This work provides valuable insights into the design of COF photocatalysts for visible-light-driven CO2 reduction.

Magneto-electrochemistry: A tool for sustainability and green chemistry
abstract: Magnetic fields provide a versatile and energy efficient strategy for modulating electrochemical processes without adding chemical reagents, mechanical stirring, or complex reactor designs. By coupling ionic currents with external magnetic fields, the resulting Lorentz-driven magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) convection accelerates mass transport and regulates interfacial kinetics at the micro- and macro-scale. These transport phenomena govern reaction rates, metal nucleation and growth, electrodeposition quality, and the long-term stability of electrochemical systems. This review examines recent advances in magnetic field assisted electrochemistry through the lens of process intensification and the 12 Principles of Green Chemistry. We discuss how magnetic fields influence fundamental processes, including electrodeposition, electrocatalysis, electrochemical energy storage, and emerging applications such as microfluidics, sensing, and dynamic autonomous systems, with a specific emphasis on the use of permanent magnets as zero-operating-energy tools for controlling transport. By evaluating sustainability metrics and life-cycle considerations, we highlight opportunities to enhance turnover frequencies and reduce the industry's reliance on critical minerals, chemical additives, or mechanical agitation. Finally, we identify key challenges that must be addressed to translate magnetic control from laboratory demonstrations to scalable electrochemical technologies. These include the need for quantitative transport models and reactor designs that can be implemented at industrially relevant scales. Overall, magnetic field assisted electrochemistry is positioned as an emerging approach for improving efficiency and circularity in the next generation of electrified chemical manufacturing.

Densification propagated closed-pores in hard carbon for high energy density sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Boosting the energy density of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) demands hard carbon (HC) anodes with a prominent low-potential plateau capacity, a key metric governed by closed-pore content. Developing efficient strategies to construct closed-pores and elucidating their formation mechanisms remain challenges. Herein, a densification-carbonization approach is proposed to lignin precursors. This physical operation intensifies the hydrogen bonding, weakens the C-H interaction and enhances the crystallite orientation. During subsequent carbonization, such modulation of molecular conformation facilitates complete dehydration through O-centered radicals and localizes graphitization via C-centered radicals, thereby promoting the formation of closed pores through layered stacking. The optimized DLHC4 delivers a reversible capacity of 386.4 mAh g⁻¹ with a competitive plateau capacity of 226.4 mAh g⁻¹, outperforming most reported biomass-derived HCs. Coupled with Na₃V₂(PO₄)₂F₃@C cathode, the assembled SIB achieves a high energy density of 297.7 Wh kg⁻¹. The efficacy and universality of this strategy is further validated for cellulose and wood powder precursors. This work provides deep insights into the construction of closed pores in hard carbons via molecular conformation modulation and establishes a green, high-yield synthetic route to boost the plateau capacity of HC anodes, which holds great promise for high-energy-density SIBs.

abstract: Electrochemical reduction of bromate (BrO3-) offers a viable route for mitigating this highly toxic disinfection byproduct in drinking water, yet its practical application is often constrained by slow reaction kinetics and insufficient interfacial mass transfer. In this study, Fe-doped TiO2 nanotube arrays (Fe-TNTs) were rationally designed as binder-free electrodes by combining electronic structure regulation with morphology engineering to enhance BrO3- electroreduction. Fe incorporation induces pronounced electronic redistribution in TiO2 and promotes surface oxygen vacancies formation, leading to improved electrical conductivity and strengthened BrO3- adsorption. Meanwhile, the ordered nanotube architecture imparted strong superhydrophilicity to the electrode surface, enabling rapid electrolyte infiltration and efficient gas bubble detachment, thereby mitigating mass-transport limitations at the electrode-electrolyte interface. As a result, the Fe-TNTs electrodes achieved nearly complete BrO3- removal efficiency at an initial concentration of 20 μM and maintained over 95% BrO3- removal efficiency across a wide pH range (5.8-9.0). Density functional theory calculations further indicated that oxygen vacancies and the Fe dopants cooperatively strengthen BrO3- adsorption and reduce the energy barriers of key reduction steps. Together, these results demonstrate an effective catalyst design approach and provide mechanistic insight into BrO3- electroreduction, highlighting the potential of Fe-TNT electrodes for practical drinking water treatment.

abstract: Adsorption-based biogas upgrading requires adsorbents exhibiting high CO 2 capacity, low CH 4 co-adsorption, and rapid regeneration under adopted operating conditions. Although pelletized metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are theoretically promising candidates, experimental datasets that explicitly link multicomponent adsorption dynamics, regeneration transients and cyclic multi-column performance remain limited. In this work, the pelletized MOF ProMOF® 9100, based on a UTSA-16 structure, was tested with a simulated biogas mixture (60/40 vol% CH 4 /CO 2 ). Breakthrough experiments demonstrated preferential CO 2 adsorption, early CH 4 roll-up due to competitive displacement and moderate dynamic selectivity. The equilibrium CO 2 uptake increased from 2.41 to 3.27 mmol g −1 over the investigated pressure range (1–8 bar), while CH 4 uptake remained below 0.4 mmol g −1 . Regeneration experiments revealed that vacuum-driven desorption was strongly diffusion-limited. Introducing a CH 4 purge (10–20% purge-to-feed ratio) accelerated the late-time desorption tail but increased methane losses. Cyclic VSA experiments at 1 bar adsorption pressure and approximately 0.1 bar desorption pressure, without purge, highlighted a marked purity/recovery trade-off. A four-column configuration without pressure equalization achieved a CH 4 purity of 97.3% at a recovery of 63.5%, whereas extending the cycle duration increased recovery to 90.4% at the expense of purity, which decreased to 85.2%. The introduction of a single pressure equalization step in a five-column configuration improved recovery to 96.9% and reduced specific energy consumption; however, this was accompanied by a further decline in product purity (82.5–86.0%). These results identify regeneration kinetics, pressure management and its dynamics as the primary limitations to achieve biomethane-grade purity using ProMOF® 9100 pellets under vacuum-only VSA operation. Overall, this study highlights the importance of process-level validation when translating promising adsorbents such as MOF's into cyclic VSA operation for biogas upgrading.

abstract: Biobased surfactants are well-established commercial products, however their production often relies on fresh feedstocks and intensive processes. This study presents a new valorization strategy in which hydroxy acids recovered from cellulose waste, such as black liquor, are converted into ester surfactants through solvent-free mechanochemical synthesis. By combining side-stream utilization with rapid and low waste synthesis, this work demonstrates an integrated approach for sustainable surfactant production. Hydroxy acids were recovered and purified, then coupled with fatty acids (C8-C18) via mechanochemical esterification using N,N′‑carbonyldiimidazole (CDI). This methodology enabled fast reactions without external heating. Product recovery was enabled by the pH-responsive behavior of the surfactants, which were anionic at pH above 3 and non-ionic at lower pH. The surfactants were further evaluated through quantitative and qualitative performance tests and compared with commercial references (SDS and Span 20) to assess their behavior in solution. Under optimized conditions, mechanochemical synthesis led to conversions above 90% across all chain lengths. The resulting esters exhibited effective surface activity, reducing surface tension to 25–40 mN m −1 , comparable to commercial surfactants SDS and Span 20. All properties followed expected trends with increasing chain length. The anionic form showed enhanced foaming performance, comparable to SDS, whereas the non-ionic form exhibited reduced foaming. Emulsion studies confirmed their ability to stabilize oil-water systems, producing dispersions with droplet sizes in the micrometer range. Green chemistry metrics indicated favorable process performance, comparable to bulk chemical production, while estimated partition coefficient values suggested good environmental compatibility.

Droplet entrainment in continuous liquid–liquid separators: Role of the small-droplet tail and uncertainty-aware hybrid modelling
abstract: Droplet entrainment in liquid–liquid gravity separators limits separation efficiency, yet both systematic experimental studies and predictive entrainment models remain scarce. In this study, 1077 steady-state operating points were obtained in a DN200 pilot-scale separator using a 1-octanol/water system, varying temperature, ionic strength, volume flow rate, dispersed-phase fraction, and inlet drop size distribution. Inlet drop size distributions were quantified by endoscopic imaging and entrained dispersed-phase fractions online by turbidity probes calibrated against gas chromatography. The results show that entrainment is governed by the small-droplet tail of the inlet drop size distribution, represented by the number-based tenth percentile d 10 ( q 0 ) . Increasing temperature shifted d 10 ( q 0 ) to larger values and thereby reduced entrainment, reproducibly within every ionic-strength campaign. Ionic strength left the small-droplet tail unchanged over most of the investigated range and shifted it only at the highest level tested. Both enter entrainment solely through d 10 ( q 0 ) and therefore do not require separate model inputs. On this basis, we formulated a reduced-order physics-based exponential model using d 10 ( q 0 ) and the critical Stokes diameter as inputs, augmented by hybrid residual-learning models based on Gaussian processes and neural networks. On internal and out-of-distribution test sets, these models, all calibrated on this single material system and separator geometry, slightly outperformed the physics baseline in point accuracy and uncertainty calibration. On external literature data from a DN150 separator and a paraffin-oil/water system, the RMSE of all models increased five- to tenfold, driven by a few under-predicted high-entrainment points. The physics-based model was the most robust in point accuracy, whereas the calibrated uncertainty of the Gaussian-process models did not transfer, with interval coverage dropping to 70%–74% against a nominal 95%.

abstract: Solar photochemical processes (SPPs) have become established as promising alternatives for the treatment of urban wastewater, as they allow for the simultaneous degradation of micropollutants and the inactivation of pathogens. However, their performance depends heavily on the photo-reactor design, particularly the capture and distribution of solar radiation. In this study, SPPs were evaluated using different oxidant concentrations (peroxymonosulfate (PMS), persulfate (PS), and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 )) in two photo-reactors: a compound parabolic collector (CPC) and a U-trough reactor. The CPC employs a reflective geometry that directs both direct and diffuse radiation toward the absorber, with an optical path length of 50 mm, while the U- trough reactor has a simpler reflective surface and an optical path length of 75 mm. The treatment with solar PMS at 1 mM proved to be the most effective SPPs. The concentration of E. coli was reduced to ≤10 CFU 100 mL −1 and viral indicators to ≤10 PFU 100 mL −1 , meeting stringent European reuse standards for urban wastewater. Furthermore, over 80% degradation of the target micropollutants was achieved. When analyzing the results in terms of accumulated UV energy per unit volume (Q UV ), the U- trough reactor showed similar efficiency to the CPC. This behavior is consistent with the optical and actinometric characterization previously reported for this reactor configuration. In summary, the U- trough solar reactor represents a promising alternative to the CPC for photochemical applications in solar water treatment.

title: A vanillin-functionalized hydrogel delivering BMP-2 for antibacterial therapy and alveolar bone regeneration in periodontitis
abstract: Treating inflammatory periodontal bone defects remains challenging. Here, we present a functionalized delivery platform by integrating vanillin methacrylate (VMA) into a GelMA hydrogel for BMP-2 delivery. By introducing methacrylate groups into bioactive natural small molecules, we enabled their covalent incorporation into the GelMA hydrogel system. While preserving their intrinsic antibacterial and anti-inflammatory activities, the retained aldehyde group of the modified molecule enables proposed reversible interactions with amino groups of BMP-2, thereby improving the release kinetics of the encapsulated BMP-2. In vitro, the functionalized hydrogel alleviated inflammation, disrupted biofilms, and promoted osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. In a rat periodontitis model, it significantly reduced alveolar bone loss and restored periodontal tissue homeostasis. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis suggested HIF-1α as a potential regulatory factor, which was further supported by inhibition experiments. This functionalization strategy based on a natural small molecule provides a facile approach to integrating multiple functions into a single delivery platform, offering promising opportunities for tissue engineering beyond periodontal applications.

Beyond CO2 dissociation: The pivotal role of O* surface species in reverse water-gas shift kinetics over nickel
abstract: This work provides a mechanistic perspective on the role of surface oxygen intermediates in the reaction kinetics of the high-temperature reverse water-gas shift (rWGS) reaction. Above 500 °C, the redox mechanism is generally accepted, typically assuming CO 2 dissociation as the rate-determining step on Ni supported catalysts. However, our microkinetic analysis, with experiments the varying CO 2 /H 2 ratios within a range of 500–800 °C, reveals that the hydrogenation of surface oxygen intermediates is as important as CO 2 dissociation. Data were collected using two different nickel catalysts (0.5 wt% and 5 wt% Ni/CeZrO 4 ), although only the intrinsic kinetic data over the 0.5 wt% Ni/CeZrO 4 were used for model development and regression analysis. Degree of Rate Control (DRC) analysis demonstrates that the relative importance of these two steps shifts as a function of the CO 2 /H 2 feed ratios and temperature. Based on this insight, we developed a Langmuir-Hinshelwood-Hougen-Watson (LHHW) model, incorporating both rate-determining steps. This model captures how the surface oxygen coverage controls overall reaction rate by affecting the apparent reaction orders and activation energy.

Role of molybdenum promotion in Ni/SiO2 catalysts for Polyolefins Hydrogenolysis
abstract: Catalytic hydrogenolysis has emerged as a promising depolymerization strategy for converting waste polyolefins into high-value hydrocarbon liquids. This work investigates bimetallic NiMo/SiO 2 catalysts for polyolefin hydrogenolysis, focusing on the role of Mo in improving activity and reaction pathways. For n-hexadecane hydrogenolysis at 300 °C and 20 bar of H 2 for 2 h, reduced NiMo/SiO 2 catalysts achieved conversions of up to 57%, nearly twice those of reduced Ni/SiO 2 catalysts. At a comparable n-hexadecane conversion of around 34%, NiMo/SiO 2 exhibits a lower methane selectivity of 12% over than the 19% of Ni/SiO 2 . For polypropylene degradation at 300 °C and 20 bar of H 2 for 30 h, NiMo/SiO 2 catalysts show a higher yield of DCM-soluble products (C 4 –C 39 ) of 55 ± 5% with a lower average molecular weight of 620–720 g/mol than that of Ni/SiO 2 catalysts, for which values are 47 ± 1% and 1160–1380 g/mol, respectively. These results indicate a higher reactivity of NiMo/SiO 2 . More notably, NiMo produced minor amounts of alkenes and aromatics. Furthermore, the yield of aromatic products gradually decreases from 2.1 to 0.7% as the reduction temperature of the NiMo/SiO 2 catalyst increases from 350 to 750 °C. Similar trends were observed in polyethylene hydrogenolysis. These findings indicate the co-existence of hydrogenolysis, dehydrogenation and aromatization of polyolefins degradation over NiMo/SiO 2 under H 2 -rich conditions. This reaction network has not been previously reported for metallic-based catalysts under H 2 -rich polyolefin hydrogenolysis conditions or in the broader literature on NiMo catalysts for petroleum hydrotreating, highlighting the unique catalytic behavior of NiMo/SiO 2 . Using H 2 -TPR, XRD, XPS, STEM-EDX, NH 3 -TPD and Py-IR, we hypothesize that the aromatic product formation is linked to the Mo-related species rather than the conventional acid-catalyzed aromatization.

title: VN/Mo2C heterostructure embedded in Co-doped nanocages as a separator coating for durable Li-S batteries
abstract: The polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish sulfur redox kinetics remain major obstacles to the commercialization of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries. Herein, we design a functional separator coating based on MOFs-derived Co-doped nanocage (Co-NC) hosting VN/Mo2C heterostructures with integrated adsorption-catalytic capabilities (VN/Mo2C/Co-NC). The Co-NC nanocage provides a large surface area as an ideal substrate for catalyst dispersion while physically restricting polysulfide shuttling. More importantly, the VN/Mo2C heterointerface enhances synergy through strong chemisorption, improved charge transfer, and reduced energy barrier for polysulfides conversion, thereby accelerating sulfur redox kinetics. Both theoretical and experimental results confirm that this physical confinement adsorption catalysis design enables efficient polysulfide capture and rapid conversion on the VN/Mo2C/Co-NC surface, effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Notably, the VN/Mo2C/Co-NC modified separator achieves an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.047% per cycle over 1,000 cycles at 1 C, demonstrating exceptional long-term cycling stability for Li-S batteries. The pouch cell maintains 800 mAh g-1 in specific capacity after 50 cycles at 0.08 C. This study proposes a rational design strategy for multifunctional electrocatalysts and offers a promising avenue for developing advanced separator technologies for high-performance battery systems.

Interfacial polarity regulation enables robust self-healing conductive elastomers for wearable motion recognition
abstract: Flexible strain sensors must withstand repeated deformation while preserving mechanical integrity, autonomous repairability, and stable signal transduction. Conductive polymer composites, however, often suffer from filler aggregation and fragile conductive networks, making it difficult to reconcile strength, self-healing capability, and sensing reliability. Here, we report an interfacial polarity regulation strategy to construct a self-healing conductive elastomer composed of furan-functionalized carbon nanotubes and Diels–Alder-crosslinked epoxidized natural rubber (ECNT). Molecular simulations, together with spectroscopic and morphological analyses, reveal that the furan-regulated interface generates localized polar domains and accessible interaction sites, thereby promoting nanotube dispersion and interfacial coupling within the elastomer matrix. The optimized ECNT-2 composite achieves a tensile strength of 7.74 MPa, an elongation at break of 467%, and a self-healing efficiency above 90% after thermal treatment. Enabled by dynamic conductive-network reconstruction and reversible covalent crosslinking, the elastomer sensor delivers a gauge factor of 3.76, response/recovery times below 180/140 ms, and stable piezoresistive signals under cyclic deformation. It reliably monitors large joint motions and subtle physiological activities, including finger bending, elbow flexion, coughing, and smiling. Coupled with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, the sensor achieves window-level validation accuracies of 100% for representative motions and 98.7% for finger gestures, supporting robotic-hand teleoperation. This work links molecular-level polarity engineering with intelligent wearable sensing, offering a rational route to robust self-healing conductive elastomers for adaptive human-machine interfaces.

Magnetron-sputtered ultrathin boron nitride on InP enabling selective photoelectrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia
abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) ammonia synthesis from nitrate offers a sustainable approach to producing valuable chemicals while mitigating waste pollution. Here, we developed an ultrathin amorphous boron nitride (BN) passivation layer (∼5 nm) via magnetron sputtering, leveraging its strong adhesion and high uniformity on InP to enhance interfacial electron transportation to surface for ammonia generation. We found that nitrogen incorporation during BN deposition lead to more chemically uniform BN layer with enhanced nitridation and reduced oxidation, significantly reducing interfacial defects and suppressing surface-state-mediated recombination between cocatalyst (∼50 nm spin-coated TiOₓ) and InP semiconductor. The innovation is combining tunneling passivation layer BN with TiOₓ catalysis with Ti O active sites for improved charge-separation efficiency and photoelectrode stability, leading to high selectivity under near-bias-free conditions. The TiOₓ/BN/InP photocathode achieves near-unity FE at 0 V vs RHE, a pioneering demonstration of an InP photocathode for outperforming selective ammonia generation from nitrate electrolytes under solar illumination. This work demonstrates the feasibility of magnetron sputtering–fabricated ultrathin BN layers for enhancing selective PEC nitrate reduction, while providing insights into the effectiveness of interface engineering strategy in enabling selective ammonia production under mild operating conditions.

Self-pumping aromatic nanofibers with a peapod-like structure for aromatherapy applications
abstract: Aromatic textiles with therapeutic, emotional and aesthetic functions hold considerable promise for healthcare applications; however, the high volatility of fragrance molecules often compromises their durability and stability. Here we present self-pumping aromatic nanofibers (SPANFs) inspired by the structure of peapods, which achieve high fragrance loading capacity and efficient release kinetics to enhance sustained efficacy of aromatic textiles. Fabricated via airflow-assisted conjugate electrospinning, the SPANFs employ a polyacrylonitrile as the sheath and an aromatic inclusion complex comprising lavender essential oil (LEO) as the core. This design allows an unprecedented core-to-sheath mass ratio (3:1), achieving an exceptional oil loading (94 mg g-1). LEO release from the SPANFs follows desired first-order kinetics through a synergistic cascade mechanism controlled by hydrogen bonds within the inclusion complex, protected by a polymer sheath, and delivered via numerous release sites. These comprehensive properties render the SPANFs exhibiting reliable self-pumping behavior for long-lasting fragrance retention and release, with ester groups persisting for two months. When fabricated into fabric, the SPANFs alleviate anxiety-like behaviors in sleep-deprived mice. These findings establish a strategy for creating durable aromatic textiles, opening avenues for integrating functional fragrances into therapeutic and wellness applications.

From passive closure to active therapy: Interfacial bridging Medi-MOF sutures for diabetic wound healing
abstract: Surgical sutures are indispensable for wound closure, but they may promote bacterial colonization and exacerbate inflammation as they are often treated as passive materials. Impaired immune function and vascular dysfunction can severely hinder wound healing particularly in diabetic wounds. Herein, a bioinspired therapeutic silk suture system was constructed which integrated interfacial engineering with responsive drug delivery to address these limitations. A curcumin-based metal–organic framework (Medi-MOF) was immobilized onto silk sutures via a urushiol-mediated interfacial layer, forming a robust coating. Benefiting from the unique molecular structure and rapid curing properties of urushiol, MOF nanoparticles can be stably anchored through a variety of interactions, including hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking and metal coordination. The system exhibited pH-responsive release behavior, in which the acidic microenvironment of infected tissues triggered accelerated degradation of MOF and rapid release of curcumin and Zn2+, while slower release under physiological conditions. Notably, immobilization onto the silk substrate further modulates release kinetics, resulting in a hierarchical mechanism that combines diffusion control with degradation-triggered release. Moreover, the inherent capillary wicking property of braided silk sutures, traditionally regarded as a drawback, is transformed into a functional advantage by enabling active drainage of pathological exudates and triggering the release of medication on demand. This “drainage–response–release” strategy established a dynamic therapeutic pathway that effectively suppressed bacterial infection, modulated inflammation, and promoted tissue regeneration. Overall, this work provided a new paradigm for transforming sutures from passive closure devices into adaptive therapeutic platforms for diabetic wound management.

abstract: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of biomass-derived oxygenates is limited by hydrogen evolution, acid-driven degradation of non-noble electrodes, and poor control of gas-evolving interfaces. Hierarchical Ni electrodes were prepared by dynamic hydrogen bubble templating on semiporous stainless steel and coupled with dodecyltrimethylammonium chloride (DTAC) interfacial regulation and Ru decoration. The macroporous, dendritic scaffold supports surface accessibility, reactant transport, and gas release, while DTAC attenuates unproductive proton reduction and improves structural persistence in acidic media. The platform was evaluated for levulinic acid (LA), 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), and furfural (FF), showing reactant-dependent selectivity. LA reduction was strongly temperature-dependent: 4-hydroxypentanoic acid-rich mixtures dominated at 5 °C, whereas γ-valerolactone (GVL) was favored at 50 °C, reaching 95.8% conversion, 88.7% Faradaic efficiency, and 92.6% GVL selectivity on DTAC-modified Ru Ni A. HMF mainly yielded 2,5-bis(hydroxymethyl)furan, while FF gave furfuryl alcohol. Density functional theory calculations on clean Ni facets provide qualitative mechanistic context for possible surface-bound LA-to-GVL pathways and their sensitivity to surface geometry and reaction sequence.

abstract: Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) represent a leading technology for next‐generation displays, yet their performance is severely hampered by interfacial non‐radiative losses, charge injection imbalance, and positive aging arising from direct contact with the metal cathode. Here, we propose a dual electron transport layer (dual-ETL) architecture consisting of ZnMgO and 2,4,6 tris(3’ (pyridin 3 yl) biphenyl 3 yl) 1,3,5 triazine (TmPPPyTz). TmPPPyTz chemically passivates oxygen vacancies on the ZnMgO surface, provides a stepwise energy cascade that buffers excessive electron injection, and physically separates ZnMgO from the Al cathode, thus suppressing the positive aging effect. The resulting red QLEDs achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 31.8%, a current efficiency of 38.9 cd A–1, and a power efficiency of 36.8 lm W–1. At an initial luminance of 100 cd m–2, the half-lifetime (T50) reaches 55 910 h, yielding more than 9-fold and 12-fold improvements over the TmPPPyTz (6 070 h) and ZnMgO (4 565 h) devices, respectively. These results demonstrate that a dual-ETL strategy combining defect passivation, charge balance regulation, and cathode interface protection offers a powerful route toward high performance QLEDs.

E7-engineered gastrodiae rhizoma-derived nanovesicles promote diabetic bone regeneration with the involvement of PINK1/parkin-mediated mitophagy
abstract: Diabetic bone defect regeneration poses a significant clinical challenge due to hyperglycemia-induced persistent oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, which disrupt bone homeostasis and impair the repair process. Plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) represent a novel class of natural, safe, and bioactive therapeutics with emerging potential in regulating cellular functions, yet their underlying mechanisms remain underexplored. Herein, we develop an integrated active-targeting and sustained-release platform by engineering Gastrodiae Rhizoma-derived nanovesicles (GDNVs) with E7 peptide for specific recognition of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and encapsulating them in a GelMA hydrogel (GelMA@E7-GDNVs) for controlled localized delivery. Our findings suggest that GDNVs are associated with enhanced mitophagy, with the PINK1/Parkin pathway being potentially involved. These effects correlate with reduced mitochondrial ROS and improved functional performance of BMSCs under high-glucose (HG) conditions. In a diabetic rat cranial defect model, the GelMA@E7-GDNVs platform significantly promotes new bone formation. This study highlights the cross-species regulatory potential of PDNVs at the organelle level, offering an innovative therapeutic strategy for diabetic bone defects characterized by natural origin, precise targeting, and sustained release. By modularly integrating plant-derived nanovesicles with engineered delivery systems, this approach establishes a scalable paradigm applicable to diverse tissue regenerative disorders.

Synergistic assembly of robust graphene-based organic conductive gel sensors via directional freezing and nonsolvent quenching
abstract: Conductive organic gel as soft electronics still face challenges such as low strength (<1 MPa), skin-modulus mismatch (typically <100 kPa for gel vs. ~100–1000 kPa for skin), and limited environmental adaptability. Graphene-functionalized hydrogels typically suffer from poor interfacial wettability between graphene nanoparticles, macromolecular backbones, and solvent molecules, making uniform dispersion difficult. Herein, we propose a robust graphene organic conductive gel fabricated by directional freezing and non-solvent quenching: polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and flashjoule graphene (FJG) are thermally dissolved in Nmethyl pyrrolidone (NMP), directionally frozen in an ice template, and finally quenched in an ethanol/water mixture. This graphene organic gel features a bioinspired ordered anisotropic structure: an ordered layered hierarchy along the parallel freezing direction, and a contracted folding structure along the perpendicular direction. With the incorporation of only 0.5 wt% FJG the hydrogel exhibits outstanding mechanical performance—namely, a Young’s modulus of 2.5 MPa, a tensile strength of 2.8 MPa, and an elongation at break of 1118%—while retaining excellent frost resistance, robust pressure sensing, low-temperature sensing capability, and exceptional sensing-cycle stability (i.e., >12,000 cycles under 30% tensile strain at 25 °C and >400 cycles under 60% tensile strain at -20 °C). This strategy thus offers valuable guidance for the rational design of nanocomposite hydrogels integrating nanoparticles and two-dimensional materials.

High-yield and scalable synthesis of bio-derived acrylic acid from lactic acid or ethyl lactate over silica-supported polyphosphate catalysts
abstract: Acrylic acid (AA) and its esters are widely used industrially but are currently derived from fossil resources. The conversion of bio-derived lactic acid (LA) or LA esters to AA offers substantial potential to reduce CO 2 emissions compared with conventional fossil-based processes. Herein, we report a high-yield route to AA via vapor-phase dehydration of LA or ethyl lactate (ELA) toward sustainable chemical production. The vapor-phase dehydration was conducted over a silica-supported polyphosphate catalyst, which was readily prepared via wet impregnation of phosphate species onto silica, followed by calcination to form polyphosphate. The effects of feed composition and catalyst properties were investigated. In the reaction using LA, the catalyst derived from NaH 2 PO 4 and K 2 HPO 4 achieved a significantly high AA yield (91.2 ± 2.6%). In the reaction using ELA, the catalyst derived from NaH 2 PO 4 and Na 2 HPO 4 provided a high total yield (89.1 ± 0.5%) of AA and ethyl acrylate. Optimizing the acid amount, acid-base balance, and alkali metal cation composition of the catalyst for each substrate (LA or ELA) is essential for achieving high AA yields. Importantly, the system also demonstrated scalability, and the reaction scale increased more than tenfold relative to previous studies that achieved yields above 75%. This approach is promising for the scalable production of bio-derived AA with high yield, supporting the realization of a sustainable society.

Direct construction of N/S-rich Zn-DMTD-MOGs for ultrafast Pb(II) removal: Synergistic chelating/monodentate coordination and LMCT mechanism
abstract: Metal-organic gels (MOGs) have attracted extensive attention in the field of heavy metal removal, owing to their advantages including ease of surface modification, good stability, hierarchical pore structure, tunable functional groups, and mild and facile preparation conditions. However, the existing MOGs still leave considerable room for performance improvement. To produce MOGs with enhanced adsorption sites, high specific surface area, and greater pore volume, this study combined ultrasound-assisted nucleation with a "high-concentration reaction" strategy and triethylamine-mediated deprotonation, thereby enabling direct coordination between 2,5-Dimercapto-1,3,4-thiadiazole (DMTD) and Zn2+. As a result, Zn-DMTD-MOGs material with higher-density N and S adsorption sites was successfully synthesized. The material exhibits a disordered particle-stacked amorphous structure with abundant mesopores (3-24 nm). Adsorption experiments demonstrate that the material achieves a trace Pb(II) removal efficiency of 96.98% within 10 s. The material achieves wide applicability over a low concentration range (< 42 mg/L) and a broad pH range (3.5-10.5), along with favorable stability, good reusability, and applicability to real water matrices. A local coordination cluster model was obtained through density functional theory (DFT) geometry optimization, and a synergistic chelating/monodentate coordination and ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) mechanism was established. The analysis reveals that the material adsorbs Pb(II) primarily through chelation at dual N/S sites and monodentate coordination at single S sites. This mechanism endows Zn-DMTD-MOGs with ultrafast adsorption kinetics and excellent cyclic stability, making them promising candidates for heavy metal remediation in drinking water sources.

title: Engineering spatially confined hydrolysis for charge-selective nanofiltration using upcycled PET membranes
abstract: Upcycling post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into high-performance nanofiltration membranes is limited by the inherent trade-off between water permeance and molecular selectivity. Here, we engineer the spatial localization of alkaline hydrolysis to selectively modify the transport-active feed-side region of upcycled PET membranes while preserving the underlying support architecture. Compared with unrestricted full-immersion hydrolysis, spatially confined hydrolysis generated an asymmetric membrane structure with more open feed-side surface features, increased nanoscale roughness, enhanced wettability, and a more negatively charged surface while maintaining the integrity of the support region. The localized reconstruction moderately enlarged the effective transport pathways, increasing the molecular-weight cut-off from approximately 343 to 714 Da while preserving molecular sieving. Under cross-flow filtration at 70 psi (4.8 bar), the optimized membrane achieved an ibuprofen permeate flux of 36.0 ± 0.6 L m −2 h −1 while retaining 91.1 ± 0.6% rejection, corresponding to a 7.2-fold increase in flux relative to pristine PET, with only a 4.8 percentage-point reduction in rejection. In contrast, unrestricted full-immersion hydrolysis produced a permeate flux of approximately 400 L m −2 h −1 but only 2.1% ibuprofen rejection, confirming that controlling the spatial extent of hydrolysis is critical for balancing transport and selectivity. The optimized membrane further exhibited preferential sulfate rejection, stable ibuprofen separation over five filtration cycles, a final flux recovery ratio of 92%, and improved resistance to sodium-humate fouling, retaining a normalized flux of 0.81 after 120 min. Performance was also largely retained under more complex feed conditions, with the optimized membrane achieving 32.0 L m −2 h −1 permeate flux and 89.5% ibuprofen rejection in an ibuprofen‑sodium humate-CaCl 2 feed, while retaining a normalized flux of 0.748 and an FRR of 86% under mixed organic-inorganic fouling conditions. Response-surface analysis identified 1.0 M NaOH, 40 °C, and 60 min as the selected hydrolysis condition providing a practical balance between ibuprofen permeate flux and rejection. These results demonstrate that engineering the spatial localization of alkaline hydrolysis provides a simple, nanofiller-free strategy for tailoring membrane transport pathways, improving the permeance-selectivity balance, and advancing the upcycling of waste PET into charge-selective nanofiltration membranes.

Machine learning strategies integrating knowledge transfer and a cascaded framework: Guiding the discovery of NIR-II organic cocrystals
abstract: Organic cocrystals represent a highly promising class of photothermal materials operating in the near-infrared second (NIR-II) window. However, efficient identification and rational design remain challenging due to the vast chemical space and the complex, nontrivial relationships between molecular structures and functional properties. In this work, we develop a cascaded dual-task (C2T) machine learning (ML) framework that effectively links cocrystal-formability recognition (M1) with NIR-II absorption identification (M2) through feature knowledge transfer. We constructed the first hierarchical organic cocrystal database, comprising 2,648 cocrystal samples and 128 NIR-II cocrystals. By integrating RDKit and PaDEL descriptors to generate dual-representation molecular features, a dual-task prediction model is established. Under small-sample conditions, both M1 and M2 achieve high predictive accuracies (>92%) and demonstrate strong generalization capabilities. Guided by the model, we discover and experimentally validate the DPQ cocrystals, which exhibits intense NIR-II absorption (up to 1200 nm) and efficient photothermal behavior (~120℃@1024 nm). Moreover, multiscale theoretical calculations combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based model interpretability elucidate the structure-property relationships from molecular architecture to macroscopic performance. This work demonstrates the potential of ML for precise cocrystal design and efficient performance identification under small-sample conditions, paving the way for ML-accelerated development of functional molecular materials.

Pristine graphene nanosheets prepared by supercritical CO2 circulating jet cavitation for MoS2-intercalated tubular nanofiltration membranes
abstract: Pristine graphene nanosheets offer a stable scaffold for laminar nanofiltration membranes, but their narrow channels and limited hydrophilicity restrict water transport. Herein, supercritical CO2 jet cavitation derived pristine graphene nanosheets were first used as membrane building blocks to construct MoS2 intercalated tubular nanofiltration membranes on porous α-Al2O3 supports. Unlike GO or rGO membranes, the pristine graphene nanosheets preserve an intact sp2 framework without strong oxidation/reduction chemistry, providing improved structural stability in aqueous filtration. MoS2 nanosheets served as hydrophilic two-dimensional spacers to regulate interlayer channels, enhance water permeance and suppress channel compaction. Meanwhile, the PEI@GA-crosslinked layer provided positively charged sites to enhance anionic dye removal. The optimized G8M2 membrane maintained rejection rates above 99% for CBB, CR, and BY, with water permeabilities of 110.32 - 132.71 L·m-2·h-1·bar-1 in single-dye filtration. In dye/NaCl mixed systems, it achieved a permeability of 126.42 L·m-2·h-1·bar-1 and a separation factor of 1998.21 for CBB/NaCl, with FRR >97% and stable operation over 72 h. This work presents an acid- and oxidant-free liquid-phase exfoliation method with heterolaminar channel engineering to construct high-permeability pristine graphene tubular membranes.

Ultralow-threshold airflow sensor for noninvasive obstructive sleep apnea monitoring and intervention system
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder worldwide, with nasal and oral airflow serving as the most direct indicators of OSA-related respiratory events. Existing respiratory monitoring sensors require philtrum attachment or nasal insertion to capture clear signals, causing discomfort and reducing sleep quality. Capturing breathing airflow in a more comfortable, noninvasive manner remains a challenge, primarily due to the limited detection threshold and slow response of current airflow sensors. Inspired by mammalian vascular networks, we propose a pneumatically sprayed, multi-level, lightweight network (PSN) as the substrate for high performance hot-film sensors for the first time. The breathable PSN facilitates efficient heat exchange and minimizes thermal inertia, resulting in an ultralow detection threshold of 0.0015 m⸱s −1 (1.5 mm⸱s −1 ) and a rapid response time of 86 ± 8.9 ms, thereby placing it among the best-performing airflow sensors reported to date. Comparative studies with the gold-standard polysomnography demonstrate the PSN sensor's high accuracy in noninvasive breath-to-breath interval measurement. Furthermore, we developed a real-time OSA intervention system. The system detected prolonged breath-to-breath intervals in real time and triggered pillow actuation, demonstrating the feasibility of closed-loop positional intervention for apnea-related respiratory events. This work provides a cost-effective strategy for high-performance airflow sensors, and offers a comfortable, efficient home-based OSA management solution.

PVA functionalized kag-MOF-enabled high performance, wide-range humidity sensor for plant microclimate monitoring
abstract: Regulation of microclimate humidity is vital for optimal performance across biological, environmental, and agricultural systems. In greenhouse cultivation, the relative humidity (RH) at the leaf boundary layer significantly influences plant transpiration, metabolism, and yield. However, achieving high-performance humidity sensing in greenhouses remains challenging. Herein, we report a dual mode (AC impedance/DC resistance), wide-range humidity sensor based on Kagome-type metal–organic framework (kag-MOF), evaluated in both its as-synthesized and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-functionalized forms for plant monitoring. PVA functionalization enhances hydrophilicity and adsorption kinetics by increasing the density of hydrophilic sites, thereby improving the sensor's response ( % ) behavior. Compared with the kag-MOF (32–96% RH range), the PVA/kag-MOF sensor extends the measurable humidity-response range to 0–96% RH, yielding DC and absolute AC sensitivities of 0.5486%/%RH (R 2 = 0.9716) and ~0.053%/%RH (R 2 ≈ 0.99), respectively, over the common 32–96% RH fitting range. It also exhibits minimum response ( τ res ) and recovery ( τ rec ) times of 21 s and 36 s, respectively with a low-humidity hysteresis error ( γ H ) of ±2.55% of full-scale deflection ( FSD ). Furthermore, the sensor demonstrates long-term operational stability exceeding 70 days, excellent humidity selectivity (anti-crossing with CO₂), and very low cross-sensitivity to temperature over 25 °C to 100 °C (<10%). The developed sensor is tested for plant monitoring, Solanum lycopersicum (tomato) and Solanum melongena (eggplant), revealing that maintaining an ambient RH of approximately 63% provides the most favorable visible plant response among the selected RH regimes tested. These findings underline the immense potential of PVA/kag-MOF as a highly stable, CO₂-tolerant humidity-sensing platform for precise, real-time monitoring of plant microclimates under controlled conditions.

Effects of biochar surface hydrophilic groups on the selective mining of seawater calcium and magnesium
abstract: Seawater mining is a sustainable strategy for mineral exploitation, yet achieving high calcium (Ca) and magnesium (Mg) selectivity remains challenging due to the complex seawater matrix. We herein propose the introduction of biochar as an effective photothermal converter to induce localized subsurface supersaturation, thereby facilitating selective Ca/Mg mineralization. By introducing biochars pyrolyzed under varying temperatures (400–800 °C), the effects of surface hydrophilic groups on the selective mining of seawater Ca/Mg were explored. At day 5, low-temperature (low-T) biochars rich in hydrophilic groups achieve a Ca capture of 0.42 ± 0.11 mmol/g with a high Ca/Mg ratio of 4.34. This selectivity arises because Ca2+ complexed by oxygen-containing hydrophilic groups serves as a template for orderly crystal growth. In sharp contrast, high-temperature (high-T) biochars capture more Ca (0.65 ± 0.12 mmol/g) but with a dropped Ca/Mg ratio of 1.99. For high-T biochars, rapid photothermal evaporation yields high localized supersaturation. This severe condition induces rapid but nonselective precipitation, further entrapping the more soluble Mg2+ into the Ca-bearing minerals. Interestingly, despite higher Mg impurities, the entrapped Mg-stabilized Ca(OH)2 and amorphous carbonates significantly enhance the reactivity of the resulting minerals, elevating reversible CO2 uptake up to 0.35 mmol/g. Consequently, biochar surface hydrophilic groups act as a critical switch to tailor either high-purity or highly reactive calcium feedstocks. These findings elucidate the fundamental role of biochar interfacial chemistry in mediating selective crystallization, offering a practical route to effectively mine seawater minerals.

abstract: Mathane pyrolysis is considered one of the protagoinsts of the energy transition as it splits methane into solid carbon and hydrogen without producing CO2. While the reaction has been studied using many substartes, its modelling is difficults as carbon accumulates in the reactor which affect therefore methae conversion. Kinetic modelling are often limited to the consideration of a pseudohomogeneous reaction rate expression coupled with an exponential decay whose parameters are empirically determined. Here, we imputate catalyst deactivation to the carbon deposition therefore obtaining a model who depends only on the intrinsic kinetic constant. Kinetic parameters were determined from pyrolytic carbon deposition-induced changes in the mesoporous structure of a wood-charcoal-derived carbon catalyst. Methane pyrolysis was investigated in a packed bed reactor over 950-1000 C and 4-40 h time-on-stream (TOS). BET analyses of the fresh and spent catalysts revealed a progressive decrease in specific surface area and pore volume, attributed to continuous pyrolytic carbon deposition. The catalyst exhibited an initial rapid deactivation followed by a quasi-stabilization regime characterized by progressive pore mouth blockage and a restructuring of pore network. During this regime, sustained activity was predominantly depended on the thermal energy supplied and the auto-catalytic contribution of deposited carbon. For extended TOS (> 20 h), a densely fused pyrolytic carbon-- catalyst (PC-CC) material was formed for both 950 C and 1000 C tests, exhibiting physical properties comparable to industrial N990 carbon black based on ASTM characterization. A mathematical model was developed to capture the pore blocking mechanism for the estimation of intrinsic kinetic constant, effectiveness factor, and Thiele modulus. Model prediction showed good agreement with experimental data, especially for short-duration test (TOS <6 h).

abstract: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (LMFP) is a promising high-voltage cathode for lithium-ion batteries, owing to its low cost and excellent safety, yet its practical application remains constrained by intrinsically low electronic conductivity, sluggish Li+ diffusion kinetics, and structural instability associated with Mn3+-induced Jahn-Teller distortion. Here, Nb-doped LMFP composites are synthesized via a lattice-engineering strategy where Nb5+ is incorporated into the octahedral transition-metal sites to simultaneously regulate lattice structure, charge transport, and Li+ migration behavior. At the structural level, the substitution of Mn2+/Fe2+ with Nb5+ ions induces controlled lattice expansion and local strain relaxation, leading to refined primary particles, narrowed particle-size distribution, and highly graphitized carbon coating. At the electronic level, the high-valence Nb5+ donor introduces an n-type doping effect via charge compensation, substantially increasing carrier concentration (by 15.8-fold) and elevating electrical conductivity to 5.30 × 10-4 S cm-1 (17-fold enhancement). At the electronic band-structure level, DFT calculations reveal that Nb 4d orbital hybridization with O 2p and Mn/Fe 3d states modifies electronic structure near the valence band maximum, weakens the Li-O covalent interaction, and stabilizes the Li+ migration pathway, thereby lowering the activation energy barrier for Li+ hopping along the [010] channel from 1.72 eV to 1.24 eV. As a result, the optimized LMFP-0.7% cathode delivers a high discharge capacity of 153.19 mAh g-1 at 0.1 C and retains 99.98 mAh g-1 after 200 cycles at 5 C. This work provides Nb5+-induced coupled lattice-electronic regulation that enhances electronic transport, accelerates Li+ kinetics, and reinforces structural stability for Mn-rich LMFP cathodes.

abstract: Catalytic upcycling of polyolefin waste to valuable chemicals via hydrogenolysis is a promising strategy; however, developing Ru-based catalysts with low gas selectivity without compromising catalytic activity for the hydrogenolysis of polyethylene remains a significant challenge. Herein, we demonstrate that incorporating strong basic sites into the support can suppress gas product formation while maintaining high activity in the hydrogenolysis of LDPE. La2O3-doped CeO2-supported Ru (Ru/La2O3-CeO2) served as a highly active heterogeneous catalyst, effectively mitigating gas production (yield: 4.6%, CH4 2.5%) and providing valuable liquid chemicals and waxes with a high yield of 95% at 513 K. Furthermore, at 523 K, the catalyst achieved both low gas selectivity (5.0%) and a high reaction rate of 16.8 greacted PE gcatalyst-1 h-1 at 99% conversion. Comprehensive characterization (including H2-TPR, XRD, TEM, XAS, CO2-TPD and XPS) revealed that the introduction of La2O3 into CeO2 generated strong basic sites, which reduced Ru particle size via metal-support interactions. These smaller Ru particles suppressed the consecutive C–C bond cleavage of LDPE, thereby significantly inhibiting CH4 formation. This work highlights the pivotal role of support basicity in tuning metal particle size for selective polyolefin upcycling.

abstract: The chilling storage process in the meat processing industry generates high-strength effluents characterized by complex lipid matrices and recalcitrant proteinaceous residues, causing severe environmental pollution. This large volume of contaminated wastewater not only hinders the circular water economy but also poses severe allergenic cross-contamination risks for meat products. The current work explores the integrated multi-staged microbubble-enhanced cold plasma activation (MB-CPA) strategy for complete remediation of real chicken-processing wastewater. First, bubble flotation removed the larger fat fragments, de-bulking wastewater by reducing the turbidity and total suspended solids (TSS) by 99 and 92%, respectively. Subsequently, exposure to MB-CPA served as a critical oxidative intervention to achieve effective reduction of recalcitrant spiked egg-protein (egg white and yolk at ∼ 28 mg/L allergens, thus neutralizing the primary biological risk to water circularity. Thereafter, a granulated activated carbon (GAC) column served as a physicochemical sink, reducing inorganic ions, metals, and residual organics to well below the regulated limits. In this way, the integrated system yielded a clean effluent that complied with discharge standards, making it suitable for industrial recycling. A preliminary Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) suggested that the integrated MB-CPA workflow provides a mandatory risk-mitigation profile, which justifies its energy-intensive nature with a high operational footprint. These findings suggest that the proposed strategy is a practical and scalable solution, offering a blueprint for transforming high-strength food effluents into reliable resources for sustainable, circular production.

abstract: Al/Ti co-doped LiFePO4/C was synthesized via high-temperature (660-780 °C) calcination of the precursors obtained by spray drying sand-milled slurries. The effects of Al/Ti co-doping and calcination temperature on morphological evolution and electrochemical performance of the materials were systematically investigated. Al/Ti co-doping reduces the band gap and shifts the conduction band minimum toward the Fermi level, effectively improving electronic conductivity. Furthermore, doping with high-valence cations effectively shortens the b-axis lattice parameters, thereby enhancing Li⁺ diffusion kinetics. At an optimal calcination temperature of 720 °C, the corresponding sample exhibits the superior electrochemical performance. It delivers a discharge specific capacity of 160.45 mAh/g at 0.1 C, representing an 8.8% improvement over the undoped counterpart (147.48 mAh/g). Moreover, it demonstrates excellent rate capability with 136.6 mAh/g at 5 C, highlighting its potential for fast-charging applications. This work demonstrates that a synergistic Al/Ti co-doping strategy coupled with an optimized calcination temperature effectively resolves the severe capacity decay of LiFePO4 at high rates. The approach, fully compatible with industrial spray‐drying and calcination processes, provides a straightforward and scalable pathway for the design of high‐performance, fast‐charging cathode materials.

Magnetically assisted micromixing in a Y-mixer probed by the Dushman–Villermaux reaction
abstract: Reactive micromixing in laminar magnetocolloidal Poiseuille microflows is investigated within a Y-mixer co-actuated by a rotating magnetic field (RMF). The Dushman–Villermaux system, comprising proton-coupled instantaneous and fast concurrent reactions fed through distinct inlets (protons versus borate/iodate/iodide), is employed as a sensitive chemical probe of molecular-scale segregation. Central to this work is whether RMF-induced intensification of macromixing necessarily cascades to molecular-scale homogenization, a question governed by the competition among magnetic, chemical, and hydrodynamic timescales. Three magnetic nanoparticle (MNP) injection strategies—proton-side, borate-side, and symmetric—are examined to isolate the respective convective contributions of spin-up flow and the Kelvin body force (KBF). Our findings reveal that magnetic forcing resulting from the interplay between magnetic torque and the KBF does not always yield monotonic improvements in reactive micromixing. While low-to-moderate forcing may exacerbate molecular-scale segregation, high-intensity forcing triggers transverse convection that significantly enhances micromixing. This behavior is dictated by the competition between magnetic-convection and Dushman-reaction timescales. Of the configurations examined, borate-side MNP injection emerges as the most effective strategy for reducing the segregation index. Ultimately, the RMF influence is governed by the intricate interplay of flow topology, MNP spatial distribution, and reaction–transport competition. Elucidating these coupled mechanisms paves the way toward magnetic process intensification and provides a robust theoretical framework for the precision control of reactive micro- and nanofluidic systems.

Lubricant-assisted powder alignment using a damped AC magnetic field for high-energy-density Nd–Fe–B magnets prepared via the pressless process
abstract: Fine Nd–Fe–B powders are essential for fabricating sintered magnets with high intrinsic coercivity; however, their magnetic alignment is hindered by the low magnetic torque and high resistance to particle rotation and rearrangement encountered during pressless processing. In this study, a damped AC magnetic-field waveform and 2-nonanone lubrication were applied to improve the alignment of fine Nd–Fe–B powders in the pressless process. Repeated impulse-field application induced post-alignment particle rearrangement and green-body cracking, whereas the damped AC waveform promoted progressive particle rotation and rearrangement while preserving green-body integrity. The addition of 2-nonanone further reduced interparticle friction and increased μ0Mr from 1.315 T without lubricant to 1.408 T under 0.5 wt.% lubricant addition. However, increasing the lubricant content also increased the residual carbon concentration and eventually reversed the μ0Hc-enhancing response to annealing. In a high-carbon magnet, the NdOHCO₃ triple-junction phase transformed during annealing into spatially separated c-Nd₂O₃ and tetragonal Nd-carbide phases. This transformation was accompanied by localized strain at the Nd-carbide/Nd₂Fe₁₄B interface, which is considered a major reason for the negative μ0Hc response. Hydrogen-assisted processing reduced the residual carbon content from 2,290 to 740 ppm and changed the annealing-induced μ0Hc response from -0.159 to +0.217 T. These results demonstrate that simultaneous control of particle mobility during magnetic alignment and lubricant-derived carbon during thermal processing is essential for achieving high energy density in the pressless process.

abstract: The lack of electronic materials that properly replicate the sensing capabilities of human skin has motivated the search for soft systems that transduce mechanical stimuli through intrinsic physicochemical mechanisms. Piezoionic hydrogels, which under mechanical deformation generate ion flux, offer a promising route toward such functionality. Here we investigate the piezoionic response of a photocurable, self-healing semi-interpenetrating polymer network hydrogel composed of poly(vinyl alcohol), acrylic acid, and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. By systematically varying cation mobility using a series of alkali metal chlorides, we correlate ionic transport with electromechanical output across planar and sandwich electrode configurations under the application of both compressive and tensile mechanical stimuli. Pressure-induced gradients in ionic concentration produce measurable voltage and current outputs when cation and anion mobilities are mismatched, providing a mechanistic analogue to biological mechanoreceptors. We further demonstrate that 3D-printed architecture enhances the piezoionic signal through strain concentration and retain functionality after damage due to the hydrogel's autonomous healing. Finally, we implement these materials as self-powered biometric sensors and mechanical energy harvesters. These results establish a milestone in the design guidelines for ionically driven tactile electronics and highlight that piezoionic materials are cornerstone materials for the next generation of soft robotics, wearable systems, and health-monitoring technologies.

Ni substitution-driven synergetic enhancement of microwave absorption and heat transfer in C/Co1-xNix foams
abstract: The ongoing integration, miniaturization, and high-frequency evolution of modern electronics impose an imperative demand for bifunctional materials integrating superior thermal conduction and efficient microwave absorption; nevertheless, the inherent trade-off between these two functionalities remains a critical obstacle restricting practical deployment. Herein, we report a straightforward one-step PVP-mediated annealing route to synthesize porous C/Co1-xNix foams (x = 0–1.0), wherein a Ni-substitution engineering is proposed to break the aforementioned performance limitation, with its feasibility comprehensively corroborated by density functional theory simulations and experimental characterizations. Theoretical calculations reveal that Ni-substitution finely modulates the electronic density, interfacial charge redistribution, work function (Wf), magnetic moment, and electron/phonon density of states of the hybrid foams. Experimentally, incremental Ni substitution triggers distinct structural rearrangement and gradual decline in SBET, alongside tunable lattice defects as well as tailored electrical and thermal conductivities. Meanwhile, the inherent interconnected porous architecture establishes unimpeded electron/phonon migration pathways for enhanced heat conductance, generates multiple EMW scattering and optimizes impedance matching for wide-band microwave dissipation. Benefiting from compositional optimization, the C/Co0.7Ni0.3 sample with 30 % Ni-substitution delivers a minimal reflection loss (-29.54 dB), an efficacious absorption bandwidth (5.52 GHz), and a high thermal conductivity (4.36 W m-1 K-1). Such outstanding comprehensive performances surpass most state-of-the-art bifunctional analogues, promising extensive applications in 5G/6G communications, aerospace equipment, and intelligent electronic devices.

In2S3/TiO2 heterostructures for enhanced photocatalytic nitrogen fixation under ambient conditions
abstract: The development of sustainable routes for ammonia production under ambient conditions is a critical challenge, driven by the high energy demand and carbon footprint of the Haber-Bosch process. Photocatalytic N 2 fixation has emerged as a promising alternative; however, conventional TiO 2 -based systems suffer from rapid charge-carrier recombination, resulting in poor efficiency. Herein, we report the design of a noble-metal-free In 2 S 3 /TiO 2 heterostructure photocatalyst for photocatalytic N 2 fixation to NH 4 + under mild conditions. The coupling of TiO 2 nanoparticles with In 2 S 3 aims to promote charge carrier separation and suppress electron-hole recombination, thereby overcoming the intrinsic limitations of bare TiO 2 . Structural, morphological, optical, and electronic characterizations confirmed the successful formation of the heterojunction and the strong interfacial interaction between the two semiconductors. UV–Vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy revealed an extended light absorption toward the visible region, while photoluminescence and XPS analyses evidenced enhanced charge separation and interfacial charge redistribution. Among the investigated compositions, the In 2 S 3 (10%)/TiO 2 sample exhibited the best photocatalytic performance, achieving an NH 3 production of 214.0 μmol·g cat −1 after 3 h of irradiation, significantly higher than pristine TiO 2 . Experimental and DFT investigations demonstrated the formation of a type-II heterojunction, promoting electron migration from In 2 S 3 to TiO 2 and suppressing electron-hole recombination. The combined experimental and theoretical results highlight the potential of noble-metal-free In 2 S 3 /TiO 2 heterostructures as efficient photocatalysts for sustainable N 2 fixation under ambient conditions.

Mechanochemical engineering of g-C3N4/TiO2 photocatalysts for optimized interfacial coupling
abstract: Ball milling has emerged as a rapid and solvent-free strategy for the synthesis of semiconductor heterojunctions, avoiding prolonged thermal treatments and extensive post-synthesis processing. In this work, g-C 3 N 4 /TiO 2 heterojunction photocatalysts were prepared by mechanochemical ball milling at different milling frequencies and durations to elucidate the influence of synthesis parameters on their structural, optoelectronic, and photocatalytic properties. Comprehensive physicochemical and optoelectronic characterization showed that mild milling promotes efficient interfacial coupling while preserving the crystallinity, porosity, and π-conjugated framework of g-C 3 N 4 , thereby enabling efficient interfacial charge transfer. In contrast, excessive milling induces particle fragmentation, partial amorphization, defect formation, and pore collapse, resulting in impaired charge transport and enhanced charge-carrier recombination. The photocatalytic performance of the resulting composites was evaluated by monitoring the visible-light-driven degradation of bisphenol A (BPA) in aqueous solution. All composites outperformed the parent materials, confirming the beneficial effect of mechanochemically induced interfacial coupling. The composite prepared at 15 Hz for 15 min exhibited the highest photocatalytic activity, achieving 33.4% BPA degradation and 14.4% TOC removal after 180 min of visible-light irradiation. Photoluminescence, time-correlated single-photon counting, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, transient photocurrent, and reactive oxygen species analyses demonstrated that mild mechanochemical treatment promotes efficient interfacial charge separation and transport. The optimized composite exhibited the highest photocurrent response, reaching approximately 0.26 μA cm −2 , and the lowest charge-transfer resistance (154 kΩ compared with 482 kΩ for pristine g-C 3 N 4 ), together with enhanced formation of reactive oxygen species, including O 2 •- . The combined optoelectronic and ROS results indicate efficient interfacial electronic coupling while preserving strongly reducing electrons associated predominantly with g-C 3 N 4 -derived electronic states. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of mechanochemical synthesis for engineering g-C 3 N 4 /TiO 2 heterojunction photocatalysts while providing fundamental structure-property-performance relationships that support the rational design and optimization of semiconductor heterojunctions for visible-light-driven photocatalytic water treatment.

Infrared light-induced photo-chargeable flexible supercapacitor utilizing InAs quantum dots – two-dimensional reduced graphene oxide composites
abstract: Photo-chargeable supercapacitors integrate light harvesting and energy storage in a single device, making them promising candidates for the next-generation smart energy systems. Herein, a symmetrical infrared (IR) light-responsive supercapacitor was fabricated by depositing two-dimensional (2D) reduced graphene oxide (rGO) sheets, followed by indium arsenide (InAs) quantum dots (QDs) on both rigid and flexible substrates. Upon IR illumination, the InAs QDs-2D rGO composite framework yields a remarkable three-fold enhancement in areal capacitance. The synergistic interplay between photo-induced carrier generation within the QD layer and the intrinsic capacitive behavior of rGO sheets not only effectively amplifies electrochemical performance under illumination but also stabilizes the system under ambient conditions. Notably, nearly 50% of the photo-induced capacitance change was preserved after turning off the light even after 3000 charge-discharge cycles, confirming the durable photoactive behavior of QDs-2D heterointerface. During implementation on flexible substrates, the device exhibited ~97% capacitance retention under mechanical bending. Electrochemical and impedance spectroscopy measurements revealed that surface charge storage at the electrode/electrolyte interface dominates under dark conditions, whereas photo-induced charge storage mechanisms are dominated by diffusion-limited processes. Hence, an InAs QDs-2D rGO heterointerface demonstrates high electrochemical performance and good stability, showing strong potential for integration into both IR and white ambient light-powered, next-generation wearable devices.
