abstract: Kojic acid (KA) is a high-value fungal secondary metabolite used in cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, but commercial production is limited by costly substrates and inefficient recovery. This study developed an integrated bioprocess for KA production by Aspergillus flavus . Agitated cultivation with glucose as the optimal carbon source markedly improved biosynthesis. An initial glucose concentration of 80 g/L, corn steep liquor as the nitrogen source, and an initial pH of 3.6 provided the highest performance in shake-flask cultivation, producing 47.0 g/L KA with a yield of 0.61 g/g. Under batch bioreactor cultivation, these conditions were successfully translated, increasing KA production to 52.8 g/L with a yield of 0.66 g/g. Fed-batch cultivation using pure glucose further increased KA production to 80.2 g/L. Replacement of pure glucose with non-detoxified glucose-rich SBP hydrolysate enabled efficient co-utilization of mixed sugars, producing 38.0 g/L KA in batch culture and 72.3 g/L in fed-batch fermentation, representing one of the highest reported KA titers from a lignocellulosic hydrolysate. For downstream processing, ethyl acetate extraction with 35% ( w / v ) ammonium sulphate significantly enhanced KA recovery, increasing extraction yields by 27% and 62% for glucose- and SBP hydrolysate-based fermentation broths, respectively, at >99% purity. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating renewable SBP hydrolysate with an intensified recovery strategy for KA bioproduction, while highlighting the need for further process and product-safety validation before downstream application.

Oxygen-mediated kinetic pathways governing selective and total oxidation over transition-metal oxides
abstract: Selective oxidation of hydrocarbons over transition-metal oxide catalysts is pivotal to chemical manufacturing, yet its broader implementation remains limited by competing pathways for total oxidation. This work investigates how selective oxidation and total oxidation proceed on oxide surfaces through an oxygen-mediated mechanistic hypothesis, using oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (ODH–C 2 ) as a representative reaction. Two catalysts, SnO 2 − NiO and MoVTeNbO, were examined using a common mean-field kinetic description that distinguishes effective non-dissociated and dissociated oxygen states associated with distinct oxygen-mediated pathways, functionally denoted as the electrophilic and nucleophilic oxygen pools, respectively. Activation energies were seeded using UBI–QEP relationships, whereas pre-exponential factors were determined from transition-state theory, statistical thermodynamics, and microscopic reversibility. The kinetic parameters were then refined by regression analysis. Within the adopted mechanistic representation, selectivity emerges from the balance between these oxygen states and the corresponding reaction pathways. Changes in this balance redistribute reaction flux between selective C–H activation and overoxidation routes, increasingly favoring total oxidation toward CO and CO 2 . This balance favors ethylene formation over MoVTeNbO, whereas SnO 2 − NiO more readily drives carbon-containing intermediates toward CO 2 . The determined kinetic and thermodynamic parameters are interpreted as effective, model-dependent quantities. The microkinetic model, applied to 2–10 atm (625–753 K), reveals that SnO 2 − NiO becomes markedly more active under pressure while MoVTeNbO retains higher ethylene selectivity, guiding reactor design under pressurized conditions for each catalyst. These findings provide a reaction-engineering basis for understanding how these pathways govern selectivity.

abstract: This work presents the development and assessment of a one-dimensional model for the reduction section of an industrial direct reduced iron (DRI) shaft furnace. Implemented in Aspen Custom Modeler, the model couples mass, energy, and momentum balances with a shrinking-core formulation for sequential iron oxide reduction. The model was compared with a reported industrial syngas operating point from the ArcelorMittal Contrecœur plant, reproducing the reference metallization degree of 93.7%. Refining the methane-related kinetics improved the prediction of carburization and outlet methane, reducing the solid-phase error from 1.14% to 0.42%. The resulting model framework was subsequently applied to predictive scenarios involving pure hydrogen, hydrogen containing residual water, oxygen-assisted hydrogen, and ammonia-assisted mixtures. Although pure hydrogen provided faster intrinsic kinetics, reactor performance was strongly limited by the thermal balance, leaving poorly active regions. Reducing the reactor length from 10 to 5 m preserved the target metallization with only a 0.76% increase in hydrogen flowrate. Residual water decreased metallization at constant total flowrate, confirming the importance of upstream moisture removal. Localized O₂ injection provided internal thermal compensation, with an optimal position near 0.2 m, recovering the metallization loss caused by a lower inlet H₂ temperature, but increasing H₂ consumption and H₂O formation. Ammonia-assisted operation achieved a maximum metallization of 97.3% at 5 mol% NH₃, whereas higher fractions reduced performance because of the endothermic cracking penalty. Overall, low-carbon DRI operation is governed by the interaction among kinetics, gas composition, thermal balance, reactor geometry, and flowrate management.

Dissolution of precipitated salt under suppressed brine backflow in microfluidic porous media
abstract: In a wide range of natural and engineering systems, multiphase flow in porous media is accompanied by salt precipitation, which can significantly alter pore structure and reduce permeability. While salt deposition is commonly associated with persistent clogging, its evolution under conditions without bulk flow remains poorly understood. In this study, we use microfluidic experiments to investigate the fate of precipitated salt under quasi-static conditions. Salt deposits are first generated during a gas-brine displacement process, after which a small amount of brine is injected to one side of the chip while a constant gas back pressure is maintained to prevent capillary brine backflow. Under these conditions, time-resolved imaging reveals that previously formed salt deposits gradually dissolve. Surprisingly, water can return into regions containing dry carbon dioxide and precipitated salt crystals, disconnected from the continuous brine phase by a relatively large distance. It accumulates around crystals, dissolving them and forming separate brine “clusters”. The resulting phase distribution remains highly heterogeneous, with isolated brine regions that do not restore effective flow pathways. Possible mechanisms for water transport to the isolated salt deposits, including surface transport and water-vapor diffusion through the gas phase, are discussed and evaluated by comparing their characteristic timescales using simplified model analyses. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized post-drying dissolution pathway in porous media, demonstrating that precipitated salt can remain dynamically active even without observable bulk brine reconnection. The results demonstrate that drying does not necessarily terminate pore-scale evolution, providing a new perspective on the long-term evolution of salt precipitation in porous media.

title: Kinetic modeling of mixed-acid nitration: From measurable rate constants to transferable parameters
abstract: Nitration in mixed acids, the ternary HNO 3 -H 2 SO 4 -H 2 O system, is among the most industrially important and hazardous reaction classes in organic chemistry, yet its kinetic behavior remains incompletely rationalized after more than a century of investigation. The central difficulty is not merely experimental: it is structural. In a strongly non-ideal medium where the concentration of the active electrophile, the nitronium ion (NO 2 + ), depends nonlinearly on acid composition, temperature, and water activity, any kinetic parameter measured under one set of conditions carries limited predictive value under another. This review examines the problem of kinetic modeling in mixed-acid nitration from a framework perspective, organizing the available approaches, i.e. empirical rate laws, activity-corrected mechanistic models, thermodynamic-kinetic coupled descriptions, computational pre-screening, and data-driven methods, according to their underlying assumptions, data requirements, and transferability. The Marziano acidity function ( M a ) and the related transformation of observed rate constants (k obs ) into intrinsic rate constants (k*) are identified as the most powerful currently available tools for obtaining kinetic parameters that are independent of acid composition and transferable across substrates and reactor configurations. The role of continuous flow microreactor technology as an enabling platform for reliable kinetic determination is critically assessed. Persistent gaps, including the absence of standardized protocols, the scarcity of validated thermodynamic models for ionic species, and the limited coverage of non-aromatic substrates, are identified, and directions toward a unified, multiscale kinetic framework for mixed-acid nitration are outlined.

Dual-functional nanozymatic microspheres reverse intervertebral disc degeneration via ferroptosis inhibition and targeted saRNA-mediated microenvironment regeneration
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is driven by an aggressive microenvironment of oxidative stress, inflammation, and cellular ferroptosis. Herein, we develop an intelligent, microenvironment-responsive hybrid microsphere platform (GMPRW) for advanced IVDD therapy. The system is fabricated by tethering nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs)-targeted, Col2a1 saRNA-loaded nanoparticles (PRWs) onto nanozymatic metal-phenolic network-coated GelMA microspheres (GMs) via reversible boronate ester bonds. Mechanistically, the GMs shroud scavenges noxious ROS, chelates iron pools, and up-regulates GPX4, suppressing apoptotic and ferroptotic cascades while repolarizing macrophages from M1 to a pro-healing M2 phenotype. Under pathological triggers, the smart boronate ester linkages fracture to liberate targeted PRWs, achieving precise intracellular saRNA delivery to drive long-term, autonomous extracellular matrix rejuvenation. In vivo, local GMPRW delivery robustly thwarts structural collapse and mitigates discogenic pain. This sequential combinatorial strategy offers an advanced platform for precise intervertebral disc engineering.

AI-accelerated hybrid reactive-nonreactive molecular dynamics simulation for polymer cross-linking
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulation based on reactive forcefield enables atomic-scale investigation of polymer cross-linking processes but is limited by high computational cost. In polymer cross-linking simulations, a large fraction of simulation time is spent in chemically inactive stages, during which the continuous use of a reactive forcefield is inefficient. In this work, an artificial intelligence-accelerated hybrid reactive-nonreactive molecular dynamics framework is developed, which adaptively switches between reactive and non-reactive forcefields to improve computational efficiency while maintaining chemical accuracy. A machine learning model is trained on reactive molecular dynamics trajectories to predict continuous reaction probability using physically interpretable structural, chemical, and energetic descriptors extracted from simulation outputs. This probabilistic criterion enables reliable identification of low-reactivity states and stable forcefield switching without manually defined heuristic rules. The proposed approach is applied to the cross-linking process of epoxy as a representative example. Compared with full reactive forcefield simulations, the hybrid approach achieves up to 80% reduction in computational cost. Structural and mechanical properties of the cross-linked epoxy network obtained from the hybrid simulations show excellent agreement with full reactive forcefield results and experimental reference data. This work provides a framework that accelerates polymer cross-linking simulations while preserving key reaction chemistry, network evolution, and final material properties. Using epoxy-amine cross-linking as a representative case, the study establishes a proof-of-concept strategy for coupling chemically faithful reactive sampling with efficient nonreactive relaxation. The framework may be extended to other reaction-relaxation systems after system-specific descriptor construction, threshold calibration, and independent validation.

HKUST-1/polymer/carbon nanotube ternary composite adsorbents for high CO2 uptake and low-voltage joule heating capability
abstract: Electrothermal regeneration of adsorbents is emerging as a promising strategy for on-demand CO 2 desorption beyond conventional thermal or vacuum-based approaches. Herein, we fabricate free-standing HKUST-1/polyethyleneimine (PEI)/single-walled carbon nanotube (CNT) ternary composite films and systematically vary their PEI and CNT contents to achieve high CO 2 adsorption capacity and low-voltage Joule heating capability for electrically assisted regeneration. In these composites, PEI acts as a molecular adhesive bridging HKUST-1 crystallites and the CNT network, while CNT percolation establishes an electrically conductive pathway for direct resistive heating. This synergistic architecture enhances CO 2 adsorption at room temperature under dry CO 2 conditions. Among the compositions investigated, the HKUST-1/PEI0.5/CNT2 adsorbent achieves a CO 2 uptake of 5.85 mmol g −1 at 100 kPa and 25 °C, together with a low desorption temperature peak at 58 °C. Under ambient Joule heating conditions, this composite reaches 94 °C at 4 V within 210 s, followed by passive cooling to near ambient temperature within 160 s. Overall, this work establishes an integrated composite design that couples high CO 2 adsorption with low-voltage, Joule-heating capability.

Single pellet profile reactor for measuring concentration and temperature patterns in porous catalyst pellets
abstract: Understanding coupled transport and reaction phenomena within porous catalyst pellets is crucial for the optimization ofheterogeneous catalytic processes. Nonetheless, experimental access to intra-pellet concentration profiles under industri-ally relevant conditions remains limited. In this work, we present a second-generation single-pellet profile reactor (SPPR)that enables simultaneous measurement of intra-pellet concentration profiles and surface temperature distributions. Thegas composition inside the pellet is measured using a movable sampling capillary and mass spectrometry analysis. Thecombination of an infrared thermography camera and a conical mirror inside the reactor enables the measurement ofcatalyst surface temperature. The reactor operates under industrially relevant conditions and allows investigations atdifferent feed temperatures and feed ratios at steady-state. The capabilities of the setup are demonstrated for CO2methanation on a cylindrical 5 mm Ni/γ-Al2O3 catalyst pellet. Pronounced intra-pellet CO2 concentration gradientsare observed despite a stoichiometric educt feed ratio, whereas H2 exhibits only minor gradients throughout the pellet.The infrared camera measurements reveal a surface temperature increase of up to 25 K with pronounced gradients inflow direction. Apart from these gradients, the pellet remains quasi isothermal at steady state. The presented reactorprovides detailed operando insights into coupled mass and heat transport phenomena at the single-pellet scale and offersa robust experimental basis for model validation and knowledge-based catalyst optimization.

title: Zeolite-supported metal chloride sorbent materials under sorption-enhanced ammonia synthesis reaction conditions for H2 storage: Mechanisms, micro-kinetics and modelling
abstract: Efficient ammonia separation is essential for the intensification of ammonia synthesis processes. Metal halides are promising ammonia sorbents because of strong and reversible interaction with ammonia and possibility to tune sorption strength through variation of metal cation and the support. In this work, MgCl₂-, CaCl₂-, and SrCl₂-supported ZSM-5 materials were investigated under an ammonia-containing atmosphere at absolute pressures of 1–8 bar and temperatures of 50–400 °C. Among the studied sorbents, MgCl₂/ZSM-5 showed the best performance, attributed to the higher charge density of Mg 2+ , which promotes ammonia coordination. Lower salt loadings gave slightly higher apparent coordination numbers, indicating improved accessibility of active sites. During the first formation of the hexaammine complex, MgCl₂/ZSM-5 underwent activation, suggesting structural rearrangement and accelerated ammonia uptake. A mean-field microkinetic model describing stepwise ammonia absorption and desorption was developed, explicitly accounting for the underlying sorption mechanism governed by both kinetic effects and thermodynamic equilibrium. The model was coupled with continuous-flow reactor formulations – continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) or axially-dispersed plug-flow reactor (AD-PFR) – depending on the Péclet number, which characterises the gas-phase transport regime, thereby bridging meso- and reactor-scale phenomena. The model successfully reproduced breakthrough and temperature-programmed desorption experiments, including three distinct desorption peaks associated with progressively stronger ammonia binding. These results identify supported MgCl₂ as a promising sorbent for high-temperature ammonia separation, relevant for hydrogen storage and transport applications, while highlighting the need for mechanically stable supports to accommodate structural expansion during ammine formation.

Solar photoreforming enables hydrogen-evolving valorisation of diverse industrial wastewaters
abstract: Treatment of industrial wastewaters faces challenges related to their broad variability. On occasions, complex pollutant composition and structure or high content of noxious contaminants may hinder typical activated sludge biological processes. This may complicate treatment and ultimate valorisation of industrial effluents. As an alternative that could be universally applied to aqueous organic waste, photocatalytic reforming, i.e. photoreforming, is a robust technology that can be activated by solar irradiation. In this work, H₂ production under simulated solar light proved efficient from fruit juice or ethoxylate surfactant wastewaters using a highly active Pt/TiO 2 photocatalyst, resulting in fast evolution from initial stages at rates up to 0.6 or 2.0 mmol g −1 h −1 , respectively. The more recalcitrant and opaque papermaking wastewaters required an induction period before hydrogen evolved at 15–30 μmol g −1 h −1 . As a major advancement, the photoreforming of a challenging effluent from ethoxylated surfactants production under natural sunlight, in an outdoor solar plant setup based on a flat panel reactor, was conducted for ten days of continuous operation. Steady and consistent decreases in chemical oxygen demand and acid neutralisation evidenced satisfactory evolution of physicochemical parameters towards discharge compliance levels. Moreover, H 2 evolution rates correlated with solar irradiance and weather conditions, proving the feasibility of wastewater valorisation by solar photoreforming.

Acoustic-anisotropy-engineered sapphire fibers for high-sensitivity quasi-distributed ultrasonic thermometry beyond 1800 °C
abstract: Spatially resolved temperature monitoring in extreme environments is critical for aerospace propulsion, energy systems, and high-temperature manufacturing, yet remains limited by the lack of sensing platforms that combine ultrahigh-temperature stability with distributed readout. Here, orientation-controlled and irradiation-stable sapphire fibers were grown using laser-heated pedestal growth (LHPG) method to serve as acoustic waveguide media for ultrasonic thermometry. Simulations and acoustic measurements reveal significant acoustic anisotropy in sapphire fibers, identifying the a-axis sapphire fiber as the optimal acoustic waveguide for enhanced thermometric sensitivity. At 1800°C, the a-axis fiber exhibits sensitivities of 19.04 ns·°C-1·m-1 and 45.64 ns·°C-1·m-1 in P-wave and T2 S-wave modes, respectively, and achieves a temperature resolution of 0.09°C, representing a record-low value for crystal-based UTS to the best of our knowledge. Building on this anisotropic acoustic response, quasi-distributed thermometry was realized through two sapphire-fiber architectures. The diameter-modulated fiber provided a compact three-zone sensing configuration up to 1800°C, with a temperature resolution better than 0.22°C and a full-scale error of 1.69%. The bundled sapphire-fiber architecture offered a reconfigurable route for high-spatial-resolution thermal-field monitoring, providing 10 sensitive areas with a spatial resolution of 1 cm and enabling stable in situ monitoring of a ~1200°C heat source for over 100 min. This work establishes an anisotropy-engineered sapphire-fiber platform for spatially resolved ultrasonic thermometry in extreme environments.

Controlled transition from hydrothermal carbonization to fulvification for artificial humic substance production from wheat straw
abstract: This study presents a controlled hydrothermal pathway for valorizing wheat straw through carbonization (HTC), humification (HTH), and fulvification (HTF) by systematically varying temperature and alkalinity. Increasing alkalinity and temperature promoted depolymerization and solubilization of lignocellulosic structures, enabling a continuous transition from solid-dominated to liquid-dominated product regimes. HTC produced the highest solid yield (67.5%) and carbon recovery (77.9%), but generated high levels of furfural and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF). Compared with HTC, HTH and HTF strongly suppressed furanic and phenolic compounds, with furfural and HMF reduced to <5 mg/kg DM and total aromatics decreased by >70% in solids and >90% in liquids. HTF reduced solid yield to 3.3% while maximizing the solubility of lactic acid (37.5 g/L) and formic acid (14.6 g/L). At 180 °C, HTF yielded substantially higher liquid-phase total organic carbon (TOC) of 50.66 g/L than HTC (16.03 g/L) and HTH (42.51 g/L). Within HTF, increasing temperature from 180 to 220 °C further enhanced carbon solubilization, with liquid-phase TOC increasing by ~32% to 66.84 g/L, indicating intensified conversion of lignocellulosic carbon into soluble organic products, in contrast to HTC and HTH, where increasing temperature led to a decrease in liquid-phase carbon content. Spectroscopic and thermal analyses showed humic- and fulvic-like structures with enhanced thermal stability at higher alkalinity. These findings show that process tuning enables targeted biomass conversion into energy-rich hydrochar via conventional HTC or more homogeneous, nutrient- and carbon-rich liquid products via HTF, opening new opportunities for agriculture and liquid-phase biorefinery research.

Engineering tunable structure–property relationships in collagen/chitosan scaffolds via 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane-mediated dual crosslinking for cartilage regeneration
abstract: Three-dimensional scaffolds for cartilage tissue engineering require mechanical integrity and controlled degradation while maintaining a bioactive microenvironment. Herein, 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane was employed as a multifunctional organosilane crosslinker to construct collagen/chitosan hybrid scaffolds through epoxy ring-opening and siloxane condensation reactions, generating a covalently integrated organic–inorganic network. This dual crosslinking mechanism enabled tunable regulation of network connectivity and scaffold architecture. Silane incorporation significantly enhanced structural organization and thermal stability, reduced swelling and enzymatic degradation, and increased compressive stiffness in a controllable manner. Spectroscopic analysis confirmed the formation of Si–O–Si networks and polymer–silane linkages, establishing a direct correlation between crosslink density and mechanical reinforcement. Among the tested formulations, the hybrid scaffold exhibited an optimized structure–property profile, supporting sustained proliferation of human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells and human chondrocytes. Under chondrogenic induction, the engineered scaffold upregulated cartilage-specific markers and maintained elevated sulfated glycosaminoglycan production in a cell-type-dependent manner, demonstrating effective coupling between mechanical adaptation and biological functionality. This work establishes an engineering-oriented framework linking GPTMS-mediated hybrid network regulation with tunable structure–property–biofunction relationships, providing a rational strategy for designing mechanically adaptive organic–inorganic hybrid scaffolds for cartilage tissue engineering. The present study primarily focuses on establishing the fundamental structure–property–biofunction relationships of the hybrid scaffolds through comprehensive physicochemical and in vitro biological evaluations, thereby providing a mechanistic basis for subsequent in vivo investigation and translational development.

abstract: Polyurethane foam (PUF) was synthesized from commercial polyether polyol and methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) to provide a representative model polyurethane for chemical upcycling. Due to its crosslinked solid structure, PUF was first liquefied via aminolysis with monoethanolamine (MEA) at 150 °C. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided additional insight into the differences in aminolysis observed under nitrogen and air. Excess MEA was subsequently removed by evaporation at 170 °C, and the remaining solution was aged overnight, yielding phase separation into a polyol-rich fraction (PRF) and 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA) rich phase. While the MDA-rich phase is typically treated as a byproduct, it can serve as a precursor for MDI. The PRF was then catalytically cracked over zeolite catalysts to produce value-added chemicals. A novel one-dimensional (1D) shaped H-MFI zeolite nanorod with enhanced external surface area and mesoporosity may contribute to interactions between polymers and catalysts. Compared to commercial H-ZSM-5, 1D-H-MFI exhibited higher selectivity toward propionaldehyde (61.8 wt% vs. 50.3 wt%) with 50% lower catalyst loading. This two-step strategy demonstrates the potential to upcycle commercial PUF into valuable chemicals.

Crosslinkable xanthene-based polymer enabling cascade-aligned bilayer hole transport for high-performance QLEDs
abstract: We report a xanthene-based polymeric hole transport material (HTM), poly(XBC-co-PBCB), incorporating a benzocyclobutene crosslinkable unit (PBCB) for solution-processed quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). Notably, although this polymer features a non-conjugated backbone system similar to conventional poly(9-vinylcarbazole) (PVK), the incorporation of a rigid π-conjugated xanthene pendant unit enables superior charge transport. This unique structural design provides a deep highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level perfectly suited for the deep HOMO of QDs, while maintaining enhanced thermal stability. As a result, it achieves a hole mobility of 1.51 × 10–5 cm2 V–1s–1 after cross-linking, which is significantly higher than that of PVK. Upon thermal treatment, it forms a cross-linked network, providing excellent solvent resistance that enables robust multilayer device fabrication. Furthermore, a bilayer hole transport structure combining the cross-linked HTM with a thin PVK interlayer enables cascade-aligned energy levels, facilitating efficient hole transport. As a result, QLED devices employing the bilayer HTL exhibit enhanced performance, achieving a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 16.27%, a maximum current efficiency (CE) of 19.04 cd A–1, and an extended operational lifetime (T50) of 10.69 h at an initial luminance of 50,000 cd m–2, representing a sixfold improvement compared to PVK-based devices. These results highlight the effectiveness of crosslinkable xanthene-based HTMs in enabling balanced charge transport and improving device stability in solution-processed QLEDs.

Polarity-driven reversible chain entanglement enables broad-frequency high damping eutectic gels for flexible sensing
abstract: Endowing flexible sensing materials with high-damping properties is a crucial strategy for achieving reliable signal monitoring. However, existing materials generally suffer from a trade-off among broad-frequency response, high damping capacity and mechanical performance. Herein, we propose a confinement strategy mediated by a polarity-induced chain-entanglement to fabricate tough gels integrating high damping with sensitive signal monitoring. The reversible polymer network with a high entanglement density markedly enhances intermolecular chain friction, enabling the gel to maintain a loss factor above 0.75 over a frequency range spanning four orders of magnitude. Meanwhile, the effective chain-entanglement network constrains the deep eutectic solvent within a confined environment, mitigating its detrimental effect on intermolecular interactions. The resulting tough gel exhibits a tensile strength of 7.8 MPa and excellent noise reduction performance in the stable acquisition of electrocardiogram signals under motion conditions. This work provides a scalable design paradigm for the construction of high-performance damping materials.

Heat balance for laboratory-scale vibratory ball mill applications
abstract: To elucidate the extent to which the kinetic energy of an impacting milling sphere is converted into heat, this work develops an energy balance model based on measurements of the surface temperature of the milling vessel in a laboratory-scale vibratory ball mill by using high-speed infrared thermography. The milling sphere motion is inferred from acoustic analysis, where three primary trajectory regimes are identified. Correlation of heating behavior with these regimes showed how impact and resulting heat generation are dependent on collision modes. Based on the rates of heat dissipation and generation as well as the known frequency of collisions, the heat generation per impact is quantified. The effect of the charge material on the amount of heat generated is analyzed for aluminum oxide, activated carbon, polyethylene, and iron. The extent of heat generation does not demonstrate a strong correlation between individual material strength and heat transfer properties, highlighting the necessity of more complex combinations of properties to properly predict mechanochemical heating behavior. Within the parameter space considered here, between 27 and 38% of the kinetic energy of the milling sphere is converted into heat in each collision. Strong, positive relationships also exist when examining the effect of sphere density on heat generated per impact.

Sustainable co-production of fibers and biochemicals from softwood bark: methanol pre-extraction and soda cooking
abstract: Burning wood bark at pulp mills generates biogenic CO 2 emissions, affecting also the aquatic organisms via wastewater treatment plant. With the limited nature of forest resources and the increasing energy self-sufficiency of mills, developing new ways of valorizing bark is imperative. The quality of bark-origin fiber is considerably better than its counterpart xylem, but bark contains more chemically reactive components. Efficient valorization of wood bark is currently hampered by lack of tailored methods of cooking and biochemicals recovery. This study aims to recover fibers and biochemicals from bark and assess their fiber's mechanical properties. Methanol pre-extraction is designed to recover 8 w /w% extractives in their unreacted form prior to cooking. Compared with bark and its resulting pulp, methanol pre-extraction reduced extractive concentrations by 66% and 75%, respectively. Surface of fiber made from post-extracted bark is clearly cleaner than that of the reference ones. Under same H-factor, the 28 w /w% pulp yield of the bark obtained with soda cooking was similar to kraft cooking. To our knowledge, effective delignification using soda is for the first time discovered. Paper sheet made from unrefined bark pulp provides 20 times higher inter-fiber bonding and 2 times higher tensile strength than sheet made from counterpart wood pulp. Valorizing these unique fibers, biochemicals, and other bark components instead of burning them for energy could create economic value for the forest industry while utilizing 200 million cubic meters of bark currently wasted globally. This approach could provide a carbon-negative alternative to synthetic textiles and fossil-based chemicals.

A self-adapting, Fe2+-triggered release system based on MOF nanocontainers for precision corrosion protection of marine steel facilities
abstract: Although stimulus-responsive nanocontainers have been explored for corrosion protection, achieving a direct coupling between corrosion progression and inhibitor delivery at the molecular level remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that a metal–organic framework (HKUST-1) engineered with molecularly imprinted recognition sites can translate localized corrosion signals into a self-regulating inhibitor release cascade. The key design lies in residual dodecyltrimethylammonium (DTA + ) templates confined within the HKUST-1 pore walls, which serve as Fe 2+ -responsive gatekeepers. During corrosion, anodically generated Fe 2+ ions selectively displace DTA + via preferential coordination, triggering a pore-level gate-opening effect that releases the preloaded inhibitor (MTP, kinetic diameter 0.7 nm) in direct proportion to corrosion activity down to 10 −6 M Fe 2+ sensitivity. This corrosion-driven feedback achieves 42.2 wt% loading capacity and 96.8% inhibition efficiency in simulated marine conditions. Using in situ electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, micro-Raman spectroscopy, and localized electrochemical mapping, we reveal that the released MTP molecules preferentially adsorb at anodic active sites through Fe S and Fe N coordination (ΔG ads = −39.2 kJ mol −1 ), progressively forming a compact bilayer-like protective film through strong interfacial adsorption and intermolecular packing, whose density dynamically adapts to corrosion severity. This Fe 2+ -responsive gatekeeper strategy establishes a universal coupling between corrosion signaling and responsive mass transport, offering a generalizable framework for designing self-adaptive protective materials that evolve with their operational environment.

A novel multiphysics lattice Boltzmann modeling approach of particle morphology for biomass pyrolysis process
abstract: Biomass pyrolysis is an effective route to convert low-grade biomass into high-value energy carriers (tar and non-condensable gases), with particle morphology exerting a significant regulatory effect on the thermochemical conversion process. As a typical fast-growing hardwood with high cellulose content (48.6%), favorable lignocellulose composition, and excellent thermal reactivity, eucalyptus serves as an ideal feedstock for pyrolysis investigation. This study adopted the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) coupled with a pyrolysis kinetic model (Three Parallel Reactions Model: three parallel primary + secondary reactions) to systematically investigate the effects of particle morphology on eucalyptus pyrolysis characteristics. Three aspects were explored: pyrolysis of elliptical cross-sectional cylindrical particles with fixed horizontal axis and variable aspect ratios (λ), product yields of particles with identical λ but different sizes, and λ variations under constant cross-sectional area. The results indicate that spherical particles promote char formation, while elliptical particles provide higher tar and gas yields. Particle size was negatively correlated with volatile production. Specifically, as λ increases from 0.250 to 1.000, the tar yield decreases by approximately 3% and the non-condensable gases yield decreases by nearly 1%. Reciprocal λ pairs exhibited thermal response asymmetry, with smaller λ(＜1.000) accelerating pyrolysis. Under constant cross-sectional area, adjusting λ affected tar/non-condensable gases yields and shortened conversion time. This study confirms the crucial role of particle morphology regulation in pyrolysis optimization, providing a theoretical basis for targeted product distribution via synergistic control of λ and particle size.

Role of Mn3+/Mn4+ redox-coupled oxygen vacancy modulation in SnO2 nanoarchitectures for ultrasensitive acetone detection
abstract: Acetone (CH 3 COCH 3 ) is a ubiquitous volatile organic compound in industrial and laboratory settings; however, its high volatility and toxicity necessitate advanced monitoring to ensure human health and occupational safety. In this work, we report a highly sensitive and selective sensor based on Mn 2 O 3 -decorated SnO 2 nanorods (MSNRs) fabricated via a sequential glancing angle deposition (GLAD) technique. By systematically tailoring the Mn 2 O 3 decoration thickness (0, 1, 3, and 5 nm), we achieved a high response of ≈204.7 toward 5 ppm CH 3 COCH 3 at 300 °C, representing a ≈ 227.3-fold enhancement compared to conventional SnO 2 thin films. The sensor demonstrates exceptional selectivity against six target gases, an ultralow theoretical detection limit of 1.5 ppb, and remarkable repeatability (CV ≈ 2.2%), even under 80% relative humidity. Surface chemical analysis indicates that the optimized Mn 4+ /(Mn 3+ +Mn 4+ ) ratio and oxygen vacancy-related components promote reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and dynamic surface redox processes, thereby facilitating efficient interfacial reactions with target gases. These synergistic structural and electronic effects demonstrate the potential of MSNRs as a versatile platform for trace-level acetone detection in airborne pollutant monitoring.

Multifunctional metal organic framework-based hydrogel for accelerating diabetic wound healing
abstract: Chronic diabetic wound remains a major clinical challenge due to its persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed re-epithelialization. Here, a miR-21-5p-loaded bimetallic metal-organic framework (RMOF) was constructed using magnesium and zinc as metal clusters, while utilizing gallic acid and indole-3-propionic acid as mixed organic ligands, enabling synergistic antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory properties besides multiple bioactivities brought by miR-21-5p. Subsequently, we developed a multifunctional in-situ forming hydrogel dressing by embedding RMOF into a polyethylene glycol (PEG) matrix that exhibits skin-like mechanical properties and sustained release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated that RMOF significantly promoted proliferation, migration, and tube formation of relevant cells, while also inducing M2 polarization of macrophages and neuronal differentiation of neural stem cells. In a diabetic rat full-thickness skin wound model, PEG-RMOF treatment markedly accelerated wound closure at about 62.3% after 10 days, enhanced collagen deposition significantly, reduced oxidative stress among the entire wound, and increased the expression of key regenerative markers, especially about Nestin and β-Catenin compared to PEG-miR group. In addition, RMOF effectively retained both miR-21-5p and metal ions abundance in wound tissues. Collectively, our research presents a versatile MOF-based hydrogel platform that integrates multiple bioactive components to coordinately promote diabetic wound healing, offering a promising strategy for chronic wound management.

DNA stable isotope probing reveals a metabolic division of labour in haloalkaline oxalate-degrading bioreactors
abstract: Biological degradation provides a sustainable approach for managing the organic impurities accumulating in Bayer liquor. However, the limited functional understanding of microbial communities in hypersaline, haloalkaline bioreactors constrains process optimisation. Here, DNA stable isotope probing combined with multivariate regression tree analysis was used to resolve the active microbial ecology of an oxalate-degrading biofilm operated under varied nitrogen and redox conditions. Oxalate removal was consistent with a synergistic metabolic division of labour, in which the genome-reduced, cell wall deficient genus Mycoplasma showed progressive 13 C-oxalate incorporation over the incubation time series, consistent with a primary degrader role whereas the facultative diazotroph Azoarcus was identified as a putative structural and nutritional contributor, associated with community performance under nitrogen limitation. Process robustness was further reinforced by a persistent physicochemically adapted community including Defluviimonas and Pseudofulvimonas that maintained biofilm integrity and functional redundancy across all operational regimes. Notably, direct evidence of anaerobic oxalate turnover within the biofilm core revealed a coupled fermentation–oxidation network, whereby anaerobic metabolites are proposed to support aerobic nitrogen fixation, rather than a single dominant removal pathway. By explicitly linking microbial function to reactor performance, this study transforms oxalate biodegradation from an experiential system into a mechanistically informed platform, enabling targeted strategies for sludge minimisation and energy-efficient dual-zone operation in extreme industrial environments.

title: Morphology-driven mass transfer in spherical carbon aerogels through interconnected diffusion pathways
Sorption Enhanced reverse Water Gas Shift (SErWGS): Optimal potassium-driven methanol suppression and zeolite type selection (LTA and FAU) under high-pressure conditions
abstract: CO hydrogenation is thermodynamically and kinetically more favorable than direct CO 2 hydrogenation, making a preceding CO 2 -to-CO conversion step an attractive route for enhancing e-fuel production. In this work, intensified e-syngas production via high-pressure CO 2 hydrogenation was investigated through the Sorption-Enhanced Reverse Water-Gas Shift ( SErWGS ) process. Particular attention was given to methanol suppression through the incorporation of low potassium loadings in the catalyst, and to the influence of zeolite type on process performance. The effect of potassium loading on catalytic activity and CH 3 OH inhibition was systematically evaluated under different temperatures and WHSV values using a Design of Experiments (DoE) methodology, which enabled the development of empirical models describing the process behavior and identification of the optimal catalyst formulation. In parallel, the performance of different zeolite adsorbents was assessed to maximize H 2 O removal and process intensification. The optimized catalyst, containing 1.5 wt% K, effectively suppressed methanol formation while maximizing CO production. The intensified SErWGS process achieved CO yields exceeding the thermodynamic equilibrium limit at the operating temperature. H 2 /CO ratios approaching those expected for complete CO 2 -to-CO conversion, and pre-breakthrough periods accounting for up to 80% of the total cycle duration. The highest CO yield obtained in this work reached 42% at 260 °C using the 3A-LTA zeolite, corresponding to a value approximately 2.5 times higher than that achieved under conventional RWGS conditions. Remarkably, this CO yield was comparable to the thermodynamic equilibrium yield expected at approximately 450 °C in a conventional rWGS process. These results validate that the SErWGS strategy can deliver performance equivalent to operating nearly 200 °C above the actual reaction temperature, highlighting its potential as an effective intensification approach for low-temperature CO 2 conversion and sustainable e-syngas production.

A unified techno-economic comparison of separation strategies for the dimethyl carbonate–methanol azeotrope
abstract: Dimethyl carbonate (DMC) is a green solvent and battery electrolyte that forms a minimum-boiling azeotrope with the excess reactant methanol (MeOH), making high-purity separation challenging. Existing studies remain fragmented across inconsistent feed compositions, thermodynamic models, and cost assumptions, which prevents a reliable comparison of competing separation technologies. This work addresses this gap through a unified techno-economic assessment of ten distillation-based separation processes, covering pressure-swing distillation (PSD), extractive distillation (ED), and azeotropic distillation (AD). All of them are evaluated on an identical feed composition, product-purity, plant-scale, thermodynamic, and utility-cost basis, with membrane assisted distillation discussed separately as a reference technology. Extractive distillation with aniline achieves the lowest total annualized cost (TAC = 2.51 M$/yr) despite its acute toxicity, while water-based azeotropic distillation is the most practical non-toxic alternative (TAC = 3.16 M$/yr) across all technology groups. Preferentially separating the dominant feed component (MeOH) reduces cost, or using MSAs that retain DMC in the liquid phase or form an azeotrope with DMC which is the minor feed component offering a transferable design heuristic for other asymmetric minimum-boiling azeotropes. Thermodynamic-model selection is shown to be a major source of design uncertainty, with NRTL, UNIQUAC, and Wilson parameter sets causing up to 30% differences in predicted reboiler duty under identical flowsheet specifications. These novel results provide a generalizable technology-selection framework for minimum-boiling homogeneous azeotropes, with explicit guidance on solvent selection, property-model risk, and intensification trade-offs applicable beyond the specific DMC/MeOH system studied here.

abstract: Deployment of direct air capture (DAC) is currently limited by sorbents with multistep synthesis, low capture capacities, slow kinetics, cycling instability, and/or high regeneration temperatures. Here, we report a one-step emulsion copolymerization of 4-vinylbenzylamine (VBA) and 1,4-divinylbenzene (DVB), in which cross-linked network formation and primary amine incorporation occur simultaneously, to prepare amine-rich porous frameworks chemically analogous to Lewatit VP OC 1065 for DAC. By varying the DVB:VBA ratio, adsorbents with different porosities and amine contents were synthesized, with amine loading being the most crucial parameter. The optimized sorbent features a CHN-derived amine loading of 5.6 mmol N g −1 and exhibits breakthrough-derived CO 2 uptakes of 0.54 mmol g −1 under dry conditions and 1.21 mmol g −1 at 80% relative humidity at 25 °C using a simulated DAC feed containing ~400 ppm CO 2 in N 2 . It reaches half of the equilibrium uptake within 2.6 min under pure CO 2 at 25 °C, exhibits a CO 2 -TPD maximum at ~60 °C, and maintains stable performance over 45 dry adsorption–desorption cycles and 10 humid breakthrough cycles. Infrared and solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopies reveal carbamate species, whose corresponding IR bands nearly disappear upon heating to 80 °C, supporting reversible CO 2 binding. Density functional theory calculations support that ammonium carbamate and hydrogen-bonded carbamic acid species can form in the proposed structure. This study demonstrates that incorporation of primary amines during polymerization provides a simple route to high-performance DAC sorbents with capture performance comparable to Lewatit VP OC 1065 and a lower CO 2 desorption peak temperature.

Wearable sweat sensors for arthritis monitoring
abstract: Arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis and gout, imposes increasing clinical and economic burdens. Current diagnostic tools such as serology, imaging, and clinical assessments are episodic, resource-intensive, and insufficient for capturing the daily dynamics of disease activity. Epidermal sweat sensing has emerged as a promising non-invasive technique for at-home physiological tracking. This review presents a comprehensive analysis and proof-of-concept for the application of wearable sweat sensors in arthritis management. The current state of detecting arthritis-related biomarkers in sweat, including specific metabolites, proteins, and markers of oxidative stress, is examined. The review surveys critical components of existing sensor architectures, ranging from substrates to transduction modalities. Methodologies for establishing sweat-blood correlations are discussed, emphasizing the physiological partitioning of biomarkers from blood to sweat. Finally, current challenges and the potential of integrated sweat-sensing systems to transform early detection are addressed.

abstract: Biological methanation of H2 and CO2 is a key Power-to-Gas pathway for coupling renewable electricity to existing natural-gas infrastructure, yet its transient response under variable H2 supply is poorly characterised. We develop a CFD model of a porous-plate bubble column biomethanation reactor with gas recirculation, validated against experimental data. At the baseline operating point both the CFD and a 1-D reduced-order model (ROM) reproduce outlet methane purity and production rate within experimental uncertainty, and capture the purity–productivity trade-off across four fresh-feed flow rates. Because CFD of the multi-thousand-second transients required for intermittency analysis is computationally prohibitive, the multi-species ROM, derived from the same governing equations, is cross-validated against the CFD, whose spatial fields confirm radial uniformity of the dissolved-H2 field to within 1%. All three species (H2, CO2, CH4) are resolved independently in both gas and dissolved phases, with species-specific Henry's-law equilibria, diffusivities, and mass-transfer coefficients, and the dissolved-CO2 pool through an explicit carbonate–bicarbonate equilibrium capturing the dissolved inorganic-carbon reservoir. Using the ROM we map steady-state regimes over biomass, recirculation, and fresh-feed rate; study flow and composition intermittency over forcing periods from 10 to 1800 s; and compare mass-transfer-dominated against biology-limited operation. A 53 s recirculation timescale buffers sub-minute fluctuations; cycle-averaged purity and productivity are set by the duty cycle, not the forcing period, with only the oscillation amplitude growing as the period lengthens. Composition intermittency gives purity-settling times of ~1200 s, far longer than gas-side recovery. Biology acts as a low-pass filter, compressing the biological methane-production-rate oscillation by ~2.5× in the biology-limited regime while leaving the gas-side envelope almost unchanged, so the gas-side signal is an unreliable proxy for biological activity.

Physics-informed neural network reconstructions of free surfaces and flow fields from sparse data in turbulent regimes, with applications in stirred tanks
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless framework for fluid dynamics, capable of solving both forward and inverse problems, and incorporating observational data into the model. However, their application to coupled multiphase turbulent flows remains limited, particularly in industrial inverse problems, where measurements may be sparse, expensive, and are often devoid of turbulence values. In this work, we develop a PINN framework for reconstructing the free surface, along with the velocity and pressure fields from sparse data, and test it on a mixing tank. Models are trained on limited velocity and pressure data from a time-averaged, axisymmetric CFD reference simulation. The data are free of direct measurements from the free surface or turbulence terms. Models are evaluated across varying impeller speeds and fluid viscosities. Both laminar and turbulent models are tested, including with eddy viscosity closures and anisotropic stresses. A Spalart–Allmaras turbulence closure is used, while including anisotropic stresses can improve the pressure and free surface predictions. From as few as 25 measurement locations, models are able to reconstruct, with low error, the velocity and pressure fields, and the final model achieves average free-surface errors below 1 mm in all tested operating conditions relative to a CFD reference. Additionally, models can accurately detect features such as additional vortices, jet splitting and impingement regions.

A molecular firewall: Spatially heterostructured polymers as intelligent, reversible thermal switches for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Thermal runaway remains a critical safety challenge for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), and existing thermal protection strategies usually exhibit irreversible responses, limiting their practical reliability. Herein, we design a spatially heterostructured conducting polymer poly(3-butylthiophene- co -3-tetradecylthiophene) (PBTDT), which exhibits a highly reversible positive temperature coefficient (PTC) effect. Synthesized by chemical oxidative copolymerization of long- and short-side-chain thiophene monomers, PBTDT possesses spatially differentiated rigid and flexible domains: the short-side-chain rigid domains suppress irreversible thermal motion of the long side chains at elevated temperatures, while the long-side-chain flexible domains retain sufficient free volume for anion re-doping upon cooling, enabling reversible resistive switching. The polymer shows a sharp resistivity increase at ~100 °C and maintains a recoverable PTC response over eight thermal cycles. When applied as a surface coating layer on the current collector, the resulting LiFePO 4 -PBTDT cathode delivers a room-temperature discharge capacity of 157 mA h g −1 and autonomously shuts down electrochemical activity at 100 °C, with the capacity dropping to only 1.4 mA h g −1 ; this shutdown-recovery behavior remains highly reversible over five thermal cycles. Under adiabatic short-circuit conditions, LiCoO 2 -PBTDT cells reach a maximum temperature of merely 147 °C, in stark contrast to 290 °C for bare LiCoO 2 cells, effectively mitigating thermal runaway hazards. This molecular firewall strategy provides a promising design concept for self-actuating, reversible safety protection to enhance the intrinsic safety of lithium-ion batteries.

Gel engineered with nanomaterials for integrated enzymatic reactors (GENIEs) for photothermal real-time PCR
abstract: Nanomaterials are frequently employed to enhance in vitro enzymatic reactions, which hold significant importance across diverse bioengineering applications. However, achieving stable dispersion of nanomaterials in these reactions —a prerequisite for practical use—remains an unsolved challenge. Here, we present Gel Engineered with Nanomaterials for Integrated Enzymatic reactors (GENIEs), a hydrogel-based platform designed to physically confine nanomaterials within a porous matrix, thereby ensuring sustained dispersion and functionality throughout the reaction. We incorporated graphene oxide (GO), a widely utilized nanomaterial, into the GENIE framework and generated reduced GO (rGO) -GENIEs via a seamless, in situ chemical reduction step. By leveraging the hydrogel as a structural scaffold, we preserved exceptional dispersity, unlocking the uncompromised photothermal performance of the embedded rGO. The heavily loaded rGO-GENIEs enabled a high-speed photothermal PCR system, achieving rapid heating (13.3 ± 0.7 °C/s) and cooling (11.3 ± 0.4 °C/s) rates via a micro-laser module. Real-time monitoring demonstrated a 95% amplification efficiency and a detection limit of 120 copies/μL for bacterial DNA. These results highlight the potential of the GENIE platform as a robust and versatile reservoir for nanomaterial-integrated assays, enabling superior performance without requiring additional anti-aggregation steps or compromising functionality.

Evaluating the industrial upscaling of apple pomace upcycling: A holistic sustainability and decision-analysis framework
abstract: Circularity and upcycling of agro-industrial co/byproducts are increasingly promoted as strategies for reducing food-processing waste, yet limited evidence exists on whether laboratory-scale valorization pathways remain sustainable when scaled to industrial conditions. This study developed a holistic sustainability and decision-analysis framework to evaluate the industrial upscaling potential of apple pomace valorization for pectin production. Six extraction pathways, conventional HCl extraction (CHE), microwave-assisted extraction (MAE), subcritical water extraction (SWE), double ultrasound-assisted extraction (DUAE), and two enzyme-assisted extraction methods (EAE-1/−2), were translated from laboratory data to industrial-scale process models and assessed across technical performance, technoeconomic feasibility, environmental life cycle impacts, social implications, and multicriteria decision analysis. Literature-derived yields indicated that CHE had the highest average pectin yield (21.32 ± 1.11%), followed by MAE (19.54 ± 1.11%), whereas EAE-1 had the lowest yield (7.64 ± 0.25%). SWE generated the greatest waste intensity, producing 108 units of waste per unit of pectin, compared with 40.7 and 41.2 units for MAE and CHE, respectively. Economically, CHE and MAE were the only pathways with pectin minimum selling prices below the current industry benchmark, at $92.64/kg and $118.05/kg, respectively, although price sensitivity analysis showed that MAE retained only a narrow margin below this benchmark under ethanol and electricity price variation. Environmentally, MAE had the lowest global warming impact for pectin production (4.11 kg CO 2 -eq/kg), whereas EAE-2 had the highest impact (32 kg CO 2 -eq/kg). An integrated Entropy-TOPSIS analysis identified MAE, DUAE, and CHE as the leading pathways, but stakeholder-priority scenarios showed that rankings shifted when economic, environmental, social, or technical dimensions were emphasized. Uncertainty and sensitivity analyses showed that MAE was the most probable preferred pathway, ranking first in 82% of Monte Carlo iterations and across 79.7% of the feasible weight space, although CHE and DUAE remained competitive under some parameter and weighting conditions. Overall, the findings demonstrate that industrial upscaling of apple pomace upcycling can introduce important technical, economic, social, environmental, and decision-uncertainty trade-offs that are not evident at laboratory scale, reinforcing the need for integrated sustainability assessment and scale-up validation before technology adoption.

title: Anion-regulated surface activation in high-entropy catalysts for water electrolysis
abstract: Electrochemical surface reconstruction, driven by anion oxidation and dissolution, governs the formation of the true active phase during the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, layered double hydroxide-derived high-entropy sulfides and phosphides (FeCoNiCrMg-S/P) are employed as model systems to elucidate how anion electronegativity regulates reconstruction pathways and catalytic activity. Spectroscopic analyses reveal that although both S and P promote electron transfer at metal centers, the higher electronegativity of S induces stronger electron delocalization, deeper oxidative reconstruction, and the formation of highly active high-valence M-OOH species with enhanced metal‑oxygen covalency, whereas P favors reconstruction into low-valent M-(OH) 2 phases with limited covalency. DFT calculations further show that the reconstructed M-OOH phase asymmetrically modulates multimetallic d -band centers, with Fe and Co downshifting to optimize oxygen-intermediate adsorption and Ni, Cr, and Mg upshifting to promote electron accumulation, synergistically lowering the OER overpotential. As a result, FeCoNiCrMg-S delivers an overpotential of 264 mV at 100 mA cm −2 with less than 1% activity decay over 110 h. This work establishes anion-electronegativity engineering as a rational strategy for directing surface reconstruction and designing high-efficiency OER electrocatalysts.

abstract: Stimuli-responsive coordination compounds with reversible optical properties are promising for sensing applications, but achieving systems that combine structural adaptability, processability, and device integration is challenging. Here, we report a two-dimensional cobalt coordination polymer, {CoCy 2 [Co(SCN) 3 ] 2 } n , ( P1 , Cy = 1,3-bis(cyanopropyl)tetramethyldisiloxane), featuring dual cobalt centers with octahedral and tetrahedral geometries, as revealed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Weakly coordinating cyanide and ambidentate thiocyanate ligands, together with a poorly stacked 2D architecture, confer high structural flexibility and enable solvent-induced reorganization of the coordination environment. P1 exhibits pronounced and reversible solvato- and vapochromic responses due to solvent-dependent changes in cobalt geometry, supported by UV–Vis and NMR studies. Incorporation of P1 into a cross-linked silicone matrix produces flexible composite films ( CP1 x ), in which tetramethyldisiloxane-flanked 2D layers allow efficient delamination, uniform dispersion, and compatibility. The composites combine mechanical robustness (tear strength 0.22–0.39 MPa), high vapor permeability, and long-term stability, enabling reliable optical responses at low P1 loadings. The hybrid material displays rapid, reversible, and repeatable color changes upon exposure to organic solvent vapors, fully recovering after desorption with no degradation over multiple cycles. Integration into a simple optical vapor-sensing platform, using RGB-to-CIELab conversion and an integrated algorithm, allows detection of organic vapors with reasonable resolutions (for example, about 20 ppm, as estimated gravimetrically for acetone).

Subcooling-controlled CO₂ hydrate formation and dissociation in porous media: Experimental investigation and empirical kinetic modeling
abstract: Geologic Carbon Storage (GCS) into low pressure depleted gas reservoirs (DGRs) may be constrained by CO 2 hydrate formation near the wellbore, potentially causing permeability impairment and flow restriction. This study investigates the kinetics of CO₂ hydrate formation and dissociation in partially brine-saturated Bentheimer sandstone containing 10 g L −1 NaCl brine at approximately 30 bar. Coreflooding experiments were conducted over a subcooling range of 4–10 °C using direct, stepwise, and ramp cooling/heating protocols. Medical X-ray computed tomography (CT) monitored temporal and axial variations in combined water + hydrate saturation as the two phases could not be distinguished directly. Hydrate saturation was estimated indirectly using a permeability-based approach informed by CT-derived volumetric changes. Statistical analyses yielded an empirical induction-time correlation and Arrhenius-type lumped apparent kinetic parameters. Induction time decreased from approximately 20 h at ΔT = 4 °C to approximately 10 min at ΔT = 10 °C, while the apparent activation energy was approximately 148 kJ mol −1 . These relationships describe the macroscopic experimental response and should not be interpreted as intrinsic kinetic constants. Furthermore, faster cooling generally shortened induction time, whereas the permeability–saturation relationship remained broadly consistent across the thermal protocols. Greater subcooling promoted faster formation and more severe permeability impairment with reduction of up to approximately 60%. Apparent dissociation onset occurred consistently 0.6–0.8 °C below the predicted bulk equilibrium temperature, potentially reflecting pore scale confinement and local thermal effect. Higher heating rates promoted faster dissociation and permeability recovery. Higher heating rates accelerated dissociation and permeability recovery. These findings are specific to partially brine saturated Bentheimer sandstone containing 10 g L −1 NaCl brine at a pressure of approximately 30 bar.

Design and sensitivity analysis of a novel multifunctional membrane reactor for methanol production using syngas from biomass gasification
abstract: This study presents a novel multifunctional reactor designed for methanol production from syngas produced via biomass gasification. The system consists of: (i) a multi-tube-in-shell membrane reactor, where methanol synthesis reactions occur on the tube side while liquid water flows on the shell side as sweep; (ii) a heat exchanger to cool down the methanol-rich product, and (iii) an alkaline electrolyser, which generates hydrogen through splitting of part of the water coming from the permeation side. Such a hydrogen stream is mixed with the feed to ensure a stoichiometric number of 2, which is optimal for methanol synthesis. A number of 24 biomass types are analysed, conducting proximate and ultimate analyses experimentally. Syngas streams are then generated by a gasification model ranging within 600–900 °C. These syngas compositions are used as feed for the proposed innovative reactor modelled in MATLAB environment. The results indicate that, due to a syngas composition richer in CO₂, the most convenient gasification temperature maximizing the methanol yield is 600 °C, at which 0.19 kmol h −1 of hydrogen must be supplied, and a maximum methanol yield of 45% ca. and a power for water splitting of 20 kW ca are obtained at a gas hourly space velocity (GHSV) of 100 h −1 . Sensitivity analyses of reactor performance to the biomass type are then carried out. Notably, the standard deviation at 600 °C is low enough (0.0035 ca.) that the yield is essentially independent of biomass type. However, at higher gasification temperatures, the standard deviation increases by one order of magnitude, suggesting a greater sensitivity to biomass. The space-time yield, which measures the reactor productivity, reaches its peak of 70 kg MeOH h −1 kg cat at 20,000 h −1 . Overall, the proposed novel technology shows good performance, which makes it suitable to be installed in real industrial contexts.

Microwave Taguchi optimisation for porous adsorbents and high CO2 capture
abstract: This study used a Taguchi orthogonal design of experiments to optimise the production of microporous activated carbons (AC) from pine sawdust (PIS), olive stones (OS), and pecan nutshells (NS) using microwave heating. Results showed that the impregnation ratio was the most critical factor, followed by biochar feedstock and microwave power. The optimum synthesis conditions were identified as NS biochar with a KOH impregnation ratio of 2:1, at 500 W microwave power for 3 min. The resulting AC exhibited a high micropore volume (0.56 cm 3 g −1 ) and specific surface area (S BET ) of 1500 m 2 g −1 . The produced ACs were evaluated for selective post-combustion CO 2 capture. Taguchi optimisation enhanced specific surface area, and maximum CO 2 uptake was 6.7, 3.6, and 2.7 mmol g −1 at 0, 25, and 40 °C, respectively. This high uptake correlated directly with the ultra-micropore volume (<0.8 nm, up to 0.36 cm 3 g −1 ). This study confirms the usefulness of Taguchi orthogonal design of experiments in reducing the required number of experiments while quantifying the relevance of key parameters during microwave-assisted activation.

Blood test on a chip: Sample-to-answer immunoassay on a structurally programmed microfluidic chip
abstract: During COVID-19, rapid antigen tests (RATs) have demonstrated their enormous potential to relax and decentralize the healthcare system for timely results. However, disease diagnosis mostly requires blood tests with quantitative readouts, which are hardly achieved by conventional lateral flow strips. Here, we report a concept of “Blood Test on a Chip” (BTOC) that streamlines the entire sample-to-answer immunoassay process on a single microfluidic chip. Without any external processes, the BTOC can operate independently based on a series of structurally programmed capillary events, including automated blood plasma separation, on-chip reaction, and a length-based quantitative result displayed on the chip. This platform demonstrated a limit of detection (LOD) of 3.78 ng/mL of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) in whole blood, which is below the clinical threshold of 4 ng/mL for PSA abnormality. Clinical validation involving 77 volunteer samples showed strong agreement between the BTOC and standard hospital tests (Lin's concordance correlation coefficient ρ ̂ c = 0.932 ). This all-in-one, self-contained chip eliminates the need for peripheral laboratory settings, offering a simple, affordable, and quantitative at-home test for telemedicine, large-scale screening in primary care and disease self-management.

title: From native tomato cutin to branched polyesters: Structural insights from supercritical-water depolymerisation
abstract: Cutin is the structural biopolyester that scaffolds the plant cuticle, forming a thermosetting matrix. It is insoluble in conventional solvents, chemically resilient and presents excellent barrier properties, preventing water loss, regulating gas permeability and protecting plants against environmental hazards. Conventional valorisation relies on batch processing with harsh chemicals that destroy the native architecture, yielding monomers rather than branched oligomers for polyester materials, and limiting mechanistic insight. Here we report a controlled depolymerisation strategy based on continuous supercritical-water hydrolysis that achieves complete solubilisation of the insoluble cutin network into soluble branched polyester oligomers (Mw ≈ 7.35 kDa) within 10.5 s of reaction time. Continued treatment further reduces Mw to ≈ 1.82 kDa at 120 s, approaching the limit of 24 h alkaline hydrolysis (≈ 1.22 kDa). Precise control of residence time reveals a hierarchical cleavage mechanism in which secondary esters at branching points hydrolyse preferentially over primary backbone esters. FTIR, NMR, GPC and GC–MS identify 10,16-dihydroxyhexadecanoic acid as the dominant monomeric unit and reveal 16-hydroxy-9Z-hexadecenoic acid as a novel SCW-specific product, consistent with a carbocation-driven dehydration pathway inaccessible under alkaline conditions. A structurally constrained network model depicts cutin as a heterogeneous crosslinked polyester dominated by 10,16-dihydroxyhexadecanoic acid, with glycerol as a branching node, C18 hydroxy acids and α,ω-diacids as linkers, and fatty acids as chain terminators. With an E -factor of 0.8 against 4.1 for alkaline hydrolysis, this process-intensified approach resolves the native architecture of cutin and establishes a scalable platform for plant polyester valorisation. Problem statement Cutin, considered the third most abundant biopolymer after cellulose and lignin, remains largely underutilised as a renewable polyester feedstock due to its highly cross-linked, insoluble structure, which severely limits processability and scalable valorisation [1] . Conventional depolymerisation strategies such as alkaline, acidic, or enzymatic hydrolysis rely on long reaction times, stoichiometric reagents, and multistep downstream processing [1] , [2] , leading to high material consumption, salt generation, and limited control over product characteristics. Although supercritical water presents a unique opportunity in biomass processing by functioning simultaneously as solvent and reaction medium [3] , its use for the depolymerisation of cutin into tunable polyester fractions remains largely unexplored. As a result, a critical gap exists in the development of fast, catalyst-free, and environmentally efficient processes capable of converting cutin-rich agro-industrial residues into functional polyester building blocks with defined molecular characteristics. Also, a data-driven model is proposed to infer representative structures of depolymerised products from experimental data.

abstract: This study investigates N O X production using single and dual atmospheric pressure plasma jets at a fixed total flow rate. The feed consists of a 16 vol% reactive gas mixture N 2 and O 2 at varied ratios, balanced in argon. By adjusting jet orientations and liquid-phase configurations, the effects of fluid dynamics and plasma geometry on N O X synthesis were systematically examined. At an O 2 /N 2 molar ratio of 2, the dual-jet configuration demonstrated up to 2.5 times increase in N O X production as compared to the single-jet setup. When the dual jets were angled at 45 degrees with respect to the gravity vector, secondary flow patterns emerged, significantly enhancing interfacial mass transfer. This improvement was further enhanced by reducing the distance between the nozzle and the liquid and using lower-viscosity liquids. Additionally, the addition of CeO 2 pallets to the bottom of the reactor resulted in an approximately 37% increase in total N O X production. These findings highlight the potential of dual-jet plasma configurations, optimized by geometric and fluidic parameters, for enhancing sustainable chemical synthesis technology.

AI-assisted design of metal-organic frameworks for hydrogen storage: From databases to generative models
abstract: Nowadays, the development of a sustainable hydrogen economy and the widespread deployment of high-capacity hydrogen storage for hydrogen vehicles and energy systems are of great importance. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with their diverse structures, have emerged as the most promising materials for next-generation gas storage due to their high surface area, tunable pore size, and diversity of chemical bonds. However, the fabrication of MOF materials through manual experimental screening is very time-consuming and costly. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms, combined with quantum databases, advanced modeling, and screening strategies for discovering MOF structures, have revolutionized materials science. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in AI-assisted discovery of novel MOF materials specifically for hydrogen storage applications. We present MOF databases, modeling strategies based on material structure descriptors and materials discovery, large language model (LLM) algorithms for automated data mining, and ML-assisted force fields (FFs) at the atomic level for hydrogen storage. Furthermore, we discuss key challenges such as data quality, model transferability, and discrepancies between simulations and experiments. Finally, this review paper outlines future prospects for this rapidly evolving interdisciplinary field, with an emphasis on advancing MOF materials discovery through accurate AI models.

Unraveling the effects of alloying and hetero-atom doping on electrochemical nitrate reduction through a systematic carbothermal shock strategy
abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO 3 RR) offers a promising route for simultaneous wastewater remediation and green ammonia production. Among various strategies to enhance NO 3 RR performance, alloying and hetero-atom doping of the catalysts have emerged as efficient approaches for tuning catalytic activity and selectivity. However, their respective roles in NO 3 RR remain unclear due to the lack of systematic comparisons using consistent fabrication approaches. Here, we present a systematic investigation of alloying and hetero-atom doping effects using a unified carbothermal shock platform. A series of Co-, Cu-, and CoCu-based catalysts with and without sulfur doping were synthesized to decouple the individual and synergistic contributions of alloy formation and hetero-atom incorporation. Among them, sulfur doped Co (Co/S) exhibits the highest activity and selectivity, achieving an NH 3 yield rate of 6305.3 μg h −1 cm −2 with a Faradaic efficiency of 90.6%. Mechanistic analyses, including kinetic isotope effect coupled with theoretical calculation reveal that sulfur doping enhances active hydrogen (*H) generation and utilization, thereby accelerating hydrogenation steps. In contrast, alloying provides moderate improvements, while their simultaneous combination can be detrimental. This work establishes a clear design-mechanism relationship governing NO 3 RR pathways, offering rational guidelines for next-generation electrocatalysts.

Multiphysics analysis of internal states in zero-gap CO2 electrolyzers
abstract: Optimization of zero-gap CO 2 electrolyzers poses challenges, as the effect of experimental parameters on performance-defining internal states is often complex. This work employs a multiphysics model to link experimental parameters (electrolyte composition, pressure and membrane properties) to the corresponding local reaction environment (local cation concentration, pH, available CO 2 and CO 2 crossover) and provide experimentalists with insight into these interactions. The results clarify non-intuitive phenomena, such as the mechanism by which thicker membranes increase cation crossover and how the effect of membrane characteristics on the system can be understood through the lens of migration and diffusion fluxes. We also explore these effects along the channel using a 1 + 1D simulation. These results demonstrate a trade-off between CO formation rates and single-pass conversion efficiency, and identify CO 2 transport from the flow channel to the catalyst layer as a limiting factor. A decreased concentration of cations near the end of the channel may further pose a challenge for the upscaling of CO 2 electrolyzers.

title: Chemical and phase equilibria of the 2-ethylhexanoic acid–sodium 2-ethylhexanoate–water–NaOH switchable hydrophilicity solvent
abstract: Switchable hydrophilicity solvents (SHSs) reversibly transition between a biphasic and a monophasic state, enabling the extraction and recovery of hydrophobic compounds with a single, tunable solvent. Recently, short- and medium-chain carboxylic acids (CAs) have emerged as greener alternatives to amines as the organic component of SHSs. Their switch is governed by the simultaneous chemical and phase equilibria (CPE) of the quaternary CA + carboxylate + inorganic base + water system. Research on the CPE of SHSs, and of reactive inhomogeneous systems in general, remains limited. Here, the CPE of the 2-ethylhexanoic acid (EHA) + sodium 2-ethylhexanoate (EHANa) + water + NaOH system was determined at 25 °C and 1 bar. Small and wide angle X-ray scattering (SWAXS) measurements and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations identified the hydrotropic solubilization of the CA by the carboxylate as a key mechanism driving the switch. The work provides the first comprehensive CPE dataset for a CA-based SHS and defines the composition window relevant to its application in extraction.
