Mechanochemical modulation of Pt–TiO2 interfaces for solar hydrogen production via photoreforming
abstract: Pt–TiO 2 photocatalysts were synthesized through a solvent–free mechanochemical ball–milling approach for photocatalytic hydrogen production via alcohol photoreforming under simulated solar irradiation. The influence of milling speed on the structural, electronic, and photocatalytic properties of the materials was systematically investigated. Mechanochemical treatment promotes homogeneous Pt dispersion on TiO 2 while preserving the anatase structure under moderate milling conditions. Pt incorporation enhances charge transfer and improves H 2 evolution compared with pristine TiO 2 and Pt dissolved in the reaction solution. The effect of different sacrificial agents was also evaluated, with methanol providing the highest H 2 production rates due to favorable oxidation pathways and reduced accumulation of surface intermediates. Under optimized conditions, the best photocatalyst reaches H 2 production rates above 1300 μmol·gcat −1 ·h −1 together with long–term stability. These results demonstrate the potential of mechanochemical synthesis as a simple and sustainable strategy for the preparation of efficient Pt–TiO 2 photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen production.

Design of ionic liquids as versatile chromatographic ligands for the purification of the recombinant interferon alpha-2b biopharmaceutical
abstract: Biopharmaceuticals, which include a wide array of recombinant proteins, are effective therapeutic agents and essential in modern healthcare systems. However, the high cost of chromatographic biological ligands often applied in their downstream processing still limits the widespread use of biopharmaceuticals. To overcome these bottlenecks, ionic liquids (ILs) covalently immobilized in spherical silica microparticles – supported ionic liquids, SILs – are herein proposed as novel synthetic ligands in preparative liquid chromatography of interferon alpha-2b (IFNα-2b), a recombinant protein used in the treatment of disorders such as hepatitis C and multiple sclerosis. Three chloride-based ILs, comprising the cations 1-methyl-3-propylimidazolium, dimethylbutylpropylammonium, and dimethylhexylpropylammonium, were synthesized, characterized, and investigated as potential ligands of chromatographic supports. Column chromatographic experiments confirmed the suitability of the designed SILs to be packed into gravity flow columns, and demonstrated their ability to bind the target protein in conditions favoring ionic or hydrophobic interactions. IL synthetic ligands immobilized onto SILs exhibit a multimodal behavior, which can be tuned to the target application. Under chromatographic conditions in which ionic conditions are applied, the SIL comprising the 1-methyl-3-propylimidazolium cation exhibited the highest selectivity, allowing a remarkable purification factor of 6.9 of the target protein IFNα-2b, being directly purified from Escherichia coli lysates.

abstract: Metal implants have been functionalized with cell-derived materials, including cell-surface components, exosomes, and extracellular matrices, as well as purified proteins and other biologics such as peptides and aptamers. However, the production costs of cell-derived materials and the limited stability of some coating materials at room temperature remain important challenges. Here, this study developed a highly stable, ultrashort dipeptide, N -acetyl-L-leucyl- l -lysine (Ac-LK), as a direct coating for the functionalization of nitinol-based implants. Ac-LK maintained its structural integrity and bioactivity across a wide temperature range. Following covalent immobilization, the peptide formed a uniform and adherent layer on the nitinol surface. In vitro, the Ac-LK-functionalized surface significantly enhanced focal adhesion formation in human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hADMSCs) and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Furthermore, the functionalized surface promoted osteogenic differentiation of hADMSCs and angiogenic responses in HUVECs when evaluated in separate in vitro experimental systems. These findings demonstrate the dual pro-osteogenic and pro-angiogenic potential of Ac-LK functionalization and highlight its promise for improving the biological performance of metal implants.

abstract: Lignin valorization offers a promising route toward sustainable biorefineries, but its use is hindered by poor solubility and structural recalcitrance. Kraft lignin (KL), a major byproduct of the pulp and paper industry, is abundant but remains underutilized. Conventional alkaline depolymerization requires harsh conditions, strong bases, and extensive neutralization, resulting in high energy consumption. In this study, a sustainable alternative using deep eutectic solvents (DESs) for integrated KL solubilization, depolymerization, and microbial conversion process is proposed. Seven DESs were screened, with L-arginine:glycerol (L-Arg:Gly) emerging as the most effective, achieving KL solubility up to 424.2 ± 26.88 g/L in 50% DES, and maintaining relatively high solubility (6.9 ± 1.43 g/L) even at just 2% DES-water mixture. Depolymerization conditions were evaluated by varying DES concentration, temperature, and reaction duration. The highest relative abundances of aromatic monomers (syringol, vanillin, and syringaldehyde) were obtained using 50% DES at 95 °C for 1 h. However, to balance KL-derived aromatic formation with microbial compatibility, 2% DES at 95 °C for 1 h was selected for fermentation. The depolymerized KL products supported successful fermentation by Pseudomonas putida KT2440, enabling growth from a low initial inoculum (OD 600 = 0.1) and reaching exponential phase within 24 h, much faster than conventional lignin fermentations. However, total lignin conversion remained limited due to the inability of P. putida to fully metabolize syringyl (S-type) compounds, which dominated the monomer profile. This highlights the need for strain engineering to expand the metabolic capacity toward hardwood-derived lignin. Overall, this work presents a biocompatible and energy-efficient alternative to conventional lignin pretreatments, establishing a foundation for future scalable lignin valorization platforms.

Oxygen-vacancy-rich Ru-doped WO3 catalyst enables electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF) in acidic media
abstract: Electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), a key biomass-derived platform molecule, is a promising route toward green production of value-added chemicals. Despite its potential, most prior studies have been carried out in alkaline electrolytes, where HMF undergoes polymerization into humins, resulting in significant losses and limiting overall efficiency. In contrast, acidic electrolytes provide excellent HMF stability but suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and catalyst degradation, limiting practical application. Here, we present a strategy to overcome these challenges through the development of a ruthenium-doped tungsten oxide (Ru-doped WO 3 ) electrocatalyst for selective anodic HMF oxidation in acidic media. Notably, unlike under the alkaline conditions, where hydroxymethyl furan carboxylic acid (HMFCA) is the main reaction intermediate, the reaction selectivity in acidic environment shifts toward 2,5-diformylfuran (DFF), favoring a controlled two-electron oxidation pathway. Both experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that the designed catalyst, enriched with oxygen vacancies (V O ) and Ru dopants, promotes HMF adsorption and DFF desorption, achieving approximately 91% selectivity for DFF at a relatively low potential of 1.3 V vs RHE at 60 °C in 1 M H 2 SO 4 . Mechanistic insights reveal that the oxidation proceeds via selective conversion of the hydroxymethyl (-CH 2 OH) group to an aldehyde (-CHO), enabling selective biomass upgrading under acidic conditions. This work offers insights into the HMF oxidation reaction mechanism in acidic environment and provides guidance for the rational design of more efficient and advanced electrocatalysts.

Rational design and tuning strategies of the physicochemical properties of MIL-53(Al)-derived ordered porous carbons
abstract: This study presents a robust and sustainable strategy for the rational design and precision tuning of hierarchically porous, alumina-decorated carbon materials derived from the MIL-53(Al) metal-organic framework (MOF). The proposed methodology enables the systematic modulation of key physicochemical properties, including alumina content, pore size distribution, pore volume, specific surface area, thermal stability, and surface defects. A fundamental finding of this research is that the ‘as-synthesized’ precursor, MIL-53(Al)(as), inherently outperforms its activated counterpart, MIL-53(Al)(lt). By utilizing the (as) phase, energy-intensive activation steps are bypassed, and residual benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate (BDC) is leveraged as an auxiliary carbon source. This results in carbon frameworks with considerably higher specific surface areas, larger pore volumes, and a greater abundance of structural defects. The architectural features of the resulting carbon, particularly its internal void space and pore size distribution, can be precisely tailored. Thus, while carbonization temperature influences the textural properties of the carbonized materials, the gas flow-to-precursor mass ratio is a more critical parameter for inducing bimodal porosity and adjusting internal cavities. Furthermore, a controlled acidic dealumination protocol (2–10% HCl, 30–80 °C, 1–5 h) was developed as a post-synthetic modulation step to effectively “unlock” the framework's porosity. This treatment can increase the specific surface area nearly fourfold, to 1500 m 2 /g, thereby exceeding that of the original MOF precursor, while also increasing thermal stability by 100 °C. The versatility of this approach was validated across a broader library of Al- and Cu-based MOFs, establishing that tuning efficiency is primarily governed by the geometry of the MOF precursor.

Dynamic reconstruction in CO2 electroreduction catalysts: mechanistic origins and rational regulation
abstract: The electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction (eCO 2 RR) presents a promising strategy for CO 2 utilization and sustainable energy conversion. However, under practical operating conditions, electrocatalysts rarely maintain structural stability and instead undergo continuous dynamic reconstruction induced by applied potentials, electrolyte environments, and reaction intermediates. Such reconstruction profoundly influences catalytic activity, selectivity, and long-term stability, while the dynamic nature of active sites poses major challenges to identifying genuine catalytic centers and establishing reliable structure-performance relationships. Therefore, clarifying the mechanisms of catalyst evolution and applying in-situ characterization techniques are essential for the rational design of efficient and stable eCO 2 RR catalysts. Focusing on dynamic reconstruction during eCO 2 RR, this review first discusses its fundamental principles from thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, and then systematically summarizes the morphological, structural, and chemical-state evolution of catalysts during reaction, with particular emphasis on surface roughening, defect generation, crystallinity variations, and interfacial regulation. We further argue that dynamic reconstruction is not merely a structural consequence, but a fundamental regulator of catalytic microenvironments and performance. By integrating catalyst design, reaction condition optimization, and morphological, electronic, and interfacial evolutions into a unified mechanistic framework, this review offers new insights into dynamic structure-performance relationships under operando conditions and outlined potential directions for future research on catalyst reconstruction.

A centralised CO2 capture strategy for small, spatially dispersed industrial emission sources
abstract: Achieving net-zero in the industrial sector requires addressing CO 2 emissions from smaller and geographically dispersed sources, such as those emitting less than 10 kt CO2 /yr. While carbon capture and storage (CCS) is a possible mitigation pathway, its viability depends on economies of scale and access to shared infrastructure, limiting its deployment for such emitters. This study investigates a strategy to extend CO 2 capture to smaller, dispersed industrial emitters, in which on-site absorption is coupled with centralised solvent regeneration via truck-based transport of CO 2 -rich and CO 2 -lean solvent. The centralised solvent regeneration (CSR) concept is benchmarked against distributed capture configurations, in which each emitter operates a standalone capture system, and against a direct air capture (DAC)–based removal pathway, using specific net CO 2 abatement and cost metrics. Two case studies addressing sparsely distributed emitters are analysed. The results show that CSR reduces investment requirements by more than 50% relative to decentralised solvent-based capture at all the emission scales investigated. Within a specific operating window depending on both the emission scale and the transport distance, CSR achieves CO 2 abatement costs, excluding downstream transport and storage, up to a factor of two lower than distributed capture and up to a factor of three lower than current estimates of DAC-based removal costs. CSR remains cost-competitive across different flue-gas compositions representative of heterogeneous industrial emission sources. Decarbonising solvent transport further increases the net CO 2 avoidance of CSR by approximately 21% and reduces its abatement costs by up to 35%. Overall, CSR emerges as a potentially scalable network configuration for direct CO 2 capture at smaller, dispersed industrial emitters, complementing carbon dioxide removal pathways.

abstract: Despite their excellent lab-scale performance in X-ray detectors, lead-based halide perovskites face critical barriers to commercial adoption due to issues of Pb toxicity, long-term stability, and challenges in fabricating scalable thick films. To overcome these limitations, we developed a Pb-free halide perovskite, CsBi3I10, which offers excellent ambient stability while eliminating environmental risks associated with Pb. Additionally, we introduced a scalable solution-assisted cold-press technique to fabricate millimeter-thick disc-shaped CsBi3I10. The incorporation of heavy elements, such as Bi and I, combined with increased thickness, significantly improves X-ray attenuation. As a result, a high detection sensitivity of 5.3 × 104[[EQUATION]] and a low limit of detection 47 [[EQUATION]] is realized. It also exhibits improved long-term ambient and operational stability. This work addresses key challenges in solution-processed devices and presents an eco-friendly, high-performance alternative for next-generation radiation detection.

Compression-enhanced inorganic-coated thermoelectric sponge with a solution-based silver selenide
abstract: The inherent brittleness of inorganic thermoelectric (TE) thin films creates a tradeoff between thickness and flexibility, which limits their ability to exploit vertical temperature gradients. We developed a TE sponge comprising a conformal coating of silver selenide (Ag 2 Se) on a melamine sponge. The Ag 2 Se coating maintains its structural integrity on the flexible melamine sponge, while the melamine sponge acts as a three-dimensional porous scaffold to provide enhanced flexibility, compressibility, and structural height for effective exploitation of vertical temperature gradients. Mechanical compression of the TE sponge by up to 80.4% yielded a 3.4-fold improvement in the TE figure of merit. A flexible thermoelectric generator (TEG) was assembled from eight pairs of TE sponges, and the resulting device achieved a maximum power output of 4.48 μW at a temperature gradient of 33.6 K. The TEG also demonstrated a stable TE performance under bending and effectively harvested heat from the human body to generate 0.033 μW from a temperature gradient of 4.9 K between the skin and ambient air. The developed strategy of combining a high-performance inorganic TE material with a flexible porous scaffold is expected to facilitate the practical application of self-powered wearable electronics.

Using extent of reaction to develop simplified kinetic models of chemical reactors with fast equilibrium reactions
abstract: This study proposes a new methodology for simplifying the development of semi-batch and continuous reactor models where some reversible reactions are fast compared to slower reactions that determine the process dynamics. The approach uses instantaneous equilibrium assumptions and extents of reaction to reformulate conventional ordinary differential equation (ODE) and partial differential equation (PDE) models. The resulting differential-algebraic equation (DAE) and partial differential-algebraic equation (PDAE) models involve fewer parameters than corresponding models without the instantaneous equilibrium assumption. The new kinetic models can be readily solved using standard numerical methods in various reactor operating modes. A pharmaceutical case study is used to illustrate how time-dependent feed addition and product removal are handled in semi-batch and continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) models. A tubular reactor model with dispersion is also developed using the new methodology, which provides a practical and generalizable framework for dynamic modeling of well-mixed reactors and reactors with spatial variation. The proposed methodology will enable straightforward modeling of complex reaction networks to aid process simulation, design, and optimization.

Solanum nigrum L.-derived extracellular vesicle-like particles promote chronic wound repair by inducing M2 macrophage polarization through autophagy-mediated inhibition of the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway
abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by a persistently dysregulated inflammatory microenvironment and impaired neovascularization, which collectively hinder tissue repair and limit effective therapeutic interventions. Herein, extracellular vesicle-like particles derived from Solanum nigrum L. (SL-EVLPs) were isolated and characterized as a plant-derived nanotherapeutic platform for diabetic wound repair. In a diabetic full-thickness wound model, topical administration of SL-EVLPs markedly enhanced angiogenesis, collagen deposition, and re-epithelialization, achieving 99.87 ± 0.13% wound closure by day 14. Transcriptomic analysis, together with histological and protein-level validation, revealed that SL-EVLPs restored macrophage autophagic activity, inhibited activation of the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway and downstream inflammasome signaling, promoted the transition from the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype to the reparative M2 phenotype, and further enhanced angiogenesis. SL-EVLPs also enhanced endothelial cell migration, angiogenic activity, and fibroblast-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling, further facilitating tissue repair. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that SL-EVLPs coordinate inflammation resolution, angiogenesis, and tissue repair through autophagy-associated macrophage polarization, underscoring their potential as a therapeutic strategy for diabetic wounds and other chronic non-healing wounds.

title: NanoChef: AI framework for simultaneous optimization of synthesis sequences and reaction conditions at autonomous laboratories
abstract: We present NanoChef , a deep learning-based framework for the simultaneous optimization of synthesis sequences and reaction conditions in autonomous laboratories. Unlike traditional AI models focused solely on continuous variables, NanoChef incorporates positional encoding and MatBERT embedding to represent reagent sequences as vectorized inputs, enabling joint modeling of sequential and continuous variables in nanoparticle (NP) synthesis. In virtual experiments, NanoChef consistently searched for the best-identified optimum across synthesis-order-sensitive landscapes in under 40 cycles. Despite the complexity of 17.5 billion candidate recipes driven by 24 possible sequences in a four-reagent system, this framework achieved an optimal recipe for Ag NP synthesis, characterized by a λ max of 513 nm and a 36% reduction in full width at half maximum within fewer than 350 experiments. This search efficiency was underscored by the reductant-last strategy, which consistently yielded optimal results across all permutations of two- to four-reagent systems. Additionally, NanoChef newly discovered an oxidant–last strategy that produces monodisperse NPs on average. By optimizing both continuous volume and the order of reagent addition, the framework redefines synthesis order as a tunable design variable and demonstrates how AI can accelerate autonomous chemistry while handling high-dimensional combinatorial challenges that exceed the capabilities of fixed-order methods.

Rare earth element selectivity in EF-hand loop 1 of lanmodulin via molecular simulations of aqueous complexation thermodynamics
abstract: Selective recovery of individual rare earth elements (REEs) from aqueous waste streams is important for sustainability but remains challenging due to identical charges and similar hydrated radii amongst REE ions. Peptides are promising selective ligands; however, rational design requires molecularlevel understanding of REE-peptide complexation thermodynamics. Here, we develop a computational framework to quantify the free energy, enthalpy, and entropy of complexation of aqueous La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, and Nd3+ with the peptide EFhand loop 1 of lanmodulin (LanM1). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with free energy perturbation and ensembleaveraged protonation state modeling are used to estimate these thermodynamic quantities. We demonstrate that peptide protonation states, governed by solution pH, influence the calculated thermodynamics and need to be incorporated to achieve agreement with experimental isothermal titration calorimetry data. Consistent with prior experimental data, the calculated complexation free energies are favorable, and entropy is found to be the dominant contribution to free energy of complexation. Relative selectivity among REE pairs is reproduced qualitatively, although magnitudes are overestimated, reflecting the intrinsically low selectivity and the challenges of modeling flexible solvated REE complexes. We evaluate the need to use density functional theory (DFT) for calculating enthalpy and find that MDbased calculations adequately capture overall enthalpic trends while avoiding the substantial computational cost of quantum methods. Overall, this work establishes a computationally tractable approach to study aqueous REE-peptide complexation thermodynamics and provides molecular level insight into the origins of selectivity, supporting the rational design of peptides for REE recovery.

Bio-derived conductive elastomers integrating autonomous self-healing, recyclability, degradability, and wearable sensing
abstract: Conductive elastomers are emerging as promising platforms for flexible and wearable electronics, yet simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, autonomous self-healing, recyclability, degradability, and biocompatibility remains challenging because most systems rely on toxic synthetic components and irreversible polymer network. Here, we report a bio-derived supramolecular conductive elastomer fabricated through room-temperature concentration-induced polymerization and concurrent self-assembly in ethanol. The dynamic network, stabilized by synergistic hydrogen bonding and zinc–carboxylate coordination interactions, suppresses depolymerization while enabling efficient network reconstruction after damage. The resultant elastomer exhibits excellent mechanical robustness, high stretchability, and complete stress self-healing efficiency after healing at 60 °C for 12 h. Notably, the material further demonstrates stable and reproducible temperature-dependent electrical responses together with highly sensitive strain-dependent resistance variations, enabling reliable temperature and strain sensing for wearable electronics. In addition, the elastomer undergoes efficient degradation in alkaline aqueous solution, predominantly yielding non-toxic thioctic acid derivatives. This work establishes a facile strategy for constructing sustainable supramolecular conductive elastomers with integrated self-healing, recyclability, degradability, and multimodal sensing capabilities, providing a pathway toward environmentally benign wearable electronic systems.

Microcellular–nanodomain engineering of fire-safe radiative-cooling polyurethane foams for low-carbon building insulation
abstract: Conventional rigid polyurethane foam (RPUF) is widely used for building insulation, yet its porous organic framework is vulnerable to solar heat accumulation, fire hazards, smoke release, and limited outdoor service durability. Here, a fire-resilient radiative-cooling polyurethane insulation foam is developed through microcellular–nanodomain engineering, in which interfacially engineered t-TiO 2 @SA-Co nanohybrids are structure-preservingly integrated within an RPUF matrix. The optimized RPUF/APP/t-TiO 2 @SA-Co preserves the intrinsic cellular framework while anchoring TiO 2 -based nanodomains within the foam skeleton and cell-wall regions, enabling coupled solar backscattering, atmospheric-window thermal emission, interfacial reinforcement, and condensed-phase fire protection. The optimized foam increases solar reflectance from 68.5% to 83.4% while maintaining a high atmospheric-window emissivity of 96.9%, enabling a maximum outdoor cooling difference of 13.1 °C. It simultaneously reduces peak heat release rate, total heat release, and total smoke release by 49.8%, 35.6%, and 65.4%, respectively, relative to pristine RPUF. TG–IR and char analyses indicate lower relative evolved-gas signals together with formation of a compact phosphorus-rich, inorganic-reinforced barrier. The foam further improves compressive strength from 352 to 420 kPa, while maintaining high antibacterial activity and exhibiting improved appearance stability after up to 50 h of solar exposure. EnergyPlus simulations connect the material-level cooling response with reduced cooling-energy demand and operational CO 2 emissions, providing a scalable route toward fire-safer and energy-efficient polymeric insulation foams.

title: Ultrafast laser-engineered black TiO2-x coatings for highly dispersed Pt catalysts with exceptional HER efficiency
abstract: The scalability of water electrolysis for hydrogen production is hindered by the high cost and limited availability of platinum-group metal (PGM) catalysts. Here, we present a rapid, additive-free strategy for fabricating highly efficient hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalysts with ultra-low platinum loading. Within seconds, laser treatment transforms metallic titanium into a nanostructured, black TiO 2-x support with a high surface area. The resulting amorphous oxide features a Ti 4+ -terminated surface and a partially reduced, conductive TiO 2-x subsurface as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy, TEM electron diffraction, and EELS analysis. This layered structure enhances charge transport and promotes strong metal–support interactions (MSI), enabling effective anchoring of highly dispersed Pt nanostructures obtained by mild annealing. The optimized catalyst, with only 3.6 μg Pt cm −2 , achieves an overpotential of 20 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in 0.1 M HClO 4 , matching commercial Pt/C despite using over five times less Pt. It also delivers a mass activity more than 3.5 times higher than Pt/C under the same conditions. Comparison of polarization curves before and after a 24 h chronopotentiometric test at 10 mA cm −2 revealed that the electrocatalytic activity was largely preserved. XPS reveals a + 1.2 eV shift in the Pt 4f binding energy relative to metallic Pt, consistent with MSI, while EELS confirms the presence of Ti 3+ in the subsurface region. DFT calculations confirmed the ability of TiO 2-x support to anchor and stabilize Pt particles, clusters, and single atoms, while simultaneously tuning their hydrogen adsorption features toward enhanced HER. This work establishes a new pathway for designing low-PGM electrocatalysts with high metal utilization, combining fabrication speed and simplicity.

abstract: Aluminum nitride (AlN) is a promising filler material for thermal interface composites owing to its high thermal conductivity. However, conventional AlN particles typically have irregular shapes and rough surfaces, which reduce flowability, lower packing density by introducing interparticle voids, and increase interfacial resistance, ultimately limiting the thermal performance of the composite. Herein, we introduce a flame-based process that forms an Al 2 O 3 -rich surface layer on AlN particles within a methane/oxygen diffusion flame while partially preserving the AlN core. This treatment significantly improves particle sphericity and surface smoothness, enabling dense packing in the resin composites. By precisely tuning the methane flow rate, we obtain composites with markedly enhanced thermal conductivity, reaching 3.2 W m −1 K −1 at 60 vol% filler loading, exceeding that (2.1 W m −1 K −1 ) obtained for untreated AlN. These findings indicate a scalable strategy for tailoring the morphology and interfacial properties of ceramic fillers, unlocking new opportunities for advanced thermal management in power electronics and high-frequency communication devices.

Decarbonising the Caribbean Sea using Cuban natural zeolites
abstract: Decarbonising marine transport represents a considerable challenge with on-board mass, space and safety constraints limiting the availability of suitable technologies. Vacuum Swing Adsorption (VSA) is a promising solution due to its ability to be retrofittable, preventing the need for a complete fuel system overhaul. For this purpose, Cuban natural zeolites are low-cost, highly abundant adsorbent materials which are attractive for carbon capture and storage (CCS), allowing the use of locally available materials in the Caribbean. Hence, in this work, Cuban natural zeolite (NZ) was modified by cation-exchanged and acid treatment to enhance the carbon capture properties. The treated zeolites were tested over 10 cycles in a VSA system under four different typical marine exhaust compositions ranging from idealised to more typical operating conditions, in order to understand the effects of the presence of N 2 , O 2 , H 2 O, CH 4 , CO, SO 2 and NO 2 on CO 2 working capacity. The highest working capacity under 8% CO 2 /air was 0.44 mmol g −1 and 0.50 mmol g −1 for the cation-exchanged and acid treated zeolites, respectively. Additionally, it was found that the presence of H 2 O, NO 2 and SO 2 have the largest impact on the CO 2 adsorption capacity, indicating the requirement for upstream pre-treatment steps. Using the experimental data, a shorthand scoping estimate was conducted on vessels typically found in the Caribbean Sea in order to estimate the deadweight tonnage (DWT) and material costs required, with the oil tanker having the lowest DWT requirement at 6.0% and none of the cases estimated to require more than $500 in adsorbent material cost.

abstract: This work reports the first experimental demonstration of a scaled-up multi-membrane reactor for ammonia synthesis, integrating four tubular carbon molecular sieve membranes (CMSMs) with two 3D-printed metallic Periodic Open Cellular Structure (POCS) supports of Gyroid and Body-Centred Cubic (BCC) geometry, manufactured in Inconel 625 by Laser Powder Bed Fusion and washcoated with a Ru-based catalyst via a scaled-up dip-spin coating procedure. The coating protocol transferred to both topologies at the larger scale without modification, with optical microscopy confirming uniform, crack-free coverage.. Novolac-based CMSM carbonized at 550 °C were characterised by organic elemental analysis, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy, confirming a defect-rich, turbostratic sp 2 carbon matrix with microporous architecture. Baseline testing in the conventional reactor over 350–450 °C and 20–40 bar(g) demonstrated that Gyroid and BCC configurations deliver virtually identical catalytic performance, reflecting the dominance of reaction kinetics and thermodynamics over geometry-dependent transport resistances. Upon membrane integration, this geometry-independence was preserved, and the membrane consistently enhanced NH 3 production rates across all operating conditions. Beyond-equilibrium operation, with H 2 conversion and NH 3 yield reproducibly exceeding thermodynamic limits, was achieved exclusively at low wight hourly space velocity (WHSV) and a sweep ratio (SW) of 4: H 2 conversion surpassed equilibrium by 30% at 400 °C and 110% at 450 °C, with NH 3 yield gains of 65% and 170% over the conventional reactor. Scaling from one to four membranes yielded a membrane-area-normalised productivity improvement of up to 424% at 350 °C and 40 bar(g), providing a strong foundation for continued scale-up of membrane reactors for ammonia synthesis.

Towards resource recovery in wastewater treatment: Integrated phosphorus and nitrogen recovery from anaerobic membrane bioreactor effluent through electrodialysis, crystallisation and membrane contactors
abstract: Nutrient recovery from wastewater is essential for transforming conventional treatment plants into resource recovery facilities. This study evaluates the feasibility of integrating electrodialysis, phosphorus crystallisation and hollow fibre membrane contactor technologies for the sequential recovery of phosphorus and nitrogen from real anaerobic membrane bioreactor effluent. Electrodialysis concentrated nutrients from 42 ± 11 to 846 ± 100 mg NH 4 -N/L and from 6.1 ± 2.9 to 102 ± 33 mg PO 4 -P/L, enabling subsequent recovery processes, while the diluted stream complied with DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/3019. Phosphorus recovery was investigated under different operational strategies, achieving 94% of recovery efficiency at pH 8.0, with hydroxyapatite identified as the predominant precipitated phase. Seeded experiments showed evidence of struvite formation. Subsequently, the phosphorus-depleted stream was adjusted to pH 9–11 to enhance ammonia transfer, and nitrogen was recovered as an ammonium sulphate solution using a hollow fibre membrane contactor with sulphuric acid as the stripping solution, achieving up to 86% of recovery efficiency. Results demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating nutrient concentration and recovery processes to valorise electrodialysis concentrated streams derived from real anaerobic membrane bioreactor effluent. This approach enables the production of nutrient based product, promoting resource recovery and circular economy strategies in wastewater treatment.

abstract: The rapid expansion of interconnected electronic systems poses increasing challenges to environmental sustainability, motivating the development of functional materials that combine high performance with end-of-life degradability. Here, we report a class of multifunctional eutectogels derived from biomass polymers, designed as versatile materials for sustainable transient electronics. These materials exhibit a unique combination of mechanical robustness, high flexibility, and long-term electrical stability, maintaining performance over three months under ambient conditions. The eutectogels display intrinsic antifreezing behaviour down to −50 °C and excellent skin compatibility, while undergoing visual soil degradation within seven weeks, demonstrating their suitability for environmentally benign applications. Their inherent ionic conductivity enables multimodal sensing capabilities, including strain sensing with a gauge factor of 1.6 and a detection limit of 0.06%, as well as reliable temperature and humidity monitoring. The materials are fully compatible with 3D printing techniques, enabling precise control over device architecture, mechanical compliance, and pressure-sensing performance. Beyond sensing, the eutectogels function as low-impact solid electrolytes in flexible supercapacitors, supporting stable operation over more than 5.000 charge–discharge cycles and enabling supercapacitor-integrated self-powered wearable systems. The combination of functional versatility and favourable environmental performance in a hypothetic industrial-scale life-cycle assessment (LCA) positions these eutectogels as promising material platform for next-generation sustainable transient electronics.

Does the nafion loading in cathode catalyst layers influence the transport and accumulation of water in PEMFCs?
abstract: Nafion loading in cathode catalyst layers (CCLs) affects proton exchange membrane fuel cell performance by influencing proton and oxygen transport within the electrode. Does it also affect water transport and accumulation? In this work, a custom-built setup is used to quantify, during galvanostatic polarization curves and current holds, membrane water crossover and liquid water accumulation within fuel cells with a CCL Nafion loading of 10 to 40 wt%, and under a range of operating conditions from hot/dry to cold/wet. Our results indicate that membrane water crossover and liquid water accumulation are influenced by Nafion loading, with the fuel cell containing 20 wt% Nafion achieving the best performance under all conditions, in part due to appropriate water rejection. During current hold experiments at 1.2 A/cm 2 , 60 ∘ C and 70% relative humidity, liquid saturation in the electrode is over 40% lower than in cells with 10 and 30 wt% ionomer. Increasing CCL Nafion loading reduces cathode-to-anode water crossover, especially when ionomer loading increases beyond 20 wt%, likely due to a shift in ORR activity away from the PEM–CCL interface. At very low CCL Nafion loading, water is produced near the membrane and has to diffuse through the entire CL. Thus, greater water accumulation is observed. At higher CCL Nafion loadings, decreased cathode-to-anode water crossover, combined with reduced electrode porosity and water diffusivity, leads to increased water accumulation. The 20 wt% Nafion case achieves optimal performance by balancing proton and gas transport, and providing a balance between water removal via crossover and transport out of the electrode, resulting in reduced water accumulation. The experimental dataset provided is ideal for model validation.

abstract: Developing high-performance and durable ultra-low Pt electrocatalysts for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a challenging task. Here, we report hybrid catalysts with exceptional oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity, composed of multi-dimensional active sites defined as the coupling of ordered intermetallic PtCo nanoparticles and single-atom M–N x –C sites on a porous crystalline nanocarbon. The in-situ incorporation of PtCo nanoparticles in nanocarbon facilitates the effective atomization and distribution of single-atoms around the ordered PtCo nanoparticles. The ORR mechanism of the hybrid catalysts is found to be a bifunctional relay pathway on multi-dimensional sites. In single-cell configuration with an ultra-low Pt loading (0.045 mg Pt cm −2 ) using industry-standard Nafion membrane, the catalyst demonstrated superior mass activities (1.57 A mg Pt −1 at 0.9 V under H 2 /O 2 and 2.81 A mg Pt −1 at 0.8 V under H 2 /Air) while retaining 71% of initial performance, highlighting the potential of the hybrid catalysts and their commercial viability. These findings are expected to pave the way for the design of ultra-low Pt catalysts for practical fuel cell applications.

abstract: High-performance activated carbons (ACs) for toluene capture were prepared from tannin (T) and wood charcoal (CC) through potassium acetate (KA) activation and urea (U) treatment to elucidate the role of N functionalization in adsorption performance. Under dry conditions, textural properties predominantly governed toluene adsorption at saturation, with the best-performing tannin-derived N-doped AC reaching 614 mg g −1 at 25 °C. In contrast, Henry constant ( K H ) analysis at very low relative pressures ( P/P 0 = 0–0.001) revealed a strong relationship between surface N density and initial toluene–surface affinity, indicating that N functionalities become particularly relevant in the low-concentration regime representative of indoor-air capture. Water-vapor adsorption, independently measured and successfully described by the Do and Do (DD) model, suggested potential moisture resistance up to approximately 40% relative humidity, as evidenced by the limited water uptake of the carbons. However, the greater affinity of N-treated ACs for water suggests that their beneficial effect on toluene affinity may be less pronounced under humid conditions. Overall, N functionalization primarily enhances low-pressure toluene–surface interactions rather than saturation capacity under dry conditions, while its effectiveness under realistic indoor-air conditions remains to be determined through direct competitive adsorption measurements.

Two-stage lactate-driven dark fermentation of household food waste for hydrogen production using an external dynamic membrane bioreactor
abstract: Lactate accumulation can constrain hydrogen (H 2 ) production during dark fermentation of real food waste (FW), yet lactate itself provides a substrate for lactate-driven dark fermentation (LD-DF). This study evaluated whether biomass retention in an external H 2 -producing dynamic membrane bioreactor (H 2 -DMBR) could intensify continuous conversion of an FW-derived lactate-rich stream into H 2 . In the first stage, an anaerobic sequencing batch reactor processing three batches of household FW generated lactate-rich effluents containing 27.2 ± 3.2 g/L lactate. These effluents were fed undiluted to the H 2 -DMBR. During membrane-assisted intensification from stages II to V, hydraulic retention time (HRT) was reduced from 24 to 9 h, a biomass-specific lactate loading range of 6.8–9.3 g lactate/g VSS-d was achieved, and the H₂ production rate doubled from 6.2 ± 0.7 to 12.5 ± 0.4 NL H₂/L-d. This intensification was primarily driven by suspended-biomass accumulation (up to 7.8 g VSS/L), with stable biomass-specific H 2 production (1.55–1.63 NL H 2 /g VSS-d) and balanced lactate supply and consumption. Molar balances supported a LD-DF complemented by residual-carbohydrate fermentation to H 2 and butyrate. At 6 h HRT, biomass-specific lactate loading reached 30.2 g lactate/g VSS-d, the highest value reached, coinciding with residual lactate accumulation, biomass loss, and lower H 2 production. Across the two-stage process, 16S rRNA gene profiles showed upstream dominance by Lactobacillus , followed by a downstream shift from Anaerostipes to Clostridium during H 2 -DMBR intensification. Overall, coupling lactate production with conversion in a biomass-retaining H 2 -DMBR intensified H 2 production from real FW, with biomass-specific lactate loading emerging as a system-specific descriptor of reactor response to increased substrate loading.

Towards generalizable wet foamability predictions: A dimensional analysis approach incorporating dynamic surface tension and symbolic regression
abstract: This study presents a groundbreaking chemical engineering approach to modeling wet foam formation through mechanical mixing and gas-sparging processes. Situated at the intersection of physico-chemistry, dimensional analysis, chemical engineering, and predictive modeling, this work utilizes an extensive experimental dataset covering a broad spectrum of operating conditions.For each foaming process examined, a single dimensionless correlation – capable of accurately predicting foam heights – is derived, irrespective of surfactant type, provided that dynamic surface tension is explicitly accounted for. The findings emphasize the pivotal role of surfactant dynamics in macroscopic foaming behavior, demonstrating that the time-dependent evolution of surface tension must be incorporated into foaming process models. This study serves as a compelling example of how chemical engineering principles can bridge molecular-scale mechanisms (e.g., surfactant migration at bubble interfaces) with macroscopic physical variables (e.g., foam height) observed at the process scale.Beyond its immediate relevance to the foaming community, this work highlights the feasibility of integrating non-constant properties into dimensional analysis frameworks – a practice rarely applied in the chemical engineering field – while adhering to rigorous similarity theory principles. Most importantly, the study underscores a broader message for chemical engineers: modern semi-empirical correlations can achieve unprecedented robustness by synergistically combining dimensional analysis (retaining physical interpretability and scalability, unlike purely data-driven approaches) with AI-driven techniques.

Direct conversion of plastic waste into nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes via in-situ nitrogen doping
abstract: Transforming plastic waste into carbon nanotubes (CNTs) through pyrolysis-catalysis process offers a promising route for waste upcycling, leveraging the high hydrocarbons content of plastics. However, the practical application of the waste-derived CNTs is often hindered by impurities and the need for post-synthesis modifications - such as nitrogen doping to enhance their functionality, a process that introduces additional complexity and inflexibility, thereby limiting the commercial viability of waste-sourced CNTs. To address these challenges, an in-situ nitrogen doping pyrolysis-catalysis strategy was developed for synthesizing functional CNTs. The as-prepared nitrogen-doped CNTs (N-CNTs) were systematically compared with those produced via ex-situ process ( i.e. , post-synthetic modification of pre-formed CNTs), including their quality, nitrogen content, and bonding species. The influence of different plastic feedstocks (polypropylene, polystyrene, high density polyethylene, low density polyethylene and mixed plastic) on the products was also investigated to evaluate the capability of the proposed in-situ approach for handling real-world plastic waste. Results demonstrated that the in-situ N-doped pyrolysis-catalysis process achieved high yields of H 2 (42 mmol g −1 plastic ) and N-CNTs (0.67 g g −1 plastic ). Moreover, the nitrogen contents of the CNTs reached 2.64–3.02 wt%, which was significantly higher than that obtained via ex-situ doping (0.62–0.70 wt%), with pyridinic nitrogen identified as the dominant species. The synthesized N-CNTs were further investigated as electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), exhibiting notable activity, excellent durability, and methanol tolerance comparable to commercial Pt/C catalysts. This study lays a foundation for advancing the valorization of plastic waste and paves the way for producing high-value CNT with tailed applications.

Bipolar membrane electrodialysis for ocean alkalinity enhancement: configuration feasibility and CO2 injection pathways
abstract: Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) requires energy-efficient methods for carbon sequestration. In this study, we tailor and experimentally evaluate two bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BPMED) configurations for OAE. BPMED incorporating anion-exchange membranes (AEMs) is a viable configuration, whereas using cation-exchange membranes (CEMs) is practically infeasible due to a continuous voltage increase linked to CEM resistance increase and precipitation. CO 2 injection was investigated either upstream of the BPMED, enabling in-situ bicarbonate formation within the alkaline compartment, or downstream of the BPMED by carbonating the alkaline product ( ex-situ ). Although the in-situ approach was designed to produce a seawater-compatible outlet pH, the product remained acidic due to extensive brucite and minor calcite precipitation within the BPMED cell, which consumed the generated alkalinity. In contrast, the ex-situ approach produced a brucite-dominated alkaline slurry, which was successfully carbonated to produce a seawater-compatible bicarbonate-enriched solution. In the short-duration 10 mA cm −2 experiment, the slurry accounted for 38% of the theoretical alkalinity production, while 37% accumulated inside the BPMED. During long-duration operation accumulated slurry inside the cell caused alkaline-compartment clogging after approximately 3 h, limiting normal operation and TA recovery; acid flushing temporarily restored both. The lowest energy consumption achieved in this work was 8.8 GJ/tonCO 2 , obtained at 20 mA cm −2 , with values across the tested conditions reaching up to 15.1 GJ/tonCO 2 . These results identify ex-situ BPMED as a viable and energy-competitive OAE strategy. Future work should focus on reducing energy consumption through enhanced TA recovery and enabling long-duration performance through reduced clogging.

Revealing competitive kinetics and thermal transitions in high-extractive biomass pyrolysis
abstract: Agro-industrial biomass pyrolysis supports sustainable energy recovery and resource efficiency, but its implementation requires detailed kinetic understanding. This study aims to determine the pyrolysis kinetics of extractive-rich Sotol bagasse (SB) and elucidate its underlying reaction behavior. This was achieved by rigorously comparing and validating advanced thermokinetic models based on thermogravimetric data collected at heating rates of 5–80 °C min −1 . The results show a strong dependence of kinetic parameters on reaction progression and reveal sequential thermal transitions governing SB decomposition. The RN-10 multi-step competitive reaction network improves the interpretation of this thermodynamic transition by establishing the interplay between devolatilization, intermediate transformation, and char evolution across distinct thermal regions. Crucially, it captures the distinct pathways of product formation across varying heating rates, providing a framework to interpret temperature-dependent changes. The resulting kinetic data further capture variations in reactivity, energy demand, and predicted product evolution during SB pyrolysis—highlighting how extractives, catalytically active alkali and alkaline-earth metals (AAEMs), and transport phenomena collectively contribute to the observed conversion behavior. The findings improve the interpretations of SB's decomposition behavior and support kinetic model development, thermal management strategies, and reactor design for extractive-rich biomass pyrolysis.

abstract: Wet SAG mill performance is governed by coupled charge motion, slurry transport, power transfer and ore breakage, but the role of slurry properties remains difficult to resolve at industrial scale. This study applies a GPU-accelerated CFD–VOF–DEM model to a full-scale 34′ SAG mill, resolving slurry and entrained air as Eulerian phases and tracking 5.7 million polydisperse ore and grinding-media particles. Five slurry conditions, in which apparent slurry viscosity, fine-ore volume fraction and slurry density vary consistently, were investigated at four mill speeds. Higher-viscosity, denser slurry conditions were associated with a lower charge shoulder position and reduced mill power draw. The decrease in power draw arose primarily from weakened particle–lifter torque transfer, whereas the slurry-induced power contribution showed only a slight increase. Ore breakage also decreased as higher-viscosity denser slurry attenuated particle motion through the slurry-pool region, suppressed above-threshold collisions and reduced the effective collision energy ratio. Across the investigated range, mill speed exerted a stronger influence than slurry conditions on breakage and liner wear by increasing cataracting motion, collision energy and particle–liner dissipation. Higher mill speeds partly compensated for slurry damping, but restoring power alone did not recover ore breakage; restoring breakage required substantially greater increases in mill speed and power, together with increased lifter wear. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for coordinating slurry conditions and mill speed to balance grinding performance, power demand and liner wear in SAG milling.

Calcium-triggered self-anchoring bilayer microneedle patch with spatiotemporally programmed TLR4 activation remodels the immune microenvironment of abdominal wall endometriosis
abstract: Abdominal wall endometriosis (AWE), a distinct clinical subtype of endometriosis, is driven by a dysregulated immune microenvironment dominated by M2 macrophages. Current surgical and hormonal therapies are limited by high recurrence (5–20%), incomplete lesion resection, systemic side effects, and unsuitability for fertility-seeking patients. Here, we design a calcium-triggered self-anchoring bilayer microneedle patch (d-MN@DDAH) that integrates mechanical interlocking, pH-responsive drug release, and spatiotemporally programmed immunomodulation for a “first attack, then repair” AWE therapy. The lower needle layer consists of oxidized alginate grafted with a TLR4-targeting peptide (DDAH) via Schiff base bonds for acid-responsive immune activation; the upper layer comprises gelatin methacryloyl loaded with citric acid (CA) for sustained repair. The patch exhibits a well-defined bilayer structure, sufficient mechanical strength for skin penetration, and calcium-triggered swelling for tissue anchoring. DDAH shows pH-dependent release, while CA displays sustained release over 14 days. The patch is non-cytotoxic and orchestrates sequential macrophage polarization from an early M1 phenotype to a reparative M2 phenotype in vitro. In vivo dynamic monitoring further confirmed an early M1-dominant phase followed by a timely M2 transition. This reprogrammed microenvironment inhibits endometriotic cell proliferation and invasion, induces apoptosis, and downregulates key pathogenic molecules including MMP-2/9 and CYP19A1. In an AWE mouse model, the d-MN@DDAH patch achieves 92.6% lesion growth inhibition, reduces fibrosis, restores immune homeostasis (M1/M2 ≈ 0.62:1), alleviates pain, and shows no systemic toxicity. This work provides a transformative, non-hormonal, and spatiotemporally programmable platform for AWE and other immune-mediated diseases.

Interfacial Modulus mismatch explains ambient–post-reaction strength decoupling in metallurgical coke during CO2 gasification
abstract: Metallurgical coke is commonly evaluated under the assumption that ambient mechanical strength and coke strength after reaction improve together. This assumption becomes unreliable in complex coal blends containing weakly caking and high-inertinite components. Here, we combine industrial data, UMAP-guided sample selection, SEM, AFM-QNM, BET/ECSA analysis, and isothermal CO 2 gasification kinetics to identify the micromechanical origin of this decoupling. Targeted samples retained robust ambient skeletons but showed pronounced interfacial debonding after gasification. AFM-QNM revealed strong modulus contrast between rigid inertinite-rich domains and the compliant mosaic matrix. To quantify this risk, we define an Effective Modulus Mismatch Index (EMMI) by coupling the inertinite/mosaic modulus ratio with optical-texture volume fractions. PSR decreased exponentially with increasing EMMI (R 2 = 0.940), whereas MSI rebounded at high mismatch. Moderate mismatch generated microporosity and active sites, while extreme mismatch formed fracture pathways that lowered the initial apparent activation energy to 82.7 kJ mol −1 and accelerated localized gasification. These results redefine high-temperature coke degradation as a mechano-chemical coupling failure, demonstrating that severe interfacial modulus mismatch between constituent phases, rather than bulk structural looseness, dictates high-temperature failure. This EMMI framework provides a novel, micromechanics-based criterion for designing coal blends that ensure genuine service stability under blast-furnace conditions.

Polyethylenimine-functionalized reduced graphene oxide for CO2 capture and rapid joule-driven regeneration
abstract: Regeneration of solid amine-based sorbents remains a key challenge for direct air capture (DAC), particularly due to strong amine-CO 2 interactions that can hinder rapid desorption. Coupling polyethylenimine (PEI), which provides abundant CO 2 -binding amine sites, with electrically conductive reduced graphene oxide (rGO) offers an attractive route to rapid, localized Joule-heated CO 2 release. Here, we report the synthesis, structural elucidation, and electrothermal performance of a PEI-functionalized rGO composite (PEI-rGO-400) optimized for rapid CO 2 desorption. Systematic thermal treatment identified 400 °C as optimal for balancing basal-plane deoxygenation with residual perimeter functional groups, enabling PEI integration through covalent amide linkages and electrostatic interactions. PEI-rGO-400 exhibits semiconductor-like negative temperature coefficient behaviour and reaches a steady-state desorption temperature of 195 °C within 3.5 min at 12 W. Under dry conditions, CO 2 uptake increased from 0.015 mmol/g at 0.04 vol% to 2.8 mmol/g at 100 vol% following 60 min exposure at 100 sccm. Temperature-programmed desorption revealed a concentration-dependent change in apparent desorption kinetics, with alkylammonium carbamate ion-pair formation at high CO 2 coverages, possibly to be associated with increased polymer interactions. Lower CO 2 loadings representative of DAC streams exhibited a lower apparent desorption activation energy, with the Redhead-derived barrier decreasing from approximately 118 to 103 kJ/mol (~12.7%). The composite maintained electrothermal reproducibility and structural integrity over 20 power cycles, demonstrating its potential for rapid electrothermal CO 2 capture and regeneration.

abstract: The search for working fluids that balance thermodynamic performance, safety, and environmental sustainability remains a pressing challenge for refrigeration and heat pump technologies. Here, we present a hybrid computational workflow combining deep generative learning with classical thermodynamic modelling to identify novel working fluid candidates. Using a graph-based diffusion model, we generate and screen molecules against a quantitative physicochemical profile derived from known working fluids. We characterise five selected candidates in depth through molecular dynamics simulations, the polar soft-SAFT equation of state, COSMO-RS calculations, and two neural network predictors for flammability and GWP. We find that the predicted thermophysical and transport properties of the candidates fall within the range of established hydrofluorocarbons. Benchmarking against R-245fa and R-134a identifies a new compound (3,3,3-trifluoro-2-methylpropene) as the most promising candidate for high-temperature heat pump applications, and confirms another (1,1,1,2,2-pentafluoropropane) as a viable refrigerant for vapour compression cycles. Our work establishes a scalable framework for the rational, data-driven discovery of next-generation working fluids.

Accurate and cost-effective partial electrolyte SOC sensing in flow batteries with a 3-electrode OCV cell
abstract: The paper presents an improved method for measuring the partial states of charge ( SOC + and SOC − ) measurements in vanadium flow batteries (VFB), based on a low-cost three-electrode open-circuit voltage ( OCV ) cell employing a simple third graphite reference electrode filled with a vanadium electrolyte solution. Typically, such measurement systems are affected by subtle parasitic phenomena that can compromise accuracy. To ensure accurate, reliable, and repeatable measurements, these effects were systematically identified, quantified, and mitigated. They included electrical effects originating from both the measurement circuitry and the hydraulic network. The former were minimized through careful impedance matching, with particular attention given to the input impedance of the data acquisition unit. The latter arise from shunt currents—i.e., unintended currents circulating through conductive electrolyte pathways that form closed loops where cell electromotive forces are acting. These represent a source of error that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been systematically investigated in OCV measurement systems for flow batteries. The stepwise procedure adopted to improve measurement accuracy by progressively eliminating these parasitic effects is described in detail. Two validation protocols are also presented. Once the OCV measurement system has been installed and calibrated, the method enables the algorithmic determination of partial SOCs from partial OCV measurements, providing a fast and accurate approach suitable for real-time SOC monitoring. Furthermore, it can be readily implemented in virtually any VFB system. The method is therefore particularly relevant for industrial-scale vanadium flow batteries, as it provides an effective tool for optimal capacity management, fast triggering the execution of maintenance procedures aimed at restoring the battery's original capacity.

Micro-CT-based permeability characterization of virgin and pyrolyzed wood using deep learning segmentation and image-based pore-scale simulations
abstract: Permeability governs gas transport in pyrolyzing wood and strongly influences predictions of devolatilization and internal pressure build-up as the pore network evolves. We present an image-based workflow to quantify how pyrolysis modifies the intrinsic permeability tensor of Pinus pinaster (maritime pine) earlywood using synchrotron micro-CT, deep-learning segmentation, and pore-scale flow simulations. Anatomically matched submicron microtomography volumes were acquired before and after in-situ pyrolysis under nitrogen, up to 525 °C. Orientation-robust 3D pore/solid segmentation was obtained using three 2D U-Net models trained on longitudinal, radial, and tangential slice sets and fused by majority vote. Steady incompressible creeping-flow simulations, with Re ≪ 1, were then performed in OpenFOAM using simpleFoam to compute the full permeability tensor. Sensitivity analyses and a permeability-based REV study selected a representative cube size of 390 µm, corresponding to 1300³ voxels. Pyrolysis slightly increased porosity and shifted local pore diameters toward smaller values. Longitudinal and radial permeabilities decreased by 47% and 24%, whereas tangential permeability increased by a factor of 5.86, substantially reducing anisotropy. These trends indicate that pyrolysis restructures transport primarily by modifying constrictions and transverse connectivity rather than uniformly enlarging conduits.

abstract: In this study, CALF-20, a scalable metal-organic framework (MOF) with high CO₂ adsorption affinity and excellent chemical stability, was investigated for photothermal CO₂ reduction. The CALF-20/Ti₃C₂ MXene was synthesized via a self-assembly approach, in which CALF-20 served as the CO₂-philic, while Ti₃C₂ nanosheets enhanced interfacial charge transfer, provided abundant active sites, and acted as an electron sink. Under light irradiation, the optimized catalyst produced 6.98, 0.37, and 0.75 μmol g −1 h −1 of CO, CH₄, and H₂, respectively. The resulting interfacial electric field promoted efficient charge separation and prolonged carrier lifetimes. Under photothermal conditions (250 °C), the production rates increased to 24.95, 2.49, and 12.48 μmol g −1 h −1 , demonstrating the strong synergy between light and heat in enhancing charge transport and reaction kinetics. This remarkable enhancement is attributed to the synergistic effects of photonic excitation and thermal activation, which generate higher-energy charge carriers, improve charge transport kinetics, and accelerate surface reaction dynamics. These findings highlight the crucial role of photo-thermal synergy in enhancing the overall efficiency of CO₂ conversion. Monochromatic light-filter experiments further revealed that the catalyst exhibited its highest photothermal activity at a wavelength of approximately 400 nm, while the lowest activity was observed near 600 nm, as evidenced by apparent quantum yields (AQYs) analysis. This work presents a promising strategy for the rational design of MOF/MXene heterojunctions for efficient solar-driven photothermal CO₂ conversion to fuels.

Thermal-gradient preservation and heat-transfer pathways in folded vertical wearable thermoelectric generators
abstract: Low thermal conductivity is generally considered desirable for preserving temperature gradients in wearable thermoelectric generators (TEGs). Here, we investigate how film thermal transport is associated with the competition between thermal shorting and distributed surface cooling in folded vertical TEGs. Folded vertical TEGs were constructed using p-type single-walled carbon nanotube/poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and Cu 2 Se/PVDF films exhibiting a nearly 60-fold difference in thermal conductivity, together with a common n-type Ag 2 Se film. An axial fin analysis using thickness-weighted effective properties of the folded multilayer stack captured the magnitude and thermal-spacing dependence of ΔT utilization for both devices, including the pronounced saturation behavior of the Cu 2 Se/PVDF device at large thermal spacing. Controlled-airflow and hot-side-shielding experiments further revealed competition between beneficial distributed cooling and parasitic hot-side heat loss. Selective hot-side shielding extended the favorable airflow regime, providing strong experimental evidence for the proposed mechanism. A 20-pair wearable TEG maintained ΔT utilization of 41.6% and 39.1% at body-to-air temperature differences of 5.1 and 10.1 K, generating maximum powers of 1.05 and 3.87 μW, respectively. These findings indicate that the role of film thermal transport in wearable TEGs depends on device geometry and thermal boundary conditions.

title: The influence of heterocyclic amino acid ionic liquids on HKUST-1 structure and gas adsorption properties
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely applied in the emitted CO 2 management, like photocatalytic reduction, carbon capture or storage, leading to reduction of greenhouse gas emission to the atmosphere. However, the positive environmental effect of MOFs utilization in the field of carbon capture can be further improved by implementing bio-based substances in the synthesis processes. In this work, the influence of naturally-derived amino acid ionic liquids (AAILs) on a highly porous HKUST-1 MOF morphology and gas sorption properties were investigated. Additionally, it was one of the first attempts to directly compare AAILs introduction methods into MOF structures: synthetical incorporation and post-synthetical impregnation. Synthetical route was proven to be vastly superior in improving CO 2 uptake (25 °C, 1 bar) – reaching up to 43% increase for sample 0.25EP modified with 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium prolinate [EMIM][Pro] with molar ratio of n Cu :n linker :n IL = 1.6:1:0.25, when compared to pristine HKUST-1. It was also observed, that the size of both anion and cation of IL have noticeable impact on the specific surface area (S BET ) of resulting MOFs – when impregned with 10% IL, the smallest [EMIM][Pro] resulted in S BET of 696 m 2 ·g −1 , whereas the biggest [BMIM][His] – 176 m 2 ·g −1 . Moreover, the experimental data was used for multiscale computational studies to assess the separation performance of AAILs-modified HKUST-1. The simulation results show that moderate incorporating AAIL enhances CO 2 retention under process-relevant conditions, doubling the retention time for 0.25EP. Additionally, the prediction of the CO 2 /CH 4 and CO 2 /N 2 mixtures separation was performed, revealing exceptional selectivity of 0.25EP, reaching up to almost 11 and 50 mol/mol respectively at low pressure range. The proposed synthetical method of bio-based ILs introduction into MOF structure was proven to be simple and highly efficient in terms of CO 2 utilization, paving the route for more environment-friendly large-scale applications.

Dual-functional CuFe2O4/WS2 nanocomposite for faradaic charge storage and tetracycline removal
abstract: Developing bifunctional materials for electrochemical energy storage and water treatment can reduce the need for separate application-specific solids. Herein, a CuFe 2 O 4 /WS 2 nanocomposite was prepared through a one-step solvothermal route and evaluated as a binder-free Faradaic electrode and tetracycline (TC) adsorbent. Structural and microscopic analyses confirmed the formation of a two-phase particle-on-sheet structure in which CuFe 2 O 4 nanoparticles were closely associated with layered WS 2 platelets. The CuFe 2 O 4 /WS 2 electrode delivered 342 F g −1 at 6 A g −1 in a three-electrode configuration using 3 M KOH and retained 90.4% of its capacitance after 5000 CV cycles. Kinetic analysis gave a b value of 0.58, indicating predominantly diffusion-dependent Faradaic charge storage with a smaller surface-controlled contribution. Density functional theory calculations revealed interfacial charge redistribution, the preservation of electronic states near the Fermi level, and stronger stabilization of hydroxyl species on CuFe 2 O 4 /WS 2 . For water treatment, the nanocomposite achieved complete TC removal from a 25 mg L −1 solution under the reference batch conditions and reached an uptake of 348.1 mg g −1 at 100 mg L −1 and 45 °C after 48 h. Adsorption kinetic fitting indicated that intraparticle diffusion contributed strongly to the uptake process, while the positive Weber–Morris intercept showed that it was not the sole rate-controlling step. Furthermore, the nanocomposite demonstrated excellent practical applicability when tested using real wastewater and great reusability potential. These results show that the CuFe 2 O 4 /WS 2 nanocomposite can serve as a bifunctional material platform for Faradaic charge storage and antibiotic adsorption.

A hydrogel based delivery system of hypoxia-preconditioned olfactory mucosa mesenchymal stem cell exosomes enhances neurovascular repair after spinal cord injury
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes persistent neurological deficits through secondary pathological events, including neuroinflammation, vascular dysfunction, neuronal loss, and glial scar formation. Exosomes derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) offer a promising cell-free strategy for SCI repair, but their rapid clearance, poor lesion site retention, and variable reparative activity limit their therapeutic efficacy. Here, we developed a chitosan/polyvinyl alcohol/glutaraldehyde hydrogel for sustained local delivery of exosomes derived from hypoxia-preconditioned olfactory mucosa MSCs, a neural-associated MSC source with potential advantages for nervous tissue repair. The isolated olfactory mucosa MSCs showed typical MSC characteristics and multilineage differentiation capacity, while hypoxic preconditioning increased hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expression. The resulting exosomes displayed typical vesicular morphology, size distribution, and marker expression. The composite hydrogel exhibited an interconnected porous architecture, flowable shear-thinning viscoelasticity, and syringe injectability, while providing prolonged release of exosome-associated protein and favorable biocompatibility in vitro and in vivo. In a rat SCI model, injection of the exosome-loaded hydrogel reduced lesion area and improved hindlimb locomotion and weight-bearing function. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses indicated that these effects were associated with modulation of inflammatory responses, angiogenesis, neural repair, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Further validation showed enhanced neuronal differentiation, increased vascular regeneration, and macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype. Compared with bone marrow MSC exosome-loaded hydrogel, the olfactory mucosa MSC exosome-loaded hydrogel produced stronger repair effects under the same delivery platform, although the specific exosomal effectors underlying this difference remain uncharacterized. This study provides a tissue-specific, biomaterial-assisted exosome delivery strategy for SCI repair.

title: Ultrasound-activated MnOx–auranofin nanoplatform for sonodynamic-immunomodulatory eradication of postoperative minimal residual disease in oral cancer
abstract: Postoperative recurrence caused by minimal residual disease (MRD) remains a major challenge in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), largely due to the difficulty of accurately eliminating residual tumor cells while simultaneously activating local antitumor immune activation. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive nanoplatform (AUR@MnOx@PEG, AMP) that integrates auranofin (AUR) and manganese oxide (MnOx) nanoflowers for localized sonodynamic-immunomodulatory therapy against postoperative tumor recurrence. The nanostructured MnOx framework enables efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation under ultrasound stimulation, while AUR disrupts tumor redox homeostasis through thioredoxin reductase inhibition, thereby amplifying oxidative stress and promoting robust immunogenic cell death (ICD). Concurrently, Mn 2+ ions released from MnOx activate the cGAS–STING signaling pathway, further enhancing innate immune activation. Ultrasound-triggered AMP induces pronounced ROS production, DAMP release (CRT exposure and HMGB1 secretion), and activation of the STING–TBK1–IRF3 signaling cascade, resulting in dendritic cell maturation and enhanced CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell infiltration. In a clinically relevant murine OSCC postoperative recurrence model, peritumoral administration of AMP combined with ultrasound significantly suppresses tumor recurrence, reduces lymph node metastatic involvement, and markedly prolongs survival without evident systemic toxicity. This work establishes a locally activated nanotherapeutic strategy that integrates sonodynamic therapy combined local immune activation to eliminate MRD and reshape the postoperative immune microenvironment, offering a promising nanomedicine approach for preventing cancer recurrence following surgical resection.

Understanding contrast agent performance of GMO@DTPA-BSA-Gd nanoassemblies via molecular dynamics
abstract: Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) remain central to clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), yet free Gd3+ release and the low relaxivity of small-molecule GBCAs continue to motivate the development of safer, more effective alternatives. Here we describe GMO@DTPA-BSA-Gd nanoassemblies, prepared from glyceryl monooleate (GMO), the high-molecular-weight Gd-chelating lipid DTPA-bis(stearylamide) gadolinium salt (DTPA-BSA-Gd), and a Pluronic F127 stabilizer. Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) showed that liquid-crystalline nanoparticles with Pn3m diamond symmetry coexisted with lamellar liposomal structures in the same dispersion. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) confirmed strong colloidal and chemical stability under storage, physiological, and endosomal conditions, with minimal Gd3+ release (≤ 4 %) over 72 h. To explain this performance, molecular dynamics were probed by 1H NMR relaxometry across a wide Larmor frequency range (10 kHz–300 MHz) at 298 and 310 K. The profiles were fitted with a two-population extension of the Solomon-Bloembergen-Morgan (SBM) model, which expresses the paramagnetic relaxation enhancement through two rotational correlation times (τR1 = 2.09 × 10-9 s, τR2 = 0.22 × 10-9 s at 298 K), reflecting the non-uniform distribution of the assemblies. The temperature-dependent fall in water residence time (τM) indicated a water exchange-limited regime, producing a longitudinal relaxivity of 14.1 mM-1s-1 at 23 MHz - higher than clinical Magnevist and Gadovist. In vitro, the nanoassemblies were biocompatible across a broad concentration range and single-cell mass spectrometry revealed cellular uptake an order of magnitude higher than Gadovist, confirmed by confocal imaging. Molecular dynamics thus emerge as the principal determinant of relaxometric performance, underscoring the promise of these nanoassemblies as next-generation high-molecular-weight MRI contrast agents.

Acoustic coupling in alkaline sono-electrolysers for hydrogen production: A hybrid study of the role of frequency and sonication mode
abstract: This work investigates the influence of ultrasound frequency (20 and 490 kHz) and sonication mode (direct and indirect) on hydrogen production in alkaline sono-electrolysis. A combined experimental and numerical approach was employed to elucidate how acoustic coupling governs the relative contributions of sonophysical and sonochemical effects to electrochemical performance. Preliminary calorimetric measurements were used to decouple the effects of acoustic power and acoustic pressure amplitude, enabling meaningful comparisons between different configurations. In direct sono-electrolysis operated at comparable acoustic power (55 ± 2 W), 490 kHz ultrasound enhanced hydrogen production by nearly threefold relative to 20 kHz, despite its lower acoustic pressure amplitude. The limited improvement observed at 20 kHz was attributed to excessively high-pressure amplitudes (6 bar), which promote bubble coalescence and degassing, thereby counteracting beneficial bubble detachment effects. To isolate amplitude effects, indirect configurations were fine-tuned to achieve quasi-identical acoustic pressure amplitudes (1.1 ± 0.1 bar). Under these conditions, hydrogen production was suppressed at both frequencies, with a near-complete inhibition at 20 kHz, highlighting the critical role of efficient acoustic delivery to the electrode–electrolyte interface. Numerical simulations at the single-bubble scale confirmed that, at low frequency, mechanical energies released during cavitation (shockwaves and microjets) exceed the chemical energy stored in hydrogen by several orders of magnitude, demonstrating the predominance of sonophysical mechanisms and the negligible contribution of sonochemistry. Overall, the results show that low frequency ultrasound enhances alkaline electrolysis primarily through frequency- and coupling-dependent mechanical effects rather than chemical activation, and that optimizing acoustic coupling, particularly through appropriate acoustic amplitude, is essential to exploit ultrasound as an energy-efficient intensification strategy for sono-electrolytic hydrogen production.
