abstract: Deep wound infections remain difficult to treat because bacteria infiltrate poorly vascularized tissues and establish biofilms that severely restrict antimicrobial penetration and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we engineer a hierarchically structured dual-layer dissolvable microneedle that integrates ultrasmall silver nanoclusters (AgNCs) with spatiotemporally programmed therapeutic functions, enabling rapid infection indication, sustained antimicrobial delivery, and microenvironment modulation for the treatment of deep biofilm-associated wound infections. The outer layer generates an immediate colorimetric indication of bacterial infection and initiates rapid Ag + release based on pH changes, whereas the inner layer delivers prolonged antimicrobial and antioxidant therapy over 24 h. In vitro studies demonstrated potent antibiofilm activity, achieving 6-log reduction in viable pathogens, accompanied by significant reductions in biofilm biomass, integrity and thickness. Beyond antimicrobial activity, the microneedle promoted wound repair through reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility, supporting faster wound closure within 12 h. In vivo evaluation using an infected burn wound model demonstrated effective elimination of S. aureus biofilm infection and accelerated wound healing over 12 days. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the AgNC-loaded MNs provide sustained localized antimicrobial activity, effective biofilm eradication, and oxidative stress modulation, representing a promising strategy for treating deep biofilm-associated chronic wound infections.

From Li-ion to dual-ion batteries: Cation–anion solvation asymmetry as a design principle for electrolytes and interphases
abstract: Dual-ion batteries (DIBs) have emerged as a promising high-voltage, low-cost energy storage platform, yet their development remains constrained by the lack of well-defined electrolyte design principles. This review introduces cation–anion solvation asymmetry as a central concept for understanding electrolyte behavior in DIBs. To capture this effect, a conceptual solvation asymmetry index (SAI) is proposed, reflecting the balance between effective cation solvation strength and anion stabilization. Within this framework, electrolyte solvents originally developed for lithium-ion batteries are systematically reinterpreted rather than directly transferred to DIB systems, linking solvent molecular structure to interphase formation and ion coordination behavior. The SAI evolution of electrolyte systems is analyzed across ester-, ether-, aqueous-, and ionic-liquid-based solvents, highlighting how their distinct physicochemical properties regulate anion activity, oxidative stability, and interfacial chemistry. Collectively, this descriptor-driven perspective establishes a unified understanding of electrolyte function in DIBs and provides actionable guidelines for the rational design of next-generation high-voltage systems.

Adamantane plasma polymers: Fluorine-free vacuum-processable triboelectric thin films for all-triboelectric nanogenerator configurations
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are major drivers in on-site power generation for smart devices, enable self-powered sensors, and introduce novel catalytic processes. Here, we demonstrate adamantane plasma polymers as versatile dual-polarity triboelectric surfaces that can exhibit either tribopositive or tribonegative behaviour by simply controlling the plasma deposition configuration, without additives or post-functionalization. By modifying the substrate orientation relative to the plasma, thin-film polymers with distinct dielectric, mechanical, secondary electron emission, and triboelectric properties are obtained. The high conformality, stability, and processability of the polymers enable their direct implementation into solid-solid, solid-liquid, and hybrid piezo-triboelectric configurations. Additional surface texturization through buckling provides voltage and current outputs as high as 90 V peak-to-peak and 0.6 μA cm −2 for a 2.8 μm (tribonegative) vs. 400 nm (tribopositive) combination with a maximum mean power density of 2.1 μW cm −2 . A maximum peak power of 200 μW is generated from salty droplets in drop-TENG configuration employing a 500 nm-thick tribopositive adamantane polymer. These layers sustain more than 10 5 cycles in solid-solid nanogenerators and 10 4 droplet impacts in solid-liquid devices. Combined with an environmentally friendly, industrially scalable synthesis route, these results position adamantane plasma polymers as a robust, versatile platform for next-generation triboelectric energy-harvesting materials.

Computational fluid dynamic-guided design of a serpentine gas diffusion electrode microbial electrosynthesis cell for continuous acetate production from CO2
abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is a promising carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technology to convert carbon dioxide (CO2) into added-value compounds. However, low production rates and high energy consumption still hinder its application on a large scale. A serpentine three-chamber gas diffusion electrode (GDE)-based MES cell was developed and compared to a basic square cell design by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and tested in real-world biotic experiments, both in batch and continuous mode. CFD model results showed a homogeneous electrolyte and CO2 distribution in the serpentine-shaped cell, resulting in the absence of ”dead zones” on the electrode surface and hydrodynamic parameters favourable to biofilm development. Biotic experiments in batch mode confirmed the superiority of the serpentine design in terms of acetate productivity from CO2. The serpentine-shaped cells were then operated in continuous mode (first time for GDE-based MES cells), showing a further 30% increase in acetate production rate than in batch operation, halving the electric energy consumption per kg of acetate produced. The cells reached a highest average production rate of 2.2 g L-1 d-1 at 1.08 days of hydraulic retention time (HRT) and were able to withstand HRTs as low as 0.81 days with minimum performance losses. This work highlights the importance of cell design and modelling for advancing MES, and the benefits that continuous operation can bring. Further improvements, especially on the electrical efficiency of the system, are key to the development of an industrially viable process.

Pd catalyst supported on aryl-bridged polysilsesquioxane for hydrogenation of p-nitrophenol: Effect of solvent and pH
abstract: Aryl-Bridged polysilsesquioxane (ABPS), a hydrophobic, mesoporous, hybrid silica material, was employed as a support for a palladium (Pd) catalyst for catalytic hydrogenation of para-nitrophenol (PNP) to para-aminophenol (PAP) using molecular hydrogen. The effect of protic and aprotic solvents on the catalytic hydrogenation activity of para-nitrophenol (PNP) was investigated, and water, with the highest proticity, was observed to give the highest PNP conversion. The PNP hydrogenation activity was also found to decrease with decreasing proticity of the solvent. The PNP hydrogenation activity and product stability were investigated at different pH levels. To study the effect of pH on PNP adsorption, equilibrium adsorption capacity of Pd/ABPS at varying pH was determined, and Pd/ABPS samples following PNP adsorption were characterized with Raman spectroscopy. PNP conversion was calculated using UV–Vis spectroscopy, and the products of the PNP hydrogenation were identified using 1 H Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (NMR), Mass Spectrometry (MS), and Raman Spectroscopy. Additionally, the performance of the Pd/ABPS catalyst was also benchmarked using Pd/AC, a commercial activated carbon-supported hydrogenation catalyst.

title: Combining physics-informed machine learning and heterogeneous transfer learning for hydrodenitrogenation of co-processed feedstocks
abstract: Accurately predicting the nitrogen content of co-processed petroleum feedstocks after hydrotreatment is a common challenge in refining, exacerbated by the limited experimental data available for each new feedstock. Transfer learning addresses this scarcity by leveraging knowledge from a related, data-rich source. For the source, the hydrodenitrogenation (HDN) of fossil vacuum gas oil, a rich dataset and an accurate prior ordinary differential equation (ODE) are available; for the target, the HDN of co-processed vacuum gas oil and tire-pyrolysis oil, the ODE structure is unknown and an additional descriptor (the tire fraction) is present, making the problem heterogeneous. To recover this unknown ODE, we propose HTL-HyODE, a heterogeneous transfer learning hybrid ODE in which small neural networks encode its unknown components while the rest is kept explicit and transferred from the source. For comparison, we also develop physics-informed variants (HTL-PINNs) of data-driven heterogeneous transfer networks. On simulated data, HTL-HyODE reduces the test mean absolute error (MAE) by up to 52% relative to a no-transfer hybrid baseline at a training size of n t = 25 when the networks are correctly placed. On experimental data, the benefit with respect to the no-transfer hybrid baseline depends on the target size and on the retained structure: at n t = 15 the best-matched structure reduces the MAE by about 50%–57%, whereas at n t = 50 the data-driven and physics-informed networks overtake it, DHTLFT-PINNs reaching the lowest error. Embedding the kinetic structure explicitly is thus most effective when it is reliable and data are scarce, while network-based transfer becomes preferable as data accumulate; the learned hybrid components remain physically consistent in both regimes.

abstract: This work reports a sustainable, high-performance hybrid polyelectrolyte hydrogel designed for dual-application in solar-driven desalination (SDD) and capacitive deionization (CDI). The matrix comprises acrylamide (AAm) covalently copolymerized with positively charged diallyldimethylammonium chloride (DADMAC) and additivated with different amount of low-cost conductive carbon-black (CB) microparticles (from 5 to 20% w/w). Incorporating permanent positive charges into the crosslinked network provides exceptional salt-swelling properties while enabling the hydrogel to function as a highly efficient and reversible anion uptake. Furthermore, CB microparticles maximize the evaporation process ensuring a UV solar absorptivity above 93%, even at low concentrations. Under solar illumination, the hydrogel yields high, constant steam generation performance, reaching evaporation rates of 7.22 ± 0.40 kg m⁻² h⁻¹, when normalized by the top projected area (ER2D) and 1.26 ± 0.02 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ in reflector-assisted omnidirectional 3D setups (ER3D). Notably, rising operational temperatures from 25 °C to 45 °C drive an increase of 37% in the ionic conductivity (from 0.35 to 0.48 mS cm⁻¹), enhancing thermal charge transport. When deployed in cyclic CDI desalinating operations, the soft polymer doubles the cell's salt adsorption capacity (SAC) compared to gel-free systems, achieving charge efficiencies of approximately 96% and 78% under zero and reverse voltage experiments, respectively. This eco-friendly hydrogel provides a scalable platform that can improve the longevity of carbon electrodes as a viable alternative to conventional methodologies.

title: De novo biosynthesis of pomegranate seed oil-equivalent lipids in engineered yeasts
abstract: Although commercially valuable, plant-derived unusual fatty acids such as punicic acid (PuA) are constrained by their limited natural distribution and the challenges associated with large-scale agricultural production. Despite advances in heterologous production, engineered systems rarely achieve the accumulation levels observed in native producers. Here, we engineered the model yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae and the non-conventional yeast Rhodosporidium toruloides to accumulate PuA as the predominant fatty acid. Building on the distinct characteristics of these two hosts, we developed tailored metabolic engineering strategies that substantially improved both PuA content and titer. Notably, R. toruloides significantly outperformed S. cerevisiae , achieving up to 57% PuA of total fatty acids, a level comparable to that of pomegranate seed oil. In a 5 L bioreactor, engineered R. toruloides produced over 4.6 g/L PuA using a two-stage process with molasses for biomass accumulation and glucose for lipid production. Comparative analysis also revealed fundamental differences between the two hosts in PuA accumulation patterns and their responses to nutrient conditions. To demonstrate the applicability of the yeast-derived oil, it was evaluated as a polymer feedstock, yielding bio-polyurethane with properties similar to those prepared from premium pomegranate seed oil. Collectively, this work establishes a yeast platform for efficient PuA production and provides strategies applicable to other structurally complex plant-derived lipids, enabling the production of advanced bio-based materials.

abstract: This study evaluates four Layered Double Hydroxides-derived mixed oxides, MgAlFeOx, MgCuAlOx, MgCuFeOx, and MgNiFeOx, to elucidate structure-performance relationships influencing sorption-enhanced water-gas shift (SEWGS) efficiency. Calcination at 500 °C yielded periclase-type structures with distinct textural and surface properties. MgCuAlOx showed the highest surface area and pore volume, whereas MgCuFeOx exhibited the largest crystallite size and the lowest porosity. At 450 °C, MgCuFeOx achieved complete CO conversion, consistent with its low Ea value, strong low-temperature reducibility, and high surface exposure of Cu2+ and oxidized Fe species. In contrast, under CO2-containing feeds at 300 °C, MgCuAlOx performed better, reaching approximately 95% CO conversion compared with 75% for MgCuFeOx. This behavior was associated with higher CO2 uptake and greater basic-site density. Cyclic testing under product-rich conditions showed that MgCuFeOx displays higher hydrogen yields and CO conversion than MgCuAlOx, after an initial adjustment. These results show that SEWGS performance depends on the operating regime: Cu-Fe redox domains favor kinetically controlled WGS operation, while Al-stabilized, high-surface-area basic matrices improve performance under equilibrium-limited CO2-rich conditions.

Tuning bifunctional Pt catalysts on Nb, Mo, and W oxide-modified carbon nanofibers for the continuous selective hydrocracking and hydroisomerization of n-hexadecane as a Fischer-Tropsch product model compound
abstract: This work investigates bifunctional Pt catalysts supported on carbon nanofibers (CNFs) modified with Nb, Mo, or W oxides for the hydroconversion of n-hexadecane as a model compound of Fischer-Tropsch (FT) products. Oxide functionalization was used to overcome the low intrinsic acidity of carbon supports by introducing proton-donating surface sites while preserving favorable textural properties. The nature of the oxide promoter strongly influenced the metal-acid balance, Pt accessibility, and catalytic behavior. At 350 °C, 20 bar and a WHSV of 7.6 h −1 , Pt supported on bare CNFs showed low activity (18.3% conversion) and a product distribution consistent with a substantial contribution from hydrogenolysis, with 7.9% selectivity to C16 isomers, whereas all oxide-modified catalysts activated hydroisomerization pathways (72.0–82.2% selectivity to C16 isomers). Pt/W-CNF500 exhibited the highest conversion (55.5%) with 85.5% total isomer selectivity and the highest share of multibranched C16 isomers, indicating an effective compromise between acidity and hydrogenation capacity. Reaction temperature mainly controlled conversion and secondary hydrocracking, while space velocity had a limited effect on selectivity. These results demonstrate that oxide-modified CNFs constitute a tunable platform for designing bifunctional catalysts for controlled upgrading of FT-derived products.

title: Fast parameter identification for elementary-step surface mechanisms using kinetically parameterized neural networks
abstract: Microkinetic models provide physically grounded descriptions of catalytic systems. However, quantitative prediction of catalyst performance requires refinement of elementary-step parameters against reactor-level measurement data. This calibration is computationally demanding because it involves repeated reactor simulations with computationally expensive microkinetic models. Surrogates that approximate the kinetic model reduce evaluation cost, but are currently tied to fixed kinetic parameters and therefore cannot be used for mechanism calibration. To address this limitation, we introduce kinetically parameterized Global Reaction Neural Network (pGRNN) surrogates that map both operating conditions and elementary-step kinetic parameters of a detailed microkinetic mechanism to species source terms. By embedding stoichiometry, thermodynamic consistency, and elementary-step structure, the surrogate replaces expensive kinetics evaluations while retaining a mechanism-consistent representation. Using the preferential CO oxidation on platinum, we show that the pGRNN predicts source terms across a broad range of operating conditions and kinetic parameters with a relative error of 1.2%. Reactor model evaluation is accelerated by a factor of 3100. The pGRNN is used in place of the kinetic model during mechanism calibration, reducing calibration time by factors of approximately 2400 for a synthetic single light-off curve and a synthetic multi-experiment campaign. Finally, we demonstrate the workflow by efficiently calibrating the mechanism against measured reactor-performance data from two experimental setups. A differentiable implementation of kinetic and reactor model further enables efficient gradient-based calibration. The proposed workflow provides an accelerated route for adapting detailed microkinetic models to catalyst-specific performance data.

abstract: Developing high-quality wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites is crucial to construct efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs). However, the high defect density and halide segregation hinder the improvement of power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability for WBG perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Herein, one carboxyl-functionalized imidazolium cation modulation strategy is reported to heal the multiple defects within WBG perovskite films by multifarious chemical bonding modes. After incorporating the additive imidazole-4-acetic acid hydrochloride (ImAcHCl), the trap-assisted nonradiative recombination at grain boundaries is suppressed, the halide segregation is mitigated, and the stability of perovskite films is improved. Moreover, this method is effective in defect passivation for different bandgaps of perovskites. Ultimately, the ImAcHCl-modified 1.68 eV WBG PSCs achieve a PCE of 24.54% ranking among the highest PCEs realized for 1.66–1.70 eV PSCs, and retain 90% of their initial PCE after 883 h of continuous maximum power point tracking. Integration with crystalline silicon subcells further enabled the construction of a perovskite/Si tandem device with a PCE of 33.06%. This work provides valuable insights into overcoming the instability challenges of the WBG perovskite film via functional group functionalization method toward high-performance WBG PSCs and perovskite/silicon TSCs.

Polysulfone nanocomposite membranes for water filtration and microcystin removal: Mechanical characterisation and multi-scheme homogenisation analysis
abstract: Polysulfone (PSf) membranes containing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) and either cerium dioxide (CeO₂) or laboratory-milled bentonite were investigated through structural characterisation, filtration testing and micromechanical analysis. Six formulations were fabricated by non-solvent-induced phase separation: pristine PSf, PSf/PVP and four nanocomposites with 0.5 or 1.0 wt% filler relative to the casting solution. Characterisation combined microscopy, spectroscopy, diffraction, wettability, water uptake, porosity, flux, fouling, tensile testing and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). The incorporation of nano-CeO₂ and nano-bentonite into the PSf/PVP membrane altered the surface morphology, increased surface hydrophilicity, and decreased the total fouling ratio. The PSf/PVP 1 wt% bentonite membrane exhibited the highest water uptake (74.67%) and the highest pure water flux (~230 L m −2 h −1 ), indicating enhanced affinity toward water and improved water filtration performance. Young's modulus ranged from 20.9 MPa (PSf/PVP) to 84.1 MPa (PSf/PVP with 1.0 wt% bentonite). The highest total microcystin removal, 76.36%, was achieved with 0.5 wt% bentonite. The storage modulus (E′) ranking of the samples, measured by DMA, remained unchanged over 25–120 °C, and each sample retained 83.5–84.3% of its 25 °C value at 120 °C. Seven analytical approaches were compared using the measured PSf/PVP tensile modulus as an effective matrix reference. At nominal filler fractions, spherical Mori–Tanaka estimates were 21.08–21.92 MPa, compared with measured nanocomposite tensile moduli of 25.63–84.07 MPa. Combined with FTIR evidence and bentonite swelling, these results are consistent with chemical interphase formation and swelling-induced crosslinking, rather than classical load transfer, as the likely dominant stiffening mechanisms.

Accelerating interfacial charge transfer via spin polarized Ni-doped Co3O4 for high-performance zinc-iron flow batteries
abstract: Interfacial charge-transfer critically governs Zn plating/stripping kinetics and determines the electrochemical performance of zinc‑iron flow batteries. However, the regulation of electron-transfer pathways at the spin-level remains unexplored. Herein, we propose a micro-interface spin engineering strategy using Ni-doped spinel Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst and reveal that the local spin configuration serves as a fundamental descriptor for regulating interfacial electron transfer pathways during zinc deposition. Guided by the Mott two-current model, Ni doping modulates the spin structure of spinel Co 3 O 4 , creating asymmetric spin-dependent channels and establishing a dominant low-resistance spin transport pathway. As a result, Ni-doped Co 3 O 4 markedly lowers the apparent activation energy for interfacial Zn/Zn 2+ charge transfer from 23.61 kJ·mol −1 to 12.79 kJ·mol −1 and exhibits the lowest charge-transfer resistance. The optimized spin-dependent transport pathway further promotes uniform Zn nucleation and surface diffusion, effectively suppressing dendrite formation. Benefiting from these advantages, the zinc‑iron flow battery maintains an energy efficiency above 80% at 100 mA·cm −2 and sustains over 600 cycles with negligible capacity decay. This work establishes a mechanistic framework linking local spin polarization with interfacial electron-transfer pathways, offering new insight into spin-regulated Zn deposition kinetics and providing a rational strategy for designing high-performance zinc-based flow batteries.

Operational strategies for industrial-scale methanol synthesis via CO2 hydrogenation under varying load conditions
abstract: Methanol is an important bulk chemical and versatile energy carrier that enables large-scale renewable energy imports due to its storability and compatibility with existing infrastructure. However, producing methanol from a fluctuating renewable hydrogen supply requires large storage capacities or load-flexible operation of the methanol synthesis process. This raises the question of how the methanol synthesis loop can be operated at part-load down to 10% without unduly shortening the catalyst lifetime. In this study, we used a one-dimensional, pseudo-homogeneous reactor model for industrial-scale methanol synthesis and integrated it into a steady-state process simulation of the entire synthesis loop. Our results demonstrate that decreasing the load increases both the hot spot temperature in the reactor and the water partial pressure. To prevent accelerated catalyst deactivation through sintering and hydrothermal sintering, we have developed operational strategies to enable load flexibility while mitigating critical operating conditions such as increased hot spot temperatures and water partial pressures. The main strategy identified for this purpose involves the combined adjustment of various operating parameters such as loop pressure and coolant temperature. Furthermore, integrating additional flexibility measures, including the stoichiometric number, purge ratio, condenser temperature, and recycling of purified methanol to the reactor inlet, reduces the required extent of pressure and temperature variation. These findings demonstrate that flexible part-load operation of methanol synthesis reactors down to 10% load is feasible without increasing catalyst deactivation.

title: Single-atom cerium alloyed high-entropy Nanosheets for ultralow-barrier alkaline hydrogen evolution
Mechanically reinforced alginate/cellulose nanofiber aerogel fibers with dual-stage oriented porous structures for thermal insulation textiles
Regulating local energy deposition to direct surface intermediate turnover in higher-alkane plasma catalysis
abstract: Nonthermal plasma-assisted CO 2 reforming of propane is usually directed toward syngas and hydrocarbons, whereas direct formation of liquid oxygenates and alcohols is challenging due to a broad C 1 -C 3 radical pool generated by propane. The key challenge is not only forming oxygenated intermediates, but also converting them into alcohol-related C O species before secondary decomposition. Here, we address this intermediate-turnover challenge by designing PtNi catalysts that couple surface chemistry with catalyst-dependent local energy deposition. Compared with plasma-only, Pt-Ni/Al 2 O 3 increased the total conversion rate from 55 to 118 mmol/g cat. h, apparent total liquid-product selectivity from 23% to 48%, and alcohol production rate from 1.1 to 2.65 mmol/g cat. h, while decreasing the energy cost from 5.0 to 2.8 MJ/mol. Time-resolved in-situ plasma-catalytic DRIFTS shows that Pt-Ni/Al 2 O 3 promotes carbonate/formate conversion toward C O and oxygenate-related C O intermediates because abundant acid-base adsorption sites, accessible Ni Pt interfaces, and stronger local discharge act together. By contrast, finer particles and stronger metal-support interaction on Ni/Pt/Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 favor oxygenated-intermediate accumulation and liquid-product formation, but stabilize formate, carbonate, and C O species and limit downstream alcohol-forming turnover. Ar dilution and CO 2 -rich feeds further increase charge transfer, discharge power, and local specific energy input, while higher flow rate limits secondary oxygenate decomposition. Under optimized ambient conditions, Pt-Ni/Al 2 O 3 achieved 78% propane conversion, 18% CO 2 conversion, and 10% alcohol selectivity, while maintaining stable performance over 300 min across three consecutive reaction-regeneration cycles. These findings establish coupled control of adsorption, local energy deposition, and residence time as a strategy for directing CO 2 -propane plasma chemistry toward liquid oxygenates and alcohols.

title: Simultaneous enhancement of energy storage density and efficiency in Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3-modified BaTiO3-based multilayer ceramic capacitors via Bi-O hybridization and phase transition engineering
N-doped carbon-encapsulated cubic FeS2 hollow nanospheres for sodium-ion storage
abstract: Iron disulfide offers a high theoretical sodium-storage capacity and attractive resource advantages, but its practical electrochemistry is limited by poor intrinsic conductivity, structural instability during repeated conversion, and an incompletely understood contribution from the sulfur sublattice. Here, nitrogen-doped carbon-encapsulated cubic FeS 2 hollow nanospheres (FeS 2 @NC) are constructed to integrate nanoscale confinement, electronic conduction, and coupled cationic-anionic redox chemistry within one architecture. The hollow framework provides internal space for conversion-induced structural variation, while the N-doped carbon layer maintains continuous electronic contact around the FeS 2 nanocrystals. As a result, FeS 2 @NC retains 391.8 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles at 4 A g −1 , corresponding to a capacity decay of only 0.013% per cycle. In the cycling test, FeS 2 @NC retains a reversible capacity of 855.1 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles at 0.3 A g −1 . In a separate rate-capability test, the electrode delivers 692.2 mAh g −1 at 0.3 A g −1 and maintains 430.6 mAh g −1 even at 10 A g −1 . More importantly, density functional theory calculations, in situ powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), and ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) are combined to follow the structural and electronic evolution of Fe and S during sodiation/desodiation, providing direct evidence that sulfur anions participate in the reversible conversion process rather than acting as an electrochemically passive sublattice. A full cell using Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 @rGO as the cathode further sustains 395.5 mAh g −1 after 60 cycles at 0.3 A g −1 . These results connect the improved electrochemical response of FeS 2 @NC with both structural confinement and reversible Fe/S redox evolution.

Overequilibria and master curves illustrated by the Wei–Prater mechanism
abstract: Developments of kinetic behavior from previous studies surrounding the conservatively perturbed equilibria (CPE) are extended to the triangular, or Wei-Prater, mechanism. Characteristics of the mechanism are derived, including the time and height of the extrema point. Analytical expressions are also produced for the master curves of the mechanism with over- or under-equilibria. Additionally, kinetic invariances of the system have been identified, and a procedure has been developed to reveal the underlying kinetic parameters via the kinetic invariances and mechanism characteristics. The Wei-Prater mechanism and its characteristics are then quantifiably compared to previously studied linear mechanisms. Finally, the Gibbs Free Energy profiles of the mechanism are analyzed, and identified as an area of further study.

abstract: Direct borohydride fuel cells (DBFCs) are promising energy conversion systems due to their high theoretical energy density, but their practical performance is limited by rapid borohydride hydrolysis and sluggish borohydride oxidation reaction (BOR) kinetics. Here, we report a plasma-engineered vacancy-rich RuO 2 /Co 3 O 4 heterostructure catalyst designed to accelerate BOR through coupled interfacial and defect modulation. The synergistic interaction between the heterointerface and oxygen vacancies tunes the electronic structure and facilitates the adsorption and conversion of key intermediates, thereby accelerating BOR kinetics. As a result, the catalyst exhibits a low overpotential of 133 mV, a charge-transfer resistance of 0.545 Ω, and a Tafel slope of 130.8 mV dec −1 . In a DBFC device, it delivers a peak power density of 361 mW cm −2 and retains 91.5% of its initial performance after 300 h of operation. These results demonstrate an effective strategy for enhancing BOR performance through coupled interface and defect engineering.

Efficient SABRE hyperpolarization using falling-film microreactors
abstract: The efficient dissolution of parahydrogen in a target solution is an essential requirement for parahydrogen-induced polarization experiments. A low transfer rate limits the exchange rate of hydrogen and reduces signal enhancement. In this study, we show the extent to which replacing typical membrane reactors with simple falling-film reactors can improve parahydrogen uptake, and in turn, signal strength, in a continuous-flow Signal Amplification by Reversible Exchange (SABRE) experiment. In the first part of this study, the falling-films were investigated using flow MRI to determine their thickness, and surface-to-volume ratio and to observe vortex structures within them. We then compared a tube-in-tube reactor with a single-channel falling film reactor and reached an 8-fold increase of signal strength for a volumetric flow rate of 3 mL min −1 . Staggered herringbone grooves were added to the open channel to homogenize the solution during polarization transfer, and in turn further promote gas dissolution. This led to an increase of up to 40% of signal enhancement. These improvements were achieved while using a falling film reactor having a smaller gas-liquid exchange area than the tube-in-tube reactor. This study emphasizes the need to consider hyperpolarization as a mass transport problem, and to investigate flow using the same technology.

title: Strengthening the role of the bioeconomy in sustainability through innovation, circularity, engineering constrains and strategic governance
abstract: Bioeconomy can make a decisive contribution to the sustainability of agriculture, fisheries, and forestry, if it is guided by clear principles: prioritizing food and feed security, safeguarding ecosystem integrity, promoting the cascading use of biomass, and ensuring the equitable distribution of value. Nevertheless, the transition towards a circular bioeconomy requires the large-scale industrial deployment of transformative, resource-efficient technologies for biomass conversion, separation, and process integration. This paper examines why the circular bioeconomy has become central to sustainable production and consumption, what role deep-tech innovation plays in accelerating its uptake, which trends will shape the sector towards 2040, and how the “valley of death” can be narrowed through circular communication and skills development. The study combines PRISMA-guided literature selection, keyword co-occurrence mapping, comparative policy assessment and an engineering and technology assessment, integrated through a systems-level synthesis organized around one organizing hypothesis, five research questions and six defining relations. The study is an evidence-informed conceptual synthesis, not a validated model, and its outcome is five propositions for future empirical testing. The transition is treated as an explicitly non-linear process exhibiting path dependence, threshold behavior and multiplicative failure: in an illustrative, uncalibrated gate model of commercialization, raising the pass probability at four successive gates from 0.6 to 0.8 raises the deployment probability from 0.13 to 0.41. Within the fourteen-record corpus, the co-occurrence network comprises 121 keywords, 111 of which form a single connected component, sustainable development showing the highest total strength (93); and European Investment Bank activity of EUR 7.1 billion per year covers approximately 6% of the estimated EUR 121.8 billion annual investment gap of the EU bioeconomy. The results are directly applicable to policy makers, practitioners, academia and entrepreneurs.

Continuous three-phase hydrogenation in a jet loop reactor: a model compound study
abstract: This proof-of-concept study investigates the continuous three-phase catalytic hydrogenation of a model compound in a jet loop reactor operated as a CSTR. Acetophenone (AP), used as a model compound for active pharmaceutical intermediate hydrogenation, was hydrogenated in two consecutive steps to 1-phenylethanol (PE) and ethylbenzene (EB) using gas-phase hydrogen over a 5 wt.% Pd/C catalyst under varying flow rates and feed AP concentrations. A previously established Langmuir-Hinshelwood kinetic model, assuming competitive and dissociative hydrogen adsorption, accurately captured the dynamic concentration profiles across most continuous operating conditions without refitting the kinetic parameters. The PE yield increased with flow rate, as shorter residence times limited the secondary PE hydrodeoxygenation to EB, and with elevated water concentration, as water inhibited the water-forming PE hydrodeoxygenation step. Experiments were conducted to evaluate the effect of different startup strategies on steady-state stabilization time during batch-to-continuous operation. Early and late switching policies were compared, with the late switch identified as the preferred startup strategy because it minimized post-switch stabilization time by initiating continuous operation from a reactor composition closer to the CSTR steady state.

title: Zn2+ intercalation triggered oxygen vacancy engineering and interlayer expansion in layered δ-MnO2 for boosted sodium storage
Interface engineering of crystalline–amorphous hollow c-Co₃S₄/a-CoxP nanocages for all-pH hydrogen evolution
abstract: Exploring highly active and stable non-noble-metal electrocatalysts is critical for the widespread adoption of hydrogen energy technologies. In this work, we report the synthesis of hollow crystalline–amorphous nanocages composed of crystalline cobalt sulfide (c-Co 3 S 4 ) and amorphous cobalt phosphide (a-Co x P), derived from ZIF-67, through precise morphology and structural modulation. These c-Co 3 S 4 /a-Co x P nanocages feature abundant electrocatalytically active sites and exhibit excellent hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity across the full pH range. The optimized nanocages achieve low overpotentials of 44 mV, 128 mV, and 119 mV at 10 mA·cm −2 in acidic, neutral, and alkaline media, respectively. This outstanding HER performance is attributed to the numerous active interfaces between crystalline Co 3 S 4 and amorphous Co x P, which enhance the exposure of active sites and facilitate electron transfer. This study highlights the potential of crystalline–amorphous interface coupling as a versatile strategy for optimizing electrocatalytic activity and paves the way for the rational design of high-performance transition metal compound catalysts.

title: Deciphering support-amine matching in resin-supported solid amine adsorbents for CO2 capture: Roles of pore structure and skeleton
Design and performance of solar concentrator assisted photocatalytic reactors for solar-to-hydrogen conversion
abstract: Solar-powered water splitting via photocatalysis provides a sustainable method towards low-carbon hydrogen generation. However, efficient capture and utilisation of solar energy remains a key challenge for existing reactor designs. Whilst Compound Parabolic Concentrators (CPCs) can enhance the Solar-To-Hydrogen (STH) efficiency of photocatalytic systems, to date the optimal designs have not been developed. To address this knowledge gap, we report a methodology to design optimised solar photocatalytic reactors and predict their performance for maximum hydrogen production. Reactor design features for four geographically diverse locations – London, Cardiff, Cairo and Chennai – are presented and shown to achieve Annual Optical Efficiency (AOE) of 74.2%, 78.4%, 89.1% and 84.8% respectively. The model incorporates real life solar and climatic conditions with accompanying experiments enabling validation of the model results. Experimental data is used to predict the total hydrogen production for peak summer months for several geometric configurations across all four locations. Experimental results show that STH peaked at 353 K. This integrated experimental-computational framework provides valuable insights into the optimisation of solar concentrator design to maximise hydrogen generation and advances the development of sustainable hydrogen production technologies.

Direct in situ Raman evidence of particle formation in a continuous microjet reactor
abstract: Continuous-flow synthesis provides significant advantages for nano- and microparticle production, including precise control over particle size, enhanced reproducibility, and scalability. The microjet reactor (MJR) has emerged as a promising platform for the continuous synthesis of a wide range of materials. However, direct experimental evidence for particle formation within the reactor chamber under real operating conditions has remained elusive. In this study, we present a modified microjet reactor equipped with a sapphire window that enables real-time, in situ Raman spectroscopy of precipitation processes at the jet collision zone. Three model systems, i.e. strontium sulfate, silver phosphate, and calcium sulfate, were selected based on solubility and Raman activity criteria. In situ Raman analysis revealed direct evidence of nucleation and particle formation for SrSO4 and Ag3PO4 inside the reactor. In contrast, no in situ signal for CaSO4 could be detected due to its significantly lower supersaturation and resulting low nucleation rate under the given conditions. These results confirm that Raman spectroscopy can provide valuable insight into continuous particle formation in high-flow-rate microreactors.

Split-T7 transcriptional promoter encoding molecular logic circuit for versatile cell-free diagnostics
abstract: Cell-free systems are promising tools for molecular diagnostics, yet they remain limited by low multiplexing capacity and background interference. Here, a multiplex cell-free diagnostic platform termed BOLT (Bi-locked Orchestrated Logic-triggered Transcription amplification platform) has been developed by a split-T7 transcriptional promoter strategy. BOLT encodes a molecular logic circuit by locking the split T7 promoter fragments within independent programmable metastable hairpins. Target-triggered strand displacement serves as the circuit input, simultaneously unlocking these conformational gates to drive the output of promoter assembly. The bi-locked design strictly suppresses background leakage by raising the thermodynamic barrier against spontaneous assembly, thereby ensuring the reconstituted promoter drives orthogonal RNA aptamer transcription for crosstalk-free multiplexing. BOLT achieved HPV16 and HPV18 genotyping within 1 h, with femtomolar sensitivity and high qPCR concordance in cervical swab samples, demonstrating ≥96.3% sensitivity and 100% specificity. This split-promoter logic strategy provides a programmable framework for high-fidelity multiplexed cell-free diagnostics.

Gelatin–itaconate enables room-temperature extrusion-based 3D printing as a high-performance, sustainable alternative to GelMA
abstract: Gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) is a widely used photocrosslinkable biomaterial for tissue engineering and biofabrication; however, its synthesis relies on petroleum-derived methacrylic anhydride/acid, and its precursor formulations generally require low-temperature processing to achieve sufficient printability. Here, we present gelatin–itaconate (GelIA), synthesized using bio-based itaconic acid, as a sustainable alternative to GelMA for room-temperature extrusion-based 3D printing. To isolate the influence of functional-group chemistry, GelIA and GelMA were synthesized with equivalent degrees of functionalization (36–38%) and systematically characterized by TNBS assay, ¹H NMR, FTIR, SEM, rheology, in situ photorheology, compression testing, swelling, enzymatic degradation, tissue adhesion, and printability evaluation. Compared with GelMA, GelIA exhibited higher precursor viscosity, pronounced shear-thinning behavior, improved structural recovery, and enabled stable extrusion-based 3D printing at 21–23 °C using only 5% (w/v) polymer, whereas GelMA with the same degree of functionalization was not printable under identical conditions. Following photocrosslinking, GelIA formed a more interconnected hydrogel network with enhanced viscoelastic properties, higher effective crosslink density, improved compressive properties, superior tissue adhesion, and greater structural integrity, resulting in enhanced stress-relaxation behavior. Despite exhibiting a higher swelling capacity, GelIA degraded more slowly than GelMA, indicating improved hydrogel stability. These findings validate our hypothesis that the additional carboxylic acid functionality of bio-based itaconate strengthens intermolecular interactions within the gelatin network, thereby improving both precursor rheology and hydrogel performance without increasing polymer concentration. Collectively, GelIA represents not only a sustainable, high-performance alternative to GelMA but also demonstrates how rational functional-group engineering can be exploited to regulate intermolecular interactions, enabling next-generation photocrosslinkable bioinks for room-temperature biofabrication and tissue engineering.

Wearable microneedle potentiometric sensors with temperature correction for potassium monitoring toward precision plant nutrition
abstract: Continuous nutrient monitoring in plants offers a transformative approach to tailored fertilization, ensuring optimal growth and environmental sustainability. Potassium is a vital macronutrient involved in key physiological processes such as stomatal regulation and photosynthesis. In response to global food security challenges and climate change, this work presents the development of 3D-printed microneedle (MN)-based potentiometric sensors for real-time, in-planta potassium monitoring. The core novelty of this work lies in the fabrication process, which uses highly versatile 3D printing to miniaturize the MN-based sensor, making it the smallest reported MN potentiometric sensor, and in its capability for extended monitoring, reporting the longest in-planta monitoring period. The polymeric MN arrays were metallized through sputtering and coated with ion-selective membranes. The resulting sensor exhibited a near-Nernstian response of 59.4 ± 0.61 mV log a K+ −1 , a fast time of response (t 95% < 60 s), and demonstrated exceptional analytical robustness across various pH levels, temperatures, and sap compositions. To ensure field-ready accuracy, a temperature correction model was integrated into the readout system. The sensor's performance was validated against ion chromatography, with errors ranging from 1.4% to 11.1% depending on the plant species. Crucially, the MN sensor was successfully applied to monitor potassium dynamics in tomato leaves over five days. The versatility of 3D printing facilitates rapid design adaptation for different plant species and organ placement. This research introduces a scalable platform for real-time in-planta potassium tracking, which could eventually support efforts to optimize crop yields and reduce the environmental footprint of modern agriculture.

abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) is hindered by catalyst deactivation and the high costs of conventional hydrogen-reduction-based regeneration. In this study, we propose a novel Ni-substituted SrTiO 3 (STN) catalyst system enabling full activity recovery via a simplified self-regeneration without the need for additional H 2 reduction DRM (SR-DRM) scenario. This study employs a multidisciplinary approach to bridge atomic-level catalyst dynamics and industrial-scale sustainability through a multi-scale evaluation. At the atomic scale, spectroscopic analysis and CO 2 pulse tests reveal a structural memory effect where lattice-confined Ni 3+ and high oxygen mobility drive reversible Ni exsolution and self-regeneration. This microscopic resilience facilitates process-level innovation by eliminating external hydrogen and minimizing downtime. To evaluate systemic impact, techno-economic and life-cycle assessments (TEA/LCA) were integrated. Based on the scenario-based process simulation under identical operating conditions, SR-DRM showed an additional 328.4 ton/year of syngas production (1.9% increase) and approximately 22.19 ton H 2 /year of hydrogen savings (2.0% increase) under identical operating conditions, together with 6.2% reduction of levelized cost of hydrogen and a 18.6% reduction in global warming potential. The economic and environmental benefits are mainly caused by SR-DRM operation. By reconciling fundamental materials science with rigorous process evaluation, this framework demonstrates how atomic-scale lattice design dictates macroscopic economic and environmental viability, offering a new paradigm for sustainable carbon capture and utilization.
